transliteration.text: utá ǀ vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ sahasya ǀ pra-vidvā́n ǀ mártaḥ ǀ mártam ǀ marcáyati ǀ dvayéna ǀátaḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ stavamāna ǀ stuvántam ǀ ágne ǀ mā́kiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ duḥ-itā́ya ǀ dhāyīḥ ǁ

Sukta 147.translation: “When, Son of Strength, a man skilful (in deception) assails another man with a doubly (malignant prayer), do you,Agni, duly propitiated, protect him who worships you (from its effects); consign us not to misfortune.”
Sukta 147.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त वा॒ यः स॑हस्य प्रवि॒द्वान्मर्तो॒ मर्तं॑ म॒र्चय॑ति द्व॒येन॑ । अत॑: पाहि स्तवमान स्तु॒वन्त॒मग्ने॒ माकि॑र्नो दुरि॒ताय॑ धायीः

devanagari.text: मथीद्यदीं विष्टो मातरिश्वा होतारं विश्वाप्सुं विश्वदेव्यं ।नि यं दधुर्मनुष्यासु विक्षु स्वर्ण चित्रं वपुषे विभावं ॥
मथीत् । यत् । ईम् । विष्टः । मातरिश्वा । होतारम् । विश्वऽअप्सुम् । विश्वऽदेव्यम् ।नि । यम् । दधुः । मनुष्यासु । विक्षु । स्वः । न । चित्रम् । वपुषे । विभाऽवम् ॥

transliteration.text: máthīt ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ viṣṭáḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ hótāram ǀ viśvá-apsum ǀ viśvá-devyam ǀní ǀ yám ǀ dadhúḥ ǀ manuṣyā́su ǀ vikṣú ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ citrám ǀ vápuṣe ǀ vibhā́-vam ǁ

Sukta 148.translation: “The wind, penetrating (amidst the fuel), has excited (Agni), the invoker (of the gods), the multiform, the minister of all the deities, whom they have established amongst mortal worshippers for the accomplishment of sacrifice, like the wonderful and variously radiant sun.”
Sukta 148.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मथी॒द्यदीं॑ वि॒ष्टो मा॑त॒रिश्वा॒ होता॑रं वि॒श्वाप्सुं॑ वि॒श्वदे॑व्यम् । नि यं द॒धुर्म॑नु॒ष्या॑सु वि॒क्षु स्व१॒॑र्ण चि॒त्रं वपु॑षे वि॒भाव॑म्

devanagari.text: ददानमिन्न ददभंत मन्माग्निर्वरूथं मम तस्य चाकन् ।जुषंत विश्वान्यस्य कर्मोपस्तुतिं भरमाणस्य कारोः ॥
ददानम् । इत् । न । ददभन्त । मन्म । अग्निः । वरूथम् । मम । तस्य । चाकन् ।जुषन्त । विश्वानि । अस्य । कर्म । उपऽस्तुतिम् । भरमाणस्य । कारोः ॥

transliteration.text: dadānám ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ dadabhanta ǀ mánma ǀ agníḥ ǀ várūtham ǀ máma ǀ tásya ǀ cākan ǀjuṣánta ǀ víśvāni ǀ asya ǀ kárma ǀ úpa-stutim ǀ bháramāṇasya ǀ kāróḥ ǁ

Sukta 148.translation: “Let not (my enemies) prevail against me, when presenting acceptable (oblations), for (Agni) is desirous of my so offered adoration, and all they (the gods) are gratified by the (pious) acts of me, the reciter of their praise, and the celebrator (of the sacrifice).”
Sukta 148.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द॒दा॒नमिन्न द॑दभन्त॒ मन्मा॒ग्निर्वरू॑थं॒ मम॒ तस्य॑ चाकन् । जु॒षन्त॒ विश्वा॑न्यस्य॒ कर्मोप॑स्तुतिं॒ भर॑माणस्य का॒रोः

devanagari.text: नित्ये चिन्नु यं सदने जगृभ्रे प्रशस्तिभिर्दधिरे यज्ञियासः ।प्र सू नयंत गृभयंत इष्टावश्वासो न रथ्यो रारहाणाः ॥
नित्ये । चित् । नु । यम् । सदने । जगृभ्रे । प्रशस्तिऽभिः । दधिरे । यज्ञियासः ।प्र । सु । नयन्त । गृभयन्तः । इष्टौ । अश्वासः । न । रथ्यः । ररहाणाः ॥

transliteration.text: nítye ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ yám ǀ sádane ǀ jagṛbhré ǀ práśasti-bhiḥ ǀ dadhiré ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀprá ǀ sú ǀ nayanta ǀ gṛbháyantaḥ ǀ iṣṭáu ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ rarahāṇā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 148.translation: “Him, whom the worshippers lay hold of in his perpetual abode, they detain by their praises, and the holders convey him diligently to the sacrifice, as rapid coursers, harnessed to a car, (bear the rider to his destination).”
Sukta 148.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नित्ये॑ चि॒न्नु यं सद॑ने जगृ॒भ्रे प्रश॑स्तिभिर्दधि॒रे य॒ज्ञिया॑सः । प्र सू न॑यन्त गृ॒भय॑न्त इ॒ष्टावश्वा॑सो॒ न र॒थ्यो॑ रारहा॒णाः

devanagari.text: पुरूणि दस्मो नि रिणाति जंभैराद्रोचते वन आ विभावा ।आदस्य वातो अनु वाति शोचिरस्तुर्न शर्यामसनामनु द्यून् ॥

transliteration.text: purū́ṇi ǀ dasmáḥ ǀ ní ǀ riṇāti ǀ jámbhaiḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ rocate ǀ váne ǀ ā́ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀā́t ǀ asya ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vāti ǀ śocíḥ ǀ ástuḥ ǀ ná ǀ śáryām ǀ asanā́m ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǁ

Sukta 148.translation: “The destroyer, (Agni), consumes numerous (trees) by his flames, and shares with manifold radiance in the forest; the favouring wind blows (the flames) onwards day by day, like the swift arrows (śaryāiṣavaḥ śaramayyaḥ--Nirukta5.4) of an archer.”
Sukta 148.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पु॒रूणि॑ द॒स्मो नि रि॑णाति॒ जम्भै॒राद्रो॑चते॒ वन॒ आ वि॒भावा॑ । आद॑स्य॒ वातो॒ अनु॑ वाति शो॒चिरस्तु॒र्न शर्या॑मस॒नामनु॒ द्यून्

devanagari.text: न यं रिपवो न रिषण्यवो गर्भे संतं रेषणा रेषयंति ।अंधा अपश्या न दभन्नभिख्या नित्यास ईं प्रेतारो अरक्षन् ॥
न । यम् । रिपवः । न । रिषण्यवः । गर्भे । सन्तम् । रेषणाः । रेषयन्ति ।अन्धाः । अपश्याः । न । दभन् । अभिऽख्या । नित्यासः । ईम् । प्रेतारः । अरक्षन् ॥

transliteration.text: ná ǀ yám ǀ ripávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ riṣaṇyávaḥ ǀ gárbhe ǀ sántam ǀ reṣaṇā́ḥ ǀ reṣáyanti ǀandhā́ḥ ǀ apaśyā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ dabhan ǀ abhi-khyā́ ǀ nítyāsaḥ ǀ īm ǀ pretā́raḥ ǀ arakṣan ǁ

Sukta 148.translation: “The blind (of intellect), or those who see not (physically), detract not from his glory, whom no enemies no malevolent adversaries, harm, even whilst yet in (his) embryo (condition), for his constant encouragers defend him.”
Sukta 148.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न यं रि॒पवो॒ न रि॑ष॒ण्यवो॒ गर्भे॒ सन्तं॑ रेष॒णा रे॒षय॑न्ति । अ॒न्धा अ॑प॒श्या न द॑भन्नभि॒ख्या नित्या॑स ईं प्रे॒तारो॑ अरक्षन्

devanagari.text: महः स राय एषते पतिर्दन्निन इनस्य वसुनः पद आ ।उप ध्रजंतमद्रयो विधन्नित् ॥
महः । सः । रायः । आ । ईषते । पतिः । दन् । इनः । इनस्य । वसुनः । पदे । आ ।उप । ध्रजन्तम् । अद्रयः । विधन् । इत् ॥

transliteration.text: maháḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īṣate ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǀ ináḥ ǀ inásya ǀ vásunaḥ ǀ padé ǀ ā́ ǀúpa ǀ dhrájantam ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ vidhán ǀ ít ǁ

Sukta 149.translation: “Agni, the lord of great wealth, the granter (of desires) comes (to the plural ce of sacrifice); he, the lord of lords, comes to the plural ce of affluence, (the altar); the stones prepare (the libation fo rhim) as he approaches.”
Sukta 149.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒हः स रा॒य एष॑ते॒ पति॒र्दन्नि॒न इ॒नस्य॒ वसु॑नः प॒द आ । उप॒ ध्रज॑न्त॒मद्र॑यो वि॒धन्नित्

devanagari.text: स यो वृषा नरां न रोदस्योः श्रवोभिरस्ति जीवपीतसर्गः ।प्र यः सस्राणः शिश्रीत योनौ ॥
सः । यः । वृषा । नराम् । न । रोदस्योः । श्रवःऽभिः । अस्ति । जीवपीतऽसर्गः ।प्र । यः । सस्राणः । शिश्रीत । योनौ ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ narā́m ǀ ná ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀ śrávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ásti ǀ jīvápīta-sargaḥ ǀprá ǀ yáḥ ǀ sasrāṇáḥ ǀ śiśrītá ǀ yónau ǁ

Sukta 149.translation: “He, who is, as it were, the genitive rator of men as well as of heaven and earth, of whom creation has imbibed life, abides with his glories; he it is who, entering into the womb (of being), procreates (all living creatures).”
Sukta 149.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स यो वृषा॑ न॒रां न रोद॑स्यो॒: श्रवो॑भि॒रस्ति॑ जी॒वपी॑तसर्गः । प्र यः स॑स्रा॒णः शि॑श्री॒त योनौ॑

devanagari.text: आ यः पुरं नार्मिणीमदीदेदत्यः कविर्नभन्यो नार्वा ।सूरो न रुरुक्वाञ्छतात्मा ॥
आ । यः । पुरम् । नार्मिणीम् । अदीदेत् । अत्यः । कविः । नभन्यः । न । अर्वा ।सूरः । न । रुरुक्वान् । शतऽआत्मा ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ púram ǀ nā́rmiṇīm ǀ ádīdet ǀ átyaḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ nabhanyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ árvā ǀsū́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ rurukvā́n ǀ śatá-ātmā ǁ

Sukta 149.translation: “He who is wise, and goes (wheresoever he will), like the rapid ethereal (wind), has lighted up the delightful spot, (the altar), and, identical with many forms, is radiant as the sun.”
Sukta 149.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ यः पुरं॒ नार्मि॑णी॒मदी॑दे॒दत्य॑: क॒विर्न॑भ॒न्यो॒३॒॑ नार्वा॑ । सूरो॒ न रु॑रु॒क्वाञ्छ॒तात्मा॑

devanagari.text: अभि द्विजन्मा त्री रोचनानि विश्वा रजांसि शुशुचानो अस्थात् ।होता यजिष्ठो अपां सधस्थे ॥

Sukta 149.translation: “He the twice-born, illuminating the three bright (regions), and shining over all the lustrous spheres, the adorable invoker of the gods, is present at the plural ce where the waters are collected.”

Sukta 149.translation: “He is the offerer of oblations, who is of twofold birth; and, through desire of (sacrificial) food, has in his keeping all good things; the man who presents offerings to him is the parent of excellent offspring.”

Sukta 150.translation: “(I ask you also to withhold your favour) from (those) two godless (person ns), from the rich man, who acknowledging you not as his lord, is chary of gifts at sacred rites, and from him who rarely praises (the gods).”

Sukta 150.translation: “SageAgni, the mortal (who propitiates you) becomes a moon in heaven, the most eminent of the great (deities); may we, therefore, ever be in an especial manner your worshippers.”
Sukta 150.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स च॒न्द्रो वि॑प्र॒ मर्त्यो॑ म॒हो व्राध॑न्तमो दि॒वि । प्रप्रेत्ते॑ अग्ने व॒नुष॑: स्याम

Sukta 151.translation: “Heaven and earth have been terrified by the strength and the noise (of him), whom pious worshippers, desirous of acquiring cattle, have genitive rated by their (sacred) acts, amidst the waters (of the firmament), at the sacrifice, as a friend for the preservation of living beings, the benefactor (of man), and entitled to adoration.”

Sukta 151.translation: “Since they, (the priests), like friends, have prepared for you both, (MitraandVaruṇaa libation) of the abundantly-flowing and spontaneousSoma, therefore do you consent to come to the rite of the worshipper, and listen, showerers (of blessings), to the (prayers of the) householdeṛ ”

Sukta 151.translation: “For the sake (of obtaining) great vigour, showerers (of benefits), men glorify your birth from heaven and earth, which is to be extolled, inasmuch as you bestow (his desires) upon the worshipper (as the reward) of his sacrifice, and accept the rite (that is solemnized) with praise and oblation.”

Sukta 151.translation: “Powerful divinities, most acceptable to you both is that spot, (where you are worshipped); accepters of sacrifice, proclaim the great ceremony (as duly performed); for you two connect the efficacious and comprehensive rise with the vast heaven, like a cow with a burden.”

Sukta 151.translation: “You bring (the cattle) to their acceptable (pasture) upon earth, whence the milk-yielding cows, protected by your power, return unharmed to their stalls; they cry to the sun (in heaven) above, both at evening and at dawn, as one (cries aloud) who detects a thief.”

Sukta 151.translation: “The tresses ofAgniminister,MitraandVaruṇa, to your sacrifice, when you honour (with your presence) the sacrificial chamber; send down of your own accord (the rain), and prosper our offerings, for you have command over the praise of the pious men.”

Sukta 151.translation: “Come to the devout (worshipper), who, glorifying you, and providing (all that is) acceptable, presents you with oblations; (to him), the sage, the invoker, who offers you worship; accept his sacrifice; favourably disposed towards us, (accept) our praises.”

devanagari.text: युवां यज्ञैः प्रथमा गोभिरंजत ऋतावाना मनसो न प्रयुक्तिषु ।भरंति वां मन्मना संयता गिरोऽदृप्यता मनसा रेवदाशाथे ॥

transliteration.text: yuvā́m ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ añjate ǀ ṛ́ta-vānā ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ prá-yuktiṣu ǀbháranti ǀ vām ǀ mánmanā ǀ sam-yátā ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ádṛpyatā ǀ mánasā ǀ revát ǀ āśāthe íti ǁ

Sukta 151.translation: “Accepter of sacrifices, you are the first whom (worshippers) propitiate with offerings, the produce of the cow; like (the application) of the mind (in the first instrumental nce) to the results (of the senses); hymns (prompted) by thoughts wholly intent upon you, celebrate (your praise); do you, with humble minds, bestow upon us wealth.”
Sukta 151.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वां य॒ज्ञैः प्र॑थ॒मा गोभि॑रञ्जत॒ ऋता॑वाना॒ मन॑सो॒ न प्रयु॑क्तिषु । भर॑न्ति वां॒ मन्म॑ना सं॒यता॒ गिरोऽदृ॑प्यता॒ मन॑सा रे॒वदा॑शाथे

devanagari.text: रेवद्वयो दधाथे रेवदाशाथे नरा मायाभिरितऊति माहिनं ।न वां द्यावोऽहभिर्नोत सिंधवो न देवत्वं पणयो नानशुर्मघं ॥
रेवत् । वयः । दधाथे इति । रेवत् । आशाथे इति । नरा । मायाभिः । इतऽऊति । माहिनम् ।न । वाम् । द्यावः । अहऽभिः । न । उत । सिन्धवः । न । देवऽत्वम् । पणयः । न । आनशुः । मघम् ॥

transliteration.text: revát ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhāthe íti ǀ revát ǀ āśāthe íti ǀ nárā ǀ māyā́bhiḥ ǀ itá-ūti ǀ mā́hinam ǀná ǀ vām ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ áha-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ utá ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ deva-tvám ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ānaśuḥ ǀ maghám ǁ

Sukta 151.translation: “You distribute food, accompanied by riches; you bestow upon us, leaders (of sacrifice), wealth, ample, and defended by your wise provisions; the days with the nights have not attained your divinity; neither have the rivers, nor have theasuras, and they have not obtained (your) wealth.”
Sukta 151.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रे॒वद्वयो॑ दधाथे रे॒वदा॑शाथे॒ नरा॑ मा॒याभि॑रि॒तऊ॑ति॒ माहि॑नम् । न वां॒ द्यावोऽह॑भि॒र्नोत सिन्ध॑वो॒ न दे॑व॒त्वं प॒णयो॒ नान॑शुर्म॒घम्

devanagari.text: युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे युवोरच्छिद्रा मंतवो ह सर्गाः ।अवातिरतमनृतानि विश्व ऋतेन मित्रावरुणा सचेथे ॥
युवम् । वस्त्राणि । पीवसा । वसाथे इति । युवोः । अच्छिद्राः । मन्तवः । ह । सर्गाः ।अव । अतिरतम् । अनृतानि । विश्वा । ऋतेन । मित्रावरुणा । सचेथे इति ॥

transliteration.text: yuvám ǀ vástrāṇi ǀ pīvasā́ ǀ vasāthe íti ǀ yuvóḥ ǀ ácchidrāḥ ǀ mántavaḥ ǀ ha ǀ sárgāḥ ǀáva ǀ atiratam ǀ ánṛtāni ǀ víśvā ǀ ṛténa ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ sacethe íti ǁ

Sukta 152.translation: “RobustMitraandVaruṇa, you wear vestments (of light); your natures are to be regarded as without defect; you annihilate all untruths; you associate (us) with sacrifice.”
Sukta 152.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वं वस्त्रा॑णि पीव॒सा व॑साथे यु॒वोरच्छि॑द्रा॒ मन्त॑वो ह॒ सर्गा॑: । अवा॑तिरत॒मनृ॑तानि॒ विश्व॑ ऋ॒तेन॑ मित्रावरुणा सचेथे

devanagari.text: एतच्चन त्वो वि चिकेतदेषां सत्यो मंत्रः कविशस्त ऋघावान् ।त्रिरश्रिं हंति चतुरश्रिरुग्रो देवनिदो ह प्रथमा अजूर्यन् ॥
एतत् । चन । त्वः । वि । चिकेतत् । एषाम् । सत्यः । मन्त्रः । कविऽशस्तः । ऋघावान् ।त्रिःऽअश्रिम् । हन्ति । चतुःऽअश्रिः । उग्रः । देवऽनिदः । ह । प्रथमाः । अजूर्यन् ॥

transliteration.text: etát ǀ caná ǀ tvaḥ ǀ ví ǀ ciketat ǀ eṣām ǀ satyáḥ ǀ mántraḥ ǀ kavi-śastáḥ ǀ ṛ́ghāvān ǀtriḥ-áśrim ǀ hanti ǀ cátuḥ-aśriḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ deva-nídaḥ ǀ ha ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ ajūryan ǁ

Sukta 152.translation: “He amongst those (who are your followers), who observes truth, who is considerate, who is commended by the wise, who is able to (inflict) harm, carefully weighs (the means whereby), fierce and well-armed, he slays (a foe) less efficiently accoutred, and (by which) the revilers of the gods, however mighty, may perish.”
Sukta 152.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒तच्च॒न त्वो॒ वि चि॑केतदेषां स॒त्यो मन्त्र॑: कविश॒स्त ऋघा॑वान् । त्रि॒रश्रिं॑ हन्ति॒ चतु॑रश्रिरु॒ग्रो दे॑व॒निदो॒ ह प्र॑थ॒मा अ॑जूर्यन्

devanagari.text: अपादेति प्रथमा पद्वतीनां कस्तद्वां मित्रावरुणा चिकेत ।गर्भो भारं भरत्या चिदस्य ऋतं पिपर्त्यनृतं नि तारीत् ॥
अपात् । एति । प्रथमा । पत्ऽवतीनाम् । कः । तत् । वाम् । मित्रावरुणा । आ । चिकेत ।गर्भः । भारम् । भरति । आ । चित् । अस्य । ऋतम् । पिपर्ति । अनृतम् । नि । तारीत् ॥

transliteration.text: apā́t ǀ eti ǀ prathamā́ ǀ pat-vátīnām ǀ káḥ ǀ tát ǀ vām ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ ā́ ǀ ciketa ǀgárbhaḥ ǀ bhārám ǀ bharati ǀ ā́ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ ṛtám ǀ píparti ǀ ánṛtam ǀ ní ǀ tārīt ǁ

Sukta 152.translation: “Who knows,MitraandVaruṇa, that it is your doing, that the footless dawn is the precursor of footed beings; and that your infant (progeny, the sun), sustains the burden of this (world); he diffuses (the) truth (of light), and disperses the falsehood (of darkness).”
Sukta 152.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒पादे॑ति प्रथ॒मा प॒द्वती॑नां॒ कस्तद्वां॑ मित्रावरु॒णा चि॑केत । गर्भो॑ भा॒रं भ॑र॒त्या चि॑दस्य ऋ॒तं पिप॒र्त्यनृ॑तं॒ नि ता॑रीत्

devanagari.text: प्रयंतमित्परि जारं कनीनां पश्यामसि नोपनिपद्यमानं ।अनवपृग्णा वितता वसानं प्रियं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम ॥

transliteration.text: pra-yántam ǀ ít ǀ pári ǀ jārám ǀ kanī́nām ǀ páśyāmasi ǀ ná ǀ upa-nipádyamānam ǀánava-pṛgṇā ǀ ví-tatā ǀ vásānam ǀ priyám ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhā́ma ǁ

Sukta 152.translation: “We behold the lover of the maiden (dawns), ever in movement, never resting for an instrumental nt, wearing inseparable and diffusive (radiance), the beloved abode ofMitraandVaruṇa”
Sukta 152.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र॒यन्त॒मित्परि॑ जा॒रं क॒नीनां॒ पश्या॑मसि॒ नोप॑नि॒पद्य॑मानम् । अन॑वपृग्णा॒ वित॑ता॒ वसा॑नं प्रि॒यं मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ धाम॑

devanagari.text: अनश्वो जातो अनभीशुरर्वा कनिक्रदत्पतयदूर्ध्वसानुः ।अचित्तं ब्रह्म जुजुषुर्युवानः प्र मित्रे धाम वरुणे गृणंतः ॥

transliteration.text: anaśváḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ anabhīśúḥ ǀ árvā ǀ kánikradat ǀ patayat ǀ ūrdhvá-sānuḥ ǀacíttam ǀ bráhma ǀ jujuṣuḥ ǀ yúvānaḥ ǀ prá ǀ mitré ǀ dhā́ma ǀ váruṇe ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǁ

Sukta 152.translation: “Without steeds, without stay, (he is nevertheless) borne swift-moving and loud-sounding; he travels, ascending higher and higher, connecting the inconceivable mystery (of sacred rites) with the radiance (abiding) inMitraandVaruṇa, (which men), eulogizing, glorify.”
Sukta 152.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒न॒श्वो जा॒तो अ॑नभी॒शुरर्वा॒ कनि॑क्रदत्पतयदू॒र्ध्वसा॑नुः । अ॒चित्तं॒ ब्रह्म॑ जुजुषु॒र्युवा॑न॒: प्र मि॒त्रे धाम॒ वरु॑णे गृ॒णन्त॑:

devanagari.text: आ धेनवो मामतेयमवंतीर्ब्रह्मप्रियं पीपयन्त्सस्मिन्नूधन् ।पित्वो भिक्षेत वयुनानि विद्वानासाविवासन्नदितिमुरुष्येत् ॥
आ । धेनवः । मामतेयम् । अवन्तीः । ब्रह्मऽप्रियम् । पीपयन् । सस्मिन् । ऊधन् ।पित्वः । भिक्षेत । वयुनानि । विद्वान् । आसा । आऽविवासन् । अदितिम् । उरुष्येत् ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ māmateyám ǀ ávantīḥ ǀ brahma-príyam ǀ pīpayan ǀ sásmin ǀ ū́dhan ǀpitváḥ ǀ bhikṣeta ǀ vayúnāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ āsā́ ǀ ā-vívāsan ǀ áditim ǀ uruṣyet ǁ

Sukta 152.translation: “May the cow, propitious to the devout son ofMamatā, be possessed of well-filled udders; knowing the rites (necessary to be performed), let him beg (the residue) of the offerings for his eating, and worshipping (you both) complete the perfect (ceremony).”
Sukta 152.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ धे॒नवो॑ मामते॒यमव॑न्तीर्ब्रह्म॒प्रियं॑ पीपय॒न्त्सस्मि॒न्नूध॑न् । पि॒त्वो भि॑क्षेत व॒युना॑नि वि॒द्वाना॒साविवा॑स॒न्नदि॑तिमुरुष्येत्

devanagari.text: आ वां मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं नमसा देवाववसा ववृत्यां ।अस्माकं ब्रह्म पृतनासु सह्या अस्माकं वृष्टिर्दिव्या सुपारा ॥
आ । वाम् । मित्रावरुणा । हव्यऽजुष्टिम् । नमसा । देवौ । अवसा । ववृत्याम् ।अस्माकम् । ब्रह्म । पृतनासु । सह्याः । अस्माकम् । वृष्टिः । दिव्या । सुऽपारा ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ havyá-juṣṭim ǀ námasā ǀ devau ǀ ávasā ǀ vavṛtyām ǀasmā́kam ǀ bráhma ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ sahyāḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ vṛṣṭíḥ ǀ divyā́ ǀ su-pārā́ ǁ

Sukta 152.translation: “DivineMitraandVaruṇa, may I render the oblation acceptable to you with reverence and prayer; may the sacred rite enable us (to overcome) in battles, and may the heavenly rain be to us the means of satisfying our wants.”
Sukta 152.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ वां॑ मित्रावरुणा ह॒व्यजु॑ष्टिं॒ नम॑सा देवा॒वव॑सा ववृत्याम् । अ॒स्माकं॒ ब्रह्म॒ पृत॑नासु सह्या अ॒स्माकं॑ वृ॒ष्टिर्दि॒व्या सु॑पा॒रा

devanagari.text: यजामहे वां महः सजोषा हव्येभिर्मित्रावरुणा नमोभिः ।घृतैर्घृतस्नू अध यद्वामस्मे अध्वर्यवो न धीतिभिर्भरंति ॥
यजामहे । वाम् । महः । सऽजोषाः । हव्येभिः । मित्रावरुणा । नमःऽभिः ।घृतैः । घृतस्नू इति घृतऽस्नू । अध । यत् । वाम् । अस्मे इति । अध्वर्यवः । न । धीतिऽभिः । भरन्ति ॥

transliteration.text: yájāmahe ǀ vām ǀ maháḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ havyébhiḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀghṛtáiḥ ǀ ghṛtasnū íti ghṛta-snū ǀ ádha ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ asmé íti ǀ adhvaryávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀ bháranti ǁ

Sukta 153.translation: “MightyMitraandVaruṇa, dispensers of butter, we worship you, rejoicing, with oblations; with reverential homage, and with (offerings of) water; so that our ministrant priests may propitiate you by (our) devotions.”
Sukta 153.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यजा॑महे वां म॒हः स॒जोषा॑ ह॒व्येभि॑र्मित्रावरुणा॒ नमो॑भिः । घृ॒तैर्घृ॑तस्नू॒ अध॒ यद्वा॑म॒स्मे अ॑ध्व॒र्यवो॒ न धी॒तिभि॒र्भर॑न्ति

devanagari.text: प्रस्तुतिर्वां धाम न प्रयुक्तिरयामि मित्रावरुणा सुवृक्तिः ।अनक्ति यद्वां विदथेषु होता सुम्नं वां सूरिर्वृषणावियक्षन् ॥
प्रऽस्तुतिः । वाम् । धाम । न । प्रऽयुक्तिः । अयामि । मित्रावरुणा । सुऽवृक्तिः ।अनक्ति । यत् । वाम् । विदथेषु । होता । सुम्नम् । वाम् । सूरिः । वृषणौ । इयक्षन् ॥

transliteration.text: prá-stutiḥ ǀ vām ǀ dhā́ma ǀ ná ǀ prá-yuktiḥ ǀ áyāmi ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ su-vṛktíḥ ǀanákti ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ hótā ǀ sumnám ǀ vām ǀ sūríḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ íyakṣan ǁ

Sukta 153.translation: “The purpose of worshipping you,MitraandVaruṇa, is not the performance, but (even by so much) I may attain to your glory, and there is acquittance (of my duty); for when the priest offers you oblations in sacrifices, then the pious man, showerers (of benefits), being desirous of worshipping you, (obtains) felicity.”
Sukta 153.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रस्तु॑तिर्वां॒ धाम॒ न प्रयु॑क्ति॒रया॑मि मित्रावरुणा सुवृ॒क्तिः । अ॒नक्ति॒ यद्वां॑ वि॒दथे॑षु॒ होता॑ सु॒म्नं वां॑ सू॒रिर्वृ॑षणा॒विय॑क्षन्

devanagari.text: पीपाय धेनुरदितिर्ऋताय जनाय मित्रावरुणा हविर्दे ।हिनोति यद्वां विदथे सपर्यन्त्स रातहव्यो मानुषो न होता ॥
पीपाय । धेनुः । अदितिः । ऋताय । जनाय । मित्रावरुणा । हविःऽदे ।हिनोति । यत् । वाम् । विदथे । सपर्यन् । सः । रातऽहव्यः । मानुषः । न । होता ॥

transliteration.text: pīpā́ya ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ jánāya ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ haviḥ-dé ǀhinóti ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ vidáthe ǀ saparyán ǀ sáḥ ǀ rātá-havyaḥ ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǁ

Sukta 153.translation: “Let the productive cow,MitraandVaruṇa, furnish abundant nutriment to the pious man who presents you with oblations, as when Rātahavya, glorifying you, propitiates you in the solemnity, like the ministrant priest of a man (who instrumental tutes the rite).”
Sukta 153.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पी॒पाय॑ धे॒नुरदि॑तिॠ॒ताय॒ जना॑य मित्रावरुणा हवि॒र्दे । हि॒नोति॒ यद्वां॑ वि॒दथे॑ सप॒र्यन्त्स रा॒तह॑व्यो॒ मानु॑षो॒ न होता॑

devanagari.text: उत वां विक्षु मद्यास्वंधो गाव आपश्च पीपयंत देवीः ।उतो नो अस्य पूर्व्यः पतिर्दन्वीतं पातं पयस उस्रियायाः ॥
उत । वाम् । विक्षु । मद्यासु । अन्धः । गावः । आपः । च । पीपयन्त । देवीः ।उतो इति । नः । अस्य । पूर्व्यः । पतिः । दन् । वीतम् । पातम् । पयसः । उस्रियायाः ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ vām ǀ vikṣú ǀ mádyāsu ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ca ǀ pīpayanta ǀ devī́ḥ ǀutó íti ǀ naḥ ǀ asyá ǀ pūrvyáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǀ vītám ǀ pātám ǀ páyasaḥ ǀ usríyāyāḥ ǁ

Sukta 153.translation: “May the divine cows, and the waters, supply you with (sacrificial) food, for the prosperity of the people whom you favour; or may (Agni), the former protector of this (our patron), be the donor (of the oblation); eat (of the butter and curds), drink of the milk of the kine.”
Sukta 153.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त वां॑ वि॒क्षु मद्या॒स्वन्धो॒ गाव॒ आप॑श्च पीपयन्त दे॒वीः । उ॒तो नो॑ अ॒स्य पू॒र्व्यः पति॒र्दन्वी॒तं पा॒तं पय॑स उ॒स्रिया॑याः

devanagari.text: विष्णोर्नु कं वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यः पार्थिवानि विममे रजांसि ।यो अस्कभायदुत्तरं सधस्थं विचक्रमाणस्त्रेधोरुगायः ॥
विष्णोः । नु । कम् । वीर्याणि । प्र । वोचम् । यः । पार्थिवानि । विऽममे । रजांसि ।यः । अस्कभायत् । उत्ऽतरम् । सधऽस्थम् । विऽचक्रमाणः । त्रेधा । उरुऽगायः ॥

transliteration.text: víṣṇoḥ ǀ nú ǀ kam ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǀ prá ǀ vocam ǀ yáḥ ǀ pā́rthivāni ǀ vi-mamé ǀ rájāṃsi ǀyáḥ ǀ áskabhāyat ǀ út-taram ǀ sadhá-stham ǀ vi-cakramāṇáḥ ǀ tredhā́ ǀ uru-gāyáḥ ǁ

Sukta 154.translation: “Earnetly I glorify the exploits ofViṣṇu, who made thethree worlds; who sustained the lofty aggregate site (of the spheres); thrice traversing (the whole); who is praised by the exalted.”
Sukta 154.sanskrit_wisdomlib: विष्णो॒र्नु कं॑ वी॒र्या॑णि॒ प्र वो॑चं॒ यः पार्थि॑वानि विम॒मे रजां॑सि । यो अस्क॑भाय॒दुत्त॑रं स॒धस्थं॑ विचक्रमा॒णस्त्रे॒धोरु॑गा॒यः

devanagari.text: प्र तद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येण मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः ।यस्योरुषु त्रिषु विक्रमणेष्वधिक्षियंति भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
प्र । तत् । विष्णुः । स्तवते । वीर्येण । मृगः । न । भीमः । कुचरः । गिरिऽस्थाः ।यस्य । उरुषु । त्रिषु । विऽक्रमणेषु । अधिऽक्षियन्ति । भुवनानि । विश्वा ॥

transliteration.text: prá ǀ tát ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ stavate ǀ vīryéṇa ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ kucaráḥ ǀ giri-sthā́ḥ ǀyásya ǀ urúṣu ǀ triṣú ǀ vi-krámaṇeṣu ǀ adhi-kṣiyánti ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ

Sukta 154.translation: “Viṣṇuis therefore glorified, that by his prowess he is like a fearful, ravenous, and mountain-haunting wild beast, and because of that in his three paces all worlds abide.”
Sukta 154.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र तद्विष्णु॑: स्तवते वी॒र्ये॑ण मृ॒गो न भी॒मः कु॑च॒रो गि॑रि॒ष्ठाः । यस्यो॒रुषु॑ त्रि॒षु वि॒क्रम॑णेष्वधिक्षि॒यन्ति॒ भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑

devanagari.text: प्र विष्णवे शूषमेतु मन्म गिरिक्षित उरुगायाय वृष्णे ।य इदं दीर्घं प्रयतं सधस्थमेको विममे त्रिभिरित्पदेभिः ॥
प्र । विष्णवे । शूषम् । एतु । मन्म । गिरिऽक्षिते । उरुऽगायाय । वृष्णे ।यः । इदम् । दीर्घम् । प्रऽयतम् । सधऽस्थम् । एकः । विऽममे । त्रिऽभिः । इत् । पदेभिः ॥

transliteration.text: prá ǀ víṣṇave ǀ śūṣám ǀ etu ǀ mánma ǀ giri-kṣíte ǀ uru-gāyā́ya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀyáḥ ǀ idám ǀ dīrghám ǀ prá-yatam ǀ sadhá-stham ǀ ékaḥ ǀ vi-mamé ǀ tri-bhíḥ ǀ ít ǀ padébhiḥ ǁ

Sukta 154.translation: “May acceptable vigour attendViṣṇu, who abides in prayer, the hymned of many, the showerer (of benefits), who alone made, by three steps, this spacious and durable aggregate (of thethree worlds).”
Sukta 154.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र विष्ण॑वे शू॒षमे॑तु॒ मन्म॑ गिरि॒क्षित॑ उरुगा॒याय॒ वृष्णे॑ । य इ॒दं दी॒र्घं प्रय॑तं स॒धस्थ॒मेको॑ विम॒मे त्रि॒भिरित्प॒देभि॑:

devanagari.text: यस्य त्री पूर्णा मधुना पदान्यक्षीयमाणा स्वधया मदंति ।य उ त्रिधातु पृथिवीमुत द्यामेको दाधार भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
यस्य । त्री । पूर्णा । मधुना । पदानि । अक्षीयमाणा । स्वधया । मदन्ति ।यः । ऊं इति । त्रिऽधातु । पृथिवीम् । उत । द्याम् । एकः । दाधार । भुवनानि । विश्वा ॥

transliteration.text: yásya ǀ trī́ ǀ pūrṇā́ ǀ mádhunā ǀ padā́ni ǀ ákṣīyamāṇā ǀ svadháyā ǀ mádanti ǀyáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ utá ǀ dyā́m ǀ ékaḥ ǀ dādhā́ra ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ

Sukta 154.translation: “Whose three imperishable paces, filled with ambrosia, delight (mankind) with sacred food; who verily alone upholds the three elements, and earth and heaven.”
Sukta 154.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्य॒ त्री पू॒र्णा मधु॑ना प॒दान्यक्षी॑यमाणा स्व॒धया॒ मद॑न्ति । य उ॑ त्रि॒धातु॑ पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्यामेको॑ दा॒धार॒ भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑

devanagari.text: तदस्य प्रियमभि पाथो अश्यां नरो यत्र देवयवो मदंति ।उरुक्रमस्य स हि बंधुरित्था विष्णोः पदे परमे मध्व उत्सः ॥
तत् । अस्य । प्रियम् । अभि । पाथः । अश्याम् । नरः । यत्र । देवऽयवः । मदन्ति ।उरुऽक्रमस्य । सः । हि । बन्धुः । इत्था । विष्णोः । पदे । परमे । मध्वः । उत्सः ॥

transliteration.text: tát ǀ asya ǀ priyám ǀ abhí ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ aśyām ǀ náraḥ ǀ yátra ǀ deva-yávaḥ ǀ mádanti ǀuru-kramásya ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ bándhuḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ padé ǀ paramé ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ útsaḥ ǁ

Sukta 154.translation: “May I attain his favourite path, in which god-seeking men delight; (the path) of that wide-steppingViṣṇu, in whose exalted station there is a (perpetual) flow of felicity; for to such a degree is he the friend (of the pious).”
Sukta 154.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तद॑स्य प्रि॒यम॒भि पाथो॑ अश्यां॒ नरो॒ यत्र॑ देव॒यवो॒ मद॑न्ति । उ॒रु॒क्र॒मस्य॒ स हि बन्धु॑रि॒त्था विष्णो॑: प॒दे प॑र॒मे मध्व॒ उत्स॑:

devanagari.text: ता वां वास्तून्युश्मसि गमध्यै यत्र गावो भूरिशृंगा अयासः ।अत्राह तदुरुगायस्य वृष्णः परमं पदमव भाति भूरि ॥
ता । वाम् । वास्तूनि । उश्मसि । गमध्यै । यत्र । गावः । भूरिऽशृङ्गाः । अयासः ।अत्र । अह । तत् । उरुऽगायस्य । वृष्णः । परमम् । पदम् । अव । भाति । भूरि ॥

transliteration.text: tā́ ǀ vām ǀ vā́stūni ǀ uśmasi ǀ gámadhyai ǀ yátra ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ bhū́ri-śṛṅgāḥ ǀ ayā́saḥ ǀátra ǀ áha ǀ tát ǀ uru-gāyásya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ paramám ǀ padám ǀ áva ǀ bhāti ǀ bhū́ri ǁ

Sukta 154.translation: “We pary (toViṣṇu) that you may both go to those regions where the many-pointed and wide-spreading rays (of light expand); for here the supreme station of the many-hymned, the showerer (of benefits), shines (with) great (splendour).”
Sukta 154.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ता वां॒ वास्तू॑न्युश्मसि॒ गम॑ध्यै॒ यत्र॒ गावो॒ भूरि॑शृङ्गा अ॒यास॑: । अत्राह॒ तदु॑रुगा॒यस्य॒ वृष्ण॑: पर॒मं प॒दमव॑ भाति॒ भूरि॑

devanagari.text: प्र वः पांतमंधसो धियायते महे शूराय विष्णवे चार्चत ।या सानुनि पर्वतानामदाभ्या महस्तस्थतुरर्वतेव साधुना ॥
प्र । वः । पान्तम् । अन्धसः । धियाऽयते । महे । शूराय । विष्णवे । च । अर्चत ।या । सानुनि । पर्वतानाम् । अदाभ्या । महः । तस्थतुः । अर्वताऽइव । साधुना ॥

transliteration.text: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ pā́ntam ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ dhiyā-yaté ǀ mahé ǀ śū́rāya ǀ víṣṇave ǀ ca ǀ arcata ǀyā́ ǀ sā́nuni ǀ párvatānām ǀ ádābhyā ǀ maháḥ ǀ tasthátuḥ ǀ árvatā-iva ǀ sādhúnā ǁ

Sukta 155.translation: “Offer your nutritious viands to the great hero, (Indra), who is plural ased by praise, and toViṣṇu, the two invincible deities who ride upon the radiant summit of the clouds as upon a well-trained steed.”
Sukta 155.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र व॒: पान्त॒मन्ध॑सो धियाय॒ते म॒हे शूरा॑य॒ विष्ण॑वे चार्चत । या सानु॑नि॒ पर्व॑ताना॒मदा॑भ्या म॒हस्त॒स्थतु॒रर्व॑तेव सा॒धुना॑

devanagari.text: त्वेषमित्था समरणं शिमीवतोरिंद्राविष्णू सुतपा वामुरुष्यति ।या मर्त्याय प्रतिधीयमानमित्कृशानोरस्तुरसनामुरुष्यथः ॥
त्वेषम् । इत्था । सम्ऽअरणम् । शिमीऽवतोः । इन्द्राविष्णू इति । सुतऽपाः । वाम् । उरुष्यति ।या । मर्त्याय । प्रतिऽधीयमानम् । इत् । कृशानोः । अस्तुः । असनाम् । उरुष्यथः ॥

transliteration.text: tveṣám ǀ itthā́ ǀ sam-áraṇam ǀ śímī-vatoḥ ǀ índrāviṣṇū íti ǀ suta-pā́ḥ ǀ vām ǀ uruṣyati ǀyā́ ǀ mártyāya ǀ prati-dhīyámānam ǀ ít ǀ kṛśā́noḥ ǀ ástuḥ ǀ asanā́m ǀ uruṣyáthaḥ ǁ

Sukta 155.translation: “IndraandViṣṇu, the devout worshipper glorifies the radiant approach of you two, who are the granters of desires, and who bestow upon the mortal who worships you an immediately-receivable (reward), through the distribution of that fire which is the scatterer (of desired blessings).”
Sukta 155.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वे॒षमि॒त्था स॒मर॑णं॒ शिमी॑वतो॒रिन्द्रा॑विष्णू सुत॒पा वा॑मुरुष्यति । या मर्त्या॑य प्रतिधी॒यमा॑न॒मित्कृ॒शानो॒रस्तु॑रस॒नामु॑रु॒ष्यथ॑:

devanagari.text: ता ईं वर्धंति मह्यस्य पौंस्यं नि मातरा नयति रेतसे भुजे ।दधाति पुत्रोऽवरं परं पितुर्नाम तृतीयमधि रोचने दिवः ॥
ताः । ईम् । वर्धन्ति । महि । अस्य । पौंस्यम् । नि । मातरा । नयति । रेतसे । भुजे ।दधाति । पुत्रः । अवरम् । परम् । पितुः । नाम । तृतीयम् । अधि । रोचने । दिवः ॥

transliteration.text: tā́ḥ ǀ īm ǀ vardhanti ǀ máhi ǀ asya ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ ní ǀ mātárā ǀ nayati ǀ rétase ǀ bhujé ǀdádhāti ǀ putráḥ ǀ ávaram ǀ páram ǀ pitúḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ tṛtī́yam ǀ ádhi ǀ rocané ǀ diváḥ ǁ

Sukta 155.translation: “These (oblations) augment his (Indra's), mighty manhood, by which he fits the parents (of all creatures heaven and earth), for genitive ration and enjoyment; whereby, in the upper region of the sky, the son has an inferior and superior appellation, and a third (name) of father.”
Sukta 155.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ता ईं॑ वर्धन्ति॒ मह्य॑स्य॒ पौंस्यं॒ नि मा॒तरा॑ नयति॒ रेत॑से भु॒जे । दधा॑ति पु॒त्रोऽव॑रं॒ परं॑ पि॒तुर्नाम॑ तृ॒तीय॒मधि॑ रोच॒ने दि॒वः

devanagari.text: तत्तदिदस्य पौंस्यं गृणीमसीनस्य त्रातुरवृकस्य मीळ्हुषः ।यः पार्थिवानि त्रिभिरिद्विगामभिरुरु क्रमिष्टोरुगायाय जीवसे ॥
तत्ऽतत् । इत् । अस्य । पौंस्यम् । गृणीमसि । इनस्य । त्रातुः । अवृकस्य । मीळ्हुषः ।यः । पार्थिवानि । त्रिऽभिः । इत् । विगामऽभिः । उरु । क्रमिष्ट । उरुऽगायाय । जीवसे ॥

transliteration.text: tát-tat ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀ inásya ǀ trātúḥ ǀ avṛkásya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ pā́rthivāni ǀ tri-bhíḥ ǀ ít ǀ vígāma-bhiḥ ǀ urú ǀ krámiṣṭa ǀ uru-gāyā́ya ǀ jīváse ǁ

Sukta 155.translation: “Therefore, verily, we celebrate the manhood of that lord (of all), the preserver, the innocuous, the vigorous who traversed the three regions with three wide steps in different directions for the many-praised (preservation of) existence.”
Sukta 155.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तत्त॒दिद॑स्य॒ पौंस्यं॑ गृणीमसी॒नस्य॑ त्रा॒तुर॑वृ॒कस्य॑ मी॒ळ्हुष॑: । यः पार्थि॑वानि त्रि॒भिरिद्विगा॑मभिरु॒रु क्रमि॑ष्टोरुगा॒याय॑ जी॒वसे॑

devanagari.text: द्वे इदस्य क्रमणे स्वर्दृशोऽभिख्याय मर्त्यो भुरण्यति ।तृतीयमस्य नकिरा दधर्षति वयश्चन पतयंतः पतत्रिणः ॥
द्वे इति । इत् । अस्य । क्रमणे इति । स्वःऽदृशः । अभिऽख्याय । मर्त्यः । भुरण्यति ।तृतीयम् । अस्य । नकिः । आ । दधर्षति । वयः । चन । पतयन्तः । पतत्रिणः ॥

transliteration.text: dvé íti ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ krámaṇe íti ǀ svaḥ-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ abhi-khyā́ya ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ bhuraṇyati ǀtṛtī́yam ǀ asya ǀ nákiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dadharṣati ǀ váyaḥ ǀ caná ǀ patáyantaḥ ǀ patatríṇaḥ ǁ

Sukta 155.translation: “Man glorifying (Viṣṇu), tracks two steps of that heaven-beholding (deity), but he apprehends not the third; nor can the soaring-winged birds (pursue it).”
Sukta 155.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्वे इद॑स्य॒ क्रम॑णे स्व॒र्दृशो॑ऽभि॒ख्याय॒ मर्त्यो॑ भुरण्यति । तृ॒तीय॑मस्य॒ नकि॒रा द॑धर्षति॒ वय॑श्च॒न प॒तय॑न्तः पत॒त्रिण॑:

devanagari.text: चतुर्भिः साकं नवतिं च नामभिश्चक्रं न वृत्तं व्यतीँरवीविपत् ।बृहच्छरीरो विमिमान ऋक्वभिर्युवाकुमारः प्रत्येत्याहवं ॥

transliteration.text: catúḥ-bhiḥ ǀ sākám ǀ navatím ǀ ca ǀ nā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ ná ǀ vṛttám ǀ vyátīn ǀ avīvipat ǀbṛhát-śarīraḥ ǀ vi-mímānaḥ ǀ ṛ́kva-bhiḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ ákumāraḥ ǀ práti ǀ eti ǀ ā-havám ǁ

Sukta 155.translation: “He causes, by his gyrations, ninety and four periodical revolutions, like a circular wheel, vast of body, and evolving in many forms, through the praises (addressed to him); ever young, though not infantine, he comes at our invocations.”
Sukta 155.sanskrit_wisdomlib: च॒तुर्भि॑: सा॒कं न॑व॒तिं च॒ नाम॑भिश्च॒क्रं न वृ॒त्तं व्यतीँ॑रवीविपत् । बृ॒हच्छ॑रीरो वि॒मिमा॑न॒ ऋक्व॑भि॒र्युवाकु॑मार॒: प्रत्ये॑त्याह॒वम्

devanagari.text: भवा मित्रो न शेव्यो घृतासुतिर्विभूतद्युम्न एवया उ सप्रथाः ।अधा ते विष्णो विदुषा चिदर्ध्यः स्तोमो यज्ञश्च राध्यो हविष्मता ॥

transliteration.text: bháva ǀ mitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ śévyaḥ ǀ ghṛtá-āsutiḥ ǀ víbhūta-dyumnaḥ ǀ eva-yā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sa-práthāḥ ǀádha ǀ te ǀ viṣṇo íti ǀ vidúṣā ǀ cit ǀ árdhyaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ca ǀ rā́dhyaḥ ǀ havíṣmatā ǁ

Sukta 156.translation: “Be (to us),Viṣṇu, like a friend, the giver of happiness, the acepter of oblations, abounding with food, the granter of protection, and every way accessible; on which account your praise is to be repeatedly recited by the wise, and your worship to be celebrated by the offerer of oblations.”
Sukta 156.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भवा॑ मि॒त्रो न शेव्यो॑ घृ॒तासु॑ति॒र्विभू॑तद्युम्न एव॒या उ॑ स॒प्रथा॑: । अधा॑ ते विष्णो वि॒दुषा॑ चि॒दर्ध्य॒: स्तोमो॑ य॒ज्ञश्च॒ राध्यो॑ ह॒विष्म॑ता

devanagari.text: यः पूर्व्याय वेधसे नवीयसे सुमज्जानये विष्णवे ददाशति ।यो जातमस्य महतो महि ब्रवत्सेदु श्रवोभिर्युज्यं चिदभ्यसत् ॥

transliteration.text: yáḥ ǀ pūrvyā́ya ǀ vedháse ǀ návīyase ǀ sumát-jānaye ǀ víṣṇave ǀ dádāśati ǀyáḥ ǀ jātám ǀ asya ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ máhi ǀ brávat ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śrávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ yújyam ǀ cit ǀ abhí ǀ asat ǁ

Sukta 156.translation: “He who presents (offerings) toViṣṇu, the ancient, the creator, the recent, the self-born; he who celebrates the great birth of that mighty one; he verily possessed of abundance, attains (the station) that is to be sought (by all).”
Sukta 156.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यः पू॒र्व्याय॑ वे॒धसे॒ नवी॑यसे सु॒मज्जा॑नये॒ विष्ण॑वे॒ ददा॑शति । यो जा॒तम॑स्य मह॒तो महि॒ ब्रव॒त्सेदु॒ श्रवो॑भि॒र्युज्यं॑ चिद॒भ्य॑सत्

devanagari.text: तमु स्तोतारः पूर्व्यं यथा विद ऋतस्य गर्भं जनुषा पिपर्तन ।आस्य जानंतो नाम चिद्विवक्तन महस्ते विष्णो सुमतिं भजामहे ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ stotāraḥ ǀ pūrvyám ǀ yáthā ǀ vidá ǀ ṛtásya ǀ gárbham ǀ janúṣā ǀ pipartana ǀā́ ǀ asya ǀ jānántaḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ cit ǀ vivaktana ǀ maháḥ ǀ te ǀ viṣṇo íti ǀ su-matím ǀ bhajāmahe ǁ

Sukta 156.translation: “Hymners, propitiate of your own accord that ancientViṣṇu, since you know him as the germ of sacrifice, cognizant of his greatness, celebrate his name; may we, Viṣṇu, enjoy your favour.”
Sukta 156.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तमु॑ स्तोतारः पू॒र्व्यं यथा॑ वि॒द ऋ॒तस्य॒ गर्भं॑ ज॒नुषा॑ पिपर्तन । आस्य॑ जा॒नन्तो॒ नाम॑ चिद्विवक्तन म॒हस्ते॑ विष्णो सुम॒तिं भ॑जामहे

devanagari.text: तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विना क्रतुं सचंत मारुतस्य वेधसः ।दाधार दक्षमुत्तममहर्विदं व्रजं च विष्णुः सखिवाँ अपोर्णुते ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ asya ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ tám ǀ aśvínā ǀ krátum ǀ sacanta ǀ mā́rutasya ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀdādhā́ra ǀ dákṣam ǀ ut-tamám ǀ ahaḥ-vídam ǀ vrajám ǀ ca ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ sákhi-vān ǀ apa-ūrṇuté ǁ

Sukta 156.translation: “The royalVaruṇaassociates (himself) with the sacrifice of the pious worshipper, assisted by the company of the priests; theAśvins(unite with it);Viṣṇu, with his friend (Indra), possesses supreme heaven-conferring power, and sits upon the clouds.”
Sukta 156.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तम॑स्य॒ राजा॒ वरु॑ण॒स्तम॒श्विना॒ क्रतुं॑ सचन्त॒ मारु॑तस्य वे॒धस॑: । दा॒धार॒ दक्ष॑मुत्त॒मम॑ह॒र्विदं॑ व्र॒जं च॒ विष्णु॒: सखि॑वाँ अपोर्णु॒ते

devanagari.text: आ यो विवाय सचथाय दैव्य इंद्राय विष्णुः सुकृते सुकृत्तरः ।वेधा अजिन्वत्त्रिषधस्थ आर्यमृतस्य भागे यजमानमाभजत् ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vivā́ya ǀ sacáthāya ǀ dáivyaḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ sukṛ́t-taraḥ ǀvedhā́ḥ ǀ ajinvat ǀ tri-sadhastháḥ ǀ ā́ryam ǀ ṛtásya ǀ bhāgé ǀ yájamānam ǀ ā́ ǀ abhajat ǁ

Sukta 156.translation: “The divineViṣṇu, the best of the doers of good deeds, who came to the pious instrumental tutor of the rite, to assist (at its celebration), knowing (the desire of the worshipper), and present at the three connected periods (of worship), shows favour to teArya, and admits the author if the ceremony to a share of the sacrifice.”
Sukta 156.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ यो वि॒वाय॑ स॒चथा॑य॒ दैव्य॒ इन्द्रा॑य॒ विष्णु॑: सु॒कृते॑ सु॒कृत्त॑रः । वे॒धा अ॑जिन्वत्त्रिषध॒स्थ आर्य॑मृ॒तस्य॑ भा॒गे यज॑मान॒माभ॑जत्

devanagari.text: अबोध्यग्निर्ज्म उदेति सूर्यो व्युषाश्चंद्रा मह्यावो अर्चिषा ।आयुक्षातामश्विना यातवे रथं प्रासावीद्देवः सविता जगत्पृथक् ॥

transliteration.text: ábodhi ǀ agníḥ ǀ jmáḥ ǀ út ǀ eti ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ví ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ candrā́ ǀ mahī́ ǀ āvaḥ ǀ arcíṣā ǀáyukṣātām ǀ aśvínā ǀ yā́tave ǀ rátham ǀ prá ǀ asāvīt ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ jágat ǀ pṛ́thak ǁ

Sukta 157.translation: “Agniis awakened upon earth; the Sun rises; the spreading dawn, exhilarating (all) by her radiance, has dispersed (the darkness); harness, (therefore),Aśvinsyour chariot, to come (to the sacrifice), that the divineSavitāmay animate allbeings to (the performance of) their several (duties).”
Sukta 157.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अबो॑ध्य॒ग्निर्ज्म उदे॑ति॒ सूर्यो॒ व्यु१॒॑षाश्च॒न्द्रा म॒ह्या॑वो अ॒र्चिषा॑ । आयु॑क्षाताम॒श्विना॒ यात॑वे॒ रथं॒ प्रासा॑वीद्दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता जग॒त्पृथ॑क्

transliteration.text: yát ǀ yuñjā́the íti ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ aśvinā ǀ rátham ǀ ghṛténa ǀ naḥ ǀ mádhunā ǀ kṣatrám ǀ ukṣatam ǀasmā́kam ǀ bráhma ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ jinvatam ǀ vayám ǀ dhánā ǀ śū́ra-sātā ǀ bhajemahi ǁ

Sukta 157.translation: “When,Aśvins, you harness your bounty-shedding chariot, refresh our strength with trickling honey; bestow (abundant) food upon our people; may we acquire riches in the strife of heroes.”
Sukta 157.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद्यु॒ञ्जाथे॒ वृष॑णमश्विना॒ रथं॑ घृ॒तेन॑ नो॒ मधु॑ना क्ष॒त्रमु॑क्षतम् । अ॒स्माकं॒ ब्रह्म॒ पृत॑नासु जिन्वतं व॒यं धना॒ शूर॑साता भजेमहि

devanagari.text: अर्वाङ् त्रिचक्रो मधुवाहनो रथो जीराश्वो अश्विनोर्यातु सुष्टुतः ।त्रिवंधुरो मघवा विश्वसौभगः शं न आ वक्षद्द्विपदे चतुष्पदे ॥

Sukta 157.translation: “May the three-wheeled car of theAśvins, drawn by swift horses, laden with honey, three-canopied, filled with treasure, and every way auspicious, come to our presence, and bring prosperity to our people and our cattle.”

Sukta 157.translation: “Bring us,Aśvins, vigour; animate us with your honied speech; prolong our existence; wipe away our sins; destroy our foes; be ever our associates.”

Sukta 157.translation: “You,Aśvins, sustain the germ in all moving creatures; you are in the interior of all beings; do you, showerers of benefits, supply (for our own use) fire and water and the trees of the forest.”

Sukta 157.translation: “You two are physicians, (conversant) with (all) medicaments; you ride in a chariot (drawn by) well-trained steeds; therefore, mighty (divinities), resolutely uphold (the worshipper), who, with a mind (devoted to you), offers you oblations.”

Sukta 158.translation: “Dasras, showerers (of benefits), granters of dwellings, dispellers of sin, cognizant of many (things), increasing (through praise), and fulfillers (of desires), inasmuch as Aucatthya offer you (sacrificial) wealth, and you protect (your worshippers) with unobjectionable aids, bestow uponus (our prayers).”

Sukta 158.translation: “Granters of dwellings, who may make you offerings so propitiatory of that your good will, that (invoked) by our adoration, to the site of the altar, you may entertain (favourable intentions towards us), and grant us kine rich in milk, coming with minds made up to grant the desires (of the worshipper).”

Sukta 158.translation: “In like manner,Aśvins, as your strong-drawn (car), able to cross (the sea), was plural ced,harnessed, in the middle of the water, for (the rescue of) the son ofTugra, so may I attain to your preserving protection (with the same alacrity) as a victorious hero (returns home) with bounding steeds.”

Sukta 158.translation: “May the praise addressed to you,Aśvins, preserve the son of Ucatthya; let not those revolving (days and nights) exhaust me; let not the ten times kindled fire consume me; let it not be, that one who is your, (dependant), bound (with bonds), should of himself bite the earth.”

Sukta 158.translation: “Let not the maternal waters swallow me, since the slaves hurled down this decrepit (old man); in like manner as Traitana wounded his head, so has the slave wounded his own, and has struck his breast and shoulders.”

Sukta 159.translation: “Verily I propitiate, by my invocations, the mind of the benevolent father, and the great and spontaneous (affection) of the mother (of all beings). The parents, with kindness, have secured, by their excellent protections, the vast and manifold immortality of their progeny.”
Sukta 159.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त म॑न्ये पि॒तुर॒द्रुहो॒ मनो॑ मा॒तुर्महि॒ स्वत॑व॒स्तद्धवी॑मभिः । सु॒रेत॑सा पि॒तरा॒ भूम॑ चक्रतुरु॒रु प्र॒जाया॑ अ॒मृतं॒ वरी॑मभिः

Sukta 159.translation: “These, your children, the performers of good works, and of goodly appearance, recognize you as their great parents, through experience of former (kindness); preserve uninterrupted stability in the functions of your progeny, whether stationary or moving, (depending for existence) on none other than you.”
Sukta 159.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते सू॒नव॒: स्वप॑सः सु॒दंस॑सो म॒ही ज॑ज्ञुर्मा॒तरा॑ पू॒र्वचि॑त्तये । स्था॒तुश्च॑ स॒त्यं जग॑तश्च॒ धर्म॑णि पु॒त्रस्य॑ पाथः प॒दमद्व॑याविनः

devanagari.text: ते मायिनो ममिरे सुप्रचेतसो जामी सयोनी मिथुना समोकसा ।नव्यंनव्यं तंतुमा तन्वते दिवि समुद्रे अंतः कवयः सुदीतयः ॥

Sukta 159.translation: “Those provident and intelligent sisters, (the rays of light), conceived of the same womb, (ever) united (with each other), and dwelling in the same abode, metre out (all things); knowing (their functions), and bright-shining, they spread in ever new (directions) throughout the radiant firmament.”
Sukta 159.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते मा॒यिनो॑ ममिरे सु॒प्रचे॑तसो जा॒मी सयो॑नी मिथु॒ना समो॑कसा । नव्यं॑नव्यं॒ तन्तु॒मा त॑न्वते दि॒वि स॑मु॒द्रे अ॒न्तः क॒वय॑: सुदी॒तय॑:

Sukta 159.translation: “We solicit today of the divine sun, his favour being propitiated, that wealth which is desirable. Benignant Heaven and Earth, bestow upon us riches, (consisting of) habitations and hundreds (of cattle and the like).”
Sukta 159.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तद्राधो॑ अ॒द्य स॑वि॒तुर्वरे॑ण्यं व॒यं दे॒वस्य॑ प्रस॒वे म॑नामहे । अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ द्यावापृथिवी सुचे॒तुना॑ र॒यिं ध॑त्तं॒ वसु॑मन्तं शत॒ग्विन॑म्

Sukta 160.translation: “Those two, the divine Heaven and Earth, are the diffusers of happiness on all, encouragers of truth, able to sustain the water (of the rains), auspicious of birth, and energetic (in action); in the interval between whom proceeds the pure and divine Sun for (the discharge of his) duties.”
Sukta 160.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते हि द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी वि॒श्वश॑म्भुव ऋ॒ताव॑री॒ रज॑सो धार॒यत्क॑वी । सु॒जन्म॑नी धि॒षणे॑ अ॒न्तरी॑यते दे॒वो दे॒वी धर्म॑णा॒ सूर्य॒: शुचि॑:

transliteration.text: uru-vyácasā ǀ mahínī íti ǀ asaścátā ǀ pitā́ ǀ mātā́ ǀ ca ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ rakṣataḥ ǀsudhṛ́ṣṭame íti su-dhṛ́ṣṭame ǀ vapuṣyé íti ǀ ná ǀ ródasī íti ǀ pitā́ ǀ yát ǀ sīm ǀ abhí ǀ rūpáiḥ ǀ ávāsayat ǁ

Sukta 160.translation: “Wide-spreading, vast, unconnected, the father and mother (of all beings), they two preservethe worlds. Resolute, as if (for the good) of embodied (beings), are Heaven and Earth, and the father ahs invested evry thing with (visible) forms.”
Sukta 160.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒रु॒व्यच॑सा म॒हिनी॑ अस॒श्चता॑ पि॒ता मा॒ता च॒ भुव॑नानि रक्षतः । सु॒धृष्ट॑मे वपु॒ष्ये॒३॒॑ न रोद॑सी पि॒ता यत्सी॑म॒भि रू॒पैरवा॑सयत्

Sukta 160.translation: “The pure and the resolute son of (these) parents, the bearer (of rewards), sanctifies the worlds by his intelligence;. as well as the cow (the earth), and the vigorous bull (the heaven), and daily milks the pellucid milk (of the sky).”
Sukta 160.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स वह्नि॑: पु॒त्रः पि॒त्रोः प॒वित्र॑वान्पु॒नाति॒ धीरो॒ भुव॑नानि मा॒यया॑ । धे॒नुं च॒ पृश्निं॑ वृष॒भं सु॒रेत॑सं वि॒श्वाहा॑ शु॒क्रं पयो॑ अस्य दुक्षत

transliteration.text: ayám ǀ devā́nām ǀ apásām ǀ apáḥ-tamaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ jajā́na ǀ ródasī íti ǀ viśvá-śambhuvā ǀví ǀ yáḥ ǀ mamé ǀ rájasī íti ǀ sukratu-yáyā ǀ ajárebhiḥ ǀ skámbhanebhiḥ ǀ sám ǀ ānṛce ǁ

Sukta 160.translation: “He it is, amongst gods (the most divine), amongst (pious) works the most pious, who gave birth to the all-delighting heaven and earth; who measured them both, and, for the sake of holy rites, propped them up with undecaying pillars.”
Sukta 160.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं दे॒वाना॑म॒पसा॑म॒पस्त॑मो॒ यो ज॒जान॒ रोद॑सी वि॒श्वश॑म्भुवा । वि यो म॒मे रज॑सी सुक्रतू॒यया॒जरे॑भि॒: स्कम्भ॑नेभि॒: समा॑नृचे

transliteration.text: té íti ǀ naḥ ǀ gṛṇāné íti ǀ mahinī íti ǀ máhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ kṣatrám ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ dhāsathaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀyéna ǀ abhí ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀ tatánāma ǀ viśváhā ǀ panā́yyam ǀ ójaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ sám ǀ invatam ǁ

Sukta 160.translation: “Glorified by us, grant to us, Heaven and Earth abundant food and great strength; whereby we may daily multiply mankind; bestow upon us commendable vigour.”
Sukta 160.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते नो॑ गृणा॒ने म॑हिनी॒ महि॒ श्रव॑: क्ष॒त्रं द्या॑वापृथिवी धासथो बृ॒हत् । येना॒भि कृ॒ष्टीस्त॒तना॑म वि॒श्वहा॑ प॒नाय्य॒मोजो॑ अ॒स्मे समि॑न्वतम्

transliteration.text: kím ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śréṣṭhaḥ ǀ kím ǀ yáviṣṭhaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ajagan ǀ kím ǀ īyate ǀ dūtyám ǀ kát ǀ yát ǀ ūcimá ǀná ǀ nindima ǀ camasám ǀ yáḥ ǀ mahā-kuláḥ ǀ agne ǀ bhrātaḥ ǀ drúṇaḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhūtím ǀ ūdima ǁ

Sukta 161.translation: “Is this our senior or our junior who has come (to us); has he come upon a message (from the gods); what is it we should say?Agni,brother, we revile not the ladle which is of exalted race; verily we assert the dignity of the wooden (implement).”
Sukta 161.sanskrit_wisdomlib: किमु॒ श्रेष्ठ॒: किं यवि॑ष्ठो न॒ आज॑ग॒न्किमी॑यते दू॒त्यं१॒॑ कद्यदू॑चि॒म । न नि॑न्दिम चम॒सं यो म॑हाकु॒लोऽग्ने॑ भ्रात॒र्द्रुण॒ इद्भू॒तिमू॑दिम

Sukta 161.translation: “Make fourfold the single ladle; so the gods command you; and for that purpose have I come, sons ofSudhanvan; if you accomplish this, you will be entitled to sacrifices along with the gods.”

Sukta 161.translation: “Then said they, in answer toAgni, the messenger (of the gods). Whatever is to be done, whether a horse is to be made, or a car is to be made, or a cow is to be made, or the two (old parents) are to be made young, having done all these (acts), Brother Agni, we are then ready to do (what you desire) to be done.”

Sukta 161.translation: “WhenTvaṣṭāsaid: let us slay those who have profaned the ladle, (designed) for the drinking of the gods; then they made use of other names for one another as the libation was poured out; and the maiden (mother) propitiated them by different appellations.”

Sukta 161.translation: “Ṛbhus, reposing in the solar orb, you inquire: who awakens us, unapprehensive (Sun), to this office (of sending rain). The Sun replies: the awakener is the wind; and the year (being ended), you again today light up this (world).”
Sukta 161.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सु॒षु॒प्वांस॑ ऋभव॒स्तद॑पृच्छ॒तागो॑ह्य॒ क इ॒दं नो॑ अबूबुधत् । श्वानं॑ ब॒स्तो बो॑धयि॒तार॑मब्रवीत्संवत्स॒र इ॒दम॒द्या व्य॑ख्यत

devanagari.text: दिवा यांति मरुतो भूम्याग्निरयं वातो अंतरिक्षेण याति ।अद्भिर्याति वरुणः समुद्रैर्युष्माँ इच्छंतः शवसो नपातः ॥

transliteration.text: divā́ ǀ yānti ǀ marútaḥ ǀ bhū́myā ǀ agníḥ ǀ ayám ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ antárikṣeṇa ǀ yāti ǀat-bhíḥ ǀ yāti ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ samudráiḥ ǀ yuṣmā́n ǀ icchántaḥ ǀ śavasaḥ ǀ napātaḥ ǁ

Sukta 161.translation: “Sons of Strength, theMaruts, desirous of your coming, advance from the sky;Agnicomes (to meet you) from the earth; the wind traverses the firmament; andVaruṇacomes with undulating waters.”
Sukta 161.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वा या॑न्ति म॒रुतो॒ भूम्या॒ग्निर॒यं वातो॑ अ॒न्तरि॑क्षेण याति । अ॒द्भिर्या॑ति॒ वरु॑णः समु॒द्रैर्यु॒ष्माँ इ॒च्छन्त॑: शवसो नपातः

devanagari.text: मा नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिंद्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतः परि ख्यन् ।यद्वाजिनो देवजातस्य सप्तेः प्रवक्ष्यामो विदथे वीर्याणि ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “Let neitherMitranorVaruṇa,Aryaman, Āyu,Indra,Ṛbhukṣin,nor theMaruts, censure us; when we proclaim in the sacrifice the virtus of the swift horse sprung from the gods.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा नो॑ मि॒त्रो वरु॑णो अर्य॒मायुरिन्द्र॑ ऋभु॒क्षा म॒रुत॒: परि॑ ख्यन् । यद्वा॒जिनो॑ दे॒वजा॑तस्य॒ सप्ते॑: प्रव॒क्ष्यामो॑ वि॒दथे॑ वी॒र्या॑णि

devanagari.text: यन्निर्णिजा रेक्णसा प्रावृतस्य रातिं गृभीतां मुखतो नयंति ।सुप्राङजो मेम्यद्विश्वरूप इंद्रापूष्णोः प्रियमप्येति पाथः ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ niḥ-níjā ǀ rékṇasā ǀ prā́vṛtasya ǀ rātím ǀ gṛbhītā́m ǀ mukhatáḥ ǀ náyanti ǀsú-prāṅ ǀ ajáḥ ǀ mémyat ǀ viśvá-rūpaḥ ǀ indrāpūṣṇóḥ ǀ priyám ǀ ápi ǀ eti ǀ pā́thaḥ ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “When they, (the priests), bring the prepared offering to the presence (of the horse), who has been bathed and decorated with rich (trappings), the various-coloured goat going before him, bleating, becomes an acceptable offering toIndraandPūṣan.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यन्नि॒र्णिजा॒ रेक्ण॑सा॒ प्रावृ॑तस्य रा॒तिं गृ॑भी॒तां मु॑ख॒तो नय॑न्ति । सुप्रा॑ङ॒जो मेम्य॑द्वि॒श्वरू॑प इन्द्रापू॒ष्णोः प्रि॒यमप्ये॑ति॒ पाथ॑:

devanagari.text: एष छागः पुरो अश्वेन वाजिना पूष्णो भागो नीयते विश्वदेव्यः ।अभिप्रियं यत्पुरोळाशमर्वता त्वष्टेदेनं सौश्रवसाय जिन्वति ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ chā́gaḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ áśvena ǀ vājínā ǀ pūṣṇáḥ ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ nīyate ǀ viśvá-devyaḥ ǀabhi-príyam ǀ yát ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ árvatā ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ ít ǀ enam ǀ sauśravasā́ya ǀ jinvati ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “This goat, the portion of Pu+ṣan fit for all the gods, is brought first with the fleet courser, to thatTvaṣṭāmay prepare him along with the horse, as an acceptable preliminary offering for the (sacrificial) food.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष च्छाग॑: पु॒रो अश्वे॑न वा॒जिना॑ पू॒ष्णो भा॒गो नी॑यते वि॒श्वदे॑व्यः । अ॒भि॒प्रियं॒ यत्पु॑रो॒ळाश॒मर्व॑ता॒ त्वष्टेदे॑नं सौश्रव॒साय॑ जिन्वति

devanagari.text: यद्धविष्यमृतुशो देवयानं त्रिर्मानुषाः पर्यश्वं नयंति ।अत्रा पूष्णः प्रथमो भाग एति यज्ञं देवेभ्यः प्रतिवेदयन्नजः ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ haviṣyám ǀ ṛtu-śáḥ ǀ deva-yā́nam ǀ tríḥ ǀ mā́nuṣāḥ ǀ pári ǀ áśvam ǀ náyanti ǀátra ǀ pūṣṇáḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ eti ǀ yajñám ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ prati-vedáyan ǀ ajáḥ ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “When the priests at the season (of the ceremony), lead forth the horse, the offering devoted to the gods, thrice round (the sacrificial fire); then the goat, the portion ofPūṣan, goes first, announcing the sacrificer to the gods.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद्ध॑वि॒ष्य॑मृतु॒शो दे॑व॒यानं॒ त्रिर्मानु॑षा॒: पर्यश्वं॒ नय॑न्ति । अत्रा॑ पू॒ष्णः प्र॑थ॒मो भा॒ग ए॑ति य॒ज्ञं दे॒वेभ्य॑: प्रतिवे॒दय॑न्न॒जः

devanagari.text: होताध्वर्युरावया अग्निमिंधो ग्रावग्राभ उत शंस्ता सुविप्रः ।तेन यज्ञेन स्वरंकृतेन स्विष्टेन वक्षणा आ पृणध्वं ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “The invoker of the gods, the minister of the rite, the offerer of the oblation, the kindler of the fire, the bruiser of theSoma, the director of the ceremony, the saage (superintendent of the whole); do you replenish the rivers by this well-ordered, well-conducted, sacrifice.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: होता॑ध्व॒र्युराव॑या अग्निमि॒न्धो ग्रा॑वग्रा॒भ उ॒त शंस्ता॒ सुवि॑प्रः । तेन॑ य॒ज्ञेन॒ स्व॑रंकृतेन॒ स्वि॑ष्टेन व॒क्षणा॒ आ पृ॑णध्वम्

transliteration.text: yūpa-vraskā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ yé ǀ yūpa-vāhā́ḥ ǀ caṣā́lam ǀ yé ǀ aśva-yūpā́ya ǀ tákṣati ǀyé ǀ ca ǀ árvate ǀ pácanam ǀ sam-bháranti ǀ utó íti ǀ téṣām ǀ abhí-gūrtiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ invatu ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “Whether they be those who cut the (sacrificial)post, or those who bear the post, or those who fasten the rings on the top of the post, to which the horse (is bound); or those who prepare the vessels in which the food of the horse is dressed; let the exertions of them all fulfil our expectation.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यू॒प॒व्र॒स्का उ॒त ये यू॑पवा॒हाश्च॒षालं॒ ये अ॑श्वयू॒पाय॒ तक्ष॑ति । ये चार्व॑ते॒ पच॑नं स॒म्भर॑न्त्यु॒तो तेषा॑म॒भिगू॑र्तिर्न इन्वतु

devanagari.text: उप प्रागात्सुमन्मेऽधायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्ठः ।अन्वेनं विप्रा ऋषयो मदंति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबंधुं ॥

transliteration.text: úpa ǀ prá ǀ agāt ǀ su-mát ǀ me ǀ adhāyi ǀ mánma ǀ devā́nām ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vītá-pṛṣṭhaḥ ǀánu ǀ enam ǀ víprāḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ madanti ǀ devā́nām ǀ puṣṭé ǀ cakṛma ǀ su-bándhum ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “May my desire be of itself accomplished, such as it has been entertained, that the smooth-backed steed should come to (gratify) the expectations of the gods; we have made him well-secured for the nutriment of the gods; let the wise saints now rejoice.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उप॒ प्रागा॑त्सु॒मन्मे॑ऽधायि॒ मन्म॑ दे॒वाना॒माशा॒ उप॑ वी॒तपृ॑ष्ठः । अन्वे॑नं॒ विप्रा॒ ऋष॑यो मदन्ति दे॒वानां॑ पु॒ष्टे च॑कृमा सु॒बन्धु॑म्

transliteration.text: yát ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ dā́ma ǀ sam-dā́nam ǀ árvataḥ ǀ yā́ ǀ śīrṣaṇyā́ ǀ raśanā́ ǀ rájjuḥ ǀ asya ǀyát ǀ vā ǀ gha ǀ asya ǀ prá-bhṛtam ǀ āsyé ǀ tṛ́ṇam ǀ sárvā ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ ápi ǀ devéṣu ǀ astu ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “May the halter and the heel-ropes of the fleet courser, and the head-ropes, the  girths, and any other (part of the harness); and the grass that has been put into his mouth; may all these be with you, (horse), amongst the gods.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद्वा॒जिनो॒ दाम॑ सं॒दान॒मर्व॑तो॒ या शी॑र्ष॒ण्या॑ रश॒ना रज्जु॑रस्य । यद्वा॑ घास्य॒ प्रभृ॑तमा॒स्ये॒३॒॑ तृणं॒ सर्वा॒ ता ते॒ अपि॑ दे॒वेष्व॑स्तु

यत् । अश्वस्य । क्रविषः । मक्षिका । आश । यत् । वा । स्वरौ । स्वऽधितौ । रिप्तम् । अस्ति ।यत् । हस्तयोः । शमितुः । यत् । नखेषु । सर्वा । ता । ते । अपि । देवेषु । अस्तु ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ áśvasya ǀ kravíṣaḥ ǀ mákṣikā ǀ ā́śa ǀ yát ǀ vā ǀ svárau ǀ svá-dhitau ǀ riptám ǀ ásti ǀyát ǀ hástayoḥ ǀ śamitúḥ ǀ yát ǀ nakhéṣu ǀ sárvā ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ ápi ǀ devéṣu ǀ astu ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “Whatever the flies may eat of the raw flesh of the horse; whatever (grease) is smeared upon the brush or upon the axe; (what is smeared) upon thehandsor the nails of the immolator, may all this be with you, (horse), amongst the gods.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यदश्व॑स्य क्र॒विषो॒ मक्षि॒काश॒ यद्वा॒ स्वरौ॒ स्वधि॑तौ रि॒प्तमस्ति॑ । यद्धस्त॑योः शमि॒तुर्यन्न॒खेषु॒ सर्वा॒ ता ते॒ अपि॑ दे॒वेष्व॑स्तु

devanagari.text: यदूवध्यमुदरस्यापवाति य आमस्य क्रविषो गंधो अस्ति ।सुकृता तच्छमितारः कृण्वंतूत मेधं शृतपाकं पचंतु ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “Whatever undigested grass fall from this belly; whatever particle of raw flesh may remain; let the immolators make the whole free from defect, and so cook the pure (offering) that it may be perfectly dressed.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यदूव॑ध्यमु॒दर॑स्याप॒वाति॒ य आ॒मस्य॑ क्र॒विषो॑ ग॒न्धो अस्ति॑ । सु॒कृ॒ता तच्छ॑मि॒तार॑: कृण्वन्तू॒त मेधं॑ शृत॒पाकं॑ पचन्तु

devanagari.text: यत्ते गात्रादग्निना पच्यमानादभि शूलं निहतस्यावधावति ।मा तद्भूम्यामा श्रिषन्मा तृणेषु देवेभ्यस्तदुशद्भ्यो रातमस्तु ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “Whatever (portion) of your slaughtered (body) fall from your carcass when it is being roasted by the fire, (escaping) from the spit; let it not be left on the ground,nor on the (sacred) grass, but let it (all) be given to the longing gods.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यत्ते॒ गात्रा॑द॒ग्निना॑ प॒च्यमा॑नाद॒भि शूलं॒ निह॑तस्याव॒धाव॑ति । मा तद्भूम्या॒मा श्रि॑ष॒न्मा तृणे॑षु दे॒वेभ्य॒स्तदु॒शद्भ्यो॑ रा॒तम॑स्तु

devanagari.text: ये वाजिनं परिपश्यंति पक्वं य ईमाहुः सुरभिर्निर्हरेति ।ये चार्वतो मांसभिक्षामुपासत उतो तेषामभिगूर्तिर्न इन्वतु ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “Let their exertions be for our good who watch the cooking of the horse; who say, it is fragrant; therefore give us some; who solicit the flesh of the horse as alms.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ये वा॒जिनं॑ परि॒पश्य॑न्ति प॒क्वं य ई॑मा॒हुः सु॑र॒भिर्निर्ह॒रेति॑ । ये चार्व॑तो मांसभि॒क्षामु॒पास॑त उ॒तो तेषा॑म॒भिगू॑र्तिर्न इन्वतु

devanagari.text: यन्नीक्षणं माँस्पचन्या उखाया या पात्राणि यूष्ण आसेचनानि ।ऊष्मण्यापिधाना चरूणामंकाः सूनाः परि भूषंत्यश्वं ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “The stick that is dipped into the cauldron in which the flesh is boiled; the vessels that distribute the broth; the covers of the dishes, the skewers, the knives, all do honour (to the horse).”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यन्नीक्ष॑णं माँ॒स्पच॑न्या उ॒खाया॒ या पात्रा॑णि यू॒ष्ण आ॒सेच॑नानि । ऊ॒ष्म॒ण्या॑पि॒धाना॑ चरू॒णाम॒ङ्काः सू॒नाः परि॑ भूष॒न्त्यश्व॑म्

devanagari.text: निक्रमणं निषदनं विवर्तनं यच्च पड्बीशमर्वतः ।यच्च पपौ यच्च घासिं जघास सर्वा ता ते अपि देवेष्वस्तु ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “May the plural ce of going forth, of tarrying, of rolling on the ground; the foot-fastening of the horse, (the water) that he has drunk, the grass that he has eaten; may all these be thine among the gods.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नि॒क्रम॑णं नि॒षद॑नं वि॒वर्त॑नं॒ यच्च॒ पड्बी॑श॒मर्व॑तः । यच्च॑ प॒पौ यच्च॑ घा॒सिं ज॒घास॒ सर्वा॒ ता ते॒ अपि॑ दे॒वेष्व॑स्तु

Sukta 162.translation: “Let not smoke-smellingAgnicause you, (horse), to utter sound; let not the glowing cauldron, odoriferous (with its contents), be overturned; the gods accept a horse that has been selected (for sacrifice); that has been led (round the fire); that has been devoutly offered, and has been consecrated by (the exclamation), vaṣat.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा त्वा॒ग्निर्ध्व॑नयीद्धू॒मग॑न्धि॒र्मोखा भ्राज॑न्त्य॒भि वि॑क्त॒ जघ्रि॑: । इ॒ष्टं वी॒तम॒भिगू॑र्तं॒ वष॑ट्कृतं॒ तं दे॒वास॒: प्रति॑ गृभ्ण॒न्त्यश्व॑म्

Sukta 162.translation: “The cloth which they spread as a covering for the horse; the golden (trappings with which they decorate him), the head-ropes, the foot-ropes, all these they offer as acceptable to the gods.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यदश्वा॑य॒ वास॑ उपस्तृ॒णन्त्य॑धीवा॒सं या हिर॑ण्यान्यस्मै । सं॒दान॒मर्व॑न्तं॒ पड्बी॑शं प्रि॒या दे॒वेष्वा या॑मयन्ति

Sukta 162.translation: “Whoever has goaded you in your paces, either with heel or with whip, whilst nothing in your strength-- all these (vexations) I pour out with holy prayers, as oblation with the ladle.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यत्ते॑ सा॒दे मह॑सा॒ शूकृ॑तस्य॒ पार्ष्ण्या॑ वा॒ कश॑या वा तु॒तोद॑ । स्रु॒चेव॒ ता ह॒विषो॑ अध्व॒रेषु॒ सर्वा॒ ता ते॒ ब्रह्म॑णा सूदयामि

devanagari.text: चतुस्त्रिंशद्वाजिनो देवबंधोर्वंक्रीरश्वस्य स्वधितिः समेति ।अच्छिद्रा गात्रा वयुना कृणोत परुष्परुरनुघुष्या वि शस्त ॥

Sukta 162.translation: “The axe penetrates the thirty-four ribs of the swift horse; the beloved of the gods, (the immolators), cut up (the horse) with skill, so that the limbs may be unperforated, and recapitulating joint by joint.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: चतु॑स्त्रिंशद्वा॒जिनो॑ दे॒वब॑न्धो॒र्वङ्क्री॒रश्व॑स्य॒ स्वधि॑ति॒: समे॑ति । अच्छि॑द्रा॒ गात्रा॑ व॒युना॑ कृणोत॒ परु॑ष्परुरनु॒घुष्या॒ वि श॑स्त

Sukta 162.translation: “There is one immolator of the radiant horse, which is Time; there are two that hold him fast; such of your limbs as I cut up in due season, I offer them, made into balls (of meat) upon the fire.”
Sukta 162.sanskrit_wisdomlib: एक॒स्त्वष्टु॒रश्व॑स्या विश॒स्ता द्वा य॒न्तारा॑ भवत॒स्तथ॑ ऋ॒तुः । या ते॒ गात्रा॑णामृतु॒था कृ॒णोमि॒ ताता॒ पिण्डा॑नां॒ प्र जु॑होम्य॒ग्नौ

transliteration.text: mā́ ǀ tvā ǀ tapat ǀ priyáḥ ǀ ātmā́ ǀ api-yántam ǀ mā́ ǀ svá-dhitiḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ tisthipat ǀ te ǀmā́ ǀ te ǀ gṛdhnúḥ ǀ avi-śastā́ ǀ ati-hā́ya ǀ chidrā́ ǀ gā́trāṇi ǀ asínā ǀ míthu ǀ karíti kaḥ ǁ

Sukta 162.translation: “Let not your precious body grieve you, who are going verily (to the gods); let not the axe linger in your body; let not the greedy and unskilful (immolator) missing the members, mangle your limbs needlessly with his knife.”

Sukta 162.translation: “Verily at this moment you do not die; nor are you harmed; for you go by auspicious paths to the gods. The horses ofIndra, the steeds of theMarutsshall be yoked (to their ears), and a courser shall be plural ced in the shaft of the ass of theAśvins(to bear you to heaven).”

Sukta 162.translation: “May this horse bring to us all-sustaining wealth, with abundance of cows of excellent horses, and ofmaleoffspring; may the spirited steed bring us exemption from wickedness; may this horse, offered in oblation, procure for us bodily vigour.”

Sukta 163.translation: “Your great birth, O Horse, is to be glorified; whether first springing from the firmament or from the water inasmuchas you have neighed (auspiciously), for you have the wings of the falcon and the limbs of the deer.”

Sukta 163.translation: “Tritaharnessed the horse which was given byyama;Indrafirst mounted him, andgandharvaseized his reins.Vasus, you fabricated the horse from the sun.”

Sukta 163.translation: “The full-haunched, slender-waistd, high-spirited, and celestial coursers (of the sun), gallop along like swans in rows, when the horses spread along the heavenly path.”

Sukta 163.translation: “The horse proceeds to that assembly which is most excellent; to the presence of his father and his mother, (heaven and earth). Go, (Horse), today rejoicing to the gods, that (the sacrifice) may yield blessings to the donor.”

Sukta 164.translation: “I have beheld the Lord of men with seven sons; of which delightful and benevolent (deity), who is the object of our invocation, there is an all-pervadingmiddlebrother, and a third brother, well fed with (oblationsof)ghee.”

Sukta 164.translation: “Who has seen the primeval (being) at the time of his being born; what is that endowed with substance which the unsubstantial sustains; from earth are the breath and blood; but where is thesoul; who may repair to the sage to ask this?”

Sukta 164.translation: “Immature (in understanding) undiscerning in mind, I inquire of those things which are hidden (even) from the gods; (what are) the seven threads which the sages have spread to envelop the sun, in whom all abide?”

Sukta 164.translation: “Ignorant, I inquire of the sages who know (the truth); not as one knowing (do I inquire), for the sake of (gaining) knowledge; what is that one alone, who has upheld these six spheres in the form of the unborn?”

Sukta 164.translation: “Let him who knows this (truth) quickly declare it; the mysterious condition of the beautiful ever-moving (sun); the rays shed (their) milk from his (exalted) head investing his form with radiance; they have drunk up the water by the paths (by which they were poured forth).”

devanagari.text: माता पितरमृत आ बभाज धीत्यग्रे मनसा सं हि जग्मे ।सा बीभत्सुर्गर्भरसा निविद्धा नमस्वंत इदुपवाकमीयुः ॥

transliteration.text: mātā́ ǀ pitáram ǀ ṛté ǀ ā́ ǀ babhāja ǀ dhītī́ ǀ ágre ǀ mánasā ǀ sám ǀ hí ǀ jagmé ǀsā́ ǀ bībhatsúḥ ǀ gárbha-rasā ǀ ní-viddhā ǀ námasvantaḥ ǀ ít ǀ upa-vākám ǀ īyuḥ ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “The mother, (earth), worships the father, (sun), with holy rites, for the sake of water; but he has anticipated (her wants) in his mind; whereupon desirous of progeny, she is penetrated by the dews of impregnation, and, (all) expectant of abundance, exchange words (of congratulation).”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा॒ता पि॒तर॑मृ॒त आ ब॑भाज धी॒त्यग्रे॒ मन॑सा॒ सं हि ज॒ग्मे । सा बी॑भ॒त्सुर्गर्भ॑रसा॒ निवि॑द्धा॒ नम॑स्वन्त॒ इदु॑पवा॒कमी॑युः

devanagari.text: युक्ता मातासीद्धुरि दक्षिणाया अतिष्ठद्गर्भो वृजनीष्वंतः ।अमीमेद्वत्सो अनु गामपश्यद्विश्वरूप्यं त्रिषु योजनेषु ॥
युक्ता । माता । आसीत् । धुरि । दक्षिणायाः । अतिष्ठत् । गर्भः । वृजनीषु । अन्तरिति ।अमीमेत् । वत्सः । अनु । गाम् । अपश्यत् । विश्वऽरूप्यम् । त्रिषु । योजनेषु ॥

transliteration.text: yuktā́ ǀ mātā́ ǀ āsīt ǀ dhurí ǀ dákṣiṇāyāḥ ǀ átiṣṭhat ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ vṛjanī́ṣu ǀ antáríti ǀámīmet ǀ vatsáḥ ǀ ánu ǀ gā́m ǀ apaśyat ǀ viśva-rūpyám ǀ triṣú ǀ yójaneṣu ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “The mother, (sky), was associated in (sustaining) the burden of the fulfiller of desires, (the earth); the embryo (water) rested within the (womb of the) clouds; thereupon the calf bellowed, and beheld the omniform cow in the three combinations.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒क्ता मा॒तासी॑द्धु॒रि दक्षि॑णाया॒ अति॑ष्ठ॒द्गर्भो॑ वृज॒नीष्व॒न्तः । अमी॑मेद्व॒त्सो अनु॒ गाम॑पश्यद्विश्वरू॒प्यं॑ त्रि॒षु योज॑नेषु

devanagari.text: तिस्रो मातॄस्त्रीन्पितॄन्बिभ्रदेक ऊर्ध्वस्तस्थौ नेमव ग्लापयंति ।मंत्रयंते दिवो अमुष्य पृष्ठे विश्वविदं वाचमविश्वमिन्वां ॥
तिस्रः । मातॄः । त्रीन् । पितॄन् । बिभ्रत् । एकः । ऊर्ध्वः । तस्थौ । न । ईम् । अव । ग्लपयन्ति ।मन्त्रयन्ते । दिवः । अमुष्य । पृष्ठे । विश्वऽविदम् । वाचम् । अविश्वऽमिन्वाम् ॥

transliteration.text: tisráḥ ǀ mātṝ́ḥ ǀ trī́n ǀ pitṝ́n ǀ bíbhrat ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ tasthau ǀ ná ǀ īm ǀ áva ǀ glapayanti ǀmantráyante ǀ diváḥ ǀ amúṣya ǀ pṛṣṭhé ǀ viśva-vídam ǀ vā́cam ǀ áviśva-minvām ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “The one sole (sun), having three mothers and three fathers, stood on high; none ever over-weary him; the (gods) on the summit of the sky take counsel respecting him in language all-comprehending (but) not extending to all.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ति॒स्रो मा॒तॄस्त्रीन्पि॒तॄन्बिभ्र॒देक॑ ऊ॒र्ध्वस्त॑स्थौ॒ नेमव॑ ग्लापयन्ति । म॒न्त्रय॑न्ते दि॒वो अ॒मुष्य॑ पृ॒ष्ठे वि॑श्व॒विदं॒ वाच॒मवि॑श्वमिन्वाम्

devanagari.text: द्वादशारं नहि तज्जराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य ।आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः ॥
द्वादशऽअरम् । नहि । तत् । जराय । वर्वर्ति । चक्रम् । परि । द्याम् । ऋतस्य ।आ । पुत्राः । अग्ने । मिथुनासः । अत्र । सप्त । शतानि । विंशतिः । च । तस्थुः ॥

transliteration.text: dvā́daśa-aram ǀ nahí ǀ tát ǀ járāya ǀ várvarti ǀ cakrám ǀ pári ǀ dyā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀā́ ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ mithunā́saḥ ǀ átra ǀ saptá ǀ śatā́ni ǀ viṃśatíḥ ǀ ca ǀ tasthuḥ ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “The twelve-spoked wheel, of the true (sun) revolves round the heavens, and never (tends) to decay; seven hundred and twenty children in pais,Agni, abide in it.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्वाद॑शारं न॒हि तज्जरा॑य॒ वर्व॑र्ति च॒क्रं परि॒ द्यामृ॒तस्य॑ । आ पु॒त्रा अ॑ग्ने मिथु॒नासो॒ अत्र॑ स॒प्त श॒तानि॑ विंश॒तिश्च॑ तस्थुः

devanagari.text: पंचपादं पितरं द्वादशाकृतिं दिव आहुः परे अर्धे पुरीषिणं ।अथेमे अन्य उपरे विचक्षणं सप्तचक्रे षळर आहुरर्पितं ॥
पञ्चऽपादम् । पितरम् । द्वादशऽआकृतिम् । दिवः । आहुः । परे । अर्धे । पुरीषिणम् ।अथ । इमे । अन्ये । उपरे । विऽचक्षणम् । सप्तऽचक्रे । षट्ऽअरे । आहुः । अर्पितम् ॥

transliteration.text: páñca-pādam ǀ pitáram ǀ dvā́daśa-ākṛtim ǀ diváḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀ páre ǀ árdhe ǀ purīṣíṇam ǀátha ǀ imé ǀ anyé ǀ úpare ǀ vi-cakṣaṇám ǀ saptá-cakre ǀ ṣáṭ-are ǀ āhuḥ ǀ árpitam ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “They have termed the five-footed, twelve-formed parent, Puriṣin, when in the further hemisphere of the sky; and others have termed inArpita, when in the hither (portion of the sky); shining in his seven-wheeled car), each (wheel) having six spokes.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पञ्च॑पादं पि॒तरं॒ द्वाद॑शाकृतिं दि॒व आ॑हु॒: परे॒ अर्धे॑ पुरी॒षिण॑म् । अथे॒मे अ॒न्य उप॑रे विचक्ष॒णं स॒प्तच॑क्रे॒ षळ॑र आहु॒रर्पि॑तम्

devanagari.text: पंचारे चक्रे परिवर्तमाने तस्मिन्ना तस्थुर्भुवनानि विश्वा ।तस्य नाक्षस्तप्यते भूरिभारः सनादेव न शीर्यते सनाभिः ॥
पञ्चऽअरे । चक्रे । परिऽवर्तमाने । तस्मिन् । आ । तस्थुः । भुवनानि । विश्वा ।तस्य । न । अक्षः । तप्यते । भूरिऽभारः । सनात् । एव । न । शीर्यते । सऽनाभिः ॥

transliteration.text: páñca-are ǀ cakré ǀ pari-vártamāne ǀ tásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀtásya ǀ ná ǀ ákṣaḥ ǀ tapyate ǀ bhū́ri-bhāraḥ ǀ sanā́t ǀ evá ǀ ná ǀ śīryate ǀ sá-nābhiḥ ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “All beings abide in this five-spoked revolving wheel; the heavily-loaded axle is never heated; its eternal compact nave is never worn away.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पञ्चा॑रे च॒क्रे प॑रि॒वर्त॑माने॒ तस्मि॒न्ना त॑स्थु॒र्भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ । तस्य॒ नाक्ष॑स्तप्यते॒ भूरि॑भारः स॒नादे॒व न शी॑र्यते॒ सना॑भिः

devanagari.text: सनेमि चक्रमजरं वि वावृत उत्तानायां दश युक्ता वहंति ।सूर्यस्य चक्षू रजसैत्यावृतं तस्मिन्नार्पिता भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
सऽनेमि । चक्रम् । अजरम् । वि । ववृते । उत्तानायाम् । दश । युक्ताः । वहन्ति ।सूर्यस्य । चक्षुः । रजसा । एति । आऽवृतम् । तस्मिन् । आर्पिता । भुवनानि । विश्वा ॥

transliteration.text: sá-nemi ǀ cakrám ǀ ajáram ǀ ví ǀ vavṛte ǀ uttānā́yām ǀ dáśa ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ vahanti ǀsū́ryasya ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ rájasā ǀ eti ǀ ā́-vṛtam ǀ tásmin ǀ ā́rpitā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “The even-fellied, undecaying wheel, repeatedly revolves; ten, united on the upper surface, bear (the world); the orb of the sun proceeds, invested with water, and in it are all beings deposited.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सने॑मि च॒क्रम॒जरं॒ वि वा॑वृत उत्ता॒नायां॒ दश॑ यु॒क्ता व॑हन्ति । सूर्य॑स्य॒ चक्षू॒ रज॑सै॒त्यावृ॑तं॒ तस्मि॒न्नार्पि॑ता॒ भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑

devanagari.text: साकंजानां सप्तथमाहुरेकजं षळिद्यमा ऋषयो देवजा इति ।तेषामिष्टानि विहितानि धामशः स्थात्रे रेजंते विकृतानि रूपशः ॥
साकम्ऽजानाम् । सप्तथम् । आहुः । एकऽजम् । षट् । इत् । यमाः । ऋषयः । देवऽजाः । इति ।तेषाम् । इष्टानि । विऽहितानि । धामऽशः । स्थात्रे । रेजन्ते । विऽकृतानि । रूपऽशः ॥

transliteration.text: sākam-jā́nām ǀ saptátham ǀ āhuḥ ǀ eka-jám ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ ít ǀ yamā́ḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ deva-jā́ḥ ǀ íti ǀtéṣām ǀ iṣṭā́ni ǀ ví-hitāni ǀ dhāma-śáḥ ǀ sthātré ǀ rejante ǀ ví-kṛtāni ǀ rūpa-śáḥ ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “Of those that are born together, sages have called the seventh single-born; for six are twins, and are moveable, and born of the gods; their desirable (properties), plural ced severally in their proper abode, are various (also) in form, and revolve for (the benefit of) that which is stationary.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सा॒कं॒जानां॑ स॒प्तथ॑माहुरेक॒जं षळिद्य॒मा ऋष॑यो देव॒जा इति॑ । तेषा॑मि॒ष्टानि॒ विहि॑तानि धाम॒शः स्था॒त्रे रे॑जन्ते॒ विकृ॑तानि रूप॒शः

devanagari.text: स्त्रियः सतीस्ताँ उ मे पुंस आहुः पश्यदक्षण्वान्न वि चेतदंधः ।कविर्यः पुत्रः स ईमा चिकेत यस्ता विजानात्स पितुष्पितासत् ॥
स्त्रियः । सतीः । तान् । ऊं इति । मे । पुंसः । आहुः । पश्यत् । अक्षण्ऽवान् । न । वि । चेतत् । अन्धः ।कविः । यः । पुत्रः । सः । ईम् । आ । चिकेत । यः । ता । विऽजानात् । सः । पितुः । पिता । असत् ॥

transliteration.text: stríyaḥ ǀ satī́ḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ me ǀ puṃsáḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀ páśyat ǀ akṣaṇ-vā́n ǀ ná ǀ ví ǀ cetat ǀ andháḥ ǀkavíḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ putráḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ ā́ ǀ ciketa ǀ yáḥ ǀ tā́ ǀ vi-jānā́t ǀ sáḥ ǀ pitúḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ asat ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “They have called thes, my virtuous feminine les,males; he who has eyes beholds; the blind man sees not; he whois a sage son understands this, and he who discriminates is the father of the father.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्त्रिय॑: स॒तीस्ताँ उ॑ मे पुं॒स आ॑हु॒: पश्य॑दक्ष॒ण्वान्न वि चे॑तद॒न्धः । क॒विर्यः पु॒त्रः स ई॒मा चि॑केत॒ यस्ता वि॑जा॒नात्स पि॒तुष्पि॒तास॑त्

devanagari.text: अवः परेण पर एनावरेण पदा वत्सं बिभ्रती गौरुदस्थात् ।सा कद्रीची कं स्विदर्धं परागात्क्व स्वित्सूते नहि यूथे अंतः ॥
अवः । परेण । परः । एना । अवरेण । पदा । वत्सम् । बिभ्रती । गौः । उत् । अस्थात् ।सा । कद्रीची । कम् । स्वित् । अर्धम् । परा । अगात् । क्व । स्वित् । सूते । नहि । यूथे । अन्तरिति ॥

transliteration.text: aváḥ ǀ páreṇa ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ ávareṇa ǀ padā́ ǀ vatsám ǀ bíbhratī ǀ gáuḥ ǀ út ǀ asthāt ǀsā́ ǀ kadrī́cī ǀ kám ǀ svit ǀ árdham ǀ párā ǀ agāt ǀ kvá ǀ svit ǀ sūte ǀ nahí ǀ yūthé ǀ antáríti ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “The cow, holding her calf underneath with her fore-feet, and then above with her hind-feet, has risen up; whither is she gone; to whom has she turned back when half-way; where does she bear young; it is not amidst the herd.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒वः परे॑ण प॒र ए॒नाव॑रेण प॒दा व॒त्सं बिभ्र॑ती॒ गौरुद॑स्थात् । सा क॒द्रीची॒ कं स्वि॒दर्धं॒ परा॑गा॒त्क्व॑ स्वित्सूते न॒हि यू॒थे अ॒न्तः

devanagari.text: अवः परेण पितरं यो अस्यानुवेद पर एनावरेण ।कवीयमानः क इह प्र वोचद्देवं मनः कुतो अधि प्रजातं ॥
अवः । परेण । पितरम् । यः । अस्य । अनुऽवेद । परः । एना । अवरेण ।कविऽयमानः । कः । इह । प्र । वोचत् । देवम् । मनः । कुतः । अधि । प्रऽजातम् ॥

transliteration.text: aváḥ ǀ páreṇa ǀ pitáram ǀ yáḥ ǀ asya ǀ anu-véda ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ ávareṇa ǀkavi-yámānaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ ihá ǀ prá ǀ vocat ǀ devám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ kútaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ prá-jātam ǁ

Sukta 164.translation: “He who knows the protector of this (world) as the inferior associated with the superior, and the superior associated with the inferior, he is, as it were, a sage; but who in this world can expound (it); whence is the divine mind in its supremacy engendereḍ ”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒वः परे॑ण पि॒तरं॒ यो अ॑स्यानु॒वेद॑ प॒र ए॒नाव॑रेण । क॒वी॒यमा॑न॒: क इ॒ह प्र वो॑चद्दे॒वं मन॒: कुतो॒ अधि॒ प्रजा॑तम्

devanagari.text: ये अर्वांचस्ताँ उ पराच आहुर्ये परांचस्ताँ उ अर्वाच आहुः ।इंद्रश्च या चक्रथुः सोम तानि धुरा न युक्ता रजसो वहंति ॥

Sukta 164.translation: “Those which (the sages) have termed descending, they have also termed ascending; and those they have termed ascending, they have also called descending; and those (orbits) which your,SomaandIndra, have made, bear along the worlds like (oxen) yoked to a twain.”

Sukta 164.translation: “Two birds associated together, and mutual friends, take refuge in the same tree; one of them eats the sweet fig; the other abstaining from food, merely looks on.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्वा सु॑प॒र्णा स॒युजा॒ सखा॑या समा॒नं वृ॒क्षं परि॑ षस्वजाते । तयो॑र॒न्यः पिप्प॑लं स्वा॒द्वत्त्यन॑श्नन्न॒न्यो अ॒भि चा॑कशीति

Sukta 164.translation: “Where the smooth-gliding (rays), cognizant (of their duty), distil the perpetual portion of ambrosia (water); there has the lord and steadfast protector all beings consigned me, (though) immature (in wisdom).”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यत्रा॑ सुप॒र्णा अ॒मृत॑स्य भा॒गमनि॑मेषं वि॒दथा॑भि॒स्वर॑न्ति । इ॒नो विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य गो॒पाः स मा॒ धीर॒: पाक॒मत्रा वि॑वेश

Sukta 164.translation: “In the tree into which the smooth-gliding (rays) feeders on the sweet (produce), enter, and again bring forth (light) over all, they have called the fruit sweet, but he partakes not of it who knows not the protector (of the universe).”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्मि॑न्वृ॒क्षे म॒ध्वद॑: सुप॒र्णा नि॑वि॒शन्ते॒ सुव॑ते॒ चाधि॒ विश्वे॑ । तस्येदा॑हु॒: पिप्प॑लं स्वा॒द्वग्रे॒ तन्नोन्न॑श॒द्यः पि॒तरं॒ न वेद॑

Sukta 164.translation: “They who know the station ofAgniupon the earth; the station ofVāyuthat was fabricated from the firmament; and that station of the Sun which is plural ced in heaven, obtain immortality.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद्गा॑य॒त्रे अधि॑ गाय॒त्रमाहि॑तं॒ त्रैष्टु॑भाद्वा॒ त्रैष्टु॑भं नि॒रत॑क्षत । यद्वा॒ जग॒ज्जग॒त्याहि॑तं प॒दं य इत्तद्वि॒दुस्ते अ॑मृत॒त्वमा॑नशुः

Sukta 164.translation: “He constructs the prayer with thegāyatrīmetre; with the prayer (he constructs) theSoma, and with thetriṣṭubhmetre the couplet (or triplet); with the couplet (or triplet) he constructs the hymn with (verses of) two or four distichs; and with the syllable they construct the seven metres.”

Sukta 164.translation: “With the hymns in thejagatīmetre he fixed the rain in heaven, and surveyed the Sun in therathantara. They have declared three divisions of thegāyatrīmetre, whence it surpasses (all the rest) in force and majesty.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: जग॑ता॒ सिन्धुं॑ दि॒व्य॑स्तभायद्रथंत॒रे सूर्यं॒ पर्य॑पश्यत् । गा॒य॒त्रस्य॑ स॒मिध॑स्ति॒स्र आ॑हु॒स्ततो॑ म॒ह्ना प्र रि॑रिचे महि॒त्वा

Sukta 164.translation: “I invoke the cow that is easily milked, that the handy milker may milk her; maySavitāaccept this our excellent libation, that his heat may (thereby) increase; it is for this, verily, that I earnestly invoke him.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उप॑ ह्वये सु॒दुघां॑ धे॒नुमे॒तां सु॒हस्तो॑ गो॒धुगु॒त दो॑हदेनाम् । श्रेष्ठं॑ स॒वं स॑वि॒ता सा॑विषन्नो॒ऽभी॑द्धो घ॒र्मस्तदु॒ षु प्र वो॑चम्

Sukta 164.translation: “She comes lowing, abounding in rich (products), desiring her calf in her mind;may this cow grant her milk to theAśvins; may she thrive for our great advantage.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: हि॒ङ्कृ॒ण्व॒ती व॑सु॒पत्नी॒ वसू॑नां व॒त्समि॒च्छन्ती॒ मन॑सा॒भ्यागा॑त् । दु॒हाम॒श्विभ्यां॒ पयो॑ अ॒घ्न्येयं सा व॑र्धतां मह॒ते सौभ॑गाय

Sukta 164.translation: “The cow bellows for her calf, (who stands) with winking eyes, and lows as (she proceeds to lick his forehead; she utters a cry, as, anxious, she sees the moisture in the corners of his mouth, and nourishes him with her milk.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: गौर॑मीमे॒दनु॑ व॒त्सं मि॒षन्तं॑ मू॒र्धानं॒ हिङ्ङ॑कृणो॒न्मात॒वा उ॑ । सृक्वा॑णं घ॒र्मम॒भि वा॑वशा॒ना मिमा॑ति मा॒युं पय॑ते॒ पयो॑भिः

Sukta 164.translation: “He, too, bellows, and the cow utters inarticulate sounds, as, encompassed by him, she repairs to her stall; (influenced) by her instrumental ncts, she acts like a human being, and, radiant, manifests her nature.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं स शि॑ङ्क्ते॒ येन॒ गौर॒भीवृ॑ता॒ मिमा॑ति मा॒युं ध्व॒सना॒वधि॑ श्रि॒ता । सा चि॒त्तिभि॒र्नि हि च॒कार॒ मर्त्यं॑ वि॒द्युद्भव॑न्ती॒ प्रति॑ व॒व्रिमौ॑हत

Sukta 164.translation: “Life endowed with breath, eager (in discharge of its functions), reposes, steady, in the midst of its (proper) abodes; the life of the mortal body, cognate with the mortal frame, endures immortal (sustained) by (obsequial) offerings.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒नच्छ॑ये तु॒रगा॑तु जी॒वमेज॑द्ध्रु॒वं मध्य॒ आ प॒स्त्या॑नाम् । जी॒वो मृ॒तस्य॑ चरति स्व॒धाभि॒रम॑र्त्यो॒ मर्त्ये॑ना॒ सयो॑निः

Sukta 164.translation: “I have beheld the unwearied protector of the universe, the sun, travelling upwards, the downwards by various paths;invested with aggregative and diffusive radiance, he revolves in the midst of the regions.”

Sukta 164.translation: “He who has made (this state of things) does not comprehend it; he who has beheld it, has it also verily hidden (from him); he, whilst yet enveloped in his mother's womb, is subject to many births, and has entered upon evil.”

Sukta 164.translation: “The heaven is my parent and progenitor; the navel (of the earth) is my kinsman; the spacious earth is my mother. The womb (of all beings) lies between the two uplifted ladles, and in it the parent has deposited the germ (of the fruitfulness) of the daughter.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्यौर्मे॑ पि॒ता ज॑नि॒ता नाभि॒रत्र॒ बन्धु॑र्मे मा॒ता पृ॑थि॒वी म॒हीयम् । उ॒त्ता॒नयो॑श्च॒म्वो॒३॒॑र्योनि॑र॒न्तरत्रा॑ पि॒ता दु॑हि॒तुर्गर्भ॒माधा॑त्

devanagari.text: पृच्छामि त्वा परमंतं पृथिव्याः पृच्छामि यत्र भुवनस्य नाभिः ।पृच्छामि त्वा वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतः पृच्छामि वाचः परमं व्योम ॥

Sukta 164.translation: “I ask you, (instrumental tutor of the rite), what is the uttermost end of the earth; I ask you, where is the navel of the world. I ask you, what is the fecundating power of the rain-shedding steed; I ask you, what is the supreme heaven of (holy) speech.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पृ॒च्छामि॑ त्वा॒ पर॒मन्तं॑ पृथि॒व्याः पृ॒च्छामि॒ यत्र॒ भुव॑नस्य॒ नाभि॑: । पृ॒च्छामि॑ त्वा॒ वृष्णो॒ अश्व॑स्य॒ रेत॑: पृ॒च्छामि॑ वा॒चः प॑र॒मं व्यो॑म

Sukta 164.translation: “This altar is the uttermost end of the earth; this sacrifice is the navel of the world; thisSomais the fecundating power of the rain-shedding steed; thisBrahmāis the supreme heavn of (holy) speech.”

Sukta 164.translation: “The seven (sustaining), the embryo (rain) for half a year, the fecundating (element) of the world, abide, by appointment, in the various functions ofViṣṇu. By their intelligence they pervade in thought all around (them), for they are intelligent and diffusive.”

Sukta 164.translation: “I distinguish not if I am this all; for I go perplexed, and bound in mind; when the first-born (perceptions) of the truth reach me, then immediately shall I obtain a portion (of the meaning) of that (sacred) word.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न वि जा॑नामि॒ यदि॑वे॒दमस्मि॑ नि॒ण्यः संन॑द्धो॒ मन॑सा चरामि । य॒दा माग॑न्प्रथम॒जा ऋ॒तस्यादिद्वा॒चो अ॑श्नुवे भा॒गम॒स्याः

Sukta 164.translation: “The immortal cognate with the mortal, affected by (desire of) enjoyment, goes to the lower or the upper (sphere); but (men beholding them) associated, going everywhere (in this world together); going everywhere (in other worlds together); have comprehended the one, but have not comprehended the other.”

Sukta 164.translation: “All the gods have taken their seats upon this supreme heaven, the imperishable (text) of  theVeda; what will he, who knows not this, do with the Veda? but they who do know it, they are perfect.”

Sukta 164.translation: “Cow, may you be rich in milk through abundant fodder; that we also may be rich (in abundance); eat grass at all seasons, and, roaming (at will), drink pure water.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सू॒य॒व॒साद्भग॑वती॒ हि भू॒या अथो॑ व॒यं भग॑वन्तः स्याम । अ॒द्धि तृण॑मघ्न्ये विश्व॒दानीं॒ पिब॑ शु॒द्धमु॑द॒कमा॒चर॑न्ती

Sukta 164.translation: “The sound (of the clouds) has been uttered, fabricating the waters, and being one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed, or infinite in the highest heaven.”
