Sukta 164.translation: “From her the clouds shed abundant rain, and thence (the people of) the four quarters live; thence the moisture spreads (to the grain), and the universe exists.”

Sukta 164.translation: “I beheld near (me) the smoke of burning cow-dung; and by that tall-pervading mean (effect, discovered the cause (fire); the priests have theSomaox, for such are their first duties.”

Sukta 164.translation: “The three, with beautiful tresses, look down in their several seasons upon the earth; one of them, when the year is ended, shears (the ground); one, by his acts, overlooks the universe; the course of one is visible, though not his form.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्रय॑: के॒शिन॑ ऋतु॒था वि च॑क्षते संवत्स॒रे व॑पत॒ एक॑ एषाम् । विश्व॒मेको॑ अ॒भि च॑ष्टे॒ शची॑भि॒र्ध्राजि॒रेक॑स्य ददृशे॒ न रू॒पम्

Sukta 164.translation: “Four are the definite grades of spech; thoseBrahmaṇaswho are wise know them; three, deposited in secret, indicate no meaning; men speak the fourth grade of speech.”
Sukta 164.sanskrit_wisdomlib: च॒त्वारि॒ वाक्परि॑मिता प॒दानि॒ तानि॑ विदुर्ब्राह्म॒णा ये म॑नी॒षिण॑: । गुहा॒ त्रीणि॒ निहि॑ता॒ नेङ्ग॑यन्ति तु॒रीयं॑ वा॒चो म॑नु॒ष्या॑ वदन्ति

Sukta 164.translation: “They have styled (him, the Sun),Indra,Mitra,Varuṇa,Agni, and he is the celestial, well-wingedGarutmat, for learned priests call one by many names as they speak of Agni,Yama,Mātariśvan.”

Sukta 164.translation: “The smooth-gliding wafters (of the rain, the solar rays), clothing the waters with a dark cloud, ascend to heaven; they come down again from the dwelling of the rain, and immediately the earth is moistened with water.”

Sukta 164.translation: “The fellies are twelve; the wheel is one; three are the axles; but who knows it? within it are collected 360 (spokes), which are, as it were, moveable and immoveable.”

Sukta 164.translation: “Sarasvatī, that retiring breast, which is the source of delight, with which you bestow all good things, which is the container of wealth, the distributor of riches, the giver of good (fortune); that (bodom) do you lay open at this season for our nourishment.”

Sukta 164.translation: “The gods sacrifice with sacrifice, for such are their first duties; those mighty ones assemble in heaven, where the divinities who are to be propitiated (by sacred rites) abide.”

Sukta 165.translation: “(Indraspeaks): With what auspicious fortune have theMaruts, who are of one age, one residence, one dignity, watered (the earth) together; with what intention; whence have they come; showerers of rain, they venerate through desire of wealth, the energy (that is genitive rated in the world by rain).”

Sukta 165.translation: “Since the experienced intellect of a venerable (sage), competent to bestow praise upon (you), who deserve praise, has been exerted for us; do you,Maruts, come to the presence of the devout (worshipper), who, glorifying (you), worships you with these holy rites.”

Sukta 165.translation: “This praise,Maruts, is for you; this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations). May the praise reach you, for (the good of your) person ns, so that we may (thence) obtain food, strength, and long life.”

Sukta 166.translation: “We proclaim eagerly,Maruts, your ancient greatness, for (the sake of inducing) your prompt appearance, as the indication of (the approach of) the showerer (of benefits). Loud-roaring and mighty Maruts, you exert your vigorous energies for the advance (to the sacrifice), as if it was to battle.”

Sukta 166.translation: “Ever accepting the sweet (libation), as (they would) a son, they sport plural yfully at sacrifices, demolishing (all intruders); theRudrascome to the offerer of prayers and oblations, for his protection, and powerul as they are, do him no harm.”

Sukta 166.translation: “To him, the presenter (of offerings), the protecting and immortalMaruts, (gratified) by the oblation, have given abundance of riches; they, the bestowers of happiness, becoming, as it were, the friends (of the worshipper), sprinkle the regions plural ntifully with water.”

Sukta 166.translation: “Those, your coursers, which traverse the regions in their speed, proceed, self-guided; all worlds, all dwellings, are alarmed, for marvellous is your coming; (such fear as is felt) when spears are thrust forth (in battle).”

Sukta 166.translation: “Maruts, all good things are in your cars; on your shoulders abides emulous strength; at your resting-plural ces on the road refreshments (are ready); the axle of your (chariot) wheels holds them firmly together.”
Sukta 166.sanskrit_wisdomlib: विश्वा॑नि भ॒द्रा म॑रुतो॒ रथे॑षु वो मिथ॒स्पृध्ये॑व तवि॒षाण्याहि॑ता । अंसे॒ष्वा व॒: प्रप॑थेषु खा॒दयोऽक्षो॑ वश्च॒क्रा स॒मया॒ वि वा॑वृते

Sukta 166.translation: “Maruts, in your arms, propitious to man, are many good things; on your breasts are golden (ornaments) brilliant and conspicuous; while garlands (hang) on your shoulders; sharp are (the edges of) your weapons; the Maruts have various decorations, as birds have (many-coloured) wings.”
Sukta 166.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भूरी॑णि भ॒द्रा नर्ये॑षु बा॒हुषु॒ वक्ष॑स्सु रु॒क्मा र॑भ॒सासो॑ अ॒ञ्जय॑: । अंसे॒ष्वेता॑: प॒विषु॑ क्षु॒रा अधि॒ वयो॒ न प॒क्षान्व्यनु॒ श्रियो॑ धिरे

Sukta 166.translation: “Maruts, mighty with mighty power, all-pervading, manifest afar off, as the gods (are made manifest) by the constellations; exhilarating, soft-tongued, speaking genitive ly with your mouths, associated withIndra, glorified by praise; (come to our sacrifice).”

Sukta 166.translation: “Such, well-bornMaruts, is your greatness, that your munificence is as long (continued) as the function ofAditi; andIndradoes not exceed, by his own liberality, (the value of) that which you have bestowed upon the devout man (who worships you).”
Sukta 166.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तद्व॑: सुजाता मरुतो महित्व॒नं दी॒र्घं वो॑ दा॒त्रमदि॑तेरिव व्र॒तम् । इन्द्र॑श्च॒न त्यज॑सा॒ वि ह्रु॑णाति॒ तज्जना॑य॒ यस्मै॑ सु॒कृते॒ अरा॑ध्वम्

Sukta 166.translation: “Your alliance with us,Maruts, is of a long duration on which account, immortals, accept our ample praise and, having accepted ourlaudation, be gratified, leaders (of sacrifice), by our holy acts, through this (your) favourable disposition towards mankind.”
Sukta 166.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तद्वो॑ जामि॒त्वं म॑रुत॒: परे॑ यु॒गे पु॒रू यच्छंस॑ममृतास॒ आव॑त । अ॒या धि॒या मन॑वे श्रु॒ष्टिमाव्या॑ सा॒कं नरो॑ दं॒सनै॒रा चि॑कित्रिरे

Sukta 166.translation: “Quick-movingMaruts, we augment the long (offered ceremony) upon your mighty (approach), whereby men triumph in war; may we obtain, by these our sacrifices, your wished-for (presence).”

Sukta 166.translation: “This praise,Maruts, is for you; this hymn is for you; (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring (by his laudations); may the praise reach you (for the good of your) person ns, so that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.”

Sukta 167.translation: “May your thousand benefits,Indra, come to us; may a thousand kinds of abundant food come to us, lord of horses; may a thousand (sorts of wealth) come to exhilarate us; may thousands of horses be ours.”

Sukta 167.translation: “May theMarutscome to our presence with benefaction; may they who are possessed of knowledge (come) with most excellent and brilliant (treasures), since their glorious horses, theNiyutas, gather wealth even on the farther shore of the sea.”

Sukta 167.translation: “The radiant, ever-movingMaruts, have mingled with (their) associate, (lightning), like (youths) with common women; the formidable divinities do not overwhelm heaven and earth (with rain), but promote their prosperity through (friendly) regard.”

Sukta 167.translation: “Rodasī, the associate of the scatterers (of the clouds), with dishevelled tresses, and mind devoted to her lords, woos them to associate (with her); radiant in form, she has ascended the car of the restless (Maruts) asSūrya(ascended the car of theAśvins), and comes hither (with the celerity) of the sun.”

Sukta 167.translation: “I celebrate that greatness of theMaruts, which is true, and worthy of celebration, inasmuch as their high-minded,haughty, and ever-enduring (bride), supports a flourishing progeny.”

Sukta 167.translation: “MitraandVaruṇa, andAryaman, defend (this) sacrifice from (all that is) reprehensible, and destroy (all that are) unworthy. They cause the yet unfallen and showering (rains) to descend, when,Maruts, the water-yielding (season) gives increase to this (world).”

Sukta 167.translation: “None of us,Maruts, have attained, either nearly or remotely, the limit of your strength; those (Maruts), increasing in energy and vigour, overwhelm their enemies like an ocean.”

Sukta 167.translation: “Let us, who are beloved ofIndra, glorify him today; let us glorify him tomorrow, at the sacred rite; let us glorify him for our great (good), in future days as of old, so thatṚbhukṣinmay ever be favourable to us amongst men.”

Sukta 168.translation: “Maruts, at every sacrifice your alacrity is uniform; you, verily, discharge your every function for the benefit of the gods; therefore, do I invite you to come hither, by sacred hymns, for (the sake of) your powerful protection of heaven and earth, and your benevolent praise.”

Sukta 168.translation: “Mutually supported, they descend readily from the sky; immortalMaruts, animate us by your own words (to praise you); exempt from toil, present at many (sacrifices), brilliant-eyed, the Maruts ahve shaken the firmest mountains.”
Sukta 168.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव॒ स्वयु॑क्ता दि॒व आ वृथा॑ ययु॒रम॑र्त्या॒: कश॑या चोदत॒ त्मना॑ । अ॒रे॒णव॑स्तुविजा॒ता अ॑चुच्यवुर्दृ॒ळ्हानि॑ चिन्म॒रुतो॒ भ्राज॑दृष्टयः

transliteration.text: káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ṛṣṭi-vidyutaḥ ǀ réjati ǀ tmánā ǀ hánvā-iva ǀ jihváyā ǀdhanva-cyútaḥ ǀ iṣā́m ǀ ná ǀ yā́mani ǀ puru-práiṣāḥ ǀ ahanyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ étaśaḥ ǁ

Sukta 168.translation: “Maruts, lightning-armed, who, (standing) amongst you, sets you of yourselves in motion, as the jaws are (set in motion) by the tongue; as falling rains(are essential) for the obtaining of food, so (those, desirous of sustenance), excite you in various ways, like a horse in (his) daily (training).”

Sukta 168.translation: “Where,Maruts, is the limit of the vast region (whence you come); where is the beginning of that to which you proceed; when you scatter the dense vapour like light grass, and hurl down the brilliant rain-cloud by the thunderbolt.”
Sukta 168.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क्व॑ स्विद॒स्य रज॑सो म॒हस्परं॒ क्वाव॑रं मरुतो॒ यस्मि॑न्नाय॒य । यच्च्या॒वय॑थ विथु॒रेव॒ संहि॑तं॒ व्यद्रि॑णा पतथ त्वे॒षम॑र्ण॒वम्

Sukta 168.translation: “Like your possession of treasure,Maruts, is your liberality; ministerial (ofIndra's bounty), heaven-bestowing, brilliant, fruitful, favourable to the husbandman, propitious; it is like the donation of a wealthy (donor), prompt (of distribution), and like the all-subduing force of theasuras.”
Sukta 168.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सा॒तिर्न वोऽम॑वती॒ स्व॑र्वती त्वे॒षा विपा॑का मरुत॒: पिपि॑ष्वती । भ॒द्रा वो॑ रा॒तिः पृ॑ण॒तो न दक्षि॑णा पृथु॒ज्रयी॑ असु॒र्ये॑व॒ जञ्ज॑ती

devanagari.text: प्रति ष्टोभंति सिंधवः पविभ्यो यदभ्रियां वाचमुदीरयंति ।अव स्मयंत विद्युतः पृथिव्यां यदी घृतं मरुतः प्रुष्णुवंति ॥

transliteration.text: práti ǀ stobhanti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ paví-bhyaḥ ǀ yát ǀ abhríyām ǀ vā́cam ǀ ut-īráyanti ǀáva ǀ smayanta ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ yádi ǀ ghṛtám ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pruṣṇuvánti ǁ

Sukta 168.translation: “The rivers are arrested by the thunderbolts when they utter the voice of the clouds; but the lightnings smile in the firmament when theMarutssprinkle water on the earth.”
Sukta 168.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रति॑ ष्टोभन्ति॒ सिन्ध॑वः प॒विभ्यो॒ यद॒भ्रियां॒ वाच॑मुदी॒रय॑न्ति । अव॑ स्मयन्त वि॒द्युत॑: पृथि॒व्यां यदी॑ घृ॒तं म॒रुत॑: प्रुष्णु॒वन्ति॑

devanagari.text: असूत पृश्निर्महते रणाय त्वेषमयासां मरुतामनीकं ।ते सप्सरासोऽजनयंताभ्वमादित्स्वधामिषिरां पर्यपश्यन् ॥

transliteration.text: ásūta ǀ pṛ́śniḥ ǀ mahaté ǀ ráṇāya ǀ tveṣám ǀ ayā́sām ǀ marútām ǀ ánīkam ǀté ǀ sapsarā́saḥ ǀ ajanayanta ǀ ábhvam ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ svadhā́m ǀ iṣirā́m ǀ pári ǀ apaśyan ǁ

Sukta 168.translation: “Pṛśnibore the brilliant troop of the quick-movingMarutsfor the great combat (with the clouds), whereupon (mankind) immediately beheld the desiderated food.”
Sukta 168.sanskrit_wisdomlib: असू॑त॒ पृश्नि॑र्मह॒ते रणा॑य त्वे॒षम॒यासां॑ म॒रुता॒मनी॑कम् । ते स॑प्स॒रासो॑ऽजनय॒न्ताभ्व॒मादित्स्व॒धामि॑षि॒रां पर्य॑पश्यन्

Sukta 168.translation: “This praise,Maruts, is for you; this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations); may the praise reach you for (the good of your) person ns, so that we may thence obtain food, strength and long life.”
Sukta 168.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष व॒: स्तोमो॑ मरुत इ॒यं गीर्मा॑न्दा॒र्यस्य॑ मा॒न्यस्य॑ का॒रोः । एषा या॑सीष्ट त॒न्वे॑ व॒यां वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

Sukta 169.translation: “You,Indra, are mighty from the might of those of whom you are the protector against abandonment therefore, creator of theMaruts, favourably-minded towards us, grant us those blessings which are most dear to you.”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒हश्चि॒त्त्वमि॑न्द्र य॒त ए॒तान्म॒हश्चि॑दसि॒ त्यज॑सो वरू॒ता । स नो॑ वेधो म॒रुतां॑ चिकि॒त्वान्त्सु॒म्ना व॑नुष्व॒ तव॒ हि प्रेष्ठा॑

Sukta 169.translation: “Rulers over all men, and impelling towards man the water-shedding clouds, they are united,Indra, (with you); the host ofMarutsis delighted by (your) acquisition of heaven-bestowing wealth.”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अयु॑ज्रन्त इन्द्र वि॒श्वकृ॑ष्टीर्विदा॒नासो॑ नि॒ष्षिधो॑ मर्त्य॒त्रा । म॒रुतां॑ पृत्सु॒तिर्हास॑माना॒ स्व॑र्मीळ्हस्य प्र॒धन॑स्य सा॒तौ

Sukta 169.translation: “Your weapon,Indra, is athandfor our (good); theMarutssend down the long-accusative ulated rain;Agniis blazing for the ceremony; the oblations encompass him as the waters (surround) an island.”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अम्य॒क्सा त॑ इन्द्र ऋ॒ष्टिर॒स्मे सने॒म्यभ्वं॑ म॒रुतो॑ जुनन्ति । अ॒ग्निश्चि॒द्धि ष्मा॑त॒से शु॑शु॒क्वानापो॒ न द्वी॒पं दध॑ति॒ प्रयां॑सि

Sukta 169.translation: “Do you,Indra, quickly grant us that wealth (which you possess, for we gratify) the donor with a most worthy present; we, your praisers, offer to you, the ready giver of boons, the laudations that would propitiate you; (and the priests) nourish you with sacrificial food, as they cherish the bosom (of a feminine le for the sakeof replenishing it) with sweet (milk).”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं तू न॑ इन्द्र॒ तं र॒यिं दा॒ ओजि॑ष्ठया॒ दक्षि॑णयेव रा॒तिम् । स्तुत॑श्च॒ यास्ते॑ च॒कन॑न्त वा॒योः स्तनं॒ न मध्व॑: पीपयन्त॒ वाजै॑:

Sukta 169.translation: “Your riches,Indra, are most delighting; the exciters of any one desirous to sacrifice; may thoseMarutsbe propitious to us; the divine beings who were anxious to go first to the ceremony.”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वे राय॑ इन्द्र तो॒शत॑माः प्रणे॒तार॒: कस्य॑ चिदृता॒योः । ते षु णो॑ म॒रुतो॑ मृळयन्तु॒ ये स्मा॑ पु॒रा गा॑तू॒यन्ती॑व दे॒वाः

devanagari.text: प्रति प्र याहींद्र मीळ्हुषो नॄन्महः पार्थिवे सदने यतस्व ।अध यदेषां पृथुबुध्नास एतास्तीर्थे नार्यः पौंस्यानि तस्थुः ॥

Sukta 169.translation: “Go,Indra, to the mighty rain-shedding leaders (of the clouds), and exert yourself in (thine) aerial dwelling; for their broad-footed steeds stand (firm), like the manly energies of an enemy in the field of battle.”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रति॒ प्र या॑हीन्द्र मी॒ळ्हुषो॒ नॄन्म॒हः पार्थि॑वे॒ सद॑ने यतस्व । अध॒ यदे॑षां पृथुबु॒ध्नास॒ एता॑स्ती॒र्थे नार्यः पौंस्या॑नि त॒स्थुः

transliteration.text: práti ǀ ghorā́ṇām ǀ étānām ǀ ayā́sām ǀ marútām ǀ śṛṇve ǀ ā-yatā́m ǀ upabdíḥ ǀyé ǀ mártyam ǀ pṛtanā-yántam ǀ ū́maiḥ ǀ ṛṇa-vā́nam ǀ ná ǀ patáyanta ǀ sárgaiḥ ǁ

Sukta 169.translation: “The noise of the formidable, dark-coloured, swift-moving and advancingMaruts, is everywhere echoed; (the noise) of them who strike down their mortal (foes) gathering in a host against them, by their self-defending blows, as (they strike down) a contemptible enemy.”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रति॑ घो॒राणा॒मेता॑नाम॒यासां॑ म॒रुतां॑ शृण्व आय॒तामु॑प॒ब्दिः । ये मर्त्यं॑ पृतना॒यन्त॒मूमै॑ॠणा॒वानं॒ न प॒तय॑न्त॒ सर्गै॑:

devanagari.text: त्वं मानेभ्य इंद्र विश्वजन्या रदा मरुद्भिः शुरुधो गोअग्राः ।स्तवानेभिः स्तवसे देव देवैर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ mā́nebhyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ viśvá-janyā ǀ ráda ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ śurúdhaḥ ǀ gó-agrāḥ ǀstávānebhiḥ ǀ stavase ǀ deva ǀ deváiḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ

Sukta 169.translation: “Associated with theMaruts, do you,Indra, for your own honour and the good of all, pierce the exhilarating receptacles of the waters, for you, Indra, are glorified by the lauded divinities; may we obtain for you food, strength, and long life.”
Sukta 169.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं माने॑भ्य इन्द्र वि॒श्वज॑न्या॒ रदा॑ म॒रुद्भि॑: शु॒रुधो॒ गोअ॑ग्राः । स्तवा॑नेभिः स्तवसे देव दे॒वैर्वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

devanagari.text: न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतं ।अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं वि नश्यति ॥

Sukta 170.translation: “(Indraspeaks): It is not certain what today or what tomorrow will yield to us; who comprehends this mystery; verily, the mind of any other (being) is of an unsteady (nature), and even that which has been profoundly studied, is (in time) forgotten.”
Sukta 170.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न नू॒नमस्ति॒ नो श्वः कस्तद्वे॑द॒ यदद्भु॑तम् । अ॒न्यस्य॑ चि॒त्तम॒भि सं॑च॒रेण्य॑मु॒ताधी॑तं॒ वि न॑श्यति

devanagari.text: किं न इंद्र जिघांससि भ्रातरो मरुतस्तव ।तेभिः कल्पस्व साधुया मा नः समरणे वधीः ॥

transliteration.text: kím ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ jighāṃsasi ǀ bhrā́taraḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ táva ǀtébhiḥ ǀ kalpasva ǀ sādhu-yā́ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sam-áraṇe ǀ vadhīḥ ǁ

Sukta 170.translation: “(Agstya): Why,Indra, do you purpose to slay us; theMarutsare your brothers; share with them (the offering) in peace; destroy us not in enmity.”
Sukta 170.sanskrit_wisdomlib: किं न॑ इन्द्र जिघांससि॒ भ्रात॑रो म॒रुत॒स्तव॑ । तेभि॑: कल्पस्व साधु॒या मा न॑: स॒मर॑णे वधीः

devanagari.text: किं नो भ्रातरगस्त्य सखा सन्नति मन्यसे ।विद्मा हि ते यथा मनोऽस्मभ्यमिन्न दित्ससि ॥

Sukta 170.translation: “(Indra): Wherefore, brotherAgastya, do you, who are my friend, treat me with regard; verily, we know what is in your mind; you do not intend to give us anything.”
Sukta 170.sanskrit_wisdomlib: किं नो॑ भ्रातरगस्त्य॒ सखा॒ सन्नति॑ मन्यसे । वि॒द्मा हि ते॒ यथा॒ मनो॒ऽस्मभ्य॒मिन्न दि॑त्ससि

devanagari.text: अरं कृण्वंतु वेदिं समग्निमिंधतां पुरः ।तत्रामृतस्य चेतनं यज्ञं ते तनवावहै ॥

Sukta 170.translation: “(Agastya): Let the priests decorate the altar; let them kindle the fire to the east; and then let us both consummate the sacrifice, the inspirerof immortal (wisdom).”
Sukta 170.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अरं॑ कृण्वन्तु॒ वेदिं॒ सम॒ग्निमि॑न्धतां पु॒रः । तत्रा॒मृत॑स्य॒ चेत॑नं य॒ज्ञं ते॑ तनवावहै

devanagari.text: त्वमीशिषे वसुपते वसूनां त्वं मित्राणां मित्रपते धेष्ठः ।इंद्र त्वं मरुद्भिः सं वदस्वाध प्राशान ऋतुथा हवींषि ॥

Sukta 170.translation: “(Agastya); You, Vasupati, are the lord of riches; you, Mitrapati, are the firm stay (of us), your friends; declare,Indra, along with theMaruts, (your approval of our acts), and partake of the oblation offered in due season.”
Sukta 170.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वमी॑शिषे वसुपते॒ वसू॑नां॒ त्वं मि॒त्राणां॑ मित्रपते॒ धेष्ठ॑: । इन्द्र॒ त्वं म॒रुद्भि॒: सं व॑द॒स्वाध॒ प्राशा॑न ऋतु॒था ह॒वींषि॑

Sukta 171.translation: “I approach you,Maruts, with this reverential homage, and with a hymn implore your favour against eager (foes); with minds pacified by our praises, suppress your anger, and let loose your horses.”
Sukta 171.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रति॑ व ए॒ना नम॑सा॒हमे॑मि सू॒क्तेन॑ भिक्षे सुम॒तिं तु॒राणा॑म् । र॒रा॒णता॑ मरुतो वे॒द्याभि॒र्नि हेळो॑ ध॒त्त वि मु॑चध्व॒मश्वा॑न्

Sukta 171.translation: “This praise, accompanied by offerings,Maruts, is for you, offered from the heart; accept it, divinities, with favour, and come with willing minds (to receive) these (laudations), for you are the augmenters of sacrificial food.”
Sukta 171.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष व॒: स्तोमो॑ मरुतो॒ नम॑स्वान्हृ॒दा त॒ष्टो मन॑सा धायि देवाः । उपे॒मा या॑त॒ मन॑सा जुषा॒णा यू॒यं हि ष्ठा नम॑स॒ इद्वृ॒धास॑:

transliteration.text: stutā́saḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ mṛḷayantu ǀ utá ǀ stutáḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhaḥ ǀūrdhvā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ santu ǀ komyā́ ǀ vánāni ǀ áhāni ǀ víśvā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ jigīṣā́ ǁ

Sukta 171.translation: “May theMaruts, now hymned, bestow happiness upon us; mayMaghavan, now glorified, be propitious to us; Maruts, may all the ensuing days that may be expected by us prove gratifying and full of enjoyment.”
Sukta 171.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्तु॒तासो॑ नो म॒रुतो॑ मृळयन्तू॒त स्तु॒तो म॒घवा॒ शम्भ॑विष्ठः । ऊ॒र्ध्वा न॑: सन्तु को॒म्या वना॒न्यहा॑नि॒ विश्वा॑ मरुतो जिगी॒षा

devanagari.text: अस्मादहं तविषादीषमाण इंद्राद्भिया मरुतो रेजमानः ।युष्मभ्यं हव्या निशितान्यासन्तान्यारे चकृमा मृळता नः ॥

transliteration.text: asmā́t ǀ ahám ǀ taviṣā́t ǀ ī́ṣamāṇaḥ ǀ índrāt ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ réjamānaḥ ǀyuṣmábhyam ǀ havyā́ ǀ ní-śitāni ǀ āsan ǀ tā́ni ǀ āré ǀ cakṛma ǀ mṛḷáta ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 171.translation: “Maruts, through fear of that violentIndra, I fly, trembling, (from his presence); the oblations that had been prepared for you have been put away; nevertheless, have patience with us.”
Sukta 171.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्माद॒हं त॑वि॒षादीष॑माण॒ इन्द्रा॑द्भि॒या म॑रुतो॒ रेज॑मानः । यु॒ष्मभ्यं॑ ह॒व्या निशि॑तान्यास॒न्तान्या॒रे च॑कृमा मृ॒ळता॑ नः

Sukta 171.translation: “The rays of the ever-recurring mornings, favoured,Indra, by your vigour, confer consciousness as they shine; showerer of benefits, ancient (of days), bestower of strength, fierce, (and attended), by the fierceMaruts, grant us (abundant) food.”

Sukta 171.translation: “Do you,Indra, cherish the vigorous leaders (of the rains), be free from displeasure against theMaruts; overcoming (our) enemies along with the intelligent (Maruts), support us (so that) we may obtain food, strength, and long life.”

Sukta 172.translation: “Maruts, liberal benefactors, protect my people, (although I be) as insignificant as grass; lift us up, that we may live.”

Sukta 173.translation: “The priests chant the heaven-ascendingsāma, as you know (it), for such (praise) do we venerate as the cause of increase and conferrer of heaven, whence the kine, unimpeded, do honour to the divine (Indra), who is seated on the sacred grass.”

Sukta 173.translation: “The showerer (of the oblation, the offerer of the sacrifice, assisted) by (the priests), presenting the oblations which have been provided by himself, adores (Indra), in order that he may hasten (to the rite), as a (thirsty) deer to the water. The mortal invoker (of the gods), O mighty Indra, whilst glorifying them who are desirous of praise, presents a twofold offering (to you).”

Sukta 173.translation: “Those people, who, jointly worshippingIndra, diligently endeavour, O hero, to propitiate you, the invigorator in combats, the guide in the right way; provide, for his gratification, with sacrificial viands.”

devanagari.text: एवा हि ते शं सवना समुद्र आपो यत्त आसु मदंति देवीः ।विश्वा ते अनु जोष्या भूद्गौः सूरींश्चिद्यदि धिषा वेषि जनान् ॥

transliteration.text: evá ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ śám ǀ sávanā ǀ samudré ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ āsú ǀ mádanti ǀ devī́ḥ ǀvíśvā ǀ te ǀ ánu ǀ jóṣyā ǀ bhūt ǀ gáuḥ ǀ sūrī́n ǀ cit ǀ yádi ǀ dhiṣā́ ǀ véṣi ǀ jánān ǁ

Sukta 173.translation: “The libations (offered) to you are, verily, the cause of happiness, since the divine waters (effused) in the firmament for the benefit of mankind afford you satisfaction. All praise,Indra, is acceptable to you, and you reward with understanding those who praise you.”
Sukta 173.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा हि ते॒ शं सव॑ना समु॒द्र आपो॒ यत्त॑ आ॒सु मद॑न्ति दे॒वीः । विश्वा॑ ते॒ अनु॒ जोष्या॑ भू॒द्गौः सू॒रीँश्चि॒द्यदि॑ धि॒षा वेषि॒ जना॑न्

devanagari.text: असाम यथा सुषखाय एन स्वभिष्टयो नरां न शंसैः ।असद्यथा न इंद्रो वंदनेष्ठास्तुरो न कर्म नयमान उक्था ॥
असाम । यथा । सुऽसखायः । एन । सुऽअभिष्टयः । नराम् । न । शंसैः ।असत् । यथा । नः । इन्द्रः । वन्दनेऽस्थाः । तुरः । न । कर्म । नयमानः । उक्था ॥

transliteration.text: ásāma ǀ yáthā ǀ su-sakhā́yaḥ ǀ ena ǀ su-abhiṣṭáyaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ ná ǀ śáṃsaiḥ ǀásat ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vandane-sthā́ḥ ǀ turáḥ ǀ ná ǀ kárma ǀ náyamānaḥ ǀ ukthā́ ǁ

Sukta 173.translation: “May we be, as it were, your valued friends, O Lord, and obtain our desires, like those (who gain their objects) by the praise of princes. MayIndra, propitiated by our eulogies, be brought to the sacrifice by our hymns.”
Sukta 173.sanskrit_wisdomlib: असा॑म॒ यथा॑ सुष॒खाय॑ एन स्वभि॒ष्टयो॑ न॒रां न शंसै॑: । अस॒द्यथा॑ न॒ इन्द्रो॑ वन्दने॒ष्ठास्तु॒रो न कर्म॒ नय॑मान उ॒क्था

devanagari.text: विष्पर्धसो नरां न शंसैरस्माकासदिंद्रो वज्रहस्तः ।मित्रायुवो न पूर्पतिं सुशिष्टौ मध्यायुव उप शिक्षंति यज्ञैः ॥
विऽस्पर्धसः । नराम् । न । शंसैः । अस्माक । असत् । इन्द्रः । वज्रऽहस्तः ।मित्रऽयुवः । न । पूःऽपतिम् । सुऽशिष्टौ । मध्यऽयुवः । उप । शिक्षन्ति । यज्ञैः ॥

transliteration.text: ví-spardhasaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ ná ǀ śáṃsaiḥ ǀ asmā́ka ǀ asat ǀ índraḥ ǀ vájra-hastaḥ ǀmitra-yúvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pū́ḥ-patim ǀ sú-śiṣṭau ǀ madhya-yúvaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ śikṣanti ǀ yajñáiḥ ǁ

Sukta 173.translation: “Emulous in commendation, like (those contending for the favour) of men, mayIndra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, be equally (a friend) to us; like those who, desirous of his friendship, (conciliate) the lord of a city (ruling) with good government, so do our intermediate (representatives) propitiate (Indra) with sacrifices.”
Sukta 173.sanskrit_wisdomlib: विष्प॑र्धसो न॒रां न शंसै॑र॒स्माका॑स॒दिन्द्रो॒ वज्र॑हस्तः । मि॒त्रा॒युवो॒ न पूर्प॑तिं॒ सुशि॑ष्टौ मध्या॒युव॒ उप॑ शिक्षन्ति य॒ज्ञैः

devanagari.text: यज्ञो हि ष्मेंद्रं कश्चिदृंधञ्जुहुराणश्चिन्मनसा परियन् ।तीर्थे नाच्छा तातृषाणमोको दीर्घो न सिध्रमा कृणोत्यध्वा ॥
यज्ञः । हि । स्म । इन्द्रम् । कः । चित् । ऋन्धन् । जुहुराणः । चित् । मनसा । परिऽयन् ।तीर्थे । न । अच्छ । ततृषाणम् । ओकः । दीर्घः । न । सिध्रम् । आ । कृणोति । अध्वा ॥

transliteration.text: yajñáḥ ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ índram ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ ṛndhán ǀ juhurāṇáḥ ǀ cit ǀ mánasā ǀ pari-yán ǀtīrthé ǀ ná ǀ áccha ǀ tatṛṣāṇám ǀ ókaḥ ǀ dīrgháḥ ǀ ná ǀ sidhrám ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ ádhvā ǁ

Sukta 173.translation: “One man propitiatesIndra, augmenting (his vigour) by sacrifice; another, who is insincere, worships (him), with mind averted, (to worldly thoughts); (to the first he is) like a lake to a thirsty (pilgrim) near a sacred spot; (to the other) like a long road, which retards the end (of the journey).”
Sukta 173.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य॒ज्ञो हि ष्मेन्द्रं॒ कश्चि॑दृ॒न्धञ्जु॑हुरा॒णश्चि॒न्मन॑सा परि॒यन् । ती॒र्थे नाच्छा॑ तातृषा॒णमोको॑ दी॒र्घो न सि॒ध्रमा कृ॑णो॒त्यध्वा॑

devanagari.text: मो षू ण इंद्रात्र पृत्सु देवैरस्ति हि ष्मा ते शुष्मिन्नवयाः ।महश्चिद्यस्य मीळ्हुषो यव्या हविष्मतो मरुतो वंदते गीः ॥
मो इति । सु । नः । इन्द्र । अत्र । पृत्ऽसु । देवैः । अस्ति । हि । स्म । ते । शुष्मिन् । अवऽयाः ।महः । चित् । यस्य । मीळ्हुषः । यव्या । हविष्मतः । मरुतः । वन्दते । गीः ॥

transliteration.text: mó íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ átra ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ deváiḥ ǀ ásti ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ te ǀ śuṣmin ǀ ava-yā́ḥ ǀmaháḥ ǀ cit ǀ yásya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀ yavyā́ ǀ havíṣmataḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ vándate ǀ gī́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 173.translation: “Indra, associated with theMarutsin battles (with the clouds), abandon us not; for a share of the offering is set apart, mighty one, for you, for whom, the shedder of rain and accepter of oblations, the worship is offered with oblations, whilst the hymn glorifies the Marutṣ ”
Sukta 173.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मो षू ण॑ इ॒न्द्रात्र॑ पृ॒त्सु दे॒वैरस्ति॒ हि ष्मा॑ ते शुष्मिन्नव॒याः । म॒हश्चि॒द्यस्य॑ मी॒ळ्हुषो॑ य॒व्या ह॒विष्म॑तो म॒रुतो॒ वन्द॑ते॒ गीः

devanagari.text: एष स्तोम इंद्र तुभ्यमस्मे एतेन गातुं हरिवो विदो नः ।आ नो ववृत्याः सुविताय देव विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
एषः । स्तोमः । इन्द्र । तुभ्यम् । अस्मे इति । एतेन । गातुम् । हरिऽवः । विदः । नः ।आ । नः । ववृत्याः । सुविताय । देव । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ indra ǀ túbhyam ǀ asmé íti ǀ eténa ǀ gātúm ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ vidaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vavṛtyāḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ deva ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ

Sukta 173.translation: “This hymn,Indra, is addressed to you. Lord of steeds, learn by it the way to our sacrifice, and come hither for our good, that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.”
Sukta 173.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष स्तोम॑ इन्द्र॒ तुभ्य॑म॒स्मे ए॒तेन॑ गा॒तुं ह॑रिवो विदो नः । आ नो॑ ववृत्याः सुवि॒ताय॑ देव वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

devanagari.text: त्वं राजेंद्र ये च देवा रक्षा नॄन्पाह्यसुर त्वमस्मान् ।त्वं सत्पतिर्मघवा नस्तरुत्रस्त्वं सत्यो वसवानः सहोदाः ॥
त्वम् । राजा । इन्द्र । ये । च । देवाः । रक्ष । नॄन् । पाहि । असुर । त्वम् । अस्मान् ।त्वम् । सत्ऽपतिः । मघऽवा । नः । तरुत्रः । त्वम् । सत्यः । वसवानः । सहःऽदाः ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ rā́jā ǀ indra ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ rákṣa ǀ nṝ́n ǀ pāhí ǀ asura ǀ tvám ǀ asmā́n ǀtvám ǀ sát-patiḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ naḥ ǀ tárutraḥ ǀ tvám ǀ satyáḥ ǀ vásavānaḥ ǀ sahaḥ-dā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “You,Indra, are king; they who are gods (are subject) to you; therefore, scatterer (of foes), do you protect and cherish us men; you are the protector of the good, the possessor of wealth, the extricator of us (from sin); you are true, the invester (of all with your lustre) the giver of strength.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं राजे॑न्द्र॒ ये च॑ दे॒वा रक्षा॒ नॄन्पा॒ह्य॑सुर॒ त्वम॒स्मान् । त्वं सत्प॑तिर्म॒घवा॑ न॒स्तरु॑त्र॒स्त्वं स॒त्यो वस॑वानः सहो॒दाः

devanagari.text: दनो विश इंद्र मृध्रवाचः सप्त यत्पुरः शर्म शारदीर्दर्त् ।ऋणोरपो अनवद्यार्णा यूने वृत्रं पुरुकुत्साय रंधीः ॥
दनः । विशः । इन्द्र । मृध्रऽवाचः । सप्त । यत् । पुरः । शर्म । शारदीः । दर्त् ।ऋणोः । अपः । अनवद्य । अर्णाः । यूने । वृत्रम् । पुरुऽकुत्साय । रन्धीः ॥

transliteration.text: dánaḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ indra ǀ mṛdhrá-vācaḥ ǀ saptá ǀ yát ǀ púraḥ ǀ śárma ǀ śā́radīḥ ǀ dárt ǀṛṇóḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ anavadya ǀ árṇāḥ ǀ yū́ne ǀ vṛtrám ǀ puru-kútsāya ǀ randhīḥ ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “You have humbled the people, suing for pardon when you have destroyed their seven new cities; you the irrproachable have dispersed the flowing waters; you have destroyedVṛtrafor the sake of the youthfulPurukutsa.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दनो॒ विश॑ इन्द्र मृ॒ध्रवा॑चः स॒प्त यत्पुर॒: शर्म॒ शार॑दी॒र्दर्त् । ऋ॒णोर॒पो अ॑नव॒द्यार्णा॒ यूने॑ वृ॒त्रं पु॑रु॒कुत्सा॑य रन्धीः

devanagari.text: अजा वृत इंद्र शूरपत्नीर्द्यां च येभिः पुरुहूत नूनं ।रक्षो अग्निमशुषं तूर्वयाणं सिंहो न दमे अपांसि वस्तोः ॥
अज । वृतः । इन्द्र । शूरऽपत्नीः । द्याम् । च । येभिः । पुरुऽहूत । नूनम् ।रक्षो इति । अग्निम् । अशुषम् । तूर्वयाणम् । सिंहः । न । दमे । अपांसि । वस्तोः ॥

transliteration.text: ája ǀ vṛ́taḥ ǀ indra ǀ śū́ra-patnīḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ ca ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ puru-hūta ǀ nūnám ǀrákṣo íti ǀ agním ǀ aśúṣam ǀ tū́rvayāṇam ǀ siṃháḥ ǀ ná ǀ dáme ǀ ápāṃsi ǀ vástoḥ ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “Go the cities inhabited by therākṣasas, and thence to heaven (attended), receiver of many sacrifices by those who (attend you). Defend, like a lion, the untamed, quick-movingAgni, that he may abide in his dwelling, fulfilling his functions.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अजा॒ वृत॑ इन्द्र॒ शूर॑पत्नी॒र्द्यां च॒ येभि॑: पुरुहूत नू॒नम् । रक्षो॑ अ॒ग्निम॒शुषं॒ तूर्व॑याणं सिं॒हो न दमे॒ अपां॑सि॒ वस्तो॑:

devanagari.text: शेषन्नु त इंद्र सस्मिन्योनौ प्रशस्तये पवीरवस्य मह्ना ।सृजदर्णांस्यव यद्युधा गास्तिष्ठद्धरी धृषता मृष्ट वाजान् ॥
शेषन् । नु । ते । इन्द्र । सस्मिन् । योनौ । प्रऽशस्तये । पवीरवस्य । मह्ना ।सृजत् । अर्णांसि । अव । यत् । युधा । गाः । तिष्ठत् । हरी इति । धृषता । मृष्ट । वाजान् ॥

transliteration.text: śéṣan ǀ nú ǀ té ǀ indra ǀ sásmin ǀ yónau ǀ prá-śastaye ǀ pávīravasya ǀ mahnā́ ǀsṛját ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ áva ǀ yát ǀ yudhā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ tíṣṭhat ǀ hárī íti ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ mṛṣṭa ǀ vā́jān ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “Let (your foes,Indra), humbled by the might of your thunderbolt rest in their own station, for your glory; when you move, (armed) with your weapons, you send down the waters; arresting your horses, increase, by your power, (the abundance of) food.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शेष॒न्नु त इ॑न्द्र॒ सस्मि॒न्योनौ॒ प्रश॑स्तये॒ पवी॑रवस्य म॒ह्ना । सृ॒जदर्णां॒स्यव॒ यद्यु॒धा गास्तिष्ठ॒द्धरी॑ धृष॒ता मृ॑ष्ट॒ वाजा॑न्

devanagari.text: वह कुत्समिंद्र यस्मिञ्चाकन्त्स्यूमन्यू ऋज्रा वातस्याश्वा ।प्र सूरश्चक्रं वृहतादभीकेऽभि स्पृधो यासिषद्वज्रबाहुः ॥
वह । कुत्सम् । इन्द्र । यस्मिन् । चाकन् । स्यूमन्यू इति । ऋज्रा । वातस्य । अश्वा ।प्र । सूरः । चक्रम् । वृहतात् । अभीके । अभि । स्पृधः । यासिषत् । वज्रऽबाहुः ॥

transliteration.text: váha ǀ kútsam ǀ indra ǀ yásmin ǀ cākán ǀ syūmanyū́ íti ǀ ṛjrā́ ǀ vā́tasya ǀ áśvā ǀprá ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ vṛhatāt ǀ abhī́ke ǀ abhí ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ yāsiṣat ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “Bear,Indra, with your obedient horses, as swift as the wind, (the sage)Kutsa, to that ceremony (to which) you desire (to convey him); let the sun bring near the wheel of his chariot, and let the thunder-armed advance against his opponents.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वह॒ कुत्स॑मिन्द्र॒ यस्मि॑ञ्चा॒कन्त्स्यू॑म॒न्यू ऋ॒ज्रा वात॒स्याश्वा॑ । प्र सूर॑श्च॒क्रं वृ॑हताद॒भीके॒ऽभि स्पृधो॑ यासिष॒द्वज्र॑बाहुः

devanagari.text: जघन्वाँ इंद्र मित्रेरूञ्चोदप्रवृद्धो हरिवो अदाशून् ।प्र ये पश्यन्नर्यमणं सचायोस्त्वया शूर्ता वहमाना अपत्यं ॥
जघन्वान् । इन्द्र । मित्रेरून् । चोदऽप्रवृद्धः । हरिऽवः । अदाशून् ।प्र । ये । पश्यन् । अर्यमणम् । सचा । आयोः । त्वया । शूर्ताः । वहमानाः । अपत्यम् ॥

transliteration.text: jaghanvā́n ǀ indra ǀ mitrérūn ǀ codá-pravṛddhaḥ ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ ádāśūn ǀprá ǀ yé ǀ páśyan ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ sácā ǀ āyóḥ ǀ tváyā ǀ śūrtā́ḥ ǀ váhamānāḥ ǀ ápatyam ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “Indra, lord of steeds, invigorated by our animating praise, you have slain those who make you no offerings and disturb your worshippers; but they who look upon you as (their) protector, and are associated for (the presentation of sacrificial) food, obtain from the posterity.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ज॒घ॒न्वाँ इ॑न्द्र मि॒त्रेरू॑ञ्चो॒दप्र॑वृद्धो हरिवो॒ अदा॑शून् । प्र ये पश्य॑न्नर्य॒मणं॒ सचा॒योस्त्वया॑ शू॒र्ता वह॑माना॒ अप॑त्यम्

devanagari.text: रपत्कविरिंद्रार्कसातौ क्षां दासायोपबर्हणीं कः ।करत्तिस्रो मघवा दानुचित्रा नि दुर्योणे कुयवाचं मृधि श्रेत् ॥
रपत् । कविः । इन्द्र । अर्कऽसातौ । क्षाम् । दासाय । उपऽबर्हणीम् । करिति कः ।करत् । तिस्रः । मघऽवा । दानुऽचित्राः । नि । दुर्योणे । कुयवाचम् । मृधि । श्रेत् ॥

transliteration.text: rápat ǀ kavíḥ ǀ indra ǀ arká-sātau ǀ kṣā́m ǀ dāsā́ya ǀ upa-bárhaṇīm ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀkárat ǀ tisráḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ dā́nu-citrāḥ ǀ ní ǀ duryoṇé ǀ kúyavācam ǀ mṛdhí ǀ śret ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “The sage praises you,Indra, for the grant of desirable (food), since you have made the earth the bed of theasura;Maghavanhas made the three (regions) marvellous by his gifts, and has destroyed for (the prince) Duryoṇi (the asura), Kuyavāca, in combat.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रप॑त्क॒विरि॑न्द्रा॒र्कसा॑तौ॒ क्षां दा॒सायो॑प॒बर्ह॑णीं कः । कर॑त्ति॒स्रो म॒घवा॒ दानु॑चित्रा॒ नि दु॑र्यो॒णे कुय॑वाचं मृ॒धि श्रे॑त्

devanagari.text: सना ता त इंद्र नव्या आगुः सहो नभोऽविरणाय पूर्वीः ।भिनत्पुरो न भिदो अदेवीर्ननमो वधरदेवस्य पीयोः ॥
सना । ता । ते । इन्द्र । नव्याः । आ । अगुः । सहः । नभः । अविऽरणाय । पूर्वीः ।भिनत् । पुरः । न । भिदः । अदेवीः । ननमः । वधः । अदेवस्य । पीयोः ॥

transliteration.text: sánā ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ návyāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aguḥ ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ nábhaḥ ǀ ávi-raṇāya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀbhinát ǀ púraḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhídaḥ ǀ ádevīḥ ǀ nanámaḥ ǀ vádhaḥ ǀ ádevasya ǀ pīyóḥ ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “The sages have celebrated your everlasting (as well as your) recent (exploits, in achieving which) you have endured many injuries in putting an end to war; verily, you have demolished hostile and undivine cities; you have bowed down the thunderbolt of the undivineasura.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सना॒ ता त॑ इन्द्र॒ नव्या॒ आगु॒: सहो॒ नभोऽवि॑रणाय पू॒र्वीः । भि॒नत्पुरो॒ न भिदो॒ अदे॑वीर्न॒नमो॒ वध॒रदे॑वस्य पी॒योः

devanagari.text: त्वं धुनिरिंद्र धुनिमतीर्ऋणोरपः सीरा न स्रवंतीः ।प्र यत्समुद्रमति शूर पर्षि पारया तुर्वशं यदुं स्वस्ति ॥
त्वम् । धुनिः । इन्द्र । धुनिऽमतीः । ऋणोः । अपः । सीराः । न । स्रवन्तीः ।प्र । यत् । समुद्रम् । अति । शूर । पर्षि । पारय । तुर्वशम् । यदुम् । स्वस्ति ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ dhúniḥ ǀ indra ǀ dhúni-matīḥ ǀ ṛṇóḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ sīrā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ srávantīḥ ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ samudrám ǀ áti ǀ śūra ǀ párṣi ǀ pāráya ǀ turváśam ǀ yádum ǀ svastí ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “You,Indra, are the terrifier (of your foes); you have made the trembling waters overspread (the earth) like flowing rivers; but, hero, when you fill the ocean you have protected in their well-beingTurvaśaandYadu.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं धुनि॑रिन्द्र॒ धुनि॑मतीॠ॒णोर॒पः सी॒रा न स्रव॑न्तीः । प्र यत्स॑मु॒द्रमति॑ शूर॒ पर्षि॑ पा॒रया॑ तु॒र्वशं॒ यदुं॑ स्व॒स्ति

devanagari.text: त्वमस्माकमिंद्र विश्वध स्या अवृकतमो नरां नृपाता ।स नो विश्वासां स्पृधां सहोदा विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
त्वम् । अस्माकम् । इन्द्र । विश्वध । स्याः । अवृकऽतमः । नराम् । नृऽपाता ।सः । नः । विश्वासाम् । स्पृधाम् । सहःऽदाः । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ indra ǀ viśvádha ǀ syāḥ ǀ avṛká-tamaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ nṛ-pātā́ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvāsām ǀ spṛdhā́m ǀ sahaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ

Sukta 174.translation: “Be you,Indra, at all times our especial defender; the preserver of our people, the bestower of strength upon all these our emulous (followers); that we may obtain food, strength, and long life.”
Sukta 174.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वम॒स्माक॑मिन्द्र वि॒श्वध॑ स्या अवृ॒कत॑मो न॒रां नृ॑पा॒ता । स नो॒ विश्वा॑सां स्पृ॒धां स॑हो॒दा वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

devanagari.text: मत्स्यपायि ते महः पात्रस्येव हरिवो मत्सरो मदः ।वृषा ते वृष्ण इंदुर्वाजी सहस्रसातमः ॥
मत्सि । अपायि । ते । महः । पात्रस्यऽइव । हरिऽवः । मत्सरः । मदः ।वृषा । ते । वृष्णे । इन्दुः । वाजी । सहस्रऽसातमः ॥

transliteration.text: mátsi ǀ ápāyi ǀ te ǀ máhaḥ ǀ pā́trasya-iva ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ matsaráḥ ǀ mádaḥ ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ te ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ índuḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ sahasra-sā́tamaḥ ǁ

Sukta 175.translation: “Lord of steeds, you are exhilarated when the sacred (Soma) has been imbibed by you as by its (appropriate) vessel; for to you, showerer (of benefits), it is exhilarating, inebriating, invigorating, the yielder of delight, (satisfying as) food, and the giver of a thousand (plural asures).”
Sukta 175.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मत्स्यपा॑यि ते॒ मह॒: पात्र॑स्येव हरिवो मत्स॒रो मद॑: । वृषा॑ ते॒ वृष्ण॒ इन्दु॑र्वा॒जी स॑हस्र॒सात॑मः

devanagari.text: आ नस्ते गंतु मत्सरो वृषा मदो वरेण्यः ।सहावाँ इंद्र सानसिः पृतनाषाळमर्त्यः ॥
आ । नः । ते । गन्तु । मत्सरः । वृषा । मदः । वरेण्यः ।सहऽवान् । इन्द्र । सानसिः । पृतनाषाट् । अमर्त्यः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ te ǀ gantu ǀ matsaráḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ mádaḥ ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀsahá-vān ǀ indra ǀ sānasíḥ ǀ pṛtanāṣā́ṭ ǀ ámartyaḥ ǁ

Sukta 175.translation: “May oursomalibation reach you, (for it is) exhilarating, invigorating, inebriating, most precious; it is companionable,Indra, enjoyable, the over-thrower of hosts, immortal.”
Sukta 175.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ न॑स्ते गन्तु मत्स॒रो वृषा॒ मदो॒ वरे॑ण्यः । स॒हावाँ॑ इन्द्र सान॒सिः पृ॑तना॒षाळम॑र्त्यः

devanagari.text: त्वं हि शूरः सनिता चोदयो मनुषो रथं ।सहावान्दस्युमव्रतमोषः पात्रं न शोचिषा ॥
त्वम् । हि । शूरः । सनिता । चोदयः । मनुषः । रथम् ।सहऽवान् । दस्युम् । अव्रतम् । ओषः । पात्रम् । न । शोचिषा ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ hí ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ sánitā ǀ codáyaḥ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ rátham ǀsahá-vān ǀ dásyum ǀ avratám ǀ óṣaḥ ǀ pā́tram ǀ ná ǀ śocíṣā ǁ

Sukta 175.translation: “You are a hero, a benefactor, accelerate the vehicle of man (that bears him to heaven); consume, mightyone, the irreligiousDasyu, as a (woode) vessel is burnt by fire.”
Sukta 175.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं हि शूर॒: सनि॑ता चो॒दयो॒ मनु॑षो॒ रथ॑म् । स॒हावा॒न्दस्यु॑मव्र॒तमोष॒: पात्रं॒ न शो॒चिषा॑

devanagari.text: मुषाय सूर्यं कवे चक्रमीशान ओजसा ।वह शुष्णाय वधं कुत्सं वातस्याश्वैः ॥
मुषाय । सूर्यम् । कवे । चक्रम् । ईशानः । ओजसा ।वह । शुष्णाय । वधम् । कुत्सम् । वातस्य । अश्वैः ॥

transliteration.text: muṣāyá ǀ sū́ryam ǀ kave ǀ cakrám ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ ójasā ǀváha ǀ śúṣṇāya ǀ vadhám ǀ kútsam ǀ vā́tasya ǀ áśvaiḥ ǁ

Sukta 175.translation: “SageIndra, who are the lord, you have carried off by your strength one wheel of (the chariot of) the sun. Take up your bolt for the death ofŚuṣṇa, and proceed with your horses, swift as the wind, toKutsa.”
Sukta 175.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मु॒षा॒य सूर्यं॑ कवे च॒क्रमीशा॑न॒ ओज॑सा । वह॒ शुष्णा॑य व॒धं कुत्सं॒ वात॒स्याश्वै॑:

devanagari.text: शुष्मिंतमो हि ते मदो द्युम्निंतम उत क्रतुः ।वृत्रघ्ना वरिवोविदा मंसीष्ठा अश्वसातमः ॥
शुष्मिन्ऽतमः । हि । ते । मदः । द्युम्निन्ऽतमः । उत । क्रतुः ।वृत्रऽघ्ना । वरिवःऽविदा । मंसीष्ठाः । अश्वऽसातमः ॥

transliteration.text: śuṣmín-tamaḥ ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ mádaḥ ǀ dyumnín-tamaḥ ǀ utá ǀ krátuḥ ǀvṛtra-ghnā́ ǀ varivaḥ-vídā ǀ maṃsīṣṭhā́ḥ ǀ aśva-sā́tamaḥ ǁ

Sukta 175.translation: “Your inebriety is most intense; nevertheless, your acts (for our good) are most beneficent. You desire, bountiful giver of horses, that (both your inebriety and your beneficence should be the means of) destroying enemies and distributing riches.”
Sukta 175.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शु॒ष्मिन्त॑मो॒ हि ते॒ मदो॑ द्यु॒म्निन्त॑म उ॒त क्रतु॑: । वृ॒त्र॒घ्ना व॑रिवो॒विदा॑ मंसी॒ष्ठा अ॑श्व॒सात॑मः

devanagari.text: यथा पूर्वेभ्यो जरितृभ्य इंद्र मय इवापो न तृष्यते बभूथ ।तामनु त्वा निविदं जोहवीमि विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
यथा । पूर्वेभ्यः । जरितृऽभ्यः । इन्द्र । मयःऽइव । आपः । न । तृष्यते । बभूथ ।ताम् । अनु । त्वा । निऽविदम् । जोहवीमि । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥

transliteration.text: yáthā ǀ pū́rvebhyaḥ ǀ jaritṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ máyaḥ-iva ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ tṛ́ṣyate ǀ babhū́tha ǀtā́m ǀ ánu ǀ tvā ǀ ni-vídam ǀ johavīmi ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ

Sukta 175.translation: “InasmuchIndra, as you have been the (giver of) happiness to your ancient encomiasts, like water to one who is thirsty, therefore I constantly repeat this your praise, that I may thence obtain food, strength and long life.”
Sukta 175.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यथा॒ पूर्वे॑भ्यो जरि॒तृभ्य॑ इन्द्र॒ मय॑ इ॒वापो॒ न तृष्य॑ते ब॒भूथ॑ । तामनु॑ त्वा नि॒विदं॑ जोहवीमि वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

devanagari.text: मत्सि नो वस्यइष्टय इंद्रमिंदो वृषा विश ।ऋघायमाण इन्वसि शत्रुमंति न विंदसि ॥
मत्सि । नः । वस्यःऽइष्टये । इन्द्रम् । इन्दो इति । वृषा । आ । विश ।ऋघायमाणः । इन्वसि । शत्रुम् । अन्ति । न । विन्दसि ॥

transliteration.text: mátsi ǀ naḥ ǀ vásyaḥ-iṣṭaye ǀ índram ǀ indo íti ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ ā́ ǀ viśa ǀṛghāyámāṇaḥ ǀ invasi ǀ śátrum ǀ ánti ǀ ná ǀ vindasi ǁ

Sukta 176.translation: “Soma, exhilarateIndra(at the sacrifice we offer), for the sake of obtaining wealth; pervade him, showerer (ofbenefits), for when imbibed you are the annihilator (of enemies), and suffer not a foe to be nigh.”
Sukta 176.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मत्सि॑ नो॒ वस्य॑इष्टय॒ इन्द्र॑मिन्दो॒ वृषा वि॑श । ऋ॒घा॒यमा॑ण इन्वसि॒ शत्रु॒मन्ति॒ न वि॑न्दसि

devanagari.text: तस्मिन्ना वेशया गिरो य एकश्चर्षणीनां ।अनु स्वधा यमुप्यते यवं न चर्कृषद्वृषा ॥
तस्मिन् । आ । वेशय । गिरः । यः । एकः । चर्षणीनाम् ।अनु । स्वधा । यम् । उप्यते । यवम् । न । चर्कृषत् । वृषा ॥

transliteration.text: tásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ veśaya ǀ gíraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀánu ǀ svadhā́ ǀ yám ǀ upyáte ǀ yávam ǀ ná ǀ cárkṛṣat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǁ

Sukta 176.translation: “Pervade with our praise him who is the sole sustainer of men, to whom the oblation is presented and who, the showerer (of benefits), causes (every desire) to bud like barley.”
Sukta 176.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तस्मि॒न्ना वे॑शया॒ गिरो॒ य एक॑श्चर्षणी॒नाम् । अनु॑ स्व॒धा यमु॒प्यते॒ यवं॒ न चर्कृ॑ष॒द्वृषा॑

devanagari.text: यस्य विश्वानि हस्तयोः पंच क्षितीनां वसु ।स्पाशयस्व यो अस्मध्रुग्दिव्येवाशनिर्जहि ॥

Sukta 176.translation: “In whosehands are all the treasures (that are desired by) the five classes of beings; destroy,Indra, him who oppresses us; slay him, (as if you were yourself) the heavenly thunderbolt.”
Sukta 176.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्य॒ विश्वा॑नि॒ हस्त॑यो॒: पञ्च॑ क्षिती॒नां वसु॑ । स्पा॒शय॑स्व॒ यो अ॑स्म॒ध्रुग्दि॒व्येवा॒शनि॑र्जहि

devanagari.text: असुन्वंतं समं जहि दूणाशं यो न ते मयः ।अस्मभ्यमस्य वेदनं दद्धि सूरिश्चिदोहते ॥

Sukta 176.translation: “Slay every one who offers not libations, however difficult to be destroyed; slay every one who is no delight to you; bestow upon us his wealth, for the pious (worshipper) deserves it.”
Sukta 176.sanskrit_wisdomlib: असु॑न्वन्तं समं जहि दू॒णाशं॒ यो न ते॒ मय॑: । अ॒स्मभ्य॑मस्य॒ वेद॑नं द॒द्धि सू॒रिश्चि॑दोहते

devanagari.text: आवो यस्य द्विबर्हसोऽर्केषु सानुषगसत् ।आजाविंद्रस्येंदो प्रावो वाजेषु वाजिनं ॥

Sukta 176.translation: “Soma, you protect him in whose prayers, doubly devout, there is the combination (of praise and oblation); protect, especially,Indrain war; protect the vigorous Indra in battles.”
Sukta 176.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आवो॒ यस्य॑ द्वि॒बर्ह॑सो॒ऽर्केषु॑ सानु॒षगस॑त् । आ॒जाविन्द्र॑स्येन्दो॒ प्रावो॒ वाजे॑षु वा॒जिन॑म्

Sukta 176.translation: “InasmuchIndra, as you have been the giver of happiness to your ancient encomiasts, like water to one who is thirsty, therefore I constantly repeat this your praise, that I may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.”
Sukta 176.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यथा॒ पूर्वे॑भ्यो जरि॒तृभ्य॑ इन्द्र॒ मय॑ इ॒वापो॒ न तृष्य॑ते ब॒भूथ॑ । तामनु॑ त्वा नि॒विदं॑ जोहवीमि वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

devanagari.text: आ चर्षणिप्रा वृषभो जनानां राजा कृष्टीनां पुरुहूत इंद्रः ।स्तुतः श्रवस्यन्नवसोप मद्रिग्युक्त्वा हरी वृषणा याह्यर्वाङ् ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ carṣaṇi-prā́ḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ rā́jā ǀ kṛṣṭīnā́m ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀstutáḥ ǀ śravasyán ǀ ávasā ǀ úpa ǀ madrík ǀ yuktvā́ ǀ hárī íti ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǁ

Sukta 177.translation: “MayIndra, who is the cherisher of men, the benefactor of mankind,t he lord of men, the adored of many, (come to us), Indra, who are praised (by us), and are desirous of the oblation, harness your vigorous steeds, and come down to me for (my preservation).”
Sukta 177.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ च॑र्षणि॒प्रा वृ॑ष॒भो जना॑नां॒ राजा॑ कृष्टी॒नां पु॑रुहू॒त इन्द्र॑: । स्तु॒तः श्र॑व॒स्यन्नव॒सोप॑ म॒द्रिग्यु॒क्त्वा हरी॒ वृष॒णा या॑ह्य॒र्वाङ्

transliteration.text: yé ǀ te ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ vṛṣabhā́saḥ ǀ indra ǀ brahma-yújaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-rathāsaḥ ǀ átyāḥ ǀtā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ tébhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ hávāmahe ǀ tvā ǀ suté ǀ indra ǀ sóme ǁ

Sukta 177.translation: “Mount,Indra, your steeds, who are young and vigorous, tractable to prayer, and harnessed to a bounty-shedding car; come down with them to us. We invoke you, Indra, the libation being poured out.”
Sukta 177.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ये ते॒ वृष॑णो वृष॒भास॑ इन्द्र ब्रह्म॒युजो॒ वृष॑रथासो॒ अत्या॑: । ताँ आ ति॑ष्ठ॒ तेभि॒रा या॑ह्य॒र्वाङ्हवा॑महे त्वा सु॒त इ॑न्द्र॒ सोमे॑

Sukta 177.translation: “Ascend your bounty-shedding car, for you theSoma, the showerer of benefits, is effused, the sweet libations are prepared. Bounty-sheddingIndra, having harnessed them, come with your vigorous steeds for (the good of) mankind; come with your rapid (car) to my presence.”
Sukta 177.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ ति॑ष्ठ॒ रथं॒ वृष॑णं॒ वृषा॑ ते सु॒तः सोम॒: परि॑षिक्ता॒ मधू॑नि । यु॒क्त्वा वृष॑भ्यां वृषभ क्षिती॒नां हरि॑भ्यां याहि प्र॒वतोप॑ म॒द्रिक्

Sukta 177.translation: “This is the sacrifice offered to the gods; this is the offering of the victim; these are the prayers; this,Indra, is theSoma; the sacred grass is ready strewn; come, therefore, Indra, quickly, sit down, drink (the libation); here let loose your steeds.”
Sukta 177.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं य॒ज्ञो दे॑व॒या अ॒यं मि॒येध॑ इ॒मा ब्रह्मा॑ण्य॒यमि॑न्द्र॒ सोम॑: । स्ती॒र्णं ब॒र्हिरा तु श॑क्र॒ प्र या॑हि॒ पिबा॑ नि॒षद्य॒ वि मु॑चा॒ हरी॑ इ॒ह

Sukta 177.translation: “Glorified by us,Indra, come to (our) presence to accept the prayers of the venerable offerer (of the oblation); so that we may ever enjoy prosperity through your protection, and thence obtain food, strength and long life.”
Sukta 177.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ओ सुष्टु॑त इन्द्र याह्य॒र्वाङुप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि मा॒न्यस्य॑ का॒रोः । वि॒द्याम॒ वस्तो॒रव॑सा गृ॒णन्तो॑ वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

Sukta 178.translation: “Inasmuch,Indra, as the praise by which you are (induced to bestow) protection on your adorers is heard (by all), therefore disappoint not the desire (that would raise us) to greatness; may I obtain, through your (favour), all things that are obtainable by man.”
Sukta 178.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद्ध॒ स्या त॑ इन्द्र श्रु॒ष्टिरस्ति॒ यया॑ ब॒भूथ॑ जरि॒तृभ्य॑ ऊ॒ती । मा न॒: कामं॑ म॒हय॑न्त॒मा ध॒ग्विश्वा॑ ते अश्यां॒ पर्याप॑ आ॒योः

Sukta 178.translation: “Let not the royalIndrafrustrate those our actions, which the sisters, (Day and Night), are directing to their object. May these invigorating offerings propitiate hi, so that he may bestow upon us friendly (regard), and (abundant) food.”
Sukta 178.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न घा॒ राजेन्द्र॒ आ द॑भन्नो॒ या नु स्वसा॑रा कृ॒णव॑न्त॒ योनौ॑ । आप॑श्चिदस्मै सु॒तुका॑ अवेष॒न्गम॑न्न॒ इन्द्र॑: स॒ख्या वय॑श्च

devanagari.text: जेता नृभिरिंद्रः पृत्सु शूरः श्रोता हवं नाधमानस्य कारोः ।प्रभर्ता रथं दाशुष उपाक उद्यंता गिरो यदि च त्मना भूत् ॥

Sukta 178.translation: “Indra, the hero, the victor in battles, along with the leaders (of his hosts, theMaruts), will hear the invocation of his supplicating worshipper, and when disposed to accept his praises, will, of his own accord, drive his chariot close to the donor (of the oblation).”
Sukta 178.sanskrit_wisdomlib: जेता॒ नृभि॒रिन्द्र॑: पृ॒त्सु शूर॒: श्रोता॒ हवं॒ नाध॑मानस्य का॒रोः । प्रभ॑र्ता॒ रथं॑ दा॒शुष॑ उपा॒क उद्य॑न्ता॒ गिरो॒ यदि॑ च॒ त्मना॒ भूत्

Sukta 178.translation: “Verily,Indrathrough desire of (sacrificial) food, is the devourer (of that which is presented) by (his) worshippers, and overcomes (the adversaries) of his friend; in the many-voiced assembly (of men), Indra, the faithful (performer of his promise), commending (the piety) of his worshipper, approves of the (offered) food.”
Sukta 178.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा नृभि॒रिन्द्र॑: सुश्रव॒स्या प्र॑खा॒दः पृ॒क्षो अ॒भि मि॒त्रिणो॑ भूत् । स॒म॒र्य इ॒षः स्त॑वते॒ विवा॑चि सत्राक॒रो यज॑मानस्य॒ शंस॑:

devanagari.text: त्वया वयं मघवन्निंद्र शत्रूनभि ष्याम महतो मन्यमानान् ।त्वं त्राता त्वमु नो वृधे भूर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥

Sukta 178.translation: “By you, opulentIndra, may we overcome our mighty and formidable enemies; you are our protector; may you be propitious to our prosperity, that we may thence obtain food, strength and long life.”
Sukta 178.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वया॑ व॒यं म॑घवन्निन्द्र॒ शत्रू॑न॒भि ष्या॑म मह॒तो मन्य॑मानान् । त्वं त्रा॒ता त्वमु॑ नो वृ॒धे भू॑र्वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

devanagari.text: पूर्वीरहं शरदः शश्रमाणा दोषा वस्तोरुषसो जरयंतीः ।मिनाति श्रियं जरिमा तनूनामप्यू नु पत्नीर्वृषणो जगम्युः ॥

Sukta 179.translation: “(Lopāmudrā): Many years have I been serving you diligently, both day and night, and through mornings, bringing on old age; decay now impairs the beauty of my limbs; what, therefore, is now (to be done); let husbands approach their wives.”
Sukta 179.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पू॒र्वीर॒हं श॒रद॑: शश्रमा॒णा दो॒षा वस्तो॑रु॒षसो॑ ज॒रय॑न्तीः । मि॒नाति॒ श्रियं॑ जरि॒मा त॒नूना॒मप्यू॒ नु पत्नी॒र्वृष॑णो जगम्युः

devanagari.text: ये चिद्धि पूर्व ऋतसाप आसन्त्साकं देवेभिरवदन्नृतानि ।ते चिदवासुर्नह्यंतमापुः समू नु पत्नीर्वृषभिर्जगम्युः ॥

Sukta 179.translation: “The ancient sages, disseminators of truth, who, verily, conversed of tuths with the gods, begot (progeny), nor thereby violated (their vow of continence), therefore should wives be approached by their husbands.”
Sukta 179.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ये चि॒द्धि पूर्व॑ ऋत॒साप॒ आस॑न्त्सा॒कं दे॒वेभि॒रव॑दन्नृ॒तानि॑ । ते चि॒दवा॑सुर्न॒ह्यन्त॑मा॒पुः समू॒ नु पत्नी॒र्वृष॑भिर्जगम्युः

Sukta 179.translation: “(Agastya): Penance has not been practised in vain; since the gods protect us, we may indulge all our desires; in this world we may triumph in many conflicts, if we exert ourselves mutually together.”
Sukta 179.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न मृषा॑ श्रा॒न्तं यदव॑न्ति दे॒वा विश्वा॒ इत्स्पृधो॑ अ॒भ्य॑श्नवाव । जया॒वेदत्र॑ श॒तनी॑थमा॒जिं यत्स॒म्यञ्चा॑ मिथु॒नाव॒भ्यजा॑व

Sukta 179.translation: “Desire, either from this cause or from that, has come upon me whilst engaged in prayer and suppressing (passion); letLopāmudrāapproach her husband; the unsteady feminine le beguiles the firm and resolute man.”
Sukta 179.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न॒दस्य॑ मा रुध॒तः काम॒ आग॑न्नि॒त आजा॑तो अ॒मुत॒: कुत॑श्चित् । लोपा॑मुद्रा॒ वृष॑णं॒ नी रि॑णाति॒ धीर॒मधी॑रा धयति श्व॒सन्त॑म्

devanagari.text: इमं नु सोममंतितो हृत्सु पीतमुप ब्रुवे ।यत्सीमागश्चकृमा तत्सु मृळतु पुलुकामो हि मर्त्यः ॥

Sukta 179.translation: “(Pupil): I beseech theSoma, which has been drunk in my heart, that it may fully expiate the sin we have committed; man is subject to many desires.”
Sukta 179.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मं नु सोम॒मन्ति॑तो हृ॒त्सु पी॒तमुप॑ ब्रुवे । यत्सी॒माग॑श्चकृ॒मा तत्सु मृ॑ळतु पुलु॒कामो॒ हि मर्त्य॑:

Sukta 179.translation: “Agastya, a venerable sage, working with (fit) implements, desiring progeny, offspring, and strength, practised both classes (of obligations), and received true benedictions from the gods.”
Sukta 179.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒गस्त्य॒: खन॑मानः ख॒नित्रै॑: प्र॒जामप॑त्यं॒ बल॑मि॒च्छमा॑नः । उ॒भौ वर्णा॒वृषि॑रु॒ग्रः पु॑पोष स॒त्या दे॒वेष्वा॒शिषो॑ जगाम

Sukta 180.translation: “Aśvins, your horses are traversers of the (three) regions, when your chariot proceeds to (its desired) quarters; the golden fellies of your wheels grant (whatever is wished for); drinking theSoma, you participate in the morning (rite).”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वो रजां॑सि सु॒यमा॑सो॒ अश्वा॒ रथो॒ यद्वां॒ पर्यर्णां॑सि॒ दीय॑त् । हि॒र॒ण्यया॑ वां प॒वय॑: प्रुषाय॒न्मध्व॒: पिब॑न्ता उ॒षस॑: सचेथे

Sukta 180.translation: “Direct downwards (the course) of your (car) swift moving, variously going, friendly to man, and to be especially venerated, when all adorable, your sister (dawn) prepares (for your approach), and (the instrumental tutor of the ceremony) worships you, drinkers of theSoma, for the sake (of obtaining) strength and food.”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वमत्य॒स्याव॑ नक्षथो॒ यद्विप॑त्मनो॒ नर्य॑स्य॒ प्रय॑ज्योः । स्वसा॒ यद्वां॑ विश्वगूर्ती॒ भरा॑ति॒ वाजा॒येट्टे॑ मधुपावि॒षे च॑

devanagari.text: युवं पय उस्रियायामधत्तं पक्वमामायामव पूर्व्यं गोः ।अंतर्यद्वनिनो वामृतप्सू ह्वारो न शुचिर्यजते हविष्मान् ॥

transliteration.text: yuvám ǀ páyaḥ ǀ usríyāyām ǀ adhattam ǀ pakvám ǀ āmā́yām ǀ áva ǀ pū́rvyam ǀ góḥ ǀantáḥ ǀ yát ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ vām ǀ ṛtapsū ítyṛta-psū ǀ hvāráḥ ǀ ná ǀ śúciḥ ǀ yájate ǀ havíṣmān ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “Youhave restored milk to the cow; you have (brought) down the prior mature (secretion) into the unripe (or barren udder) of the cow; the devout offerer of the oblation worships you, whose forms are truth, (as vigilant in the midst of the ceremony), as a thief (in the midst) of a thicket.”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वं पय॑ उ॒स्रिया॑यामधत्तं प॒क्वमा॒माया॒मव॒ पूर्व्यं॒ गोः । अ॒न्तर्यद्व॒निनो॑ वामृतप्सू ह्वा॒रो न शुचि॒र्यज॑ते ह॒विष्मा॑न्

devanagari.text: युवं ह घर्मं मधुमंतमत्रयेऽपो न क्षोदोऽवृणीतमेषे ।तद्वां नरावश्विना पश्वइष्टी रथ्येव चक्रा प्रति यंति मध्वः ॥
युवम् । ह । घर्मम् । मधुऽमन्तम् । अत्रये । अपः । न । क्षोदः । अवृणीतम् । एषे ।तत् । वाम् । नरौ । अश्विना । पश्वःऽइष्टिः । रथ्याऽइव । चक्रा । प्रति । यन्ति । मध्वः ॥

transliteration.text: yuvám ǀ ha ǀ gharmám ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ átraye ǀ apáḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣódaḥ ǀ avṛṇītam ǀ eṣé ǀtát ǀ vām ǀ narau ǀ aśvinā ǀ páśvaḥ-iṣṭiḥ ǀ ráthyā-iva ǀ cakrā́ ǀ práti ǀ yanti ǀ mádhvaḥ ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “You rendered the heat as soothing as sweet butter toAtri; wishing (for relief), and invested it with coolness,like water; therefore, for you,Aśvins, leaders (of rites) the fire-offering (is made); to you theSoma(drips) run like chariot wheels (down a declivity).”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वं ह॑ घ॒र्मं मधु॑मन्त॒मत्र॑ये॒ऽपो न क्षोदो॑ऽवृणीतमे॒षे । तद्वां॑ नरावश्विना॒ पश्व॑इष्टी॒ रथ्ये॑व च॒क्रा प्रति॑ यन्ति॒ मध्व॑:

devanagari.text: आ वां दानाय ववृतीय दस्रा गोरोहेण तौग्र्यो न जिव्रिः ।अपः क्षोणी सचते माहिना वां जूर्णो वामक्षुरंहसो यजत्रा ॥
आ । वाम् । दानाय । ववृतीय । दस्रा । गोः । ओहेन । तौग्र्यः । न । जिव्रिः ।अपः । क्षोणी इति । सचते । माहिना । वाम् । जूर्णः । वाम् । अक्षुः । अंहसः । यजत्रा ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ dānā́ya ǀ vavṛtīya ǀ dasrā ǀ góḥ ǀ óhena ǀ taugryáḥ ǀ ná ǀ jívriḥ ǀapáḥ ǀ kṣoṇī́ íti ǀ sacate ǀ mā́hinā ǀ vām ǀ jūrṇáḥ ǀ vām ǀ ákṣuḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ yajatrā ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “Dasras, may I bring you, by the vehicle of my prayers, (hither), to bestow (upon me your aid), like the infirm son ofTugra; heaven and earth combine (to worship you) through your greatness; may this, your aged (worshipper), adorable (Aśvins), enjoy long life, (exempt) from sin.”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ वां॑ दा॒नाय॑ ववृतीय दस्रा॒ गोरोहे॑ण तौ॒ग्र्यो न जिव्रि॑: । अ॒पः क्षो॒णी स॑चते॒ माहि॑ना वां जू॒र्णो वा॒मक्षु॒रंह॑सो यजत्रा

devanagari.text: नि यद्युवेथे नियुतः सुदानू उप स्वधाभिः सृजथः पुरंधिं ।प्रेषद्वेषद्वातो न सूरिरा महे ददे सुव्रतो न वाजं ॥
नि । यत् । युवेथे इति । निऽयुतः । सुदानू इति सुऽदानू । उप । स्वधाभिः । सृजथः । पुरम्ऽधिम् ।प्रेषत् । वेषत् । वातः । न । सूरिः । आ । महे । ददे । सुऽव्रतः । न । वाजम् ॥

transliteration.text: ní ǀ yát ǀ yuvéthe íti ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀ úpa ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀ sṛjathaḥ ǀ púram-dhim ǀpréṣat ǀ véṣat ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ná ǀ sūríḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ mahé ǀ dade ǀ su-vratáḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́jam ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “Bountiful givers, when you yoke your horses you replenish the earth with viands; may this your worshipper be (swift) as the wind to propitiate and plural ase you, that, through your great (favour), he may, like a pious man, obtain food.”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नि यद्यु॒वेथे॑ नि॒युत॑: सुदानू॒ उप॑ स्व॒धाभि॑: सृजथ॒: पुरं॑धिम् । प्रेष॒द्वेष॒द्वातो॒ न सू॒रिरा म॒हे द॑दे सुव्र॒तो न वाज॑म्

devanagari.text: वयं चिद्धि वां जरितारः सत्या विपन्यामहे वि पणिर्हितावान् ।अधा चिद्धि ष्माश्विनावनिंद्या पाथो हि ष्मा वृषणावंतिदेवं ॥
वयम् । चित् । हि । वाम् । जरितारः । सत्याः । विपन्यामहे । वि । पणिः । हितऽवान् ।अध । चित् । हि । स्म । अश्विनौ । अनिन्द्या । पाथः । हि । स्म । वृषणौ । अन्तिऽदेवम् ॥

transliteration.text: vayám ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ jaritā́raḥ ǀ satyā́ḥ ǀ vipanyā́mahe ǀ ví ǀ paṇíḥ ǀ hitá-vān ǀádha ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ aśvinau ǀ anindyā ǀ pātháḥ ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ánti-devam ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “Your sincere adorers, we verily praise you in various ways. The pitcher has been plural ced (ready for theSoma). IrreproachableAśvins, showerers (of benefits) drink freely of the juice in the presence of the gods.”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: व॒यं चि॒द्धि वां॑ जरि॒तार॑: स॒त्या वि॑प॒न्याम॑हे॒ वि प॒णिर्हि॒तावा॑न् । अधा॑ चि॒द्धि ष्मा॑श्विनावनिन्द्या पा॒थो हि ष्मा॑ वृषणा॒वन्ति॑देवम्

devanagari.text: युवां चिद्धि ष्माश्विनावनु द्यून्विरुद्रस्य प्रस्रवणस्य सातौ ।अगस्त्यो नरां नृषु प्रशस्तः काराधुनीव चितयत्सहस्रैः ॥
युवाम् । चित् । हि । स्म । अश्विनौ । अनु । द्यून् । विऽरुद्रस्य । प्रऽस्रवणस्य । सातौ ।अगस्त्यः । नराम् । नृषु । प्रऽशस्तः । काराधुनीऽइव । चितयत् । सहस्रैः ॥

transliteration.text: yuvā́m ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ aśvinau ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀ ví-rudrasya ǀ pra-srávaṇasya ǀ sātáu ǀagástyaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ nṛ́ṣu ǀ prá-śastaḥ ǀ kā́rādhunī-iva ǀ citayat ǀ sahásraiḥ ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “Aśvins,Agastya, eminent among the leader of men, arouses you daily with numerous (invocations) like an instrumental ument of sound, for the sake of obtaining a manifold (flow) of a torrent (of rain).”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वां चि॒द्धि ष्मा॑श्विना॒वनु॒ द्यून्विरु॑द्रस्य प्र॒स्रव॑णस्य सा॒तौ । अ॒गस्त्यो॑ न॒रां नृषु॒ प्रश॑स्त॒: कारा॑धुनीव चितयत्स॒हस्रै॑:

devanagari.text: प्र यद्वहेथे महिना रथस्य प्र स्यंद्रा याथो मनुषो न होता ।धत्तं सूरिभ्य उत वा स्वश्व्यं नासत्या रयिषाचः स्याम ॥
प्र । यत् । वहेथे इति । महिना । रथस्य । प्र । स्यन्द्रा । याथः । मनुषः । न । होता ।धत्तम् । सूरिऽभ्यः । उत । वा । सुऽअश्व्यम् । नासत्या । रयिऽसाचः । स्याम ॥

transliteration.text: prá ǀ yát ǀ váhethe íti ǀ mahinā́ ǀ ráthasya ǀ prá ǀ syandrā ǀ yāthaḥ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǀdhattám ǀ sūrí-bhyaḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ su-áśvyam ǀ nā́satyā ǀ rayi-sā́caḥ ǀ syāma ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “When, by the virtue of your chariot, you come (to the sacrifice), and when, like the ministering priest (after discharging his rfunction), you depart, gliding away, you give to the devout (worshippers a reward), thogh it be store of good horses; may we be enriched,Nāsatyās(by your favour).”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र यद्वहे॑थे महि॒ना रथ॑स्य॒ प्र स्य॑न्द्रा याथो॒ मनु॑षो॒ न होता॑ । ध॒त्तं सू॒रिभ्य॑ उ॒त वा॒ स्वश्व्यं॒ नास॑त्या रयि॒षाच॑: स्याम

devanagari.text: तं वां रथं वयमद्या हुवेम स्तोमैरश्विना सुविताय नव्यं ।अरिष्टनेमिं परि द्यामियानं विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
तम् । वाम् । रथम् । वयम् । अद्य । हुवेम । स्तोमैः । अश्विना । सुविताय । नव्यम् ।अरिष्टऽनेमिम् । परि । द्याम् । इयानम् । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ vām ǀ rátham ǀ vayám ǀ adyá ǀ huvema ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ návyam ǀáriṣṭa-nemim ǀ pári ǀ dyā́m ǀ iyānám ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ

Sukta 180.translation: “We invoke today,Aśvins, with hymns, for the sake of good things, your praiseworthy chariot of undamaged wheels, and traversing the sky, that we may obtain (from it) food, strength and long life.”
Sukta 180.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तं वां॒ रथं॑ व॒यम॒द्या हु॑वेम॒ स्तोमै॑रश्विना सुवि॒ताय॒ नव्य॑म् । अरि॑ष्टनेमिं॒ परि॒ द्यामि॑या॒नं वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

devanagari.text: कदु प्रेष्ठाविषां रयीणामध्वर्यंता यदुन्निनीथो अपां ।अयं वां यज्ञो अकृत प्रशस्तिं वसुधिती अवितारा जनानां ॥
कत् । ऊं इति । प्रेष्ठौ । इषाम् । रयीणाम् । अध्वर्यन्ता । यत् । उत्ऽनिनीथः । अपाम् ।अयम् । वाम् । यज्ञः । अकृत । प्रऽशस्तिम् । वसुधिती इति वसुऽधिती । अवितारा । जनानाम् ॥

transliteration.text: kát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ préṣṭhau ǀ iṣā́m ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ adhvaryántā ǀ yát ǀ ut-ninītháḥ ǀ apā́m ǀayám ǀ vām ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ akṛta ǀ prá-śastim ǀ vásudhitī íti vásu-dhitī ǀ ávitārā ǀ janānām ǁ

Sukta 181.translation: “When, beloved (Aśvins), do you bear aloft (the materials) of food and riches, that, desirous of the sacrifice, you may send down the rain; this sacrifice offers you adoration, givers of riches, protectors of men.”
Sukta 181.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कदु॒ प्रेष्टा॑वि॒षां र॑यी॒णाम॑ध्व॒र्यन्ता॒ यदु॑न्निनी॒थो अ॒पाम् । अ॒यं वां॑ य॒ज्ञो अ॑कृत॒ प्रश॑स्तिं॒ वसु॑धिती॒ अवि॑तारा जनानाम्

devanagari.text: आ वामश्वासः शुचयः पयस्पा वातरंहसो दिव्यासो अत्याः ।मनोजुवो वृषणो वीतपृष्ठा एह स्वराजो अश्विना वहंतु ॥
आ । वाम् । अश्वासः । शुचयः । पयःऽपाः । वातऽरंहसः । दिव्यासः । अत्याः ।मनःऽजुवः । वृषणः । वीतऽपृष्ठाः । आ । इह । स्वऽराजः । अश्विना । वहन्तु ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ payaḥ-pā́ḥ ǀ vā́ta-raṃhasaḥ ǀ divyā́saḥ ǀ átyāḥ ǀmanaḥ-júvaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ vītá-pṛṣṭhāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ sva-rā́jaḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ vahantu ǁ

Sukta 181.translation: “Aśvins, may your horses, pure, rain-drinking, swift as the wind, heaven-born, quick-moving, fleet as thought, vigorous, well-backed, and self-irradiating, bring you hither.”
Sukta 181.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ वा॒मश्वा॑स॒: शुच॑यः पय॒स्पा वात॑रंहसो दि॒व्यासो॒ अत्या॑: । म॒नो॒जुवो॒ वृष॑णो वी॒तपृ॑ष्ठा॒ एह स्व॒राजो॑ अ॒श्विना॑ वहन्तु

devanagari.text: आ वां रथोऽवनिर्न प्रवत्वान्त्सृप्रवंधुरः सुविताय गम्याः ।वृष्णः स्थातारा मनसो जवीयानहंपूर्वो यजतो धिष्ण्या यः ॥
आ । वाम् । रथः । अवनिः । न । प्रवत्वान् । सृप्रऽवन्धुरः । सुविताय । गम्याः ।वृष्णः । स्थातारा । मनसः । जवीयान् । अहम्ऽपूर्वः । यजतः । धिष्ण्या । यः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ avániḥ ǀ ná ǀ pravátvān ǀ sṛprá-vandhuraḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ gamyāḥ ǀvṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ sthātārā ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jávīyān ǀ aham-pūrváḥ ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ dhiṣṇyā ǀ yáḥ ǁ

Sukta 181.translation: “Aśvins, excellent and steady, may your chariot, vast as the earth, broad-fronted, rapid as the rain (fleet) as thought, cumulative and adorable, come hither for (our) good.”
Sukta 181.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ वां॒ रथो॒ऽवनि॒र्न प्र॒वत्वा॑न्त्सृ॒प्रव॑न्धुरः सुवि॒ताय॑ गम्याः । वृष्ण॑: स्थातारा॒ मन॑सो॒ जवी॑यानहम्पू॒र्वो य॑ज॒तो धि॑ष्ण्या॒ यः

devanagari.text: इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा नामभिः स्वैः ।जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥

Sukta 181.translation: “Born here (in the middle region) and here (in the upper region), you are glorified together, as faultless in your forms and (perfect in) your own many excellences; one (of you) the victorious son (of the firmament), the devout (promoter) of sacred sacrifice, the other, the auspicious son of heaven, (each) upholds (the world).”
Sukta 181.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒हेह॑ जा॒ता सम॑वावशीतामरे॒पसा॑ त॒न्वा॒३॒॑ नाम॑भि॒: स्वैः । जि॒ष्णुर्वा॑म॒न्यः सुम॑खस्य सू॒रिर्दि॒वो अ॒न्यः सु॒भग॑: पु॒त्र ऊ॑हे

Sukta 181.translation: “Aśvins, may the golden-coloured (car of one of you), traversing at will the quarters of space, come to our dwellings; may mankind encourage the horses of the other by food, by friction, and by shouts.”

Sukta 181.translation: “(One of you), the disperser (of the clouds), likeIndra, the annihilator (of his foes), desirous of the oblation, proceeds (bestowing) abundant food. (Devout worshippers) cherish with (sacrificial) viands, (the faculties) of the other, for the sake of favours, which flow upon us like swelling rivers.”
Sukta 181.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र वां॑ श॒रद्वा॑न्वृष॒भो न नि॒ष्षाट् पू॒र्वीरिष॑श्चरति॒ मध्व॑ इ॒ष्णन् । एवै॑र॒न्यस्य॑ पी॒पय॑न्त॒ वाजै॒र्वेष॑न्तीरू॒र्ध्वा न॒द्यो॑ न॒ आगु॑:

Sukta 181.translation: “Aśvins, creators, the perpetual threefold hymn addressed to you, has been uttered, (to secure) your steady (favour); thus glorified protect him who solicits (your bounty), and whether moving or resting, hear his invocation.”
Sukta 181.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अस॑र्जि वां॒ स्थवि॑रा वेधसा॒ गीर्बा॒ळ्हे अ॑श्विना त्रे॒धा क्षर॑न्ती । उप॑स्तुताववतं॒ नाध॑मानं॒ याम॒न्नया॑मञ्छृणुतं॒ हवं॑ मे

Sukta 181.translation: “May the praise of your resplendent forms, (uttered) in the hall of sacrifice, thrice strewn with sacred grass, bring prosperity to the conductors (of the sacrifice). Showerers (of benefits), may the raining-cloud, proceeding to man, nourish him lik a a sprinkling of water.”

Sukta 181.translation: “The wise offerer of oblations, likePūṣan, praises you,Aśvins, as (he would praise)Agniand Uṣā, (at the season) at which I invoke you praising with devotion that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.”

Sukta 182.translation: “The information, sage (priests), has been received; be ready with your praises, for the (benefit) showering car (of theAśvinshas arrived); propitiate (the divinities), for they show favour to the doer of good works; they are entitled to praise, rich in benevolence to mankind the grandsons of heaven, and observers of holy rites.”

Sukta 182.translation: “Dasras, in truth most imperial, adorable, swifter than the winds, and eminent in good works, riders in a car, and most distinguished charioteers, bring hither your car, full heaped up with ambrosia, and with it come,Aśvins, to the donor (of the offering).”

Sukta 182.translation: “What makes you here,Aśvins; why do you tarry, (where) any man who makes no oblation is respected; humble him; take away the life of the niggard; grant light to the pious man striving to speak your praise.”
Sukta 182.sanskrit_wisdomlib: किमत्र॑ दस्रा कृणुथ॒: किमा॑साथे॒ जनो॒ यः कश्चि॒दह॑विर्मही॒यते॑ । अति॑ क्रमिष्टं जु॒रतं॑ प॒णेरसुं॒ ज्योति॒र्विप्रा॑य कृणुतं वच॒स्यवे॑

Sukta 182.translation: “Annihilate,Aśvins, the dogs who bark at us; slay them warring (against us); you know their (means of harm); render every word of him who praises you affluent in precious (rewards); acceptNāsatyas, both of you, may praise.”

transliteration.text: yuvám ǀ etám ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ síndhuṣu ǀ plavám ǀ ātman-vántam ǀ pakṣíṇam ǀ taugryā́ya ǀ kám ǀyéna ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ niḥ-ūháthuḥ ǀ su-paptaní ǀ petathuḥ ǀ kṣódasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǁ

Sukta 182.translation: “You constructed a plural asant, substantial winged bark, borne on the ocean waters for the son ofTugra, by which, with minddevoted to the gods, you bore him up, and quickly descending (from the sky), you made a path for him across the great waters.”
Sukta 182.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वमे॒तं च॑क्रथु॒: सिन्धु॑षु प्ल॒वमा॑त्म॒न्वन्तं॑ प॒क्षिणं॑ तौ॒ग्र्याय॒ कम् । येन॑ देव॒त्रा मन॑सा निरू॒हथु॑: सुपप्त॒नी पे॑तथु॒: क्षोद॑सो म॒हः

devanagari.text: अवविद्धं तौग्र्यमप्स्वंतरनारंभणे तमसि प्रविद्धं ।चतस्रो नावो जठलस्य जुष्टा उदश्विभ्यामिषिताः पारयंति ॥

Sukta 182.translation: “Four ships launched into the midst of the receptable (of the waters), sent by theAśvins, brought safe to shore the son ofTugra, who had been cast headlong into the waters (by his foes), and plural nged in extricable darkness.”
Sukta 182.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव॑विद्धं तौ॒ग्र्यम॒प्स्व१॒॑न्तर॑नारम्भ॒णे तम॑सि॒ प्रवि॑द्धम् । चत॑स्रो॒ नावो॒ जठ॑लस्य॒ जुष्टा॒ उद॒श्विभ्या॑मिषि॒ताः पा॑रयन्ति

Sukta 182.translation: “What was the tree that was stationed in the midst of the ocean, to which the supplicating son ofTugraclung; as leaves (are caught hold of) for the support of a falling animal; you,Aśvins, bore him up to safety, to your great renown.”
Sukta 182.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कः स्वि॑द्वृ॒क्षो निःष्ठि॑तो॒ मध्ये॒ अर्ण॑सो॒ यं तौ॒ग्र्यो ना॑धि॒तः प॒र्यष॑स्वजत् । प॒र्णा मृ॒गस्य॑ प॒तरो॑रिवा॒रभ॒ उद॑श्विना ऊहथु॒: श्रोम॑ताय॒ कम्

Sukta 182.translation: “May the praise which your devout adorers have uttered be acceptable to you,Nāsatyas, leaders (in pious rites); be propitiated today by the libations of our assembly, that we may obtain food, strength and long life.”
Sukta 182.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तद्वां॑ नरा नासत्या॒वनु॑ ष्या॒द्यद्वां॒ माना॑स उ॒चथ॒मवो॑चन् । अ॒स्माद॒द्य सद॑सः सो॒म्यादा वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

Sukta 183.translation: “Showerers of benefits, harness the car which has three benches, three wheels, and is as quick as thought; with which, embellished with three metals, you come to the dwelling of the pious (worshipper), and in which you travel like a bird with wings.”
Sukta 183.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तं यु॑ञ्जाथां॒ मन॑सो॒ यो जवी॑यान्त्रिवन्धु॒रो वृ॑षणा॒ यस्त्रि॑च॒क्रः । येनो॑पया॒थः सु॒कृतो॑ दुरो॒णं त्रि॒धातु॑ना पतथो॒ विर्न प॒र्णैः

Sukta 183.translation: “Your easy-rolling car alights upon the earth, where favourable to the sacred rite, you stop for the sake of the (sacrificial) food; may this hymn, promotive of your person nal (welfare), be associated with your forms, and do you unite with the dawn, the daughter of heaven.”
Sukta 183.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सु॒वृद्रथो॑ वर्तते॒ यन्न॒भि क्षां यत्तिष्ठ॑थ॒: क्रतु॑म॒न्तानु॑ पृ॒क्षे । वपु॑र्वपु॒ष्या स॑चतामि॒यं गीर्दि॒वो दु॑हि॒त्रोषसा॑ सचेथे

Sukta 183.translation: “Ascend your rolling car, which approaches the sacred rite of the offerer of the oblation; the car in which,Nāsatyas, leaders, you purpose to come to the sacrifice, and proceed to the dwelling (of the worshipper), for (bestowing upon him) offspring, and for his own (good).”
Sukta 183.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ ति॑ष्ठतं सु॒वृतं॒ यो रथो॑ वा॒मनु॑ व्र॒तानि॒ वर्त॑ते ह॒विष्मा॑न् । येन॑ नरा नासत्येष॒यध्यै॑ व॒र्तिर्या॒थस्तन॑याय॒ त्मने॑ च

Sukta 183.translation: “Let not the wolf, let not the she-wolf, harm me safe (in your protection); abandon me not, nor deliver me (to another). This your share (of the offering) is prepared; this prayer,Dasras, (is addressed) to you; these treasures ofSomaare for you.”

Sukta 183.translation: “Gotama, Purimiḷha,Atri, (each) offering oblations, invokes you for his protection; like unto a wayfarer, who (makes for his intended direction) by a straight (path) do you,Dasras, come (direct) to my invocation).”
Sukta 183.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वां गोत॑मः पुरुमी॒ळ्हो अत्रि॒र्दस्रा॒ हव॒तेऽव॑से ह॒विष्मा॑न् । दिशं॒ न दि॒ष्टामृ॑जू॒येव॒ यन्ता मे॒ हवं॑ नास॒त्योप॑ यातम्

Sukta 183.translation: “(Through your aid)Aśvins, we cross over this (limit of) darkness; to you this (our) hymn has been addressed; come hither by the paths traversed by the gods, that we may obtain food, and strength, and long life.”
Sukta 183.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अता॑रिष्म॒ तम॑सस्पा॒रम॒स्य प्रति॑ वां॒ स्तोमो॑ अश्विनावधायि । एह या॑तं प॒थिभि॑र्देव॒यानै॑र्वि॒द्यामे॒षं वृ॒जनं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम्

Sukta 184.translation: “We invoke you two, (Aśvins), today; the same two on any other day; when the morning dawns.Nāsatyas, grandsons of heaven, wherever you may be, the pious reciter (of the hymn) invokes you with praises on behalf of the liberal donor (of the offering).”
Sukta 184.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ता वा॑म॒द्य ताव॑प॒रं हु॑वेमो॒च्छन्त्या॑मु॒षसि॒ वह्नि॑रु॒क्थैः । नास॑त्या॒ कुह॑ चि॒त्सन्ता॑व॒र्यो दि॒वो नपा॑ता सु॒दास्त॑राय

Sukta 184.translation: “Showerers (of benefits), rejoicing in (our) libations), make us happy, and destroy the niggard (withholder) of offerings; hear, leaders, with your ears, my praises addressed to you with pure words, for you are seekers (after praise), you are retentive (of laudation).”
Sukta 184.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्मे ऊ॒ षु वृ॑षणा मादयेथा॒मुत्प॒णीँर्ह॑तमू॒र्म्या मद॑न्ता । श्रु॒तं मे॒ अच्छो॑क्तिभिर्मती॒नामेष्टा॑ नरा॒ निचे॑तारा च॒ कर्णै॑:

devanagari.text: श्रिये पूषन्निषुकृतेव देवा नासत्या वहतुं सूर्यायाः ।वच्यंते वां ककुहा अप्सु जाता युगा जूर्णेव वरुणस्य भूरेः ॥

transliteration.text: śriyé ǀ pūṣan ǀ iṣukṛ́tā-iva ǀ devā́ ǀ nā́satyā ǀ vahatúm ǀ sūryā́yāḥ ǀvacyánte ǀ vām ǀ kakuhā́ḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ yugā́ ǀ jūrṇā́-iva ǀ váruṇasya ǀ bhū́reḥ ǁ

Sukta 184.translation: “DivineAśvins, in whom is no untruth, (darting) like arrows to acquire glory, and to carry offSūrya, to you are addressed the prayers that are recited at holy rites, for (the completion of) the uninterrupted, sin-removing (sacrifice), as ancient ages (offered them).”
Sukta 184.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श्रि॒ये पू॑षन्निषु॒कृते॑व दे॒वा नास॑त्या वह॒तुं सू॒र्याया॑: । व॒च्यन्ते॑ वां ककु॒हा अ॒प्सु जा॒ता यु॒गा जू॒र्णेव॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ भूरे॑:

devanagari.text: अस्मे सा वां माध्वी रातिरस्तु स्तोमं हिनोतं मान्यस्य कारोः ।अनु यद्वां श्रवस्या सुदानू सुवीर्याय चर्षणयो मदंति ॥

transliteration.text: asmé íti ǀ sā́ ǀ vām ǀ mādhvī íti ǀ rātíḥ ǀ astu ǀ stómam ǀ hinotam ǀ mānyásya ǀ kāróḥ ǀánu ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ śravasyā́ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀ su-vī́ryāya ǀ carṣaṇáyaḥ ǀ mádanti ǁ

Sukta 184.translation: “Receivers of the oblation, may your liberality be displayed towards us; be plural ased with the hymn of the venerable author, so that men may honour the instrumental tutor of the ceremony, as (they honour) you, liberal donors, for the sake of renown.”
Sukta 184.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्मे सा वां॑ माध्वी रा॒तिर॑स्तु॒ स्तोमं॑ हिनोतं मा॒न्यस्य॑ का॒रोः । अनु॒ यद्वां॑ श्रव॒स्या॑ सुदानू सु॒वीर्या॑य चर्ष॒णयो॒ मद॑न्ति

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ vām ǀ stómaḥ ǀ aśvinau ǀ akāri ǀ mā́nebhiḥ ǀ magha-vānā ǀ su-vṛktí ǀyātám ǀ vartíḥ ǀ tánayāya ǀ tmáne ǀ ca ǀ agástye ǀ nāsatyā ǀ mádantā ǁ

Sukta 184.translation: “Aśvins, possessors of wealth, this sin-removing hymn has been addressed to you, together with respectful (oblations);Nāsatyasbe favourable toAgastya; come to his dwelling for (conferring on him) progeny, and for his own (good).”
Sukta 184.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष वां॒ स्तोमो॑ अश्विनावकारि॒ माने॑भिर्मघवाना सुवृ॒क्ति । या॒तं व॒र्तिस्तन॑याय॒ त्मने॑ चा॒गस्त्ये॑ नासत्या॒ मद॑न्ता

Sukta 184.translation: “(Through your aid),Aśvins, we cross over the limit of darkness; to you this (our hymn) has been addressed; come hither by the path traversed by thd gods, thatwe may obtain food, strength and long life.”

Sukta 185.translation: “Which of these two, (Heaven and Earth), is prior which posterior; how were they engendered; (declare), sages, who knows this? verily, you uphold the universe of itself, and the days (and nights) revolve as if they had wheels.”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क॒त॒रा पूर्वा॑ कत॒राप॑रा॒योः क॒था जा॒ते क॑वय॒: को वि वे॑द । विश्वं॒ त्मना॑ बिभृतो॒ यद्ध॒ नाम॒ वि व॑र्तेते॒ अह॑नी च॒क्रिये॑व

Sukta 185.translation: “Footless and motionless, they sustain numerous moving and footed races, as a son is even (nursed) on the lap of his parents; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भूरिं॒ द्वे अच॑रन्ती॒ चर॑न्तं प॒द्वन्तं॒ गर्भ॑म॒पदी॑ दधाते । नित्यं॒ न सू॒नुं पि॒त्रोरु॒पस्थे॒ द्यावा॒ रक्ष॑तं पृथिवी नो॒ अभ्वा॑त्

Sukta 185.translation: “I solicit ofAditi, wealth, without pain or decay, like heaven (in fullness of enjoyment), exempt from injury, and abounding in food; grant, Heaven and Earth, such wealth to him who praises you; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ने॒हो दा॒त्रमदि॑तेरन॒र्वं हु॒वे स्व॑र्वदव॒धं नम॑स्वत् । तद्रो॑दसी जनयतं जरि॒त्रे द्यावा॒ रक्ष॑तं पृथिवी नो॒ अभ्वा॑त्

Sukta 185.translation: “May we ever be (devoted to) that Heaven and Earth, who are not subject to annoyance, who satisfy (all beings) with food, who have the gods (and men) for sons, and who are both endowed with the double (condition) of the divine days (and nights); defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).”

Sukta 185.translation: “Going always together, equally young, and of the like termination, sisters, and kindred, and scenting the navel of the world, plural ced on their lap as its parents; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सं॒गच्छ॑माने युव॒ती सम॑न्ते॒ स्वसा॑रा जा॒मी पि॒त्रोरु॒पस्थे॑ । अ॒भि॒जिघ्र॑न्ती॒ भुव॑नस्य॒ नाभिं॒ द्यावा॒ रक्ष॑तं पृथिवी नो॒ अभ्वा॑त्

Sukta 185.translation: “I invoke to the sacrifice, for the preservation of gods (and men), the two vast, all-supporting, and mighty parents (of the rain and corn); who, beautiful in form, sustain ambrosial (showers); defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒र्वी सद्म॑नी बृह॒ती ऋ॒तेन॑ हु॒वे दे॒वाना॒मव॑सा॒ जनि॑त्री । द॒धाते॒ ये अ॒मृतं॑ सु॒प्रती॑के॒ द्यावा॒ रक्ष॑तं पृथिवी नो॒ अभ्वा॑त्

devanagari.text: उर्वी पृथ्वी बहुले दूरेअंते उप ब्रुवे नमसा यज्ञे अस्मिन् ।दधाते ये सुभगे सुप्रतूर्ती द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥

transliteration.text: urvī́ íti ǀ pṛthvī́ íti ǀ bahulé íti ǀ dūréante íti dūré-ante ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀ námasā ǀ yajñé ǀ asmín ǀdadhā́te íti ǀ yé íti ǀ subháge íti su-bháge ǀ suprátūrtī íti su-prátūrtī ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ

Sukta 185.translation: “I glorify with reverence, at this sacrifice, (the two), who are vast, expansive, multiform, infinite, auspicious;who support (all beings) by their bounty; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒र्वी पृ॒थ्वी ब॑हु॒ले दू॒रेअ॑न्ते॒ उप॑ ब्रुवे॒ नम॑सा य॒ज्ञे अ॒स्मिन् । द॒धाते॒ ये सु॒भगे॑ सु॒प्रतू॑र्ती॒ द्यावा॒ रक्ष॑तं पृथिवी नो॒ अभ्वा॑त्

devanagari.text: देवान्वा यच्चकृमा कच्चिदागः सखायं वा सदमिज्जास्पतिं वा ।इयं धीर्भूया अवयानमेषां द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥

transliteration.text: devā́n ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ cakṛmá ǀ kát ǀ cit ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ sákhāyam ǀ vā ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ jā́ḥ-patim ǀ vā ǀiyám ǀ dhī́ḥ ǀ bhūyāḥ ǀ ava-yā́nam ǀ eṣām ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ

Sukta 185.translation: “May this sacrifice be the means of expiating those offences which we may have committed against the gods, against a friend at any time, against a son-in-law; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दे॒वान्वा॒ यच्च॑कृ॒मा कच्चि॒दाग॒: सखा॑यं वा॒ सद॒मिज्जास्प॑तिं वा । इ॒यं धीर्भू॑या अव॒यान॑मेषां॒ द्यावा॒ रक्ष॑तं पृथिवी नो॒ अभ्वा॑त्

devanagari.text: उभा शंसा नर्या मामविष्टामुभे मामूती अवसा सचेतां ।भूरि चिदर्यः सुदास्तरायेषा मदंत इषयेम देवाः ॥

transliteration.text: ubhā́ ǀ śáṃsā ǀ náryā ǀ mā́m ǀ aviṣṭām ǀ ubhé íti ǀ mā́m ǀ ūtī́ íti ǀ ávasā ǀ sacetām ǀbhū́ri ǀ cit ǀ aryáḥ ǀ sudā́ḥ-tarāya ǀ iṣā́ ǀ mádantaḥ ǀ iṣayema ǀ devāḥ ǁ

Sukta 185.translation: “May both these, accepting praise, and friendly to man, be favourable to me; may they both be associated as guardians for my protection; deities, we your adorers, propitiating you with (sacrificial) food, desire ample (wealth), for the sake of makign liberal donations.”
Sukta 185.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒भा शंसा॒ नर्या॒ माम॑विष्टामु॒भे मामू॒ती अव॑सा सचेताम् । भूरि॑ चिद॒र्यः सु॒दास्त॑राये॒षा मद॑न्त इषयेम देवाः

devanagari.text: ऋतं दिवे तदवोचं पृथिव्या अभिश्रावाय प्रथमं सुमेधाः ।पातामवद्याद्दुरितादभीके पिता माता च रक्षतामवोभिः ॥
