transliteration.text: alātṛṇáḥ ǀ valáḥ ǀ indra ǀ vrajáḥ ǀ góḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ hántoḥ ǀ bháyamānaḥ ǀ ví ǀ āra ǀsu-gā́n ǀ patháḥ ǀ akṛṇot ǀ niḥ-áje ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ āvan ǀ vā́ṇīḥ ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ dhámantīḥ ǁ

Sukta 30.translation: “The heavy cloud, the receptacle of water, dreading you its destroyer, opened out before (you had cast your bolt); thenIndramade easily-traversed paths for the waters to issue, and desirable and loud sounding they proceeded to the (waters of the earth) invoked of many.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ला॒तृ॒णो व॒ल इ॑न्द्र व्र॒जो गोः पु॒रा हन्तो॒र्भय॑मानो॒ व्या॑र । सु॒गान्प॒थो अ॑कृणोन्नि॒रज॒ा गाः प्राव॒न्वाणी॑: पुरुहू॒तं धम॑न्तीः

devanagari.text: एको द्वे वसुमती समीची इंद्र आ पप्रौ पृथिवीमुत द्यां ।उतांतरिक्षादभि नः समीक इषो रथीः सयुजः शूर वाजान् ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “Indraalone has filled the two,both earth and heaven mutually combined, and abounding with wealth; do you hero, mounted in your car, come with your harnessed horses from the firmament, impatient to be near us.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: एको॒ द्वे वसु॑मती समी॒ची इन्द्र॒ आ प॑प्रौ पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्याम् । उ॒तान्तरि॑क्षाद॒भि न॑: समी॒क इ॒षो र॒थीः स॒युज॑: शूर॒ वाजा॑न्

transliteration.text: díśaḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mināti ǀ prá-diṣṭāḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ háryaśva-prasūtāḥ ǀsám ǀ yát ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ vi-mócanam ǀ kṛṇute ǀ tát ǀ tú ǀ asya ǁ

Sukta 30.translation: “Sūryaharms not the quarters (of the horizon), set open daily (for his journey), the progeny ofHaryaśva; when he has traversed the roads (he is to travel), then he lets loose his horses, for such is his office.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दिश॒: सूर्यो॒ न मि॑नाति॒ प्रदि॑ष्टा दि॒वेदि॑वे॒ हर्य॑श्वप्रसूताः । सं यदान॒ळध्व॑न॒ आदिदश्वै॑र्वि॒मोच॑नं कृणुते॒ तत्त्व॑स्य

Sukta 30.translation: “Al,l me are anxious to behold the great and variegated host (of the solar rays) at the issuing of the dawn after the night has been displaced; and when the morning has come, they recognize the many great and glorious acts ofIndra.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दिदृ॑क्षन्त उ॒षसो॒ याम॑न्न॒क्तोर्वि॒वस्व॑त्या॒ महि॑ चि॒त्रमनी॑कम् । विश्वे॑ जानन्ति महि॒ना यदागा॒दिन्द्र॑स्य॒ कर्म॒ सुकृ॑ता पु॒रूणि॑

devanagari.text: महि ज्योतिर्निहितं वक्षणास्वामा पक्वं चरति बिभ्रती गौः ।विश्वं स्वाद्म संभृतमुस्रियायां यत्सीमिंद्रो अदधाद्भोजनाय ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “A great light has been shed upon the rivers; the cow yet immature grazes, charged with the ripe (milk), forIndrahas plural ced in the cow all this collected sweetness for food.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: महि॒ ज्योति॒र्निहि॑तं व॒क्षणा॑स्वा॒मा प॒क्वं च॑रति॒ बिभ्र॑ती॒ गौः । विश्वं॒ स्वाद्म॒ सम्भृ॑तमु॒स्रिया॑यां॒ यत्सी॒मिन्द्रो॒ अद॑धा॒द्भोज॑नाय

devanagari.text: इंद्र दृह्य यामकोशा अभूवन्यज्ञाय शिक्ष गृणते सखिभ्यः ।दुर्मायवो दुरेवा मर्त्यासो निषंगिणो रिपवो हंत्वासः ॥

transliteration.text: índra ǀ dṛ́hya ǀ yāma-kośā́ḥ ǀ abhūvan ǀ yajñā́ya ǀ śikṣa ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀduḥ-māyávaḥ ǀ duḥ-évāḥ ǀ mártyāsaḥ ǀ niṣaṅgíṇaḥ ǀ ripávaḥ ǀ hántvāsaḥ ǁ

Sukta 30.translation: “Indra, be firm, for there are obstructors of your path; secure to the worshipper and his friends (the means of completing) the sacrifice; mortal enemies bearing bows, armed with mischievous weapons, and coming with evil intent, must be destroyed (by you).”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॒ दृह्य॑ यामको॒शा अ॑भूवन्य॒ज्ञाय॑ शिक्ष गृण॒ते सखि॑भ्यः । दु॒र्मा॒यवो॑ दु॒रेवा॒ मर्त्या॑सो निष॒ङ्गिणो॑ रि॒पवो॒ हन्त्वा॑सः

Sukta 30.translation: “The sound (of your bolt) has been heard by the approaching foes; hurl upon them the consuming thunder-bolt, cut them up by the root, oppose;Maghavan, overcome, slay therākṣasas, complete (the sacrifice).”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सं घोष॑: शृण्वेऽव॒मैर॒मित्रै॑र्ज॒ही न्ये॑ष्व॒शनिं॒ तपि॑ष्ठाम् । वृ॒श्चेम॒धस्ता॒द्वि रु॑जा॒ सह॑स्व ज॒हि रक्षो॑ मघवन्र॒न्धय॑स्व

Sukta 30.translation: “plural ck therākṣasas,Indra, by the root; cut as under the middle, blight the summit; to whatever remote (regions) you have driven the sinner, cast upon the enemy of theVedayour consuming weapon.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उद्वृ॑ह॒ रक्ष॑: स॒हमू॑लमिन्द्र वृ॒श्चा मध्यं॒ प्रत्यग्रं॑ शृणीहि । आ कीव॑तः सल॒लूकं॑ चकर्थ ब्रह्म॒द्विष्॒ तपु॑षिं हे॒तिम॑स्य

Sukta 30.translation: “Regulator (of the world, provide us) with horses for our welfare, and when you are seated near to us may we become mighty, enjoying abundant food, and ample riches, and may there be to us wealth accompanied by progeny.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्व॒स्तये॑ वा॒जिभि॑श्च प्रणेत॒: सं यन्म॒हीरिष॑ आ॒सत्सि॑ पू॒र्वीः । रा॒यो व॒न्तारो॑ बृह॒तः स्या॑मा॒स्मे अ॑स्तु॒ भग॑ इन्द्र प्र॒जावा॑न्

devanagari.text: आ नो भर भगमिंद्र द्युमंतं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके ।ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनां ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “Bring to us,Indra, splendid affluence; we rely on the bounty of you who are fond of giving; our desire is as insatiable as the fire of the ocean; appease it, lord of infinite riches.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ नो॑ भर॒ भग॑मिन्द्र द्यु॒मन्तं॒ नि ते॑ दे॒ष्णस्य॑ धीमहि प्ररे॒के । ऊ॒र्व इ॑व पप्रथे॒ कामो॑ अ॒स्मे तमा पृ॑ण वसुपते॒ वसू॑नाम्

Sukta 30.translation: “Gratify this our desire (of wealth) with cows, with horses, with shining treasure, and make us renowned; the wiseKuśikas, desirous of heaven, offer praise to youIndra, with pious (prayers).”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मं कामं॑ मन्दया॒ गोभि॒रश्वै॑श्च॒न्द्रव॑ता॒ राध॑सा प॒प्रथ॑श्च । स्व॒र्यवो॑ म॒तिभि॒स्तुभ्यं॒ विप्रा॒ इन्द्रा॑य॒ वाह॑: कुशि॒कासो॑ अक्रन्

Sukta 30.translation: “Indra, lord of cattle, (divide the clouds and send us) rain, whence nutritious food may come to us; showerer (of benefits), you are spread through the sky, and powerful through truth;Maghavan, consider yourself as our protector.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ नो॑ गो॒त्रा द॑र्दृहि गोपते॒ गाः सम॒स्मभ्यं॑ स॒नयो॑ यन्तु॒ वाजा॑: । दि॒वक्षा॑ असि वृषभ स॒त्यशु॑ष्मो॒ऽस्मभ्यं॒ सु म॑घवन्बोधि गो॒दाः

Sukta 30.translation: “We invoke for our protection the opulentIndradistinguished in this combat; the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.”

Sukta 31.translation: “The sonless father, regulating (the contract), refers to his grandson, (the son) of his daughter, and relying on the efficiency of the rite, honours (his son-in-law) with valuable gifts; the father, trusting to the impregnation of the daughter, supports himself with a tranquil mind.”

Sukta 31.translation: “(A son) born of the body, does not transfer (paternal) wealth to a sister; he has made (her) the recptacle of the embryo of the husband; if the parents procreate children (of either sex), one is the performer of holy acts, the other is to be enriched (with gifts).”

Sukta 31.translation: “For the worship of the resplendent (Indra),Agni, glowing with flame, has begotten mighty sons; great was the germ, and great was their birth, and great was their efficacy, for the worship ofHaryaśva.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ग्निर्ज॑ज्ञे जु॒ह्वा॒३॒॑ रेज॑मानो म॒हस्पु॒त्राँ अ॑रु॒षस्य॑ प्र॒यक्षे॑ । म॒हान्गर्भो॒ मह्या जा॒तमे॑षां म॒ही प्र॒वृद्धर्य॑श्वस्य य॒ज्ञैः

Sukta 31.translation: “The victorious (Maruts) associated (withIndrawhen contending withVṛtra) perceived a great light issuing from the darkness. The dawns recognizing him (as the sun) arose, and Indra was the sole sovereign of the rays (of light).”

Sukta 31.translation: “The seven intelligent ages (theaṅgirasas) having ascertained that (the cows) were concealed in the strong (cavern), propitiated (Indra) by mental devotion; they recovered them all by the path of sacrifice; for Indra, knowing (their pious acts), and offering them homage, entered (the cave).”

Sukta 31.translation: “WhenSaramādiscovered the broken (entrance) of the mountain, thenIndramade great and ample (provision) for her young, as previously (promised); then the sure-footed (animal), forest recognizing their lowing, proceeded, and came to the presence of the imperishable kine.”

Sukta 31.translation: “The most sage (Indra), desirous of the friendship of the (aṅgirasas), went to the cave, and the mountain yielded its contents to the valiant (deity), aided by the youthfulMaruts, equally wishing (to conciliate the sages); the destroyer (of theasuras) recovered (the cattle), and immediately aṅgirasas became his worshipper.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अग॑च्छदु॒ विप्र॑तमः सखी॒यन्नसू॑दयत्सु॒कृते॒ गर्भ॒मद्रि॑: । स॒सान॒ मर्यो॒ युव॑भिर्मख॒स्यन्नथा॑भव॒दङ्गि॑राः स॒द्यो अर्च॑न्

Sukta 31.translation: “May he who is the type of all that is excellent the anticipator (of his foes), he who knows all that is born, who destroysŚuṣṇa, the far-seeing, the restorer of cattle may he, a friend coming from heaven, honouring us as his friends, be free from all reproach.”

Sukta 31.translation: “Theaṅgirasas, with minds intent on their cattle, (sat down to worshipIndra) with hymns, following the road to immortality; great was their person verance by which they sought for months to accomplish (their ends).”

Sukta 31.translation: “Contemplating their own (cattle) giving milk to their former progeny (theaṅgirasas) were delighted; their shouts spread through heaven and earth; they replaced the recovered kine in their plural ces, and stationed guards over the cows.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒म्पश्य॑माना अमदन्न॒भि स्वं पय॑: प्र॒त्नस्य॒ रेत॑सो॒ दुघा॑नाः । वि रोद॑सी अतप॒द्घोष॑ एषां जा॒ते नि॒ष्ठामद॑धु॒र्गोषु॑ वी॒रान्

Sukta 31.translation: “Indra, the slayer ofVṛtra,let loose the milch kine, assisted by theMaruts, born for his aid, and entitled to praises and oblations, and the excellent (cows) contributing abundantly to sacred offerings, and yielding the butter of libation, milked for him sweet (sacrificial) food.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स जा॒तेभि॑र्वृत्र॒हा सेदु॑ ह॒व्यैरुदु॒स्रिया॑ असृज॒दिन्द्रो॑ अ॒र्कैः । उ॒रू॒च्य॑स्मै घृ॒तव॒द्भर॑न्ती॒ मधु॒ स्वाद्म॑ दुदुह॒अ जेन्या॒ गौः

Sukta 31.translation: “They (theaṅgirasas) performing pious acts made for their protector a spacious and splendid abode which they celebrated; seated (at the sacrifice) and supporting with the pillar (of the firmament) the parents (of all things heaven and earth), they established the rapidIndraon high (in heaven).”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पि॒त्रे चि॑च्चक्रु॒: सद॑नं॒ सम॑स्मै॒ महि॒ त्विषी॑मत्सु॒कृतो॒ वि हि ख्यन् । वि॒ष्क॒भ्नन्त॒: स्कम्भ॑नेना॒ जनि॑त्री॒ आसी॑ना ऊ॒र्ध्वं र॑भ॒सं वि मि॑न्वन्

Sukta 31.translation: “Inasmuch as our devout praise has appointed a thiriving ruler for the regulation of heaven and earth, to whom faultless and appropriate commendations (are due), therefore are all the energies ofIndraspontaneously exerted.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒ही यदि॑ धि॒षणा॑ शि॒श्नथे॒ धात्स॑द्यो॒वृधं॑ वि॒भ्वं१॒॑ रोद॑स्योः । गिरो॒ यस्मि॑न्ननव॒द्याः स॑मी॒चीर्विश्वा॒ इन्द्रा॑य॒ तवि॑षी॒रनु॑त्ताः

Sukta 31.translation: “I wish,Indra, for your friendship, and (the exercise of) your powers;many heroes come to the slayer ofVṛtra; we offer to you, sage, great praise and oblations; consider yourself,Maghavan, as our protector.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मह्या ते॑ स॒ख्यं व॑श्मि श॒क्तीरा वृ॑त्र॒घ्ने नि॒युतो॑ यन्ति पू॒र्वीः । महि॑ स्तो॒त्रमव॒ आग॑न्म सू॒रेर॒स्माकं॒ सु म॑घवन्बोधि गो॒पाः

Sukta 31.translation: “Wide fields, vast treasure, (spacious) pastures has the much-knowing (Indra) bestowed upon his friends; the radiant Indra with the leaders (of rites, theMaruts) genitive rated the sun, the dawn, the earth and fire.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: महि॒ क्षेत्रं॑ पु॒रु श्च॒न्द्रं वि॑वि॒द्वानादित्सखि॑भ्यश्च॒रथं॒ समै॑रत् । इन्द्रो॒ नृभि॑रजन॒द्दीद्या॑नः सा॒कं सूर्य॑मु॒षसं॑ गा॒तुम॒ग्निम्

Sukta 31.translation: “This lowly-mindedIndrahas created the wide-spread, commingled, all-delighting waters; and they, purifying the sweet (libations) with the sage purifiers, and being benevolent (to all), proceed with (the revolutions) of days and nights.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒पश्चि॑दे॒ष वि॒भ्वो॒३॒॑ दमू॑ना॒: प्र स॒ध्रीची॑रसृजद्वि॒श्वश्च॑न्द्राः । मध्व॑: पुना॒नाः क॒विभि॑: प॒वित्रै॒र्द्युभि॑र्हिन्वन्त्य॒क्तुभि॒र्धनु॑त्रीः

Sukta 31.translation: “The two adorable (alternations of) day and night, upholding (all things) by the might of the sun, successively revolve; your sincere and acceptable friends (theMaruts) are ready to encounter (your foes) and maintain your greatness.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अनु॑ कृ॒ष्णे वसु॑धिती जिहाते उ॒भे सूर्य॑स्य मं॒हना॒ यज॑त्रे । परि॒ यत्ते॑ महि॒मानं॑ वृ॒जध्यै॒ सखा॑य इन्द्र॒ काम्या॑ ऋजि॒प्याः

Sukta 31.translation: “Slayer ofVṛtra, do you, who is long lived the showerer (of benefits), the giver of food, be the lord of our true praises, repairing (to the sacrifice), come to us great, with great, friendly, and auspicious protections.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पति॑र्भव वृत्रहन्त्सू॒नृता॑नां गि॒रां वि॒श्वायु॑र्वृष॒भो व॑यो॒धाः । आ नो॑ गहि स॒ख्येभि॑: शि॒वेभि॑र्म॒हान्म॒हीभि॑रू॒तिभि॑: सर॒ण्यन्

Sukta 31.translation: “Worshipping him with reverence, like anaṅgiras, I make the ancient (Indra) renovate to accept the oblation; destroy the many impious oppressors (of your worshippers) and bestow upon us,Maghavan, yours own (wealth) for our acceptance.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तम॑ङ्गिर॒स्वन्नम॑सा सप॒र्यन्नव्यं॑ कृणोमि॒ सन्य॑से पुरा॒जाम् । द्रुहो॒ वि या॑हि बहु॒ला अदे॑वी॒: स्व॑श्च नो मघवन्त्सा॒तये॑ धाः

Sukta 31.translation: “You purifying water have been spread abroad; fill their beds for our welfare; riding on the car, defend us from the malevolent, and make us quickly the conquerors of cattle.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मिह॑: पाव॒काः प्रत॑ता अभूवन्त्स्व॒स्ति न॑: पिपृहि पा॒रमा॑साम् । इन्द्र॒ त्वं र॑थि॒रः पा॑हि नो रि॒षो म॒क्षूम॑क्षू कृणुहि गो॒जितो॑ नः

Sukta 31.translation: “Indra, the slayer ofVṛtra, the lord of herds, has discovered the cattle, and by his radiant effulgence driven away the black (asuras), and indicating with veracity (to theaṅgirasas) the honest (kine), heshutthe gate uon all their own cattle.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अदे॑दिष्ट वृत्र॒हा गोप॑ति॒र्गा अ॒न्तः कृ॒ष्णाँ अ॑रु॒षैर्धाम॑भिर्गात् । प्र सू॒नृता॑ दि॒शमा॑न ऋ॒तेन॒ दुर॑श्च॒ विश्वा॑ अवृणो॒दप॒ स्वाः

Sukta 31.translation: “We invoke for our protection the opulentIndra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praise), terriblein battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.”
Sukta 31.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ । शृ॒ण्वन्त॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नन्तं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नाम्

devanagari.text: इंद्र सोमं सोमपते पिबेमं माध्यंदिनं सवनं चारु यत्ते ।प्रप्रुथ्या शिप्रे मघवन्नृजीषिन्विमुच्या हरी इह मादयस्व ॥

Sukta 32.translation: “Indra, lord of theSoma, drink this Soma which is grateful to you at noon-day sacrifice,Maghavan, partake of the spiritless Soma, unyoke your horses, and filling their jaws (with fodder), exhilarate them at this ceremony.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॒ सोमं॑ सोमपते॒ पिबे॒मं माध्यं॑दिनं॒ सव॑नं॒ चारु॒ यत्ते॑ । प्र॒प्रुथ्या॒ शिप्रे॑ मघवन्नृजीषिन्वि॒मुच्या॒ हरी॑ इ॒ह मा॑दयस्व

Sukta 32.translation: “Indra, drink theSomamixed with milk, with butter-milk, or fresh; we offer it for your exhilaration, associated with the devout company of theMarutsand theRudras; drink it till you are satisfied.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: गवा॑शिरं म॒न्थिन॑मिन्द्र शु॒क्रं पिबा॒ सोमं॑ ररि॒मा ते॒ मदा॑य । ब्र॒ह्म॒कृता॒ मारु॑तेना ग॒णेन॑ स॒जोषा॑ रु॒द्रैस्तृ॒पदा वृ॑षस्व

Sukta 32.translation: “These are theMaruts,Indra, who, worshipping your prowess, augment your withering force (by their aid); attended by theRudras, drink, wielder of the thunder-bolt, and handsome-chinned, at the noon-day sacrifice.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ये ते॒ शुष्मं॒ ये तवि॑षी॒मव॑र्ध॒न्नर्च॑न्त इन्द्र म॒रुत॑स्त॒ ओज॑: । माध्यं॑दिने॒ सव॑ने वज्रहस्त॒ पिबा॑ रु॒द्रेभि॒: सग॑णः सुशिप्र

Sukta 32.translation: “Those were theMarutswho were the strength ofIndra, and genitive ly encouraged him; animated by whom he pierced the vital part ofVṛtra, fancying himself vulnerable.”

Sukta 32.translation: “Phased with the sacrifice, as if it was that ofManu, drink,Indra, theSoma, for the sake of perpetual vigour; come, lord of the tawny steeds, with the adorableMaruts, and with the traversers (of the air); send down the waters (of the firmament) to (blend with) the waters of the earth.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒नु॒ष्वदि॑न्द्र॒ सव॑नं जुषा॒णः पिबा॒ सोमं॒ शश्व॑ते वी॒र्या॑य । स आ व॑वृत्स्व हर्यश्व य॒ज्ञैः स॑र॒ण्युभि॑र॒पो अर्णा॑ सिसर्षि

Sukta 32.translation: “Inasmuch as you have slain with active strife the slumbering, darking, water-investingVṛtra, you have let forth the bright waters like horses (rushing) into battle.”

Sukta 32.translation: “Therefore we sacrifice with reverence to the vast and mightyIndra, who is adorable, undecaying, young; whose magnitude the unbounded heaven and earth have not measures, nor can measure.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यजा॑म॒ इन्नम॑सा वृ॒द्धमिन्द्रं॑ बृ॒हन्त॑मृ॒ष्वम॒जरं॒ युवा॑नम् । यस्य॑ प्रि॒ये म॒मतु॑र्य॒ज्ञिय॑स्य॒ न रोद॑सी महि॒मानं॑ म॒माते॑

Sukta 32.translation: “All the gods cannot detract from the many glorious exploits, and pious works ofIndra; he who has upheld earth, and heaven, and the firmament, and who, the performer of great deeds, has engendered the sun and the dawn.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॑स्य॒ कर्म॒ सुकृ॑ता पु॒रूणि॑ व्र॒तानि॑ दे॒वा न मि॑नन्ति॒ विश्वे॑ । दा॒धार॒ यः पृ॑थि॒वीं द्यामु॒तेमां ज॒जान॒ सूर्य॑मु॒षसं॑ सु॒दंसा॑:

Sukta 32.translation: “Doer of no wrong, such was your true greatness, that as soon as born, you have quaffed theSoma; neither the heavens, nor days, nor months, nor years, resist the force of you who is mighty.”

Sukta 32.translation: “As soon as born in the highest heaven, you have quaffed,Indra, theSomafor your exhilaration; and when you had pervaded the heaven and earth, you became the primary artificer (of creation).”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं स॒द्यो अ॑पिबो जा॒त इ॑न्द्र॒ मदा॑य॒ सोमं॑ पर॒मे व्यो॑मन् । यद्ध॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी आवि॑वेशी॒रथा॑भवः पू॒र्व्यः का॒रुधा॑याः

Sukta 32.translation: “Indra, from whom many are born; you who is vigorous have slain Ahi, enveloping the slumbering water and confiding in his prowess; yet the heaven apprehended not your greatness as you remained concealing the earth by on eof your flames.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अह॒न्नहिं॑ परि॒शया॑न॒मर्ण॑ ओजा॒यमा॑नं तुविजात॒ तव्या॑न् । न ते॑ महि॒त्वमनु॑ भू॒दध॒ द्यौर्यद॒न्यया॑ स्फि॒ग्या॒३॒॑ क्षामव॑स्थाः

Sukta 32.translation: “This our sacrifice,Indra, is your augmentation, for the rite in which theSomais effused is acceptable to you do you who is deserving of worship protect the worshipper by (the efficacy of) the worship, and may this sacrifice strengthen your thunderbolt for the slaying of Ahi.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य॒ज्ञो हि त॑ इन्द्र॒ वर्ध॑नो॒ भूदु॒त प्रि॒यः सु॒तसो॑मो मि॒येध॑: । य॒ज्ञेन॑ य॒ज्ञम॑व य॒ज्ञिय॒: सन्य॒ज्ञस्ते॒ वज्र॑महि॒हत्य॑ आवत्

Sukta 32.translation: “The worshipper, by his conservatory sacrifice, has madeIndrapresent; may Ibring him to my presence to obtain new wealth, him who has been exalted by praise, whether ancient, medieval, or recent.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य॒ज्ञेनेन्द्र॒मव॒सा च॑क्रे अ॒र्वागैनं॑ सु॒म्नाय॒ नव्य॑से ववृत्याम् । यः स्तोमे॑भिर्वावृ॒धे पू॒र्व्येभि॒र्यो म॑ध्य॒मेभि॑रु॒त नूत॑नेभिः

Sukta 32.translation: “When the thought of glorifyingIndraentered my mind, then I gave birth (to his praises); may I laud him before encountering distant (evil) days, whereby he may guide us beyond sin; for those on both sides of us invoke him, as (those on either bank of a river hail) a passenger in a boat.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि॒वेष॒ यन्मा॑ धि॒षणा॑ ज॒जान॒ स्तवै॑ पु॒रा पार्या॒दिन्द्र॒मह्न॑: । अंह॑सो॒ यत्र॑ पी॒पर॒द्यथा॑ नो ना॒वेव॒ यान्त॑मु॒भये॑ हवन्ते

Sukta 32.translation: “The vase is filled for him (withSoma); welcomeIndra; I pour it out for you to drink, as a water-carrier (pours water) from his bag; may the grateful Soma flow in reverence round Indra for his exhilaration.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आपू॑र्णो अस्य क॒लश॒: स्वाहा॒ सेक्ते॑व॒ कोशं॑ सिसिचे॒ पिब॑ध्यै । समु॑ प्रि॒या आव॑वृत्र॒न्मदा॑य प्रदक्षि॒णिद॒भि सोमा॑स॒ इन्द्र॑म्

Sukta 32.translation: “Invoked of many, the deep ocean arrests you not, nor do the accompanying mountains (stay you); and therefore, summoned by your friends, you have repressed the strong flame abiding in the abyss.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न त्वा॑ गभी॒रः पु॑रुहूत॒ सिन्धु॒र्नाद्र॑य॒: परि॒ षन्तो॑ वरन्त । इ॒त्था सखि॑भ्य इषि॒तो यदि॒न्द्रा दृ॒ळ्हं चि॒दरु॑जो॒ गव्य॑मू॒र्वम्

Sukta 32.translation: “We invoke for our protection the opulentIndra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ । शृ॒ण्वन्त॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नन्तं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नाम्

Sukta 33.translation: “Rushing from the flanks of the mountains, eager (to reach the sea) like two mares with loosened reins contending (with each other in speed), like two fair mother cows (hastening) to caress (their calves), the Vipās' andŚutudri, flow readily with (united) waterṣ ”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र पर्व॑तानामुश॒ती उ॒पस्था॒दश्वे॑ इव॒ विषि॑ते॒ हास॑माने । गावे॑व शु॒भ्रे मा॒तरा॑ रिहा॒णे विपा॑ट् छुतु॒द्री पय॑सा जवेते

Sukta 33.translation: “Impelled byIndra, soliciting (his commands), you go to the ocean like charioteers (to their goal); flowing together, and swelling with (your) waves, bright (rivers) one of you proceeds to the other.”

Sukta 33.translation: “I repaired to the most material river; I went to the wide auspicious Vipās', flowing together to a common receptacle, like parent cows (hastening to) caress the calf.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अच्छा॒ सिन्धुं॑ मा॒तृत॑मामयासं॒ विपा॑शमु॒र्वीं सु॒भगा॑मगन्म । व॒त्समि॑व मा॒तरा॑ संरिहा॒णे स॑मा॒नं योनि॒मनु॑ सं॒चर॑न्ती

Sukta 33.translation: “The rivers speak: Fertilizing (the land) with this (our) current, we are flowing to the receptacle which has been appointed by the deity (Indra); the course appointed for our going (permits) not of delay; of what is the sage desirious, that he addresses the rivers?”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ना व॒यं पय॑सा॒ पिन्व॑माना॒ अनु॒ योनिं॑ दे॒वकृ॑तं॒ चर॑न्तीः । न वर्त॑वे प्रस॒वः सर्ग॑तक्तः किं॒युर्विप्रो॑ न॒द्यो॑ जोहवीति

Sukta 33.translation: “Viśvāmitraspeaks: Rivers, charged with water, rest a moment from your course at my request, who go to gather theSoma; I, the son ofKuśika, desirous of protection, address with earnest prayer especially the river before me.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रम॑ध्वं मे॒ वच॑से सो॒म्याय॒ ऋता॑वरी॒रुप॑ मुहू॒र्तमेवै॑: । प्र सिन्धु॒मच्छा॑ बृह॒ती म॑नी॒षाव॒स्युर॑ह्वे कुशि॒कस्य॑ सू॒नुः

Sukta 33.translation: “The rivers speak;Indra, the wielder of the thunder-bolt, dug our channels when he slew Ahi the blocker-up of rivers; the divine and well-handedSavitāhas led us (on our path), and obedient tohis commands we flow (as) ample (streams).”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रो॑ अ॒स्माँ अ॑रद॒द्वज्र॑बाहु॒रपा॑हन्वृ॒त्रं प॑रि॒धिं न॒दीना॑म् । दे॒वो॑ऽनयत्सवि॒ता सु॑पा॒णिस्तस्य॑ व॒यं प्र॑स॒वे या॑म उ॒र्वीः

Sukta 33.translation: “Viśvāmitraspeaks: Ever is that heroic exploit ofIndrato be celebrated when he cut Ahi to pieces, and with his thunderbolt destroyed the surrounding (obstructors of the rain), whence the waters proceed in the direction they desire.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र॒वाच्यं॑ शश्व॒धा वी॒र्यं१॒॑ तदिन्द्र॑स्य॒ कर्म॒ यदहिं॑ विवृ॒श्चत् । वि वज्रे॑ण परि॒षदो॑ जघा॒नाय॒न्नापोऽय॑नमि॒च्छमा॑नाः

Sukta 33.translation: “The rivers speak: Praiser ofIndra, forget not this speech, nor the worlds that (you have addressed to us) for future ages (to reverence); celebrator (of holy rites), be favourable to us in solemn prayers; treat us not after the (arrogant fashion) of men; salutation be to you!”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒तद्वचो॑ जरित॒र्मापि॑ मृष्ठा॒ आ यत्ते॒ घोषा॒नुत्त॑रा यु॒गानि॑ । उ॒क्थेषु॑ कारो॒ प्रति॑ नो जुषस्व॒ मा नो॒ नि क॑: पुरुष॒त्रा नम॑स्ते

Sukta 33.translation: “Viśvāmitraspeaks: Listen, sister (streams), kindly to him who praises you; who has come from afar with a waggon and chariot; bow down lowly; become easily fordable; remain, rivers, lower than the axle (of the wheel) with your currents.”

Sukta 33.translation: “The rivers speak: Hymner, we hear your words, that you have come from afar with a wagon and chariot; we bow down before you; like a woman nursing (her child), like a maiden bending to embrace a man, (so will we do) for you.”

Sukta 33.translation: “Viśvāmitraspeaks: (Since), rivers, (you have allowed me to cross), so may theBharataspass over (your united stream); may the troop desiring to cross the water, permitted (by you), and impelled byIndra, pass; then let the course appinted for your going (be resumed); I have recourse to the favour of you who are worthy of adoration.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद॒ङ्ग त्वा॑ भर॒ताः सं॒तरे॑युर्ग॒व्यन्ग्राम॑ इषि॒त इन्द्र॑जूतः । अर्षा॒दह॑ प्रस॒वः सर्ग॑तक्त॒ आ वो॑ वृणे सुम॒तिं य॒ज्ञिया॑नाम्

Sukta 33.translation: “TheBharatāsseeking cattle passed over; the sage enjoyed the favour of the rivers; streams dispensing food, productive of wealth, spread abundance, fill (your beds), flow swiftly.”

Sukta 33.translation: “Let your waves (rivers) so flow that the pin of the yoke may be above (their) waters; leave the traces full, and may (the two streams), exempt from misfortune or defect, and uncensured, exhibit no (present) increase.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उद्व॑ ऊ॒र्मिः शम्या॑ ह॒न्त्वापो॒ योक्त्रा॑णि मुञ्चत । मादु॑ष्कृतौ॒ व्ये॑नसा॒घ्न्यौ शून॒मार॑ताम्

Sukta 34.translation: “Indra, the destroyer of cities, possessed of wealth manifesting (his greatness), merciless to his enemies has overspread the day with his radiance; attracted by prayer, increasing in bulk, and armed with many weapons, he has delighted both heaven and earth.”
Sukta 34.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॑: पू॒र्भिदाति॑र॒द्दास॑म॒र्कैर्वि॒दद्व॑सु॒र्दय॑मानो॒ वि शत्रू॑न् । ब्रह्म॑जूतस्त॒न्वा॑ वावृधा॒नो भूरि॑दात्र॒ आपृ॑ण॒द्रोद॑सी उ॒भे

Sukta 34.translation: “Decorating you, I address sincere prayers to you who are adorable and mighty, for the sake of (obtaining) food; you,Indraare the preceder of men the descendants ofmanu, and of the descendants of the gods.”
Sukta 34.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒खस्य॑ ते तवि॒षस्य॒ प्र जू॒तिमिय॑र्मि॒ वाच॑म॒मृता॑य॒ भूष॑न् । इन्द्र॑ क्षिती॒नाम॑सि॒ मानु॑षीणां वि॒शां दैवी॑नामु॒त पू॑र्व॒यावा॑

Sukta 34.translation: “Indra, of glorious deeds, destroyedVṛtra; resistless in combat, he has overcome the deceivers resolved to consume him; he slew the mutilated (demon lurking) in the woods, and made manifest the (stolen) kine (that had been hidden) in the night.”

transliteration.text: úpo íti ǀ nayasva ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ tapuḥ-pā́ ǀ utá ǀ īm ǀ ava ǀ tvám ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀgrásetām ǀ áśvā ǀ ví ǀ muca ǀ ihá ǀ śóṇā ǀ divé-dive ǀ sa-dṛ́śīḥ ǀ addhi ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “Showerer (of benefits), giver of food, guide hither your vigorous horses, defending (us) against foes, and protect (your worshippers); here unharness the bay steeds, and give them fodder, and you eat daily suitable food.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उपो॑ नयस्व॒ वृष॑णा तपु॒ष्पोतेम॑व॒ त्वं वृ॑षभ स्वधावः । ग्रसे॑ता॒मश्वा॒ वि मु॑चे॒ह शोणा॑ दि॒वेदि॑वे स॒दृशी॑रद्धि धा॒नाः

devanagari.text: ब्रह्मणा ते ब्रह्मयुजा युनज्मि हरी सखाया सधमाद आशू ।स्थिरं रथं सुखमिंद्राधितिष्ठन्प्रजानन्विद्वाँ उप याहि सोमं ॥
ब्रह्मणा । ते । ब्रह्मऽयुजा । युनज्मि । हरी इति । सखाया । सधऽमादे । आशू इति ।स्थिरम् । रथम् । सुऽखम् । इन्द्र । अधिऽतिष्ठन् । प्रऽजानन् । विद्वान् । उप । याहि । सोमम् ॥

transliteration.text: bráhmaṇā ǀ te ǀ brahma-yújā ǀ yunajmi ǀ hárī íti ǀ sákhāyā ǀ sadha-mā́de ǀ āśū́ íti ǀsthirám ǀ rátham ǀ su-khám ǀ indra ǀ adhi-tíṣṭhan ǀ pra-jānán ǀ vidvā́n ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǀ sómam ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “I harness with prayer your horses, who are to be harnessed with prayer, who are allies and swift-paced in battle; arise, and all-knowingIndra, mounting on your firm and easy chariot, come to the libation.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ब्रह्म॑णा ते ब्रह्म॒युजा॑ युनज्मि॒ हरी॒ सखा॑या सध॒माद॑ आ॒शू । स्थि॒रं रथं॑ सु॒खमि॑न्द्राधि॒तिष्ठ॑न्प्रजा॒नन्वि॒द्वाँ उप॑ याहि॒ सोम॑म्

devanagari.text: मा ते हरी वृषणा वीतपृष्ठा नि रीरमन्यजमानासो अन्ये ।अत्यायाहि शश्वतो वयं तेऽरं सुतेभिः कृणवाम सोमैः ॥
मा । ते । हरी इति । वृषणा । वीतऽपृष्ठा । नि । रीरमन् । यजमानासः । अन्ये ।अतिऽआयाहि । शश्वतः । वयम् । ते । अरम् । सुतेभिः । कृणवाम । सोमैः ॥

transliteration.text: mā́ ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ vītá-pṛṣṭhā ǀ ní ǀ rīraman ǀ yájamānāsaḥ ǀ anyé ǀati-ā́yāhi ǀ śáśvataḥ ǀ vayám ǀ te ǀ áram ǀ sutébhiḥ ǀ kṛṇavāma ǀ sómaiḥ ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “Let not other sacrifices attract your vigorous and smooth-backed steeds; disregarding others, come perpetually hither, that we may propitiate you sufficiently with effusedSomalibations.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा ते॒ हरी॒ वृष॑णा वी॒तपृ॑ष्ठा॒ नि री॑रम॒न्यज॑मानासो अ॒न्ये । अ॒त्याया॑हि॒ शश्व॑तो व॒यं तेऽरं॑ सु॒तेभि॑: कृणवाम॒ सोमै॑:

devanagari.text: तवायं सोमस्त्वमेह्यर्वाङ् शश्वत्तमं सुमना अस्य पाहि ।अस्मिन्यज्ञे बर्हिष्या निषद्या दधिष्वेमं जठर इंदुमिंद्र ॥
तव । अयम् । सोमः । त्वम् । आ । इहि । अर्वाङ् । शश्वत्ऽतमम् । सुऽमनाः । अस्य । पाहि ।अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । बर्हिषि । आ । निऽसद्य । दधिष्व । इमम् । जठरे । इन्दुम् । इन्द्र ॥

transliteration.text: táva ǀ ayám ǀ sómaḥ ǀ tvám ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ śaśvat-tamám ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ asyá ǀ pāhi ǀasmín ǀ yajñé ǀ barhíṣi ǀ ā́ ǀ ni-sádya ǀ dadhiṣvá ǀ imám ǀ jaṭháre ǀ índum ǀ indra ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “Thissomalibation is for you; come down, and well disposed, drink of it unceasingly; seated on the grass at this sacrifice, takeIndra, this (libation) into your belly.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तवा॒यं सोम॒स्त्वमेह्य॒र्वाङ्छ॑श्वत्त॒मं सु॒मना॑ अ॒स्य पा॑हि । अ॒स्मिन्य॒ज्ञे ब॒र्हिष्या नि॒षद्या॑ दधि॒ष्वेमं ज॒ठर॒ इन्दु॑मिन्द्र

devanagari.text: स्तीर्णं ते बर्हिः सुत इंद्र सोमः कृता धाना अत्तवे ते हरिभ्यां ।तदोकसे पुरुशाकाय वृष्णे मरुत्वते तुभ्यं राता हवींषि ॥
स्तीर्णम् । ते । बर्हिः । सुतः । इन्द्र । सोमः । कृताः । धानाः । अत्तवे । ते । हरिऽभ्याम् ।तत्ऽओकसे । पुरुऽशाकाय । वृष्णे । मरुत्वते । तुभ्यम् । राता । हवींषि ॥

transliteration.text: stīrṇám ǀ te ǀ barhíḥ ǀ sutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ sómaḥ ǀ kṛtā́ḥ ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǀ áttave ǀ te ǀ hári-bhyām ǀtát-okase ǀ puru-śā́kāya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ marútvate ǀ túbhyam ǀ rātā́ ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “The sacred grass is strewn for you; theSoma,Indra, is poured forth; the grain wherewith to feed your horses is prepared; the oblations are offered to you abiding on the sacred grass, who is praised of many, and is the showerer (of benefits), attended by theMaruts.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्ती॒र्णं ते॑ ब॒र्हिः सु॒त इ॑न्द्र॒ सोम॑: कृ॒ता धा॒ना अत्त॑वे ते॒ हरि॑भ्याम् । तदो॑कसे पुरु॒शाका॑य॒ वृष्णे॑ म॒रुत्व॑ते॒ तुभ्यं॑ रा॒ता ह॒वींषि॑

devanagari.text: इमं नरः पर्वतास्तुभ्यमापः समिंद्र गोभिर्मधुमंतमक्रन् ।तस्यागत्या सुमना ऋष्व पाहि प्रजानन्विद्वान्पथ्या अनु स्वाः ॥
इमम् । नरः । पर्वताः । तुभ्यम् । आपः । सम् । इन्द्र । गोभिः । मधुऽमन्तम् । अक्रन् ।तस्य । आऽगत्य । सुऽमनाः । ऋष्व । पाहि । प्रऽजानन् । विद्वान् । पथ्याः । अनु । स्वाः ॥

transliteration.text: imám ǀ náraḥ ǀ párvatāḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ sám ǀ indra ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ akran ǀtásya ǀ ā-gátya ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ ṛṣva ǀ pāhi ǀ pra-jānán ǀ vidvā́n ǀ pathyā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ svā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “The leaders (of the ceremony) have prepared for you,Indra, this (libation), sweetened with milk, the stones, the water; beautiful Indra, who is favourably disposed, and who is wise, knowing well (the worship) that is according to your peculiar paths, come and drink of this libation.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मं नर॒: पर्व॑ता॒स्तुभ्य॒माप॒: समि॑न्द्र॒ गोभि॒र्मधु॑मन्तमक्रन् । तस्या॒गत्या॑ सु॒मना॑ ऋष्व पाहि प्रजा॒नन्वि॒द्वान्प॒थ्या॒३॒॑ अनु॒ स्वाः

devanagari.text: याँ आभजो मरुत इंद्र सोमे ये त्वामवर्धन्नभवन्गणस्ते ।तेभिरेतं सजोषा वावशानोऽग्नेः पिब जिह्वया सोममिंद्र ॥
यान् । आ । अभजः । मरुतः । इन्द्र । सोमे । ये । त्वाम् । अवर्धन् । अभवन् । गणः । ते ।तेभिः । एतम् । सऽजोषाः । वावशानः । अग्नेः । पिब । जिह्वया । सोमम् । इन्द्र ॥

transliteration.text: yā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ ábhajaḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ indra ǀ sóme ǀ yé ǀ tvā́m ǀ ávardhan ǀ ábhavan ǀ gaṇáḥ ǀ te ǀtébhiḥ ǀ etám ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ vāvaśānáḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ piba ǀ jihváyā ǀ sómam ǀ indra ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “Associated,Indra, with thoseMarutswith whom you have shared in the libation, who encouraged you (in battle), and are your attendant troop, drink, desirous of theSoma, along with them, with the tongue ofAgni.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: याँ आभ॑जो म॒रुत॑ इन्द्र॒ सोमे॒ ये त्वामव॑र्ध॒न्नभ॑वन्ग॒णस्ते॑ । तेभि॑रे॒तं स॒जोषा॑ वावशा॒नो॒३॒॑ऽग्नेः पि॑ब जि॒ह्वया॒ सोम॑मिन्द्र

devanagari.text: इंद्र पिब स्वधया चित्सुतस्याग्नेर्वा पाहि जिह्वया यजत्र ।अध्वर्योर्वा प्रयतं शक्र हस्ताद्धोतुर्वा यज्ञं हविषो जुषस्व ॥
इन्द्र । पिब । स्वधया । चित् । सुतस्य । अग्नेः । वा । पाहि । जिह्वया । यजत्र ।अध्वर्योः । वा । प्रऽयतम् । शक्र । हस्तात् । होतुः । वा । यज्ञम् । हविषः । जुषस्व ॥

transliteration.text: índra ǀ píba ǀ svadháyā ǀ cit ǀ sutásya ǀ agnéḥ ǀ vā ǀ pāhi ǀ jihváyā ǀ yajatra ǀadhvaryóḥ ǀ vā ǀ prá-yatam ǀ śakra ǀ hástāt ǀ hótuḥ ǀ vā ǀ yajñám ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ juṣasva ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “AdorableIndra, drink of the effused libation, either by your own effort, or through the tongue ofAgni; drink it,Śakra, offered by thehandof theadhvaryu, or accept the presentation of the oblation (from the hand) of theHotā.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॒ पिब॑ स्व॒धया॑ चित्सु॒तस्या॒ग्नेर्वा॑ पाहि जि॒ह्वया॑ यजत्र । अ॒ध्व॒र्योर्वा॒ प्रय॑तं शक्र॒ हस्ता॒द्धोतु॑र्वा य॒ज्ञं ह॒विषो॑ जुषस्व

devanagari.text: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ ।शृण्वंतमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नंतं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानां ॥
शुनम् । हुवेम । मघऽवानम् । इन्द्रम् । अस्मिन् । भरे । नृऽतमम् । वाजऽसातौ ।शृण्वन्तम् । उग्रम् । ऊतये । समत्ऽसु । घ्नन्तम् । वृत्राणि । सम्ऽजितम् । धनानाम् ॥

transliteration.text: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ

Sukta 35.translation: “We invoke for our protection the opulentIndradistinguished in this combat; the leader in the food bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.”
Sukta 35.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ । शृ॒ण्वन्त॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नन्तं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नाम्

devanagari.text: इमामू षु प्रभृतिं सातये धाः शश्वच्छश्वदूतिभिर्यादमानः ।सुतेसुते वावृधे वर्धनेभिर्यः कर्मभिर्महद्भिः सुश्रुतो भूत् ॥
इमाम् । ऊं इति । सु । प्रऽभृतिम् । सातये । धाः । शश्वत्ऽशश्वत् । ऊतिऽभिः । यादमानः ।सुतेऽसुते । ववृधे । वर्धनेभिः । यः । कर्मऽभिः । महत्ऽभिः । सुऽश्रुतः । भूत् ॥

transliteration.text: imā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ prá-bhṛtim ǀ sātáye ǀ dhāḥ ǀ śáśvat-śaśvat ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ yā́damānaḥ ǀsuté-sute ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ várdhanebhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ kárma-bhiḥ ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ sú-śrutaḥ ǀ bhū́t ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “Indra, who is constantly seeking (association) with your allies (theMaruts) accept this, our offering (made) for the grant (from you of riches); for you are one who grows with augmenting energies, through reiterated libations, and has been renowned for glorious deeds.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मामू॒ षु प्रभृ॑तिं सा॒तये॑ धा॒: शश्व॑च्छश्वदू॒तिभि॒र्याद॑मानः । सु॒तेसु॑ते वावृधे॒ वर्ध॑नेभि॒र्यः कर्म॑भिर्म॒हद्भि॒: सुश्रु॑तो॒ भूत्

devanagari.text: इंद्राय सोमाः प्रदिवो विदाना ऋभुर्येभिर्वृषपर्वा विहायाः ।प्रयम्यमानान्प्रति षू गृभायेंद्र पिब वृषधूतस्य वृष्णः ॥
इन्द्राय । सोमाः । प्रऽदिवः । विदानाः । ऋभुः । येभिः । वृषऽपर्वा । विऽहायाः ।प्रऽयम्यमानान् । प्रति । सु । गृभाय । इन्द्र । पिब । वृषऽधूतस्य । वृष्णः ॥

transliteration.text: índrāya ǀ sómāḥ ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ vídānāḥ ǀ ṛbhúḥ ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-parvā ǀ ví-hāyāḥ ǀpra-yamyámānān ǀ práti ǀ sú ǀ gṛbhāya ǀ índra ǀ píba ǀ vṛ́ṣa-dhūtasya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “ToIndrahave libations been presented in the days of old, whereby he has become illustrious, the regulator of time, the granter of desires; accept, Indra, these prescribed (offerings), and drink of this auspicous (Soma), expressed by the stones.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑य॒ सोमा॑: प्र॒दिवो॒ विदा॑ना ऋ॒भुर्येभि॒र्वृष॑पर्वा॒ विहा॑याः । प्र॒य॒म्यमा॑ना॒न्प्रति॒ षू गृ॑भा॒येन्द्र॒ पिब॒ वृष॑धूतस्य॒ वृष्ण॑:

devanagari.text: पिबा वर्धस्व तव घा सुतास इंद्र सोमासः प्रथमा उतेमे ।यथापिबः पूर्व्याँ इंद्र सोमाँ एवा पाहि पन्यो अद्या नवीयान् ॥
पिब । वर्धस्व । तव । घ । सुतासः । इन्द्र । सोमासः । प्रथमाः । उत । इमे ।यथा । अपिबः । पूर्व्यान् । इन्द्र । सोमान् । एव । पाहि । पन्यः । अद्य । नवीयान् ॥

transliteration.text: píba ǀ várdhasva ǀ táva ǀ gha ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ índra ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ imé ǀyáthā ǀ ápibaḥ ǀ pūrvyā́n ǀ indra ǀ sómān ǀ evá ǀ pāhi ǀ pányaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ návīyān ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “Drink,Indra, and thrive; yours are these (present) libations, as were the primitive libations; you who is adorable, drink today the recent libations, as you drank those of old.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पिबा॒ वर्ध॑स्व॒ तव॑ घा सु॒तास॒ इन्द्र॒ सोमा॑सः प्रथ॒मा उ॒तेमे । यथापि॑बः पू॒र्व्याँ इ॑न्द्र॒ सोमाँ॑ ए॒वा पा॑हि॒ पन्यो॑ अ॒द्या नवी॑यान्

devanagari.text: महाँ अमत्रो वृजने विरप्श्युग्रं शवः पत्यते धृष्ण्वोजः ।नाह विव्याच पृथिवी चनैनं यत्सोमासो हर्यश्वममंदन् ॥
महान् । अमत्रः । वृजने । विऽरप्शी । उग्रम् । शवः । पत्यते । धृष्णु । ओजः ।न । अह । विव्याच । पृथिवी । चन । एनम् । यत् । सोमासः । हरिऽअश्वम् । अमन्दन् ॥

transliteration.text: mahā́n ǀ ámatraḥ ǀ vṛjáne ǀ vi-rapśī́ ǀ ugrám ǀ śávaḥ ǀ patyate ǀ dhṛṣṇú ǀ ójaḥ ǀná ǀ áha ǀ vivyāca ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ caná ǀ enam ǀ yát ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ hári-aśvam ǀ ámandan ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “The greatIndra, the victorious in battle, the defier of foes; his fierce strength and resolute vigour are exerted; verily the earth does not contain him, neither (does the heaven), when theSomalibations exhilarate the lord of the tawny steeds.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒हाँ अम॑त्रो वृ॒जने॑ विर॒प्श्यु१॒॑ग्रं शव॑: पत्यते धृ॒ष्ण्वोज॑: । नाह॑ विव्याच पृथि॒वी च॒नैनं॒ यत्सोमा॑सो॒ हर्य॑श्व॒मम॑न्दन्

devanagari.text: महाँ उग्रो वावृधे वीर्याय समाचक्रे वृषभः काव्येन ।इंद्रो भगो वाजदा अस्य गावः प्र जायंते दक्षिणा अस्य पूर्वीः ॥
महान् । उग्रः । ववृधे । वीर्याय । सम्ऽआचक्रे । वृषभः । काव्येन ।इन्द्रः । भगः । वाजऽदाः । अस्य । गावः । प्र । जायन्ते । दक्षिणाः । अस्य । पूर्वीः ॥

transliteration.text: mahā́n ǀ ugráḥ ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ vīryā́ya ǀ sam-ā́cakre ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ kā́vyena ǀíndraḥ ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ vāja-dā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ prá ǀ jāyante ǀ dákṣiṇāḥ ǀ asya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “The mighty, fierce, auspiciousIndra, the showerer (of benefits), augments (in power) as he is animated for heroic (acts) by praise; his cattle are genitive rated givers of food; many are his donations.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒हाँ उ॒ग्रो वा॑वृधे वी॒र्या॑य स॒माच॑क्रे वृष॒भः काव्ये॑न । इन्द्रो॒ भगो॑ वाज॒दा अ॑स्य॒ गाव॒: प्र जा॑यन्ते॒ दक्षि॑णा अस्य पू॒र्वीः

devanagari.text: प्र यत्सिंधवः प्रसवं यथायन्नापः समुद्रं रथ्येव जग्मुः ।अतश्चिदिंद्रः सदसो वरीयान्यदीं सोमः पृणति दुग्धो अंशुः ॥
प्र । यत् । सिन्धवः । प्रऽसवम् । यथा । आयन् । आपः । समुद्रम् । रथ्याऽइव । जग्मुः ।अतः । चित् । इन्द्रः । सदसः । वरीयान् । यत् । ईम् । सोमः । पृणति । दुग्धः । अंशुः ॥

transliteration.text: prá ǀ yát ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ pra-savám ǀ yáthā ǀ ā́yan ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ rathyā́-iva ǀ jagmuḥ ǀátaḥ ǀ cit ǀ índraḥ ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ várīyān ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ sómaḥ ǀ pṛṇáti ǀ dugdháḥ ǀ aṃśúḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “As the rivers pursue their course, the waters rush to the ocean like the drivers of cars (to a goal), so the vastIndra(hastens) from his dwelling (in the firmament), when the humble Som alibation propitiates him.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र यत्सिन्ध॑वः प्रस॒वं यथाय॒न्नाप॑: समु॒द्रं र॒थ्ये॑व जग्मुः । अत॑श्चि॒दिन्द्र॒: सद॑सो॒ वरी॑या॒न्यदीं॒ सोम॑: पृ॒णति॑ दु॒ग्धो अं॒शुः

devanagari.text: समुद्रेण सिंधवो यादमाना इंद्राय सोमं सुषुतं भरंतः ।अंशुं दुहंति हस्तिनो भरित्रैर्मध्वः पुनंति धारया पवित्रैः ॥
समुद्रेण । सिन्धवः । यादमानाः । इन्द्राय । सोमम् । सुऽसुतम् । भरन्तः ।अंशुम् । दुहन्ति । हस्तिनः । भरित्रैः । मध्वः । पुनन्ति । धारया । पवित्रैः ॥

transliteration.text: samudréṇa ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ yā́damānāḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ sómam ǀ sú-sutam ǀ bhárantaḥ ǀaṃśúm ǀ duhanti ǀ hastínaḥ ǀ bharítraiḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ punanti ǀ dhā́rayā ǀ pavítraiḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “As the rivers are solicitious (to mix) with the ocean, so (are the priests) bearing the efficient libation toIndra; holding in theirhandsthey milk theSoma, and purify the sweet Soma (as they fall) indrops through the purifying filters.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒मु॒द्रेण॒ सिन्ध॑वो॒ याद॑माना॒ इन्द्रा॑य॒ सोमं॒ सुषु॑तं॒ भर॑न्तः । अं॒शुं दु॑हन्ति ह॒स्तिनो॑ भ॒रित्रै॒र्मध्व॑: पुनन्ति॒ धार॑या प॒वित्रै॑:

devanagari.text: ह्रदा इव कुक्षयः सोमधानाः समी विव्याच सवना पुरूणि ।अन्ना यदिंद्रः प्रथमा व्याश वृत्रं जघन्वाँ अवृणीत सोमं ॥
ह्रदाःऽइव । कुक्षयः । सोमऽधानाः । सम् । ईमिति । विव्याच । सवना । पुरूणि ।अन्ना । यत् । इन्द्रः । प्रथमा । वि । आश । वृत्रम् । जघन्वान् । अवृणीत । सोमम् ॥

transliteration.text: hradā́ḥ-iva ǀ kukṣáyaḥ ǀ soma-dhā́nāḥ ǀ sám ǀ īmíti ǀ vivyāca ǀ sávanā ǀ purū́ṇi ǀánnā ǀ yát ǀ índraḥ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ ví ǀ ā́śa ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ avṛṇīta ǀ sómam ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “The stomach ofIndra(is) as capacious (a receptacle) ofSoma, as a lake, for he has partaken of it at many sacrifices; and inasmuch as he has eaten the first (sacrificial) viands, he has been the slayer ofVṛtra, and has shared the Soma (with the gods).”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ह्र॒दा इ॑व कु॒क्षय॑: सोम॒धाना॒: समी॑ विव्याच॒ सव॑ना पु॒रूणि॑ । अन्ना॒ यदिन्द्र॑: प्रथ॒मा व्याश॑ वृ॒त्रं ज॑घ॒न्वाँ अ॑वृणीत॒ सोम॑म्

devanagari.text: आ तू भर माकिरेतत्परि ष्ठाद्विद्मा हि त्वा वसुपतिं वसूनां ।इंद्र यत्ते माहिनं दत्रमस्त्यस्मभ्यं तद्धर्यश्व प्र यंधि ॥
आ । तु । भर । माकिः । एतत् । परि । स्थात् । विद्म । हि । त्वा । वसुऽपतिम् । वसूनाम् ।इन्द्र । यत् । ते । माहिनम् । दत्रम् । अस्ति । अस्मभ्यम् । तत् । हरिऽअश्व । प्र । यन्धि ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ tú ǀ bhara ǀ mā́kiḥ ǀ etát ǀ pári ǀ sthāt ǀ vidmá ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ vásu-patim ǀ vásūnām ǀíndra ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ mā́hinam ǀ dátram ǀ ásti ǀ asmábhyam ǀ tát ǀ hari-aśva ǀ prá ǀ yandhi ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “Quickly,Indra, bring (wealth); let no one impede you, for we know you to be the lord of wealth, of all treasures; and since, Indra, your greatness is munificence, therefore, lord of the tawny steeds, grant us (riches).”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ तू भ॑र॒ माकि॑रे॒तत्परि॑ ष्ठाद्वि॒द्मा हि त्वा॒ वसु॑पतिं॒ वसू॑नाम् । इन्द्र॒ यत्ते॒ माहि॑नं॒ दत्र॒मस्त्य॒स्मभ्यं॒ तद्ध॑र्यश्व॒ प्र य॑न्धि

devanagari.text: अस्मे प्र यंधि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निंद्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः ।अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीरांछश्वत इंद्र शिप्रिन् ॥
अस्मे इति । प्र । यन्धि । मघऽवन् । ऋजीषिन् । इन्द्र । रायः । विश्वऽवारस्य । भूरेः ।अस्मे इति । शतम् । शरदः । जीवसे । धाः । अस्मे इति । वीरान् । शश्वतः । इन्द्र । शिप्रिन् ॥

transliteration.text: asmé íti ǀ prá ǀ yandhi ǀ magha-van ǀ ṛjīṣin ǀ índra ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ viśvá-vārasya ǀ bhū́reḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ śatám ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ jīváse ǀ dhāḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ vīrā́n ǀ śáśvataḥ ǀ indra ǀ śiprin ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “OpulentIndra, receiver of the spiritlessSoma, give to us riches in universally desired quantity; grant us to live a hundred years; bestow upon us, Indra wiht the handsome chin, numerous posterity.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्मे प्र य॑न्धि मघवन्नृजीषि॒न्निन्द्र॑ रा॒यो वि॒श्ववा॑रस्य॒ भूरे॑: । अ॒स्मे श॒तं श॒रदो॑ जी॒वसे॑ धा अ॒स्मे वी॒राञ्छश्व॑त इन्द्र शिप्रिन्

devanagari.text: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ ।शृण्वंतमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नंतं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानां ॥
शुनम् । हुवेम । मघऽवानम् । इन्द्रम् । अस्मिन् । भरे । नृऽतमम् । वाजऽसातौ ।शृण्वन्तम् । उग्रम् । ऊतये । समत्ऽसु । घ्नन्तम् । वृत्राणि । सम्ऽजितम् । धनानाम् ॥

transliteration.text: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “We invoke for our protection the opulentIndra, distinguished in this combat; the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ । शृ॒ण्वन्त॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नन्तं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नाम्

devanagari.text: वार्त्रहत्याय शवसे पृतनाषाह्याय च ।इंद्र त्वा वर्तयामसि ॥
वार्त्रऽहत्याय । शवसे । पृतनाऽसह्याय । च ।इन्द्र । त्वा । आ । वर्तयामसि ॥

transliteration.text: vā́rtra-hatyāya ǀ śávase ǀ pṛtanā-sáhyāya ǀ ca ǀíndra ǀ tvā ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “We excite you,Indra, to exert the strength that destroysVṛtra, and overpowers hostile armies.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वार्त्र॑हत्याय॒ शव॑से पृतना॒षाह्या॑य च । इन्द्र॒ त्वा व॑र्तयामसि

devanagari.text: अर्वाचीनं सु ते मन उत चक्षुः शतक्रतो ।इंद्र कृण्वंतु वाघतः ॥
अर्वाचीनम् । सु । ते । मनः । उत । चक्षुः । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो ।इन्द्र । कृण्वन्तु । वाघतः ॥

transliteration.text: arvācī́nam ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ utá ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀíndra ǀ kṛṇvántu ǀ vāghátaḥ ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “May your praisers,Indra, who is worshipped in a hundred rites, direct your mind and your eyes towards us.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒र्वा॒चीनं॒ सु ते॒ मन॑ उ॒त चक्षु॑: शतक्रतो । इन्द्र॑ कृ॒ण्वन्तु॑ वा॒घत॑:

devanagari.text: नामानि ते शतक्रतो विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिरीमहे ।इंद्राभिमातिषाह्ये ॥
नामानि । ते । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो । विश्वाभिः । गीःऽभिः । ईमहे ।इन्द्र । अभिमातिऽसह्ये ॥

transliteration.text: nā́māni ǀ te ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ īmahe ǀíndra ǀ abhimāti-sáhye ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “We recite,Indra, who is worshipped in a hundred rites, (your many) names in all our hymns for strength to resist our foes.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नामा॑नि ते शतक्रतो॒ विश्वा॑भिर्गी॒र्भिरी॑महे । इन्द्रा॑भिमाति॒षाह्ये॑

devanagari.text: पुरुष्टुतस्य धामभिः शतेन महयामसि ।इंद्रस्य चर्षणीधृतः ॥
पुरुऽस्तुतस्य । धामऽभिः । शतेन । महयामसि ।इन्द्रस्य । चर्षणिऽधृतः ॥

transliteration.text: puru-stutásya ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ śaténa ǀ mahayāmasi ǀíndrasya ǀ carṣaṇi-dhṛ́taḥ ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “We repeat the praise of the many-laudedIndrathe supporter of man, invested with a hundred glories.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पु॒रु॒ष्टु॒तस्य॒ धाम॑भिः श॒तेन॑ महयामसि । इन्द्र॑स्य चर्षणी॒धृत॑:

devanagari.text: इंद्रं वृत्राय हंतवे पुरुहूतमुप ब्रुवे ।भरेषु वाजसातये ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “I invoke you,Indra, who is invoked of many for the slaying ofVṛtra, and the granting of food (as the spoil) of battle.”

devanagari.text: वाजेषु सासहिर्भव त्वामीमहे शतक्रतो ।इंद्र वृत्राय हंतवे ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “Be victorious,Indra, in battles; we solicit you, object of many rites, to destroyVṛtra.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वाजे॑षु सास॒हिर्भ॑व॒ त्वामी॑महे शतक्रतो । इन्द्र॑ वृ॒त्राय॒ हन्त॑वे

devanagari.text: द्युम्नेषु पृतनाज्ये पृत्सुतूर्षु श्रवःसु च ।इंद्र साक्ष्वाभिमातिषु ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “Overcome,Indra, those who are adverse to us in riches, in battle, in hostile hosts, in strength.”

devanagari.text: शुष्मिंतमं न ऊतये द्युम्निनं पाहि जागृविं ।इंद्र सोमं शतक्रतो ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “Drink,Indra, object of many rites, for our preservation, the most invigorating, fame-conferring, sleep-dispelling,Soma.”

Sukta 37.translation: “Indra, object of many rites, I regard the organs of sense, that exist in the five races (of beings dependent) on you as yours.”

devanagari.text: अगन्निंद्र श्रवो बृहद्द्युम्नं दधिष्व दुष्टरं ।उत्ते शुष्मं तिरामसि ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “May the abundant (sacrificial) food (we offer) reach you,Indra; grant us wealth that may not easily be surpassed; we augment your vigour (by our offerings).”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अग॑न्निन्द्र॒ श्रवो॑ बृ॒हद्द्यु॒म्नं द॑धिष्व दु॒ष्टर॑म् । उत्ते॒ शुष्मं॑ तिरामसि

devanagari.text: अर्वावतो न आ गह्यथो शक्र परावतः ।उ लोको यस्ते अद्रिव इंद्रेह तत आ गहि ॥

transliteration.text: arvā-vátaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ átho íti ǀ śakra ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀūṃ íti ǀ lokáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ índra ǀ ihá ǀ tátaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “COme to usŚakra, whether from afar or nigh; whatever,Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, be your region, come from thence hither.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒र्वा॒वतो॑ न॒ आ ग॒ह्यथो॑ शक्र परा॒वत॑: । उ॒ लो॒को यस्ते॑ अद्रिव॒ इन्द्रे॒ह तत॒ आ ग॑हि

devanagari.text: अभि तष्टेव दीधया मनीषामत्यो न वाजी सुधुरो जिहानः ।अभि प्रियाणि मर्मृशत्पराणि कवीँरिच्छामि संदृशे सुमेधाः ॥

transliteration.text: abhí ǀ táṣṭā-iva ǀ dīdhaya ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vājī́ ǀ su-dhúraḥ ǀ jíhānaḥ ǀabhí ǀ priyā́ṇi ǀ mármṛśat ǀ párāṇi ǀ kavī́n ǀ icchāmi ǀ sam-dṛ́śe ǀ su-medhā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Repeat (toIndra) pious praise, as a carpenter (plural nes the wood), and engaging (zealously in sacred rites), as a quick horse bearing well his burden; endowed with intelligence, and refllecting upon the future acts acceptable (to Indra), I desire to behold the sages (whohave gone to heaven).”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि तष्टे॑व दीधया मनी॒षामत्यो॒ न वा॒जी सु॒धुरो॒ जिहा॑नः । अ॒भि प्रि॒याणि॒ मर्मृ॑श॒त्परा॑णि क॒वीँरि॑च्छामि सं॒दृशे॑ सुमे॒धाः

transliteration.text: inā́ ǀ utá ǀ pṛccha ǀ jánima ǀ kavīnā́m ǀ manaḥ-dhṛ́taḥ ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ takṣata ǀ dyā́m ǀimā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ te ǀ pra-nyáḥ ǀ várdhamānāḥ ǀ mánaḥ-vātāḥ ǀ ádha ǀ nú ǀ dhármaṇi ǀ gman ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Ask of the lords (of earth, the holy teachers), the birth of those deified sages, who with well-governed minds, and diligent in sacred rites, fabricated the heavens; and may these propitiatory (praises), augmenting (your power) and rapid as the wind, reach you at this solemn rite.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒नोत पृ॑च्छ॒ जनि॑मा कवी॒नां म॑नो॒धृत॑: सु॒कृत॑स्तक्षत॒ द्याम् । इ॒मा उ॑ ते प्र॒ण्यो॒३॒॑ वर्ध॑माना॒ मनो॑वाता॒ अध॒ नु धर्म॑णि ग्मन्

devanagari.text: नि षीमिदत्र गुह्या दधाना उत क्षत्राय रोदसी समंजन् ।सं मात्राभिर्ममिरे येमुरुर्वी अंतर्मही समृते धायसे धुः ॥

transliteration.text: ní ǀ sīm ǀ ít ǀ átra ǀ gúhyā ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ utá ǀ kṣatrā́ya ǀ ródasī íti ǀ sám ǀ añjan ǀsám ǀ mā́trābhiḥ ǀ mamiré ǀ yemúḥ ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ antáḥ ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ sámṛte íti sám-ṛte ǀ dhā́yase ǀ dhuríti dhuḥ ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Comprehending hidden (mysteries) here on earth, they have, through their power, made manifest (the things of) heaven and earth; they have set limits to themby their elements; they connected them both mutually united, wide-spread and vast, and fixed the intermediate (firmament) to sustain them.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नि षी॒मिदत्र॒ गुह्या॒ दधा॑ना उ॒त क्ष॒त्राय॒ रोद॑सी॒ सम॑ञ्जन् । सं मात्रा॑भिर्ममि॒रे ये॒मुरु॒र्वी अ॒न्तर्म॒ही समृ॑ते॒ धाय॑से धुः

devanagari.text: आतिष्ठंतं परि विश्वे अभूषंछ्रियो वसानश्चरति स्वरोचिः ।महत्तद्वृष्णो असुरस्य नामा विश्वरूपो अमृतानि तस्थौ ॥

transliteration.text: ā-tíṣṭhantam ǀ pári ǀ víśve ǀ abhūṣan ǀ śríyaḥ ǀ vásānaḥ ǀ carati ǀ svá-rociḥ ǀmahát ǀ tát ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ nā́ma ǀ ā́ ǀ viśvá-rūpaḥ ǀ amṛ́tāni ǀ tasthau ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “They all ornamented (Indra) standing (in his car) and, clothed in beauty, he proceeds self-radiant; wonderful are the acts of that showerer (of benefits), the influencer (of consciences), who omniform, presides over the ambrosial (waters).”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒तिष्ठ॑न्तं॒ परि॒ विश्वे॑ अभूष॒ञ्छ्रियो॒ वसा॑नश्चरति॒ स्वरो॑चिः । म॒हत्तद्वृष्णो॒ असु॑रस्य॒ नामा वि॒श्वरू॑पो अ॒मृता॑नि तस्थौ

transliteration.text: ásūta ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ jyā́yān ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ śurúdhaḥ ǀ santi ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀdívaḥ ǀ napātā ǀ vidáthasya ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ kṣatrám ǀ rājānā ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ dadhāthe íti ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “The showerer (of benefits), the preceder and elder (of the gods), genitive rated (the waters); they are the abundant allayers of his thirst; sovereignIndraandVaruṇa, grandsons of heaven, you possess the wealth (that is to be acquired) by the rites of the splendid sacrifice.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: असू॑त॒ पूर्वो॑ वृष॒भो ज्याया॑नि॒मा अ॑स्य शु॒रुध॑: सन्ति पू॒र्वीः । दिवो॑ नपाता वि॒दथ॑स्य धी॒भिः क्ष॒त्रं रा॑जाना प्र॒दिवो॑ दधाथे

transliteration.text: trī́ṇi ǀ rājānā ǀ vidáthe ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ pári ǀ víśvāni ǀ bhūṣathaḥ ǀ sádāṃsi ǀápaśyam ǀ átra ǀ mánasā ǀ jaganvā́n ǀ vraté ǀ gandharvā́n ǀ ápi ǀ vāyú-keśān ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “RoyalIndraandVaruṇa, embellish the three universal sacrifices (and make them) full (of all requisites) for this celebration; you have gone to the rite, for I have beheld in my mind, at this solemnity, thegandharvaswith hair (waving) in the wind.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्रीणि॑ राजाना वि॒दथे॑ पु॒रूणि॒ परि॒ विश्वा॑नि भूषथ॒: सदां॑सि । अप॑श्य॒मत्र॒ मन॑सा जग॒न्वान्व्र॒ते ग॑न्ध॒र्वाँ अपि॑ वा॒युके॑शान्

devanagari.text: तदिन्न्वस्य वृषभस्य धेनोरा नामभिर्ममिरे सक्म्यं गोः ।अन्यदन्यदसुर्यं वसाना नि मायिनो ममिरे रूपमस्मिन् ॥

transliteration.text: tát ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ dhenóḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ nā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ mamire ǀ sákmyam ǀ góḥ ǀanyát-anyat ǀ asuryám ǀ vásānāḥ ǀ ní ǀ māyínaḥ ǀ mamire ǀ rūpám ǀ asmin ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Those who, for (the sake of) the showerer (of benefits), milk the agreeable (produce) of the cow, (who is known) by (many) names, they invested with the diversified strength (of theasuras) and practising delusive art have deposited their own nature in him.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तदिन्न्व॑स्य वृष॒भस्य॑ धे॒नोरा नाम॑भिर्ममिरे॒ सक्म्यं॒ गोः । अ॒न्यद॑न्यदसु॒र्यं१॒॑ वसा॑ना॒ नि मा॒यिनो॑ ममिरे रू॒पम॑स्मिन्

transliteration.text: tát ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ savitúḥ ǀ nákiḥ ǀ me ǀ hiraṇyáyīm ǀ amátim ǀ yā́m ǀ áśiśret ǀā́ ǀ su-stutī́ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ viśvaminvé íti viśvam-invé ǀ ápi-iva ǀ yóṣā ǀ jánimāni ǀ vavre ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “No one (distinguishes) my golden lustre from that of thisSavitā, in which (lustre) he has taken refuge; gratified by pious praise, he cherishes the all-fostering heaven and earth as a woman cherishes her offspring.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तदिन्न्व॑स्य सवि॒तुर्नकि॑र्मे हिर॒ण्ययी॑म॒मतिं॒ यामशि॑श्रेत् । आ सु॑ष्टु॒ती रोद॑सी विश्वमि॒न्वे अपी॑व॒ योषा॒ जनि॑मानि वव्रे

devanagari.text: युवं प्रत्नस्य साधथो महो यद्दैवी स्वस्तिः परि णः स्यातं ।गोपाजिह्वस्य तस्थुषो विरूपा विश्वे पश्यंति मायिनः कृतानि ॥

transliteration.text: yuvám ǀ pratnásya ǀ sādhathaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ yát ǀ dáivī ǀ svastíḥ ǀ pári ǀ naḥ ǀ syātam ǀgopā́jihvasya ǀ tasthúṣaḥ ǀ ví-rūpā ǀ víśve ǀ paśyanti ǀ māyínaḥ ǀ kṛtā́ni ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “You two secure the great felicity of the ancient (worshipper), that which is happiness in heaven; do you (therefore) be even about us; all those who exercise illusion, contemplate the manifold expoits of the everlasting and blandly-speakingIndra.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वं प्र॒त्नस्य॑ साधथो म॒हो यद्दैवी॑ स्व॒स्तिः परि॑ णः स्यातम् । गो॒पाजि॑ह्वस्य त॒स्थुषो॒ विरू॑पा॒ विश्वे॑ पश्यन्ति मा॒यिन॑: कृ॒तानि॑

devanagari.text: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ ।शृण्वंतमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नंतं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानां ॥
शुनम् । हुवेम । मघऽवानम् । इन्द्रम् । अस्मिन् । भरे । नृऽतमम् । वाजऽसातौ ।शृण्वन्तम् । उग्रम् । ऊतये । समत्ऽसु । घ्नन्तम् । वृत्राणि । सम्ऽजितम् । धनानाम् ॥

transliteration.text: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “We invoke for our protection the opulentIndra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ । शृ॒ण्वन्त॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नन्तं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नाम्

devanagari.text: इंद्रं मतिर्हृद आ वच्यमानाच्छा पतिं स्तोमतष्टा जिगाति ।या जागृविर्विदथे शस्यमानेंद्र यत्ते जायते विद्धि तस्य ॥

transliteration.text: índram ǀ matíḥ ǀ hṛdáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vacyámānā ǀ áccha ǀ pátim ǀ stóma-taṣṭā ǀ jigāti ǀyā́ ǀ jā́gṛviḥ ǀ vidáthe ǀ śasyámānā ǀ índra ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ jā́yate ǀ viddhí ǀ tásya ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “The praise that is prompted by the heart, and is uttered by the reciters of sacred hymns, proceeds to the presence of the lord, and is his awakener when repeated at the sacrifice; be cognizantIndra, of this praise, which is born for you.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रं॑ म॒तिर्हृ॒द आ व॒च्यमा॒नाच्छा॒ पतिं॒ स्तोम॑तष्टा जिगाति । या जागृ॑विर्वि॒दथे॑ श॒स्यमा॒नेन्द्र॒ यत्ते॒ जाय॑ते वि॒द्धि तस्य॑

devanagari.text: दिवश्चिदा पूर्व्या जायमाना वि जागृविर्विदथे शस्यमाना ।भद्रा वस्त्राण्यर्जुना वसाना सेयमस्मे सनजा पित्र्या धीः ॥

transliteration.text: diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ pūrvyā́ ǀ jā́yamānā ǀ ví ǀ jā́gṛviḥ ǀ vidáthe ǀ śasyámānā ǀbhadrā́ ǀ vástrāṇi ǀ árjunā ǀ vásānā ǀ sā́ ǀ iyám ǀ asmé íti ǀ sana-jā́ ǀ pítryā ǀ dhī́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “That praise which is begotten before (the dawn) of day is the awakener ofIndra, when repeated at the (morning) sacrifice; auspicious and clothed in white raiment is this our ancient and paternal hymn.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वश्चि॒दा पू॒र्व्या जाय॑माना॒ वि जागृ॑विर्वि॒दथे॑ श॒स्यमा॑ना । भ॒द्रा वस्त्रा॒ण्यर्जु॑ना॒ वसा॑ना॒ सेयम॒स्मे स॑न॒जा पित्र्या॒ धीः

devanagari.text: यमा चिदत्र यमसूरसूत जिह्वाया अग्रं पतदा ह्यस्थात् ।वपूंषि जाता मिथुना सचेते तमोहना तपुषो बुध्न एता ॥

Sukta 39.translation: “The parent of twins (the dawn), has brought forth the twin (Aśvins) on this occasion, (in the praise of whom) the tip of my tongue remains tremulous; they two, the dispersers of darkness, combine, assuming bodies as a pair (of twins) at the origin of the day.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य॒मा चि॒दत्र॑ यम॒सूर॑सूत जि॒ह्वाया॒ अग्रं॒ पत॒दा ह्यस्था॑त् । वपूं॑षि जा॒ता मि॑थु॒ना स॑चेते तमो॒हना॒ तपु॑षो बु॒ध्न एता॑

devanagari.text: नकिरेषां निंदिता मर्त्येषु ये अस्माकं पितरो गोषु योधाः ।इंद्र एषां दृंहिता माहिनावानुद्गोत्राणि ससृजे दंसनावान् ॥

Sukta 39.translation: “There are no revilers among men of those who were our progenitors and combatants for (the recovery of) the cattle; for the mightyIndra, the achiever of great deeds, liberated for them the numerous herds.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नकि॑रेषां निन्दि॒ता मर्त्ये॑षु॒ ये अ॒स्माकं॑ पि॒तरो॒ गोषु॑ यो॒धाः । इन्द्र॑ एषां दृंहि॒ता माहि॑नावा॒नुद्गो॒त्राणि॑ ससृजे दं॒सना॑वान्

devanagari.text: सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरभिज्ञ्वा सत्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन् ।सत्यं तदिंद्रो दशभिर्दशग्वैः सूर्यं विवेद तमसि क्षियंतं ॥

Sukta 39.translation: “A friend, accompanied by the faithful friends who had celebrated the nine months rite, and tracking the cows upon their knees, and in like manner accompanied by those ten who had accomplished the ten months' rite,Indramade manifest the true (light of the sun) (theretofore) dweling in (the) darkness (of the cave).”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सखा॑ ह॒ यत्र॒ सखि॑भि॒र्नव॑ग्वैरभि॒ज्ञ्वा सत्व॑भि॒र्गा अ॑नु॒ग्मन् । स॒त्यं तदिन्द्रो॑ द॒शभि॒र्दश॑ग्वै॒: सूर्यं॑ विवेद॒ तम॑सि क्षि॒यन्त॑म्

devanagari.text: इंद्रो मधु संभृतमुस्रियायां पद्वद्विवेद शफवन्नमे गोः ।गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हमप्सु हस्ते दधे दक्षिणे दक्षिणावान् ॥

transliteration.text: índraḥ ǀ mádhu ǀ sám-bhṛtam ǀ usríyāyām ǀ pat-vát ǀ viveda ǀ śaphá-vat ǀ náme ǀ góḥ ǀgúhā ǀ hitám ǀ gúhyam ǀ gūḷhám ǀ ap-sú ǀ háste ǀ dadhe ǀ dákṣiṇe ǀ dákṣiṇa-vān ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “Indradiscovered the sweet milk secreted in the cow, and thereupon, brought forth (from their concealment) the herd (of cattle) having feet and having hoofs; munificent (in gifts), he held in his righthandthat which had been hidden in the cavern, which was concealed in the waters.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रो॒ मधु॒ सम्भृ॑तमु॒स्रिया॑यां प॒द्वद्वि॑वेद श॒फव॒न्नमे॒ गोः । गुहा॑ हि॒तं गुह्यं॑ गू॒ळ्हम॒प्सु हस्ते॑ दधे॒ दक्षि॑णे॒ दक्षि॑णावान्

devanagari.text: ज्योतिर्वृणीत तमसो विजानन्नारे स्याम दुरितादभीके ।इमा गिरः सोमपाः सोमवृद्ध जुषस्वेंद्र पुरुतमस्य कारोः ॥
ज्योतिः । वृणीत । तमसः । विऽजानन् । आरे । स्याम । दुःऽइतात् । अभीके ।इमाः । गिरः । सोमऽपाः । सोमऽवृद्ध । जुषस्व । इन्द्र । पुरुऽतमस्य । कारोः ॥

transliteration.text: jyótiḥ ǀ vṛṇīta ǀ támasaḥ ǀ vi-jānán ǀ āré ǀ syāma ǀ duḥ-itā́t ǀ abhī́ke ǀimā́ḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ soma-pāḥ ǀ soma-vṛddha ǀ juṣásva ǀ indra ǀ puru-támasya ǀ kāróḥ ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “The discriminating (Indra) has separated the light from the darkness; may we, removed afar from evil, be ever in security; Indra, drinker of theSoma, who is nurished by Soma, be plural ased with these praises of your worshipper who is the discomfiter of his foes.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ज्योति॑र्वृणीत॒ तम॑सो विजा॒नन्ना॒रे स्या॑म दुरि॒ताद॒भीके॑ । इ॒मा गिर॑: सोमपाः सोमवृद्ध जु॒षस्वे॑न्द्र पुरु॒तम॑स्य का॒रोः
