transliteration.text: kathā́ ǀ śárdhāya ǀ marútām ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ kathā́ ǀ sūré ǀ bṛhaté ǀ pṛcchyámānaḥ ǀpráti ǀ bravaḥ ǀ áditaye ǀ turā́ya ǀ sā́dha ǀ diváḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “Why tell it to the veracious company of theMaruts? why, even when asked, to the mighty sun? why repeat it toAditi, or to the swift wind? fulfil, all-knowingJātavedas, (the worship) of heaven.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क॒था शर्धा॑य म॒रुता॑मृ॒ताय॑ क॒था सू॒रे बृ॑ह॒ते पृ॒च्छ्यमा॑नः । प्रति॑ ब्र॒वोऽदि॑तये तु॒राय॒ साधा॑ दि॒वो जा॑तवेदश्चिकि॒त्वान्

devanagari.text: ऋतेन ऋतं नियतमीळ आ गोरामा सचा मधुमत्पक्वमग्ने ।कृष्णा सती रुशता धासिनैषा जामर्येण पयसा पीपाय ॥

transliteration.text: ṛténa ǀ ṛtám ǀ ní-yatam ǀ īḷe ǀ ā́ ǀ góḥ ǀ āmā́ ǀ sácā ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ pakvám ǀ agne ǀkṛṣṇā́ ǀ satī́ ǀ rúśatā ǀ dhāsínā ǀ eṣā́ ǀ jā́maryeṇa ǀ páyasā ǀ pīpāya ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “I solicit,Agni, the milk of the cow, essential for the sacrifice; yet immature, (she possesses) the sweet and ripe (fluid); black though she be, yet with her white nutritious milk she maintains mankind in existence.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तेन॑ ऋ॒तं निय॑तमीळ॒ आ गोरा॒मा सचा॒ मधु॑मत्प॒क्वम॑ग्ने । कृ॒ष्णा स॒ती रुश॑ता धा॒सिनै॒षा जाम॑र्येण॒ पय॑सा पीपाय

devanagari.text: ऋतेन हि ष्मा वृषभश्चिदक्तः पुमाँ अग्निः पयसा पृष्ठ्येन ।अस्पंदमानो अचरद्वयोधा वृषा शुक्रं दुदुहे पृश्निरूधः ॥

transliteration.text: ṛténa ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ cit ǀ aktáḥ ǀ púmān ǀ agníḥ ǀ páyasā ǀ pṛṣṭhyéna ǀáspandamānaḥ ǀ acarat ǀ vayaḥ-dhā́ḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ śukrám ǀ duduhe ǀ pṛ́śniḥ ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “ThemaleAgni, the showerer (of benefits), has been sprinkled by the genitive ine sustaining milk; the giver of food proceeds unswerving (from his course), and the sun, the shedder of rain, has milked the white (fluid) of the udder (of the firmament).”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तेन॒ हि ष्मा॑ वृष॒भश्चि॑द॒क्तः पुमाँ॑ अ॒ग्निः पय॑सा पृ॒ष्ठ्ये॑न । अस्प॑न्दमानो अचरद्वयो॒धा वृषा॑ शु॒क्रं दु॑दुहे॒ पृश्नि॒रूध॑:

devanagari.text: ऋतेनाद्रिं व्यसन्भिदंतः समंगिरसो नवंत गोभिः ।शुनं नरः परि षदन्नुषासमाविः स्वरभवज्जाते अग्नौ ॥
ऋतेन । अद्रिम् । वि । असन् । भिदन्तः । सम् । अङ्गिरसः । नवन्त । गोभिः ।शुनम् । नरः । परि । सदन् । उषसम् । आविः । स्वः । अभवत् । जाते । अग्नौ ॥

transliteration.text: ṛténa ǀ ádrim ǀ ví ǀ asan ǀ bhidántaḥ ǀ sám ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ navanta ǀ góbhiḥ ǀśunám ǀ náraḥ ǀ pári ǀ sadan ǀ uṣásam ǀ āvíḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ jāté ǀ agnáu ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “By the sacrifice, theAṅgirasas, rending the mountain asunder, have thrown it open, and returned with the cows; the leaders (of holy rites) have arrived happily at the dawn, and the sun was manifest asAgniwas engendered.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तेनाद्रिं॒ व्य॑सन्भि॒दन्त॒: समङ्गि॑रसो नवन्त॒ गोभि॑: । शु॒नं नर॒: परि॑ षदन्नु॒षास॑मा॒विः स्व॑रभवज्जा॒ते अ॒ग्नौ

devanagari.text: ऋतेन देवीरमृता अमृक्ता अर्णोभिरापो मधुमद्भिरग्ने ।वाजी न सर्गेषु प्रस्तुभानः प्र सदमित्स्रवितवे दधन्युः ॥

transliteration.text: ṛténa ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ ámṛktāḥ ǀ árṇaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ mádhumat-bhiḥ ǀ agne ǀvājī́ ǀ ná ǀ sárgeṣu ǀ pra-stubhānáḥ ǀ prá ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ srávitave ǀ dadhanyuḥ ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “By sacrifice,Agni, the divine rivers, immortal, unobstructed, continue perpetually to flow with sweet waters, like a horse that is being urged in his speed.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तेन॑ दे॒वीर॒मृता॒ अमृ॑क्ता॒ अर्णो॑भि॒रापो॒ मधु॑मद्भिरग्ने । वा॒जी न सर्गे॑षु प्रस्तुभा॒नः प्र सद॒मित्स्रवि॑तवे दधन्युः

devanagari.text: मा कस्य यक्षं सदमिद्धुरो गा मा वेशस्य प्रमिनतो मापेः ।मा भ्रातुरग्ने अनृजोर्ऋणं वेर्मा सख्युर्दक्षं रिपोर्भुजेम ॥
मा । कस्य । यक्षम् । सदम् । इत् । हुरः । गाः । मा । वेशस्य । प्रऽमिनतः । मा । आपेः ।मा । भ्रातुः । अग्ने । अनृजोः । ऋणम् । वेः । मा । सख्युः । दक्षम् । रिपोः । भुजेम ॥

transliteration.text: mā́ ǀ kásya ǀ yakṣám ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ huráḥ ǀ gāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ veśásya ǀ pra-minatáḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ āpéḥ ǀmā́ ǀ bhrā́tuḥ ǀ agne ǀ ánṛjoḥ ǀ ṛṇám ǀ veḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ sákhyuḥ ǀ dákṣam ǀ ripóḥ ǀ bhujema ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “Go not ever,Agni, to the sacrifice of any one who injures us; nor to that of a malevolent neighbour, nor to that of an (unnatural) relation; accept not the due (oblation) from an insincere brother; let us not derive enjoyment from the enemy of a friend.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा कस्य॑ य॒क्षं सद॒मिद्धु॒रो गा॒ मा वे॒शस्य॑ प्रमिन॒तो मापेः । मा भ्रातु॑रग्ने॒ अनृ॑जोॠ॒णं वे॒र्मा सख्यु॒र्दक्षं॑ रि॒पोर्भु॑जेम

devanagari.text: रक्षा णो अग्ने तव रक्षणेभी रारक्षाणः सुमख प्रीणानः ।प्रति ष्फुर वि रुज वीड्वंहो जहि रक्षो महि चिद्वावृधानं ॥
रक्ष । नः । अग्ने । तव । रक्षणेभिः । ररक्षाणः । सुऽमख । प्रीणानः ।प्रति । स्फुर । वि । रुज । वीळु । अंहः । जहि । रक्षः । महि । चित् । ववृधानम् ॥

transliteration.text: rákṣa ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ táva ǀ rákṣaṇebhiḥ ǀ rarakṣāṇáḥ ǀ su-makha ǀ prīṇānáḥ ǀpráti ǀ sphura ǀ ví ǀ ruja ǀ vīḷú ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ jahí ǀ rákṣaḥ ǀ máhi ǀ cit ǀ vavṛdhānám ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “Agni, worthily worshipped, counservator, conciliated (by our offerings), protect us with your protections; enlighten us; entirely extirpate our sin; overcome the great and exultingrākṣasas.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रक्षा॑ णो अग्ने॒ तव॒ रक्ष॑णेभी रारक्षा॒णः सु॑मख प्रीणा॒नः । प्रति॑ ष्फुर॒ वि रु॑ज वी॒ड्वंहो॑ ज॒हि रक्षो॒ महि॑ चिद्वावृधा॒नम्

devanagari.text: एभिर्भव सुमना अग्ने अर्कैरिमान्त्स्पृश मन्मभिः शूर वाजान् ।उत ब्रह्माण्यंगिरो जुषस्व सं ते शस्तिर्देववाता जरेत ॥

transliteration.text: ebhíḥ ǀ bhava ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ agne ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ imā́n ǀ spṛśa ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǀ śūra ǀ vā́jān ǀutá ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀ juṣasva ǀ sám ǀ te ǀ śastíḥ ǀ devá-vātā ǀ jareta ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “Be propitiated,Agni, by these hymns, accept, hero, these (sacrificial) viands (presented) with praises; be plural ased,Aṅgiras, by our prayers; may the adoration addressed to the gods exalt you. (TaittirīyaSamhitā 10.62.5)”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒भिर्भ॑व सु॒मना॑ अग्ने अ॒र्कैरि॒मान्त्स्पृ॑श॒ मन्म॑भिः शूर॒ वाजा॑न् । उ॒त ब्रह्मा॑ण्यङ्गिरो जुषस्व॒ सं ते॑ श॒स्तिर्दे॒ववा॑ता जरेत

devanagari.text: एता विश्वा विदुषे तुभ्यं वेधो नीथान्यग्ने निण्या वचांसि ।निवचना कवये काव्यान्यशंसिषं मतिभिर्विप्र उक्थैः ॥

transliteration.text: etā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ vidúṣe ǀ túbhyam ǀ vedhaḥ ǀ nīthā́ni ǀ agne ǀ niṇyā́ ǀ vácāṃsi ǀni-vácanā ǀ kaváye ǀ kā́vyāni ǀ áśaṃsiṣam ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǁ

Sukta 3.translation: “Agni, creator, to you who are wise, acquainted with the past, I address, oḥ sage, these soliciting mysterious words, (these) ever-to-be-recited poems, together with praises and prayers.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ता विश्वा॑ वि॒दुषे॒ तुभ्यं॑ वेधो नी॒थान्य॑ग्ने नि॒ण्या वचां॑सि । नि॒वच॑ना क॒वये॒ काव्या॒न्यशं॑सिषं म॒तिभि॒र्विप्र॑ उ॒क्थैः

devanagari.text: कृणुष्व पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीं याहि राजेवामवाँ इभेन ।तृष्वीमनु प्रसितिं द्रूणानोऽस्तासि विध्य रक्षसस्तपिष्ठैः ॥

transliteration.text: kṛṇuṣvá ǀ pā́jaḥ ǀ prá-sitim ǀ ná ǀ pṛthvī́m ǀ yāhí ǀ rā́jā-iva ǀ áma-vān ǀ íbhena ǀtṛṣvī́m ǀ ánu ǀ prá-sitim ǀ drūṇānáḥ ǀ ástā ǀ asi ǀ vídhya ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ tápiṣṭhaiḥ ǁ

Sukta 4.translation: “Put forth your strength,Agni, as a fowler spreads a capacious snare; proceed like a king attended by his followers on his elephant; you are the scatterer (of your foes); following the swift-moving host consume therākṣasaswith your fiercest flames.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कृ॒णु॒ष्व पाज॒: प्रसि॑तिं॒ न पृ॒थ्वीं या॒हि राजे॒वाम॑वाँ॒ इभे॑न । तृ॒ष्वीमनु॒ प्रसि॑तिं द्रूणा॒नोऽस्ता॑सि॒ विध्य॑ र॒क्षस॒स्तपि॑ष्ठैः

devanagari.text: तव भ्रमास आशुया पतंत्यनु स्पृश धृषता शोशुचानः ।तपूंष्यग्ने जुह्वा पतंगानसंदितो वि सृज विष्वगुल्काः ॥

Sukta 4.translation: “Your swift and errant flames descend (on everyside); fierce-shining with vigour consume (the foe); scatter,Agni, with the ladle (of oblation), scorching flames and sparks, and brands.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तव॑ भ्र॒मास॑ आशु॒या प॑त॒न्त्यनु॑ स्पृश धृष॒ता शोशु॑चानः । तपूं॑ष्यग्ने जु॒ह्वा॑ पतं॒गानसं॑दितो॒ वि सृ॑ज॒ विष्व॑गु॒ल्काः

Sukta 4.translation: “Do you, who are most rapid, direct your (flames) against opposing (rays), and, unresisted, become the protector of this your people against the calumniator who is remote or who is nigh; let no malevolent (foe) prevail against us (who are) your worshippers.”

Sukta 4.translation: “Sharp-weaponedAgni, rise up; spread wide (your flames) against (therākṣasas); entirely consume the foes; blazing Agni, burn down him who acts as an enemy towards us like a piece of dry timber.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उद॑ग्ने तिष्ठ॒ प्रत्या त॑नुष्व॒ न्य१॒॑मित्राँ॑ ओषतात्तिग्महेते । यो नो॒ अरा॑तिं समिधान च॒क्रे नी॒चा तं ध॑क्ष्यत॒सं न शुष्क॑म्

devanagari.text: ऊर्ध्वो भव प्रति विध्याध्यस्मदाविष्कृणुष्व दैव्यान्यग्ने ।अव स्थिरा तनुहि यातुजूनां जामिमजामिं प्र मृणीहि शत्रून् ॥

transliteration.text: ūrdhváḥ ǀ bhava ǀ práti ǀ vidhya ǀ ádhi ǀ asmát ǀ āvíḥ ǀ kṛṇuṣva ǀ dáivyāni ǀ agne ǀáva ǀ sthirā́ ǀ tanuhi ǀ yātu-jū́nām ǀ jāmím ǀ ájāmim ǀ prá ǀ mṛṇīhi ǀ śátrūn ǁ

Sukta 4.translation: “Rise up,Agni, chastise those who overpower us; manifest your divine energies; slacken the strone (bow strings) of the malignant kings; destroy those (who are hostile), whether kindred or unallied.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऊ॒र्ध्वो भ॑व॒ प्रति॑ वि॒ध्याध्य॒स्मदा॒विष्कृ॑णुष्व॒ दैव्या॑न्यग्ने । अव॑ स्थि॒रा त॑नुहि यातु॒जूनां॑ जा॒मिमजा॑मिं॒ प्र मृ॑णीहि॒ शत्रू॑न्

devanagari.text: स ते जानाति सुमतिं यविष्ठ य ईवते ब्रह्मणे गातुमैरत् ।विश्वान्यस्मै सुदिनानि रायो द्युम्नान्यर्यो वि दुरो अभि द्यौत् ॥

Sukta 4.translation: “He experiences your good favour, young (of the gods), who offers praise to you aBrahman, coming quickly (to bestow felicity); to him are all prosperous days and wealth (of cattle) and treasures; do you as the lord of sacrifice, shine upon his dwelling.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स ते॑ जानाति सुम॒तिं य॑विष्ठ॒ य ईव॑ते॒ ब्रह्म॑णे गा॒तुमैर॑त् । विश्वा॑न्यस्मै सु॒दिना॑नि रा॒यो द्यु॒म्नान्य॒र्यो वि दुरो॑ अ॒भि द्यौ॑त्

Sukta 4.translation: “May the liberal man ever be prosperous who propitiate you with constant oblations and praises; may all the days in his arduous life be prosperous, and may this (his) sacrifice be (productive of reward).”

Sukta 4.translation: “I reverence your good favour,Agni; may this reiterated and resounding hymn convey due praise to your presence; may we be possessed of good horses and good cars, that we may pay you homage; and do you daily bestow upon us riches.”

Sukta 4.translation: “May every one of his own accord diligently worship you, shining in the (hall) morning and evening, every day; thus, sporting in our dwellings, (enjoying) the wealth (of hostile) man, may we with happy hearts worship you.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒ह त्वा॒ भूर्या च॑रे॒दुप॒ त्मन्दोषा॑वस्तर्दीदि॒वांस॒मनु॒ द्यून् । क्रीळ॑न्तस्त्वा सु॒मन॑सः सपेमा॒भि द्यु॒म्ना त॑स्थि॒वांसो॒ जना॑नाम्

Sukta 4.translation: “YouAgni, are the protector of him who, possessed of good horses and a golden car, approaches you with a chariot laden with wealth; you are the friend of him who gratifies you be the due performance of hospitality to you.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्त्वा॒ स्वश्व॑: सुहिर॒ण्यो अ॑ग्न उप॒याति॒ वसु॑मता॒ रथे॑न । तस्य॑ त्रा॒ता भ॑वसि॒ तस्य॒ सखा॒ यस्त॑ आति॒थ्यमा॑नु॒षग्जुजो॑षत्

Sukta 4.translation: “Invoker (of the gods), young (of the deities) possessed of excellent wisdom, through the alliance (with you produced) by holy texts, which came to me from my fatherGotama, I demolish the powerful (demons); do you who are the humbler (of foes), be cognizant of our praises.”

Sukta 4.translation: “All-wiseAgni, may your protecting (rays), unslumbering alert, propitious, unslothful, benignant, unwearied, co-operating, having taken their plural ce (at this sacrifice), preserve us.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अस्व॑प्नजस्त॒रण॑यः सु॒शेवा॒ अत॑न्द्रासोऽवृ॒का अश्र॑मिष्ठाः । ते पा॒यव॑: स॒ध्र्य॑ञ्चो नि॒षद्याग्ने॒ तव॑ नः पान्त्वमूर

Sukta 4.translation: “Those your protecting (rays),Agni, which, beholding (what had chanced), preserved the blind son ofMamatāfrom misfortune; he, knowing all things, cherished those benevolent (rays), and his enemies, intending to destroy him, wrought him no harm.”

Sukta 4.translation: “Agni, who are freed from shame, by you we are made opulent; by you we are protected; may we, through your guidance, attain abundant food; cherisher of truth, destroy both (sorts of calumniators), those who are nigh, those who are far off, and in due course fulfil (our desires).”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वया॑ व॒यं स॑ध॒न्य१॒॑स्त्वोता॒स्तव॒ प्रणी॑त्यश्याम॒ वाजा॑न् । उ॒भा शंसा॑ सूदय सत्यतातेऽनुष्ठु॒या कृ॑णुह्यह्रयाण

Sukta 4.translation: “May we propitiate you,Agni, by this fuel; accept the praise that is recited by us; consume the unadoringrākṣasas; you are to be honoured by (your) friends, preserve us from the reproach of the oppressor and the reviler.”

Sukta 5.translation: “How may we present rejoicing (fit offering) toAgnithe showerer (of benefits); toVaiśvānara, he, who, bright with great lustre, sustains the heaven, with his entire vast and insupportable (bulk), as a pillar (sustains a roof).”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वै॒श्वा॒न॒राय॑ मी॒ळ्हुषे॑ स॒जोषा॑: क॒था दा॑शेमा॒ग्नये॑ बृ॒हद्भाः । अनू॑नेन बृह॒ता व॒क्षथे॒नोप॑ स्तभायदुप॒मिन्न रोध॑:

Sukta 5.translation: “Reproach not the divine (Agni), who, accepting the oblation, has given this wealth to me, his mortal (worshipper) of mature (intellect); Agni, who is wise, immortal, discriminating, (who is)Vaiśvānara, chief conductor (of rites), the mighty.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा नि॑न्दत॒ य इ॒मां मह्यं॑ रा॒तिं दे॒वो द॒दौ मर्त्या॑य स्व॒धावा॑न् । पाका॑य॒ गृत्सो॑ अ॒मृतो॒ विचे॑ता वैश्वान॒रो नृत॑मो य॒ह्वो अ॒ग्निः

Sukta 5.translation: “MayAgni, filling both (the middling and most excellent condition), bright shining, of manifold vigour, the showerer of (benefits), the possessor of affluence, (who comprehends), by (his) wisdom the mysterious sacred hymn, as (they track) the footsteps of a (missing) cow, reveal (the sense) to me.”

Sukta 5.translation: “May the sharp-toothedAgni, possessed of excellent wealth, consume with his fierce radiance those (adversaries) who injure the firm and valued glories of the sapientVaruṇaandMitra.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र ताँ अ॒ग्निर्ब॑भसत्ति॒ग्मज॑म्भ॒स्तपि॑ष्ठेन शो॒चिषा॒ यः सु॒राधा॑: । प्र ये मि॒नन्ति॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ धाम॑ प्रि॒या मि॒त्रस्य॒ चेत॑तो ध्रु॒वाणि॑

Sukta 5.translation: “Like women who have no brethren, going (about from their own to their father's house), women adverse to their lords going astray, so the wicked, false (in thought), false (in speech), they give birth to this deep abyss (of hell).”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भ्रा॒तरो॒ न योष॑णो॒ व्यन्त॑: पति॒रिपो॒ न जन॑यो दु॒रेवा॑: । पा॒पास॒: सन्तो॑ अनृ॒ता अ॑स॒त्या इ॒दं प॒दम॑जनता गभी॒रम्

Sukta 5.translation: “Purifier,Agni, bestow on me, not neglecting your worship, this acceptable and vast (wealth), like a heavy load on a feeble (bearer), together with invigorating food; (wealth), secure, abundant, tangible, and consisting of the seven elements.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒दं मे॑ अग्ने॒ किय॑ते पाव॒कामि॑नते गु॒रुं भा॒रं न मन्म॑ । बृ॒हद्द॑धाथ धृष॒ता ग॑भी॒रं य॒ह्वं पृ॒ष्ठं प्रय॑सा स॒प्तधा॑तु

Sukta 5.translation: “May our (self) purifying praise, suited to his glory, and accompanied by worship, quickly attain to that omniform (Vaiśvānara) whose swift-ascending brilliant (orb) is stationed on the east of the earth, to mount, like the sun, above this immoveable heaven.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तमिन्न्वे॒३॒॑व स॑म॒ना स॑मा॒नम॒भि क्रत्वा॑ पुन॒ती धी॒तिर॑श्याः । स॒सस्य॒ चर्म॒न्नधि॒ चारु॒ पृश्ने॒रग्रे॑ रु॒प आरु॑पितं॒ जबा॑रु

Sukta 5.translation: “What objection (can be offered) to this my assertion, that they affirm that the milk of the kine, which (the milkers) obtain like water, is plural ced in concealment (byVaiśvānara), and cherishes the excellent and valued expanse of the wide earth.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र॒वाच्यं॒ वच॑स॒: किं मे॑ अ॒स्य गुहा॑ हि॒तमुप॑ नि॒णिग्व॑दन्ति । यदु॒स्रिया॑णा॒मप॒ वारि॑व॒ व्रन्पाति॑ प्रि॒यं रु॒पो अग्रं॑ प॒दं वेः

Sukta 5.translation: “I recognize this adorable assemblage of the great (deities), which from of old the milk-shedding cow affects, shining above the region of water, (the firmament), in secret; swift gliding, swift moving.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒दमु॒ त्यन्महि॑ म॒हामनी॑कं॒ यदु॒स्रिया॒ सच॑त पू॒र्व्यं गौः । ऋ॒तस्य॑ प॒दे अधि॒ दीद्या॑नं॒ गुहा॑ रघु॒ष्यद्र॑घु॒यद्वि॑वेद

Sukta 5.translation: “Then, radiant in association with the parents, (heaven and earth), he is awakened (to drink) the agreeable secretion of the cow, and the tongue of the assiduous (performer of holy rites), the resplendent showerer (of benefits), approaching the excellent station of the maternal (cow), seeks to drink the milk.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अध॑ द्युता॒नः पि॒त्रोः सचा॒साम॑नुत॒ गुह्यं॒ चारु॒ पृश्ने॑: । मा॒तुष्प॒दे प॑र॒मे अन्ति॒ षद्गोर्वृष्ण॑: शो॒चिष॒: प्रय॑तस्य जि॒ह्वा

devanagari.text: ऋतं वोचे नमसा पृच्छ्यमानस्तवाशसा जातवेदो यदीदं ।त्वमस्य क्षयसि यद्ध विश्वं दिवि यदु द्रविणं यत्पृथिव्यां ॥

Sukta 5.translation: “Interrogated with respect, I declare the truth, that this (wealth is acquired),Jātavedas, by the praise of you; you rule over it, (over) all that (it may be), the wealth that is in heaven or on earth.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तं वो॑चे॒ नम॑सा पृ॒च्छ्यमा॑न॒स्तवा॒शसा॑ जातवेदो॒ यदी॒दम् । त्वम॒स्य क्ष॑यसि॒ यद्ध॒ विश्वं॑ दि॒वि यदु॒ द्रवि॑णं॒ यत्पृ॑थि॒व्याम्

Sukta 5.translation: “What is the value of this (wealth) to us? what is its advantage? inform us,Jātavedas, for you know; (tell us) what is the best (course) for us on this secret path, so that we may follow unreproached the direct road.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: किं नो॑ अ॒स्य द्रवि॑णं॒ कद्ध॒ रत्नं॒ वि नो॑ वोचो जातवेदश्चिकि॒त्वान् । गुहाध्व॑नः पर॒मं यन्नो॑ अ॒स्य रेकु॑ प॒दं न नि॑दा॒ना अग॑न्म

Sukta 5.translation: “Wha tis the limit, what are the objects, which is the desirable (end) to which we rush like swift (chargers) to the battle? when for us will the divine dawns, the brides of the immortal (sun), overspread (the world) with light.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: का म॒र्यादा॑ व॒युना॒ कद्ध॑ वा॒ममच्छा॑ गमेम र॒घवो॒ न वाज॑म् । क॒दा नो॑ दे॒वीर॒मृत॑स्य॒ पत्नी॒: सूरो॒ वर्णे॑न ततनन्नु॒षास॑:

devanagari.text: अनिरेण वचसा फल्ग्वेन प्रतीत्येन कृधुनातृपासः ।अधा ते अग्ने किमिहा वदंत्यनायुधास आसता सचंतां ॥

Sukta 5.translation: “(Men are) not satisfied by unproductive, frivolous, inconclusive, scanty speech; then what,Agni, do they here say to you? devoid of the implements (of worship), let them suffer from distress.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒नि॒रेण॒ वच॑सा फ॒ल्ग्वे॑न प्र॒तीत्ये॑न कृ॒धुना॑तृ॒पास॑: । अधा॒ ते अ॑ग्ने॒ किमि॒हा व॑दन्त्यनायु॒धास॒ आस॑ता सचन्ताम्

Sukta 5.translation: “For the prosperity of this (instrumental tutor of the rite), the host (of the flames) of the kindled (Agni), the showerer (of benefits), the giver of dwellings, has blazed in the hall (of sacrifice); clothed in radiance, beautiful in semblance, and glorified by many, he shines like a man with opulence.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्य श्रि॒ये स॑मिधा॒नस्य॒ वृष्णो॒ वसो॒रनी॑कं॒ दम॒ आ रु॑रोच । रुश॒द्वसा॑नः सु॒दृशी॑करूपः क्षि॒तिर्न रा॒या पु॑रु॒वारो॑ अद्यौत्

devanagari.text: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णो अध्वरस्य होतरग्ने तिष्ठ देवताता यजीयान् ।त्वं हि विश्वमभ्यसि मन्म प्र वेधसश्चित्तिरसि मनीषां ॥

Sukta 6.translation: “Agni, ministrant of the sacrifice, do you who are entitled to worship, be above usin this offering to the gods; for you prevail over all that is desirable; you inspire the praise of the worshipper.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऊ॒र्ध्व ऊ॒ षु णो॑ अध्वरस्य होत॒रग्ने॒ तिष्ठ॑ दे॒वता॑ता॒ यजी॑यान् । त्वं हि विश्व॑म॒भ्यसि॒ मन्म॒ प्र वे॒धस॑श्चित्तिरसि मनी॒षाम्

devanagari.text: अमूरो होता न्यसादि विक्ष्वग्निर्मंद्रो विदथेषु प्रचेताः ।ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सवितेवाश्रेन्मेतेव धूमं स्तभायदुप द्यां ॥

Sukta 6.translation: “The unperplexed, the sagacious, exhilaratingAgni, the ministrant priest, has been plural ced among men for (the celebration of) sacrifices; like the sun, he spreads light above, and props the smoke above the sky like a pillar.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अमू॑रो॒ होता॒ न्य॑सादि वि॒क्ष्व१॒॑ग्निर्म॒न्द्रो वि॒दथे॑षु॒ प्रचे॑ताः । ऊ॒र्ध्वं भा॒नुं स॑वि॒तेवा॑श्रे॒न्मेते॑व धू॒मं स्त॑भाय॒दुप॒ द्याम्

Sukta 6.translation: “The ladle filled (with butter) is prepared; prompt (in act), opulent (with the oblation), the multiplying (priest), conducting (the worship) of the gods, circumambulates (the fire); the newly-trimmedpostis set up, the impending shining axe falls upon the victims.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य॒ता सु॑जू॒र्णी रा॒तिनी॑ घृ॒ताची॑ प्रदक्षि॒णिद्दे॒वता॑तिमुरा॒णः । उदु॒ स्वरु॑र्नव॒जा नाक्रः प॒श्वो अ॑नक्ति॒ सुधि॑तः सु॒मेक॑:

Sukta 6.translation: “When the sacred grass is strewn and the fire is kindled, theAdhvaryurises, propitiating (the gods), andAgni, the offerer of the oblation, ancient and multiplying (the offering), thrice circumambulates (the victim) like a keeper of cattle.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्ती॒र्णे ब॒र्हिषि॑ समिधा॒ने अ॒ग्ना ऊ॒र्ध्वो अ॑ध्व॒र्युर्जु॑जुषा॒णो अ॑स्थात् । पर्य॒ग्निः प॑शु॒पा न होता॑ त्रिवि॒ष्ट्ये॑ति प्र॒दिव॑ उरा॒णः

devanagari.text: परि त्मना मितद्रुरेति होताग्निर्मंद्रो मधुवचा ऋतावा ।द्रवंत्यस्य वाजिनो न शोका भयंते विश्वा भुवना यदभ्राट् ॥

Sukta 6.translation: “Agni, the sacrificer, the exhilarator, the sweet-spoken, the object of sacrifice, moving measuredly, circumambulates (the victim) of his own (accord); the bright (rays) of him (fed) with (sacrificial) food, spread around; all the regions are alarmed when he blazes.”

Sukta 6.translation: “Bright-shining,Agni, beautiful and auspicious is the semblance of you who are terrible and wide-spreading, for (the nights) hide not your splendour with darkness, nor do the malignant (spirits) inflict any injury on your person n.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भ॒द्रा ते॑ अग्ने स्वनीक सं॒दृग्घो॒रस्य॑ स॒तो विषु॑णस्य॒ चारु॑: । न यत्ते॑ शो॒चिस्तम॑सा॒ वर॑न्त॒ न ध्व॒स्मान॑स्त॒न्वी॒३॒॑ रेप॒ आ धु॑:

Sukta 6.translation: “Of whom, progenitor (of mankind), the benevolence is never checked; whose parents need not urge him to exertion; so that the well-satisfied, purifyingAgnishines like a friend among men, the descendants ofManu.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न यस्य॒ सातु॒र्जनि॑तो॒रवा॑रि॒ न मा॒तरा॑पि॒तरा॒ नू चि॑दि॒ष्टौ । अधा॑ मि॒त्रो न सुधि॑तः पाव॒को॒३॒॑ऽग्निर्दी॑दाय॒ मानु॑षीषु वि॒क्षु

Sukta 6.translation: “Agni, whom the twice five sisters dwelling among men, the descendants ofManu, have engendered, like feminine les, (awaking) him at dawn, feeding on oblations, brilliant of goodly aspect, and shharp as an axe.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्विर्यं पञ्च॒ जीज॑नन्त्सं॒वसा॑ना॒: स्वसा॑रो अ॒ग्निं मानु॑षीषु वि॒क्षु । उ॒ष॒र्बुध॑मथ॒र्यो॒३॒॑ न दन्तं॑ शु॒क्रं स्वासं॑ पर॒शुं न ति॒ग्मम्

Sukta 6.translation: “Your horses,Agni, breathing foam, red-coloured, straight-going well-plural ced, bright-shining, vigorous, well-membered, and of graceful form, are summoned to the worthy of the gods.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तव॒ त्ये अ॑ग्ने ह॒रितो॑ घृत॒स्ना रोहि॑तास ऋ॒ज्वञ्च॒: स्वञ्च॑: । अ॒रु॒षासो॒ वृष॑ण ऋजुमु॒ष्का आ दे॒वता॑तिमह्वन्त द॒स्माः

Sukta 6.translation: “Those, your rays,Agni, triumphant, wide-spreading, radiant, adorable, go like hawk-faced horses (to their  goal), loud-sounding like the company of theMaruts.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ये ह॒ त्ये ते॒ सह॑माना अ॒यास॑स्त्वे॒षासो॑ अग्ने अ॒र्चय॒श्चर॑न्ति । श्ये॒नासो॒ न दु॑वस॒नासो॒ अर्थं॑ तुविष्व॒णसो॒ मारु॑तं॒ न शर्ध॑:

Sukta 6.translation: “Well-kindledAgni, for you the prayer has been composed; may (the priest) propitiate (you) by (his) praise; the (sacrificer) offers worship; bestow upon us manifold (wealth); desiring (riches), men sit down adoring Agni, the invoker of the gods, the glorifier of mankind.”
Sukta 6.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अका॑रि॒ ब्रह्म॑ समिधान॒ तुभ्यं॒ शंसा॑त्यु॒क्थं यज॑ते॒ व्यू॑ धाः । होता॑रम॒ग्निं मनु॑षो॒ नि षे॑दुर्नम॒स्यन्त॑ उ॒शिज॒: शंस॑मा॒योः

Sukta 7.translation: “This invoker of the gods and minister of frequent worship, who is to be glorified at sacrifices, has been plural ced first (of the gods) by the performers of the rite; theAgniwhom Apnavāna and otherBhṛguslighted in the woods for the sake of all men, marvellous (in his acts), and soverign (over all).”
Sukta 7.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यमि॒ह प्र॑थ॒मो धा॑यि धा॒तृभि॒र्होता॒ यजि॑ष्ठो अध्व॒रेष्वीड्य॑: । यमप्न॑वानो॒ भृग॑वो विरुरु॒चुर्वने॑षु चि॒त्रं वि॒भ्वं॑ वि॒शेवि॑शे

devanagari.text: अग्ने कदा त आनुषग्भुवद्देवस्य चेतनं ।अधा हि त्वा जगृभ्रिरे मर्तासो विक्ष्वीड्यं ॥

Sukta 7.translation: “When,Agni, is the light of you, bright-shining, to be manifested; for therefore have mortals accepted you as to be worshipped among mankind.”

Sukta 7.translation: “Contemplating you in every dwelling, truthful intelligent, (brilliant with sparks) like the sky with stars, the perfecter of all sacrifices.”

transliteration.text: āśúm ǀ dūtám ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ carṣaṇī́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀā́ ǀ jabhruḥ ǀ ketúm ǀ āyávaḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavāṇam ǀ viśé-viśe ǁ

Sukta 7.translation: “Men have brought, for the sake of all people, the swift messenger of the worshipper (to the gods), who (rules) over all mankind, the manifester, the resplendent.”
Sukta 7.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒शुं दू॒तं वि॒वस्व॑तो॒ विश्वा॒ यश्च॑र्ष॒णीर॒भि । आ ज॑भ्रुः के॒तुमा॒यवो॒ भृग॑वाणं वि॒शेवि॑शे

transliteration.text: tám ǀ īm ǀ hótāram ǀ ānuṣák ǀ cikitvā́ṃsam ǀ ní ǀ sedire ǀraṇvám ǀ pāvaká-śociṣam ǀ yájiṣṭham ǀ saptá ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ

Sukta 7.translation: “They (the worshippers) have seated him in his due order, the invoker (of the gods), the intelligent, the agreeable, the purifyingly-radiant, the performer of frequent sacrifice, (brilliant) with seven flames.”

devanagari.text: स मानुषीषु दूळभो विक्षु प्रावीरमर्त्यः ।दूतो विश्वेषां भुवत् ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ mā́nuṣīṣu ǀ duḥ-dábhaḥ ǀ vikṣú ǀ pra-avī́ḥ ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀdūtáḥ ǀ víśveṣām ǀ bhuvat ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “May thatAgni, who is difficult to overcome, who is immortal, who is pre-eminent among men the descendants ofManu, becomes the messenger of all the gods.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स मानु॑षीषु दू॒ळभो॑ वि॒क्षु प्रा॒वीरम॑र्त्यः । दू॒तो विश्वे॑षां भुवत्

devanagari.text: स सद्म परि णीयते होता मंद्रो दिविष्टिषु ।उत पोता नि षीदति ॥
सः । सद्म । परि । नीयते । होता । मन्द्रः । दिविष्टिषु ।उत । पोता । नि । सीदति ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ sádma ǀ pári ǀ nīyate ǀ hótā ǀ mandráḥ ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǀutá ǀ pótā ǀ ní ǀ sīdati ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “He is conveyed into the sacrificial hall as theHotāto be adored at sacrifices, or as thePotāhe sits down (on the sacred grass).”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स सद्म॒ परि॑ णीयते॒ होता॑ म॒न्द्रो दिवि॑ष्टिषु । उ॒त पोता॒ नि षी॑दति

devanagari.text: उत ग्ना अग्निरध्वर उतो गृहपतिर्दमे ।उत ब्रह्मा नि षीदति ॥
उत । ग्नाः । अग्निः । अध्वरे । उतो इति । गृहऽपतिः । दमे ।उत । ब्रह्मा । नि । सीदति ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ gnā́ḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ utó íti ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ dáme ǀutá ǀ brahmā́ ǀ ní ǀ sīdati ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “Agnimay be the officiating priest at the sacrifice, or the master of the house in the sacrificial chamber, or he sits down as theBrahman.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त ग्ना अ॒ग्निर॑ध्व॒र उ॒तो गृ॒हप॑ति॒र्दमे॑ । उ॒त ब्र॒ह्मा नि षी॑दति

devanagari.text: वेषि ह्यध्वरीयतामुपवक्ता जनानां ।हव्या च मानुषाणां ॥
वेषि । हि । अध्वरिऽयताम् । उपऽवक्ता । जनानाम् ।हव्या । च । मानुषाणाम् ॥

transliteration.text: véṣi ǀ hí ǀ adhvari-yatā́m ǀ upa-vaktā́ ǀ jánānām ǀhavyā́ ǀ ca ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “You, who are the director (of the ceremonial), accept the oblations of devoutly-worshipping men the descendants ofManu.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वेषि॒ ह्य॑ध्वरीय॒तामु॑पव॒क्ता जना॑नाम् । ह॒व्या च॒ मानु॑षाणाम्

devanagari.text: वेषीद्वस्य दूत्यं यस्य जुजोषो अध्वरं ।हव्यं मर्तस्य वोळ्हवे ॥
वेषि । इत् । ऊं इति । अस्य । दूत्यम् । यस्य । जुजोषः । अध्वरम् ।हव्यम् । मर्तस्य । वोळ्हवे ॥

transliteration.text: véṣi ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ asya ǀ dūtyám ǀ yásya ǀ jújoṣaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀhavyám ǀ mártasya ǀ vóḷhave ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “You are willing (to fulfil) the office of messenger for the mortal whose oblations at the sacrifice you are plural ased to convey.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वेषीद्व॑स्य दू॒त्यं१॒॑ यस्य॒ जुजो॑षो अध्व॒रम् । ह॒व्यं मर्त॑स्य॒ वोळ्ह॑वे

devanagari.text: अस्माकं जोष्यध्वरमस्माकं यज्ञमंगिरः ।अस्माकं शृणुधी हवं ॥
अस्माकम् । जोषि । अध्वरम् । अस्माकम् । यज्ञम् । अङ्गिरः ।अस्माकम् । शृणुधि । हवम् ॥

transliteration.text: asmā́kam ǀ joṣi ǀ adhvarám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ yajñám ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ śṛṇudhi ǀ hávam ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “Be plural ased by our sacrifice; (be plural ased)Aṅgiras, by our offering hear our invocation.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्माकं॑ जोष्यध्व॒रम॒स्माकं॑ य॒ज्ञम॑ङ्गिरः । अ॒स्माकं॑ शृणुधी॒ हव॑म्

devanagari.text: परि ते दूळभो रथोऽस्माँ अश्नोतु विश्वतः ।येन रक्षसि दाशुषः ॥
परि । ते । दुःऽदभः । रथः । अस्मान् । अश्नोतु । विश्वतः ।येन । रक्षसि । दाशुषः ॥

transliteration.text: pári ǀ te ǀ duḥ-dábhaḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ aśnotu ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀyéna ǀ rákṣasi ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “May your inviolable car, whereby you defend the donors of oblations, be everywhere around us.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॑ ते दू॒ळभो॒ रथो॒ऽस्माँ अ॑श्नोतु वि॒श्वत॑: । येन॒ रक्ष॑सि दा॒शुष॑:

devanagari.text: अग्ने तमद्याश्वं न स्तोमैः क्रतुं न भद्रं हृदिस्पृशं ।ऋध्यामा त ओहैः ॥
अग्ने । तम् । अद्य । अश्वम् । न । स्तोमैः । क्रतुम् । न । भद्रम् । हृदिऽस्पृशम् ।ऋध्याम । ते । ओहैः ॥

transliteration.text: ágne ǀ tám ǀ adyá ǀ áśvam ǀ ná ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ krátum ǀ ná ǀ bhadrám ǀ hṛdi-spṛ́śam ǀṛdhyā́ma ǀ te ǀ óhaiḥ ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “We celebrate you today,Agni, who are like a horse (in conveying our burden) with your praises, conveying (our wishes to the gods), and (who are) like a benefactor, propitious and affectionate.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अग्ने॒ तम॒द्याश्वं॒ न स्तोमै॒: क्रतुं॒ न भ॒द्रं हृ॑दि॒स्पृश॑म् । ऋ॒ध्यामा॑ त॒ ओहै॑:

devanagari.text: अधा ह्यग्ने क्रतोर्भद्रस्य दक्षस्य साधोः ।रथीर्ऋतस्य बृहतो बभूथ ॥
अध । हि । अग्ने । क्रतोः । भद्रस्य । दक्षस्य । साधोः ।रथीः । ऋतस्य । बृहतः । बभूथ ॥

transliteration.text: ádha ǀ hí ǀ agne ǀ krátoḥ ǀ bhadrásya ǀ dákṣasya ǀ sādhóḥ ǀrathī́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ babhū́tha ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Be now the conveyer,Agni, of our auspicious, powerful, efficacious, truthful, and great sacrifice.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अधा॒ ह्य॑ग्ने॒ क्रतो॑र्भ॒द्रस्य॒ दक्ष॑स्य सा॒धोः । र॒थीॠ॒तस्य॑ बृह॒तो ब॒भूथ॑

devanagari.text: एभिर्नो अर्कैर्भवा नो अर्वाङ् स्वर्ण ज्योतिः ।अग्ने विश्वेभिः सुमना अनीकैः ॥
एभिः । नः । अर्कैः । भव । नः । अर्वाङ् । स्वः । न । ज्योतिः ।अग्ने । विश्वेभिः । सुऽमनाः । अनीकैः ॥

transliteration.text: ebhíḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ bháva ǀ naḥ ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ jyótiḥ ǀágne ǀ víśvebhiḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ ánīkaiḥ ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Agni, who like the sun are light, propitiated by these our hymns, come to our presence with all your hosts (of radiance).”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒भिर्नो॑ अ॒र्कैर्भवा॑ नो अ॒र्वाङ्स्व१॒॑र्ण ज्योति॑: । अग्ने॒ विश्वे॑भिः सु॒मना॒ अनी॑कैः

devanagari.text: आभिष्टे अद्य गीर्भिर्गृणंतोऽग्ने दाशेम ।प्र ते दिवो न स्तनयंति शुष्माः ॥
आभिः । ते । अद्य । गीःऽभिः । गृणन्तः । अग्ने । दाशेम ।प्र । ते । दिवः । न । स्तनयन्ति । शुष्माः ॥

transliteration.text: ābhíḥ ǀ te ǀ adyá ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ ágne ǀ dā́śema ǀprá ǀ te ǀ diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ stanayanti ǀ śúṣmāḥ ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Glorifying you,Agni, today, with these our praises, may we offer you (oblations); your (flames), bright as those of the sun, roar aloud.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒भिष्टे॑ अ॒द्य गी॒र्भिर्गृ॒णन्तोऽग्ने॒ दाशे॑म । प्र ते॑ दि॒वो न स्त॑नयन्ति॒ शुष्मा॑:

devanagari.text: तव स्वादिष्ठाग्ने संदृष्टिरिदा चिदह्न इदा चिदक्तोः ।श्रिये रुक्मो न रोचत उपाके ॥
तव । स्वादिष्ठा । अग्ने । सम्ऽदृष्टिः । इदा । चित् । अह्नः । इदा । चित् । अक्तोः ।श्रिये । रुक्मः । न । रोचते । उपाके ॥

transliteration.text: táva ǀ svā́diṣṭhā ǀ ágne ǀ sám-dṛṣṭiḥ ǀ idā́ ǀ cit ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ idā́ ǀ cit ǀ aktóḥ ǀśriyé ǀ rukmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ rocate ǀ upāké ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Your lovely radiance,Agni, whether by day or by night, shines upon (all objects) like an ornament (to give them) beauty.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तव॒ स्वादि॒ष्ठाग्ने॒ संदृ॑ष्टिरि॒दा चि॒दह्न॑ इ॒दा चि॑द॒क्तोः । श्रि॒ये रु॒क्मो न रो॑चत उपा॒के

devanagari.text: घृतं न पूतं तनूररेपाः शुचि हिरण्यं ।तत्ते रुक्मो न रोचत स्वधावः ॥
घृतम् । न । पूतम् । तनूः । अरेपाः । शुचि । हिरण्यम् ।तत् । ते । रुक्मः । न । रोचत । स्वधाऽवः ॥

transliteration.text: ghṛtám ǀ ná ǀ pūtám ǀ tanū́ḥ ǀ arepā́ḥ ǀ śúci ǀ híraṇyam ǀtát ǀ te ǀ rukmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ rocata ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Giver of sustenance, (Agni), your favour is free from fault, like clarified butter; your pure and golden lustre shines like an ornament.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: घृ॒तं न पू॒तं त॒नूर॑रे॒पाः शुचि॒ हिर॑ण्यम् । तत्ते॑ रु॒क्मो न रो॑चत स्वधावः

devanagari.text: कृतं चिद्धि ष्मा सनेमि द्वेषोऽग्न इनोषि मर्तात् ।इत्था यजमानादृतावः ॥
कृतम् । चित् । हि । स्म । सनेमि । द्वेषः । अग्ने । इनोषि । मर्तात् ।इत्था । यजमानात् । ऋतऽवः ॥

transliteration.text: kṛtám ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ sánemi ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ ágne ǀ inóṣi ǀ mártāt ǀitthā́ ǀ yájamānāt ǀ ṛta-vaḥ ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Truthful,Agni, verily you remove from the mortal who instrumental tutes (your) worship, whatever sin has been committed (by him) of old.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कृ॒तं चि॒द्धि ष्मा॒ सने॑मि॒ द्वेषोऽग्न॑ इ॒नोषि॒ मर्ता॑त् । इ॒त्था यज॑मानादृतावः

devanagari.text: शिवा नः सख्या संतु भ्रात्राग्ने देवेषु युष्मे ।सा नो नाभिः सदने सस्मिन्नूधन् ॥
शिवा । नः । सख्या । सन्तु । भ्रात्रा । अग्ने । देवेषु । युष्मे इति ।सा । नः । नाभिः । सदने । सस्मिन् । ऊधन् ॥

transliteration.text: śivā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ sántu ǀ bhrātrā́ ǀ ágne ǀ devéṣu ǀ yuṣmé íti ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ sádane ǀ sásmin ǀ ū́dhan ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “May our friendly and fraternal attentions to your deities prove fortunate; for such (attentions shown) in every sacrifice (form) our security in the sphere (of the gods).”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शि॒वा न॑: स॒ख्या सन्तु॑ भ्रा॒त्राग्ने॑ दे॒वेषु॑ यु॒ष्मे । सा नो॒ नाभि॒: सद॑ने॒ सस्मि॒न्नूध॑न्

devanagari.text: भद्रं ते अग्ने सहसिन्ननीकमुपाक आ रोचते सूर्यस्य ।रुशद्दृशे ददृशे नक्तया चिदरूक्षितं दृश आ रूपे अन्नं ॥
भद्रम् । ते । अग्ने । सहसिन् । अनीकम् । उपाके । आ । रोचते । सूर्यस्य ।रुशत् । दृशे । ददृशे । नक्तऽया । चित् । अरूक्षितम् । दृशे । आ । रूपे । अन्नम् ॥

transliteration.text: bhadrám ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ sahasin ǀ ánīkam ǀ upāké ǀ ā́ ǀ rocate ǀ sū́ryasya ǀrúśat ǀ dṛśé ǀ dadṛśe ǀ nakta-yā́ ǀ cit ǀ árūkṣitam ǀ dṛśé ǀ ā́ ǀ rūpé ǀ ánnam ǁ

Sukta 11.translation: “PowerfulAgni, your auspicious radiance shines upon the proximity of the sun (by day); your bright and visible (lustre) is conspicuous by night, as the bland and plural asing food (of sacrifice, the oblation) becomes manifest in your form.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भ॒द्रं ते॑ अग्ने सहसि॒न्ननी॑कमुपा॒क आ रो॑चते॒ सूर्य॑स्य । रुश॑द्दृ॒शे द॑दृशे नक्त॒या चि॒दरू॑क्षितं दृ॒श आ रू॒पे अन्न॑म्

devanagari.text: वि षाह्यग्ने गृणते मनीषां खं वेपसा तुविजात स्तवानः ।विश्वेभिर्यद्वावनः शुक्र देवैस्तन्नो रास्व सुमहो भूरि मन्म ॥
वि । साहि । अग्ने । गृणते । मनीषाम् । खम् । वेपसा । तुविऽजात । स्तवानः ।विश्वेभिः । यत् । ववनः । शुक्र । देवैः । तत् । नः । रास्व । सुऽमहः । भूरि । मन्म ॥

transliteration.text: ví ǀ sāhi ǀ agne ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ khám ǀ vépasā ǀ tuvi-jāta ǀ stávānaḥ ǀvíśvebhiḥ ǀ yát ǀ vavánaḥ ǀ śukra ǀ deváiḥ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ rāsva ǀ su-mahaḥ ǀ bhū́ri ǀ mánma ǁ

Sukta 11.translation: “Agni, who are engendered repeatedly, and glorified by sacrifice, set open heaven to him who offers you adoration; resplendent (Agni), bestow upon us that ample and acceptable (wealth), which, radiant (deity), you with all the gods, have given (to other worshippers).”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि षा॑ह्यग्ने गृण॒ते म॑नी॒षां खं वेप॑सा तुविजात॒ स्तवा॑नः । विश्वे॑भि॒र्यद्वा॒वन॑: शुक्र दे॒वैस्तन्नो॑ रास्व सुमहो॒ भूरि॒ मन्म॑

devanagari.text: त्वदग्ने काव्या त्वन्मनीषास्त्वदुक्था जायंते राध्यानि ।त्वदेति द्रविणं वीरपेशा इत्थाधिये दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥

Sukta 11.translation: “The offerings (to the gods) are engendered,Agni, of you; from you (proceed) praises; from you effective prayers; from you come a vigorous frame and wealth to man who worships with sincerity and offers oblations.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वद॑ग्ने॒ काव्या॒ त्वन्म॑नी॒षास्त्वदु॒क्था जा॑यन्ते॒ राध्या॑नि । त्वदे॑ति॒ द्रवि॑णं वी॒रपे॑शा इ॒त्थाधि॑ये दा॒शुषे॒ मर्त्या॑य

Sukta 11.translation: “From you, who are vigorous, to conveyer of oblations, the vast, the granter of what is desired, is born (a son) of real strength; from you comes wealth approved of by the gods, the source of happiness; from you,Agni, (is obtained) a swift unarrested horse.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वद्वा॒जी वा॑जम्भ॒रो विहा॑या अभिष्टि॒कृज्जा॑यते स॒त्यशु॑ष्मः । त्वद्र॒यिर्दे॒वजू॑तो मयो॒भुस्त्वदा॒शुर्जू॑जु॒वाँ अ॑ग्ने॒ अर्वा॑

transliteration.text: tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ prathamám ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ devám ǀ bhártā ǀ amṛta ǀ mandrá-jihvam ǀdveṣaḥ-yútam ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsanti ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ dámūnasam ǀ gṛhá-patim ǀ ámūram ǁ

Sukta 11.translation: “ImmortalAgni, devout mortals worship with holy rites you the first deity (of the gods), whose tongue exhilarates (them), the dissipator of sin, the humiliator (of the demons) the lord of the mansion, the unperplexed.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वाम॑ग्ने प्रथ॒मं दे॑व॒यन्तो॑ दे॒वं मर्ता॑ अमृत म॒न्द्रजि॑ह्वम् । द्वे॒षो॒युत॒मा वि॑वासन्ति धी॒भिर्दमू॑नसं गृ॒हप॑ति॒ममू॑रम्

devanagari.text: आरे अस्मदमतिमारे अंह आरे विश्वां दुर्मतिं यन्निपासि ।दोषा शिवः सहसः सूनो अग्ने यं देव आ चित्सचसे स्वस्ति ॥

Sukta 11.translation: “Agni, son of strength, since you protect (your worshippers), far (remove) from us all iniquity; far (remove from us) sin; far (from us) all evil thoughts; for proeperous is he of whom you who are radiant by night promote the well-being.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒रे अ॒स्मदम॑तिमा॒रे अंह॑ आ॒रे विश्वां॑ दुर्म॒तिं यन्नि॒पासि॑ । दो॒षा शि॒वः स॑हसः सूनो अग्ने॒ यं दे॒व आ चि॒त्सच॑से स्व॒स्ति

devanagari.text: यस्त्वामग्न इनधते यतस्रुक्त्रिस्ते अन्नं कृणवत्सस्मिन्नहन् ।स सु द्युम्नैरभ्यस्तु प्रसक्षत्तव क्रत्वा जातवेदश्चिकित्वान् ॥

Sukta 12.translation: “May he who with uplifted ladle kindles you, and thrice every day presents to you the (sacrificial) food, knowing your glory,Jātavedas, to be invigorated by the act, surpass (all others) in riches.”
Sukta 12.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्त्वाम॑ग्न इ॒नध॑ते य॒तस्रु॒क्त्रिस्ते॒ अन्नं॑ कृ॒णव॒त्सस्मि॒न्नह॑न् । स सु द्यु॒म्नैर॒भ्य॑स्तु प्र॒सक्ष॒त्तव॒ क्रत्वा॑ जातवेदश्चिकि॒त्वान्

Sukta 12.translation: “He who, labouring diligently, brings you fuel, honouring,Agni, your great glory; he who kindles you in the evening and at dawn; he, prosperous and destroying his enemies, acquires riches.”
Sukta 12.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒ध्मं यस्ते॑ ज॒भर॑च्छश्रमा॒णो म॒हो अ॑ग्ने॒ अनी॑क॒मा स॑प॒र्यन् । स इ॑धा॒नः प्रति॑ दो॒षामु॒षासं॒ पुष्य॑न्र॒यिं स॑चते॒ घ्नन्न॒मित्रा॑न्

Sukta 12.translation: “Agniis the possessor of great strength of excellent food of riches, the young (of the gods); abounding in sustenance, he gives to the mortal who worships him precious (wealth) according to (his devotion).”

Sukta 12.translation: “If, young (of the gods), with the inconsiderateness common to men, we have ever committed any offence against you, make us free from the defects of earth efface entirely,Agniour offences.”

Sukta 12.translation: “Let not us,Agni, who are your friends, ever suffer harm from any great or comprehensive offence against either gods or men; bestow forgiveness upon our sons and grandsons, the reward of what has been well done.”
Sukta 12.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒हश्चि॑दग्न॒ एन॑सो अ॒भीक॑ ऊ॒र्वाद्दे॒वाना॑मु॒त मर्त्या॑नाम् । मा ते॒ सखा॑य॒: सद॒मिद्रि॑षाम॒ यच्छा॑ तो॒काय॒ तन॑याय॒ शं योः

Sukta 12.translation: “AdorableVasus, in like manner as you have liberated the cow bound by the foot, so set us free entirely from sin; and may our existence,Agni, be prolonged.”
Sukta 12.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यथा॑ ह॒ त्यद्व॑सवो गौ॒र्यं॑ चित्प॒दि षि॒ताममु॑ञ्चता यजत्राः । ए॒वो ष्व१॒॑स्मन्मु॑ञ्चता॒ व्यंह॒: प्र ता॑र्यग्ने प्रत॒रं न॒ आयु॑:

Sukta 13.translation: “Favourably-minded,Agnihas manifested (his might) in regard to the wealth-bestowing procession of the resplendent dawns; proceed,Aśvins, to the dwelling of the pious (worshipper); the divine sun rises with splendour.”
Sukta 13.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रत्य॒ग्निरु॒षसा॒मग्र॑मख्यद्विभाती॒नां सु॒मना॑ रत्न॒धेय॑म् । या॒तम॑श्विना सु॒कृतो॑ दुरो॒णमुत्सूर्यो॒ ज्योति॑षा दे॒व ए॑ति

devanagari.text: ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद्द्रप्सं दविध्वद्गविषो न सत्वा ।अनु व्रतं वरुणो यंति मित्रो यत्सूर्यं दिव्यारोहयंति ॥

transliteration.text: ūrdhvám ǀ bhānúm ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ aśret ǀ drapsám ǀ dávidhvat ǀ go-iṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ sátvā ǀánu ǀ vratám ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yanti ǀ mitráḥ ǀ yát ǀ sū́ryam ǀ diví ǀ ā-roháyanti ǁ

Sukta 13.translation: “The divineSavitādiffuses his light on high, dispersing the dew, and like a vigorous (bull) ardent for the cow; thenVaruṇa, andMitra, and other (divinities), hasten to (fulfil) their offices when they elevate the sun in the sky.”
Sukta 13.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऊ॒र्ध्वं भा॒नुं स॑वि॒ता दे॒वो अ॑श्रेद्द्र॒प्सं दवि॑ध्वद्गवि॒षो न सत्वा॑ । अनु॑ व्र॒तं वरु॑णो यन्ति मि॒त्रो यत्सूर्यं॑ दि॒व्या॑रो॒हय॑न्ति

devanagari.text: यं सीमकृण्वंतमसे विपृचे ध्रुवक्षेमा अनवस्यंतो अर्थं ।तं सूर्यं हरितः सप्त यह्वीः स्पशं विश्वस्य जगतो वहंति ॥
यम् । सीम् । अकृण्वन् । तमसे । विऽपृचे । ध्रुवऽक्षेमाः । अनवऽस्यन्तः । अर्थम् ।तम् । सूर्यम् । हरितः । सप्त । यह्वीः । स्पशम् । विश्वस्य । जगतः । वहन्ति ॥

transliteration.text: yám ǀ sīm ǀ ákṛṇvan ǀ támase ǀ vi-pṛ́ce ǀ dhruvá-kṣemāḥ ǀ ánava-syantaḥ ǀ ártham ǀtám ǀ sū́ryam ǀ harítaḥ ǀ saptá ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǀ spáśam ǀ víśvasya ǀ jágataḥ ǀ vahanti ǁ

Sukta 13.translation: “Seven great courses convey that sun, whom the (deities), occupants of enduring mansions, and not heedless (of their offices), have formed for the driving away of darkness, (and who is) the animator of the whole world.”
Sukta 13.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यं सी॒मकृ॑ण्व॒न्तम॑से वि॒पृचे॑ ध्रु॒वक्षे॑मा॒ अन॑वस्यन्तो॒ अर्थ॑म् । तं सूर्यं॑ ह॒रित॑: स॒प्त य॒ह्वीः स्पशं॒ विश्व॑स्य॒ जग॑तो वहन्ति

devanagari.text: वहिष्ठेभिर्विहरन्यासि तंतुमवव्ययन्नसितं देव वस्म ।दविध्वतो रश्मयः सूर्यस्य चर्मेवावाधुस्तमो अप्स्वंतः ॥

transliteration.text: váhiṣṭhebhiḥ ǀ vi-háran ǀ yāsi ǀ tántum ǀ ava-vyáyan ǀ ásitam ǀ deva ǀ vásma ǀdávidhvataḥ ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ cárma-iva ǀ áva ǀ adhuḥ ǀ támaḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáríti ǁ

Sukta 13.translation: “Divine (sun), you proceed with most powerful (horses), spreading your web (or rays), and cutting down the black abode (of night); the tremulous rays of the sun throw off the darknes which is spread like a skin over the firmament.”
Sukta 13.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वहि॑ष्ठेभिर्वि॒हर॑न्यासि॒ तन्तु॑मव॒व्यय॒न्नसि॑तं देव॒ वस्म॑ । दवि॑ध्वतो र॒श्मय॒: सूर्य॑स्य॒ चर्मे॒वावा॑धु॒स्तमो॑ अ॒प्स्व१॒॑न्तः

devanagari.text: अनायतो अनिबद्धः कथायं न्यङ्ङुत्तानोऽव पद्यते न ।कया याति स्वधया को ददर्श दिवः स्कंभः समृतः पाति नाकं ॥

transliteration.text: ánāyataḥ ǀ áni-baddhaḥ ǀ kathā́ ǀ ayám ǀ nyáṅ ǀ uttānáḥ ǀ áva ǀ padyate ǀ ná ǀkáyā ǀ yāti ǀ svadháyā ǀ káḥ ǀ dadarśa ǀ diváḥ ǀ skambháḥ ǀ sám-ṛtaḥ ǀ pāti ǀ nā́kam ǁ

Sukta 13.translation: “This sun, not far removed, and unobstructed, whether (looking) downwards or looking upwards, is harmed by no one; what is the power by which he travels? who has (truly) beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven, sustains the sky?”
Sukta 13.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अना॑यतो॒ अनि॑बद्धः क॒थायं न्य॑ङ्ङुत्ता॒नोऽव॑ पद्यते॒ न । कया॑ याति स्व॒धया॒ को द॑दर्श दि॒वः स्क॒म्भः समृ॑तः पाति॒ नाक॑म्

devanagari.text: प्रत्यग्निरुषसो जातवेदा अख्यद्देवो रोचमाना महोभिः ।आ नासत्योरुगाया रथेनेमं यज्ञमुप नो यातमच्छ ॥

transliteration.text: práti ǀ agníḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀ ákhyat ǀ deváḥ ǀ rócamānāḥ ǀ máhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀā́ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ uru-gāyā́ ǀ ráthena ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ yātam ǀ áccha ǁ

Sukta 14.translation: “The resplendentAgni, by whom all is known, has manifested (his might) in regard to the dawns radiant with lustre; far-goingNāsatyas, come with your car to this our sacrifice.”
Sukta 14.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रत्य॒ग्निरु॒षसो॑ जा॒तवे॑दा॒ अख्य॑द्दे॒वो रोच॑माना॒ महो॑भिः । आ ना॑सत्योरुगा॒या रथे॑ने॒मं य॒ज्ञमुप॑ नो यात॒मच्छ॑

devanagari.text: ऊर्ध्वं केतुं सविता देवो अश्रेज्ज्योतिर्विश्वस्मै भुवनाय कृण्वन् ।आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अंतरिक्षं वि सूर्यो रश्मिभिश्चेकितानः ॥

transliteration.text: ūrdhvám ǀ ketúm ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ aśret ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ víśvasmai ǀ bhúvanāya ǀ kṛṇván ǀā́ ǀ aprāḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ antárikṣam ǀ ví ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ cékitānaḥ ǁ

Sukta 14.translation: “The divineSavitādisplays his banner on high, diffusing light through all worlds; contemplating (all things), the sun has filled heaven and earth and the firmament with his rays.”
Sukta 14.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऊ॒र्ध्वं के॒तुं स॑वि॒ता दे॒वो अ॑श्रे॒ज्ज्योति॒र्विश्व॑स्मै॒ भुव॑नाय कृ॒ण्वन् । आप्रा॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अ॒न्तरि॑क्षं॒ वि सूर्यो॑ र॒श्मिभि॒श्चेकि॑तानः

devanagari.text: आवहंत्यरुणीर्ज्योतिषागान्मही चित्रा रश्मिभिश्चेकिताना ।प्रबोधयंती सुविताय देव्युषा ईयते सुयुजा रथेन ॥

transliteration.text: ā-váhantī ǀ aruṇī́ḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ mahī́ ǀ citrā́ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ cékitānā ǀpra-bodháyantī ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ devī́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ īyate ǀ su-yújā ǀ ráthena ǁ

Sukta 14.translation: “The great and intelligent dawn, variegated with (many-coloured) rays of purple tint, bringing opulence, has come with (her) lustre; the divine Uṣas, arousing (the sleepers), proceeds with her well-harnessed car (to distribute) felicity.”
Sukta 14.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒वह॑न्त्यरु॒णीर्ज्योति॒षागा॑न्म॒ही चि॒त्रा र॒श्मिभि॒श्चेकि॑ताना । प्र॒बो॒धय॑न्ती सुवि॒ताय॑ दे॒व्यु१॒॑षा ई॑यते सु॒युजा॒ रथे॑न

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ váhiṣṭhāḥ ǀ ihá ǀ té ǀ vahantu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀimé ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ madhu-péyāya ǀ sómāḥ ǀ asmín ǀ yajñé ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ mādayethām ǁ

Sukta 14.translation: “May those robust and active horses bring you, (Aśvins), hither at the breaking of the dawn, and may theseSomajuices prepared, showerers (of benefits), for your drinking, exhilarate you at this (our sacrifice).”
Sukta 14.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ वां॒ वहि॑ष्ठा इ॒ह ते व॑हन्तु॒ रथा॒ अश्वा॑स उ॒षसो॒ व्यु॑ष्टौ । इ॒मे हि वां॑ मधु॒पेया॑य॒ सोमा॑ अ॒स्मिन्य॒ज्ञे वृ॑षणा मादयेथाम्

Sukta 14.translation: “This sun, not far removed and unobstructed, whether looking downwards or looking upwards, is harmed by no one; what is the power by which he travels? who has (truly) beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven, sustains the sky.”
Sukta 14.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अना॑यतो॒ अनि॑बद्धः क॒थायं न्य॑ङ्ङुत्ता॒नोऽव॑ पद्यते॒ न । कया॑ याति स्व॒धया॒ को द॑दर्श दि॒वः स्क॒म्भः समृ॑तः पाति॒ नाक॑म्

Sukta 15.translation: “Agni, the invoker (of the gods), like a horse (that bears a burden), is brought to our sacrifice; a deity adorable among deities.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ग्निर्होता॑ नो अध्व॒रे वा॒जी सन्परि॑ णीयते । दे॒वो दे॒वेषु॑ य॒ज्ञिय॑:

devanagari.text: परि त्रिविष्ट्यध्वरं यात्यग्नी रथीरिव ।आ देवेषु प्रयो दधत् ॥

transliteration.text: pári ǀ tri-viṣṭí ǀ adhvarám ǀ yā́ti ǀ agníḥ ǀ rathī́ḥ-iva ǀā́ ǀ devéṣu ǀ práyaḥ ǀ dádhat ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “Agni, thrice (a day), comes to our sacrifice like charioteer, bearing the sacrificial food to the gods.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॑ त्रिवि॒ष्ट्य॑ध्व॒रं यात्य॒ग्नी र॒थीरि॑व । आ दे॒वेषु॒ प्रयो॒ दध॑त्

devanagari.text: परि वाजपतिः कविरग्निर्हव्यान्यक्रमीत् ।दधद्रत्नानि दाशुषे ॥

Sukta 15.translation: “The sage,Agni, the lord of food, has encompassed the oblation, giving precious things to the donor.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॒ वाज॑पतिः क॒विर॒ग्निर्ह॒व्यान्य॑क्रमीत् । दध॒द्रत्ना॑नि दा॒शुषे॑

devanagari.text: अयं यः सृंजये पुरो दैववाते समिध्यते ।द्युमाँ अमित्रदंभनः ॥
अयम् । यः । सृञ्जये । पुरः । दैवऽवाते । सम्ऽइध्यते ।द्युऽमान् । अमित्रऽदम्भनः ॥

transliteration.text: ayám ǀ yáḥ ǀ sṛ́ñjaye ǀ puráḥ ǀ daiva-vāté ǀ sam-idhyáte ǀdyu-mā́n ǀ amitra-dámbhanaḥ ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “Radiant as thisAgni, the subduer of foes, who is kindled on the (altar) of the cast as (he was kindled) forSṛñjaya, the son of Devavāta.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं यः सृञ्ज॑ये पु॒रो दै॑ववा॒ते स॑मि॒ध्यते॑ । द्यु॒माँ अ॑मित्र॒दम्भ॑नः

devanagari.text: अस्य घा वीर ईवतोऽग्नेरीशीत मर्त्यः ।तिग्मजंभस्य मीळ्हुषः ॥

transliteration.text: ásya ǀ gha ǀ vīráḥ ǀ ī́vataḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ īśīta ǀ mártyaḥ ǀtigmá-jambhasya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “May the mortal who is strenuous (in worship) acquire authority over thisAgni, the sharp-rayed, the showerer (of benefits).”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अस्य॑ घा वी॒र ईव॑तो॒ऽग्नेरी॑शीत॒ मर्त्य॑: । ति॒ग्मज॑म्भस्य मी॒ळ्हुष॑:

devanagari.text: तमर्वंतं न सानसिमरुषं न दिवः शिशुं ।मर्मृज्यंते दिवेदिवे ॥
तम् । अर्वन्तम् । न । सानसिम् । अरुषम् । न । दिवः । शिशुम् ।मर्मृज्यन्ते । दिवेऽदिवे ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ árvantam ǀ ná ǀ sānasím ǀ aruṣám ǀ ná ǀ diváḥ ǀ śíśum ǀmarmṛjyánte ǀ divé-dive ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “They diligently worship him daily who is like a horse (to convey oblations), who is liberal and resplendent as the son of heaven, (the sun).”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तमर्व॑न्तं॒ न सा॑न॒सिम॑रु॒षं न दि॒वः शिशु॑म् । म॒र्मृ॒ज्यन्ते॑ दि॒वेदि॑वे

devanagari.text: बोधद्यन्मा हरिभ्यां कुमारः साहदेव्यः ।अच्छा न हूत उदरं ॥
बोधत् । यत् । मा । हरिऽभ्याम् । कुमारः । साहऽदेव्यः ।अच्छ । न । हूतः । उत् । अरम् ॥

transliteration.text: bódhat ǀ yát ǀ mā ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ kumāráḥ ǀ sāha-devyáḥ ǀáccha ǀ ná ǀ hūtáḥ ǀ út ǀ aram ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “When the prince, the son ofSahadeva, promised (to present) me with two horses, I withdrew not when called before him.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: बोध॒द्यन्मा॒ हरि॑भ्यां कुमा॒रः सा॑हदे॒व्यः । अच्छा॒ न हू॒त उद॑रम्

devanagari.text: उत त्या यजता हरी कुमारात्साहदेव्यात् ।प्रयता सद्य आ ददे ॥
उत । त्या । यजता । हरी इति । कुमारात् । साहऽदेव्यात् ।प्रऽयता । सद्यः । आ । ददे ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ tyā́ ǀ yajatā́ ǀ hárī íti ǀ kumārā́t ǀ sāha-devyā́t ǀprá-yatā ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dade ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “But immediately accepted those two excellent and well-trained horses from the prince, the son ofSahadeva.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त त्या य॑ज॒ता हरी॑ कुमा॒रात्सा॑हदे॒व्यात् । प्रय॑ता स॒द्य आ द॑दे

devanagari.text: एष वां देवावश्विना कुमारः साहदेव्यः ।दीर्घायुरस्तु सोमकः ॥
एषः । वाम् । देवौ । अश्विना । कुमारः । साहऽदेव्यः ।दीर्घऽआयुः । अस्तु । सोमकः ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ vām ǀ devau ǀ aśvinā ǀ kumāráḥ ǀ sāha-devyáḥ ǀdīrghá-āyuḥ ǀ astu ǀ sómakaḥ ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “DivineAśvins, may this prince,Somaka, the son ofSahadeva, your (worshipper), enjoy long life.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष वां॑ देवावश्विना कुमा॒रः सा॑हदे॒व्यः । दी॒र्घायु॑रस्तु॒ सोम॑कः

devanagari.text: तं युवं देवावश्विना कुमारं साहदेव्यं ।दीर्घायुषं कृणोतन ॥
तम् । युवम् । देवौ । अश्विना । कुमारम् । साहऽदेव्यम् ।दीर्घऽआयुषम् । कृणोतन ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ yuvám ǀ devau ǀ aśvinā ǀ kumārám ǀ sāha-devyám ǀdīrghá-āyuṣam ǀ kṛṇotana ǁ

Sukta 15.translation: “DivineAśvins, do you two make the prince, the son ofSahadeva, long-lived.”
Sukta 15.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तं यु॒वं दे॑वावश्विना कुमा॒रं सा॑हदे॒व्यम् । दी॒र्घायु॑षं कृणोतन

devanagari.text: आ सत्यो यातु मघवाँ ऋजीषी द्रवंत्वस्य हरय उप नः ।तस्मा इदंधः सुषुमा सुदक्षमिहाभिपित्वं करते गृणानः ॥
आ । सत्यः । यातु । मघऽवान् । ऋजीषी । द्रवन्तु । अस्य । हरयः । उप । नः ।तस्मै । इत् । अन्धः । सुसुम । सुऽदक्षम् । इह । अभिऽपित्वम् । करते । गृणानः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ satyáḥ ǀ yātu ǀ maghá-vān ǀ ṛjīṣī́ ǀ drávantu ǀ asya ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀtásmai ǀ ít ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ susuma ǀ su-dákṣam ǀ ihá ǀ abhi-pitvám ǀ karate ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “May the truthfulMaghavanthe accepter of the spiritlessSoma, come to us; may his horses hasten to us; to him we offer this sacrifice, the very potent beverage; may he grant the fulfilment of our desires.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ स॒त्यो या॑तु म॒घवाँ॑ ऋजी॒षी द्रव॑न्त्वस्य॒ हर॑य॒ उप॑ नः । तस्मा॒ इदन्ध॑: सुषुमा सु॒दक्ष॑मि॒हाभि॑पि॒त्वं क॑रते गृणा॒नः

devanagari.text: अव स्य शूराध्वनो नांतेऽस्मिन्नो अद्य सवने मंदध्यै ।शंसात्युक्थमुशनेव वेधाश्चिकितुषे असुर्याय मन्म ॥
अव । स्य । शूर । अध्वनः । न । अन्ते । अस्मिन् । नः । अद्य । सवने । मन्दध्यै ।शंसाति । उक्थम् । उशनाऽइव । वेधाः । चिकितुषे । असुर्याय । मन्म ॥

transliteration.text: áva ǀ sya ǀ śūra ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ánte ǀ asmín ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ sávane ǀ mandádhyai ǀśáṃsāti ǀ ukthám ǀ uśánā-iva ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǀ cikitúṣe ǀ asuryā́ya ǀ mánma ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Hero,Indra, set us free today to give you exhilaration at this sacrifice, as (they let loose a horse) at the end of the road; may the worshipper, likeUśanās, repeat an acceptable prayer to you, the knower (of all things), the destroyer of theasuras.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव॑ स्य शू॒राध्व॑नो॒ नान्ते॒ऽस्मिन्नो॑ अ॒द्य सव॑ने म॒न्दध्यै॑ । शंसा॑त्यु॒क्थमु॒शने॑व वे॒धाश्चि॑कि॒तुषे॑ असु॒र्या॑य॒ मन्म॑

devanagari.text: कविर्न निण्यं विदथानि साधन्वृषा यत्सेकं विपिपानो अर्चात् ।दिव इत्था जीजनत्सप्त कारूनह्ना चिच्चक्रुर्वयुना गृणंतः ॥
कविः । न । निण्यम् । विदथानि । साधन् । वृषा । यत् । सेकम् । विऽपिपानः । अर्चात् ।दिवः । इत्था । जीजनत् । सप्त । कारून् । अह्ना । चित् । चक्रुः । वयुना । गृणन्तः ॥

transliteration.text: kavíḥ ǀ ná ǀ niṇyám ǀ vidáthāni ǀ sā́dhan ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ yát ǀ sékam ǀ vi-pipānáḥ ǀ árcāt ǀdiváḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ jījanat ǀ saptá ǀ kārū́n ǀ áhnā ǀ cit ǀ cakruḥ ǀ vayúnā ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Like a sage (knowing) what is hidden, and fulfilling sacred rites, so the showerer (of benefits), quaffing copiously the effused (libation), exults (in the draught), and he genitive rates the seven efficient (rays) from heaven, which, being glorified, have made (manifest) the objects of (human) perception by day.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क॒विर्न नि॒ण्यं वि॒दथा॑नि॒ साध॒न्वृषा॒ यत्सेकं॑ विपिपा॒नो अर्चा॑त् । दि॒व इ॒त्था जी॑जनत्स॒प्त का॒रूनह्ना॑ चिच्चक्रुर्व॒युना॑ गृ॒णन्त॑:

devanagari.text: स्वर्यद्वेदि सुदृशीकमर्कैर्महि ज्योती रुरुचुर्यद्ध वस्तोः ।अंधा तमांसि दुधिता विचक्षे नृभ्यश्चकार नृतमो अभिष्टौ ॥

transliteration.text: sváḥ ǀ yát ǀ védi ǀ su-dṛ́śīkam ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ máhi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ rurucuḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ vástoḥ ǀandhā́ ǀ támāṃsi ǀ dúdhitā ǀ vi-cákṣe ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ cakāra ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ abhíṣṭau ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “When the vast luminous heaven manifested by the rays (of light) is displayed, then are (the deities) resplendent according to (their heavenly) abode; the chief of leaders, (Indra), in his approach has scattered the thick glooms so that men may see.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्व१॒॑र्यद्वेदि॑ सु॒दृशी॑कम॒र्कैर्महि॒ ज्योती॑ रुरुचु॒र्यद्ध॒ वस्तो॑: । अ॒न्धा तमां॑सि॒ दुधि॑ता वि॒चक्षे॒ नृभ्य॑श्चकार॒ नृत॑मो अ॒भिष्टौ॑

devanagari.text: ववक्ष इंद्रो अमितमृजीष्युभे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा ।अतश्चिदस्य महिमा वि रेच्यभि यो विश्वा भुवना बभूव ॥

transliteration.text: vavakṣé ǀ índraḥ ǀ ámitam ǀ ṛjīṣī́ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ā́ ǀ paprau ǀ ródasī íti ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀátaḥ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ mahimā́ ǀ ví ǀ reci ǀ abhí ǀ yáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ babhū́va ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Indra, as the accepter of the staleSoma, sustains infinite greatness, and has filled both heaven and earth by his magnitude; therefore has the vastness of him who has surpassed all the regions, exceeded (the world).”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: व॒व॒क्ष इन्द्रो॒ अमि॑तमृजी॒ष्यु१॒॑भे आ प॑प्रौ॒ रोद॑सी महि॒त्वा । अत॑श्चिदस्य महि॒मा वि रे॑च्य॒भि यो विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना ब॒भूव॑

devanagari.text: विश्वानि शक्रो नर्याणि विद्वानपो रिरेच सखिभिर्निकामैः ।अश्मानं चिद्ये बिभिदुर्वचोभिर्व्रजं गोमंतमुशिजो वि वव्रुः ॥

transliteration.text: víśvāni ǀ śakráḥ ǀ náryāṇi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ apáḥ ǀ rireca ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ ní-kāmaiḥ ǀáśmānam ǀ cit ǀ yé ǀ bibhidúḥ ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ vrajám ǀ gó-mantam ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vavruríti vavruḥ ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Knowing all things profitable for men,Śakrahas, with his willing friends (theMaruts), sent forth the waters, for they, with (loud) shouts, divided the clouds, and, desiring (to fulfil) their office, set open the pasturage of the cows (of theAṅgirasas).”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: विश्वा॑नि श॒क्रो नर्या॑णि वि॒द्वान॒पो रि॑रेच॒ सखि॑भि॒र्निका॑मैः । अश्मा॑नं चि॒द्ये बि॑भि॒दुर्वचो॑भिर्व्र॒जं गोम॑न्तमु॒शिजो॒ वि व॑व्रुः

transliteration.text: apáḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ vavri-vā́ṃsam ǀ párā ǀ ahan ǀ prá ǀ āvat ǀ te ǀ vájram ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ sá-cetāḥ ǀprá ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ samudríyāṇi ǀ ainoḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ bhávan ǀ śávasā ǀ śūra ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Your protecting thunderbolt has slainVṛtraobstructing the (issue of the waters), the conscious earth (co-operating) with you; valiant hero, preserver (of the regions), send down by your strength the waters of the firmament.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒पो वृ॒त्रं व॑व्रि॒वांसं॒ परा॑ह॒न्प्राव॑त्ते॒ वज्रं॑ पृथि॒वी सचे॑ताः । प्रार्णां॑सि समु॒द्रिया॑ण्यैनो॒: पति॒र्भव॒ञ्छव॑सा शूर धृष्णो

devanagari.text: अपो यदद्रिं पुरुहूत दर्दराविर्भुवत्सरमा पूर्व्यं ते ।स नो नेता वाजमा दर्षि भूरिं गोत्रा रुजन्नंगिरोभिर्गृणानः ॥

transliteration.text: apáḥ ǀ yát ǀ ádrim ǀ puru-hūta ǀ dárdaḥ ǀ āvíḥ ǀ bhuvat ǀ sarámā ǀ pūrvyám ǀ te ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ netā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ ā́ ǀ darṣi ǀ bhū́rim ǀ gotrā́ ǀ ruján ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Invoked of many, when you had divided the cloud for (the escape of) the waters,Saramāappeared before you; and you, the bringer of abundant food, have shown us favour, dividing the clouds and glorified by theAṅgirasas.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒पो यदद्रिं॑ पुरुहूत॒ दर्द॑रा॒विर्भु॑वत्स॒रमा॑ पू॒र्व्यं ते॑ । स नो॑ ने॒ता वाज॒मा द॑र्षि॒ भूरिं॑ गो॒त्रा रु॒जन्नङ्गि॑रोभिर्गृणा॒नः

devanagari.text: अच्छा कविं नृमणो गा अभिष्टौ स्वर्षाता मघवन्नाधमानं ।ऊतिभिस्तमिषणो द्युम्नहूतौ नि मायावानब्रह्मा दस्युरर्त ॥

transliteration.text: áccha ǀ kavím ǀ nṛ-manaḥ ǀ gāḥ ǀ abhíṣṭau ǀ sváḥ-sātā ǀ magha-van ǀ nā́dhamānam ǀūtí-bhiḥ ǀ tám ǀ iṣaṇaḥ ǀ dyumná-hūtau ǀ ní ǀ māyā́-vān ǀ ábrahmā ǀ dásyuḥ ǀ arta ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Maghavan, who are honoured by men, you have repaired to the presence of the sage for (the sake of) bestowing (upon him) wealth, and when soliciting (you) in his need (for aid); defending (him) with your protection, the guileful, impiousDasyuhas been destroyed in the contest for the spoil.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अच्छा॑ क॒विं नृ॑मणो गा अ॒भिष्टौ॒ स्व॑र्षाता मघव॒न्नाध॑मानम् । ऊ॒तिभि॒स्तमि॑षणो द्यु॒म्नहू॑तौ॒ नि मा॒यावा॒नब्र॑ह्मा॒ दस्यु॑रर्त

devanagari.text: आ दस्युघ्ना मनसा याह्यस्तं भुवत्ते कुत्सः सख्ये निकामः ।स्वे योनौ नि षदतं सरूपा वि वां चिकित्सदृतचिद्ध नारी ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ dasyu-ghnā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ yāhi ǀ ástam ǀ bhúvat ǀ te ǀ kútsaḥ ǀ sakhyé ǀ ní-kāmaḥ ǀsvé ǀ yónau ǀ ní ǀ sadatam ǀ sá-rūpā ǀ ví ǀ vām ǀ cikitsat ǀ ṛta-cít ǀ ha ǀ nā́rī ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “With a mind resolved on killing theDasyu, you came (to his dwelling), andKutsawas eager for your friendship; now have you two alighted in his, (Indra's), habitation, and being entirely similar in form the truthful woman has been perplexed (to discriminate between you).”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ द॑स्यु॒घ्ना मन॑सा या॒ह्यस्तं॒ भुव॑त्ते॒ कुत्स॑: स॒ख्ये निका॑मः । स्वे योनौ॒ नि ष॑दतं॒ सरू॑पा॒ वि वां॑ चिकित्सदृत॒चिद्ध॒ नारी॑

devanagari.text: यासि कुत्सेन सरथमवस्युस्तोदो वातस्य हर्योरीशानः ।ऋज्रा वाजं न गध्यं युयूषन्कविर्यदहन्पार्याय भूषात् ॥

transliteration.text: yā́si ǀ kútsena ǀ sa-rátham ǀ avasyúḥ ǀ todáḥ ǀ vā́tasya ǀ háryoḥ ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀṛjrā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ ná ǀ gádhyam ǀ yúyūṣan ǀ kavíḥ ǀ yát ǀ áhan ǀ pā́ryāya ǀ bhū́ṣāt ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “You go withKutsain the same chariot, determined to defend him; (you) who are the tormentor (of foes), the lord of horses (of the speech) of the wind; on the same day wherein, yoking (to the car) the straight-going steeds, as if to receive food, the sage (Kutsa) has been enabled to cross over (the sea) of calamity.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यासि॒ कुत्से॑न स॒रथ॑मव॒स्युस्तो॒दो वात॑स्य॒ हर्यो॒रीशा॑नः । ऋ॒ज्रा वाजं॒ न गध्यं॒ युयू॑षन्क॒विर्यदह॒न्पार्या॑य॒ भूषा॑त्

devanagari.text: कुत्साय शुष्णमशुषं नि बर्हीः प्रपित्वे अह्नः कुयवं सहस्रा ।सद्यो दस्यून्प्र मृण कुत्स्येन प्र सूरश्चक्रं वृहतादभीके ॥

transliteration.text: kútsāya ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ aśúṣam ǀ ní ǀ barhīḥ ǀ pra-pitvé ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ kúyavam ǀ sahásrā ǀsadyáḥ ǀ dásyūn ǀ prá ǀ mṛṇa ǀ kutsyéna ǀ prá ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ vṛhatāt ǀ abhī́ke ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “ForKutsa, you have slain the unhappyŚuṣṇaand in the forepart of the day, attended by thousands (you have slain)Kuyavawith the thunderbolt; you have swiftly destroyed theDasyus, and you have cut them to pieces in the battle, with the wheel (of the chariot of) the sun.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कुत्सा॑य॒ शुष्ण॑म॒शुषं॒ नि ब॑र्हीः प्रपि॒त्वे अह्न॒: कुय॑वं स॒हस्रा॑ । स॒द्यो दस्यू॒न्प्र मृ॑ण कु॒त्स्येन॒ प्र सूर॑श्च॒क्रं वृ॑हताद॒भीके॑

devanagari.text: त्वं पिप्रुं मृगयं शूशुवांसमृजिश्वने वैदथिनाय रंधीः ।पंचाशत्कृष्णा नि वपः सहस्रात्कं न पुरो जरिमा वि दर्दः ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ píprum ǀ mṛ́gayam ǀ śūśu-vā́ṃsam ǀ ṛjíśvane ǀ vaidathinā́ya ǀ randhīḥ ǀpañcāśát ǀ kṛṣṇā́ ǀ ní ǀ vapaḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ átkam ǀ ná ǀ púraḥ ǀ jarimā́ ǀ ví ǀ dardaríti dardaḥ ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “You have subjugated Pipru and the mightyMṛgayāfor the sake of Ṛjiṣvan, the son of Vidathin, you have slain the fifty thousandKṛṣṇas; and, as old age (destroys) life, you have demolished the cities (ofŚambara).”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं पिप्रुं॒ मृग॑यं शूशु॒वांस॑मृ॒जिश्व॑ने वैदथि॒नाय॑ रन्धीः । प॒ञ्चा॒शत्कृ॒ष्णा नि व॑पः स॒हस्रात्कं॒ न पुरो॑ जरि॒मा वि द॑र्दः

transliteration.text: sū́raḥ ǀ upāké ǀ tanvám ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ ví ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ céti ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ várpaḥ ǀmṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ hastī́ ǀ táviṣīm ǀ uṣāṇáḥ ǀ siṃháḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ bíbhrat ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “While having (your) person n in the proximity of the sun, your form becomes redolent of ambrosia, and you are like the deer-like elephant, consuming the strength (of the strong), and are like a terrible lion when wielding your weapons.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सूर॑ उपा॒के त॒न्वं१॒॑ दधा॑नो॒ वि यत्ते॒ चेत्य॒मृत॑स्य॒ वर्प॑: । मृ॒गो न ह॒स्ती तवि॑षीमुषा॒णः सिं॒हो न भी॒म आयु॑धानि॒ बिभ्र॑त्

devanagari.text: इंद्रं कामा वसूयंतो अग्मन्त्स्वर्मीळ्हे न सवने चकानाः ।श्रवस्यवः शशमानास उक्थैरोको न रण्वा सुदृशीव पुष्टिः ॥

Sukta 16.translation: “Relying (uponIndra) for protection, and desirous of riches, (pious men) repair to him soliciting his presence in the sacrifice, as if in the battle, asking for food, celebrating his praise with hymns, for he is the refuge (of his worshippers), and resembles the grateful and lovely (goddess) of nutrition.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रं॒ कामा॑ वसू॒यन्तो॑ अग्म॒न्त्स्व॑र्मीळ्हे॒ न सव॑ने चका॒नाः । श्र॒व॒स्यव॑: शशमा॒नास॑ उ॒क्थैरोको॒ न र॒ण्वा सु॒दृशी॑व पु॒ष्टिः

Sukta 16.translation: “Let us invoke that graciousIndrawho has made so many things good for man; who, bestowing enviable opulence, quickly brings acceptable food to a worshipper like me.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तमिद्व॒ इन्द्रं॑ सु॒हवं॑ हुवेम॒ यस्ता च॒कार॒ नर्या॑ पु॒रूणि॑ । यो माव॑ते जरि॒त्रे गध्यं॑ चिन्म॒क्षू वाजं॒ भर॑ति स्पा॒र्हरा॑धाः

transliteration.text: tigmā́ ǀ yát ǀ antáḥ ǀ aśániḥ ǀ pátāti ǀ kásmin ǀ cit ǀ śūra ǀ muhuké ǀ jánānām ǀghorā́ ǀ yát ǀ arya ǀ sám-ṛtiḥ ǀ bhávāti ǀ ádha ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ gopā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 16.translation: “Hero,indra, when in any conflict of men the sharp thunderbolt falls in the midst (of them), and when, lord there is a terrible battle, then the defender of our person ns is made known.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ति॒ग्मा यद॒न्तर॒शनि॒: पता॑ति॒ कस्मि॑ञ्चिच्छूर मुहु॒के जना॑नाम् । घो॒रा यद॑र्य॒ समृ॑ति॒र्भवा॒त्यध॑ स्मा नस्त॒न्वो॑ बोधि गो॒पाः

devanagari.text: भुवोऽविता वामदेवस्य धीनां भुवः सखावृको वाजसातौ ।त्वामनु प्रमतिमा जगन्मोरुशंसो जरित्रे विश्वध स्याः ॥

Sukta 16.translation: “Be you the protector of the pious acts ofVāmadeva; be you in battle an unfailing friend; we come to you, eminent in wisdom; may you be ever benignant to your praiser.”
Sukta 16.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भुवो॑ऽवि॒ता वा॒मदे॑वस्य धी॒नां भुव॒: सखा॑वृ॒को वाज॑सातौ । त्वामनु॒ प्रम॑ति॒मा ज॑गन्मोरु॒शंसो॑ जरि॒त्रे वि॒श्वध॑ स्याः

devanagari.text: एभिर्नृभिरिंद्र त्वायुभिष्ट्वा मघवद्भिर्मघवन्विश्व आजौ ।द्यावो न द्युम्नैरभि संतो अर्यः क्षपो मदेम शरदश्च पूर्वीः ॥

Sukta 16.translation: “In every battle,Maghavan, may we, along with those men who trust in you and offer rich gifts, like those who are resplendent with riches, triumphing over their foes, glorify you many nights and years.”

Sukta 16.translation: “Therefore we offer to the vigorousIndra, the showerer (of benefits), holy adoration, that he may never withdraw his friendly (actions) from us, and that he may be our powerful protector, the defender of (our) person ns, as theBhṛgus(fabricate) a car (for use).”

Sukta 16.translation: “Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we possessed of chariots, be ever delighted in (your) praise.”

Sukta 17.translation: “At the birth of you who are resplendent, trembled the heaven (and) trembled the earth through fear of your wrath; the mighty clouds were confined; they destroyed (the distress of drought), spreading the waters over the dry plural ces.”

Sukta 17.translation: “The subduer of foes, manifesting his energy and hurling his thunderbolt, shattered the mountain by his strength; he slewVṛtrawith the thunderbolt, exulting, and the waters whose obstructor was destroyed rushed forth with rapidity.”

Sukta 17.translation: “ThisMaghavan, who destroys assembled hosts, is he who is renowned as chief in battles; he brings the food which he bestows (upon the worshipper); may we be held dear in his friendship.”

Sukta 17.translation: “This (Indra), is renowned, whether conquering or slaying (his foes), or whether in conflict he recovers the cattle; when Indra truly entertains anger all that is stationary or moveable is in fear of him.”

Sukta 17.translation: “Indra, the lord of opulence, who has overcomemany (enemies), has completely won (their) cattle, (their) gold, (their) horses; chief leader by his energies, praised by these his worshippers, he is the distributor of riches, the bestower of wealth.”

Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त मा॒ता म॑हि॒षमन्व॑वेनद॒मी त्वा॑ जहति पुत्र दे॒वाः । अथा॑ब्रवीद्वृ॒त्रमिन्द्रो॑ हनि॒ष्यन्त्सखे॑ विष्णो वित॒रं वि क्र॑मस्व

devanagari.text: कस्ते मातरं विधवामचक्रच्छयुं कस्त्वामजिघांसच्चरंतं ।कस्ते देवो अधि मार्डीक आसीद्यत्प्राक्षिणाः पितरं पादगृह्य ॥
कः । ते । मातरम् । विधवाम् । अचक्रत् । शयुम् । कः । त्वाम् । अजिघांसत् । चरन्तम् ।कः । ते । देवः । अधि । मार्डीके । आसीत् । यत् । प्र । अक्षिणाः । पितरम् । पादऽगृह्य ॥

transliteration.text: káḥ ǀ te ǀ mātáram ǀ vidhávām ǀ acakrat ǀ śayúm ǀ káḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ ajighāṃsat ǀ cárantam ǀkáḥ ǀ te ǀ deváḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ mārḍīké ǀ āsīt ǀ yát ǀ prá ǀ ákṣiṇāḥ ǀ pitáram ǀ pāda-gṛ́hya ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Who has made your mother a widow? who has sought to slay the sleeping and the walking? what deity has been more gracious than you since you have slain the father, having seized him by the foot?”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कस्ते॑ मा॒तरं॑ वि॒धवा॑मचक्रच्छ॒युं कस्त्वाम॑जिघांस॒च्चर॑न्तम् । कस्ते॑ दे॒वो अधि॑ मार्डी॒क आ॑सी॒द्यत्प्राक्षि॑णाः पि॒तरं॑ पाद॒गृह्य॑

devanagari.text: अवर्त्या शुन आंत्राणि पेचे न देवेषु विविदे मर्डितारं ।अपश्यं जायाममहीयमानामधा मे श्येनो मध्वा जभार ॥
अवर्त्या । शुनः । आन्त्राणि । पेचे । न । देवेषु । विविदे । मर्डितारम् ।अपश्यम् । जायाम् । अमहीयमानाम् । अध । मे । श्येनः । मधु । आ । जभार ॥

transliteration.text: ávartyā ǀ śúnaḥ ǀ āntrā́ṇi ǀ pece ǀ ná ǀ devéṣu ǀ vivide ǀ marḍitā́ram ǀápaśyam ǀ jāyā́m ǀ ámahīyamānām ǀ ádha ǀ me ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ mádhu ǀ ā́ ǀ jabhāra ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “In extreme destitution I have cooked the entrails of a dog; I have not found a comforter among the gods; I have beheld my wife disrsepected; then the falcon, (Indra), has brought to me sweet water.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव॑र्त्या॒ शुन॑ आ॒न्त्राणि॑ पेचे॒ न दे॒वेषु॑ विविदे मर्डि॒तार॑म् । अप॑श्यं जा॒यामम॑हीयमाना॒मधा॑ मे श्ये॒नो मध्वा ज॑भार

devanagari.text: एवा त्वामिंद्र वज्रिन्नत्र विश्वे देवासः सुहवास ऊमाः ।महामुभे रोदसी वृद्धमृष्वं निरेकमिद्वृणते वृत्रहत्ये ॥
एव । त्वाम् । इन्द्र । वज्रिन् । अत्र । विश्वे । देवासः । सुऽहवासः । ऊमाः ।महाम् । उभे इति । रोदसी इति । वृद्धम् । ऋष्वम् । निः । एकम् । इत् । गृणते । वृत्रऽहत्ये ॥

transliteration.text: evá ǀ tvā́m ǀ indra ǀ vajrin ǀ átra ǀ víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ su-hávāsaḥ ǀ ū́māḥ ǀmahā́m ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ vṛddhám ǀ ṛṣvám ǀ níḥ ǀ ékam ǀ ít ǀ gṛṇate ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Indra, wielder of the thuderbolt, all the protecting deities who are reverently invoked, and both the heaven and the earth, glorify you who are verily one alone, mighty, vast, and plural asing of aspect, for the destruction ofVṛtra.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा त्वामि॑न्द्र वज्रि॒न्नत्र॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वास॑: सु॒हवा॑स॒ ऊमा॑: । म॒हामु॒भे रोद॑सी वृ॒द्धमृ॒ष्वं निरेक॒मिद्वृ॑णते वृत्र॒हत्ये॑

devanagari.text: अवासृजंत जिव्रयो न देवा भुवः सम्राळिंद्र सत्ययोनिः ।अहन्नहिं परिशयानमर्णः प्र वर्तनीररदो विश्वधेनाः ॥
अव । असृजन्त । जिव्रयः । न । देवाः । भुवः । सम्ऽराट् । इन्द्र । सत्यऽयोनिः ।अहन् । अहिम् । परिऽशयानम् । अर्णः । प्र । वर्तनीः । अरदः । विश्वऽधेनाः ॥

transliteration.text: áva ǀ asṛjanta ǀ jívrayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀ indra ǀ satyá-yoniḥ ǀáhan ǀ áhim ǀ pari-śáyānam ǀ árṇaḥ ǀ prá ǀ vartanī́ḥ ǀ aradaḥ ǀ viśvá-dhenāḥ ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “As elders (send forth their young), so the gods have sent you (againstVṛtra); thence you became,Indrawho is the abode of truth, the soverign of the world; you have slain the slumbering Ahi for (the release of) the water and have marked out (the channels of) all the delighting rivers.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अवा॑सृजन्त॒ जिव्र॑यो॒ न दे॒वा भुव॑: स॒म्राळि॑न्द्र स॒त्ययो॑निः । अह॒न्नहिं॑ परि॒शया॑न॒मर्ण॒: प्र व॑र्त॒नीर॑रदो वि॒श्वधे॑नाः

devanagari.text: अतृप्णुवंतं वियतमबुध्यमबुध्यमानं सुषुपाणमिंद्र ।सप्त प्रति प्रवत आशयानमहिं वज्रेण वि रिणा अपर्वन् ॥
अतृप्णुवन्तम् । विऽयतम् । अबुध्यम् । अबुध्यमानम् । सुसुपानम् । इन्द्र ।सप्त । प्रति । प्रऽवतः । आऽशयानम् । अहिम् । वज्रेण । वि । रिणाः । अपर्वन् ॥

transliteration.text: átṛpṇuvantam ǀ ví-yatam ǀ abudhyám ǀ ábudhyamānam ǀ susupānám ǀ indra ǀsaptá ǀ práti ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ ā-śáyānam ǀ áhim ǀ vájreṇa ǀ ví ǀ riṇāḥ ǀ aparván ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “On the day of full moon you have slain with the thunderbolt the insatiable, unnerved, ignorant, unapprehending, slumbering Ahi, obstructing the gliding-downward-flowing (streams).”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अतृ॑प्णुवन्तं॒ विय॑तमबु॒ध्यमबु॑ध्यमानं सुषुपा॒णमि॑न्द्र । स॒प्त प्रति॑ प्र॒वत॑ आ॒शया॑न॒महिं॒ वज्रे॑ण॒ वि रि॑णा अप॒र्वन्

devanagari.text: अक्षोदयच्छवसा क्षाम बुध्नं वार्ण वातस्तविषीभिरिंद्रः ।दृळ्हान्यौभ्नादुशमान ओजोऽवाभिनत्ककुभः पर्वतानां ॥
अक्षोदयत् । शवसा । क्षाम । बुध्नम् । वाः । न । वातः । तविषीभिः । इन्द्रः ।दृळ्हानि । औभ्नात् । उशमानः । ओजः । अव । अभिनत् । ककुभः । पर्वतानाम् ॥

transliteration.text: ákṣodayat ǀ śávasā ǀ kṣā́ma ǀ budhnám ǀ vā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀdṛḷhā́ni ǀ aubhnāt ǀ uśámānaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ áva ǀ abhinat ǀ kakúbhaḥ ǀ párvatānām ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Indra, by his strength, has agitated the exhausted firmament, as wind, by its violent (gusts, agitates) the water; exulting in his strength, he has divided the solid (clouds), and has shattered the peaks of the mountains.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अक्षो॑दय॒च्छव॑सा॒ क्षाम॑ बु॒ध्नं वार्ण वात॒स्तवि॑षीभि॒रिन्द्र॑: । दृ॒ळ्हान्यौ॑भ्नादु॒शमा॑न॒ ओजोऽवा॑भिनत्क॒कुभ॒: पर्व॑तानाम्

devanagari.text: अभि प्र दद्रुर्जनयो न गर्भं रथा इव प्र ययुः साकमद्रयः ।अतर्पयो विसृत उब्ज ऊर्मींत्वं वृताँ अरिणा इंद्र सिंधून् ॥
अभि । प्र । दद्रुः । जनयः । न । गर्भम् । रथाःऽइव । प्र । ययुः । साकम् । अद्रयः ।अतर्पयः । विऽसृतः । उब्जः । ऊर्मीन् । त्वम् । वृतान् । अरिणाः । इन्द्र । सिन्धून् ॥

transliteration.text: abhí ǀ prá ǀ dadruḥ ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ gárbham ǀ ráthāḥ-iva ǀ prá ǀ yayuḥ ǀ sākám ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀátarpayaḥ ǀ vi-sṛ́taḥ ǀ ubjáḥ ǀ ūrmī́n ǀ tvám ǀ vṛtā́n ǀ ariṇāḥ ǀ indra ǀ síndhūn ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “TheMarutshave hastened to you like mother to their young; like chariots they have rushed in along (with you); you,Indra, have satisfied the following streams; you have shattered the clouds; you have set free the obstructed rivers.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि प्र द॑द्रु॒र्जन॑यो॒ न गर्भं॒ रथा॑ इव॒ प्र य॑युः सा॒कमद्र॑यः । अत॑र्पयो वि॒सृत॑ उ॒ब्ज ऊ॒र्मीन्त्वं वृ॒ताँ अ॑रिणा इन्द्र॒ सिन्धू॑न्

devanagari.text: त्वं महीमवनिं विश्वधेनां तुर्वीतये वय्याय क्षरंतीं ।अरमयो नमसैजदर्णः सुतरणाँ अकृणोरिंद्र सिंधून् ॥
त्वम् । महीम् । अवनिम् । विश्वऽधेनाम् । तुर्वीतये । वय्याय । क्षरन्तीम् ।अरमयः । नमसा । एजत् । अर्णः । सुऽतरणान् । अकृणोः । इन्द्र । सिन्धून् ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ mahī́m ǀ avánim ǀ viśvá-dhenām ǀ turvī́taye ǀ vayyā́ya ǀ kṣárantīm ǀáramayaḥ ǀ námasā ǀ éjat ǀ árṇaḥ ǀ su-taraṇā́n ǀ akṛṇoḥ ǀ indra ǀ síndhūn ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “You have made the vast, all-cherishing, and exuberant earth, delighted with (abundant) food, and tremulous water, for (the sake of)Turvītiand Vayyā; you have made the rivers easy to be crosseḍ ”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं म॒हीम॒वनिं॑ वि॒श्वधे॑नां तु॒र्वीत॑ये व॒य्या॑य॒ क्षर॑न्तीम् । अर॑मयो॒ नम॒सैज॒दर्ण॑: सुतर॒णाँ अ॑कृणोरिन्द्र॒ सिन्धू॑न्

devanagari.text: प्राग्रुवो नभन्वो न वक्वा ध्वस्रा अपिन्वद्युवतीर्ऋतज्ञाः ।धन्वान्यज्राँ अपृणक्तृषाणाँ अधोगिंद्रः स्तर्यो दंसुपत्नीः ॥
प्र । अग्रुवः । नभन्वः । न । वक्वाः । ध्वस्राः । अपिन्वत् । युवतीः । ऋतऽज्ञाः ।धन्वानि । अज्रान् । अपृणक् । तृषाणान् । अधोक् । इन्द्रः । स्तर्यः । दंऽसुपत्नीः ॥

transliteration.text: prá ǀ agrúvaḥ ǀ nabhanváḥ ǀ ná ǀ vákvāḥ ǀ dhvasrā́ḥ ǀ apinvat ǀ yuvatī́ḥ ǀ ṛta-jñā́ḥ ǀdhánvāni ǀ ájrān ǀ apṛṇak ǀ tṛṣāṇā́n ǀ ádhok ǀ índraḥ ǀ staryáḥ ǀ dáṃ-supatnīḥ ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Indrahas filled the youthful rivers, the parents of plural nty, the corroders (of their banks), like  armies destructive (of their foes); he has inundated the dry lands, and (satisfied) the thirsty travellers; he has milked the barren cows whom theasurashad become the lords of.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्राग्रुवो॑ नभ॒न्वो॒३॒॑ न वक्वा॑ ध्व॒स्रा अ॑पिन्वद्युव॒तीॠ॑त॒ज्ञाः । धन्वा॒न्यज्राँ॑ अपृणक्तृषा॒णाँ अधो॒गिन्द्र॑: स्त॒र्यो॒३॒॑ दंसु॑पत्नीः

devanagari.text: पूर्वीरुषसः शरदश्च गूर्ता वृत्रं जघन्वाँ असृजद्वि सिंधून् ।परिष्ठिता अतृणद्बद्बधानाः सीरा इंद्रः स्रवितवे पृथिव्या ॥
पूर्वीः । उषसः । शरदः । च । गूर्ताः । वृत्रम् । जघन्वान् । असृजत् । वि । सिन्धून् ।परिऽस्थिताः । अतृणत् । बद्बधानाः । सीराः । इन्द्रः । स्रवितवे । पृथिव्या ॥

transliteration.text: pūrvī́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ ca ǀ gūrtā́ḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ asṛjat ǀ ví ǀ síndhūn ǀpári-sthitāḥ ǀ atṛṇat ǀ badbadhānā́ḥ ǀ sīrā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ srávitave ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Having slainVṛtra, he has liberated many mornings and years (that had been) swallowed up by darkness, and has set the rivers free;Indrahas released the imprisoned rivers, encompassed (by the cloud), to flow upon the earth.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पू॒र्वीरु॒षस॑: श॒रद॑श्च गू॒र्ता वृ॒त्रं ज॑घ॒न्वाँ अ॑सृज॒द्वि सिन्धू॑न् । परि॑ष्ठिता अतृणद्बद्बधा॒नाः सी॒रा इन्द्र॒: स्रवि॑तवे पृथि॒व्या

devanagari.text: वम्रीभिः पुत्रमग्रुवो अदानं निवेशनाद्धरिव आ जभर्थ ।व्यंधो अख्यदहिमाददानो निर्भूदुखच्छित्समरंत पर्व ॥
वम्रीभिः । पुत्रम् । अग्रुवः । अदानम् । निऽवेशनात् । हरिऽवः । आ । जभर्थ ।वि । अन्धः । अख्यत् । अहिम् । आऽददानः । निः । भूत् । उखऽछित् । सम् । अरन्त । पर्व ॥

transliteration.text: vamrī́bhiḥ ǀ putrám ǀ agrúvaḥ ǀ adānám ǀ ni-véśanāt ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jabhartha ǀví ǀ andháḥ ǀ akhyat ǀ áhim ǀ ā-dadānáḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ bhūt ǀ ukha-chít ǀ sám ǀ aranta ǀ párva ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Lord of horses, you have brought the son of Agru from his dwelling, where he was being devoured by the ants; when extricated, although blind, he distinguished the serpent; and when he came forth the joints that had been sundered in the ant-hill were restrung.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: व॒म्रीभि॑: पु॒त्रम॒ग्रुवो॑ अदा॒नं नि॒वेश॑नाद्धरिव॒ आ ज॑भर्थ । व्य१॒॑न्धो अ॑ख्य॒दहि॑माददा॒नो निर्भू॑दुख॒च्छित्सम॑रन्त॒ पर्व॑

devanagari.text: प्र ते पूर्वाणि करणानि विप्राविद्वाँ आह विदुषे करांसि ।यथायथा वृष्ण्यानि स्वगूर्तापांसि राजन्नर्याविवेषीः ॥

Sukta 20.translation: “May the illustriousIndra, the granter of desires, come to us, whether from afar or nigh, for our protection; he who is the lord of men, armed with the thunderbolt, overcoming his foes in conflict and in combats, (attended) by the most illustrious (Maruts).”

Sukta 20.translation: “MayIndra, looking down upon us, come with his steeds to our presence for our protection and enrichment; may the mighty thunderer, the possessor of wealth, (aiding us) in battle, be present at this our sacrifice.”

Sukta 20.translation: “Harm us not, but cherish us,Indra; bestow upon us that abundant wealth which it is yours to give to the donor (of the oblation); praising you, we celebrate you at this sacred rite, which is new and excellent, and (at which the oblation) is proper to be presented.”

Sukta 20.translation: “Glorified (in the past) glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever delighted in your praise.”

Sukta 21.translation: “MayIndracome to us for protection, and being praised (by us), may the mighty hero be exhilarated along with (us) at this rite; he whose energies are many; may he, like the radiant sun, recruit his own overpowering vigour.”

Sukta 21.translation: “Glorify the powerful leaders of that renowned and opulent (Indra), whose victorious and protecting energy rules over men, like a universal sovereign entitled to veneration.”

Sukta 21.translation: “MayIndra, accompanied by theMarutscome quickly for our protection, from the heaven, from the earth, from the firmament, or from the waters; from the sphere of the sun, from (any) distant region, from the abode of the rains.”

Sukta 21.translation: “We glorify, in solemn rites, thisIndrawho rules over substantial, abundant riches; who by his prowess is victor over (hostile) hosts; who by his munificence brings excellent (wealth) to the presence (of his worshippers).”

Sukta 21.translation: “Let the invoking priest bring to our dwellings that (Indra) who, firmly fixing the (world) returns food for (sacrificial food), and (utters) a voice enjoining (men) to worship; he who is to be propitiated by praises, who is adored by many.”

Sukta 21.translation: “When the repeaters of (his) commendations, abiding in the dwelling of the worshipper, approachIndrawith praise, may he who is our (great) sustainer in conflicts, whose wrath is difficult to be (appeased), becomes the ministering priest of the master of the house.”

Sukta 21.translation: “Inasmuch as he has opened the doors of the cloud, and has supplied the rapid courses of the waters with (additional) torrents, so when the pious have recourse toIndrafor food, he finds (it) in the haunt of theGauraandGavaya.”

Sukta 21.translation: “Your auspicioushands,Indra, are the doers of good deeds; your two hands, Indra, are the extenders of wealth to him who praises you; what, Indra, is this delay? why do you not exhilarate us? why are you not delighted to make us gifts?”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भ॒द्रा ते॒ हस्ता॒ सुकृ॑तो॒त पा॒णी प्र॑य॒न्तारा॑ स्तुव॒ते राध॑ इन्द्र । का ते॒ निष॑त्ति॒: किमु॒ नो म॑मत्सि॒ किं नोदु॑दु हर्षसे॒ दात॒वा उ॑

Sukta 21.translation: “Thus (glorified),Indra, who is faithful (to his word), the lord of wealth, the slayer ofVṛtra, bestows rihes on man; so you, the praised of many, give us riches for our pious acts, that I may eat of your divine food.”

Sukta 21.translation: “Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever delighted in your praise.”

Sukta 22.translation: “Since the great and mightyIndrais propitiated by our (oblations), since he desires (them) from us, may he, the possessor of opulence, who comes wielding the thunderbolt of his strength, accept the (sacrificial) food, the hymn, theSomalibation, and the prayers.”
