Sukta 22.translation: “The showerer (of benefits), casting with hishandsthe quadrangular bolt that causes rain, fierce, the chief of leaders, the achiever of (glorious) acts, is desirous of the prosperity of the investing Paruṣṇi (river), whose (bordering) districts he has frequented through regard.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वृषा॒ वृष॑न्धिं॒ चतु॑रश्रि॒मस्य॑न्नु॒ग्रो बा॒हुभ्यां॒ नृत॑म॒: शची॑वान् । श्रि॒ये परु॑ष्णीमु॒षमा॑ण॒ ऊर्णां॒ यस्या॒: पर्वा॑णि स॒ख्याय॑ वि॒व्ये

Sukta 22.translation: “Who diine, most divine, as soon as born (was endowed) with abundant viands, and great energies, holding in his arms the willing thunderbolt, and causing by his strength (both) heaven and earth to tremble.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यो दे॒वो दे॒वत॑मो॒ जाय॑मानो म॒हो वाजे॑भिर्म॒हद्भि॑श्च॒ शुष्मै॑: । दधा॑नो॒ वज्रं॑ बा॒ह्वोरु॒शन्तं॒ द्याममे॑न रेजय॒त्प्र भूम॑

Sukta 22.translation: “All the high plural ces, and the many low paces, the heaven and the earth, trembled (through fear) of the mighty (Indra) at his birth; the strong (Indra) cherishes the parents of the moving (Sun), and the winds, like men, make a noise in their peregrination.”

Sukta 22.translation: “Of you,Indra, who are mighty, great are deeds, and to be proclaimed at all sacrifices, inasmuch as, high-minded hero, you, sustaining (the world), have by your strength slain Ahi with the resistless thunderbolt.”

Sukta 22.translation: “Most powerfulIndra, all these, your exploits, are verily true: (through fear of you), the showerer (of benefits), the cows shed (milk) from their udders; then, benevolent-minded (Indra), the rivers, fearing you, flow with rapidity.”

Sukta 22.translation: “EnduringIndra, bestow upon us energies, excellent, superior, powerful; bring under subjection to us enemies deserving of death; demolish the weapon of the malevolent man.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्मे वर्षि॑ष्ठा कृणुहि॒ ज्येष्ठा॑ नृ॒म्णानि॑ स॒त्रा स॑हुरे॒ सहां॑सि । अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ वृ॒त्रा सु॒हना॑नि रन्धि ज॒हि वध॑र्व॒नुषो॒ मर्त्य॑स्य

Sukta 22.translation: “Hear our praises,Indra, and bestow upon us many kinds of food; fulfil all our desires, and know yourself,Maghavan, to be to us the donor of cattle.”

Sukta 22.translation: “Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in (your) praise.”

Sukta 23.translation: “In what manner may (any one) extol the mightyIndra? at the sacrifice of what worshipper may he, propitiated, be present, drinking the sacrificialSomabeverage, desirous of the (sacred) food, and plural ased (by the oblation)? the mighty Indra is borne (to the rite) for the purpose of bestowing brilliant wealth.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क॒था म॒हाम॑वृध॒त्कस्य॒ होतु॑र्य॒ज्ञं जु॑षा॒णो अ॒भि सोम॒मूध॑: । पिब॑न्नुशा॒नो जु॒षमा॑णो॒ अन्धो॑ वव॒क्ष ऋ॒ष्वः शु॑च॒ते धना॑य

Sukta 23.translation: “What hero has enjoyed his fellowship (in battle)? who has been a sharer in his benevolent thoughts? when does any one appreciate his wonderful bounty? when is he (presen) for the promotion of the prosperity of the man who glorifies and worships him?”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: को अ॑स्य वी॒रः स॑ध॒माद॑माप॒ समा॑नंश सुम॒तिभि॒: को अ॑स्य । कद॑स्य चि॒त्रं चि॑किते॒ कदू॒ती वृ॒धे भु॑वच्छशमा॒नस्य॒ यज्यो॑:

Sukta 23.translation: “How is thatIndrahears (the worshipper) who invokes him? and, hearing, how does he know his necessities? what are his gifts of old; why have they termed him the fulfiller (of the desires) of him who offers praise?”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क॒था शृ॑णोति हू॒यमा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑: क॒था शृ॒ण्वन्नव॑सामस्य वेद । का अ॑स्य पू॒र्वीरुप॑मातयो ह क॒थैन॑माहु॒: पपु॑रिं जरि॒त्रे

Sukta 23.translation: “How does he who glorifiesIndra, and is diligent in his worship, although encountering opposition, obtain from him wealth? may the divine Indra be the appreciation of my praises, when accepting the sacrificial food he is propitiated towards me.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क॒था स॒बाध॑: शशमा॒नो अ॑स्य॒ नश॑द॒भि द्रवि॑णं॒ दीध्या॑नः । दे॒वो भु॑व॒न्नवे॑दा म ऋ॒तानां॒ नमो॑ जगृ॒भ्वाँ अ॒भि यज्जुजो॑षत्

Sukta 23.translation: “When, in what manner, at the dawning of this morning, has the divineIndraaccepted the friendship of a mortal? when and in what manner, (is) his friendship (manifested) to the friends who have spread out the desirable and suitable (offering) before him?”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क॒था कद॒स्या उ॒षसो॒ व्यु॑ष्टौ दे॒वो मर्त॑स्य स॒ख्यं जु॑जोष । क॒था कद॑स्य स॒ख्यं सखि॑भ्यो॒ ये अ॑स्मि॒न्कामं॑ सु॒युजं॑ तत॒स्रे

Sukta 23.translation: “May we in any manner proclaim your friendship for your friends? when may (we make known) your fraternal regard? the efforts of the well-lookingIndraare for the happiness of all; the wonderful form of the moving (Indra) is, like the sun, ever wished for.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: किमादम॑त्रं स॒ख्यं सखि॑भ्यः क॒दा नु ते॑ भ्रा॒त्रं प्र ब्र॑वाम । श्रि॒ये सु॒दृशो॒ वपु॑रस्य॒ सर्गा॒: स्व१॒॑र्ण चि॒त्रत॑ममिष॒ आ गोः

Sukta 23.translation: “Resolving to kil the oppressing, malevolent (rākṣasi), not acknowledgingIndra, he sharpened his sharp weapons for (her) destruction, and the fierce (Indra) the canceller of debts, has kept afar the unknown dawns in which the debts (are to be paid).”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्रुहं॒ जिघां॑सन्ध्व॒रस॑मनि॒न्द्रां तेति॑क्ते ति॒ग्मा तु॒जसे॒ अनी॑का । ऋ॒णा चि॒द्यत्र॑ ऋण॒या न॑ उ॒ग्रो दू॒रे अज्ञा॑ता उ॒षसो॑ बबा॒धे

Sukta 23.translation: “Many are the waters of ṛta; the adoration of ṛta destroys iniquities; the intelligent and brilliant praise of ṛta has opened the deaf (ears) of man.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तस्य॒ हि शु॒रुध॒: सन्ति॑ पू॒र्वीॠ॒तस्य॑ धी॒तिर्वृ॑जि॒नानि॑ हन्ति । ऋ॒तस्य॒ श्लोको॑ बधि॒रा त॑तर्द॒ कर्णा॑ बुधा॒नः शु॒चमा॑न आ॒योः

Sukta 23.translation: “Many are the stable, sustaining, delightful forms of the embodied ṛta; the ṛta are (the pious) expectant of food; by ṛta have the kine entered into the sacrifice.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तस्य॑ दृ॒ळ्हा ध॒रुणा॑नि सन्ति पु॒रूणि॑ च॒न्द्रा वपु॑षे॒ वपूं॑षि । ऋ॒तेन॑ दी॒र्घमि॑षणन्त॒ पृक्ष॑ ऋ॒तेन॒ गाव॑ ऋ॒तमा वि॑वेशुः

Sukta 23.translation: “The (worshipper) subjecting ṛta (to his will) verily enjoys ṛta; the strength ṛta is (developed) with speed, and is desirous of (possessing) water; to ṛta belong the wide and profound heaven and earth; supreme kine, they yield their milk to ṛta.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तं ये॑मा॒न ऋ॒तमिद्व॑नोत्यृ॒तस्य॒ शुष्म॑स्तुर॒या उ॑ ग॒व्युः । ऋ॒ताय॑ पृ॒थ्वी ब॑हु॒ले ग॑भी॒रे ऋ॒ताय॑ धे॒नू प॑र॒मे दु॑हाते

Sukta 23.translation: “Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in our praise.”

Sukta 24.translation: “What suitable praise may bring the son of strength,Indra, before us, to give us wealth; the hero, the lord of cattle, is the donor, oḥ man, of the wealth of his adversaries to him who glorifies him.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: का सु॑ष्टु॒तिः शव॑सः सू॒नुमिन्द्र॑मर्वाची॒नं राध॑स॒ आ व॑वर्तत् । द॒दिर्हि वी॒रो गृ॑ण॒ते वसू॑नि॒ स गोप॑तिर्नि॒ष्षिधां॑ नो जनासः

Sukta 24.translation: “He,Indra, is to be invoked for the destruction ofVṛtra; he, the deservedly praised, is to be worshipped; the real donor of wealth, he,Maghavan, gives wealth, (acquired) in battle, to the mortal offers him prayer and libations.”

Sukta 24.translation: “Men verily call upon him in battle; the (devout) inflicters of austerity upon their person ns constitute him their preserver; when both (the worshipper and the priest) approach together the bountifulIndra, men (succeed) in (obtaining) the gift of sons and grandsons.”

Sukta 24.translation: “PowerfulIndra, men variously dispersed, come mutually together to celebrate sacred rites for the sake of obtaining rain; when men who are combatants assemble in battle, there are some of them who rely upon Indra.”

Sukta 24.translation: “Thereupon some verily worship the powerful (Indra); thereupon one man prepares the buttered cake that he may offer it to (Indra); thereupon the offerer of theSomahe distinguishes from him who presents no libation; thereupon some one rejoices to worship the showerer (of benefits).”

Sukta 24.translation: “Indrabestows wealth upon him who offers a libation to him, desiring it, though in another sphere; and, with a humble mind, makes him who is devoted to him his friend in combats.”

Sukta 24.translation: “Indraaccepting graciously the praises of his devoted (worshipper), who today pours out the libation to him who toasts the buttered cakes, or fries barley for Indra, exercises towards him the power that grants his desires.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य इन्द्रा॑य सु॒नव॒त्सोम॑म॒द्य पचा॑त्प॒क्तीरु॒त भृ॒ज्जाति॑ धा॒नाः । प्रति॑ मना॒योरु॒चथा॑नि॒ हर्य॒न्तस्मि॑न्दध॒द्वृष॑णं॒ शुष्म॒मिन्द्र॑:

Sukta 24.translation: “When the destroyer (of enemies) distinguishes a mortal foe; when the lord is engaged in the long (continued) battle, (his) bride summons to the dwelling the showerer (of benefits), encompassed by the offerers of the libation.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य॒दा स॑म॒र्यं व्यचे॒दृघा॑वा दी॒र्घं यदा॒जिम॒भ्यख्य॑द॒र्यः । अचि॑क्रद॒द्वृष॑णं॒ पत्न्यच्छा॑ दुरो॒ण आ निशि॑तं सोम॒सुद्भि॑:

Sukta 24.translation: “A man has realized a small price for an article of great value, and again coming (to the buyer he says) this has not been sold; I require the full price; but he does not recover a small price by a large (equivalent); whether helpless or clever they adhere to their bargain.”

Sukta 26.translation: “I gave the earth to the venerable (Manu); I have bestowed rain upon the mortal who presents (oblations); I have let forth the sounding waters; the gods obey my will.”

Sukta 26.translation: “Exhilarated (by theSomabeverage) I have destroyed the ninety and nine cities ofŚambara, the hundredth I gave to be occupied byDivodāsawhen I protected him,Atithigva, at his sacrifice. ”

Sukta 26.translation: “May this bird,Maruts, be pre-eminent over (other) hawks, since with a wheelless car the swift-winged bore theSoma, accepted by the gods, toManu.”

Sukta 26.translation: “When the bird, intimidating (its guardians), carried off from hence (theSoma) it was at large; (flying) swift as thought along the vast path (of the firmament), it went rapidly with the sweet Soma, and the hawks thence acquired the celebrity in this world.”

Sukta 26.translation: “The straight-flying hawk, conveying theSomafrom afar; the bird, attended by the gods, brought, resolute of purpose, the adorable exhilarating Soma, having taken it from that lofty heaven.”

Sukta 26.translation: “Having taken it, the hawk brought theSomawith him to a thousand and ten thousand sacrifices, and this being provided, the performer of many (great) deeds, the unbewildered (Indra) destroyed, in the exhilaration of the Soma, (his) bewildered foes.”

Sukta 27.translation: “Being still in the germ, I have known all the births of these divinities in their order; a hundred bodies of metal confined me, but as a hawk I came forth with speed.”

Sukta 27.translation: “When the hawk screamed (with exultation) on his descent from heaven, and (the guardians of theSoma) perceived that the Soma was (carried away) by it then, the archer ofKṛśānu, pursuing with the speed of thought, and stringing his bow, let fly an arrow against it.”

Sukta 27.translation: “The straight-flying hawk carried off theSomafrom above the vast heaven, as (theAśvinscarried off)Bhujyufrom the region ofIndra, and a falling feather from the middle of the bird dropped from him wounded in the conflict.”

Sukta 27.translation: “Now mayMaghavanaccept the pure nutitious (sacrificial) food in a white pitcher, mixed with milk and curds, offered by the priests; the upper part of the sweet (beverage) to drink for his exhilaration; may the hero accept (it) to drink for (his) exhilaration.”

Sukta 28.translation: “Through that friendship,Soma, which has united you with your (friend)Indra, he has made the waters flow for man; he has slain Ahi; he has sent forth the seven rivers, and has opened theshut-up sources (of the streams).”
Sukta 28.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वा यु॒जा तव॒ तत्सो॑म स॒ख्य इन्द्रो॑ अ॒पो मन॑वे स॒स्रुत॑स्कः । अह॒न्नहि॒मरि॑णात्स॒प्त सिन्धू॒नपा॑वृणो॒दपि॑हितेव॒ खानि॑

devanagari.text: त्वा युजा नि खिदत्सूर्यस्येंद्रश्चक्रं सहसा सद्य इंदो ।अधि ष्णुना बृहता वर्तमानं महो द्रुहो अप विश्वायु धायि ॥

Sukta 28.translation: “With you,Soma, for his ally,Indrahas quickly taken off by force the wheel of the chariot of the sun, abiding above with the vast and stationary (firmament); the everywhere going wheel (of the car) of the great oppressor has been taken away.”
Sukta 28.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वा यु॒जा नि खि॑द॒त्सूर्य॒स्येन्द्र॑श्च॒क्रं सह॑सा स॒द्य इ॑न्दो । अधि॒ ष्णुना॑ बृह॒ता वर्त॑मानं म॒हो द्रु॒हो अप॑ वि॒श्वायु॑ धायि

Sukta 28.translation: “Indrahas slain theDasyus,Soma, in battle;Agnihas consumed them before the noon; he (Indra) has destroyed the whole of many thosands, as (robbers are the destroyers of those) going upon (their own) business, in a difficult and dangerous (plural ce).”
Sukta 28.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अह॒न्निन्द्रो॒ अद॑हद॒ग्निरि॑न्दो पु॒रा दस्यू॑न्म॒ध्यंदि॑नाद॒भीके॑ । दु॒र्गे दु॑रो॒णे क्रत्वा॒ न या॒तां पु॒रू स॒हस्रा॒ शर्वा॒ नि ब॑र्हीत्

Sukta 28.translation: “Indra, you have made theseDasyusdevoid of all (good qualities); you have made the races without rites abject; may you, (Somaand Indra), repel (and) destroy (your) enemies; accept (our) homage for their destruction.”
Sukta 28.sanskrit_wisdomlib: विश्व॑स्मात्सीमध॒माँ इ॑न्द्र॒ दस्यू॒न्विशो॒ दासी॑रकृणोरप्रश॒स्ताः । अबा॑धेथा॒ममृ॑णतं॒ नि शत्रू॒नवि॑न्देथा॒मप॑चितिं॒ वध॑त्रैः

devanagari.text: एवा सत्यं मघवाना युवं तदिंद्रश्च सोमोर्वमश्व्यं गोः ।आदर्दृतमपिहितान्यश्ना रिरिचथुः क्षाश्चित्ततृदाना ॥

Sukta 28.translation: “Possessors of wealth, destroyers of foes,IndraandSoma, it is indeed true that you have distributed great numbers of horses, and of the cattle which had been concealed and the land which you had recovered by your strength.”
Sukta 28.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा स॒त्यं म॑घवाना यु॒वं तदिन्द्र॑श्च सोमो॒र्वमश्व्यं॒ गोः । आद॑र्दृत॒मपि॑हिता॒न्यश्ना॑ रिरि॒चथु॒: क्षाश्चि॑त्ततृदा॒ना

devanagari.text: आ नः स्तुत उप वाजेभिरूती इंद्र याहि हरिभिर्मंदसानः ।तिरश्चिदर्यः सवना पुरूण्यांगूषेभिर्गृणानः सत्यराधाः ॥

Sukta 29.translation: “Honoured with accepted (sacrificial) viands, come,Indra, exulting, with your steeds, to our many rites, for our protection; you who are the lord, glorified by hymns, whose wealth is truth.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ न॑: स्तु॒त उप॒ वाजे॑भिरू॒ती इन्द्र॑ या॒हि हरि॑भिर्मन्दसा॒नः । ति॒रश्चि॑द॒र्यः सव॑ना पु॒रूण्या॑ङ्गू॒षेभि॑र्गृणा॒नः स॒त्यरा॑धाः

Sukta 29.translation: “Then her shattered wagon reposed (on the bank) of the Vipās' (river), and she departed from afar.”

Sukta 29.translation: “You have spread abroad upon the earth, by your contrivance, the swollenSindhuwhen arrested (on its course).”

Sukta 29.translation: “By valour you have carried off the wealth ofŚuṣṇa, when you had demolished his cities.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त शुष्ण॑स्य धृष्णु॒या प्र मृ॑क्षो अ॒भि वेद॑नम् । पुरो॒ यद॑स्य सम्पि॒णक्

Sukta 29.translation: “You have slain the slaveŚambara, the son Kulitara hurling him off the huge mountain.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त दा॒सं कौ॑लित॒रं बृ॑ह॒तः पर्व॑ता॒दधि॑ । अवा॑हन्निन्द्र॒ शम्ब॑रम्

Sukta 29.translation: “You have slain the five hundreds and thousands (of the followers) of the slave Varin, (surrounding) him like the fellies (round the spokes of the wheel).”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त दा॒सस्य॑ व॒र्चिन॑: स॒हस्रा॑णि श॒ताव॑धीः । अधि॒ पञ्च॑ प्र॒धीँरि॑व

Sukta 29.translation: “You,Indra, who areŚatakratu, have made Parāvṛj, the son of Agru, participant in sacred hymns.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त त्यं पु॒त्रम॒ग्रुव॒: परा॑वृक्तं श॒तक्र॑तुः । उ॒क्थेष्विन्द्र॒ आभ॑जत्

Sukta 29.translation: “The lord of acts, the wiseIndra, has borne across (their difficulties),TurvaśasandYadu, when denied inauguration.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त त्या तु॒र्वशा॒यदू॑ अस्ना॒तारा॒ शची॒पति॑: । इन्द्रो॑ वि॒द्वाँ अ॑पारयत्

Sukta 29.translation: “You have slain at once those twoĀryas,ArṇaandCitraratha, (dwellig) on the opposite (bank) of theSarayu.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त त्या स॒द्य आर्या॑ स॒रयो॑रिन्द्र पा॒रत॑: । अर्णा॑चि॒त्रर॑थावधीः

Sukta 29.translation: “Slayer ofVṛtrayou have restored the (one who was) blind, the (other who was) lame, both abandoned by their kin); (it is not possible) to exceed the happiness what is given by you.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अनु॒ द्वा ज॑हि॒ता न॑यो॒ऽन्धं श्रो॒णं च॑ वृत्रहन् । न तत्ते॑ सु॒म्नमष्ट॑वे

Sukta 29.translation: “Indrahas overturned a hundred stone-built cities for Divodās, the donor of oblations.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श॒तम॑श्म॒न्मयी॑नां पु॒रामिन्द्रो॒ व्या॑स्यत् । दिवो॑दासाय दा॒शुषे॑

Sukta 29.translation: “He put to sleep, by delusion, with his destructive (weapons), thirty thousand of the servile (races), for the sake ofDabhīti.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अस्वा॑पयद्द॒भीत॑ये स॒हस्रा॑ त्रिं॒शतं॒ हथै॑: । दा॒साना॒मिन्द्रो॑ मा॒यया॑

Sukta 29.translation: “Slayer ofVṛtra, you are the same to all your worshippers, the lord of cattle, who cast down all these (your enemies).”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स घेदु॒तासि॑ वृत्रहन्त्समा॒न इ॑न्द्र॒ गोप॑तिः । यस्ता विश्वा॑नि चिच्यु॒षे

Sukta 29.translation: “When, indeed,Indra, you excite your vigorous manhood, there is no one at the present time who may resist it.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त नू॒नं यदि॑न्द्रि॒यं क॑रि॒ष्या इ॑न्द्र॒ पौंस्य॑म् । अ॒द्या नकि॒ष्टदा मि॑नत्

Sukta 29.translation: “Destroyer of foes, may the divineAryamandistribute your precious wealth; (may)Pūṣa(bestow it), (may),Bhaga(bestow it); may the toothless deity bestow the desired wealth.”
Sukta 29.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वा॒मंवा॑मं त आदुरे दे॒वो द॑दात्वर्य॒मा । वा॒मं पू॒षा वा॒मं भगो॑ वा॒मं दे॒वः करू॑ळती

devanagari.text: नकिरिंद्र त्वदुत्तरो न ज्यायाँ अस्ति वृत्रहन् ।नकिरेवा यथा त्वं ॥
नकिः । इन्द्र । त्वत् । उत्ऽतरः । न । ज्यायान् । अस्ति । वृत्रऽहन् ।नकिः । एव । यथा । त्वम् ॥

transliteration.text: nákiḥ ǀ indra ǀ tvát ǀ út-taraḥ ǀ ná ǀ jyā́yān ǀ asti ǀ vṛtra-han ǀnákiḥ ǀ evá ǀ yáthā ǀ tvám ǁ

Sukta 30.translation: “There is no one,Indra, superior to you; no one more excellent (than you); slayer ofVṛtrathere is no one, verily, such as you are. ”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नकि॑रिन्द्र॒ त्वदुत्त॑रो॒ न ज्यायाँ॑ अस्ति वृत्रहन् । नकि॑रे॒वा यथा॒ त्वम्

devanagari.text: सत्रा ते अनु कृष्टयो विश्वा चक्रेव वावृतुः ।सत्रा महाँ असि श्रुतः ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “Verily men are attached to you as are all the wheels (to the body of the wagon); in truth you are great and renowned.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒त्रा ते॒ अनु॑ कृ॒ष्टयो॒ विश्वा॑ च॒क्रेव॑ वावृतुः । स॒त्रा म॒हाँ अ॑सि श्रु॒तः

devanagari.text: विश्वे चनेदना त्वा देवास इंद्र युयुधुः ।यदहा नक्तमातिरः ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “Verily all the gods, with you (for) their strength, have warred (with theasuras); wherefore you have destroyed by day and by night.”

devanagari.text: यत्रोत बाधितेभ्यश्चक्रं कुत्साय युध्यते ।मुषाय इंद्र सूर्यं ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “In wihc (contests), for the sake ofKutsaand his allies, you hae stolen,Indra, the (wheel of the car) of the sun.”

devanagari.text: यत्र देवाँ ऋघायतो विश्वाँ अयुध्य एक इत् ।त्वमिंद्र वनूँरहन् ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “In which (contest) you singly indeed have warred with all those opposing the gods; you,Indra, have slain the malignant.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यत्र॑ दे॒वाँ ऋ॑घाय॒तो विश्वाँ॒ अयु॑ध्य॒ एक॒ इत् । त्वमि॑न्द्र व॒नूँरह॑न्

devanagari.text: यत्रोत मर्त्याय कमरिणा इंद्र सूर्यं ।प्रावः शचीभिरेतशं ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “In which (contests),Indrayou have, for the sake of a mortal, discomfited the sun, and have protectedEtaśaby (your) exploits.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यत्रो॒त मर्त्या॑य॒ कमरि॑णा इन्द्र॒ सूर्य॑म् । प्राव॒: शची॑भि॒रेत॑शम्

devanagari.text: किमादुतासि वृत्रहन्मघवन्मन्युमत्तमः ।अत्राह दानुमातिरः ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “Wherefore, slayer ofVṛtra, opulentIndra, have you thereupon become most incensed, and in consequence, have slain the son ofDanu(Vṛtra) in this firmament.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: किमादु॒तासि॑ वृत्रह॒न्मघ॑वन्मन्यु॒मत्त॑मः । अत्राह॒ दानु॒माति॑रः

devanagari.text: एतद्घेदुत वीर्यमिंद्र चकर्थ पौंस्यं ।स्त्रियं यद्दुर्हणायुवं वधीर्दुहितरं दिवः ॥

transliteration.text: etát ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ utá ǀ vīryám ǀ índra ǀ cakártha ǀ páuṃsyam ǀstríyam ǀ yát ǀ duḥ-hanāyúvam ǀ vádhīḥ ǀ duhitáram ǀ diváḥ ǁ

Sukta 30.translation: “Inasmuch,Indra, as you have displayed such manly prowess, you have slain the woman, the daughter of the sky, when meditating mischief.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒तद्घेदु॒त वी॒र्य१॒॑मिन्द्र॑ च॒कर्थ॒ पौंस्य॑म् । स्त्रियं॒ यद्दु॑र्हणा॒युवं॒ वधी॑र्दुहि॒तरं॑ दि॒वः

devanagari.text: दिवश्चिद्घा दुहितरं महान्महीयमानां ।उषासमिंद्र सं पिणक् ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “YouIndra, who are mighty, have enriched glorious dawn, the daughter of heaven.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वश्चि॑द्घा दुहि॒तरं॑ म॒हान्म॑ही॒यमा॑नाम् । उ॒षास॑मिन्द्र॒ सं पि॑णक्

devanagari.text: अपोषा अनसः सरत्संपिष्टादह बिभ्युषी ।नि यत्सीं शिश्नथद्वृषा ॥

transliteration.text: ápa ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ánasaḥ ǀ sarat ǀ sám-piṣṭāt ǀ áha ǀ bibhyúṣī ǀní ǀ yát ǀ sīm ǀ śiśnáthat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǁ

Sukta 30.translation: “The terrified Uṣas descended from the broken wagon when the (showerer of benefits) had smashed it.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अपो॒षा अन॑सः सर॒त्सम्पि॑ष्टा॒दह॑ बि॒भ्युषी॑ । नि यत्सीं॑ शि॒श्नथ॒द्वृषा॑

devanagari.text: एतदस्या अनः शये सुसंपिष्टं विपाश्या ।ससार सीं परावतः ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “Then her shattered wagon reposed (on the bank) of the Vipās' (river), and she departed from afar.”

devanagari.text: उत सिंधुं विबाल्यं वितस्थानामधि क्षमि ।परि ष्ठा इंद्र मायया ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ síndhum ǀ vi-bālyám ǀ vi-tasthānā́m ǀ ádhi ǀ kṣámi ǀpári ǀ sthāḥ ǀ indra ǀ māyáyā ǁ

devanagari.text: उत शुष्णस्य धृष्णुया प्र मृक्षो अभि वेदनं ।पुरो यदस्य संपिणक् ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “By valour you have carried off the wealth ofŚuṣṇa, when you had demolished his cities.”

devanagari.text: उत दासं कौलितरं बृहतः पर्वतादधि ।अवाहन्निंद्र शंबरं ॥

devanagari.text: उत दासस्य वर्चिनः सहस्राणि शतावधीः ।अधि पंच प्रधीँरिव ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “You have slain the five hundreds and thousands (of the followers) of the slave Varin, (surrounding) him like the fellies (round the spokes of the wheel).”

devanagari.text: उत त्यं पुत्रमग्रुवः परावृक्तं शतक्रतुः ।उक्थेष्विंद्र आभजत् ॥

devanagari.text: उत त्या तुर्वशायदू अस्नातारा शचीपतिः ।इंद्रो विद्वाँ अपारयत् ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “The lord of acts, the wiseIndra, has borne across (their difficulties),TurvaśasandYadu, when denied inauguration.”

devanagari.text: उत त्या सद्य आर्या सरयोरिंद्र पारतः ।अर्णाचित्ररथावधीः ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “You have slain at once those twoĀryas,ArṇaandCitraratha, (dwellig) on the opposite (bank) of theSarayu.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त त्या स॒द्य आर्या॑ स॒रयो॑रिन्द्र पा॒रत॑: । अर्णा॑चि॒त्रर॑थावधीः

devanagari.text: अनु द्वा जहिता नयोऽंधं श्रोणं च वृत्रहन् ।न तत्ते सुम्नमष्टवे ॥

devanagari.text: शतमश्मन्मयीनां पुरामिंद्रो व्यास्यत् ।दिवोदासाय दाशुषे ॥

Sukta 30.translation: “Indrahas overturned a hundred stone-built cities for Divodās, the donor of oblations.”

Sukta 32.translation: “WiseIndra, I praise your brown (horses); bestower of kine, (who are) not regardless (of your worshippers); with those two steeds terrify not our cattle.”

Sukta 33.translation: “I send my prayer as a messenger to theṛbhus; I solicit (of them) the cow, the yielder of the white milk, for the dilution (of theSomalibation); for they, as swift as the wind, the doers of good works, were borne quickly across the firmament by rapid steeds.”

Sukta 33.translation: “When theṛbhus, by honouring their parents with renovated (youth), and by other works, had achieved enough, they thereupon proceeded to the society of the gods, and, considerate, they bring nourishment to the devout (worshipper).”

Sukta 33.translation: “May they who rendered their decrepid and dropsy parents, when, like two dryposts, again perpetually young,Vāja, Vibhavan, andṚbhuassociated withIndra, drinkers of theSomajuice, protect our sacrifice.”

Sukta 33.translation: “When theṚbhus, reposing for twelve days, remained in the hospitality of the uncealable (sun) they rendered the fields fertile, they led forth the rivers, plural nts sprung upon the waste, and waters (spread over) the low (plural ces).”

Sukta 33.translation: “The gods were plural ased by their works, illustrious in act and in thought;Vājawas the artificer of the gods,ṚbhukṣinofIndra, Vibhavan ofVaruṇa.”

Sukta 33.translation: “May thoseṚbhuswho gratified the horses (ofIndra) by pious praise, who constructed for Indra his two docile steeds, bestow upon us satiety of riches, and wealth (of cattle), like those who devise prosperity for a friend.”

Sukta 33.translation: “The gods verily have given you the beverage at the (third sacrifice of the) day, and its exhilarqation, not through regard, but (as the gift of one) wearied out (by penance);Ṛbhus, who are so (eminent), grant us, verily, wealth at this third (diurnal) sacrifice.”

Sukta 34.translation: “Ṛbhus, who posses wealth, comprising cattle, food, progeny, dwellings, and abundant sustenance, do you, who are the first drinkers (of theSoma), bestow upon us, when exhilarated, (that wealth and upon those) who laud your liberality.”

Sukta 36.translation: “The glorious three-wheeled car (of theAśvinsmade,Ṛbhusby you) traverses the firmament without horses, without reins; great was that proclamation of your divine (power), by which, Ṛbhus, you cherish heaven and earth.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒न॒श्वो जा॒तो अ॑नभी॒शुरु॒क्थ्यो॒३॒॑ रथ॑स्त्रिच॒क्रः परि॑ वर्तते॒ रज॑: । म॒हत्तद्वो॑ दे॒व्य॑स्य प्र॒वाच॑नं॒ द्यामृ॑भवः पृथि॒वीं यच्च॒ पुष्य॑थ

devanagari.text: रथं ये चक्रुः सुवृतं सुचेतसोऽविह्वरंतं मनसस्परि ध्यया ।ताँ ऊ न्वस्य सवनस्य पीतय आ वो वाजा ऋभवो वेदयामसि ॥

Sukta 36.translation: “We invoke you respectfully,VājasandṚbhus, to drink of this libation, for you are the wise sages, who, by mental meditation, made the well-constructed undeviating car (of theAśvins).”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रथं॒ ये च॒क्रुः सु॒वृतं॑ सु॒चेत॒सोऽवि॑ह्वरन्तं॒ मन॑स॒स्परि॒ ध्यया॑ । ताँ ऊ॒ न्व१॒॑स्य सव॑नस्य पी॒तय॒ आ वो॑ वाजा ऋभवो वेदयामसि

devanagari.text: तद्वो वाजा ऋभवः सुप्रवाचनं देवेषु विभ्वो अभवन्महित्वनं ।जिव्री यत्संता पितरा सनाजुरा पुनर्युवाना चरथाय तक्षथ ॥

Sukta 36.translation: “Therefore,Vāja,Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, was your greatness proclaimed among the gods, that you made your aged and inform parents young (and able) to go (withere they would).”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तद्वो॑ वाजा ऋभवः सुप्रवाच॒नं दे॒वेषु॑ विभ्वो अभवन्महित्व॒नम् । जिव्री॒ यत्सन्ता॑ पि॒तरा॑ सना॒जुरा॒ पुन॒र्युवा॑ना च॒रथा॑य॒ तक्ष॑थ

devanagari.text: एकं वि चक्र चमसं चतुर्वयं निश्चर्मणो गामरिणीत धीतिभिः ।अथा देवेष्वमृतत्वमानश श्रुष्टी वाजा ऋभवस्तद्व उक्थ्यं ॥

transliteration.text: ékam ǀ ví ǀ cakra ǀ camasám ǀ cátuḥ-vayam ǀ níḥ ǀ cármaṇaḥ ǀ gā́m ǀ ariṇīta ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀátha ǀ devéṣu ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaśa ǀ śruṣṭī́ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ ukthyám ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “You have made the single ladle fourfold; by your (marvellous) acts you have clothed the cow with a (new) hide; therefore you have obtained immortality among the gods; such acts,VājasandṚbhus, are to be eagerly glorified.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: एकं॒ वि च॑क्र चम॒सं चतु॑र्वयं॒ निश्चर्म॑णो॒ गाम॑रिणीत धी॒तिभि॑: । अथा॑ दे॒वेष्व॑मृत॒त्वमा॑नश श्रु॒ष्टी वा॑जा ऋभव॒स्तद्व॑ उ॒क्थ्य॑म्

devanagari.text: ऋभुतो रयिः प्रथमश्रवस्तमो वाजश्रुतासो यमजीजनन्नरः ।विभ्वतष्टो विदथेषु प्रवाच्यो यं देवासोऽवथा स विचर्षणिः ॥

transliteration.text: ṛbhutáḥ ǀ rayíḥ ǀ prathamáśravaḥ-tamaḥ ǀ vā́ja-śrutāsaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ájījanan ǀ náraḥ ǀvibhva-taṣṭáḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ pra-vā́cyaḥ ǀ yám ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ ávatha ǀ sáḥ ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “From theṚbhusmay wealth, the best and most productive of food, (come to me); that which the leaders of rites renowned together with theVājas, have engendered; that which has been fabricated by Vibhvan and is to be celebrated at sacrifice; that which, deities you protect, that is to be beheld.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒भु॒तो र॒यिः प्र॑थ॒मश्र॑वस्तमो॒ वाज॑श्रुतासो॒ यमजी॑जन॒न्नर॑: । वि॒भ्व॒त॒ष्टो वि॒दथे॑षु प्र॒वाच्यो॒ यं दे॑वा॒सोऽव॑था॒ स विच॑र्षणिः

devanagari.text: स वाज्यर्वा स ऋषिर्वचस्यया स शूरो अस्ता पृतनासु दुष्टरः ।स रायस्पोषं स सुवीर्यं दधे यं वाजो विभ्वाँ ऋभवो यमाविषुः ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ árvā ǀ sáḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ vacasyáyā ǀ sáḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ ástā ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ dustáraḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ sáḥ ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ dadhe ǀ yám ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ ví-bhvā ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ā́viṣuḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “He is vigorous and skilled in war, he is a ṛṣi worthy of homage, he is a hero, the discomfiter of foes, invincible in battles, he is possessed of ample wealth, and (is blessed) with excellent posterity, whomVājaand Vibhvan, whom theṚbhusprotect.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स वा॒ज्यर्वा॒ स ऋषि॑र्वच॒स्यया॒ स शूरो॒ अस्ता॒ पृत॑नासु दु॒ष्टर॑: । स रा॒यस्पोषं॒ स सु॒वीर्यं॑ दधे॒ यं वाजो॒ विभ्वाँ॑ ऋ॒भवो॒ यमावि॑षुः

transliteration.text: śréṣṭham ǀ vaḥ ǀ péśaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhāyi ǀ darśatám ǀ stómaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ tám ǀ jujuṣṭana ǀdhī́rāsaḥ ǀ hí ǀ sthá ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ vipaḥ-cítaḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ vaḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ ā́ ǀ vedayāmasi ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “An excellent and agreeable form has been assumed by you; (this is our own) praise;VājasandṚbhusbe gratified (thereby), for you are wise, experienced, and intelligent; such we make you known (to be) by this (our) prayer.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श्रेष्ठं॑ व॒: पेशो॒ अधि॑ धायि दर्श॒तं स्तोमो॑ वाजा ऋभव॒स्तं जु॑जुष्टन । धीरा॑सो॒ हि ष्ठा क॒वयो॑ विप॒श्चित॒स्तान्व॑ ए॒ना ब्रह्म॒णा वे॑दयामसि

devanagari.text: यूयमस्मभ्यं धिषणाभ्यस्परि विद्वांसो विश्वा नर्याणि भोजना ।द्युमंतं वाजं वृषशुष्ममुत्तममा नो रयिमृभवस्तक्षता वयः ॥

transliteration.text: yūyám ǀ asmábhyam ǀ dhiṣáṇābhyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vidvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ náryāṇi ǀ bhójanā ǀdyu-mántam ǀ vā́jam ǀ vṛ́ṣa-śuṣmam ǀ ut-tamám ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ takṣata ǀ ā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “Do you who are wise, (bestow) upon us, in requital of our praises, all enjoyments that are good for man and fabricate for us,Ṛbhus, riches and food, resplendent invigorating, overpowering (foes), and most excellent.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यू॒यम॒स्मभ्यं॑ धि॒षणा॑भ्य॒स्परि॑ वि॒द्वांसो॒ विश्वा॒ नर्या॑णि॒ भोज॑ना । द्यु॒मन्तं॒ वाजं॒ वृष॑शुष्ममुत्त॒ममा नो॑ र॒यिमृ॑भवस्तक्ष॒ता वय॑:

devanagari.text: इह प्रजामिह रयिं रराणा इह श्रवो वीरवत्तक्षता नः ।येन वयं चितयेमात्यन्यांतं वाजं चित्रमृभवो ददा नः ॥

transliteration.text: ihá ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ ihá ǀ rayím ǀ rárāṇāḥ ǀ ihá ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ vīrá-vat ǀ takṣata ǀ naḥ ǀyéna ǀ vayám ǀ citáyema ǀ áti ǀ anyā́n ǀ tám ǀ vā́jam ǀ citrám ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ dada ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 36.translation: “Gratified (by your worship), fabricate for us, on this occasion, progeny and wealth, and reputation, with numerous adherents; grant to us,Ṛbhus, abundant sustenance wherewith we may greatly excel others.”
Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒ह प्र॒जामि॒ह र॒यिं ररा॑णा इ॒ह श्रवो॑ वी॒रव॑त्तक्षता नः । येन॑ व॒यं चि॒तये॒मात्य॒न्यान्तं वाजं॑ चि॒त्रमृ॑भवो ददा नः

devanagari.text: उप नो वाजा अध्वरमृभुक्षा देवा यात पथिभिर्देवयानैः ।यथा यज्ञं मनुषो विक्ष्वासु दधिध्वे रण्वाः सुदिनेष्वह्नां ॥

transliteration.text: úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ ṛbhukṣāḥ ǀ dévāḥ ǀ yātá ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ deva-yā́naiḥ ǀyáthā ǀ yajñám ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ vikṣú ǀ āsú ǀ dadhidhvé ǀ raṇvāḥ ǀ su-díneṣu ǀ áhnām ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “DivineVājas,Ṛbhus, come to our sacrifice by the path travelled by the gods, inasmuch as you, gracious (Ṛbhus), have maintained sacrifice among the people, (the progeny) ofManu, for (the sake of) securing the prosperous course of days.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उप॑ नो वाजा अध्व॒रमृ॑भुक्षा॒ देवा॑ या॒त प॒थिभि॑र्देव॒यानै॑: । यथा॑ य॒ज्ञं मनु॑षो वि॒क्ष्वा॒३॒॑सु द॑धि॒ध्वे र॑ण्वाः सु॒दिने॒ष्वह्ना॑म्

transliteration.text: té ǀ vaḥ ǀ hṛdé ǀ mánase ǀ santu ǀ yajñā́ḥ ǀ júṣṭāsaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ ghṛtá-nirnijaḥ ǀ guḥ ǀprá ǀ vaḥ ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ harayanta ǀ pūrṇā́ḥ ǀ krátve ǀ dákṣāya ǀ harṣayanta ǀ pītā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “May these sacrifices be (acceptable) to you in heart and mind; may today the sufficient (juices) mixed with butter to you; the full libations are prepared for you; may they, when drunk, animate you for glorious deeds.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते वो॑ हृ॒दे मन॑से सन्तु य॒ज्ञा जुष्टा॑सो अ॒द्य घृ॒तनि॑र्णिजो गुः । प्र व॑: सु॒तासो॑ हरयन्त पू॒र्णाः क्रत्वे॒ दक्षा॑य हर्षयन्त पी॒ताः

devanagari.text: त्र्युदायं देवहितं यथा वः स्तोमो वाजा ऋभुक्षणो ददे वः ।जुह्वे मनुष्वदुपरासु विक्षु युष्मे सचा बृहद्दिवेषु सोमं ॥

transliteration.text: tri-udāyám ǀ devá-hitam ǀ yáthā ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ dadé ǀ vaḥ ǀjuhvé ǀ manuṣvát ǀ úparāsu ǀ vikṣú ǀ yuṣmé íti ǀ sácā ǀ bṛhát-diveṣu ǀ sómam ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “As the offering suited to the gods at the third (daily) sacrifice supports, you,Vājas, Ṛbhukṣans; as the praise (then recited supports you); therefore, likeManu, I offer you theSomajuice, along with the very radiant (deities) among the people assembled at the solemnity.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्र्यु॒दा॒यं दे॒वहि॑तं॒ यथा॑ व॒: स्तोमो॑ वाजा ऋभुक्षणो द॒दे व॑: । जु॒ह्वे म॑नु॒ष्वदुप॑रासु वि॒क्षु यु॒ष्मे सचा॑ बृ॒हद्दि॑वेषु॒ सोम॑म्

devanagari.text: पीवोअश्वाः शुचद्रथा हि भूतायःशिप्रा वाजिनः सुनिष्काः ।इंद्रस्य सूनो शवसो नपातोऽनु वश्चेत्यग्रियं मदाय ॥

transliteration.text: pī́vaḥ-aśvāḥ ǀ śucát-rathāḥ ǀ hí ǀ bhūtá ǀ áyaḥ-śiprāḥ ǀ vājinaḥ ǀ su-niṣkā́ḥ ǀíndrasya ǀ sūno íti ǀ śavasaḥ ǀ napātaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vaḥ ǀ ceti ǀ agriyám ǀ mádāya ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “Vājins, you are borne by stout horses mounted on a brilliant car, have jaws of metal and are possessed of treasures; sons ofIndra, grandsons of strength, this last sacrifice is for your exhilaration.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पीवो॑अश्वाः शु॒चद्र॑था॒ हि भू॒ताय॑:शिप्रा वाजिनः सुनि॒ष्काः । इन्द्र॑स्य सूनो शवसो नपा॒तोऽनु॑ वश्चेत्यग्रि॒यं मदा॑य

devanagari.text: ऋभुमृभुक्षणो रयिं वाजे वाजिंतमं युजं ।इंद्रस्वंतं हवामहे सदासातममश्विनं ॥

transliteration.text: ṛbhúm ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ rayím ǀ vā́je ǀ vājín-tamam ǀ yújam ǀíndrasvantam ǀ havāmahe ǀ sadā-sā́tamam ǀ aśvínam ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “We invoke you, Ṛbhukṣans, for splendid wealth, mutually co-operating, most invigorating in war, affecting the senses, ever munificent, and comprehending horses.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒भुमृ॑भुक्षणो र॒यिं वाजे॑ वा॒जिन्त॑मं॒ युज॑म् । इन्द्र॑स्वन्तं हवामहे सदा॒सात॑मम॒श्विन॑म्

devanagari.text: सेदृभवो यमवथ यूयमिंद्रश्च मर्त्यं ।स धीभिरस्तु सनिता मेधसाता सो अर्वता ॥
सः । इत् । ऋभवः । यम् । अवथ । यूयम् । इन्द्रः । च । मर्त्यम् ।सः । धीभिः । अस्तु । सनिता । मेधऽसाता । सः । अर्वता ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ávatha ǀ yūyám ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ mártyam ǀsáḥ ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ astu ǀ sánitā ǀ medhá-sātā ǀ sáḥ ǀ árvatā ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “May the man whom you,ṚbhusandIndra, favour, be ever liberal by his acts, and possessed of a horse at the sacrifice.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सेदृ॑भवो॒ यमव॑थ यू॒यमिन्द्र॑श्च॒ मर्त्य॑म् । स धी॒भिर॑स्तु॒ सनि॑ता मे॒धसा॑ता॒ सो अर्व॑ता

devanagari.text: वि नो वाजा ऋभुक्षणः पथश्चितन यष्टवे ।अस्मभ्यं सूरयः स्तुता विश्वा आशास्तरीषणि ॥
वि । नः । वाजाः । ऋभुक्षणः । पथः । चितन । यष्टवे ।अस्मभ्यम् । सूरयः । स्तुताः । विश्वाः । आशाः । तरीषणि ॥

transliteration.text: ví ǀ naḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ patháḥ ǀ citana ǀ yáṣṭave ǀasmábhyam ǀ sūrayaḥ ǀ stutā́ḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ tarīṣáṇi ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “Vājas, Ṛbhukṣaṇs, direct us in the way to sacrifice; for you, who are intelligent, being glorified (by us), are able to traverse all the quarters (of space).”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि नो॑ वाजा ऋभुक्षणः प॒थश्चि॑तन॒ यष्ट॑वे । अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ सूरयः स्तु॒ता विश्वा॒ आशा॑स्तरी॒षणि॑

devanagari.text: तं नो वाजा ऋभुक्षण इंद्र नासत्या रयिं ।समश्वं चर्षणिभ्य आ पुरु शस्त मघत्तये ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ naḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ índra ǀ nā́satyā ǀ rayím ǀsám ǀ áśvam ǀ carṣaṇí-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ purú ǀ śasta ǀ magháttaye ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “Vājas, Ṛbhukṣaṇs,Indra,Nāsatyas, command that ample wealth with horses be sent to men for their enrichment.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तं नो॑ वाजा ऋभुक्षण॒ इन्द्र॒ नास॑त्या र॒यिम् । समश्वं॑ चर्ष॒णिभ्य॒ आ पु॒रु श॑स्त म॒घत्त॑ये

devanagari.text: उतो हि वां दात्रा संति पूर्वा या पूरुभ्यस्त्रसदस्युर्नितोशे ।क्षेत्रासां ददथुरुर्वरासां घनं दस्युभ्यो अभिभूतिमुग्रं ॥

transliteration.text: utó íti ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ dātrā́ ǀ sánti ǀ pū́rvā ǀ yā́ ǀ pūrú-bhyaḥ ǀ trasádasyuḥ ǀ ni-tośé ǀkṣetra-sā́m ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ urvarā-sā́m ǀ ghanám ǀ dásyu-bhyaḥ ǀ abhí-bhūtim ǀ ugrám ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Trasadasyuhas bestowed upon many the ancient (gifts) which were obtained by the liberal (prince) through your (favour, Heaven and Earth) you two have given a horse, a son, a weapon (for the destruction) of theDasyus, fierce and foe-subduing.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒तो हि वां॑ दा॒त्रा सन्ति॒ पूर्वा॒ या पू॒रुभ्य॑स्त्र॒सद॑स्युर्नितो॒शे । क्षे॒त्रा॒सां द॑दथुरुर्वरा॒सां घ॒नं दस्यु॑भ्यो अ॒भिभू॑तिमु॒ग्रम्

devanagari.text: उत वाजिनं पुरुनिष्षिध्वानं दधिक्रामु ददथुर्विश्वकृष्टिं ।ऋजिप्यं श्येनं प्रुषितप्सुमाशुं चर्कृत्यमर्यो नृपतिं न शूरं ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ vājínam ǀ puruniḥ-sídhvānam ǀ dadhi-krā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ viśvá-kṛṣṭim ǀṛjipyám ǀ śyenám ǀ pruṣitá-psum ǀ āśúm ǀ carkṛ́tyam ǀ aryáḥ ǀ nṛ-pátim ǀ ná ǀ śū́ram ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “And you two have given the swift Dadhikrā, the repeller of many (foes), the defender of all men, the straight-going, the graceful-moving, the resplendent, the rapid, the destroyer of enemies like a heroic prince.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त वा॒जिनं॑ पुरुनि॒ष्षिध्वा॑नं दधि॒क्रामु॑ ददथुर्वि॒श्वकृ॑ष्टिम् । ऋ॒जि॒प्यं श्ये॒नं प्रु॑षि॒तप्सु॑मा॒शुं च॒र्कृत्य॑म॒र्यो नृ॒पतिं॒ न शूर॑म्

devanagari.text: यं सीमनु प्रवतेव द्रवंतं विश्वः पूरुर्मदति हर्षमाणः ।पड्भिर्गृध्यंतं मेधयुं न शूरं रथतुरं वातमिव ध्रजंतं ॥

transliteration.text: yám ǀ sīm ǀ ánu ǀ pravátā-iva ǀ drávantam ǀ víśvaḥ ǀ pūrúḥ ǀ mádati ǀ hárṣamāṇaḥ ǀpaṭ-bhíḥ ǀ gṛ́dhyantam ǀ medha-yúm ǀ ná ǀ śū́ram ǀ ratha-túram ǀ vā́tam-iva ǀ dhrájantam ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Whom all men, rejoicing, praise, rushing everywhere, as if down a precipice, springing with his feet like a hero eager for war, drawing a car, and going as swift as the wind.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यं सी॒मनु॑ प्र॒वते॑व॒ द्रव॑न्तं॒ विश्व॑: पू॒रुर्मद॑ति॒ हर्ष॑माणः । प॒ड्भिर्गृध्य॑न्तं मेध॒युं न शूरं॑ रथ॒तुरं॒ वात॑मिव॒ ध्रज॑न्तम्

devanagari.text: यः स्मारुंधानो गध्या समत्सु सनुतरश्चरति गोषु गच्छन् ।आविर्ऋजीको विदथा निचिक्यत्तिरो अरतिं पर्याप आयोः ॥

transliteration.text: yáḥ ǀ sma ǀ ā-rundhānáḥ ǀ gádhyā ǀ samát-su ǀ sánu-taraḥ ǀ cárati ǀ góṣu ǀ gácchan ǀāvíḥ-ṛjīkaḥ ǀ vidáthā ǀ ni-cíkyat ǀ tiráḥ ǀ aratím ǀ pári ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ āyóḥ ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Who, opposing the mingled multitude in battles, rushes eager, passing through the regions, whose vigour is manifestl, who, understanding what is to be known, puts to shame the adversary of the (pious) man.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यः स्मा॑रुन्धा॒नो गध्या॑ स॒मत्सु॒ सनु॑तर॒श्चर॑ति॒ गोषु॒ गच्छ॑न् । आ॒विॠ॑जीको वि॒दथा॑ नि॒चिक्य॑त्ति॒रो अ॑र॒तिं पर्याप॑ आ॒योः

devanagari.text: उत स्मैनं वस्त्रमथिं न तायुमनु क्रोशंति क्षितयो भरेषु ।नीचायमानं जसुरिं न श्येनं श्रवश्चाच्छा पशुमच्च यूथं ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ sma ǀ enam ǀ vastra-máthim ǀ ná ǀ tāyúm ǀ ánu ǀ krośanti ǀ kṣitáyaḥ ǀ bháreṣu ǀnīcā́ ǀ áyamānam ǀ jásurim ǀ ná ǀ śyenám ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ ca ǀ áccha ǀ paśu-mát ǀ ca ǀ yūthám ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Whom men call after in battles, as after a thief carrying off a garment, or as (after) a hungry hawk pouncing (upon his prey); they call after him, hastening to obtain food, or a herd of cattle.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्मै॑नं वस्त्र॒मथिं॒ न ता॒युमनु॑ क्रोशन्ति क्षि॒तयो॒ भरे॑षु । नी॒चाय॑मानं॒ जसु॑रिं॒ न श्ये॒नं श्रव॒श्चाच्छा॑ पशु॒मच्च॑ यू॒थम्

devanagari.text: उत स्मासु प्रथमः सरिष्यन्नि वेवेति श्रेणिभी रथानां ।स्रजं कृण्वानो जन्यो न शुभ्वा रेणुं रेरिहत्किरणं ददश्वान् ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ sma ǀ āsu ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ sariṣyán ǀ ní ǀ veveti ǀ śréṇi-bhiḥ ǀ ráthānām ǀsrájam ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ jányaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śúbhvā ǀ reṇúm ǀ rérihat ǀ kiráṇam ǀ dadaśvā́n ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “And who, issuing forth the first in those encounters, rushes in various directions with rows of chariots; like an elegant (courser), friendly to man, decorated with a garland, raising the dust, and champing his bit.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्मा॑सु प्रथ॒मः स॑रि॒ष्यन्नि वे॑वेति॒ श्रेणि॑भी॒ रथा॑नाम् । स्रजं॑ कृण्वा॒नो जन्यो॒ न शुभ्वा॑ रे॒णुं रेरि॑हत्कि॒रणं॑ दद॒श्वान्

devanagari.text: उत स्य वाजी सहुरिर्ऋतावा शुश्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये ।तुरं यतीषु तुरयन्नृजिप्योऽधि भ्रुवोः किरते रेणुमृंजन् ॥
उत । स्यः । वाजी । सहुरिः । ऋतऽवा । शुश्रूषमाणः । तन्वा । सऽमर्ये ।तुरम् । यतीषु । तुरयन् । ऋजिप्यः । अधि । भ्रुवोः । किरते । रेणुम् । ऋञ्जन् ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ syáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ sáhuriḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ śúśrūṣamāṇaḥ ǀ tanvā́ ǀ sa-maryé ǀtúram ǀ yatī́ṣu ǀ turáyan ǀ ṛjipyáḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ bhruvóḥ ǀ kirate ǀ reṇúm ǀ ṛñján ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “And that swift (horse) enduring in battle, bestowing food, and doing service with his limbs, rushing swiftly upon the quick-moving (host of the enemy), going straight onward, and tossing up the dust, throws it above his brows.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्य वा॒जी सहु॑रिॠ॒तावा॒ शुश्रू॑षमाणस्त॒न्वा॑ सम॒र्ये । तुरं॑ य॒तीषु॑ तु॒रय॑न्नृजि॒प्योऽधि॑ भ्रु॒वोः कि॑रते रे॒णुमृ॒ञ्जन्

devanagari.text: उत स्मास्य तन्यतोरिव द्योर्ऋघायतो अभियुजो भयंते ।यदा सहस्रमभि षीमयोधीद्दुर्वर्तुः स्मा भवति भीम ऋंजन् ॥
उत । स्म । अस्य । तन्यतोःऽइव । द्योः । ऋघायतः । अभिऽयुजः । भयन्ते ।यदा । सहस्रम् । अभि । सीम् । अयोधीत् । दुःऽवर्तुः । स्म । भवति । भीमः । ऋञ्जन् ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ sma ǀ asya ǀ tanyatóḥ-iva ǀ dyóḥ ǀ ṛghāyatáḥ ǀ abhi-yújaḥ ǀ bhayante ǀyadā́ ǀ sahásram ǀ abhí ǀ sīm ǀ áyodhīt ǀ duḥ-vártuḥ ǀ sma ǀ bhavati ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ṛñján ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “And the adversaries of that foe-destroying steed, like (those) of the brilliant thunderbolt, are alarmed; for when he contends, even against thousands on every side, then, rousing (his spirit), he is fearful and irresistible.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्मा॑स्य तन्य॒तोरि॑व॒ द्योॠ॑घाय॒तो अ॑भि॒युजो॑ भयन्ते । य॒दा स॒हस्र॑म॒भि षी॒मयो॑धीद्दु॒र्वर्तु॑: स्मा भवति भी॒म ऋ॒ञ्जन्

devanagari.text: उत स्मास्य पनयंति जना जूतिं कृष्टिप्रो अभिभूतिमाशोः ।उतैनमाहुः समिथे वियंतः परा दधिक्रा असरत्सहस्रैः ॥
उत । स्म । अस्य । पनयन्ति । जनाः । जूतिम् । कृष्टिऽप्रः । अभिऽभूतिम् । आशोः ।उत । एनम् । आहुः । सम्ऽइथे । विऽयन्तः । परा । दधिऽक्राः । असरत् । सहस्रैः ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ sma ǀ asya ǀ panayanti ǀ jánāḥ ǀ jūtím ǀ kṛṣṭi-práḥ ǀ abhí-bhūtim ǀ āśóḥ ǀutá ǀ enam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ sam-ithé ǀ vi-yántaḥ ǀ párā ǀ dadhi-krā́ḥ ǀ asarat ǀ sahásraiḥ ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Men praise the overpowering rapidty of that fleet (steed), who is the accomplisher (of the desires) of mankind, and following him to battle, they have said, Dadhikrā with (his) thousands has gone forth against the foe.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्मा॑स्य पनयन्ति॒ जना॑ जू॒तिं कृ॑ष्टि॒प्रो अ॒भिभू॑तिमा॒शोः । उ॒तैन॑माहुः समि॒थे वि॒यन्त॒: परा॑ दधि॒क्रा अ॑सरत्स॒हस्रै॑:

devanagari.text: आ दधिक्राः शवसा पंच कृष्टीः सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान ।सहस्रसाः शतसा वाज्यर्वा पृणक्तु मध्वा समिमा वचांसि ॥
आ । दधिऽक्राः । शवसा । पञ्च । कृष्टीः । सूर्यःऽइव । ज्योतिषा । अपः । ततान ।सहस्रऽसाः । शतऽसाः । वाजी । अर्वा । पृणक्तु । मध्वा । सम् । इमा । वचांसि ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ dadhi-krā́ḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ páñca ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ-iva ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ apáḥ ǀ tatāna ǀsahasra-sā́ḥ ǀ śata-sā́ḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ árvā ǀ pṛṇáktu ǀ mádhvā ǀ sám ǀ imā́ ǀ vácāṃsi ǁ

Sukta 38.translation: “Dadhikrā has spread abroad the five classes of beings by his strength, as the sun (diffuses) the waters by his radiance; may he, the giver of hundreds and thousands, associate these praises with agreeable (rewards).”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ द॑धि॒क्राः शव॑सा॒ पञ्च॑ कृ॒ष्टीः सूर्य॑ इव॒ ज्योति॑षा॒पस्त॑तान । स॒ह॒स्र॒साः श॑त॒सा वा॒ज्यर्वा॑ पृ॒णक्तु॒ मध्वा॒ समि॒मा वचां॑सि

devanagari.text: आशुं दधिक्रां तमु नु ष्टवाम दिवस्पृथिव्या उत चर्किराम ।उच्छंतीर्मामुषसः सूदयंत्वति विश्वानि दुरितानि पर्षन् ॥
आशुम् । दधिऽक्राम् । तम् । ऊं इति । नु । स्तवाम । दिवः । पृथिव्याः । उत । चर्किराम ।उच्छन्तीः । माम् । उषसः । सूदयन्तु । अति । विश्वानि । दुःऽइतानि । पर्षन् ॥

transliteration.text: āśúm ǀ dadhi-krā́m ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ stavāma ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ carkirāma ǀucchántīḥ ǀ mā́m ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sūdayantu ǀ áti ǀ víśvāni ǀ duḥ-itā́ni ǀ parṣan ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “Verily we praise that swift Dadhikrā and scatter (proved before him) from heaven and earth; may the gloom-dispelling dawns preserve for me (all good things), and bear me beyond all evils.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒शुं द॑धि॒क्रां तमु॒ नु ष्ट॑वाम दि॒वस्पृ॑थि॒व्या उ॒त च॑र्किराम । उ॒च्छन्ती॒र्मामु॒षस॑: सूदय॒न्त्वति॒ विश्वा॑नि दुरि॒तानि॑ पर्षन्

devanagari.text: महश्चर्कर्म्यर्वतः क्रतुप्रा दधिक्राव्णः पुरुवारस्य वृष्णः ।यं पूरुभ्यो दीदिवांसं नाग्निं ददथुर्मित्रावरुणा ततुरिं ॥
महः । चर्कर्मि । अर्वतः । क्रतुऽप्राः । दधिऽक्राव्णः । पुरुऽवारस्य । वृष्णः ।यम् । पूरुऽभ्यः । दीदिऽवांसम् । न । अग्निम् । ददथुः । मित्रावरुणा । ततुरिम् ॥

transliteration.text: maháḥ ǀ carkarmi ǀ árvataḥ ǀ kratu-prā́ḥ ǀ dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ puru-vā́rasya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀyám ǀ pūrú-bhyaḥ ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsam ǀ ná ǀ agním ǀ dadáthuḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ táturim ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “Fulfiller of religious rites, I reiterate the praise of the great Dadhikrā, the liberal, many-honoured showerer (of benefits), whomMitraandVaruṇagave for the good of many, the transporter (beyond calamity), as brilliant asAgni.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒हश्च॑र्क॒र्म्यर्व॑तः क्रतु॒प्रा द॑धि॒क्राव्ण॑: पुरु॒वार॑स्य॒ वृष्ण॑: । यं पू॒रुभ्यो॑ दीदि॒वांसं॒ नाग्निं द॒दथु॑र्मित्रावरुणा॒ ततु॑रिम्

devanagari.text: यो अश्वस्य दधिक्राव्णो अकारीत्समिद्धे अग्ना उषसो व्युष्टौ ।अनागसं तमदितिः कृणोतु स मित्रेण वरुणेना सजोषाः ॥
यः । अश्वस्य । दधिऽक्राव्णः । अकारीत् । सम्ऽइद्धे । अग्नौ । उषसः । विऽउष्टौ ।अनागसम् । तम् । अदितिः । कृणोतु । सः । मित्रेण । वरुणेन । सऽजोषाः ॥

transliteration.text: yáḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ ákārīt ǀ sám-iddhe ǀ agnáu ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀánāgasam ǀ tám ǀ áditiḥ ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ sáḥ ǀ mitréṇa ǀ váruṇena ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “MayAditi, consentient withMitraandVaruṇarender him free from sin who has performed the worship of the steed Dadhikrā, when the fire has been kindled at the opening of the dawn.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यो अश्व॑स्य दधि॒क्राव्णो॒ अका॑री॒त्समि॑द्धे अ॒ग्ना उ॒षसो॒ व्यु॑ष्टौ । अना॑गसं॒ तमदि॑तिः कृणोतु॒ स मि॒त्रेण॒ वरु॑णेना स॒जोषा॑:

devanagari.text: दधिक्राव्ण इष ऊर्जो महो यदमन्महि मरुतां नाम भद्रं ।स्वस्तये वरुणं मित्रमग्निं हवामह इंद्रं वज्रबाहुं ॥
दधिऽक्राव्णः । इषः । ऊर्जः । महः । यत् । अमन्महि । मरुताम् । नाम । भद्रम् ।स्वस्तये । वरुणम् । मित्रम् । अग्निम् । हवामहे । इन्द्रम् । वज्रऽबाहुम् ॥

transliteration.text: dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ iṣáḥ ǀ ūrjáḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ yát ǀ ámanmahi ǀ marútām ǀ nā́ma ǀ bhadrám ǀsvastáye ǀ váruṇam ǀ mitrám ǀ agním ǀ hávāmahe ǀ índram ǀ vájra-bāhum ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “While we glorify the name of the great Dadhikrā the means of sustenance and of strength, the prosperity of those who praise (him), let us invoke (also) for our welfareVaruṇa,Mitra,Agni, andIndra, the bearer of the thunderbolt.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द॒धि॒क्राव्ण॑ इ॒ष ऊ॒र्जो म॒हो यदम॑न्महि म॒रुतां॒ नाम॑ भ॒द्रम् । स्व॒स्तये॒ वरु॑णं मि॒त्रम॒ग्निं हवा॑मह॒ इन्द्रं॒ वज्र॑बाहुम्

devanagari.text: इंद्रमिवेदुभये वि ह्वयंत उदीराणा यज्ञमुपप्रयंतः ।दधिक्रामु सूदनं मर्त्याय ददथुर्मित्रावरुणा नो अश्वं ॥
इन्द्रम्ऽइव । इत् । उभये । वि । ह्वयन्ते । उत्ऽईराणाः । यज्ञम् । उपऽप्रयन्तः ।दधिऽक्राम् । ऊं इति । सूदनम् । मर्त्याय । ददथुः । मित्रावरुणा । नः । अश्वम् ॥

transliteration.text: índram-iva ǀ ít ǀ ubháye ǀ ví ǀ hvayante ǀ ut-ī́rāṇāḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ upa-prayántaḥ ǀdadhi-krā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sū́danam ǀ mártyāya ǀ dadáthuḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ naḥ ǀ áśvam ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “Those who are preparing for battle, those who are proceeding to sacrifice, both invoke (Dadhikra) as if (he was)Indra;MitraandVaruṇahave given to us the horse Dadhikrā as an encourager to man.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॑मि॒वेदु॒भये॒ वि ह्व॑यन्त उ॒दीरा॑णा य॒ज्ञमु॑पप्र॒यन्त॑: । द॒धि॒क्रामु॒ सूद॑नं॒ मर्त्या॑य द॒दथु॑र्मित्रावरुणा नो॒ अश्व॑म्

devanagari.text: दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषं जिष्णोरश्वस्य वाजिनः ।सुरभि नो मुखा करत्प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषत् ॥
दधिऽक्राव्णः । अकारिषम् । जिष्णोः । अश्वस्य । वाजिनः ।सुरभि । नः । मुखा । करत् । प्र । नः । आयूंषि । तारिषत् ॥

transliteration.text: dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ akāriṣam ǀ jiṣṇóḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ vājínaḥ ǀsurabhí ǀ naḥ ǀ múkhā ǀ karat ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yūṃṣi ǀ tāriṣat ǁ

Sukta 39.translation: “I have celebrated the praise of Dadhikrā, the rapid and victorious stee; may he make our mouths fragrant, may he prolong our lives.”
Sukta 39.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द॒धि॒क्राव्णो॑ अकारिषं जि॒ष्णोरश्व॑स्य वा॒जिन॑: । सु॒र॒भि नो॒ मुखा॑ कर॒त्प्र ण॒ आयूं॑षि तारिषत्

devanagari.text: दधिक्राव्ण इदु नु चर्किराम विश्वा इन्मामुषसः सूदयंतु ।अपामग्नेरुषसः सूर्यस्य बृहस्पतेरांगिरसस्य जिष्णोः ॥
दधिऽक्राव्णः । इत् । ऊं इति । नु । चर्किराम । विश्वा । इत् । माम् । उषसः । सूदयन्तु ।अपाम् । अग्नेः । उषसः । सूर्यस्य । बृहस्पतेः । आङ्गिरसस्य । जिष्णोः ॥

transliteration.text: dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ carkirāma ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ mā́m ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sūdayantu ǀapā́m ǀ agnéḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ bṛ́haspáteḥ ǀ āṅgirasásya ǀ jiṣṇóḥ ǁ

Sukta 40.translation: “May we repeatedly recite (the praise) of Dadhikrāvaṇ; may all rising dawns excite me (to the adoration) of the waters, ofAgni, of Uṣas, ofSūrya, ofBṛhaspati, and ofJiṣṇu, the son ofAṅgiras.”
Sukta 40.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द॒धि॒क्राव्ण॒ इदु॒ नु च॑र्किराम॒ विश्वा॒ इन्मामु॒षस॑: सूदयन्तु । अ॒पाम॒ग्नेरु॒षस॒: सूर्य॑स्य॒ बृह॒स्पते॑राङ्गिर॒सस्य॑ जि॒ष्णोः

devanagari.text: सत्वा भरिषो गविषो दुवन्यसच्छ्रवस्यादिष उषसस्तुरण्यसत् ।सत्यो द्रवो द्रवरः पतंगरो दधिक्रावेषमूर्जं स्वर्जनत् ॥

Sukta 40.translation: “May Dadhikrāvaṇ, the active, the cherisher, the giver of cattle, who abides with the devout, the swift-going, be willing to accept (the sacrificial) food at the time of the desirable dawn; may he who is true, moving, rapid, and leaping like a grasshopper, produce (for us) food, strength and heaven.”
Sukta 40.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सत्वा॑ भरि॒षो ग॑वि॒षो दु॑वन्य॒सच्छ्र॑व॒स्यादि॒ष उ॒षस॑स्तुरण्य॒सत् । स॒त्यो द्र॒वो द्र॑व॒रः प॑तंग॒रो द॑धि॒क्रावेष॒मूर्जं॒ स्व॑र्जनत्

devanagari.text: उत स्मास्य द्रवतस्तुरण्यतः पर्णं न वेरनु वाति प्रगर्धिनः ।श्येनस्येव ध्रजतो अंकसं परि दधिक्राव्णः सहोर्जा तरित्रतः ॥

transliteration.text: utá ǀ sma ǀ asya ǀ drávataḥ ǀ turaṇyatáḥ ǀ parṇám ǀ ná ǀ véḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vāti ǀ pra-gardhínaḥ ǀśyenásya-iva ǀ dhrájataḥ ǀ aṅkasám ǀ pári ǀ dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ sahá ǀ ūrjā́ ǀ táritrataḥ ǁ

Sukta 40.translation: “And after him who is quick-going, hastening, eager (to arrive at his goald, men) follow (as other birds pursue) the flight of a swift (bird) striving together to keep up by the side of Dadhikrāvan. the transporter (of others) as swift as a hawk.”
Sukta 40.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्मा॑स्य॒ द्रव॑तस्तुरण्य॒तः प॒र्णं न वेरनु॑ वाति प्रग॒र्धिन॑: । श्ये॒नस्ये॑व॒ ध्रज॑तो अङ्क॒सं परि॑ दधि॒क्राव्ण॑: स॒होर्जा तरि॑त्रतः

devanagari.text: उत स्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि ।क्रतुं दधिक्रा अनु संतवीत्वत्पथामंकांस्यन्वापनीफणत् ॥

Sukta 40.translation: “And that horse bound by his neck, his flanks, his mouth, accelerates his paces; Dadhikrā increasing in vigour after the (sacred rite), following the windings of the roads, goes still more rapidly.”
Sukta 40.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्य वा॒जी क्षि॑प॒णिं तु॑रण्यति ग्री॒वायां॑ ब॒द्धो अ॑पिक॒क्ष आ॒सनि॑ । क्रतुं॑ दधि॒क्रा अनु॑ सं॒तवी॑त्वत्प॒थामङ्कां॒स्यन्वा॒पनी॑फणत्

transliteration.text: haṃsáḥ ǀ śuci-sát ǀ vásuḥ ǀ antarikṣa-sát ǀ hótā ǀ vedi-sát ǀ átithiḥ ǀ duroṇa-sát ǀnṛ-sát ǀ vara-sát ǀ ṛta-sát ǀ vyoma-sát ǀ ap-jā́ḥ ǀ go-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛta-jā́ḥ ǀ adri-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛtám ǁ

Sukta 40.translation: “He is theHaṃsa, (the sun), dwelling;Vasu(the wind), dwelling in the firmament; the invoker of the gods (Agni), dwelling on the altar; the guest (of the worshipper), dweling in the house (as the culinary fire); the dweller among men, (as consciousness), the dweller in the most excellent (orbl, the sun), the dweller in truth, the dweller in the sky (the air), born in the waters, in the rays of light, in the verity (of manifestation) in the (eastern) mountain, the truth (itself).”
Sukta 40.sanskrit_wisdomlib: हं॒सः शु॑चि॒षद्वसु॑रन्तरिक्ष॒सद्धोता॑ वेदि॒षदति॑थिर्दुरोण॒सत् । नृ॒षद्व॑र॒सदृ॑त॒सद्व्यो॑म॒सद॒ब्जा गो॒जा ऋ॑त॒जा अ॑द्रि॒जा ऋ॒तम्

devanagari.text: इंद्रा को वां वरुणा सुम्नमाप स्तोमो हविष्माँ अमृतो न होता ।यो वां हृदि क्रतुमाँ अस्मदुक्तः पस्पर्शदिंद्रावरुणा नमस्वान् ॥

transliteration.text: índrā ǀ káḥ ǀ vām ǀ varuṇā ǀ sumnám ǀ āpa ǀ stómaḥ ǀ havíṣmān ǀ amṛ́taḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǀyáḥ ǀ vām ǀ hṛdí ǀ krátu-mān ǀ asmát ǀ uktáḥ ǀ paspárśat ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ námasvān ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “Indra(andVaruṇa), Varuṇa (and Indra), what praise of you accompanied by oblations may obtain for us felicity, (such as) the immortal invoker of the gods, (Agni, may bestow); may (the praise) which is addressed by us to you both, Indra and Varuṇa, sanctified by acts and prompted by veneration, touch your heartṣ ”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॒ को वां॑ वरुणा सु॒म्नमा॑प॒ स्तोमो॑ ह॒विष्माँ॑ अ॒मृतो॒ न होता॑ । यो वां॑ हृ॒दि क्रतु॑माँ अ॒स्मदु॒क्तः प॒स्पर्श॑दिन्द्रावरुणा॒ नम॑स्वान्

devanagari.text: इंद्रा ह यो वरुणा चक्र आपी देवौ मर्तः सख्याय प्रयस्वान् ।स हंति वृत्रा समिथेषु शत्रूनवोभिर्वा महद्भिः स प्र शृण्वे ॥

transliteration.text: índrā ǀ ha ǀ yáḥ ǀ váruṇā ǀ cakré ǀ āpī́ íti ǀ deváu ǀ mártaḥ ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ práyasvān ǀsáḥ ǀ hanti ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ sam-ithéṣu ǀ śátrūn ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ vā ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ prá ǀ śṛṇve ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “DivineIndraandVaruṇa, the mortal diligent in offering (you) sacrificial food, who has through friendship made you his kinsmen, destroys (his own) sins, and his enemies in battle; and by your great favours he becomes renowned.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑ ह॒ यो वरु॑णा च॒क्र आ॒पी दे॒वौ मर्त॑: स॒ख्याय॒ प्रय॑स्वान् । स ह॑न्ति वृ॒त्रा स॑मि॒थेषु॒ शत्रू॒नवो॑भिर्वा म॒हद्भि॒: स प्र शृ॑ण्वे

devanagari.text: इंद्रा ह रत्नं वरुणा धेष्ठेत्था नृभ्यः शशमानेभ्यस्ता ।यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादयैते ॥

transliteration.text: índrā ǀ ha ǀ rátnam ǀ váruṇā ǀ dhéṣṭhā ǀ itthā́ ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ śaśamānébhyaḥ ǀ tā́ ǀyádi ǀ sákhāyā ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ sómaiḥ ǀ sutébhiḥ ǀ su-prayásā ǀ mādáyaite íti ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “IndraandVaruṇa(you are) most liberal givers of wealth to men praising you in various ways, when as friends well plural ed with (sacrificial) food, you are exhilarated by theSomajuice effused through friendship.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑ ह॒ रत्नं॒ वरु॑णा॒ धेष्ठे॒त्था नृभ्य॑: शशमा॒नेभ्य॒स्ता । यदी॒ सखा॑या स॒ख्याय॒ सोमै॑: सु॒तेभि॑: सुप्र॒यसा॑ मा॒दयै॑ते

devanagari.text: इंद्रा युवं वरुणा दिद्युमस्मिन्नोजिष्ठमुग्रा नि वधिष्टं वज्रं ।यो नो दुरेवो वृकतिर्दभीतिस्तस्मिन्मिमाथामभिभूत्योजः ॥

Sukta 41.translation: “FierceIndraandVaruṇayou hurled the bright-shining and most mighty thunderbolt against this (our foe), who is difficult ot be resisted by us; (who is) rapacious, malevolent; grant us strength to overcome him.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑ यु॒वं व॑रुणा दि॒द्युम॑स्मि॒न्नोजि॑ष्ठमुग्रा॒ नि व॑धिष्टं॒ वज्र॑म् । यो नो॑ दु॒रेवो॑ वृ॒कति॑र्द॒भीति॒स्तस्मि॑न्मिमाथाम॒भिभू॒त्योज॑:

Sukta 41.translation: “IndraandVaruṇa, be the exciters of this our praise, as the bull is of the cows; may that cow (of praise) yield us (reward), like a large cow that has gone forth to pasture, whose thousand channels (are filled) with milk.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑ यु॒वं व॑रुणा भू॒तम॒स्या धि॒यः प्रे॒तारा॑ वृष॒भेव॑ धे॒नोः । सा नो॑ दुहीय॒द्यव॑सेव ग॒त्वी स॒हस्र॑धारा॒ पय॑सा म॒ही गौः

Sukta 41.translation: “MayIndraandVaruṇa, the overthrowers (of foes), be around us with (their) protections; (that thereby we may have) good sons and grandsons, and fertile lands, and long life, and virility.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तो॒के हि॒ते तन॑य उ॒र्वरा॑सु॒ सूरो॒ दृशी॑के॒ वृष॑णश्च॒ पौंस्ये॑ । इन्द्रा॑ नो॒ अत्र॒ वरु॑णा स्याता॒मवो॑भिर्द॒स्मा परि॑तक्म्यायाम्

transliteration.text: yuvā́m ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ ávase ǀ pūrvyā́ya ǀ pári ǀ prábhūtī íti prá-bhūtī ǀ go-íṣaḥ ǀ svāpī íti su-āpī ǀvṛṇīmáhe ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ priyā́ya ǀ śū́rā ǀ máṃhiṣṭhā ǀ pitárā-iva ǀ śambhū́ íti śam-bhū́ ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “Desirous of (possessing) cattlle, we have recourse to you,IndraandVaruṇa, for full protection, you who are powerful and kind as (kinsmen); we have recourse to you, adorable heroes, for (your) friendship and affection, (to you who are), like parents, givers of happiness.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒वामिद्ध्यव॑से पू॒र्व्याय॒ परि॒ प्रभू॑ती ग॒विष॑: स्वापी । वृ॒णी॒महे॑ स॒ख्याय॑ प्रि॒याय॒ शूरा॒ मंहि॑ष्ठा पि॒तरे॑व श॒म्भू

devanagari.text: ता वां धियोऽवसे वाजयंतीराजिं न जग्मुर्युवयूः सुदानू ।श्रिये न गाव उप सोममस्थुरिंद्रं गिरो वरुणं मे मनीषाः ॥

transliteration.text: tā́ḥ ǀ vām ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ ávase ǀ vāja-yántīḥ ǀ ājím ǀ ná ǀ jagmuḥ ǀ yuva-yū́ḥ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀśriyé ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sómam ǀ asthuḥ ǀ índram ǀ gíraḥ ǀ váruṇam ǀ me ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “Liberal givers, those (our) praises soliciting (abundant) food have proceeded to you for (your) protection; longing for you as (soldiers long) for battle, and as cattle approach theSomafor (its) advantage, so my heartfelt hymns (approach)IndraandVaruṇa.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ता वां॒ धियोऽव॑से वाज॒यन्ती॑रा॒जिं न ज॑ग्मुर्युव॒यूः सु॑दानू । श्रि॒ये न गाव॒ उप॒ सोम॑मस्थु॒रिन्द्रं॒ गिरो॒ वरु॑णं मे मनी॒षाः

devanagari.text: इमा इंद्रं वरुणं मे मनीषा अग्मन्नुप द्रविणमिच्छमानाः ।उपेमस्थुर्जोष्टार इव वस्वो रघ्वीरिव श्रवसो भिक्षमाणाः ॥
इमाः । इन्द्रम् । वरुणम् । मे । मनीषाः । अग्मन् । उप । द्रविणम् । इच्छमानाः ।उप । ईम् । अस्थुः । जोष्टारःऽइव । वस्वः । रघ्वीःऽइव । श्रवसः । भिक्षमाणाः ॥

transliteration.text: imā́ḥ ǀ índram ǀ váruṇam ǀ me ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǀ ágman ǀ úpa ǀ dráviṇam ǀ icchámānāḥ ǀúpa ǀ īm ǀ asthuḥ ǀ joṣṭā́raḥ-iva ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ raghvī́ḥ-iva ǀ śrávasaḥ ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “These my earnest praises approachIndraandVaruṇa, desirous to obtain wealth, as dependants attend (upon an opulent man) for the sake of riches, like humble (feminine les) begging for food.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मा इन्द्रं॒ वरु॑णं मे मनी॒षा अग्म॒न्नुप॒ द्रवि॑णमि॒च्छमा॑नाः । उपे॑मस्थुर्जो॒ष्टार॑ इव॒ वस्वो॑ र॒घ्वीरि॑व॒ श्रव॑सो॒ भिक्ष॑माणाः

devanagari.text: अश्व्यस्य त्मना रथ्यस्य पुष्टेर्नित्यस्य रायः पतयः स्याम ।ता चक्राणा ऊतिभिर्नव्यसीभिरस्मत्रा रायो नियुतः सचंतां ॥
अश्व्यस्य । त्मना । रथ्यस्य । पुष्टेः । नित्यस्य । रायः । पतयः । स्याम ।ता । चक्राणौ । ऊतिऽभिः । नव्यसीभिः । अस्मऽत्रा । रायः । निऽयुतः । सचन्ताम् ॥

transliteration.text: áśvyasya ǀ tmánā ǀ ráthyasya ǀ puṣṭéḥ ǀ nítyasya ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ syāma ǀtā́ ǀ cakrāṇáu ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ návyasībhiḥ ǀ asma-trā́ ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ sacantām ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “May we of our own (right) be the masters of permanent riches, comprising horses, chariots, and nourishment; may those two, traversing (the regions), direct theirNiyutsteeds towards us, associating (them) with riches and with recent protections.”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अश्व्य॑स्य॒ त्मना॒ रथ्य॑स्य पु॒ष्टेर्नित्य॑स्य रा॒यः पत॑यः स्याम । ता च॑क्रा॒णा ऊ॒तिभि॒र्नव्य॑सीभिरस्म॒त्रा रायो॑ नि॒युत॑: सचन्ताम्

devanagari.text: आ नो बृहंता बृहतीभिरूती इंद्र यातं वरुण वाजसातौ ।यद्दिद्यवः पृतनासु प्रक्रीळांतस्य वां स्याम सनितार आजेः ॥
आ । नः । बृहन्ता । बृहतीभिः । ऊती । इन्द्र । यातम् । वरुण । वाजऽसातौ ।यत् । दिद्यवः । पृतनासु । प्रऽक्रीळान् । तस्य । वाम् । स्याम । सनितारः । आजेः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bṛhantā ǀ bṛhatī́bhiḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ índra ǀ yātám ǀ varuṇa ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀyát ǀ didyávaḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ pra-krī́ḷān ǀ tásya ǀ vām ǀ syāma ǀ sanitā́raḥ ǀ ājéḥ ǁ

Sukta 41.translation: “MightyIndraandVaruṇa, come to us in battle with (your) powerful protections, and where the bright (weapons) plural y amidst the (hostile) hosts, may we triumph in that conflict (through) your (favour).”
Sukta 41.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ नो॑ बृहन्ता बृह॒तीभि॑रू॒ती इन्द्र॑ या॒तं व॑रुण॒ वाज॑सातौ । यद्दि॒द्यव॒: पृत॑नासु प्र॒क्रीळा॒न्तस्य॑ वां स्याम सनि॒तार॑ आ॒जेः

devanagari.text: मम द्विता राष्ट्रं क्षत्रियस्य विश्वायोर्विश्वे अमृता यथा नः ।क्रतुं सचंते वरुणस्य देवा राजामि कृष्टेरुपमस्य वव्रेः ॥

transliteration.text: máma ǀ dvitā́ ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ kṣatríyasya ǀ viśvá-āyoḥ ǀ víśve ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀkrátum ǀ sacante ǀ váruṇasya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ rā́jāmi ǀ kṛṣṭéḥ ǀ upamásya ǀ vavréḥ ǁ

Sukta 42.translation: “Twofold is my empire, that of the wholekṣatriyarace, and all the immortals are ours; the gods associate me with the acts ofVaruṇa; I rule over (those) of the proximate form of man.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मम॑ द्वि॒ता रा॒ष्ट्रं क्ष॒त्रिय॑स्य वि॒श्वायो॒र्विश्वे॑ अ॒मृता॒ यथा॑ नः । क्रतुं॑ सचन्ते॒ वरु॑णस्य दे॒वा राजा॑मि कृ॒ष्टेरु॑प॒मस्य॑ व॒व्रेः

devanagari.text: अहं राजा वरुणो मह्यं तान्यसुर्याणि प्रथमा धारयंत ।क्रतुं सचंते वरुणस्य देवा राजामि कृष्टेरुपमस्य वव्रेः ॥

transliteration.text: ahám ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ tā́ni ǀ asuryā́ṇi ǀ prathamā́ ǀ dhārayanta ǀkrátum ǀ sacante ǀ váruṇasya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ rā́jāmi ǀ kṛṣṭéḥ ǀ upamásya ǀ vavréḥ ǁ

Sukta 42.translation: “I am the kingVaruṇa; on me (the gods) bestow those principal energies (that are) destructive of theasuras; (they) associate me with the worship of Varuṇa; I rule over (the nets) of the proximate form of man.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒हं राजा॒ वरु॑णो॒ मह्यं॒ तान्य॑सु॒र्या॑णि प्रथ॒मा धा॑रयन्त । क्रतुं॑ सचन्ते॒ वरु॑णस्य दे॒वा राजा॑मि कृ॒ष्टेरु॑प॒मस्य॑ व॒व्रेः

devanagari.text: अहमिंद्रो वरुणस्ते महित्वोर्वी गभीरे रजसी सुमेके ।त्वष्टेव विश्वा भुवनानि विद्वान्त्समैरयं रोदसी धारयं च ॥

transliteration.text: ahám ǀ índraḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ té íti ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ gabhīré íti ǀ rájasī íti ǀ suméke íti su-méke ǀtváṣṭā-iva ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ sám ǀ airayam ǀ ródasī íti ǀ dhāráyam ǀ ca ǁ

Sukta 42.translation: “I amIndra, I amVaruṇa, I am those two in greatness; (I am) the vast, profound, beautiful, heaven and earth; intelligent, I giveTvaṣṭā-like animation to all beings; I uphold earth and heaven].”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒हमिन्द्रो॒ वरु॑ण॒स्ते म॑हि॒त्वोर्वी ग॑भी॒रे रज॑सी सु॒मेके॑ । त्वष्टे॑व॒ विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि वि॒द्वान्त्समै॑रयं॒ रोद॑सी धा॒रयं॑ च

devanagari.text: अहमपो अपिन्वमुक्षमाणा धारयं दिवं सदन ऋतस्य ।ऋतेन पुत्रो अदितेर्ऋतावोत त्रिधातु प्रथयद्वि भूम ॥

Sukta 42.translation: “I have distributed the moisture-shedding waters; I have upheld the sky as the abode of the water; by the water I have become the preserver of the water, the son ofAditi, illustrating the threefold elementary space.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒हम॒पो अ॑पिन्वमु॒क्षमा॑णा धा॒रयं॒ दिवं॒ सद॑न ऋ॒तस्य॑ । ऋ॒तेन॑ पु॒त्रो अदि॑तेॠ॒तावो॒त त्रि॒धातु॑ प्रथय॒द्वि भूम॑

devanagari.text: मां नरः स्वश्वा वाजयंतो मां वृताः समरणे हवंते ।कृणोम्याजिं मघवाहमिंद्र इयर्मि रेणुमभिभूत्योजाः ॥

transliteration.text: mā́m ǀ náraḥ ǀ su-áśvāḥ ǀ vājáyantaḥ ǀ mā́m ǀ vṛtā́ḥ ǀ sam-áraṇe ǀ havante ǀkṛṇómi ǀ ājím ǀ maghá-vā ǀ ahám ǀ índraḥ ǀ íyarmi ǀ reṇúm ǀ abhíbhūti-ojāḥ ǁ

Sukta 42.translation: “Warriors well mounted, ardent for contest invoke me; selected (combatants invoke) me in battle; I, the affluentIndra, instrumental gate the conflict, and, endowed with victorious prowess, I raise up the dust (in the battle).”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मां नर॒: स्वश्वा॑ वा॒जय॑न्तो॒ मां वृ॒ताः स॒मर॑णे हवन्ते । कृ॒णोम्या॒जिं म॒घवा॒हमिन्द्र॒ इय॑र्मि रे॒णुम॒भिभू॑त्योजाः

devanagari.text: अहं ता विश्वा चकरं नकिर्मा दैव्यं सहो वरते अप्रतीतं ।यन्मा सोमासो ममदन्यदुक्थोभे भयेते रजसी अपारे ॥

Sukta 42.translation: “I have done all these (deeds); no one resists my divine, unsurpassed vigour; and when theSomajuices, when sacred songs, exhilarate me, then the unbounded heaven and earth are both alarmed.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒हं ता विश्वा॑ चकरं॒ नकि॑र्मा॒ दैव्यं॒ सहो॑ वरते॒ अप्र॑तीतम् । यन्मा॒ सोमा॑सो म॒मद॒न्यदु॒क्थोभे भ॑येते॒ रज॑सी अपा॒रे

devanagari.text: विदुष्टे विश्वा भुवनानि तस्य ता प्र ब्रवीषि वरुणाय वेधः ।त्वं वृत्राणि शृण्विषे जघन्वांत्वं वृताँ अरिणा इंद्र सिंधून् ॥

Sukta 42.translation: “All beings recognize you (Varuṇa), and your, worshipper, address these (encomiums) to Varuṇa; you,Indra, are renowned as slayingVṛtra; you have set the obstructed rivers free to flow.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि॒दुष्टे॒ विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि॒ तस्य॒ ता प्र ब्र॑वीषि॒ वरु॑णाय वेधः । त्वं वृ॒त्राणि॑ शृण्विषे जघ॒न्वान्त्वं वृ॒ताँ अ॑रिणा इन्द्र॒ सिन्धू॑न्

devanagari.text: अस्माकमत्र पितरस्त आसन्त्सप्त ऋषयो दौर्गहे बध्यमाने ।त आयजंत त्रसदस्युमस्या इंद्रं न वृत्रतुरमर्धदेवं ॥
अस्माकम् । अत्र । पितरः । ते । आसन् । सप्त । ऋषयः । दौःऽगहे । बध्यमाने ।ते । आ । अयजन्त । त्रसदस्युम् । अस्याः । इन्द्रम् । न । वृत्रऽतुरम् । अर्धऽदेवम् ॥

transliteration.text: asmā́kam ǀ átra ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ té ǀ āsan ǀ saptá ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ dauḥ-gahé ǀ badhyámāne ǀté ǀ ā́ ǀ ayajanta ǀ trasádasyum ǀ asyāḥ ǀ índram ǀ ná ǀ vṛtra-túram ǀ ardha-devám ǁ

Sukta 42.translation: “The seven ṛṣis were the protectors of this our (kingdom) when the son of Durgaha was in bonds; performing worship they obtained for (hisqueen) from the favour ofIndraandVaruṇa,Trasadasyu, like Indra the slayer of foes, dwelling near the gods.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्माक॒मत्र॑ पि॒तर॒स्त आ॑सन्त्स॒प्त ऋष॑यो दौर्ग॒हे ब॒ध्यमा॑ने । त आय॑जन्त त्र॒सद॑स्युमस्या॒ इन्द्रं॒ न वृ॑त्र॒तुर॑मर्धदे॒वम्

devanagari.text: पुरुकुत्सानी हि वामदाशद्धव्येभिरिंद्रावरुणा नमोभिः ।अथा राजानं त्रसदस्युमस्या वृत्रहणं ददथुरर्धदेवं ॥

transliteration.text: puru-kútsānī ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ ádāśat ǀ havyébhiḥ ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀátha ǀ rā́jānam ǀ trasádasyum ǀ asyāḥ ǀ vṛtra-hánam ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ ardha-devám ǁ

Sukta 42.translation: “The wife ofPurukutsapropitiated you two,IndraandVaruṇa, with oblations and prostrations, and therefore you gave her the kingTrasadasyu, the slayer of foes dwelling near the gods.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पु॒रु॒कुत्सा॑नी॒ हि वा॒मदा॑शद्ध॒व्येभि॑रिन्द्रावरुणा॒ नमो॑भिः । अथा॒ राजा॑नं त्र॒सद॑स्युमस्या वृत्र॒हणं॑ ददथुरर्धदे॒वम्

devanagari.text: राया वयं ससवांसो मदेम हव्येन देवा यवसेन गावः ।तां धेनुमिंद्रावरुणा युवं नो विश्वाहा धत्तमनपस्फुरंतीं ॥
राया । वयम् । ससऽवांसः । मदेम । हव्येन । देवाः । यवसेन । गावः ।ताम् । धेनुम् । इन्द्रावरुणा । युवम् । नः । विश्वाहा । धत्तम् । अनपऽस्फुरन्तीम् ॥

transliteration.text: rāyā́ ǀ vayám ǀ sasa-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ madema ǀ havyéna ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ yávasena ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀtā́m ǀ dhenúm ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ yuvám ǀ naḥ ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ dhattam ǀ ánapa-sphurantīm ǁ

Sukta 42.translation: “May we, glorifying you both, be delighted by riches; may the gods be plural ased by oblations, the cows by pasture; and do you,IndraandVaruṇa, daily grant us that same cow, (riches) free from any imperfection.”
Sukta 42.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रा॒या व॒यं स॑स॒वांसो॑ मदेम ह॒व्येन॑ दे॒वा यव॑सेन॒ गाव॑: । तां धे॒नुमि॑न्द्रावरुणा यु॒वं नो॑ वि॒श्वाहा॑ धत्त॒मन॑पस्फुरन्तीम्

devanagari.text: क उ श्रवत्कतमो यज्ञियानां वंदारु देवः कतमो जुषाते ।कस्येमां देवीममृतेषु प्रेष्ठां हृदि श्रेषाम सुष्टुतिं सुहव्यां ॥
कः । ऊं इति । श्रवत् । कतमः । यज्ञियानाम् । वन्दारु । देवः । कतमः । जुषाते ।कस्य । इमाम् । देवीम् । अमृतेषु । प्रेष्ठाम् । हृदि । श्रेषाम । सुऽस्तुतिम् । सुऽहव्याम् ॥

transliteration.text: káḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śravat ǀ katamáḥ ǀ yajñíyānām ǀ vandā́ru ǀ deváḥ ǀ katamáḥ ǀ juṣāte ǀkásya ǀ imā́m ǀ devī́m ǀ amṛ́teṣu ǀ préṣṭhām ǀ hṛdí ǀ śreṣāma ǀ su-stutím ǀ su-havyā́m ǁ

Sukta 43.translation: “Which of those who are entitled to sacrifice will listen (to our prayers)? which of the gods will hear our praise? which will be propitiated (by it)? upon the heart of whom among the immortals may we impress the devout affectionate adoration, accompanied by sacred oblations?”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: क उ॑ श्रवत्कत॒मो य॒ज्ञिया॑नां व॒न्दारु॑ दे॒वः क॑त॒मो जु॑षाते । कस्ये॒मां दे॒वीम॒मृते॑षु॒ प्रेष्ठां॑ हृ॒दि श्रे॑षाम सुष्टु॒तिं सु॑ह॒व्याम्

devanagari.text: को मृळाति कतम आगमिष्ठो देवानामु कतमः शंभविष्ठः ।रथं कमाहुर्द्रवदश्वमाशुं यं सूर्यस्य दुहितावृणीत ॥
कः । मृळाति । कतमः । आऽगमिष्ठः । देवानाम् । ऊं इति । कतमः । शम्ऽभविष्ठः ।रथम् । कम् । आहुः । द्रवत्ऽअश्वम् । आशुम् । यम् । सूर्यस्य । दुहिता । अवृणीत ॥

transliteration.text: káḥ ǀ mṛḷāti ǀ katamáḥ ǀ ā́-gamiṣṭhaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ katamáḥ ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhaḥ ǀrátham ǀ kám ǀ āhuḥ ǀ dravát-aśvam ǀ āśúm ǀ yám ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ duhitā́ ǀ ávṛṇīta ǁ

Sukta 43.translation: “Who will make us happy? which of the gods is the most prompt to come to our sacrifice? which is the most willing to grant us felicity? what chariot do they say is quick and drawn by rapid steeds? That which the daughter ofSūryaselected.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: को मृ॑ळाति कत॒म आग॑मिष्ठो दे॒वाना॑मु कत॒मः शम्भ॑विष्ठः । रथं॒ कमा॑हुर्द्र॒वद॑श्वमा॒शुं यं सूर्य॑स्य दुहि॒तावृ॑णीत

devanagari.text: मक्षू हि ष्मा गच्छथ ईवतो द्यूनिंद्रो न शक्तिं परितक्म्यायां ।दिव आजाता दिव्या सुपर्णा कया शचीनां भवथः शचिष्ठा ॥

transliteration.text: makṣú ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ ī́vataḥ ǀ dyū́n ǀ índraḥ ǀ ná ǀ śaktím ǀ pári-takmyāyām ǀdiváḥ ǀ ā́-jātā ǀ divyā́ ǀ su-parṇā́ ǀ káyā ǀ śácīnām ǀ bhavathaḥ ǀ śáciṣṭhā ǁ

Sukta 43.translation: “Moving, you proceed rapidly by day, asIndra, at the end of the night, (manifests his) power; descended from heaven, divine, of graceful motion, (Aśvins), by which of (your) acts are you most distinguished?”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒क्षू हि ष्मा॒ गच्छ॑थ॒ ईव॑तो॒ द्यूनिन्द्रो॒ न श॒क्तिं परि॑तक्म्यायाम् । दि॒व आजा॑ता दि॒व्या सु॑प॒र्णा कया॒ शची॑नां भवथ॒: शचि॑ष्ठा

devanagari.text: का वां भूदुपमातिः कया न आश्विना गमथो हूयमाना ।को वां महश्चित्त्यजसो अभीक उरुष्यतं माध्वी दस्रा न ऊती ॥

transliteration.text: kā́ ǀ vām ǀ bhūt ǀ úpa-mātiḥ ǀ káyā ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aśvinā ǀ gamathaḥ ǀ hūyámānā ǀkáḥ ǀ vām ǀ maháḥ ǀ cit ǀ tyájasaḥ ǀ abhī́ke ǀ uruṣyátam ǀ mādhvī íti ǀ dasrā ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ

Sukta 43.translation: “What may be the fit measure (of your merits)? invoked by what praises do you come to us? who (can exist as) the object of your great wrath?Dasras, dispensers of sweet (water), defend us with your protection.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: का वां॑ भू॒दुप॑माति॒: कया॑ न॒ आश्वि॑ना गमथो हू॒यमा॑ना । को वां॑ म॒हश्चि॒त्त्यज॑सो अ॒भीक॑ उरु॒ष्यतं॑ माध्वी दस्रा न ऊ॒ती

devanagari.text: उरु वां रथः परि नक्षति द्यामा यत्समुद्रादभि वर्तते वां ।मध्वा माध्वी मधु वां प्रुषायन्यत्सीं वां पृक्षो भुरजंत पक्वाः ॥

Sukta 43.translation: “Your chariot travels widely round the heaven until it plural ces you beyond the firmament; dispensers of sweet (water, the priests) are diluting theSomajuice with milk, that the boiled (barley) may be united with the libation offered to you.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒रु वां॒ रथ॒: परि॑ नक्षति॒ द्यामा यत्स॑मु॒द्राद॒भि वर्त॑ते वाम् । मध्वा॑ माध्वी॒ मधु॑ वां प्रुषाय॒न्यत्सीं॑ वां॒ पृक्षो॑ भु॒रज॑न्त प॒क्वाः

devanagari.text: सिंधुर्ह वां रसया सिंचदश्वान्घृणा वयोऽरुषासः परि ग्मन् ।तदू षु वामजिरं चेति यानं येन पती भवथः सूर्यायाः ॥

transliteration.text: síndhuḥ ǀ ha ǀ vām ǀ rasáyā ǀ siñcat ǀ áśvān ǀ ghṛṇā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ aruṣā́saḥ ǀ pári ǀ gman ǀtát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ vām ǀ ajirám ǀ ceti ǀ yā́nam ǀ yéna ǀ pátī íti ǀ bhávathaḥ ǀ sūryā́yāḥ ǁ

Sukta 43.translation: “The flowing (stream) has sprinkled your steeds with moisture; the radiant horses (like) birds (in swiftness) pass on, bright with lustre; well known as that quick-moving chariot, whereby you became the lords ofSūrya.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सिन्धु॑र्ह वां र॒सया॑ सिञ्च॒दश्वा॑न्घृ॒णा वयो॑ऽरु॒षास॒: परि॑ ग्मन् । तदू॒ षु वा॑मजि॒रं चे॑ति॒ यानं॒ येन॒ पती॒ भव॑थः सू॒र्याया॑:

devanagari.text: इहेह यद्वां समना पपृक्षे सेयमस्मे सुमतिर्वाजरत्ना ।उरुष्यतं जरितारं युवं ह श्रितः कामो नासत्या युवद्रिक् ॥

transliteration.text: ihá-iha ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ samanā́ ǀ papṛkṣé ǀ sā́ ǀ iyám ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ vāja-ratnā ǀuruṣyátam ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ yuvám ǀ ha ǀ śritáḥ ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ yuvadrík ǁ

Sukta 43.translation: “May the earnest praise, distributors of food, wherewith I associate you both like-minded at this sacrifice, be (beneficial) to us; do you protect your worshipper; my desire,Nāsatyas, directed towards you is gratified.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒हेह॒ यद्वां॑ सम॒ना प॑पृ॒क्षे सेयम॒स्मे सु॑म॒तिर्वा॑जरत्ना । उ॒रु॒ष्यतं॑ जरि॒तारं॑ यु॒वं ह॑ श्रि॒तः कामो॑ नासत्या युव॒द्रिक्

devanagari.text: तं वां रथं वयमद्या हुवेम पृथुज्रयमश्विना संगतिं गोः ।यः सूर्यां वहति वंधुरायुर्गिर्वाहसं पुरुतमं वसूयुं ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ vām ǀ rátham ǀ vayám ǀ adyá ǀ huvema ǀ pṛthu-jráyam ǀ aśvinā ǀ sám-gatim ǀ góḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ sūryā́m ǀ váhati ǀ vandhura-yúḥ ǀ gírvāhasam ǀ puru-támam ǀ vasu-yúm ǁ

Sukta 44.translation: “We invoke,Aśvins, today, your rapid car, the associator of the solar ray; the banked car which bearsSūrya, vast, wealthy, and laden with praises.”
