transliteration.text: índrāviṣṇū íti ǀ havíṣā ǀ vavṛdhānā́ ǀ ágra-advānā ǀ námasā ǀ rāta-havyā ǀghṛ́tāsutī íti ghṛ́ta-āsutī ǀ dráviṇam ǀ dhattam ǀ asmé íti ǀ samudráḥ ǀ sthaḥ ǀ kaláśaḥ ǀ soma-dhā́naḥ ǁ

Sukta 69.translation: “IndraandViṣṇu, feeders upon clarified butter, drinkers of he fermentedSoma, thriving upon oblations, accepting them offered with reverence, bestow upon us wealth; for you are an ocean, a pitcher, the receptacle of the libation.”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑विष्णू ह॒विषा॑ वावृधा॒नाग्रा॑द्वाना॒ नम॑सा रातहव्या । घृता॑सुती॒ द्रवि॑णं धत्तम॒स्मे स॑मु॒द्रः स्थ॑: क॒लश॑: सोम॒धान॑:

devanagari.text: इंद्राविष्णू पिबतं मध्वो अस्य सोमस्य दस्रा जठरं पृणेथां ।आ वामंधांसि मदिराण्यग्मन्नुप ब्रह्माणि शृणुतं हवं मे ॥
इन्द्राविष्णू इति । पिबतम् । मध्वः । अस्य । सोमस्य । दस्रा । जठरम् । पृणेथाम् ।आ । वाम् । अन्धांसि । मदिराणि । अग्मन् । उप । ब्रह्माणि । शृणुतम् । हवम् । मे ॥

transliteration.text: índrāviṣṇū íti ǀ píbatam ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ asyá ǀ sómasya ǀ dasrā ǀ jaṭháram ǀ pṛṇethām ǀā́ ǀ vām ǀ ándhāṃsi ǀ madirā́ṇi ǀ agman ǀ úpa ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ hávam ǀ me ǁ

Sukta 69.translation: “IndraandViṣṇu, agreeable of aspect, drink of this sweetSoma; fill with it your bellies; may the inebriating Soma reach you; hear my prayers, my invocation.”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑विष्णू॒ पिब॑तं॒ मध्वो॑ अ॒स्य सोम॑स्य दस्रा ज॒ठरं॑ पृणेथाम् । आ वा॒मन्धां॑सि मदि॒राण्य॑ग्म॒न्नुप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि शृणुतं॒ हवं॑ मे

devanagari.text: उभा जिग्यथुर्न परा जयेथे न परा जिग्ये कतरश्चनैनोः ।इंद्रश्च विष्णो यदपस्पृधेथां त्रेधा सहस्रं वि तदैरयेथां ॥
उभा । जिग्यथुः । न । परा । जयेथे इति । न । परा । जिग्ये । कतरः । चन । एनोः ।इन्द्रः । च । विष्णो इति । यत् । अपस्पृधेथाम् । त्रेधा । सहस्रम् । वि । तत् । ऐरयेथाम् ॥

transliteration.text: ubhā́ ǀ jigyathuḥ ǀ ná ǀ párā ǀ jayethe íti ǀ ná ǀ párā ǀ jigye ǀ kataráḥ ǀ caná ǀ enoḥ ǀíndraḥ ǀ ca ǀ viṣṇo íti ǀ yát ǀ ápaspṛdhethām ǀ tredhā́ ǀ sahásram ǀ ví ǀ tát ǀ airayethām ǁ

Sukta 69.translation: “You have both (ever) been victorious; never have been conquered; neither of you two has been vanquished; with whomsoever you have contended you have thrice conquered thousands.”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒भा जि॑ग्यथु॒र्न परा॑ जयेथे॒ न परा॑ जिग्ये कत॒रश्च॒नैनो॑: । इन्द्र॑श्च विष्णो॒ यदप॑स्पृधेथां त्रे॒धा स॒हस्रं॒ वि तदै॑रयेथाम्

devanagari.text: घृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियोर्वी पृथ्वी मधुदुघे सुपेशसा ।द्यावापृथिवी वरुणस्य धर्मणा विष्कभिते अजरे भूरिरेतसा ॥
घृतवती इति घृतऽवती । भुवनानाम् । अभिऽश्रिया । उर्वी इति । पृथ्वी इति । मधुदुघे इति मधुऽदुघे । सुऽपेशसा ।द्यावापृथिवी इति । वरुणस्य । धर्मणा । विस्कभिते इति विऽस्कभिते । अजरे इति । भूरिऽरेतसा ॥

transliteration.text: ghṛtávatī íti ghṛtá-vatī ǀ bhúvanānām ǀ abhi-śríyā ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ pṛthvī́ íti ǀ madhudúghe íti madhu-dúghe ǀ su-péśasā ǀdyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhármaṇā ǀ vískabhite íti ví-skabhite ǀ ajáre íti ǀ bhū́ri-retasā ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “Radiant Heaven and Earth, the asylum of created beings, you are spacious, manifold, water-yielding, lovely, separately fixed by the functions ofVaruṇa, undecaying, many-germed.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: घृ॒तव॑ती॒ भुव॑नानामभि॒श्रियो॒र्वी पृ॒थ्वी म॑धु॒दुघे॑ सु॒पेश॑सा । द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी वरु॑णस्य॒ धर्म॑णा॒ विष्क॑भिते अ॒जरे॒ भूरि॑रेतसा

devanagari.text: असश्चंती भूरिधारे पयस्वती घृतं दुहाते सुकृते शुचिव्रते ।राजंती अस्य भुवनस्य रोदसी अस्मे रेतः सिंचतं यन्मनुर्हितं ॥

असश्चन्ती इति । भूरिधारे इति भूरिऽधारे । पयस्वती इति । घृतम् । दुहाते इति । सुऽकृते । शुचिव्रते इति शुचिऽव्रते ।राजन्ती इति । अस्य । भुवनस्य । रोदसी इति । अस्मे इति । रेतः । सिञ्चतम् । यत् । मनुःऽहितम् ॥

transliteration.text: ásaścantī íti ǀ bhū́ridhāre íti bhū́ri-dhāre ǀ páyasvatī íti ǀ ghṛtám ǀ duhāte íti ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ śúcivrate íti śúci-vrate ǀrā́jantī íti ǀ asyá ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ rodasī íti ǀ asmé íti ǀ rétaḥ ǀ siñcatam ǀ yát ǀ mánuḥ-hitam ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “Uncollapsing, many-showering, water retaining, yielding moisture, beneficent, pure in act; do you two, Heaven and Earth, rulers over created beings, grant us vigour, that may be favourable to (the increase of) mankind.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अस॑श्चन्ती॒ भूरि॑धारे॒ पय॑स्वती घृ॒तं दु॑हाते सु॒कृते॒ शुचि॑व्रते । राज॑न्ती अ॒स्य भुव॑नस्य रोदसी अ॒स्मे रेत॑: सिञ्चतं॒ यन्मनु॑र्हितम्

devanagari.text: यो वामृजवे क्रमणाय रोदसी मर्तो ददाश धिषणे स साधति ।प्र प्रजाभिर्जायते धर्मणस्परि युवोः सिक्ता विषुरूपाणि सव्रता ॥
यः । वाम् । ऋजवे । क्रमणाय । रोदसी इति । मर्तः । ददाश । धिषणे इति । सः । साधति ।प्र । प्रऽजाभिः । जायते । धर्मणः । परि । युवोः । सिक्ता । विषुऽरूपाणि । सऽव्रता ॥

transliteration.text: yáḥ ǀ vām ǀ ṛjáve ǀ krámaṇāya ǀ rodasī íti ǀ mártaḥ ǀ dadā́śa ǀ dhiṣaṇe íti ǀ sáḥ ǀ sādhati ǀprá ǀ pra-jā́bhiḥ ǀ jāyate ǀ dhármaṇaḥ ǀ pári ǀ yuvóḥ ǀ siktā́ ǀ víṣu-rūpāṇi ǀ sá-vratā ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “Firm-set Heaven and Earth, the mortal who has offered (oblations) for your straight-forward course, accomplishes (his objects), he prospers with progeny, and invigorated by your operation, many beings of various forms, but similar functions, are engendeed.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यो वा॑मृ॒जवे॒ क्रम॑णाय रोदसी॒ मर्तो॑ द॒दाश॑ धिषणे॒ स सा॑धति । प्र प्र॒जाभि॑र्जायते॒ धर्म॑ण॒स्परि॑ यु॒वोः सि॒क्ता विषु॑रूपाणि॒ सव्र॑ता

devanagari.text: घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी अभीवृते घृतश्रिया घृतपृचा घृतावृधा ।उर्वी पृथ्वी होतृवूर्ये पुरोहिते ते इद्विप्रा ईळते सुम्नमिष्टये ॥
घृतेन । द्यावापृथिवी इति । अभीवृते इत्यभिऽवृते । घृतऽश्रिया । घृतऽपृचा । घृतऽवृधा ।उर्वी इति । पृथ्वी इति । होतृऽवूर्ये । पुरोहिते इति पुरःऽहिते । ते इति । इत् । विप्राः । ईळते । सुम्नम् । इष्टये ॥

transliteration.text: ghṛténa ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ abhī́vṛte ítyabhí-vṛte ǀ ghṛta-śríyā ǀ ghṛta-pṛ́cā ǀ ghṛta-vṛ́dhā ǀurvī́ íti ǀ pṛthvī́ íti ǀ hotṛ-vū́rye ǀ puróhite íti puráḥ-hite ǀ té íti ǀ ít ǀ víprāḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ sumnám ǀ iṣṭáye ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “You are surrounded, Heaven and Earth, by water; you are the asylum of water; imbued with water; the augmenters of water; vast and manifold; you are first propitiated in the sacrifice; the pious pray to you for happiness, that the sacrifice (may be celebrated).”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: घृ॒तेन॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अ॒भीवृ॑ते घृत॒श्रिया॑ घृत॒पृचा॑ घृता॒वृधा॑ । उ॒र्वी पृ॒थ्वी हो॑तृ॒वूर्ये॑ पु॒रोहि॑ते॒ ते इद्विप्रा॑ ईळते सु॒म्नमि॒ष्टये॑

devanagari.text: मधु नो द्यावापृथिवी मिमिक्षतां मधुश्चुता मधुदुघे मधुव्रते ।दधाने यज्ञं द्रविणं च देवता महि श्रवो वाजमस्मे सुवीर्यं ॥
मधु । नः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । मिमिक्षताम् । मधुऽश्चुता । मधुदुघे इति मधुऽदुघे । मधुव्रते इति मधुऽव्रते ।दधाने इति । यज्ञम् । द्रविणम् । च । देवता । महि । श्रवः । वाजम् । अस्मे इति । सुऽवीर्यम् ॥

transliteration.text: mádhu ǀ naḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ mimikṣatām ǀ madhu-ścútā ǀ madhudúghe íti madhu-dúghe ǀ mádhuvrate íti mádhu-vrate ǀdádhāne íti ǀ yajñám ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ca ǀ devátā ǀ máhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-vī́ryam ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “May Heaven and Earth, the effusers of water, the milkers of water, dischargers of the functions of water, divinities, the promoters of sacrifice, the bestowers of wealth, of renown, of food, ofmaleposterity, combine together.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मधु॑ नो॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी मि॑मिक्षतां मधु॒श्चुता॑ मधु॒दुघे॒ मधु॑व्रते । दधा॑ने य॒ज्ञं द्रवि॑णं च दे॒वता॒ महि॒ श्रवो॒ वाज॑म॒स्मे सु॒वीर्य॑म्

devanagari.text: ऊर्जं नो द्यौश्च पृथिवी च पिन्वतां पिता माता विश्वविदा सुदंससा ।संरराणे रोदसी विश्वशंभुवा सनिं वाजं रयिमस्मे समिन्वतां ॥
ऊर्जम् । नः । द्यौः । च । पृथिवी । च । पिन्वताम् । पिता । माता । विश्वऽविदा । सुऽदंससा ।संरराणे इति सम्ऽरराणे । रोदसी इति । विश्वऽशम्भुवा । सनिम् । वाजम् । रयिम् । अस्मे इति । सम् । इन्वताम् ॥

transliteration.text: ū́rjam ǀ naḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ca ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ ca ǀ pinvatām ǀ pitā́ ǀ mātā́ ǀ viśva-vídā ǀ su-dáṃsasā ǀsaṃrarāṇé íti sam-rarāṇé ǀ ródasī íti ǀ viśvá-śambhuvā ǀ saním ǀ vā́jam ǀ rayím ǀ asmé íti ǀ sám ǀ invatām ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “May father Heaven, may mother Earth, who are all-knowing, and doers of good deeds, grant us sustenance; may Heaven and Earth, mutually co-operating and promoting the happiness of all, bestow upon us posterity, food, and riches.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऊर्जं॑ नो॒ द्यौश्च॑ पृथि॒वी च॑ पिन्वतां पि॒ता मा॒ता वि॑श्व॒विदा॑ सु॒दंस॑सा । सं॒र॒रा॒णे रोद॑सी वि॒श्वश॑म्भुवा स॒निं वाजं॑ र॒यिम॒स्मे समि॑न्वताम्

Sukta 71.translation: “The divine and benevolentSavitāputs forth his golden arms for (making) donations; the adorable, youthful, sagacious (deity), stretches out hishands, filled with water, in the various services of the world.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उदु॒ ष्य दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता हि॑र॒ण्यया॑ बा॒हू अ॑यंस्त॒ सव॑नाय सु॒क्रतु॑: । घृ॒तेन॑ पा॒णी अ॒भि प्रु॑ष्णुते म॒खो युवा॑ सु॒दक्षो॒ रज॑सो॒ विध॑र्मणि

Sukta 71.translation: “May we be among the progeny of the divineSavitā, and (have power) to offer him most excellent donations; for you are he who (are absolute) in the procreation and perpetuation of many (living beings), bipeds and quadrupeds.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दे॒वस्य॑ व॒यं स॑वि॒तुः सवी॑मनि॒ श्रेष्ठे॑ स्याम॒ वसु॑नश्च दा॒वने॑ । यो विश्व॑स्य द्वि॒पदो॒ यश्चतु॑ष्पदो नि॒वेश॑ने प्रस॒वे चासि॒ भूम॑नः

Sukta 71.translation: “Do you,Savitā, posper today our dwelling with uninjurable protections, confirming happiness; do you, who are golden-tongued, (be vigilant) for our present prosperity; protect us; let not any calumniator have power (to harm) us.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अद॑ब्धेभिः सवितः पा॒युभि॒ष्ट्वं शि॒वेभि॑र॒द्य परि॑ पाहि नो॒ गय॑म् । हिर॑ण्यजिह्वः सुवि॒ताय॒ नव्य॑से॒ रक्षा॒ माकि॑र्नो अ॒घशं॑स ईशत

Sukta 71.translation: “May the divine, munificent, golden-handed, golden-jawed, adorable, sweet-spokenSavitā, rise regularly at the close of night; when he besows abundant and desirable (food) upon the donor of the oblation.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उदु॒ ष्य दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता दमू॑ना॒ हिर॑ण्यपाणिः प्रतिदो॒षम॑स्थात् । अयो॑हनुर्यज॒तो म॒न्द्रजि॑ह्व॒ आ दा॒शुषे॑ सुवति॒ भूरि॑ वा॒मम्

Sukta 71.translation: “MaySavitāput forth like an orator his golden well-formed arms; (he who), from the ends of the earth, ascends to the summit of the sky, and, moving along, delights every thing that is.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उदू॑ अयाँ उपव॒क्तेव॑ बा॒हू हि॑र॒ण्यया॑ सवि॒ता सु॒प्रती॑का । दि॒वो रोहां॑स्यरुहत्पृथि॒व्या अरी॑रमत्प॒तय॒त्कच्चि॒दभ्व॑म्

Sukta 71.translation: “Beget for us,Savitā, wealth today, wealth tomorrow, wealth day by day; you are the giver of ample wealth, of a (spacious) mansion; may we, by this praise, become partakers of wealth.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वा॒मम॒द्य स॑वितर्वा॒ममु॒ श्वो दि॒वेदि॑वे वा॒मम॒स्मभ्यं॑ सावीः । वा॒मस्य॒ हि क्षय॑स्य देव॒ भूरे॑र॒या धि॒या वा॑म॒भाज॑: स्याम

Sukta 72.translation: “Great,IndraandSoma, is that your greatness, for you have made great and principal (beings); you have made known (to men)Sūryaand the waters; you have dissipated the glooms and (desroyed) the revilers.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑सोमा॒ महि॒ तद्वां॑ महि॒त्वं यु॒वं म॒हानि॑ प्रथ॒मानि॑ चक्रथुः । यु॒वं सूर्यं॑ विवि॒दथु॑र्यु॒वं स्व१॒॑र्विश्वा॒ तमां॑स्यहतं नि॒दश्च॑

Sukta 72.translation: “IndraandSoma, you have led on the dawns; you have upraised the sun with his splendour, you have propped up the sky with he supporting pillar (of the firmament); you have spread out the earth, the mother (of all).”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑सोमा वा॒सय॑थ उ॒षास॒मुत्सूर्यं॑ नयथो॒ ज्योति॑षा स॒ह । उप॒ द्यां स्क॒म्भथु॒: स्कम्भ॑ने॒नाप्र॑थतं पृथि॒वीं मा॒तरं॒ वि

Sukta 72.translation: “IndraandSoma, you slew Ahi andVṛtra; the obstructer of the water; for which the heaven venerates you both; you have urged on the waters of the rivers until they have replenished numerous oceans.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑सोमा॒वहि॑म॒पः प॑रि॒ष्ठां ह॒थो वृ॒त्रमनु॑ वां॒ द्यौर॑मन्यत । प्रार्णां॑स्यैरयतं न॒दीना॒मा स॑मु॒द्राणि॑ पप्रथुः पु॒रूणि॑

Sukta 72.translation: “IndraandSoma, you have deposited the mature (milk) in the immature udders of the kine; you have retained the white (secretion), although notshutup within those may-coloured cattle.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑सोमा प॒क्वमा॒मास्व॒न्तर्नि गवा॒मिद्द॑धथुर्व॒क्षणा॑सु । ज॒गृ॒भथु॒रन॑पिनद्धमासु॒ रुश॑च्चि॒त्रासु॒ जग॑तीष्व॒न्तः

Sukta 72.translation: “IndraandSoma, do you promptly bestow upon us preservative, renowned (riches), accompanied by offspring; for you, fierce (divinities), have disseminated among men, strength, useful to man, victorious over hostile acts.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑सोमा यु॒वम॒ङ्ग तरु॑त्रमपत्य॒साचं॒ श्रुत्यं॑ रराथे । यु॒वं शुष्मं॒ नर्यं॑ चर्ष॒णिभ्य॒: सं वि॑व्यथुः पृतना॒षाह॑मुग्रा

Sukta 73.translation: “Bṛhaspati, who is the breaker of the mountain, the first-born (ofPrajāpati), the observer of truth, the descendant ofAṅgirasa, the partaker of the oblation, the traverser of two worlds, abiding in the region of light, is to us a father; he, the showerer, hunders and in heaven and earth.”

Sukta 74.translation: “SomaandRudra, confirm (in us the strength) ofasurasmay sacrifices in every dwelling adequately reach you; do you, possessors of the seven precious things, besow happiness upon us; happiness upon our bipeds and quadrupeds.”

Sukta 74.translation: “SomaandRudra, expel the widespread sickness that has entered into our dwellings; keep offNirṛti, so that she may be far away, and may prosperous means of sustenance be ours.”

devanagari.text: बह्वीनां पिता बहुरस्य पुत्रश्चिश्चा कृणोति समनावगत्य ।इषुधिः संकाः पृतनाश्च सर्वाः पृष्ठे निनद्धो जयति प्रसूतः ॥

transliteration.text: bahvīnā́m ǀ pitā́ ǀ bahúḥ ǀ asyá ǀ putráḥ ǀ ciścā́ ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ sámanā ǀ ava-gátya ǀiṣu-dhíḥ ǀ sáṅkāḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ ca ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ pṛṣṭhé ǀ ní-naddhaḥ ǀ jayati ǀ prá-sūtaḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The quiver, the parent of many, of whom many are the sons, clangs as it enters into the battle; slung at the back (of the warrior), prolific (of its shafts), it overcomes all shouting hosts.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ब॒ह्वी॒नां पि॒ता ब॒हुर॑स्य पु॒त्रश्चि॒श्चा कृ॑णोति॒ सम॑नाव॒गत्य॑ । इ॒षु॒धिः सङ्का॒: पृत॑नाश्च॒ सर्वा॑: पृ॒ष्ठे निन॑द्धो जयति॒ प्रसू॑तः

devanagari.text: रथे तिष्ठन्नयति वाजिनः पुरो यत्रयत्र कामयते सुषारथिः ।अभीशूनां महिमानं पनायत मनः पश्चादनु यच्छंति रश्मयः ॥
रथे । तिष्ठन् । नयति । वाजिनः । पुरः । यत्रऽयत्र । कामयते । सुऽसारथिः ।अभीशूनाम् । महिमानम् । पनायत । मनः । पश्चात् । अनु । यच्छन्ति । रश्मयः ॥

transliteration.text: ráthe ǀ tíṣṭhan ǀ nayati ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ yátra-yatra ǀ kāmáyate ǀ su-sārathíḥ ǀabhī́śūnām ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ panāyata ǀ mánaḥ ǀ paścā́t ǀ ánu ǀ yacchanti ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The skilful charioteer, standing in the car, derives his horses before him whatsoever he will; praise the efficacy of the reins, for the reins from the back (of the car compel the steeds) to follow the intention (of the driver).”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रथे॒ तिष्ठ॑न्नयति वा॒जिन॑: पु॒रो यत्र॑यत्र का॒मय॑ते सुषार॒थिः । अ॒भीशू॑नां महि॒मानं॑ पनायत॒ मन॑: प॒श्चादनु॑ यच्छन्ति र॒श्मय॑:

devanagari.text: तीव्रान्घोषान्कृण्वते वृषपाणयोऽश्वा रथेभिः सह वाजयंतः ।अवक्रामंतः प्रपदैरमित्रान् क्षिणंति शत्रूँरनपव्ययंतः ॥
तीव्रान् । घोषान् । कृण्वते । वृषऽपाणयः । अश्वाः । रथेभिः । सह । वाजयन्तः ।अवऽक्रामन्तः । प्रऽपदैः । अमित्रान् । क्षिणन्ति । शत्रून् । अनपऽव्ययन्तः ॥

transliteration.text: tīvrā́n ǀ ghóṣān ǀ kṛṇvate ǀ vṛ́ṣa-pāṇayaḥ ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ ráthebhiḥ ǀ sahá ǀ vājáyantaḥ ǀava-krā́mantaḥ ǀ prá-padaiḥ ǀ amítrān ǀ kṣiṇánti ǀ śátrūn ǀ ánapa-vyayantaḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The horses raising the dust with their hoofs, rushing on with the chariots, utter loud neighings, retreating not (from the charge), but trampling with their fore feet upon the enemies, they destroy them.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ती॒व्रान्घोषा॑न्कृण्वते॒ वृष॑पाण॒योऽश्वा॒ रथे॑भिः स॒ह वा॒जय॑न्तः । अ॒व॒क्राम॑न्त॒: प्रप॑दैर॒मित्रा॑न्क्षि॒णन्ति॒ शत्रूँ॒रन॑पव्ययन्तः

devanagari.text: रथवाहनं हविरस्य नाम यत्रायुधं निहितमस्य वर्म ।तत्रा रथमुप शग्मं सदेम विश्वाहा वयं सुमनस्यमानाः ॥
रथऽवाहनम् । हविः । अस्य । नाम । यत्र । आयुधम् । निऽहितम् । अस्य । वर्म ।तत्र । रथम् । उप । शग्मम् । सदेम । विश्वाहा । वयम् । सुऽमनस्यमानाः ॥

transliteration.text: ratha-vā́hanam ǀ havíḥ ǀ asya ǀ nā́ma ǀ yátra ǀ ā́yudham ǀ ní-hitam ǀ asya ǀ várma ǀtátra ǀ rátham ǀ úpa ǀ śagmám ǀ sadema ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ vayám ǀ su-manasyámānāḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The spoil borne off in his car, in which his weapons and armour are deposited, is the appropriate oblation of the warrior; therefore let us, exulting, daily do honour to the joy-bestowing car.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: र॒थ॒वाह॑नं ह॒विर॑स्य॒ नाम॒ यत्रायु॑धं॒ निहि॑तमस्य॒ वर्म॑ । तत्रा॒ रथ॒मुप॑ श॒ग्मं स॑देम वि॒श्वाहा॑ व॒यं सु॑मन॒स्यमा॑नाः

devanagari.text: स्वादुषंसदः पितरो वयोधाः कृच्छ्रेश्रितः शक्तीवंतो गभीराः ।चित्रसेना इषुबला अमृध्राः सतोवीरा उरवो व्रातसाहाः ॥
स्वादुऽसंसदः । पितरः । वयःऽधाः । कृच्छ्रेऽश्रितः । शक्तिऽवन्तः । गभीराः ।चित्रऽसेनाः । इषुऽबलाः । अमृध्राः । सतःऽवीराः । उरवः । व्रातऽसहाः ॥

transliteration.text: svādu-saṃsádaḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ vayaḥ-dhā́ḥ ǀ kṛcchre-śrítaḥ ǀ śákti-vantaḥ ǀ gabhīrā́ḥ ǀcitrá-senāḥ ǀ íṣu-balāḥ ǀ ámṛdhrāḥ ǀ satáḥ-vīrāḥ ǀ urávaḥ ǀ vrāta-sahā́ḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The guards (of chariot), revelling in the savoury (spoil), distributors of food, protecors in calamity, armed with spears, resolute, beautifully arranged, strong in arrows, invincible, of heroic valour, robust, and conquerors of numerous hosts.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्वा॒दु॒षं॒सद॑: पि॒तरो॑ वयो॒धाः कृ॑च्छ्रे॒श्रित॒: शक्ती॑वन्तो गभी॒राः । चि॒त्रसे॑ना॒ इषु॑बला॒ अमृ॑ध्राः स॒तोवी॑रा उ॒रवो॑ व्रातसा॒हाः

devanagari.text: ब्राह्मणासः पितरः सोम्यासः शिवे नो द्यावापृथिवी अनेहसा ।पूषा नः पातु दुरितादृतावृधो रक्षा माकिर्नो अघशंस ईशत ॥
ब्राह्मणासः । पितरः । सोम्यासः । शिवे इति । नः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । अनेहसा ।पूषा । नः । पातु । दुःऽइतात् । ऋतऽवृधः । रक्ष । माकिः । नः । अघऽशंसः । ईशत ॥

transliteration.text: brā́hmaṇāsaḥ ǀ pítaraḥ ǀ sómyāsaḥ ǀ śivé íti ǀ naḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ anehásā ǀpūṣā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pātu ǀ duḥ-itā́t ǀ ṛta-vṛdhaḥ ǀ rákṣa ǀ mā́kiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ aghá-śaṃsaḥ ǀ īśata ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “May thebrāhmaṇas, the progenitors presenters of theSoma, the observers of truth, protect us; may the faultless heaven and earth be propitious to us; mayPūṣanpreserve us from misfortune, let no calumniator prevail over us.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ब्राह्म॑णास॒: पित॑र॒: सोम्या॑सः शि॒वे नो॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अ॑ने॒हसा॑ । पू॒षा न॑: पातु दुरि॒तादृ॑तावृधो॒ रक्षा॒ माकि॑र्नो अ॒घशं॑स ईशत

devanagari.text: सुपर्णं वस्ते मृगो अस्या दंतो गोभिः संनद्धा पतति प्रसूता ।यत्रा नरः सं च वि च द्रवंति तत्रास्मभ्यमिषवः शर्म यंसन् ॥
सुऽपर्णम् । वस्ते । मृगः । अस्याः । दन्तः । गोभिः । सम्ऽनद्धा । पतति । प्रऽसूता ।यत्र । नरः । सम् । च । वि । च । द्रवन्ति । तत्र । अस्मभ्यम् । इषवः । शर्म । यंसन् ॥

transliteration.text: su-parṇám ǀ vaste ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ dántaḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ sám-naddhā ǀ patati ǀ prá-sūtā ǀyátra ǀ náraḥ ǀ sám ǀ ca ǀ ví ǀ ca ǀ drávanti ǀ tátra ǀ asmábhyam ǀ íṣavaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsan ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The arrow puts on a (feathery) wing; the (horn of the) deer is its point; it is bound with the sinews of the cow; it alights where directed; whenever men assemble or disperse, there may the shafts fall for an advantage.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सु॒प॒र्णं व॑स्ते मृ॒गो अ॑स्या॒ दन्तो॒ गोभि॒: संन॑द्धा पतति॒ प्रसू॑ता । यत्रा॒ नर॒: सं च॒ वि च॒ द्रव॑न्ति॒ तत्रा॒स्मभ्य॒मिष॑व॒: शर्म॑ यंसन्

devanagari.text: ऋजीते परि वृङ्धि नोऽश्मा भवतु नस्तनूः ।सोमो अधि ब्रवीतु नोऽदितिः शर्म यच्छतु ॥
ऋजीते । परि । वृङ्धि । नः । अश्मा । भवतु । नः । तनूः ।सोमः । अधि । ब्रवीतु । नः । अदितिः । शर्म । यच्छतु ॥

transliteration.text: ṛ́jīte ǀ pári ǀ vṛṅdhi ǀ naḥ ǀ áśmā ǀ bhavatu ǀ naḥ ǀ tanū́ḥ ǀsómaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ bravītu ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatu ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “Straight-flying (arrow), defend us; may our bodies be stone; maySomaspeak to us encouragement; mayAditigrant us success.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋजी॑ते॒ परि॑ वृङ्धि॒ नोऽश्मा॑ भवतु नस्त॒नूः । सोमो॒ अधि॑ ब्रवीतु॒ नोऽदि॑ति॒: शर्म॑ यच्छतु

devanagari.text: आ जंघंति सान्वेषां जघनाँ उप जिघ्नते ।अश्वाजनि प्रचेतसोऽश्वान्त्समत्सु चोदय ॥
आ । जङ्घन्ति । सानु । एषाम् । जघनान् । उप । जिघ्नते ।अश्वऽअजनि । प्रऽचेतसः । अश्वान् । समत्ऽसु । चोदय ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ jaṅghanti ǀ sā́nu ǀ eṣām ǀ jaghánān ǀ úpa ǀ jighnate ǀáśva-ajani ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ áśvān ǀ samát-su ǀ codaya ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “Whip, with which the skilful (charioteers) last their thighs and scourge their flanks, urge the horses in battles.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ ज॑ङ्घन्ति॒ सान्वे॑षां ज॒घनाँ॒ उप॑ जिघ्नते । अश्वा॑जनि॒ प्रचे॑त॒सोऽश्वा॑न्त्स॒मत्सु॑ चोदय

devanagari.text: अहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुं ज्याया हेतिं परिबाधमानः ।हस्तघ्नो विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान्पुमान्पुमांसं परि पातु विश्वतः ॥
अहिःऽइव । भोगैः । परि । एति । बाहुम् । ज्यायाः । हेतिम् । परिऽबाधमानः ।हस्तऽघ्नः । विश्वा । वयुनानि । विद्वान् । पुमान् । पुमांसम् । परि । पातु । विश्वतः ॥

transliteration.text: áhiḥ-iva ǀ bhogáiḥ ǀ pári ǀ eti ǀ bāhúm ǀ jyā́yāḥ ǀ hetím ǀ pari-bā́dhamānaḥ ǀhasta-ghnáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ vayúnāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ púmān ǀ púmāṃsam ǀ pári ǀ pātu ǀ viśvátaḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The ward of the fore-arm protecting it from the abrasion of the bow-string, surrounds the arm like a snake with its convulutions; may the brave man, experienced in the arts of war, defend a combatant on every side.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अहि॑रिव भो॒गैः पर्ये॑ति बा॒हुं ज्याया॑ हे॒तिं प॑रि॒बाध॑मानः । ह॒स्त॒घ्नो विश्वा॑ व॒युना॑नि वि॒द्वान्पुमा॒न्पुमां॑सं॒ परि॑ पातु वि॒श्वत॑:

devanagari.text: आलाक्ता या रुरुशीर्ष्ण्यथो यस्या अयो मुखं ।इदं पर्जन्यरेतस इष्वै देव्यै बृहन्नमः ॥
आलऽअक्ता । या । रुरुऽशीर्ष्णी । अथो इति । यस्याः । अयः । मुखम् ।इदम् । पर्जन्यऽरेतसे । इष्वै । देव्यै । बृहत् । नमः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́la-aktā ǀ yā́ ǀ rúru-śīrṣṇī ǀ átho íti ǀ yásyāḥ ǀ áyaḥ ǀ múkham ǀidám ǀ parjánya-retase ǀ íṣvai ǀ devyái ǀ bṛhát ǀ námaḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “This praise (be offered) to the large celestial arrow, the growth ofParjanya, whose point is anointed with venom, whose blade is iron.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आला॑क्ता॒ या रुरु॑शी॒र्ष्ण्यथो॒ यस्या॒ अयो॒ मुख॑म् । इ॒दं प॒र्जन्य॑रेतस॒ इष्वै॑ दे॒व्यै बृ॒हन्नम॑:

devanagari.text: अवसृष्टा परा पत शरव्ये ब्रह्मसंशिते ।गच्छामित्रान्प्र पद्यस्व मामीषां कं चनोच्छिषः ॥
अवऽसृष्टा । परा । पत । शरव्ये । ब्रह्मऽसंशिते ।गच्छ । अमित्रान् । प्र । पद्यस्व । मा । अमीषाम् । कम् । चन । उत् । शिषः ॥

transliteration.text: áva-sṛṣṭā ǀ párā ǀ pata ǀ śáravye ǀ bráhma-saṃśite ǀgáccha ǀ amítrān ǀ prá ǀ padyasva ǀ mā́ ǀ amī́ṣām ǀ kám ǀ caná ǀ út ǀ śiṣaḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “Arrow, wheted by charms, fly when discharged; go light among the adversaries, spare not one of the enemy.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव॑सृष्टा॒ परा॑ पत॒ शर॑व्ये॒ ब्रह्म॑संशिते । गच्छा॒मित्रा॒न्प्र प॑द्यस्व॒ मामीषां॒ कं च॒नोच्छि॑षः

devanagari.text: यत्र बाणाः संपतंति कुमारा विशिखा इव ।तत्रा नो ब्रह्मणस्पतिरदितिः शर्म यच्छतु विश्वाहा शर्म यच्छतु ॥

Sukta 2.translation: “Agni, kindled (into flame), come to our presence in the same chariot withIndra, and with the swiftmoving gods; mayAditi, the mother of excellent sons, sit down on the sacred grass, and may the immortal godsbe satisfied with the reverentially-offered oblation.”
Sukta 2.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ या॑ह्यग्ने समिधा॒नो अ॒र्वाङिन्द्रे॑ण दे॒वैः स॒रथं॑ तु॒रेभि॑: । ब॒र्हिर्न॑ आस्ता॒मदि॑तिः सुपु॒त्रा स्वाहा॑ दे॒वा अ॒मृता॑ मादयन्ताम्

devanagari.text: अग्निं वो देवमग्निभिः सजोषा यजिष्ठं दूतमध्वरे कृणुध्वं ।यो मर्त्येषु निध्रुविर्ऋतावा तपुर्मूर्धा घृतान्नः पावकः ॥

Sukta 3.translation: “Appoint (gods) the most adorable, divineAgni, consentient with (all other) fires, your messenger at thesacrifice; him who is permanently present among men, the observer of truth, who is crowned with flame, thepurifier, whose food is butter.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ग्निं वो॑ दे॒वम॒ग्निभि॑: स॒जोषा॒ यजि॑ष्ठं दू॒तम॑ध्व॒रे कृ॑णुध्वम् । यो मर्त्ये॑षु॒ निध्रु॑विॠ॒तावा॒ तपु॑र्मूर्धा घृ॒तान्न॑: पाव॒कः

Sukta 3.translation: “When, like a neighing steed about to feed upon the forage, (Agni) springs up from the vast-enclosing(forest) then the wind fans his flame; and black, (Agni), is your course.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रोथ॒दश्वो॒ न यव॑सेऽवि॒ष्यन्य॒दा म॒हः सं॒वर॑णा॒द्व्यस्था॑त् । आद॑स्य॒ वातो॒ अनु॑ वाति शो॒चिरध॑ स्म ते॒ व्रज॑नं कृ॒ष्णम॑स्ति

Sukta 3.translation: “The kindled undecaying flames of you, the newly born, the showerer, rise up; the luminous smokespreads along the sky; and you,Agni, proceed as their messenger to the gods.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उद्यस्य॑ ते॒ नव॑जातस्य॒ वृष्णोऽग्ने॒ चर॑न्त्य॒जरा॑ इधा॒नाः । अच्छा॒ द्याम॑रु॒षो धू॒म ए॑ति॒ सं दू॒तो अ॑ग्न॒ ईय॑से॒ हि दे॒वान्

Sukta 3.translation: “The light of whom quickly spreads over the earth when with his teeth (of flame) he devours his food;your blaze rushes along like a charging host, whenAgni, of goodly aspect, you spread with your flame (amongthe trees) as if (they were) barley.”
Sukta 3.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि यस्य॑ ते पृथि॒व्यां पाजो॒ अश्रे॑त्तृ॒षु यदन्ना॑ स॒मवृ॑क्त॒ जम्भै॑: । सेने॑व सृ॒ष्टा प्रसि॑तिष्ट एति॒ यवं॒ न द॑स्म जु॒ह्वा॑ विवेक्षि

Sukta 3.translation: “Men cherish that youthfulAgniat evening and at dawn, as (they tend) a horse; lighting him as a guestin his proper station; the radiance of the showerer (of benefits), to whom the oblation is offered, shines brightly.”

Sukta 3.translation: “ResplendentAgni, when you shine nigh athandlike gold, your appearance is beautiful; your mightissues like the thunderbolt from the firmament, and like the wonderful sun, you display your lustre.”

Sukta 3.translation: “When we present to you,Agni, the sacred offerings with oblations mixed with butter and milk, thenprotect us with those vast unbounded, innumerable golden cities and metals.”

Sukta 3.translation: “Son of strength,Jātavedas, with those unobstructed (splendours) which belong to you, a munificentdonor, and with those praises wherewiḥ you protect people with their posterity, do you protect us yourworshippers and praisers.”

Sukta 3.translation: “When the brightAgni, radiant with his own diffusive lustre, issues (from the touchwood) like asharpened axe; and he who is desirable, the doer of great deeds, the purifier, is born of his two parents; (heappears) for the worship of the gods.”

Sukta 3.translation: “Illumine for us,Agni, these auspicious (riches); may we possess (a son) intelligent, the celebrator ofsacred rites; may all (good things) be your praisers, and to him who eulogizes (you); and do you ever cherish uswith blessings.”

Sukta 4.translation: “Offer your sacred oblation, and praise the bright and radiantAgni, who passes with wisdom between alldivine and human beings.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र व॑: शु॒क्राय॑ भा॒नवे॑ भरध्वं ह॒व्यं म॒तिं चा॒ग्नये॒ सुपू॑तम् । यो दैव्या॑नि॒ मानु॑षा ज॒नूंष्य॒न्तर्विश्वा॑नि वि॒द्मना॒ जिगा॑ति

Sukta 4.translation: “May the sagaciousAgnibe our conductor from the time that he is orn, most youthful, of his mother; hewho, bright-toothed, attacks the forest, and quickly devours his abundant food.”

Sukta 4.translation: “Whom mortals apprehend as white (shining) in the principal station of that divinity; he who assents tomanly adoration, and blazes for the good of man, and the discomfiture (of his foes).”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्य दे॒वस्य॑ सं॒सद्यनी॑के॒ यं मर्ता॑सः श्ये॒तं ज॑गृ॒भ्रे । नि यो गृभं॒ पौरु॑षेयीमु॒वोच॑ दु॒रोक॑म॒ग्निरा॒यवे॑ शुशोच

transliteration.text: ayám ǀ kavíḥ ǀ ákaviṣu ǀ prá-cetāḥ ǀ márteṣu ǀ agníḥ ǀ amṛ́taḥ ǀ ní ǀ dhāyi ǀsáḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ juhuraḥ ǀ sahasvaḥ ǀ sádā ǀ tvé íti ǀ su-mánasaḥ ǀ syāma ǁ

Sukta 4.translation: “This far-seeing, sagacious, immortalAgni, has been stationed among short-sighted mortals; harm usnot, vigorous Agni, in this world, that we may ever be devoted to you.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं क॒विरक॑विषु॒ प्रचे॑ता॒ मर्ते॑ष्व॒ग्निर॒मृतो॒ नि धा॑यि । स मा नो॒ अत्र॑ जुहुरः सहस्व॒: सदा॒ त्वे सु॒मन॑सः स्याम

devanagari.text: आ यो योनिं देवकृतं ससाद क्रत्वा ह्यग्निरमृताँ अतारीत् ।तमोषधीश्च वनिनश्च गर्भं भूमिश्च विश्वधायसं बिभर्ति ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ yónim ǀ devá-kṛtam ǀ sasā́da ǀ krátvā ǀ hí ǀ agníḥ ǀ amṛ́tān ǀ átārīt ǀtám ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ ca ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ ca ǀ gárbham ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ ca ǀ viśvá-dhāyasam ǀ bibharti ǁ

Sukta 4.translation: “The herbs, and the trees, and the earth, contain as a germ that all- supportingAgni, who occupies aplace provided by the gods, that by his functions he may convey (the offerings) to the immortals.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ यो योनिं॑ दे॒वकृ॑तं स॒साद॒ क्रत्वा॒ ह्य१॒॑ग्निर॒मृताँ॒ अता॑रीत् । तमोष॑धीश्च व॒निन॑श्च॒ गर्भं॒ भूमि॑श्च वि॒श्वधा॑यसं बिभर्ति

Sukta 4.translation: “Agnihas power to grant abundant food; he has power to grant riches withmaleposterity; vigorous Agni,let us not sit down before you devoid of sons, of beauty, of devotion.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ईशे॒ ह्य१॒॑ग्निर॒मृत॑स्य॒ भूरे॒रीशे॑ रा॒यः सु॒वीर्य॑स्य॒ दातो॑: । मा त्वा॑ व॒यं स॑हसावन्न॒वीरा॒ माप्स॑व॒: परि॑ षदाम॒ मादु॑वः

devanagari.text: परिषद्यं ह्यरणस्य रेक्णो नित्यस्य रायः पतयः स्याम ।न शेषो अग्ने अन्यजातमस्त्यचेतानस्य मा पथो वि दुक्षः ॥

Sukta 4.translation: “Wealth is competent to the acquittance of debt; may we be masters of permanent riches; that is notoffspring which is begotten by another; alter not the paths (of the genitive ration) of a blockhead.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प॒रि॒षद्यं॒ ह्यर॑णस्य॒ रेक्णो॒ नित्य॑स्य रा॒यः पत॑यः स्याम । न शेषो॑ अग्ने अ॒न्यजा॑तम॒स्त्यचे॑तानस्य॒ मा प॒थो वि दु॑क्षः

Sukta 4.translation: “One not acquitting debts, although worthy of regard, yet begotten of another, is not to be contemplatedeven in the mind (as fit) for acceptance; for verily he returns to his own house; therefore let there come to us (ason) new- born, possessed of food, victorious over foes.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न॒हि ग्रभा॒यार॑णः सु॒शेवो॒ऽन्योद॑र्यो॒ मन॑सा॒ मन्त॒वा उ॑ । अधा॑ चि॒दोक॒: पुन॒रित्स ए॒त्या नो॑ वा॒ज्य॑भी॒षाळे॑तु॒ नव्य॑:

devanagari.text: त्वमग्ने वनुष्यतो नि पाहि त्वमु नः सहसावन्नवद्यात् ।सं त्वा ध्वस्मन्वदभ्येतु पाथः सं रयिः स्पृहयाय्यः सहस्री ॥

Sukta 4.translation: “Do you,Agni, defend us against, the malignant; do you, who are endowed with strengt, (preserve us)from sin; may the (sacrificial) food come to you free from defect; may the riches that we desire come to us bythousands.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वम॑ग्ने वनुष्य॒तो नि पा॑हि॒ त्वमु॑ नः सहसावन्नव॒द्यात् । सं त्वा॑ ध्वस्म॒न्वद॒भ्ये॑तु॒ पाथ॒: सं र॒यिः स्पृ॑ह॒याय्य॑: सह॒स्री

devanagari.text: एता नो अग्ने सौभगा दिदीह्यपि क्रतुं सुचेतसं वतेम ।विश्वा स्तोतृभ्यो गृणते च संतु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

Sukta 4.translation: “Illumine for us,Agni, these auspicious (riches); may we possess (a son) intelligent, the celebrator ofsacred rites; may all (good things) be to your praisers and to him who eulogizes (you); and do you ever cherishus with blessings.”
Sukta 4.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ता नो॑ अग्ने॒ सौभ॑गा दिदी॒ह्यपि॒ क्रतुं॑ सु॒चेत॑सं वतेम । विश्वा॑ स्तो॒तृभ्यो॑ गृण॒ते च॑ सन्तु यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: प्राग्नये तवसे भरध्वं गिरं दिवो अरतये पृथिव्याः ।यो विश्वेषाममृतानामुपस्थे वैश्वानरो वावृधे जागृवद्भिः ॥

Sukta 5.translation: “Offer praise to the strongAgni, traversing without hindrance heaven and earth; he who (as)Vaiśvānaraprospers at the sacrifices of all the immortals, being associated with the awaking divinities.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्राग्नये॑ त॒वसे॑ भरध्वं॒ गिरं॑ दि॒वो अ॑र॒तये॑ पृथि॒व्याः । यो विश्वे॑षाम॒मृता॑नामु॒पस्थे॑ वैश्वान॒रो वा॑वृ॒धे जा॑गृ॒वद्भि॑:

devanagari.text: पृष्टो दिवि धाय्यग्निः पृथिव्यां नेता सिंधूनां वृषभः स्तियानां ।स मानुषीरभि विशो वि भाति वैश्वानरो वावृधानो वरेण ॥

Sukta 5.translation: “Agni, the leader of the rivers, the showerer of the waters, the radiant, has been stationed in thefirmament and upon earth;Viśvānaraaugmenting with the most excellent (oblation) shines upon human beings.”
Sukta 5.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पृ॒ष्टो दि॒वि धाय्य॒ग्निः पृ॑थि॒व्यां ने॒ता सिन्धू॑नां वृष॒भः स्तिया॑नाम् । स मानु॑षीर॒भि विशो॒ वि भा॑ति वैश्वान॒रो वा॑वृधा॒नो वरे॑ण

devanagari.text: त्वद्भिया विश आयन्नसिक्नीरसमना जहतीर्भोजनानि ।वैश्वानर पूरवे शोशुचानः पुरो यदग्ने दरयन्नदीदेः ॥

Sukta 5.translation: “Through fear of you,Vaiśvānara, the dark-complexioned races, although of many minds, arrived,abandoning their possessions, when,Agni, shining uponPuru, you have blazed, consuming the cities of his foe.”

Sukta 5.translation: “The horses (ofIndra), full of ardour, worship you,Agni; the praises (of men), dispersers (of iniquity),accompanied by oblations, (honour you), the lord of men, the conveyer of riches, theVaiśvānaraof dawns, themanifester of days.”

Sukta 5.translation: “Reverencer of friends,Agni, thVasushave concentrated vigour in you; they have been propitiated byyour acts; genitive rating vast splendour for theArya, do you, Agni, expel theDasyusfrom the dwelling.”

Sukta 5.translation: “Born in the highest heaven, you ever drink (Soma) likeVāyu; genitive rating the waters, you thunder,granting (his wishes) to your offspring, the worshipper.”

Sukta 8.translation: “This greatAgnihas been known among men as invoker (of the gods), the giver of deligh, the mighty; hehas spread (in the firmament), he, the darkpathed at large upon the earth, is nourished by the plural nts.”
Sukta 8.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यमु॒ ष्य सुम॑हाँ अवेदि॒ होता॑ म॒न्द्रो मनु॑षो य॒ह्वो अ॒ग्निः । वि भा अ॑कः ससृजा॒नः पृ॑थि॒व्यां कृ॒ष्णप॑वि॒रोष॑धीभिर्ववक्षे

Sukta 8.translation: “By what oblation,Agni, do you clothe our praise? What offering do you, when glorified, accept? When,giver of good, may we be the possessors and enjoyers of perfect and unmolested riches?”
Sukta 8.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कया॑ नो अग्ने॒ वि व॑सः सुवृ॒क्तिं कामु॑ स्व॒धामृ॑णवः श॒स्यमा॑नः । क॒दा भ॑वेम॒ पत॑यः सुदत्र रा॒यो व॒न्तारो॑ दु॒ष्टर॑स्य सा॒धोः

Sukta 8.translation: “ThisAgniis greatly celebrated by the instrumental tutor of the rite when he shines resplendent as the sun; hewho overcamePuruin battle, and shone glorious as the guest of the gods.”
Sukta 8.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रप्रा॒यम॒ग्निर्भ॑र॒तस्य॑ शृण्वे॒ वि यत्सूर्यो॒ न रोच॑ते बृ॒हद्भाः । अ॒भि यः पू॒रुं पृत॑नासु त॒स्थौ द्यु॑ता॒नो दैव्यो॒ अति॑थिः शुशोच

Sukta 8.translation: “In you,Agni, are many offerings; do you with all your flames be propitious; favourably hear (the praises)of the worshipper; and do you of auspicious manifestation being glorified, spontaneously magnify (your) person n.”
Sukta 8.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अस॒न्नित्त्वे आ॒हव॑नानि॒ भूरि॒ भुवो॒ विश्वे॑भिः सु॒मना॒ अनी॑कैः । स्तु॒तश्चि॑दग्ने शृण्विषे गृणा॒नः स्व॒यं व॑र्धस्व त॒न्वं॑ सुजात

devanagari.text: इदं वचः शतसाः संसहस्रमुदग्नये जनिषीष्ट द्विबर्हाः ।शं यत्स्तोतृभ्य आपये भवाति द्युमदमीवचातनं रक्षोहा ॥

Sukta 8.translation: “Vasi.ṣṭha illustrious in both heaven and earth, rich with a hundred and a thousand (head of cattle), hasaddressed this hymn toAgni, that such fame- conferring disease-removing, fiend-destroying (laudation) may be(the means of) happiness to the eulogists and their kindred.”
Sukta 8.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒दं वच॑: शत॒साः संस॑हस्र॒मुद॒ग्नये॑ जनिषीष्ट द्वि॒बर्हा॑: । शं यत्स्तो॒तृभ्य॑ आ॒पये॒ भवा॑ति द्यु॒मद॑मीव॒चात॑नं रक्षो॒हा

Sukta 8.translation: “WeVasiṣṭhasimplore you,Agni, son of strength, the lord of treasures, that you will quickly bestowfood upon thine adorers, who are affluent (in oblations), and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”

Sukta 9.translation: “The waster away (of living creatures), the invoker (of the gods), the giver of delight, the wisest of thewise, the purifier, (Agni), has been manifested from the lap of the dawn; he gives consciousness to both classesof beings (men and animals), oblations to the gods, and wealth to the pious.”

Sukta 9.translation: “He, the doer of great deeds, who forced open the doors of thePaṇis, recovered for us the sacredfood-bestowing (herd of kine), he who is the invoker of the gods, the giver of delight to the lowly-minded, is seenof all people dissipating the gloom of the nights.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स सु॒क्रतु॒र्यो वि दुर॑: पणी॒नां पु॑ना॒नो अ॒र्कं पु॑रु॒भोज॑सं नः । होता॑ म॒न्द्रो वि॒शां दमू॑नास्ति॒रस्तमो॑ ददृशे रा॒म्याणा॑म्

Sukta 9.translation: “Unperplexed, far-seeing elevated, resplendent, right-directing, a friend, a guest, the bestower ofprosperity upon us, the wonderfully radiant he shines before the dawns, the embryo of the waters, he hasentered into the nascent plural nts.”

Sukta 9.translation: “You,Agni, are to be glorified in (all) the ages of men; you,Jātavedas, who are illustrious whenengaged in battle; our praises wake up the kindling (Agni), him who shines with conspicuous splendour.”

Sukta 9.translation: “Repair,Agni, to the presence of the gods in your office of messenger, (sent) by the assembly engagedin prayer; neglect us not; offer worship toSarasvati, theMaruts, theAśvins, the waters, the universal gods, thatthey may bestow treasures (upon us).”

devanagari.text: त्वामग्ने समिधानो वसिष्ठो जरूथं हन्यक्षि राये पुरंधिं ।पुरुणीथा जातवेदो जरस्व यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

transliteration.text: tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ sam-idhānáḥ ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ járūtham ǀ han ǀ yákṣi ǀ rāyé ǀ púram-dhim ǀpuru-nīthā́ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ jarasva ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 9.translation: “Vasiṣṭhais kindling you,Agni; destroy the malignant; worship the object of many rites, (the company ofthe gods), on behalf of the wealthy (instrumental tutor of the sacrifice), praise (the gods),Jātavedas, with manifoldpraises, and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 9.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वाम॑ग्ने समिधा॒नो वसि॑ष्ठो॒ जरू॑थं ह॒न्यक्षि॑ रा॒ये पुरं॑धिम् । पु॒रु॒णी॒था जा॑तवेदो जरस्व यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: उषो न जारः पृथु पाजो अश्रेद्दविद्युतद्दीद्यच्छोशुचानः ।वृषा हरिः शुचिरा भाति भासा धियो हिन्वान उशतीरजीगः ॥
उषः । न । जारः । पृथु । पाजः । अश्रेत् । दविद्युतत् । दीद्यत् । शोशुचानः ।वृषा । हरिः । शुचिः । आ । भाति । भासा । धियः । हिन्वानः । उशतीः । अजीगरिति ॥

transliteration.text: uṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ jāráḥ ǀ pṛthú ǀ pā́jaḥ ǀ aśret ǀ dávidyutat ǀ dī́dyat ǀ śóśucānaḥ ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ háriḥ ǀ śúciḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhāti ǀ bhāsā́ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ hinvānáḥ ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ ajīgaríti ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Agni, like the lover of the dawn (the sun), radiant, bright, resplendent, displays extensive lustre, theshowerer (of benefits), the receiver (of oblations), he shines with splendour, encouraging holy rites; he arouses(mankind), desiring (his presence).”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒षो न जा॒रः पृ॒थु पाजो॑ अश्रे॒द्दवि॑द्युत॒द्दीद्य॒च्छोशु॑चानः । वृषा॒ हरि॒: शुचि॒रा भा॑ति भा॒सा धियो॑ हिन्वा॒न उ॑श॒तीर॑जीगः

devanagari.text: स्वर्ण वस्तोरुषसामरोचि यज्ञं तन्वाना उशिजो न मन्म ।अग्निर्जन्मानि देव आ वि विद्वांद्रवद्दूतो देवयावा वनिष्ठः ॥
स्वः । न । वस्तोः । उषसाम् । अरोचि । यज्ञम् । तन्वानाः । उशिजः । न । मन्म ।अग्निः । जन्मानि । देवः । आ । वि । विद्वान् । द्रवत् । दूतः । देवऽयावा । वनिष्ठः ॥

transliteration.text: sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ vástoḥ ǀ uṣásām ǀ aroci ǀ yajñám ǀ tanvānā́ḥ ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mánma ǀagníḥ ǀ jánmāni ǀ deváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ví ǀ vidvā́n ǀ dravát ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ deva-yā́vā ǀ vániṣṭhaḥ ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Agni, preceding the dawn, is radiant by day as the sun, and the priests celebrating the sacrifice repeathis praise; the divine, munificent Agni, the messenger (of the gods), cognizant of their birth, repairing to thedeities, hastens in various directions.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्व१॒॑र्ण वस्तो॑रु॒षसा॑मरोचि य॒ज्ञं त॑न्वा॒ना उ॒शिजो॒ न मन्म॑ । अ॒ग्निर्जन्मा॑नि दे॒व आ वि वि॒द्वान्द्र॒वद्दू॒तो दे॑व॒यावा॒ वनि॑ष्ठः

devanagari.text: अच्छा गिरो मतयो देवयंतीरग्निं यंति द्रविणं भिक्षमाणाः ।सुसंदृशं सुप्रतीकं स्वंचं हव्यवाहमरतिं मानुषाणां ॥
अच्छ । गिरः । मतयः । देवऽयन्तीः । अग्निम् । यन्ति । द्रविणम् । भिक्षमाणाः ।सुऽसन्दृशम् । सुऽप्रतीकम् । सुऽअञ्चम् । हव्यऽवाहम् । अरतिम् । मानुषाणाम् ॥

transliteration.text: áccha ǀ gíraḥ ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ deva-yántīḥ ǀ agním ǀ yanti ǀ dráviṇam ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǀsu-sandṛ́śam ǀ su-prátīkam ǀ su-áñcam ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ aratím ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Devout praises and hymns, soliciting riches, proceed toAgni, who is of plural asant aspect, agreeableform, of graceful movement, the bearer of oblations, the ruler of men.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अच्छा॒ गिरो॑ म॒तयो॑ देव॒यन्ती॑र॒ग्निं य॑न्ति॒ द्रवि॑णं॒ भिक्ष॑माणाः । सु॒सं॒दृशं॑ सु॒प्रती॑कं॒ स्वञ्चं॑ हव्य॒वाह॑मर॒तिं मानु॑षाणाम्

devanagari.text: इंद्रं नो अग्ने वसुभिः सजोषा रुद्रं रुद्रेभिरा वहा बृहंतं ।आदित्येभिरदितिं विश्वजन्यां बृहस्पतिमृक्वभिर्विश्ववारं ॥
इन्द्रम् । नः । अग्ने । वसुऽभिः । सऽजोषाः । रुद्रम् । रुद्रेभिः । आ । वह । बृहन्तम् ।आदित्येभिः । अदितिम् । विश्वऽजन्याम् । बृहस्पतिम् । ऋक्वऽभिः । विश्वऽवारम् ॥

transliteration.text: índram ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ rudrám ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ bṛhántam ǀādityébhiḥ ǀ áditim ǀ viśvá-janyām ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ ṛ́kva-bhiḥ ǀ viśvá-vāram ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Consentient with theVasus,Agni, bring hitherIndra, with theRudras, the benevolentAditi, with theĀdityas andBṛhaspati, the desired of all, with the adorable (Aṅgirasas).”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रं॑ नो अग्ने॒ वसु॑भिः स॒जोषा॑ रु॒द्रं रु॒द्रेभि॒रा व॑हा बृ॒हन्त॑म् । आ॒दि॒त्येभि॒रदि॑तिं वि॒श्वज॑न्यां॒ बृह॒स्पति॒मृक्व॑भिर्वि॒श्ववा॑रम्

devanagari.text: मंद्रं होतारमुशिजो यविष्ठमग्निं विश ईळते अध्वरेषु ।स हि क्षपावाँ अभवद्रयीणामतंद्रो दूतो यजथाय देवान् ॥

transliteration.text: mandrám ǀ hótāram ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ yáviṣṭham ǀ agním ǀ víśaḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀsáḥ ǀ hí ǀ kṣápā-vān ǀ ábhavat ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ átandraḥ ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ yajáthāya ǀ devā́n ǁ

Sukta 10.translation: “Men desiring him celebrate at sacrifices the youthfulAgni, the giver of delight, the invoker of the gods;he, the ruler of the night, has been the diligent envoy of the opulent (instrumental tutors of sacrifices) for the worship ofthe gods.”
Sukta 10.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒न्द्रं होता॑रमु॒शिजो॒ यवि॑ष्ठम॒ग्निं विश॑ ईळते अध्व॒रेषु॑ । स हि क्षपा॑वाँ॒ अभ॑वद्रयी॒णामत॑न्द्रो दू॒तो य॒जथा॑य दे॒वान्

devanagari.text: महाँ अस्यध्वरस्य प्रकेतो न ऋते त्वदमृता मादयंते ।आ विश्वेभिः सरथं याहि देवैर्न्यग्ने होता प्रथमः सदेह ॥

Sukta 11.translation: “Great are you,Agni, the manifester of the solemnity without you the immortals do not rejoice; come inthe same chariot with all the gods; sit down here the chief, the ministrant priest.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒हाँ अ॑स्यध्व॒रस्य॑ प्रके॒तो न ऋ॒ते त्वद॒मृता॑ मादयन्ते । आ विश्वे॑भिः स॒रथं॑ याहि दे॒वैर्न्य॑ग्ने॒ होता॑ प्रथ॒मः स॑दे॒ह

devanagari.text: त्वामीळते अजिरं दूत्याय हविष्मंतः सदमिन्मानुषासः ।यस्य देवैरासदो बर्हिरग्नेऽहान्यस्मै सुदिना भवंति ॥

Sukta 11.translation: “Men offering oblations, ever solicit you the quick-going (to undertake) the office of their messenger, forto him, on whose sacred grass you sit with the gods, the days are prosperous.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वामी॑ळते अजि॒रं दू॒त्या॑य ह॒विष्म॑न्त॒: सद॒मिन्मानु॑षासः । यस्य॑ दे॒वैरास॑दो ब॒र्हिर॒ग्नेऽहा॑न्यस्मै सु॒दिना॑ भवन्ति

devanagari.text: त्रिश्चिदक्तोः प्र चिकितुर्वसूनि त्वे अंतर्दाशुषे मर्त्याय ।मनुष्वदग्न इह यक्षि देवान्भवा नो दूतो अभिशस्तिपावा ॥

Sukta 11.translation: “In you,Agni, thrice in the day, (the priests) make manifest the treasures (of the oblation) for (the benefitof the) mortal donor; worship the gods on this occasion, Agni, as (you did) forManu; be our messenger, ourprotector against malignity.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्रिश्चि॑द॒क्तोः प्र चि॑कितु॒र्वसू॑नि॒ त्वे अ॒न्तर्दा॒शुषे॒ मर्त्या॑य । म॒नु॒ष्वद॑ग्न इ॒ह य॑क्षि दे॒वान्भवा॑ नो दू॒तो अ॑भिशस्ति॒पावा॑

devanagari.text: अग्निरीशे बृहतो अध्वरस्याग्निर्विश्वस्य हविषः कृतस्य ।क्रतुं ह्यस्य वसवो जुषंताथा देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहं ॥

Sukta 11.translation: “Agnipresides over the solemn rite, over every consecrated oblation; theVasusapproved of his acts;the gods have made him the bearer of the offering.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ग्निरी॑शे बृह॒तो अ॑ध्व॒रस्या॒ग्निर्विश्व॑स्य ह॒विष॑: कृ॒तस्य॑ । क्रतुं॒ ह्य॑स्य॒ वस॑वो जु॒षन्ताथा॑ दे॒वा द॑धिरे हव्य॒वाह॑म्

devanagari.text: आग्ने वह हविरद्याय देवानिंद्रज्येष्ठास इह मादयंतां ।इमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धेहि यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
आ । अग्ने । वह । हविःऽअद्याय । देवान् । इन्द्रऽज्येष्ठासः । इह । मादयन्ताम् ।इमम् । यज्ञम् । दिवि । देवेषु । धेहि । यूयम् । पात । स्वस्तिऽभिः । सदा । नः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ agne ǀ vaha ǀ haviḥ-ádyāya ǀ devā́n ǀ índra-jyeṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mādayantām ǀimám ǀ yajñám ǀ diví ǀ devéṣu ǀ dhehi ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 11.translation: “Agni, bring the gods to eat of the oblation; may they, of whomIndrais the chief, be delighted on thisoccasion; convey this sacrifice to the deities in heaven, and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 11.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आग्ने॑ वह हवि॒रद्या॑य दे॒वानिन्द्र॑ज्येष्ठास इ॒ह मा॑दयन्ताम् । इ॒मं य॒ज्ञं दि॒वि दे॒वेषु॑ धेहि यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: अगन्म महा नमसा यविष्ठं यो दीदाय समिद्धः स्वे दुरोणे ।चित्रभानुं रोदसी अंतरुर्वी स्वाहुतं विश्वतः प्रत्यंचं ॥

Sukta 12.translation: “Let us approach with profound reverence the youngest (of the gods), who shines when kindled in hisown abode; who is blazing wonderfully between heaven and earth, and, piously invoked, is coming from everyquarter.”

Sukta 12.translation: “May thatAgniwho by his greatness is the overcomer of all evils, who is praised asJātavedasin the(sacrificial) chamber, protect us, glorifying him, and affluent (in oblations), from all sin and reproach.”

Sukta 12.translation: “You areVaruṇa, you areMitra,Agni; theVasiṣṭhasaugment you with praises; may liberally distributedriches be (extant) in you, and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”

Sukta 13.translation: “Offer praise and worshp toAgni, the enlightener of all, the accepter of pious rites, the destroyer of theAsuras; propitiating him, I now present the oblation on the sacred grass toVaiśvānara, the granter of riches.”

Sukta 13.translation: “You,Agni, radiant with lustre, fill the heaven and earth (with light) as soon as born; you,Vaiśvānara,from whom wealth proceeds, has by your might liberated the gods from malevolent (foes).”

Sukta 13.translation: “When you are born,Agni, the lord, the circumambient, you watch over all creatures as a herdsman overhis cattle; be willing,Vaiśvānara, to requite our praise, and do you cherish us with blessings.”

Sukta 16.translation: “The most wiseAgniis the bearer (of oblations), as the mouth of the gods with his graceful tongue (offlame); bring riches, Agni, to the affluent (in sacrifices); encourage the donor of the oblation.”

Sukta 16.translation: “Youngest (of the gods), protect with your protections from iniquity, (and reward) with numerous citiesthose who, through the desire of extended fame, bestow riches, comprehending horses and treasure.”

Sukta 16.translation: “The divineAgni, the giver of wealth, desires the ladle filled full. Pour out (the contents), and replenish(the vessel), and then the deity bears (your oblations to the gods).”

Sukta 16.translation: “The gods have made the wise (Agni) the ministrant priest, and bearer of the sacrifice. Agni giives to theman who performs the prescribed rite and presents (the offering), wealth, with virtuousmaleposterity.”

Sukta 18.translation: “These gratifying and pious hymns, emulous (in earnestness), are addressed on this occasion to you,may the path of your riches lead downwards; may we,Indra, (diligent) in your praise, enjoy felicity.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मा उ॑ त्वा पस्पृधा॒नासो॒ अत्र॑ म॒न्द्रा गिरो॑ देव॒यन्ती॒रुप॑ स्थुः । अ॒र्वाची॑ ते प॒थ्या॑ रा॒य ए॑तु॒ स्याम॑ ते सुम॒तावि॑न्द्र॒ शर्म॑न्

devanagari.text: धेनुं न त्वा सूयवसे दुदुक्षन्नुप ब्रह्माणि ससृजे वसिष्ठः ।त्वामिन्मे गोपतिं विश्व आहा न इंद्रः सुमतिं गंत्वच्छ ॥

Sukta 18.translation: “Desirous of milking you like a milch cow at pasture,Vasiṣṭhahas let loose his prayers to you; everyone of my people proclaims you the lord of cattle; mayIndrabe present at our praises.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: धे॒नुं न त्वा॑ सू॒यव॑से॒ दुदु॑क्ष॒न्नुप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि ससृजे॒ वसि॑ष्ठः । त्वामिन्मे॒ गोप॑तिं॒ विश्व॑ आ॒हा न॒ इन्द्र॑: सुम॒तिं ग॒न्त्वच्छ॑

devanagari.text: अर्णांसि चित्पप्रथाना सुदास इंद्रो गाधान्यकृणोत्सुपारा ।शर्धंतं शिम्युमुचथस्य नव्यः शापं सिंधूनामकृणोदशस्तीः ॥

Sukta 18.translation: “The adorableIndramade the well-known deep waters (of the Paruṣṇi) fordable forSudāsa, andconverted the vehement awakening imprecation of the sacrificer into the calumnation of the rivers.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अर्णां॑सि चित्पप्रथा॒ना सु॒दास॒ इन्द्रो॑ गा॒धान्य॑कृणोत्सुपा॒रा । शर्ध॑न्तं शि॒म्युमु॒चथ॑स्य॒ नव्य॒: शापं॒ सिन्धू॑नामकृणो॒दश॑स्तीः

Sukta 18.translation: “Turvaśa, who was presiding (at solemn rites), diligent in sacrifice, (went toSudāsa) for wealth; but likefishes restricted (to the element of water), theBhrigusandDruhyusquickly assailed them; of these twoeverywhere going the friend (of Sudāsa,Indra) rescued his friend.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पु॒रो॒ळा इत्तु॒र्वशो॒ यक्षु॑रासीद्रा॒ये मत्स्या॑सो॒ निशि॑ता॒ अपी॑व । श्रु॒ष्टिं च॑क्रु॒र्भृग॑वो द्रु॒ह्यव॑श्च॒ सखा॒ सखा॑यमतर॒द्विषू॑चोः

Sukta 18.translation: “Those who dress the oblation, those who pronounce auspicious words, those who abstain frompenance, those who bear horns (in theirhands), those who bestow happiness (on the world by sacrifice), glorifythatIndra, who recovered the cattle of theAryafrom the plural nderers, who slew the enemies in battle.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ प॒क्थासो॑ भला॒नसो॑ भन॒न्तालि॑नासो विषा॒णिन॑: शि॒वास॑: । आ योऽन॑यत्सध॒मा आर्य॑स्य ग॒व्या तृत्सु॑भ्यो अजगन्यु॒धा नॄन्

Sukta 18.translation: “The evil-disposed and stupid (enemies ofSudāsa), crossing the humble Paruṣṇi river, have brokendown its banks; but he by his greatness pervades the earth, andKavi, the son of Cāyamana, like a fallingvictim, sleeps (in death).”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दु॒रा॒ध्यो॒३॒॑ अदि॑तिं स्रे॒वय॑न्तोऽचे॒तसो॒ वि ज॑गृभ्रे॒ परु॑ष्णीम् । म॒ह्नावि॑व्यक्पृथि॒वीं पत्य॑मानः प॒शुष्क॒विर॑शय॒च्चाय॑मानः

Sukta 18.translation: “The waters followed their regular course to the Paruṣṇi, nor (wandered) beyond it; the quick courser(of the king) came to the accessible plural ces, andIndramade the idly-talking enemies, with their numerousprogeny, subject among men (toSudāsa).”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ई॒युरर्थं॒ न न्य॒र्थं परु॑ष्णीमा॒शुश्च॒नेद॑भिपि॒त्वं ज॑गाम । सु॒दास॒ इन्द्र॑: सु॒तुकाँ॑ अ॒मित्रा॒नर॑न्धय॒न्मानु॑षे॒ वध्रि॑वाचः

Sukta 18.translation: “They who ride on particoloured cattle, (theMaruts), despatched byPṛṣṇiand recalling theengagement made by them with their friend (Indra), came like cattle from the pasturage, when left without aherdsman; the exultingNiyutsteeds brought them quickly (against the foe).”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ई॒युर्गावो॒ न यव॑सा॒दगो॑पा यथाकृ॒तम॒भि मि॒त्रं चि॒तास॑: । पृश्नि॑गाव॒: पृश्नि॑निप्रेषितासः श्रु॒ष्टिं च॑क्रुर्नि॒युतो॒ रन्त॑यश्च

Sukta 18.translation: “The heroIndracreated theMaruts(for the assistance of therājā), who, ambitious of fame, slewone-and-twenty of the men on the two banks (of the Paruṣṇi), as a well-looking priest lops the sacred grass inthe chamber of sacrifice.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: एकं॑ च॒ यो विं॑श॒तिं च॑ श्रव॒स्या वै॑क॒र्णयो॒र्जना॒न्राजा॒ न्यस्त॑: । द॒स्मो न सद्म॒न्नि शि॑शाति ब॒र्हिः शूर॒: सर्ग॑मकृणो॒दिन्द्र॑ एषाम्

Sukta 18.translation: “You, the bearer of the thunderbolt, did drownŚruta,Kavaṣa,Vṛddhaand afterwardsDruhyu, in thewaters; for they,Indra, who are devoted to you, and glorify you, preferring your friendship, enjoy it.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अध॑ श्रु॒तं क॒वषं॑ वृ॒द्धम॒प्स्वनु॑ द्रु॒ह्युं नि वृ॑ण॒ग्वज्र॑बाहुः । वृ॒णा॒ना अत्र॑ स॒ख्याय॑ स॒ख्यं त्वा॒यन्तो॒ ये अम॑द॒न्ननु॑ त्वा

transliteration.text: ví ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ dṛṃhitā́ni ǀ eṣām ǀ índraḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ sáhasā ǀ saptá ǀ dardaríti dardaḥ ǀví ǀ ā́navasya ǀ tṛ́tsave ǀ gáyam ǀ bhāk ǀ jéṣma ǀ pūrúm ǀ vidáthe ǀ mṛdhrá-vācam ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Indra, in his might, quickly demolished all their strongholds, and their seven (kinds of) cities; he hasgiven the dwelling of the son of Anu to Tṛtsu; may we, (by propitiating Indra), conquer in battle the ill-speakingman.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि स॒द्यो विश्वा॑ दृंहि॒तान्ये॑षा॒मिन्द्र॒: पुर॒: सह॑सा स॒प्त द॑र्दः । व्यान॑वस्य॒ तृत्स॑वे॒ गयं॑ भा॒ग्जेष्म॑ पू॒रुं वि॒दथे॑ मृ॒ध्रवा॑चम्

transliteration.text: ní ǀ gavyávaḥ ǀ ánavaḥ ǀ druhyávaḥ ǀ ca ǀ ṣaṣṭíḥ ǀ śatā́ ǀ susupuḥ ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ sahásrā ǀṣaṣṭíḥ ǀ vīrā́saḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ duvaḥ-yú ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ índrasya ǀ vīryā́ ǀ kṛtā́ni ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “The warriors of the Anus andDruhyus, intending (to carry off the) cattle, (hostile) to the pious(Sudāsa) perished to the number of sixty-six thousand six hundred and sixty; such are all the glorious acts ofIndra.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नि ग॒व्यवोऽन॑वो द्रु॒ह्यव॑श्च ष॒ष्टिः श॒ता सु॑षुपु॒: षट् स॒हस्रा॑ । ष॒ष्टिर्वी॒रासो॒ अधि॒ षड्दु॑वो॒यु विश्वेदिन्द्र॑स्य वी॒र्या॑ कृ॒तानि॑

devanagari.text: इंद्रेणैते तृत्सवो वेविषाणा आपो न सृष्टा अधवंत नीचीः ।दुर्मित्रासः प्रकलविन्मिमाना जहुर्विश्वानि भोजना सुदासे ॥

transliteration.text: índreṇa ǀ eté ǀ tṛ́tsavaḥ ǀ véviṣāṇāḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ sṛṣṭā́ḥ ǀ adhavanta ǀ nī́cīḥ ǀduḥ-mitrā́saḥ ǀ prakala-vít ǀ mímānāḥ ǀ jahúḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ bhójanā ǀ su-dā́se ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “These hostile, Tṛtsus, ignorantly contending withIndra, fled routed as rapidly as rivers on a downwardcourse, and being discomfited, abandoned all their possessions toSudāsa.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रे॑णै॒ते तृत्स॑वो॒ वेवि॑षाणा॒ आपो॒ न सृ॒ष्टा अ॑धवन्त॒ नीची॑: । दु॒र्मि॒त्रास॑: प्रकल॒विन्मिमा॑ना ज॒हुर्विश्वा॑नि॒ भोज॑ना सु॒दासे॑

devanagari.text: अर्धं वीरस्य शृतपामनिंद्रं परा शर्धंतं नुनुदे अभि क्षां ।इंद्रो मन्युं मन्युम्यो मिमाय भेजे पथो वर्तनिं पत्यमानः ॥
अर्धम् । वीरस्य । शृतऽपाम् । अनिन्द्रम् । परा । शर्धन्तम् । नुनुदे । अभि । क्षाम् ।इन्द्रः । मन्युम् । मन्युऽभ्यः । मिमाय । भेजे । पथः । वर्तनिम् । पत्यमानः ॥

transliteration.text: ardhám ǀ vīrásya ǀ śṛta-pā́m ǀ anindrám ǀ párā ǀ śárdhantam ǀ nunude ǀ abhí ǀ kṣā́m ǀíndraḥ ǀ manyúm ǀ manyu-bhyáḥ ǀ mimāya ǀ bhejé ǀ patháḥ ǀ vartaním ǀ pátyamānaḥ ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Indrahas scattered over the earth the hostile rival of the hero (Sudāsa), the senior of Indra, theappropriator of the oblation; Indra has baffled the wrath of the wratfhful enemy, and the (foe) advancing on theway (against Sudāsa) has taken the path of flight.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒र्धं वी॒रस्य॑ शृत॒पाम॑नि॒न्द्रं परा॒ शर्ध॑न्तं नुनुदे अ॒भि क्षाम् । इन्द्रो॑ म॒न्युं म॑न्यु॒म्यो॑ मिमाय भे॒जे प॒थो व॑र्त॒निं पत्य॑मानः

devanagari.text: आध्रेण चित्तद्वेकं चकार सिंह्यं चित्पेत्वेना जघान ।अव स्रक्तीर्वेश्यावृश्चदिंद्रः प्रायच्छद्विश्वा भोजना सुदासे ॥

transliteration.text: ādhréṇa ǀ cit ǀ tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ékam ǀ cakāra ǀ siṃhyám ǀ cit ǀ pétvena ǀ jaghāna ǀáva ǀ sraktī́ḥ ǀ veśyā́ ǀ avṛścat ǀ índraḥ ǀ prá ǀ ayacchat ǀ víśvā ǀ bhójanā ǀ su-dā́se ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Indra, has effected a valuable (donation) by a pauper; he has slain an old lion by a goat; he has cut theangles of the sacrificialpostwith a needle; he has given all the spoils (of the enemy) toSudāsa.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒ध्रेण॑ चि॒त्तद्वेकं॑ चकार सिं॒ह्यं॑ चि॒त्पेत्वे॑ना जघान । अव॑ स्र॒क्तीर्वे॒श्या॑वृश्च॒दिन्द्र॒: प्राय॑च्छ॒द्विश्वा॒ भोज॑ना सु॒दासे॑

devanagari.text: शश्वंतो हि शत्रवो रारधुष्टे भेदस्य चिच्छर्धतो विंद रंधिं ।मर्ताँ एनः स्तुवतो यः कृणोति तिग्मं तस्मिन्नि जहि वज्रमिंद्र ॥
शश्वन्तः । हि । शत्रवः । ररधुः । ते । भेदस्य । चित् । शर्धतः । विन्द । रन्धिम् ।मर्तान् । एनः । स्तुवतः । यः । कृणोति । तिग्मम् । तस्मिन् । नि । जहि । वज्रम् । इन्द्र ॥

transliteration.text: śáśvantaḥ ǀ hí ǀ śátravaḥ ǀ raradhúḥ ǀ te ǀ bhedásya ǀ cit ǀ śárdhataḥ ǀ vinda ǀ rándhim ǀmártān ǀ énaḥ ǀ stuvatáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ tigmám ǀ tásmin ǀ ní ǀ jahi ǀ vájram ǀ indra ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Your numerous enemies,Indra, have been reduced to subjection, effect at some time or other thesubjugation of the turbulentBheda, who holds men praising you as guilty of wickedness; hurl, Indra, your sharpthuderbolt against him.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शश्व॑न्तो॒ हि शत्र॑वो रार॒धुष्टे॑ भे॒दस्य॑ चि॒च्छर्ध॑तो विन्द॒ रन्धि॑म् । मर्ताँ॒ एन॑: स्तुव॒तो यः कृ॒णोति॑ ति॒ग्मं तस्मि॒न्नि ज॑हि॒ वज्र॑मिन्द्र

devanagari.text: आवदिंद्रं यमुना तृत्सवश्च प्रात्र भेदं सर्वताता मुषायत् ।अजासश्च शिग्रवो यक्षवश्च बलिं शीर्षाणि जभ्रुरश्व्यानि ॥

transliteration.text: ā́vat ǀ índram ǀ yamúnā ǀ tṛ́tsavaḥ ǀ ca ǀ prá ǀ átra ǀ bhedám ǀ sarvá-tātā ǀ muṣāyat ǀajā́saḥ ǀ ca ǀ śígravaḥ ǀ yákṣavaḥ ǀ ca ǀ balím ǀ śīrṣā́ṇi ǀ jabhruḥ ǀ áśvyāni ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “The dwellers on theYamunaand the Tṛtsus glorifiedIndrawhen he killedBhedain battle; the Ajas, theŚigrus, theYakṣas, offered him as a sacrifice the heads of the horses (killed in the combat).”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आव॒दिन्द्रं॑ य॒मुना॒ तृत्स॑वश्च॒ प्रात्र॑ भे॒दं स॒र्वता॑ता मुषायत् । अ॒जास॑श्च॒ शिग्र॑वो॒ यक्ष॑वश्च ब॒लिं शी॒र्षाणि॑ जभ्रु॒रश्व्या॑नि

devanagari.text: न त इंद्र सुमतयो न रायः संचक्षे पूर्वा उषसो न नूत्नाः ।देवकं चिन्मान्यमानं जघंथाव त्मना बृहतः शंबरं भेत् ॥

transliteration.text: ná ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ su-matáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ sam-cákṣe ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ná ǀ nū́tnāḥ ǀdévakam ǀ cit ǀ mānyamānám ǀ jaghantha ǀ áva ǀ tmánā ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ śámbaram ǀ bhet ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Your favours,Indra, and your bounties, whether old or new, cannot be counted like the (recurring)dawn; you have slainDevaka, the son of Mānyamāna, and of thine own will, has cast downŚambarafrom thevast (mountain).”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न त॑ इन्द्र सुम॒तयो॒ न राय॑: सं॒चक्षे॒ पूर्वा॑ उ॒षसो॒ न नूत्ना॑: । देव॑कं चिन्मान्यमा॒नं ज॑घ॒न्थाव॒ त्मना॑ बृह॒तः शम्ब॑रं भेत्

devanagari.text: प्र ये गृहादममदुस्त्वाया पराशरः शतयातुर्वसिष्ठः ।न ते भोजस्य सख्यं मृषंताधा सूरिभ्यः सुदिना व्युच्छान् ॥

Sukta 18.translation: “Parāśara, the destroyer of hundreds (ofrākṣasas), andVasiṣṭhathey who, devoted to you, haveglorified you in every dwelling, neglect not the friendship of you (their) benefactor; therefore prosperous daysdawn upon the pious.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र ये गृ॒हादम॑मदुस्त्वा॒या प॑राश॒रः श॒तया॑तु॒र्वसि॑ष्ठः । न ते॑ भो॒जस्य॑ स॒ख्यं मृ॑ष॒न्ताधा॑ सू॒रिभ्य॑: सु॒दिना॒ व्यु॑च्छान्

devanagari.text: द्वे नप्तुर्देववतः शते गोर्द्वा रथा वधूमंता सुदासः ।अर्हन्नग्ने पैजवनस्य दानं होतेव सद्म पर्येमि रेभन् ॥

transliteration.text: dvé íti ǀ náptuḥ ǀ devá-vataḥ ǀ śaté íti ǀ góḥ ǀ dvā́ ǀ ráthā ǀ vadhū́-mantā ǀ su-dā́saḥ ǀárhan ǀ agne ǀ paija-vanásya ǀ dā́nam ǀ hótā-iva ǀ sádma ǀ pári ǀ emi ǀ rébhan ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Praising the liberality ofSudāsa, the grandson of Devavat, the son ofPaijavana, the donor of twohundred cows, and of two chariots with two wives, I, worthy (of the gift), circumambulate you,Agni, like theministrant priest in the chamber (of sacrifice).”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्वे नप्तु॑र्दे॒वव॑तः श॒ते गोर्द्वा रथा॑ व॒धूम॑न्ता सु॒दास॑: । अर्ह॑न्नग्ने पैजव॒नस्य॒ दानं॒ होते॑व॒ सद्म॒ पर्ये॑मि॒ रेभ॑न्

devanagari.text: चत्वारो मा पैजवनस्य दानाः स्मद्दिष्टयः कृशनिनो निरेके ।ऋज्रासो मा पृथिविष्ठाः सुदासस्तोकं तोकाय श्रवसे वहंति ॥

transliteration.text: catvā́raḥ ǀ mā ǀ paija-vanásya ǀ dā́nāḥ ǀ smát-diṣṭayaḥ ǀ kṛśanínaḥ ǀ nireké ǀṛjrā́saḥ ǀ mā ǀ pṛthivi-sthā́ḥ ǀ su-dā́saḥ ǀ tokám ǀ tokā́ya ǀ śrávase ǀ vahanti ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Four (horses), having golden trappings, going steadily on a difficult road, celebrated on the earth, theexcellent and acceptable gifts (made) to me bySudāsa, the son ofPaijavana, bear me as a son (to obtain) foodand progeny.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: च॒त्वारो॑ मा पैजव॒नस्य॒ दाना॒: स्मद्दि॑ष्टयः कृश॒निनो॑ निरे॒के । ऋ॒ज्रासो॑ मा पृथिवि॒ष्ठाः सु॒दास॑स्तो॒कं तो॒काय॒ श्रव॑से वहन्ति

devanagari.text: यस्य श्रवो रोदसी अंतरुर्वी शीर्ष्णेशीर्ष्णे विबभाजा विभक्ता ।सप्तेदिंद्रं न स्रवतो गृणंति नि युध्यामधिमशिशादभीके ॥

transliteration.text: yásya ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ antáḥ ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ śīrṣṇé-śīrṣṇe ǀ vi-babhā́ja ǀ vi-bhaktā́ ǀsaptá ǀ ít ǀ índram ǀ ná ǀ sravátaḥ ǀ gṛṇanti ǀ ní ǀ yudhyāmadhím ǀ aśiśāt ǀ abhī́ke ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “The seven worlds praise (Sudāsa) as if he wereIndra; him whose fame (spreads) through thespacious heaven and earth; who, munificent, has distributed (wealth) on every eminent person n, and (for him) theflowing (rivers) have destroyed Yudhyamadhi in war.”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्य॒ श्रवो॒ रोद॑सी अ॒न्तरु॒र्वी शी॒र्ष्णेशी॑र्ष्णे विब॒भाजा॑ विभ॒क्ता । स॒प्तेदिन्द्रं॒ न स्र॒वतो॑ गृणन्ति॒ नि यु॑ध्याम॒धिम॑शिशाद॒भीके॑

devanagari.text: इमं नरो मरुतः सश्चतानु दिवोदासं न पितरं सुदासः ।अविष्टना पैजवनस्य केतं दूणाशं क्षत्रमजरं दुवोयु ॥

transliteration.text: imám ǀ naraḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ saścata ǀ ánu ǀ dívaḥ-dāsam ǀ ná ǀ pitáram ǀ su-dā́saḥ ǀaviṣṭána ǀ paija-vanásya ǀ kétam ǀ duḥ-náśam ǀ kṣatrám ǀ ajáram ǀ duvaḥ-yú ǁ

Sukta 18.translation: “Maruts, leaders (of rites), attend upon this (prince) as you did uponDivodāsa, the father ofSudāsa;favour the prayers of the devout son of Pijavana, and may his strength be unimpaired, undecaying].”
Sukta 18.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मं न॑रो मरुतः सश्च॒तानु॒ दिवो॑दासं॒ न पि॒तरं॑ सु॒दास॑: । अ॒वि॒ष्टना॑ पैजव॒नस्य॒ केतं॑ दू॒णाशं॑ क्ष॒त्रम॒जरं॑ दुवो॒यु

devanagari.text: यस्तिग्मशृंगो वृषभो न भीम एकः कृष्टीश्च्यावयति प्र विश्वाः ।यः शश्वतो अदाशुषो गयस्य प्रयंतासि सुष्वितराय वेदः ॥

transliteration.text: yáḥ ǀ tigmá-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀ cyaváyati ǀ prá ǀ víśvāḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ śáśvataḥ ǀ ádāśuṣaḥ ǀ gáyasya ǀ pra-yantā́ ǀ asi ǀ susví-tarāya ǀ védaḥ ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Indra, who is formidable as a sharp-horned bull, singly expels all men (from their stations); you who arethe despoiler of the ample wealth of him who makes no offerings are the giver of riches to the presenter offrequent oblations.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्ति॒ग्मशृ॑ङ्गो वृष॒भो न भी॒म एक॑: कृ॒ष्टीश्च्या॒वय॑ति॒ प्र विश्वा॑: । यः शश्व॑तो॒ अदा॑शुषो॒ गय॑स्य प्रय॒न्तासि॒ सुष्वि॑तराय॒ वेद॑:

devanagari.text: त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र कुत्समावः शुश्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये ।दासं यच्छुष्णं कुयवं न्यस्मा अरंधय आर्जुनेयाय शिक्षन् ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ indra ǀ kútsam ǀ āvaḥ ǀ śúśrūṣamāṇaḥ ǀ tanvā́ ǀ sa-maryé ǀdā́sam ǀ yát ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ kúyavam ǀ ní ǀ asmai ǀ árandhayaḥ ǀ ārjuneyā́ya ǀ śíkṣan ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Aiding him with your person n,Indra, you had defendedKutsain combat when you had subjugatedDāsa,ŚuṣṇaandKuyava, giving (their spoil) to that son ofArjuni.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं ह॒ त्यदि॑न्द्र॒ कुत्स॑माव॒: शुश्रू॑षमाणस्त॒न्वा॑ सम॒र्ये । दासं॒ यच्छुष्णं॒ कुय॑वं॒ न्य॑स्मा॒ अर॑न्धय आर्जुने॒याय॒ शिक्ष॑न्

devanagari.text: त्वं धृष्णो धृषता वीतहव्यं प्रावो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सुदासं ।प्र पौरुकुत्सिं त्रसदस्युमावः क्षेत्रसाता वृत्रहत्येषु पूरुं ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ vītá-havyam ǀ prá ǀ āvaḥ ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ su-dā́sam ǀprá ǀ páuru-kutsim ǀ trasádasyum ǀ āvaḥ ǀ kṣétra-sātā ǀ vṛtra-hátyeṣu ǀ pūrúm ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Undaunted (Indra), you had protected with all your protectionsSudāsa, the offerer of oblations; youhave protected in battles with enemies for the possession of the earthTrasadasyu, the son ofPurukutsa, andPuru.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं धृ॑ष्णो धृष॒ता वी॒तह॑व्यं॒ प्रावो॒ विश्वा॑भिरू॒तिभि॑: सु॒दास॑म् । प्र पौरु॑कुत्सिं त्र॒सद॑स्युमाव॒: क्षेत्र॑साता वृत्र॒हत्ये॑षु पू॒रुम्

devanagari.text: त्वं नृभिर्नृमणो देववीतौ भूरीणि वृत्रा हर्यश्व हंसि ।त्वं नि दस्युं चुमुरिं धुनिं चास्वापयो दभीतये सुहंतु ॥

transliteration.text: tvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ nṛ-manaḥ ǀ devá-vītau ǀ bhū́rīṇi ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ hari-aśva ǀ haṃsi ǀtvám ǀ ní ǀ dásyum ǀ cúmurim ǀ dhúnim ǀ ca ǀ ásvāpayaḥ ǀ dabhī́taye ǀ su-hántu ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “You, the lord of horses, who are honoured by men, have destroyed, along with theMaruts, numerousenemies at the sacrifice of the gods; you have put to sleep with the thunderbolt theDasyus, Chumuri, andDhuni,on behalf ofDabhīti.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं नृभि॑र्नृमणो दे॒ववी॑तौ॒ भूरी॑णि वृ॒त्रा ह॑र्यश्व हंसि । त्वं नि दस्युं॒ चुमु॑रिं॒ धुनिं॒ चास्वा॑पयो द॒भीत॑ये सु॒हन्तु॑

devanagari.text: तव च्यौत्नानि वज्रहस्त तानि नव यत्पुरो नवतिं च सद्यः ।निवेशने शततमाविवेषीरहंच वृत्रं नमुचिमुताहन् ॥

transliteration.text: táva ǀ cyautnā́ni ǀ vajra-hasta ǀ tā́ni ǀ náva ǀ yát ǀ púraḥ ǀ navatím ǀ ca ǀ sadyáḥ ǀni-véśane ǀ śata-tamā́ ǀ aviveṣīḥ ǀ áhan ǀ ca ǀ vṛtrám ǀ námucim ǀ utá ǀ ahan ǁ

Sukta 19.translation: “Such, wielder of the thunderbolt, are your mighty powers, that when you had quickly destroyed ninetyand nine cities, you have occupied the hundredth as a plural ce of abode; you have slainVṛtra, you have also slainNamuci.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तव॑ च्यौ॒त्नानि॑ वज्रहस्त॒ तानि॒ नव॒ यत्पुरो॑ नव॒तिं च॑ स॒द्यः । नि॒वेश॑ने शतत॒मावि॑वेषी॒रह॑ञ्च वृ॒त्रं नमु॑चिमु॒ताह॑न्

devanagari.text: सना ता त इंद्र भोजनानि रातहव्याय दाशुषे सुदासे ।वृष्णे ते हरी वृषणा युनज्मि व्यंतु ब्रह्माणि पुरुशाक वाजं ॥

Sukta 19.translation: “Your favours,Indra, toSudāsa, the donor (of offerings), the presenter of oblations, are infinite;showerer (of benefits), I yoke for you (your vigorous) steeds; may our prayers reach you who are mighty, towhom many rites are addressed.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सना॒ ता त॑ इन्द्र॒ भोज॑नानि रा॒तह॑व्याय दा॒शुषे॑ सु॒दासे॑ । वृष्णे॑ ते॒ हरी॒ वृष॑णा युनज्मि॒ व्यन्तु॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि पुरुशाक॒ वाज॑म्

devanagari.text: मा ते अस्यां सहसावन्परिष्टावघाय भूम हरिवः परादै ।त्रायस्व नोऽवृकेभिर्वरूथैस्तव प्रियासः सूरिषु स्याम ॥

Sukta 19.translation: “PowerfulIndra, lord of horses, let us not be exposed at this ceremony, addressed to you, to themurderous despoiler; protect us with impregnable defences; may we be held dear among your worshippers.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा ते॑ अ॒स्यां स॑हसाव॒न्परि॑ष्टाव॒घाय॑ भूम हरिवः परा॒दै । त्राय॑स्व नोऽवृ॒केभि॒र्वरू॑थै॒स्तव॑ प्रि॒यास॑: सू॒रिषु॑ स्याम

devanagari.text: प्रियास इत्ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरो मदेम शरणे सखायः ।नि तुर्वशं नि याद्वं शिशीह्यतिथिग्वाय शंस्यं करिष्यन् ॥

Sukta 19.translation: “May we,Maghavan, leaders in your adoration, regarded as dear friends, be happy in our homes; aboutto bestow felicity upon Atithigvan, humiliateTurvaśa; (humiliate) the son ofYadu.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रि॒यास॒ इत्ते॑ मघवन्न॒भिष्टौ॒ नरो॑ मदेम शर॒णे सखा॑यः । नि तु॒र्वशं॒ नि याद्वं॑ शिशीह्यतिथि॒ग्वाय॒ शंस्यं॑ करि॒ष्यन्

devanagari.text: सद्यश्चिन्नु ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरः शंसंत्युक्थशास उक्था ।ये ते हवेभिर्वि पणीँरदाशन्नस्मान्वृणीष्व युज्याय तस्मै ॥

Sukta 19.translation: “The leader (of rites), reciters of prayers, offer,Maghavan, prayers devoutly for your adoration; they bytheir praises have appropriated the wealth of the niggards; select us (as the objects) of your friendship.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒द्यश्चि॒न्नु ते म॑घवन्न॒भिष्टौ॒ नर॑: शंसन्त्युक्थ॒शास॑ उ॒क्था । ये ते॒ हवे॑भि॒र्वि प॒णीँरदा॑शन्न॒स्मान्वृ॑णीष्व॒ युज्या॑य॒ तस्मै॑

devanagari.text: एते स्तोमा नरां नृतम तुभ्यमस्मद्र्यंचो ददतो मघानि ।तेषामिंद्र वृत्रहत्ये शिवो भूः सखा च शूरोऽविता च नृणां ॥

Sukta 19.translation: “Chief leader (of rites), these praises of man addressed to you revert to us, who are the offerers of(sacrificial) riches; do you be propitious to such men, (Indra), in conflicts with enemies; be their friend, their hero,and protector.”
Sukta 19.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ते स्तोमा॑ न॒रां नृ॑तम॒ तुभ्य॑मस्म॒द्र्य॑ञ्चो॒ दद॑तो म॒घानि॑ । तेषा॑मिन्द्र वृत्र॒हत्ये॑ शि॒वो भू॒: सखा॑ च॒ शूरो॑ऽवि॒ता च॑ नृ॒णाम्

devanagari.text: नू इंद्र शूर स्तवमान ऊती ब्रह्मजूतस्तन्वा वावृधस्व ।उप नो वाजान्मिमीह्युप स्तीन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

Sukta 20.translation: “Indra, dilating in bulk, is the slayer ofVṛtra; the hero defends his worshipper promptly with hisprotection, whether he be the giver of dominion toSudāsa, or the donor repeatedly of wealth to the offerer (ofoblations).”

Sukta 20.translation: “A warrior who turns not back in battle, a combatant, one engaged in tumults, a hero, victorious over(his) foes from birth, invincible, of great vigour, thisIndrascatters (hostile) hosts and slays all (his) adversaries.”

Sukta 20.translation: “OpulentIndra, you have filled both heaven and earth with your magnitutde, your energies; Indra, thelord of horses, brandishing the thunderbolt, is gratified at sacrifices by the (sacrificial) food.”

Sukta 20.translation: “(His) progenitor begotIndra, the showerer (of benefits) for (the purpose of) war; his mother brought himforth the benefactor of man; the leader of armies who is chief over men, he is the lord, the conqueror, therecoverer of the kine, the subduer of foes.”

Sukta 20.translation: “That (wealth)Indra, which the prior has given to the posterior; which the elder may accept from theyounger; with which (the son) yet living dwells far away (separated from his father), confer, wonderful Indra, suchprecious riches upon us.”

Sukta 20.translation: “May the man who is dear to you,Indra, present (oblations); may he be your friend, wielder of thethunderbolt, he (assiduous) in donations; may we be abounding in food through this favour of you who aredevoid of cruelty, (may we be in the enjoyment of) a dwelling giving shelter to men.”

Sukta 20.translation: “For you,Maghavan, this showeringSoma(libation) cries aloud; to you the worshipper has recitedpraises; the desire of riches has fallen upon thine adorer, do you, therefore,Śakra, bestow quickly upon uswealth.”

Sukta 20.translation: “Enable us,Indra, (to partake of) food granted by you, as well as those who, opulent (in sacrificialpresentations), spontaneously offer (you oblations); may there be power in thine adorer (to repeat) manylaudations; and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
