Sukta 21.translation: “Bright sacrificial food mixed with curds and milk has been poured out;Indradelights in it from his birth;lord of bay horses, we wake you up with sacrifices, acknowledge our praises in the exhilaration of theSoma.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: असा॑वि दे॒वं गोऋ॑जीक॒मन्धो॒ न्य॑स्मि॒न्निन्द्रो॑ ज॒नुषे॑मुवोच । बोधा॑मसि त्वा हर्यश्व य॒ज्ञैर्बोधा॑ न॒: स्तोम॒मन्ध॑सो॒ मदे॑षु

Sukta 21.translation: “They repair to the sacrifice, they strew the sacred grass; the (grinding) stones at the ceremony are ofdifficulty suppressed noise; famous priests, whose voices are heard far off, bring the stones from the interior ofthe dwelling.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र य॑न्ति य॒ज्ञं वि॒पय॑न्ति ब॒र्हिः सो॑म॒मादो॑ वि॒दथे॑ दु॒ध्रवा॑चः । न्यु॑ भ्रियन्ते य॒शसो॑ गृ॒भादा दू॒रउ॑पब्दो॒ वृष॑णो नृ॒षाच॑:

Sukta 21.translation: “You, hero, have enabled the many waters arrested by Ahi to flow; by you the rivers rushed forth likecharioteers; all created worlds trembled through fear of you.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वमि॑न्द्र॒ स्रवि॑त॒वा अ॒पस्क॒: परि॑ष्ठिता॒ अहि॑ना शूर पू॒र्वीः । त्वद्वा॑वक्रे र॒थ्यो॒३॒॑ न धेना॒ रेज॑न्ते॒ विश्वा॑ कृ॒त्रिमा॑णि भी॒षा

Sukta 21.translation: “The formidable (Indra), knowing all actions beneficial to man, intimidated those (asuras) by hisweapons; Indra, exuling shook their cities; armed with his thunderbolt he slew them in his might.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भी॒मो वि॑वे॒षायु॑धेभिरेषा॒मपां॑सि॒ विश्वा॒ नर्या॑णि वि॒द्वान् । इन्द्र॒: पुरो॒ जर्हृ॑षाणो॒ वि दू॑धो॒द्वि वज्र॑हस्तो महि॒ना ज॑घान

Sukta 21.translation: “Let not thrākṣasas,Indra, do us harm; let not the evil spirits do harm to our progeny, most powerful(Indra); let the sovereign lord, (Indra), exert himself (in the restraint) of disorderly beings, so that the unchastemay not disturb our rite.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न या॒तव॑ इन्द्र जूजुवुर्नो॒ न वन्द॑ना शविष्ठ वे॒द्याभि॑: । स श॑र्धद॒र्यो विषु॑णस्य ज॒न्तोर्मा शि॒श्नदे॑वा॒ अपि॑ गुॠ॒तं न॑:

Sukta 21.translation: “You,Indra, by your function, preside over the beings (of earth); all the regions (of the world) do notsurpass your magnitude; by thine own strength you have slainVṛtra; no enemy has effected your destruction inbattle.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि क्रत्वे॑न्द्र भू॒रध॒ ज्मन्न ते॑ विव्यङ्महि॒मानं॒ रजां॑सि । स्वेना॒ हि वृ॒त्रं शव॑सा ज॒घन्थ॒ न शत्रु॒रन्तं॑ विविदद्यु॒धा ते॑

Sukta 21.translation: “The older deities have confessed your vigour superior to their destructive strength,Indrahavingsubdued his foes, gives the rich spoils (to his worshippers); they invoke Indra to obtain food.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दे॒वाश्चि॑त्ते असु॒र्या॑य॒ पूर्वेऽनु॑ क्ष॒त्राय॑ ममिरे॒ सहां॑सि । इन्द्रो॑ म॒घानि॑ दयते वि॒षह्येन्द्रं॒ वाज॑स्य जोहुवन्त सा॒तौ

Sukta 21.translation: “The worshipper has invoked you the sovereignIndra, for protection; protector of many, you have beento us the guardian of great fortune; be our defender against every overpowering (assailant).”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: की॒रिश्चि॒द्धि त्वामव॑से जु॒हावेशा॑नमिन्द्र॒ सौभ॑गस्य॒ भूरे॑: । अवो॑ बभूथ शतमूते अ॒स्मे अ॑भिक्ष॒त्तुस्त्वाव॑तो वरू॒ता

Sukta 21.translation: “May we, daily increasing in reverence, be (regarded),Indra, (as) your friends; through the protection ofyou, surpasser in greatness, may (your worshippers) repulse the attack of the foe in battle, the strength of themalevolent.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सखा॑यस्त इन्द्र वि॒श्वह॑ स्याम नमोवृ॒धासो॑ महि॒ना त॑रुत्र । व॒न्वन्तु॑ स्मा॒ तेऽव॑सा समी॒के॒३॒॑ऽभी॑तिम॒र्यो व॒नुषां॒ शवां॑सि

Sukta 21.translation: “Enable us,Indra, (to partake of) food granted by you, as well as those who, opulent (in sacrificialpresentations), spontaneously offer the (oblations); may there be ability in thine adorer (to repeat) my laudations;and do you ever cherish us wiḥ blessings.”
Sukta 21.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स न॑ इन्द्र॒ त्वय॑ताया इ॒षे धा॒स्त्मना॑ च॒ ये म॒घवा॑नो जु॒नन्ति॑ । वस्वी॒ षु ते॑ जरि॒त्रे अ॑स्तु श॒क्तिर्यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: पिबा सोममिंद्र मंदतु त्वा यं ते सुषाव हर्यश्वाद्रिः ।सोतुर्बाहुभ्यां सुयतो नार्वा ॥
पिब । सोमम् । इन्द्र । मन्दतु । त्वा । यम् । ते । सुसाव । हरिऽअश्व । अद्रिः ।सोतुः । बाहुऽभ्याम् । सुऽयतः । न । अर्वा ॥

transliteration.text: píba ǀ sómam ǀ indra ǀ mándatu ǀ tvā ǀ yám ǀ te ǀ susā́va ǀ hari-aśva ǀ ádriḥ ǀsotúḥ ǀ bāhú-bhyām ǀ sú-yataḥ ǀ ná ǀ árvā ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “Drink,Indra, theSoma; may it exhilarate you, that which the stone tightly held like a horse (by thereins), by the arms of the grinder, has expressed, lord of bay horses for you.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पिबा॒ सोम॑मिन्द्र॒ मन्द॑तु त्वा॒ यं ते॑ सु॒षाव॑ हर्य॒श्वाद्रि॑: । सो॒तुर्बा॒हुभ्यां॒ सुय॑तो॒ नार्वा॑

devanagari.text: यस्ते मदो युज्यश्चारुरस्ति येन वृत्राणि हर्यश्व हंसि ।स त्वामिंद्र प्रभूवसो ममत्तु ॥
यः । ते । मदः । युज्यः । चारुः । अस्ति । येन । वृत्राणि । हरिऽअश्व । हंसि ।सः । त्वाम् । इन्द्र । प्रभुवसो इति प्रभुऽवसो । ममत्तु ॥

transliteration.text: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ mádaḥ ǀ yújyaḥ ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀ ásti ǀ yéna ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ hari-aśva ǀ háṃsi ǀsáḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ indra ǀ prabhuvaso íti prabhu-vaso ǀ mamattu ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “May the exhilaratingSomawhich is fit for and suitable to you, by which, lord of bay horses, you slayVṛtra, exhilarate you,Indra, abounding in riches.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यस्ते॒ मदो॒ युज्य॒श्चारु॒रस्ति॒ येन॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ हर्यश्व॒ हंसि॑ । स त्वामि॑न्द्र प्रभूवसो ममत्तु

devanagari.text: बोधा सु मे मघवन्वाचमेमां यां ते वसिष्ठो अर्चति प्रशस्तिं ।इमा ब्रह्म सधमादे जुषस्व ॥
बोध । सु । मे । मघऽवन् । वाचम् । आ । इमाम् । याम् । ते । वसिष्ठः । अर्चति । प्रऽशस्तिम् ।इमा । ब्रह्म । सधऽमादे । जुषस्व ॥

transliteration.text: bódha ǀ sú ǀ me ǀ magha-van ǀ vā́cam ǀ ā́ ǀ imā́m ǀ yā́m ǀ te ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ árcati ǀ prá-śastim ǀimā́ ǀ bráhma ǀ sadha-mā́de ǀ juṣasva ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “Understand thoroughly,Maghavan, this my speech, this praise of you, whichVasiṣṭharecites; bepleased by these prayers at the sacrifice.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: बोधा॒ सु मे॑ मघव॒न्वाच॒मेमां यां ते॒ वसि॑ष्ठो॒ अर्च॑ति॒ प्रश॑स्तिम् । इ॒मा ब्रह्म॑ सध॒मादे॑ जुषस्व

devanagari.text: श्रुधी हवं विपिपानस्याद्रेर्बोधा विप्रस्यार्चतो मनीषां ।कृष्वा दुवांस्यंतमा सचेमा ॥
श्रुधि । हवम् । विऽपिपानस्य । अद्रेः । बोध । विप्रस्य । अर्चतः । मनीषाम् ।कृष्व । दुवांसि । अन्तमा । सचा । इमा ॥

transliteration.text: śrudhí ǀ hávam ǀ vi-pipānásya ǀ ádreḥ ǀ bódha ǀ víprasya ǀ árcataḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀkṛṣvá ǀ dúvāṃsi ǀ ántamā ǀ sácā ǀ imā́ ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “Hear the invocation of the (grinding) stone, (of me) repeatedly drinking (theSoma), comprehend thehymn of the adoring sage, and, friendly (with us), take to your near consideration these adorations.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श्रु॒धी हवं॑ विपिपा॒नस्याद्रे॒र्बोधा॒ विप्र॒स्यार्च॑तो मनी॒षाम् । कृ॒ष्वा दुवां॒स्यन्त॑मा॒ सचे॒मा

devanagari.text: न ते गिरो अपि मृष्ये तुरस्य न सुष्टुतिमसुर्यस्य विद्वान् ।सदा ते नाम स्वयशो विवक्मि ॥
न । ते । गिरः । अपि । मृष्ये । तुरस्य । न । सुऽस्तुतिम् । असुर्यस्य । विद्वान् ।सदा । ते । नाम । स्वऽयशः । विवक्मि ॥

transliteration.text: ná ǀ te ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ápi ǀ mṛṣye ǀ turásya ǀ ná ǀ su-stutím ǀ asuryásya ǀ vidvā́n ǀsádā ǀ te ǀ nā́ma ǀ sva-yaśaḥ ǀ vivakmi ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “Knowing of your strength, I refrain not from the praise nor from the glorification of you, the destroyer (offoes), but ever proclaim your especial care.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न ते॒ गिरो॒ अपि॑ मृष्ये तु॒रस्य॒ न सु॑ष्टु॒तिम॑सु॒र्य॑स्य वि॒द्वान् । सदा॑ ते॒ नाम॑ स्वयशो विवक्मि

devanagari.text: भूरि हि ते सवना मानुषेषु भूरि मनीषी हवते त्वामित् ।मारे अस्मन्मघवंज्योक्कः ॥
भूरि । हि । ते । सवना । मानुषेषु । भूरि । मनीषी । हवते । त्वाम् । इत् ।मा । आरे । अस्मत् । मघऽवन् । ज्योक् । करिति कः ॥

transliteration.text: bhū́ri ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ sávanā ǀ mā́nuṣeṣu ǀ bhū́ri ǀ manīṣī́ ǀ havate ǀ tvā́m ǀ ít ǀmā́ ǀ āré ǀ asmát ǀ magha-van ǀ jyók ǀ karíti kaḥ ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “Many are the sacrifices offered,Maghavan, to you among mankind; constantly does worshipper indeedinvoke you; therefore be not far nor be a long time from us.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भूरि॒ हि ते॒ सव॑ना॒ मानु॑षेषु॒ भूरि॑ मनी॒षी ह॑वते॒ त्वामित् । मारे अ॒स्मन्म॑घव॒ञ्ज्योक्क॑:

devanagari.text: तुभ्येदिमा सवना शूर विश्वा तुभ्यं ब्रह्माणि वर्धना कृणोमि ।त्वं नृभिर्हव्यो विश्वधासि ॥
तुभ्य । इत् । इमा । सवना । शूर । विश्वा । तुभ्यम् । ब्रह्माणि । वर्धना । कृणोमि ।त्वम् । नृऽभिः । हव्यः । विश्वधा । असि ॥

transliteration.text: túbhya ǀ ít ǀ imā́ ǀ sávanā ǀ śūra ǀ víśvā ǀ túbhyam ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ várdhanā ǀ kṛṇomi ǀtvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ viśvádhā ǀ asi ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “To you, hero, I indeed offer these sacrifices, to you I address these elevating praises; you are to be inall ways invoked by the leaders (of rites).”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तुभ्येदि॒मा सव॑ना शूर॒ विश्वा॒ तुभ्यं॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि॒ वर्ध॑ना कृणोमि । त्वं नृभि॒र्हव्यो॑ वि॒श्वधा॑सि

devanagari.text: नू चिन्नु ते मन्यमानस्य दस्मोदश्नुवंति महिमानमुग्र ।न वीर्यमिंद्र ते न राधः ॥
नु । चित् । नु । ते । मन्यमानस्य । दस्म । उत् । अश्नुवन्ति । महिमानम् । उग्र ।न । वीर्यम् । इन्द्र । ते । न । राधः ॥

transliteration.text: nú ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ mányamānasya ǀ dasma ǀ út ǀ aśnuvanti ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ ugra ǀná ǀ vīryám ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ ná ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “Indra, of goodly aspect, none attain the greatness of you who are to be honoured, nor, fierce Indra, yourheroism, nor your wealth.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नू चि॒न्नु ते॒ मन्य॑मानस्य द॒स्मोद॑श्नुवन्ति महि॒मान॑मुग्र । न वी॒र्य॑मिन्द्र ते॒ न राध॑:

devanagari.text: ये च पूर्व ऋषयो ये च नूत्ना इंद्र ब्रह्माणि जनयंत विप्राः ।अस्मे ते संतु सख्या शिवानि यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
ये । च । पूर्वे । ऋषयः । ये । च । नूत्नाः । इन्द्र । ब्रह्माणि । जनयन्त । विप्राः ।अस्मे इति । ते । सन्तु । सख्या । शिवानि । यूयम् । पात । स्वस्तिऽभिः । सदा । नः ॥

transliteration.text: yé ǀ ca ǀ pū́rve ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ nū́tnāḥ ǀ índra ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ janáyanta ǀ víprāḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ te ǀ santu ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ śivā́ni ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 22.translation: “May your auspicious regards,Indra, be directed towards us, as they have been to those pious sages,ancient or recent, who have originated (your) praises, and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 22.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ये च॒ पूर्व॒ ऋष॑यो॒ ये च॒ नूत्ना॒ इन्द्र॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि ज॒नय॑न्त॒ विप्रा॑: । अ॒स्मे ते॑ सन्तु स॒ख्या शि॒वानि॑ यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: उदु ब्रह्माण्यैरत श्रवस्येंद्रं समर्ये महया वसिष्ठ ।आ यो विश्वानि शवसा ततानोपश्रोता म ईवतो वचांसि ॥
उत् । ऊं इति । ब्रह्माणि । ऐरत । श्रवस्या । इन्द्रम् । सऽमर्ये । महय । वसिष्ठ ।आ । यः । विश्वानि । शवसा । ततान । उपऽश्रोता । मे । ईवतः । वचांसि ॥

transliteration.text: út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ airata ǀ śravasyā́ ǀ índram ǀ sa-maryé ǀ mahaya ǀ vasiṣṭha ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ śávasā ǀ tatā́na ǀ upa-śrotā́ ǀ me ǀ ī́vataḥ ǀ vácāṃsi ǁ

Sukta 23.translation: “(The sages) have offered prayers to (Indra) for food, worship Indra,Vasiṣṭhaat the sacrifice; may thatIndra who has spread out all (the regions) by his might, be the hearer of my words when approaching him.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उदु॒ ब्रह्मा॑ण्यैरत श्रव॒स्येन्द्रं॑ सम॒र्ये म॑हया वसिष्ठ । आ यो विश्वा॑नि॒ शव॑सा त॒तानो॑पश्रो॒ता म॒ ईव॑तो॒ वचां॑सि

devanagari.text: अयामि घोष इंद्र देवजामिरिरज्यंत यच्छुरुधो विवाचि ।नहि स्वमायुश्चिकिते जनेषु तानीदंहांस्यति पर्ष्यस्मान् ॥

Sukta 23.translation: “When,Indra, the plural nts grow up, the sound (of praise) acceptable to the gods, (uttered) by theworshipper, has been raised; by no one among men, is his own life understood; convey us beyond all those sins(by which life is shortened).”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अया॑मि॒ घोष॑ इन्द्र दे॒वजा॑मिरिर॒ज्यन्त॒ यच्छु॒रुधो॒ विवा॑चि । न॒हि स्वमायु॑श्चिकि॒ते जने॑षु॒ तानीदंहां॒स्यति॑ पर्ष्य॒स्मान्

devanagari.text: युजे रथं गवेषणं हरिभ्यामुप ब्रह्माणि जुजुषाणमस्थुः ।वि बाधिष्ट स्य रोदसी महित्वेंद्रो वृत्राण्यप्रती जघन्वान् ॥

Sukta 23.translation: “I harness (by praises) the kine-bestowing chariot (ofIndra) with his horses; (my) prayers have reachedhim who is plural ased (by devotion); he has surpassed in magnitude heaven and earth, slaying the unresistingenemies.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यु॒जे रथं॑ ग॒वेष॑णं॒ हरि॑भ्या॒मुप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि जुजुषा॒णम॑स्थुः । वि बा॑धिष्ट॒ स्य रोद॑सी महि॒त्वेन्द्रो॑ वृ॒त्राण्य॑प्र॒ती ज॑घ॒न्वान्

devanagari.text: आपश्चित्पिप्युः स्तर्यो न गावो नक्षन्नृतं जरितारस्त इंद्र ।याहि वायुर्न नियुतो नो अच्छा त्वं हि धीभिर्दयसे वि वाजान् ॥
आपः । चित् । पिप्युः । स्तर्यः । न । गावः । नक्षन् । ऋतम् । जरितारः । ते । इन्द्र ।याहि । वायुः । न । निऽयुतः । नः । अच्छ । त्वम् । हि । धीभिः । दयसे । वि । वाजान् ॥

transliteration.text: ā́paḥ ǀ cit ǀ pipyuḥ ǀ staryáḥ ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ nákṣan ǀ ṛtám ǀ jaritā́raḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀyāhí ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ ná ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ áccha ǀ tvám ǀ hí ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ dáyase ǀ ví ǀ vā́jān ǁ

Sukta 23.translation: “May the waters increase like young; may your worshippers,Indra, possess water (in abundance); comelike the wind with theNiyutsteeds, for you, (propitiated) by holy rites, verily bestow upon us food.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आप॑श्चित्पिप्युः स्त॒र्यो॒३॒॑ न गावो॒ नक्ष॑न्नृ॒तं ज॑रि॒तार॑स्त इन्द्र । या॒हि वा॒युर्न नि॒युतो॑ नो॒ अच्छा॒ त्वं हि धी॒भिर्दय॑से॒ वि वाजा॑न्

devanagari.text: ते त्वा मदा इंद्र मादयंतु शुष्मिणं तुविराधसं जरित्रे ।एको देवत्रा दयसे हि मर्तानस्मिंछूर सवने मादयस्व ॥

transliteration.text: té ǀ tvā ǀ mádāḥ ǀ indra ǀ mādayantu ǀ śuṣmíṇam ǀ tuvi-rā́dhasam ǀ jaritré ǀékaḥ ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ dáyase ǀ hí ǀ mártān ǀ asmín ǀ śūra ǀ sávane ǀ mādayasva ǁ

Sukta 23.translation: “May these inebriating draughts exhilarate you,Indra; bestow upon the praiser (a son vigorous andwealthy); for you alone among the gods are compassionate to mortals; be exhilarated here at this sacrifice.”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते त्वा॒ मदा॑ इन्द्र मादयन्तु शु॒ष्मिणं॑ तुवि॒राध॑सं जरि॒त्रे । एको॑ देव॒त्रा दय॑से॒ हि मर्ता॑न॒स्मिञ्छू॑र॒ सव॑ने मादयस्व

devanagari.text: एवेदिंद्रं वृषणं वज्रबाहुं वसिष्ठासो अभ्यर्चंत्यर्कैः ।स नः स्तुतो वीरवत्पातु गोमद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

Sukta 23.translation: “In this manner theVasiṣṭhasglorify with hymnsIndra, the showerer, the bearer of the thunderbolt; mayhe so glorified grant us wealth, comprisingmaleposterity and cattle; and do you ever cherish us with blessingṣ”
Sukta 23.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वेदिन्द्रं॒ वृष॑णं॒ वज्र॑बाहुं॒ वसि॑ष्ठासो अ॒भ्य॑र्चन्त्य॒र्कैः । स न॑: स्तु॒तो वी॒रव॑द्धातु॒ गोम॑द्यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 24.translation: “A plural ce has been prepared for you in the sacrificial chamber; proceed to it, invoked of many, along withthe leaders (of rites theMaruts), inasmuch as you are our protector, (promote our) prosperity; grant us riches; beexhilarated by theSoma.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: योनि॑ष्ट इन्द्र॒ सद॑ने अकारि॒ तमा नृभि॑: पुरुहूत॒ प्र या॑हि । असो॒ यथा॑ नोऽवि॒ता वृ॒धे च॒ ददो॒ वसू॑नि म॒मद॑श्च॒ सोमै॑:

Sukta 24.translation: “Your purpose,Indra, is apprehended, you who are mighty in the two (worlds); theSomais effused; thesweet juices are poured (into the vessels); this perfect praise uttered with loosened tongue propitiates Indra withrepeated invocations.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: गृ॒भी॒तं ते॒ मन॑ इन्द्र द्वि॒बर्हा॑: सु॒तः सोम॒: परि॑षिक्ता॒ मधू॑नि । विसृ॑ष्टधेना भरते सुवृ॒क्तिरि॒यमिन्द्रं॒ जोहु॑वती मनी॒षा

Sukta 24.translation: “Come, Rijishin, from the sky, or from the firmament, to this sacred gras, to drink theSoma; let yourhorses bear you who are vigorous to my presence to (receive my) praise and for (thine) exhilaration.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ नो॑ दि॒व आ पृ॑थि॒व्या ऋ॑जीषिन्नि॒दं ब॒र्हिः सो॑म॒पेया॑य याहि । वह॑न्तु त्वा॒ हर॑यो म॒द्र्य॑ञ्चमाङ्गू॒षमच्छा॑ त॒वसं॒ मदा॑य

Sukta 24.translation: “Lord of bay steeds, propitiated by our praise, come to us with all your protections, sharing insatisfaction, handsome-chinned, with the ancient (Maruts), overthrowing repeatedly (your) foes, and granting usa strong and vigorous (son).”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ नो॒ विश्वा॑भिरू॒तिभि॑: स॒जोषा॒ ब्रह्म॑ जुषा॒णो ह॑र्यश्व याहि । वरी॑वृज॒त्स्थवि॑रेभिः सुशिप्रा॒स्मे दध॒द्वृष॑णं॒ शुष्म॑मिन्द्र

Sukta 24.translation: “This invogorating praise, like a horse attached, to car, has been addressed to you who are mighty andfierce, the up-bearer (of the world); this thine adorer desires of you,Indra, riches; do you grant us sustenancenotorious as the sky in heaven.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष स्तोमो॑ म॒ह उ॒ग्राय॒ वाहे॑ धु॒री॒३॒॑वात्यो॒ न वा॒जय॑न्नधायि । इन्द्र॑ त्वा॒यम॒र्क ई॑ट्टे॒ वसू॑नां दि॒वी॑व॒ द्यामधि॑ न॒: श्रोम॑तं धाः

Sukta 24.translation: “In this manner,Indra, satisfy us (with the gift) of desirable (wealth); may we repeatedly experience yougreat giver; bestow upon us who are opulent (in offerings) food withmaledescendants; do you ever cherish uswith blessings.”
Sukta 24.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा न॑ इन्द्र॒ वार्य॑स्य पूर्धि॒ प्र ते॑ म॒हीं सु॑म॒तिं वे॑विदाम । इषं॑ पिन्व म॒घव॑द्भ्यः सु॒वीरां॑ यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: आ ते मह इंद्रोत्युग्र समन्यवो यत्समरंत सेनाः ।पताति दिद्युन्नर्यस्य बाह्वोर्मा ते मनो विष्वद्र्यग्वि चारीत् ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ te ǀ maháḥ ǀ indra ǀ ūtī́ ǀ ugra ǀ sá-manyavaḥ ǀ yát ǀ sam-áranta ǀ sénāḥ ǀpátāti ǀ didyút ǀ náryasya ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ viṣvadryák ǀ ví ǀ cārīt ǁ

Sukta 25.translation: “FierceIndra, when animated by like fierce armies, encounter them; let the bright (weapon) wielded bythe arms of you who are mighty and the friend of man descend for our protection; let not your all-pervading mindwander (away from us).”
Sukta 25.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ ते॑ म॒ह इ॑न्द्रो॒त्यु॑ग्र॒ सम॑न्यवो॒ यत्स॒मर॑न्त॒ सेना॑: । पता॑ति दि॒द्युन्नर्य॑स्य बा॒ह्वोर्मा ते॒ मनो॑ विष्व॒द्र्य१॒॑ग्वि चा॑रीत्

devanagari.text: नि दुर्ग इंद्र श्नथिह्यमित्रानभि ये नो मर्तासो अमंति ।आरे तं शंसं कृणुहि निनित्सोरा नो भर संभरणं वसूनां ॥

Sukta 25.translation: “Destroy,Indra, our adversaries in battle, those men who overpower us; remove far from us the calumnyof the reviler; bring to us abundance of treasures.”
Sukta 25.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नि दु॒र्ग इ॑न्द्र श्नथिह्य॒मित्राँ॑ अ॒भि ये नो॒ मर्ता॑सो अ॒मन्ति॑ । आ॒रे तं शंसं॑ कृणुहि निनि॒त्सोरा नो॑ भर स॒म्भर॑णं॒ वसू॑नाम्

devanagari.text: शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु ।जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥

transliteration.text: śatám ǀ te ǀ śiprin ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ su-dā́se ǀ sahásram ǀ śáṃsāḥ ǀ utá ǀ rātíḥ ǀ astu ǀjahí ǀ vádhaḥ ǀ vanúṣaḥ ǀ mártyasya ǀ asmé íti ǀ dyumnám ǀ ádhi ǀ rátnam ǀ ca ǀ dhehi ǁ

Sukta 25.translation: “May hundreds of your protections, handsome-chinned, be (secured) to the liberal donor (of oblations);may thousands of blessing be bestowed (upon me) as well as wealth; cast the fatal weapon on the mischievousmortal; grant us food and wealth.”
Sukta 25.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श॒तं ते॑ शिप्रिन्नू॒तय॑: सु॒दासे॑ स॒हस्रं॒ शंसा॑ उ॒त रा॒तिर॑स्तु । ज॒हि वध॑र्व॒नुषो॒ मर्त्य॑स्या॒स्मे द्यु॒म्नमधि॒ रत्नं॑ च धेहि

devanagari.text: त्वावतो हींद्र क्रत्वे अस्मि त्वावतोऽवितुः शूर रातौ ।विश्वेदहानि तविषीव उग्रँ ओकः कृणुष्व हरिवो न मर्धीः ॥

Sukta 25.translation: “I am (in dependence),Indra, upon the acts of such as you are, upon the liberality of a protector, hero,such as you; vigorous and fierce Indra, give us a dwelling for all our days; lord of bay steeds, do us no harm.”
Sukta 25.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वाव॑तो॒ ही॑न्द्र॒ क्रत्वे॒ अस्मि॒ त्वाव॑तोऽवि॒तुः शू॑र रा॒तौ । विश्वेदहा॑नि तविषीव उग्रँ॒ ओक॑: कृणुष्व हरिवो॒ न म॑र्धीः

devanagari.text: कुत्सा एते हर्यश्वाय शूषमिंद्रे सहो देवजूतमियानाः ।सत्रा कृधि सुहना शूर वृत्रा वयं तरुत्राः सनुयाम वाजं ॥

Sukta 25.translation: “These (Vasiṣṭhas) are offering grateful (adoration) to the lord of bay steeds, soliciting the strengthassigned by the gods toIndra; make our enemies, Indra, easy to be overcome, and may we, safe from peril,enjoy abundance.”

Sukta 25.translation: “In this manner,Indra, satisfy us with the gift of desirable (wealth); may we repeatedly experience yourgreat favour; bestow upon us who are opulent in offerings food withmaledescendants; do you ever cherish uswith blessings.”
Sukta 25.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा न॑ इन्द्र॒ वार्य॑स्य पूर्धि॒ प्र ते॑ म॒हीं सु॑म॒तिं वे॑विदाम । इषं॑ पिन्व म॒घव॑द्भ्यः सु॒वीरां॑ यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 26.translation: “TheSomauneffused delights notIndra; the effused juices plural ase notMaghavan, unaccompanied byprayer; therefore, I offer to him praise that he may be plural ased with; that, like a prince, he may listen to a novel(strain).”

Sukta 26.translation: “TheSomaeffused with reiterated prayer delightsIndra; the effused juices, (offered) with repeatedpraise, (exhilarate)Maghavan; therefore, (the priests), combining together and making like exertion, invoke Indrafor protection, as sons (apply) to a father.”

Sukta 26.translation: “Such exploits as his worshippers, when theSomais effused, proclaim that he has achieved, let himnow perform; mayIndra, equal (to the task) and unaided, possess all the riches (of theasuras) as a husband hiswives.”
Sukta 26.sanskrit_wisdomlib: च॒कार॒ ता कृ॒णव॑न्नू॒नम॒न्या यानि॑ ब्रु॒वन्ति॑ वे॒धस॑: सु॒तेषु॑ । जनी॑रिव॒ पति॒रेक॑: समा॒नो नि मा॑मृजे॒ पुर॒ इन्द्र॒: सु सर्वा॑:

Sukta 26.translation: “Such have they proclaimed him;Indrais still celebrated as the distributor of riches, the transporter(beyond calamity), of whom many and emulous are the protections; may acceptable benefits attend us.”

Sukta 26.translation: “Thus doesVasiṣṭhaglorifyIndra, the showerer (of benefits) upon the worshippers for the preservationof mankind; bestow upon us, (Indra), thousands of viands; do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 26.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा वसि॑ष्ठ॒ इन्द्र॑मू॒तये॒ नॄन्कृ॑ष्टी॒नां वृ॑ष॒भं सु॒ते गृ॑णाति । स॒ह॒स्रिण॒ उप॑ नो माहि॒ वाजा॑न्यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 27.translation: “Men invokeIndrain battle when those actions which lead to victory are performed; do you who arehero, the benefactor of man, the desirer of prowess, plural ce us in possession of pastures abounding with cattle.”

Sukta 27.translation: “Indra, who are the invoked of many, give to those men who are your friends that strength which,Maghavan, is thine; you, Maghavan (has forced open) the firm (shut, gates of cities); discover, discrimiantor (oftruth), the treasure now concealed.”

Sukta 27.translation: “Indrais lord of the earth and of men; (his is) the various wealth that exists upon the earth; thence hegives riches to the donor (of oblations); may he, glorified by us, bestow upon us wealth.”

Sukta 27.translation: “May the affluent and liberal,Indra, upon being invoked together (with theMaruts), quickly bestow foodfor our reservation, he whose unlimited, experienced liberality yields desirable (wealth) to those men (who arehis) friends.”

Sukta 30.translation: “Divine and powerful (Indra), come to us with your strength; be the augmenter of our riches; be to us,king of men, wielder of the thunderbolt, for (a source of) vigour, of great prowess, hero, of manhood.”

Sukta 30.translation: “Warriors invoke you, worthy to be invoked, in the variously clamorous (strife), for (the safety of their)person ns, and for the (long) enjoyment of the sun; you are a fit leader over all men; humble our enemies by thefatal (bolt).”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: हव॑न्त उ त्वा॒ हव्यं॒ विवा॑चि त॒नूषु॒ शूरा॒: सूर्य॑स्य सा॒तौ । त्वं विश्वे॑षु॒ सेन्यो॒ जने॑षु॒ त्वं वृ॒त्राणि॑ रन्धया सु॒हन्तु॑

Sukta 30.translation: “When,Indra, fortunate days arise, when you advance your emblem in battles, the strongAgni, theinvoker of the gods, summoning the gods hither for our benefit, sits down on the sacred grass.”

Sukta 30.translation: “We, divineIndra, who are yours, are they, hero, who are praising you and offering rich libations; grantto (your) pious (worshippers) an excellent abode; and may they, prosperous, attain old age.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: व॒यं ते त॑ इन्द्र॒ ये च॑ देव॒ स्तव॑न्त शूर॒ दद॑तो म॒घानि॑ । यच्छा॑ सू॒रिभ्य॑ उप॒मं वरू॑थं स्वा॒भुवो॑ जर॒णाम॑श्नवन्त

Sukta 30.translation: “Let us glorify the opulentIndra, that he may give us vast and valuable riches; he who is the chiefprotector of the religious rites of the worshippers; do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 30.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वो॒चेमेदिन्द्रं॑ म॒घवा॑नमेनं म॒हो रा॒यो राध॑सो॒ यद्दद॑न्नः । यो अर्च॑तो॒ ब्रह्म॑कृति॒मवि॑ष्ठो यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 32.translation: “TheseSoma, mixed with curds, are poured out toIndra; come, wielder of the thunderbolt, with yourhorses of our dwelling, to drink there for (your) exhilaration.”

Sukta 32.translation: “Address (toIndra), among the gods, the ample, well-uttered, and graceful prayer; many bonds entanglenot him who, by his devotion, abides in Indra.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मन्त्र॒मख॑र्वं॒ सुधि॑तं सु॒पेश॑सं॒ दधा॑त य॒ज्ञिये॒ष्वा । पू॒र्वीश्च॒न प्रसि॑तयस्तरन्ति॒ तं य इन्द्रे॒ कर्म॑णा॒ भुव॑त्

Sukta 32.translation: “What mortal,Indra, injures him who has you for his support? He who offers you (sacrificial) food,Maghavan, with faith, he obtains food on the day of the libation.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कस्तमि॑न्द्र॒ त्वाव॑सु॒मा मर्त्यो॑ दधर्षति । श्र॒द्धा इत्ते॑ मघव॒न्पार्ये॑ दि॒वि वा॒जी वाजं॑ सिषासति

Sukta 32.translation: “Animate (those men) for the destruction of their foes, who offer treasures which are dear to you, theabounder in wealth; may we, lord of bay steeds, along with (your) worshippers, pass over all difficulties by yourguidance.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒घोन॑: स्म वृत्र॒हत्ये॑षु चोदय॒ ये दद॑ति प्रि॒या वसु॑ । तव॒ प्रणी॑ती हर्यश्व सू॒रिभि॒र्विश्वा॑ तरेम दुरि॒ता

Sukta 32.translation: “Yours,Indra, is the vast valuable wealth; you cherish the middling; you rule over all that which is themost precious; no one opposes you in (the recovering of the) cattle.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तवेदि॑न्द्राव॒मं वसु॒ त्वं पु॑ष्यसि मध्य॒मम् । स॒त्रा विश्व॑स्य पर॒मस्य॑ राजसि॒ नकि॑ष्ट्वा॒ गोषु॑ वृण्वते

Sukta 32.translation: “You are celebrated as the giver of wealth to all even where battles occur; all the people of theearth--desirous of protection, solicit you, the invoked of many.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं विश्व॑स्य धन॒दा अ॑सि श्रु॒तो य ईं॒ भव॑न्त्या॒जय॑: । तवा॒यं विश्व॑: पुरुहूत॒ पार्थि॑वोऽव॒स्युर्नाम॑ भिक्षते

Sukta 32.translation: “If I were lord of as much (affluence) as you are,Indra, then might I support (your) worshippers,dispenser of wealth, and not squander it upon wickedness.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यदि॑न्द्र॒ याव॑त॒स्त्वमे॒ताव॑द॒हमीशी॑य । स्तो॒तार॒मिद्दि॑धिषेय रदावसो॒ न पा॑प॒त्वाय॑ रासीय

devanagari.text: शिक्षेयमिन्महयते दिवेदिवे राय आ कुहचिद्विदे ।नहि त्वदन्यन्मघवन्न आप्यं वस्यो अस्ति पिता चन ॥

Sukta 32.translation: “May I daily distribute wealth to the venerable wherever abiding; no other,Maghavan, than you is to besought by us; (no other is to us) a most excellent protector.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शिक्षे॑य॒मिन्म॑हय॒ते दि॒वेदि॑वे रा॒य आ कु॑हचि॒द्विदे॑ । न॒हि त्वद॒न्यन्म॑घवन्न॒ आप्यं॒ वस्यो॒ अस्ति॑ पि॒ता च॒न

Sukta 32.translation: “The prompt offers (of praise), with solemn rites combined, acquires food; I bend down with adoration toyou,Indra, the invoker of many, as a carpenter bends the wooden circumference of the wheel.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त॒रणि॒रित्सि॑षासति॒ वाजं॒ पुरं॑ध्या यु॒जा । आ व॒ इन्द्रं॑ पुरुहू॒तं न॑मे गि॒रा ने॒मिं तष्टे॑व सु॒द्र्व॑म्

Sukta 32.translation: “A man acquires not wealth by unbecoming praise; affluence devolves not upon one obstructing(sacrifice) in you,Maghavan, is the power whereby bounty (may be shown) to such as I am on the day of libation.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: न दु॑:ष्टु॒ती मर्त्यो॑ विन्दते॒ वसु॒ न स्रेध॑न्तं र॒यिर्न॑शत् । सु॒शक्ति॒रिन्म॑घव॒न्तुभ्यं॒ माव॑ते दे॒ष्णं यत्पार्ये॑ दि॒वि

Sukta 32.translation: “We glorify you, hero, (Indra), the lord of all movable and stationary things, the beholder of the universe,with ladles filled (withSoma, like (the udders of) unmilked kine.”

Sukta 32.translation: “No other such as you are, celestial or terrestrial, has been or will be born; desirous of horses, of food,of cattle affluentIndra, we invoke you.”

Sukta 32.translation: “ElderIndra, bring that (wealth to me), being the junior, for,Maghavan, you have from the beginningbeen possessed of infinite treasure, and are to be adored at repeated sacrifices.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भी ष॒तस्तदा भ॒रेन्द्र॒ ज्याय॒: कनी॑यसः । पु॒रू॒वसु॒र्हि म॑घवन्त्स॒नादसि॒ भरे॑भरे च॒ हव्य॑:

Sukta 32.translation: “Drive away,Maghavan, our enemies; render riches easy of acquisition; be our preserver in war; be theaugmenter of (the prosperity) of (your) friends.”

Sukta 32.translation: “Bring to us,Indra, wisdom, as a father (gives knowledge) to his sons; bestow wealth upon us on thisoccasion, you the invoked of many, so that we, living at the solemnity may (long) enjoy the light (of existence).”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॒ क्रतुं॑ न॒ आ भ॑र पि॒ता पु॒त्रेभ्यो॒ यथा॑ । शिक्षा॑ णो अ॒स्मिन्पु॑रुहूत॒ याम॑नि जी॒वा ज्योति॑रशीमहि

devanagari.text: मा नो अज्ञाता वृजना दुराध्यो माशिवासो अव क्रमुः ।त्वया वयं प्रवतः शश्वतीरपोऽति शूर तरामसि ॥

Sukta 32.translation: “Let no unknown, wicked, malevolent, malignant (enemies) overpower us; may we, protected by you,cross over many waters.”
Sukta 32.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा नो॒ अज्ञा॑ता वृ॒जना॑ दुरा॒ध्यो॒३॒॑ माशि॑वासो॒ अव॑ क्रमुः । त्वया॑ व॒यं प्र॒वत॒: शश्व॑तीर॒पोऽति॑ शूर तरामसि

devanagari.text: श्वित्यंचो मा दक्षिणतस्कपर्दा धियंजिन्वासो अभि हि प्रमंदुः ।उत्तिष्ठन्वोचे परि बर्हिषो नॄन्न मे दूरादवितवे वसिष्ठाः ॥

Sukta 33.translation: “The white-complexioned accomplishers of holy ceremonies, wearing the lock of hair on the right side,have afforded me delight, when, rising up I call the leaders (of rites) to the sacred grass; theVasiṣṭhas, (mysons) should never be far from me.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श्वि॒त्यञ्चो॑ मा दक्षिण॒तस्क॑पर्दा धियंजि॒न्वासो॑ अ॒भि हि प्र॑म॒न्दुः । उ॒त्तिष्ठ॑न्वोचे॒ परि॑ ब॒र्हिषो॒ नॄन्न मे॑ दू॒रादवि॑तवे॒ वसि॑ष्ठाः

devanagari.text: दूरादिंद्रमनयन्ना सुतेन तिरो वैशंतमति पांतमुग्रं ।पाशद्युम्नस्य वायतस्य सोमात्सुतादिंद्रोऽवृणीता वसिष्ठान् ॥

Sukta 33.translation: “Disgracing (Pāśadyumna), they brought from afar the fierceIndra, when drinking the ladle ofSomaathissacrifice, to (receive) the libation (ofSudāsa); Indra hastened from the effused Soma of Pāśadumna, theson of Vāyata, to theVasiṣṭhas.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दू॒रादिन्द्र॑मनय॒न्ना सु॒तेन॑ ति॒रो वै॑श॒न्तमति॒ पान्त॑मु॒ग्रम् । पाश॑द्युम्नस्य वाय॒तस्य॒ सोमा॑त्सु॒तादिन्द्रो॑ऽवृणीता॒ वसि॑ष्ठान्

devanagari.text: एवेन्नु कं सिंधुमेभिस्ततारेवेन्नु कं भेदमेभिर्जघान ।एवेन्नु कं दाशराज्ञे सुदासं प्रावदिंद्रो ब्रह्मणा वो वसिष्ठाः ॥

Sukta 33.translation: “In the same manner was he, (Sudāsa) enabled by them easily to cross theSindhuriver; in the samemanner, through them he easily slew his foe; so in like manner,Vasiṣṭhas, through your prayers, did Indradefend Sudāsa in the war with the ten kings.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वेन्नु कं॒ सिन्धु॑मेभिस्ततारे॒वेन्नु कं॑ भे॒दमे॑भिर्जघान । ए॒वेन्नु कं॑ दाशरा॒ज्ञे सु॒दासं॒ प्राव॒दिन्द्रो॒ ब्रह्म॑णा वो वसिष्ठाः

devanagari.text: जुष्टी नरो ब्रह्मणा वः पितॄणामक्षमव्ययं न किला रिषाथ ।यच्छक्वरीषु बृहता रवेणेंद्रे शुष्ममदधाता वसिष्ठाः ॥
जुष्टी । नरः । ब्रह्मणा । वः । पितॄणाम् । अक्षम् । अव्ययम् । न । किल । रिषाथ ।यत् । शक्वरीषु । बृहता । रवेण । इन्द्रे । शुष्मम् । अदधात । वसिष्ठाः ॥

transliteration.text: júṣṭī ǀ naraḥ ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ vaḥ ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ ákṣam ǀ avyayam ǀ ná ǀ kíla ǀ riṣātha ǀyát ǀ śákvarīṣu ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ ráveṇa ǀ índre ǀ śúṣmam ǀ ádadhāta ǀ vasiṣṭhāḥ ǁ

Sukta 33.translation: “By your prayers, leaders (of rites), is effected the gratificcation of your progenitors; I have set in motionthe axle (of the chariot); be no you intert, for by your sacred metres,Vasiṣṭhas, (chanted) with a loud voice, yousustain vigour inInda.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: जुष्टी॑ नरो॒ ब्रह्म॑णा वः पितॄ॒णामक्ष॑मव्ययं॒ न किला॑ रिषाथ । यच्छक्व॑रीषु बृह॒ता रवे॒णेन्द्रे॒ शुष्म॒मद॑धाता वसिष्ठाः

devanagari.text: उद्द्यामिवेत्तृष्णजो नाथितासोऽदीधयुर्दाशराज्ञे वृतासः ।वसिष्ठस्य स्तुवत इंद्रो अश्रोदुरुं तृत्सुभ्यो अकृणोदु लोकं ॥

transliteration.text: út ǀ dyā́m-iva ǀ ít ǀ tṛṣṇá-jaḥ ǀ nāthitā́saḥ ǀ ádīdhayuḥ ǀ dāśa-rājñé ǀ vṛtā́saḥ ǀvásiṣṭhasya ǀ stuvatáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ aśrot ǀ urúm ǀ tṛ́tsu-bhyaḥ ǀ akṛṇot ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǁ

Sukta 33.translation: “Suffering from thirst, soliciting (rain), supported (by the Tṛtsus) in the war with the tenrājās, (theVasiṣṭhas) madeIndraradiant as the sun; Indra heard (the praises) ofVasiṣṭhaglorifying him, and bestowed aspacious region on the Tṛtsus.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उद्द्यामि॒वेत्तृ॒ष्णजो॑ नाथि॒तासोऽदी॑धयुर्दाशरा॒ज्ञे वृ॒तास॑: । वसि॑ष्ठस्य स्तुव॒त इन्द्रो॑ अश्रोदु॒रुं तृत्सु॑भ्यो अकृणोदु लो॒कम्

devanagari.text: दंडा इवेद्गोअजनास आसन्परिच्छिन्ना भरता अर्भकासः ।अभवच्च पुरएता वसिष्ठ आदित्तृत्सूनां विशो अप्रथंत ॥

transliteration.text: daṇḍā́ḥ-iva ǀ ít ǀ go-ájanāsaḥ ǀ āsan ǀ pári-chinnāḥ ǀ bharatā́ḥ ǀ arbhakā́saḥ ǀábhavat ǀ ca ǀ puraḥ-etā́ ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ tṛ́tsūnām ǀ víśaḥ ǀ aprathanta ǁ

Sukta 33.translation: “TheBharatas, inferior (to their foes), were shorn (of their possessions), like he staves for driving cattle,(stripped of their leaves and branches); butVasiṣṭhabecame their family priest, and the people of the Tṛtsusprospered.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द॒ण्डा इ॒वेद्गो॒अज॑नास आस॒न्परि॑च्छिन्ना भर॒ता अ॑र्भ॒कास॑: । अभ॑वच्च पुरए॒ता वसि॑ष्ठ॒ आदित्तृत्सू॑नां॒ विशो॑ अप्रथन्त

devanagari.text: त्रयः कृण्वंति भुवनेषु रेतस्तिस्रः प्रजा आर्या ज्योतिरग्राः ।त्रयो घर्मास उषसं सचंते सर्वाँ इत्ताँ अनु विदुर्वसिष्ठाः ॥

Sukta 33.translation: “Three shed moisture upon the regions, three are their glorious progeny, of which the chief is night;three communicators of warmth accompany the dawn; verily theVasiṣṭhasunderstand all these.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्रय॑: कृण्वन्ति॒ भुव॑नेषु॒ रेत॑स्ति॒स्रः प्र॒जा आर्या॒ ज्योति॑रग्राः । त्रयो॑ घ॒र्मास॑ उ॒षसं॑ सचन्ते॒ सर्वाँ॒ इत्ताँ अनु॑ विदु॒र्वसि॑ष्ठाः

devanagari.text: सूर्यस्येव वक्षथो ज्योतिरेषां समुद्रस्येव महिमा गभीरः ।वातस्येव प्रजवो नान्येन स्तोमो वसिष्ठा अन्वेतवे वः ॥

transliteration.text: sū́ryasya-iva ǀ vakṣáthaḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ samudrásya-iva ǀ mahimā́ ǀ gabhīráḥ ǀvā́tasya-iva ǀ pra-javáḥ ǀ ná ǀ anyéna ǀ stómaḥ ǀ vasiṣṭhāḥ ǀ ánu-etave ǀ vaḥ ǁ

Sukta 33.translation: “The glory of theseVasi.ṣṭhas is like the splendour of the sun; their greatness as profound as (thedepth of) the ocean; your praise,Vasiṣṭhas, has the velocity of the wind; by no other can it be surpassed.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सूर्य॑स्येव व॒क्षथो॒ ज्योति॑रेषां समु॒द्रस्ये॑व महि॒मा ग॑भी॒रः । वात॑स्येव प्रज॒वो नान्येन॒ स्तोमो॑ वसिष्ठा॒ अन्वे॑तवे वः

devanagari.text: त इन्निण्यं हृदयस्य प्रकेतैः सहस्रवल्शमभि सं चरंति ।यमेन ततं परिधिं वयंतोऽप्सरस उप सेदुर्वसिष्ठाः ॥

transliteration.text: té ǀ ít ǀ niṇyám ǀ hṛ́dayasya ǀ pra-ketáiḥ ǀ sahásra-valśam ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ caranti ǀyaména ǀ tatám ǀ pari-dhím ǀ váyantaḥ ǀ apsarásaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ seduḥ ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǁ

Sukta 33.translation: “By the wisdom seated in the heart theVasiṣṭhastraverse the hidden thousand branched world, andtheApsarasassit down wearing the vesture spread out byYama.”
Sukta 33.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त इन्नि॒ण्यं हृद॑यस्य प्रके॒तैः स॒हस्र॑वल्शम॒भि सं च॑रन्ति । य॒मेन॑ त॒तं प॑रि॒धिं वय॑न्तोऽप्स॒रस॒ उप॑ सेदु॒र्वसि॑ष्ठाः

devanagari.text: विद्युतो ज्योतिः परि संजिहानं मित्रावरुणा यदपश्यतां त्वा ।तत्ते जन्मोतैकं वसिष्ठागस्त्यो यत्त्वा विश आजभार ॥

transliteration.text: vi-dyútaḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ pári ǀ sam-jíhānam ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ yát ǀ ápaśyatām ǀ tvā ǀtát ǀ te ǀ jánma ǀ utá ǀ ékam ǀ vasiṣṭha ǀ agástyaḥ ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ viśáḥ ǀ ā-jabhā́ra ǁ

Sukta 33.translation: “WhenMitraandVaruṇabeheld you,Vasiṣṭha, quitting the lustre of the lightning (for a different form),then one of your births (took plural ce), inasmuch asAgastyabore you from your (former) abode.”

Sukta 35.translation: “May heaven and earth, the first invoked, (promote) our happiness; may the firmament be happiness toour view; may the herbs, the trees, (yield) us happiness; may the victorious lord of the world, (Indra), be(favourable to) our felicity.”

Sukta 35.translation: “May the divine (Indra), with theVasus, grant us happiness; may the justly-praisedVaruṇa, with theĀdityas, be (friendly to) our happiness; may the grief-assuagingRudra, with theRudras, be (for) our happiness;mayTvaṣṭā, with the wives of the gods, be (with us) for our happiness, and hear us at this solemnity.”

Be (conducive to) our happiness;may celestial, terrestrial and aquatic things be (subservient to) our happiness.”

Sukta 35.translation: “May the divine Aja-Ekapād be (favourable to) our happiness; mayAhirbudhnya, may the firmament, be(promotive of) our happiness; may the grandson of the waters, the protector, be (the securer of) our felicity; mayPṛśni, of whom the gods are the guardians, be to us (a granter of) happiness.”

Sukta 36.translation: “PowerfulMitraandVaruṇa, to you I offer this new praise as if it were (sacrificial) food; one of you,(Varuṇa). The invincible lord, is the guide to the path (of virtue) Mitra when praised animates men to exertioṇ”

Sukta 36.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अच्छा॒यं वो॑ मरुत॒: श्लोक॑ ए॒त्वच्छा॒ विष्णुं॑ निषिक्त॒पामवो॑भिः । उ॒त प्र॒जायै॑ गृण॒ते वयो॑ धुर्यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 37.translation: “Vājas, possessors of energy, let your capacious, commendable, and unobstructed chariot bring you(hither); be satiated, handsome-chinned, with the copious triply-combined libation (poured out) for yourexhilaration at our sacrifices.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ वो॒ वाहि॑ष्ठो वहतु स्त॒वध्यै॒ रथो॑ वाजा ऋभुक्षणो॒ अमृ॑क्तः । अ॒भि त्रि॑पृ॒ष्ठैः सव॑नेषु॒ सोमै॒र्मदे॑ सुशिप्रा म॒हभि॑: पृणध्वम्

devanagari.text: यूयं ह रत्नं मघवत्सु धत्थ स्वर्दृश ऋभुक्षणो अमृक्तं ।सं यज्ञेषु स्वधावंतः पिबध्वं वि नो राधांसि मतिभिर्दयध्वं ॥

transliteration.text: yūyám ǀ ha ǀ rátnam ǀ maghávat-su ǀ dhattha ǀ svaḥ-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ ámṛktam ǀsám ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ svadhā-vantaḥ ǀ pibadhvam ǀ ví ǀ naḥ ǀ rā́dhāṃsi ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ dayadhvam ǁ

Sukta 37.translation: “For you,Ṛbhukṣins, beholders of heaven, preserve unmolested the precious (treasure) for us who areaffluent (in sacrificial offerings); do you who are possessed of strengh, drink fully at (our) solemnities, and with(favourable) minds bestow upon us riches.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यू॒यं ह॒ रत्नं॑ म॒घव॑त्सु धत्थ स्व॒र्दृश॑ ऋभुक्षणो॒ अमृ॑क्तम् । सं य॒ज्ञेषु॑ स्वधावन्तः पिबध्वं॒ वि नो॒ राधां॑सि म॒तिभि॑र्दयध्वम्

devanagari.text: उवोचिथ हि मघवंदेष्णं महो अर्भस्य वसुनो विभागे ।उभा ते पूर्णा वसुना गभस्ती न सूनृता नि यमते वसव्या ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “You,Maghavan, have determined what is to be given in the apportionment of much or of little wealth,for both yourhandsare full of treasure, and your sincere (promises) of riches do not restrain them.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒वोचि॑थ॒ हि म॑घवन्दे॒ष्णं म॒हो अर्भ॑स्य॒ वसु॑नो विभा॒गे । उ॒भा ते॑ पू॒र्णा वसु॑ना॒ गभ॑स्ती॒ न सू॒नृता॒ नि य॑मते वस॒व्या॑

devanagari.text: त्वमिंद्र स्वयशा ऋभुक्षा वाजो न साधुरस्तमेष्यृक्वा ।वयं नु ते दाश्वांसः स्याम ब्रह्म कृण्वंतो हरिवो वसिष्ठाः ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “Do you,Indra, who areṚbhukṣin, and of especial renown, who, like food, are the fulfiller (of wants),come to the dwelling of the worshipper; lord of bay horses, may we,Vasiṣṭhas, be today the donors (of theofferings) to yo, the celebrators of your praise.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वमि॑न्द्र॒ स्वय॑शा ऋभु॒क्षा वाजो॒ न सा॒धुरस्त॑मे॒ष्यृक्वा॑ । व॒यं नु ते॑ दा॒श्वांस॑: स्याम॒ ब्रह्म॑ कृ॒ण्वन्तो॑ हरिवो॒ वसि॑ष्ठाः

devanagari.text: सनितासि प्रवतो दाशुषे चिद्याभिर्विवेषो हर्यश्व धीभिः ।ववन्मा नु ते युज्याभिरूती कदा न इंद्र राय आ दशस्येः ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “Lord of bay horses, you are the giver of descending (wealth) to the donor (of the oblation), by whosesacred rites you are magnified; when may you bestow upon us riches; when may we be secure by yourappropriate protections.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सनि॑तासि प्र॒वतो॑ दा॒शुषे॑ चि॒द्याभि॒र्विवे॑षो हर्यश्व धी॒भिः । व॒व॒न्मा नु ते॒ युज्या॑भिरू॒ती क॒दा न॑ इन्द्र रा॒य आ द॑शस्येः

Sukta 37.translation: “When,Indra, will you appreciate our praise; at present you establish us (your) adorers in our dwelling;let your swift horse, (influenced) by our protracted solemnity, convey to our abode riches,maleoffspring, andfood.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वा॒सय॑सीव वे॒धस॒स्त्वं न॑: क॒दा न॑ इन्द्र॒ वच॑सो बुबोधः । अस्तं॑ ता॒त्या धि॒या र॒यिं सु॒वीरं॑ पृ॒क्षो नो॒ अर्वा॒ न्यु॑हीत वा॒जी

devanagari.text: अभि यं देवी निर्ऋतिश्चिदीशे नक्षंत इंद्रं शरदः सुपृक्षः ।उप त्रिबंधुर्जरदष्टिमेत्यस्ववेशं यं कृणवंत मर्ताः ॥

Sukta 37.translation: “Indra, the upholder of the three regions, whom the divineNirṛtiacknowledges as ruler, whom abundantyears pass over, whom mortals detain from his own abode, approaches to (recruit) his decaying strength.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि यं दे॒वी निॠ॑तिश्चि॒दीशे॒ नक्ष॑न्त॒ इन्द्रं॑ श॒रद॑: सु॒पृक्ष॑: । उप॑ त्रिब॒न्धुर्ज॒रद॑ष्टिमे॒त्यस्व॑वेशं॒ यं कृ॒णव॑न्त॒ मर्ता॑:

Sukta 37.translation: “May riches worthy of laudation come,Savitā, to us; riches that are in the bestow ofParvata; may theheavenly protector (of all) preserve us; and, do you (Universal gods), ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 37.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ नो॒ राधां॑सि सवित स्त॒वध्या॒ आ रायो॑ यन्तु॒ पर्व॑तस्य रा॒तौ । सदा॑ नो दि॒व्यः पा॒युः सि॑षक्तु यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: उदु ष्य देवः सविता ययाम हिरण्ययीममतिं यामशिश्रेत् ।नूनं भगो हव्यो मानुषेभिर्वि यो रत्ना पुरूवसुर्दधाति ॥

Sukta 38.translation: “The divineSavitāhas diffused the golden radiance on high, of which he is the asylum; verilyBhagaisto be absorbed by men who, abounding in wealth, distributes treasures (among them).”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उदु॒ ष्य दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता य॑याम हिर॒ण्ययी॑म॒मतिं॒ यामशि॑श्रेत् । नू॒नं भगो॒ हव्यो॒ मानु॑षेभि॒र्वि यो रत्ना॑ पुरू॒वसु॒र्दधा॑ति

Sukta 38.translation: “Rise upSavitā; hear (our solicitations) upon the celebration of this ceremony, (you who are) diffusinglight over the spacious earth, and bestowing human enjoyment upon men.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उदु॑ तिष्ठ सवितः श्रु॒ध्य१॒॑स्य हिर॑ण्यपाणे॒ प्रभृ॑तावृ॒तस्य॑ । व्यु१॒॑र्वीं पृ॒थ्वीम॒मतिं॑ सृजा॒न आ नृभ्यो॑ मर्त॒भोज॑नं सुवा॒नः

Sukta 38.translation: “Glorified be the divineSavitā, whom all the gods praise; may that adorable (diviniy) require our praises(with) food; may he always protect the devout with all his protections.”
Sukta 38.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अपि॑ ष्टु॒तः स॑वि॒ता दे॒वो अ॑स्तु॒ यमा चि॒द्विश्वे॒ वस॑वो गृ॒णन्ति॑ । स न॒: स्तोमा॑न्नम॒स्य१॒॑श्चनो॑ धा॒द्विश्वे॑भिः पातु पा॒युभि॒र्नि सू॒रीन्

Sukta 38.translation: “Whom the divineAditi, delighting at the birth of the divineSavitṛ, glorifies, whom the supremesoverigns,Varuṇa,Mitra,Āryaman, (and other gods) adore.”

Sukta 38.translation: “Whom those solicitous for wealth those enjoying (it), mutually worship, the benefactor of heaven andearth; mayAhirbudhnyahear us; may the protectress (the goddess of speech), cherish us with excellen cattle.”

Sukta 38.translation: “May the protector of progeny, when solicited, consent to bestow upon us the precious (wealth of thedivineSavitā; the ardent (adorer) invokes repeatedlyBhagafor protection; the less ardent solicits Bhaga forwealth.”

Sukta 38.translation: “May theVājins, with slackened speed, bringing excellent food, be (disposed) for our happiness, uponour invocations at the worship of the gods; destroying the murderer, the robber, therākṣasas, and keepingfrom us ancient maladies.”

Sukta 38.translation: “Wise, immortalVājins, observers of truth, defend us in every conflict, and for the sake of wealth; drinkof this sweet (Soma), be exhilarated (thereby) and satisfied; proceed by the paths traversed by the gods.”

Sukta 39.translation: “May the divineVasussport on this occasion upon the earth; the brilliant (Maruts) in the expansivefirmament are being worshipped; swift-moving deities, direct your paths towards us; hear (the words) of this ourmessenger, (Agni), approaching you.”

Sukta 39.translation: “These universal adorable guardian deities occupy a common station at sacrifices; worship,Agni, thosedivinities, deservers (of oblations) at the ceremony, the swiftBhaga, theNāsatyāsand Purandhi.”

Sukta 39.translation: “The oblation is offered together with praises to the adorable deities; may (Agni), unaverse to the desireof mortals, be present; bestow (upon us gods), unwasting, all-benefiting riches; and may we today be associatedwith the assembled deities.”

Sukta 43.translation: “Let the sacrifice proceed like a swift course (tot he gods); elevate, (priests), with one occurred, yourladles, charged with butter; spread for the solemnity the sacred grass;le the flames (of the burnt-offering) to thegods ascend on high.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र य॒ज्ञ ए॑तु॒ हेत्वो॒ न सप्ति॒रुद्य॑च्छध्वं॒ सम॑नसो घृ॒ताची॑: । स्तृ॒णी॒त ब॒र्हिर॑ध्व॒राय॑ सा॒धूर्ध्वा शो॒चींषि॑ देव॒यून्य॑स्थुः

Sukta 43.translation: “Let the gods sit down on the summit of the sacred grass, like children nursed on the (lap of the) mother;let the full ladle,Agni, pour (the oblaion) on the sacrificial flame; give us not up to your adversaries in battle.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ पु॒त्रासो॒ न मा॒तरं॒ विभृ॑त्रा॒: सानौ॑ दे॒वासो॑ ब॒र्हिष॑: सदन्तु । आ वि॒श्वाची॑ विद॒थ्या॑मन॒क्त्वग्ने॒ मा नो॑ दे॒वता॑ता॒ मृध॑स्कः

Sukta 43.translation: “May the adorable deities, who are the bestowers of water, the shedders of showers, be fully propitiated(by our praises); may the most precious and commendable of your treasure (be ours) today; and do you with oneaccord come hither.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते सी॑षपन्त॒ जोष॒मा यज॑त्रा ऋ॒तस्य॒ धारा॑: सु॒दुघा॒ दुहा॑नाः । ज्येष्ठं॑ वो अ॒द्य मह॒ आ वसू॑ना॒मा ग॑न्तन॒ सम॑नसो॒ यति॒ ष्ठ

Sukta 43.translation: “Be glorifiedAgni; grant us (wealth) among the people; may we, vigorous Agni, ever be undeserted byyou, but always be rejoicing and unmolested in the possession of riches; and do you, (gods), ever cherish uswith blessings.”
Sukta 43.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा नो॑ अग्ने वि॒क्ष्वा द॑शस्य॒ त्वया॑ व॒यं स॑हसाव॒न्नास्क्रा॑: । रा॒या यु॒जा स॑ध॒मादो॒ अरि॑ष्टा यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 44.translation: “For your preservation, (worshippers), I invoke, first, Dadhikrā, then theAśvins, the Dawn, the kindledAgni,Bhaga,Indra,Viṣṇu,Pūṣan,Brahmaṇaspati, theĀdityas, heaven and earth, the waters, the sun.”

Sukta 44.translation: “Arousing and animating Dadhikrā, proceeding diligently with the sacrifice; seating the divine Iḷā onthe sacred grass, let us invoke the intelligent and worthily-invokedAśvins.”

Sukta 44.translation: “Propitiating Dadhikrāvan, I glorifyAgni, Uṣas, the sun, the earth, the great brown horse ofVaruṇa,who is mindful of his adorers; may they put far away from us iniquities.”

Sukta 44.translation: “Dadhikrāvan, the swift steed, the first (of horses), knowing (his office), is in the front of the chariots (ofthe gods), consentient with Uṣas, withSūrya, wiḥ theĀdityas, with theVasus, with theAṅgirasas.”

Sukta 44.translation: “May Dadhikrā sprinkle our path (with water), that we may follow the road of sacrifice; mayAgni, thestrength of the gods, here our (invocation); may the mighty, unperplexed, universal deities hear it.”

Sukta 45.translation: “Borne by his steeds, may the divineSavitā, who is possessed of precious treasure, and filling thefirmament (with radiance), come hither, holding in hishandsmany things good for man, and (both) tranquilizingand animating living beings.”

Sukta 45.translation: “May the outspread, vast, and golden arms ofSavitāextend to the ends of the sky; verily his greatnessis glorified (by us); may the sun impart energy unto him.”

devanagari.text: स घा नो देवः सविता सहावा साविषद्वसुपतिर्वसूनि ।विश्रयमाणो अमतिमुरूचीं मर्तभोजनमध रासते नः ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ gha ǀ naḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ sahá-vā ǀ ā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ vásu-patiḥ ǀ vásūni ǀvi-śráyamāṇaḥ ǀ amátim ǀ urūcī́m ǀ marta-bhójanam ǀ ádha ǀ rāsate ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 45.translation: “May the divineSavitā, who is endowed with energy, the lord of treasure, bestow treasures upon usconcentrating infinite lustre; may he bestow upon us wealh, the source of the enjoyment of mortals.”
Sukta 45.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स घा॑ नो दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता स॒हावा सा॑विष॒द्वसु॑पति॒र्वसू॑नि । वि॒श्रय॑माणो अ॒मति॑मुरू॒चीं म॑र्त॒भोज॑न॒मध॑ रासते नः

devanagari.text: इमा गिरः सवितारं सुजिह्वं पूर्णगभस्तिमीळते सुपाणिं ।चित्रं वयो बृहदस्मे दधातु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

transliteration.text: imā́ḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ savitā́ram ǀ su-jihvám ǀ pūrṇá-gabhastim ǀ īḷate ǀ su-pāṇím ǀcitrám ǀ váyaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ asmé íti ǀ dadhātu ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 45.translation: “These praises glorify the eloquent-tongued, dextrous-handed, whosehandsare full (of wealth); may hebestow upon us manifold and abundant food; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 45.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मा गिर॑: सवि॒तारं॑ सुजि॒ह्वं पू॒र्णग॑भस्तिमीळते सुपा॒णिम् । चि॒त्रं वयो॑ बृ॒हद॒स्मे द॑धातु यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: इमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिरः क्षिप्रेषवे देवाय स्वधाव्ने ।अषाळ्हाय सहमानाय वेधसे तिग्मायुधाय भरता शृणोतु नः ॥

transliteration.text: imā́ḥ ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ sthirá-dhanvane ǀ gíraḥ ǀ kṣiprá-iṣave ǀ devā́ya ǀ svadhā́-vne ǀáṣāḷhāya ǀ sáhamānāya ǀ vedháse ǀ tigmá-āyudhāya ǀ bharata ǀ śṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 46.translation: “Offer these praises to the divineRudra, armed with the strong bow and fast-flying arrows, the bestowerof food, the invincible, the conqueror, the creator, the wielder of sharp weapons; may he hear our (praises).”
Sukta 46.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मा रु॒द्राय॑ स्थि॒रध॑न्वने॒ गिर॑: क्षि॒प्रेष॑वे दे॒वाय॑ स्व॒धाव्ने॑ । अषा॑ळ्हाय॒ सह॑मानाय वे॒धसे॑ ति॒ग्मायु॑धाय भरता शृ॒णोतु॑ नः

devanagari.text: स हि क्षयेण क्षम्यस्य जन्मनः साम्राज्येन दिव्यस्य चेतति ।अवन्नवंतीरुप नो दुरश्चरानमीवो रुद्र जासु नो भव ॥

Sukta 46.translation: “He is known by his rule over those of terrestrial birth, by his sovereignty over those of celestial (origin);protecting our progeny,Rudra, propitiating you (by praise), come to our dwellings, and be to them a guardianagainst disease.”
Sukta 46.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स हि क्षये॑ण॒ क्षम्य॑स्य॒ जन्म॑न॒: साम्रा॑ज्येन दि॒व्यस्य॒ चेत॑ति । अव॒न्नव॑न्ती॒रुप॑ नो॒ दुर॑श्चरानमी॒वो रु॑द्र॒ जासु॑ नो भव

devanagari.text: या ते दिद्युदवसृष्टा दिवस्परि क्ष्मया चरति परि सा वृणक्तु नः ।सहस्रं ते स्वपिवात भेषजा मा नस्तोकेषु तनयेषु रीरिषः ॥

transliteration.text: yā́ ǀ te ǀ didyút ǀ áva-sṛṣṭā ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀ kṣmayā́ ǀ cárati ǀ pári ǀ sā́ ǀ vṛṇaktu ǀ naḥ ǀsahásram ǀ te ǀ su-apivāta ǀ bheṣajā́ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ tokéṣu ǀ tánayeṣu ǀ ririṣaḥ ǁ

Sukta 46.translation: “May your blazing (weapon), which, discharged from heaven, traverses the earth, avoid us; thine,appeaser of the wind, are a thousand medicaments; inflict not evil upon our sons and grandsons.”
Sukta 46.sanskrit_wisdomlib: या ते॑ दि॒द्युदव॑सृष्टा दि॒वस्परि॑ क्ष्म॒या चर॑ति॒ परि॒ सा वृ॑णक्तु नः । स॒हस्रं॑ ते स्वपिवात भेष॒जा मा न॑स्तो॒केषु॒ तन॑येषु रीरिषः

devanagari.text: मा नो वधी रुद्र मा परा दा मा ते भूम प्रसितौ हीळितस्य ।आ नो भज बर्हिषि जीवशंसे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

transliteration.text: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vadhīḥ ǀ rudra ǀ mā́ ǀ párā ǀ dāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ te ǀ bhūma ǀ prá-sitau ǀ hīḷitásya ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhaja ǀ barhíṣi ǀ jīva-śaṃsé ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 46.translation: “Harm us not,Rudra; abandon us not; let us not fall under the bondage of you when displeased; makeus partakers of the life-promotion sacrifice; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 46.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मा नो॑ वधी रुद्र॒ मा परा॑ दा॒ मा ते॑ भूम॒ प्रसि॑तौ हीळि॒तस्य॑ । आ नो॑ भज ब॒र्हिषि॑ जीवशं॒से यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: आपो यं वः प्रथमं देवयंत इंद्रपानमूर्मिमकृण्वतेळः ।तं वो वयं शुचिमरिप्रमद्य घृतप्रुषं मधुमंतं वनेम ॥

transliteration.text: ā́paḥ ǀ yám ǀ vaḥ ǀ prathamám ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ indra-pā́nam ǀ ūrmím ǀ ákṛṇvata ǀ iḷáḥ ǀtám ǀ vaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ śúcim ǀ ariprám ǀ adyá ǀ ghṛta-prúṣam ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ vanema ǁ

Sukta 47.translation: “We solicit from you, Waters, today, that pure, faultless, rain- shedding, sweet essence of the earth,which devout have first consecrated as theSomaforIndra.”
Sukta 47.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आपो॒ यं व॑: प्रथ॒मं दे॑व॒यन्त॑ इन्द्र॒पान॑मू॒र्मिमकृ॑ण्वते॒ळः । तं वो॑ व॒यं शुचि॑मरि॒प्रम॒द्य घृ॑त॒प्रुषं॒ मधु॑मन्तं वनेम

devanagari.text: तमूर्मिमापो मधुमत्तमं वोऽपां नपादवत्वाशुहेमा ।यस्मिन्निंद्रो वसुभिर्मादयाते तमश्याम देवयंतो वो अद्य ॥

Sukta 47.translation: “May the swift-moving grandson of the Waters protect, Waters, your most sweet essence, wherewiḥ mayIndra and theVasusbe delighted; and may we, devoted to the gods, partake (of it).”
Sukta 47.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तमू॒र्मिमा॑पो॒ मधु॑मत्तमं वो॒ऽपां नपा॑दवत्वाशु॒हेमा॑ । यस्मि॒न्निन्द्रो॒ वसु॑भिर्मा॒दया॑ते॒ तम॑श्याम देव॒यन्तो॑ वो अ॒द्य

devanagari.text: शतपवित्राः स्वधया मदंतीर्देवीर्देवानामपि यंति पाथः ।ता इंद्रस्य न मिनंति व्रतानि सिंधुभ्यो हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥

Sukta 47.translation: “The divine Waters, the purifiers of many, gratifying men with food, pursue the paths of the gods; theyimpede not the sacred rites ofIndra; offer, (priests), the butter-charged oblation to the rivers.”
Sukta 47.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श॒तप॑वित्राः स्व॒धया॒ मद॑न्तीर्दे॒वीर्दे॒वाना॒मपि॑ यन्ति॒ पाथ॑: । ता इन्द्र॑स्य॒ न मि॑नन्ति व्र॒तानि॒ सिन्धु॑भ्यो ह॒व्यं घृ॒तव॑ज्जुहोत

devanagari.text: याः सूर्यो रश्मिभिराततान याभ्य इंद्रो अरदद्गातुमूर्मिं ।ते सिंधवो वरिवो धातना नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

transliteration.text: yā́ḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ ā-tatā́na ǀ yā́bhyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ áradat ǀ gātúm ǀ ūrmím ǀté ǀ sindhavaḥ ǀ várivaḥ ǀ dhātana ǀ naḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 47.translation: “Waters, whom the sun has evaporized by his rays, for whomIndrahas opened a path by which toissue, bestow upon us wealth; and do you (also) ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 47.sanskrit_wisdomlib: याः सूर्यो॑ र॒श्मिभि॑रात॒तान॒ याभ्य॒ इन्द्रो॒ अर॑दद्गा॒तुमू॒र्मिम् । ते सि॑न्धवो॒ वरि॑वो धातना नो यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: ऋभुक्षणो वाजा मादयध्वमस्मे नरो मघवानः सुतस्य ।आ वोऽर्वाचः क्रतवो न यातां विभ्वो रथं नर्यं वर्तयंतु ॥

transliteration.text: ṛ́bhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ mādáyadhvam ǀ asmé íti ǀ naraḥ ǀ magha-vānaḥ ǀ sutásya ǀā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ arvā́caḥ ǀ krátavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yātā́m ǀ ví-bhvaḥ ǀ rátham ǀ náryam ǀ vartayantu ǁ

Sukta 48.translation: “Ṛbhu, (Vibhu), andVāja, leaders of rites, possessors of opulence, be exhilarated by our effused(libation); may your active and powerful (horses) bring to our presence your chariot, beneficial to mankiṇḍ”
Sukta 48.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋभु॑क्षणो वाजा मा॒दय॑ध्वम॒स्मे न॑रो मघवानः सु॒तस्य॑ । आ वो॒ऽर्वाच॒: क्रत॑वो॒ न या॒तां विभ्वो॒ रथं॒ नर्यं॑ वर्तयन्तु

devanagari.text: ऋभुर्ऋभुभिरभि वः स्याम विभ्वो विभुभिः शवसा शवांसि ।वाजो अस्माँ अवतु वाजसाताविंद्रेण युजा तरुषेम वृत्रं ॥

Sukta 48.translation: “Mighty with theṚbhus, opulent with theVibhus, may we overcome by strength, the strength (of ourfoes); mayVājadefend us in battle; withIndra, our ally, may we destroy the enemy.”

Sukta 49.translation: “The waters, with their ocen-chief, proceed from the midst of the firmament, purifying (all things), flowingunceasingly; may the divine waters, whom the thunder-bearingIndra, the showerer, sent forth, protect me here(on earth).”

Sukta 49.translation: “May the waters that are in the sky, or those that flow (on the earth), those (whose channels) have beendug, or those that have sprung up spontaneously, and those that seek the ocean. All pure and purifying, maythose divine waters protect me here (on earth).”

transliteration.text: ādityā́nām ǀ ávasā ǀ nū́tanena ǀ sakṣīmáhi ǀ śármaṇā ǀ śám-tamena ǀanāgā́ḥ-tvé ǀ aditi-tvé ǀ turā́saḥ ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ dadhatu ǀ śróṣamāṇāḥ ǁ

Sukta 51.translation: “May we, through the protection of theĀdityas, be in the enjoyment of a new and comfortable dwelling;may the swift-moving Ādityas, listening to our praises, preserve this their worshipper in sinlessness andindependence.”
Sukta 51.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒दि॒त्याना॒मव॑सा॒ नूत॑नेन सक्षी॒महि॒ शर्म॑णा॒ शंत॑मेन । अ॒ना॒गा॒स्त्वे अ॑दिति॒त्वे तु॒रास॑ इ॒मं य॒ज्ञं द॑धतु॒ श्रोष॑माणाः

devanagari.text: आदित्यासो अदितिर्मादयंतां मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो रजिष्ठाः ।अस्माकं संतु भुवनस्य गोपाः पिबंतु सोममवसे नो अद्य ॥

transliteration.text: ādityā́saḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ mādayantām ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ rájiṣṭhāḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ santu ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ píbantu ǀ sómam ǀ ávase ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǁ

Sukta 51.translation: “May theĀdityasandAditi, and the uprightMitra,Āryaman, andVaruṇa, be exhilarated (by thelibation); may the guardians of the world be ours also; may they drink theSomatoday for our preservation.”
Sukta 51.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒दि॒त्यासो॒ अदि॑तिर्मादयन्तां मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा वरु॑णो॒ रजि॑ष्ठाः । अ॒स्माकं॑ सन्तु॒ भुव॑नस्य गो॒पाः पिब॑न्तु॒ सोम॒मव॑से नो अ॒द्य

devanagari.text: आदित्या विश्वे मरुतश्च विश्वे देवाश्च विश्व ऋभवश्च विश्वे ।इंद्रो अग्निरश्विना तुष्टुवाना यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

transliteration.text: ādityā́ḥ ǀ víśve ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀíndraḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ tustuvānā́ḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 51.translation: “All theĀdityas, all theMaruts, all the gods, all theṚbhus,Indra,Agni, and theAśvins, (have been)glorified (by us), do you all ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 51.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒दि॒त्या विश्वे॑ म॒रुत॑श्च॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वाश्च॒ विश्व॑ ऋ॒भव॑श्च॒ विश्वे॑ । इन्द्रो॑ अ॒ग्निर॒श्विना॑ तुष्टुवा॒ना यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: आदित्यासो अदितयः स्याम पूर्देवत्रा वसवो मर्त्यत्रा ।सनेम मित्रावरुणा सनंतो भवेम द्यावापृथिवी भवंतः ॥

transliteration.text: ādityā́saḥ ǀ áditayaḥ ǀ syāma ǀ pū́ḥ ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ martya-trā́ ǀsánema ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ sánantaḥ ǀ bhávema ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ bhávantaḥ ǁ

Sukta 52.translation: “Ādityas, may we be independent;Vasus, (dwelling) among the gods, may your protection (extend) tomortals; offering (oblations to you),MitraandVaruṇa, may we partake (of your bounty); may we, heaven andearth exist (through your favour).”
Sukta 52.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒दि॒त्यासो॒ अदि॑तयः स्याम॒ पूर्दे॑व॒त्रा व॑सवो मर्त्य॒त्रा । सने॑म मित्रावरुणा॒ सन॑न्तो॒ भवे॑म द्यावापृथिवी॒ भव॑न्तः

devanagari.text: मित्रस्तन्नो वरुणो मामहंत शर्म तोकाय तनयाय गोपाः ।मा वो भुजेमान्यजातमेनो मा तत्कर्म वसवो यच्चयध्वे ॥

Sukta 52.translation: “MayMitraandVaruṇabestow upon us felicity; (may they), the guardians (of all men, bestow felicity)upon our sons and grandsons; let us not suffer (gods), for offences committed by another; let us not,Vasus, doany act by which you may be offended.”
Sukta 52.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मि॒त्रस्तन्नो॒ वरु॑णो मामहन्त॒ शर्म॑ तो॒काय॒ तन॑याय गो॒पाः । मा वो॑ भुजेमा॒न्यजा॑त॒मेनो॒ मा तत्क॑र्म वसवो॒ यच्चय॑ध्वे

Sukta 52.translation: “TheAṅgirasas, prompt (in worship), soliciting him obtain preious (wealth) fromSavitā; may the mightyadorable parent, and the universal god alike favourable minded, approve (of the donation).”
Sukta 52.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तु॒र॒ण्यवोऽङ्गि॑रसो नक्षन्त॒ रत्नं॑ दे॒वस्य॑ सवि॒तुरि॑या॒नाः । पि॒ता च॒ तन्नो॑ म॒हान्यज॑त्रो॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वाः सम॑नसो जुषन्त

Sukta 53.translation: “Attended by a concourse (of priests) I worship the adorable and mighty Heaven and Earth withsacrifices and praises, those wo great ones of whom the gods are the sons, whom ancient sages glorifying haveformerly detained.”
Sukta 53.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र द्यावा॑ य॒ज्ञैः पृ॑थि॒वी नमो॑भिः स॒बाध॑ ईळे बृह॒ती यज॑त्रे । ते चि॒द्धि पूर्वे॑ क॒वयो॑ गृ॒णन्त॑: पु॒रो म॒ही द॑धि॒रे दे॒वपु॑त्रे

Sukta 53.translation: “plural ce before (us) in the hall of sacrifice, with new songs, the ancient parents (of all beings); come to us,Heaven and Earth, with the celestial people, for vast is your protecting (wealth).”

Sukta 53.translation: “Many, Heavan and Earth, are the treasures fit to be given to the pious donor (of the oblation); give to usthat wealth which is unlimited; and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 53.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒तो हि वां॑ रत्न॒धेया॑नि॒ सन्ति॑ पु॒रूणि॑ द्यावापृथिवी सु॒दासे॑ । अ॒स्मे ध॑त्तं॒ यदस॒दस्कृ॑धोयु यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 54.translation: “Protector of the dwelling, recognize us; be to us an excellent abode the non-inflicter of disease;whatever we ask of you, be plural ased to grant; be the bestower of happiness on our bipeds and quadrupedṣ”
Sukta 54.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वास्तो॑ष्पते॒ प्रति॑ जानीह्य॒स्मान्त्स्वा॑वे॒शो अ॑नमी॒वो भ॑वा नः । यत्त्वेम॑हे॒ प्रति॒ तन्नो॑ जुषस्व॒ शं नो॑ भव द्वि॒पदे॒ शं चतु॑ष्पदे

Sukta 54.translation: “Protector of the dwelling, be our preserver and the augmenter of our wealth; possessed of catle andhorses,Indra, may we, through your friendship, be exempt from decay; be favourable to us, like a father to hissons.”
Sukta 54.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वास्तो॑ष्पते प्र॒तर॑णो न एधि गय॒स्फानो॒ गोभि॒रश्वे॑भिरिन्दो । अ॒जरा॑सस्ते स॒ख्ये स्या॑म पि॒तेव॑ पु॒त्रान्प्रति॑ नो जुषस्व

Sukta 54.translation: “Protector of the dwelling, may we be possessed of a comfortable, delightful, opulent abode, bestowedby you; protect our wealth, whether in possession or expectaion; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us withblessings.”
Sukta 54.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वास्तो॑ष्पते श॒ग्मया॑ सं॒सदा॑ ते सक्षी॒महि॑ र॒ण्वया॑ गातु॒मत्या॑ । पा॒हि क्षेम॑ उ॒त योगे॒ वरं॑ नो यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 55.translation: “Protector of the dwelling, remover of disease, assuming all (kinds of) forms, be to us a friend, thegranter of happiness.”
Sukta 55.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒मी॒व॒हा वा॑स्तोष्पते॒ विश्वा॑ रू॒पाण्या॑वि॒शन् । सखा॑ सु॒शेव॑ एधि नः

devanagari.text: यदर्जुन सारमेय दतः पिशंग यच्छसे ।वीव भ्राजंत ऋष्टय उप स्रक्वेषु बप्सतो नि षु स्वप ॥

Sukta 55.translation: “White offspring ofSaramā, with tawny limbs, althogh barking you display your teeth against me,bristling like lances in your gums, nevertheless, to quietly to sleep.”
Sukta 55.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद॑र्जुन सारमेय द॒तः पि॑शङ्ग॒ यच्छ॑से । वी॑व भ्राजन्त ऋ॒ष्टय॒ उप॒ स्रक्वे॑षु॒ बप्स॑तो॒ नि षु स्व॑प

Sukta 55.translation: “Offspring ofSaramā, returning (to the charge), attack the pilferer or the thief; why do you assail theworshippers ofIndra? Why do you intimidate us? Go quietly to sleep.”
Sukta 55.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्ते॒नं रा॑य सारमेय॒ तस्क॑रं वा पुनःसर । स्तो॒तॄनिन्द्र॑स्य रायसि॒ किम॒स्मान्दु॑च्छुनायसे॒ नि षु स्व॑प

Sukta 55.translation: “Do you rend the hog; let the hog rend you; why do you assail the worshippers ofIndra? Why do youintimidate us? Go quietly to sleep.”
Sukta 55.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं सू॑क॒रस्य॑ दर्दृहि॒ तव॑ दर्दर्तु सूक॒रः । स्तो॒तॄनिन्द्र॑स्य रायसि॒ किम॒स्मान्दु॑च्छुनायसे॒ नि षु स्व॑प

Sukta 55.translation: “Let the mother sleep let the father sleep, let the dog sleep, let the son-in-law sleep, let all the kindredsleep, let the people (who are stationed) around sleep.”
Sukta 55.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सस्तु॑ मा॒ता सस्तु॑ पि॒ता सस्तु॒ श्वा सस्तु॑ वि॒श्पति॑: । स॒सन्तु॒ सर्वे॑ ज्ञा॒तय॒: सस्त्व॒यम॒भितो॒ जन॑:

devanagari.text: य आस्ते यश्च चरति यश्च पश्यति नो जनः ।तेषां सं हन्मो अक्षाणि यथेदं हर्म्यं तथा ॥

Sukta 55.translation: “The man who sits, or he who walks, or he who sees us, of these weshutup the eyes, so that they maybe as unconscious as the mansion.”
Sukta 55.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य आस्ते॒ यश्च॒ चर॑ति॒ यश्च॒ पश्य॑ति नो॒ जन॑: । तेषां॒ सं ह॑न्मो अ॒क्षाणि॒ यथे॒दं ह॒र्म्यं तथा॑

devanagari.text: सहस्रशृंगो वृषभो यः समुद्रादुदाचरत् ।तेना सहस्येना वयं नि जनान्त्स्वापयामसि ॥

Sukta 55.translation: “We put men to sleep through the irresisible might or the bull with a thousand horns, who rises out of theocean.”
Sukta 55.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒हस्र॑शृङ्गो वृष॒भो यः स॑मु॒द्रादु॒दाच॑रत् । तेना॑ सह॒स्ये॑ना व॒यं नि जना॑न्त्स्वापयामसि

transliteration.text: proṣṭhe-śayā́ḥ ǀ vahye-śayā́ḥ ǀ nā́rīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ talpa-śī́varīḥ ǀstríyaḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ púṇya-gandhāḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ svāpayāmasi ǁ

Sukta 56.translation: “The sage may know those white-complexioned beings (theMaruts), whom the vastPṛṣṇiborn at herudder.”

यामम् । येष्ठाः । शुभा । शोभिष्ठाः । श्रिया । सम्ऽमिश्लाः । ओजःऽभिः । उग्राः ॥

उग्रम् । वः । ओजः । स्थिरा । शवांसि । अध । मरुत्ऽभिः । गणः । तुविष्मान् ॥

Sukta 56.translation: “If,Maruts, you justly appreciate the praise of the devout offerer of (sacrificial) food, conjoined withoblations, then promptly bestow (upon us) riches, comprehending excellentmaleposterity, such as no unfriendlyman can take away.”

Sukta 56.translation: “When heroic men, filled with wrath, assemble for (the sake of conquering) many plural nts and people;then,Maruts, sons ofRudra, be our defenders in battles against our enemies.”
Sukta 56.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सं यद्धन॑न्त म॒न्युभि॒र्जना॑स॒: शूरा॑ य॒ह्वीष्वोष॑धीषु वि॒क्षु । अध॑ स्मा नो मरुतो रुद्रियासस्त्रा॒तारो॑ भूत॒ पृत॑नास्व॒र्यः

Sukta 56.translation: “You have bestowed,Maruts, many (benefits) on our forefathers, which praiseworthy (benefits) havebeen celebrated in former times; by the (favour of the) Maruts the fierce (warrior) is victorious in combats; by the(favour of the) Maruts the worshipper ever obtains food.”
Sukta 56.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भूरि॑ चक्र मरुत॒: पित्र्या॑ण्यु॒क्थानि॒ या व॑: श॒स्यन्ते॑ पु॒रा चि॑त् । म॒रुद्भि॑रु॒ग्रः पृत॑नासु॒ साळ्हा॑ म॒रुद्भि॒रित्सनि॑ता॒ वाज॒मर्वा॑

devanagari.text: अस्मे वीरो मरुतः शुष्म्यस्तु जनानां यो असुरो विधर्ता ।अपो येन सुक्षितये तरेमाध स्वमोको अभि वः स्याम ॥

Sukta 56.translation: “May ourmaleprogeny,Maruts, be vigorous, one who is intelligent, the scatterer of (hostile) men, bywhom we may cross the water (of enmity) to a secure dwelling; may we, your (servants), dwell in our own abode.”
Sukta 56.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्मे वी॒रो म॑रुतः शु॒ष्म्य॑स्तु॒ जना॑नां॒ यो असु॑रो विध॒र्ता । अ॒पो येन॑ सुक्षि॒तये॒ तरे॒माध॒ स्वमोको॑ अ॒भि व॑: स्याम

Sukta 56.translation: “MayIndra,Varuṇa,Mitra,Agni, the waters, the plural nts, the trees, be plural ased with us; may we recline inhappiness upon the lap of theMaruts; and do you ever cherish us with blessings.”
Sukta 56.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तन्न॒ इन्द्रो॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॒ग्निराप॒ ओष॑धीर्व॒निनो॑ जुषन्त । शर्म॑न्त्स्याम म॒रुता॑मु॒पस्थे॑ यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

devanagari.text: मध्वो वो नाम मारुतं यजत्राः प्र यज्ञेषु शवसा मदंति ।ये रेजयंति रोदसी चिदुर्वी पिन्वंत्युत्सं यदयासुरुग्राः ॥

Sukta 57.translation: “Adorable (Maruts), the worshippers vigorously celebrate at sacrifices your appellation of company ofthe Maruts, they who cause the spacious heaven and earth to tremble, the clouds to rain, the move everywhereterrible.”
Sukta 57.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मध्वो॑ वो॒ नाम॒ मारु॑तं यजत्रा॒: प्र य॒ज्ञेषु॒ शव॑सा मदन्ति । ये रे॒जय॑न्ति॒ रोद॑सी चिदु॒र्वी पिन्व॒न्त्युत्सं॒ यदया॑सुरु॒ग्राः

Sukta 57.translation: “TheMarutsverily are the benefactors of him who praises them, the gratifiers of the wishes of theinstitutor of the solemnity; do you, being plural ased, sit down today upon the grass at our ceremony, to partake (ofthe sacrificial food).”
Sukta 57.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नि॒चे॒तारो॒ हि म॒रुतो॑ गृ॒णन्तं॑ प्रणे॒तारो॒ यज॑मानस्य॒ मन्म॑ । अ॒स्माक॑म॒द्य वि॒दथे॑षु ब॒र्हिरा वी॒तये॑ सदत पिप्रिया॒णाः

Sukta 57.translation: “No other (deities give) such (good things) as theMaruts, as they shine with brilliant (ornaments),weapons and person ns; illumining heaven and earth, wide-radiating, they heighten their common lustre for (our)good.”

Sukta 57.translation: “May that blazing (weapon) of your,Maruts, be far from us, although, through human infirmities, we offeryou offence; let us not, adorable Maruts, be exposed to your (shaft); may your favour the source of abundance,ever be shown to us.”

Sukta 57.translation: “May theMaruts, who are irreproachable, pure, and purifying, delight in this our ceremony; protect us,adorable Maruts, with favourable thoughts; be ever anxious to sustain us with food.”
Sukta 57.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कृ॒ते चि॒दत्र॑ म॒रुतो॑ रणन्तानव॒द्यास॒: शुच॑यः पाव॒काः । प्र णो॑ऽवत सुम॒तिभि॑र्यजत्रा॒: प्र वाजे॑भिस्तिरत पु॒ष्यसे॑ नः

Sukta 57.translation: “May the glorifiedMarutspartake of the oblations, they who, accompanied by the bending waters, arethe leaders of rites; bestow water, Maruts, upon our progeny, return suitable opulence for (the donation ofsacrificial) riches.”
Sukta 57.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्तु॒तासो॑ म॒रुतो॑ व्यन्तु॒ विश्वे॑भि॒र्नाम॑भि॒र्नरो॑ ह॒वींषि॑ । ददा॑त नो अ॒मृत॑स्य प्र॒जायै॑ जिगृ॒त रा॒यः सू॒नृता॑ म॒घानि॑

Sukta 57.translation: “GlorifiedMaruts, do you all come at the time of sacrifice to the presence of the worshippers along withyour protections, for you are they who, of your own will, multiply our hundreds; do you ever cherish us withblessings.”
Sukta 57.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ स्तु॒तासो॑ मरुतो॒ विश्व॑ ऊ॒ती अच्छा॑ सू॒रीन्त्स॒र्वता॑ता जिगात । ये न॒स्त्मना॑ श॒तिनो॑ व॒र्धय॑न्ति यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 58.translation: “Offer worship to the company (of theMaruts), the associated dispensers of moisture, which is powerfulover the celestial region; the Maruts, by their greatness, oppress both heaven and earth; they spread from theearth and the firmament to heaven.”

Sukta 59.translation: “The man,Maruts, who wounds our feelings, he who, rebuked by all, yet seeks,Vasus, to kill us, hewoudl bind us in the wounds of (Varuṇa), the avenger (of iniquity), such a man do you destroy with a consumingfatal weapon.”
Sukta 59.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यो नो॑ मरुतो अ॒भि दु॑र्हृणा॒युस्ति॒रश्चि॒त्तानि॑ वसवो॒ जिघां॑सति । द्रु॒हः पाशा॒न्प्रति॒ स मु॑चीष्ट॒ तपि॑ष्ठेन॒ हन्म॑ना हन्तना॒ तम्

devanagari.text: सांतपना इदं हविर्मरुतस्तज्जुजुष्टन ।युष्माकोती रिशादसः ॥
साम्ऽतपनाः । इदम् । हविः । मरुतः । तत् । जुजुष्टन ।युष्माक । ऊती । रिशादसः ॥

transliteration.text: sā́m-tapanāḥ ǀ idám ǀ havíḥ ǀ márutaḥ ǀ tát ǀ jujuṣṭana ǀyuṣmā́ka ǀ ūtī́ ǀ riśādasaḥ ǁ

Sukta 59.translation: “Maruts, desroyers of foes, this oblaion is designed for you; do you, who are the devourers of enemies,(coming) with your protections, graciously accept it.”
Sukta 59.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सांत॑पना इ॒दं ह॒विर्मरु॑त॒स्तज्जु॑जुष्टन । यु॒ष्माको॒ती रि॑शादसः

devanagari.text: गृहमेधास आ गत मरुतो माप भूतन ।युष्माकोती सुदानवः ॥
गृहऽमेधासः । आ । गत । मरुतः । मा । अप । भूतन ।युष्माक । ऊती । सुऽदानवः ॥

transliteration.text: gṛ́ha-medhāsaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gata ǀ márutaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ápa ǀ bhūtana ǀyuṣmā́ka ǀ ūtī́ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǁ

Sukta 59.translation: “Objects of domestic worship, munificentMaruts, come with your protections; go not away.”
Sukta 59.sanskrit_wisdomlib: गृह॑मेधास॒ आ ग॑त॒ मरु॑तो॒ माप॑ भूतन । यु॒ष्माको॒ती सु॑दानवः

devanagari.text: इहेह वः स्वतवसः कवयः सूर्यत्वचः ।यज्ञं मरुत आ वृणे ॥
इहऽइह । वः । स्वऽतवसः । कवयः । सूर्यऽत्वचः ।यज्ञम् । मरुतः । आ । वृणे ॥

transliteration.text: ihá-iha ǀ vaḥ ǀ sva-tavasaḥ ǀ kávayaḥ ǀ sū́rya-tvacaḥ ǀyajñám ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṇe ǁ

Sukta 59.translation: “Maruts, of independent strength, who are far-seeing, glorious as the sun, come hither, come hither, Iinvoke you to the sacrifice.”
Sukta 59.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒हेह॑ वः स्वतवस॒: कव॑य॒: सूर्य॑त्वचः । य॒ज्ञं म॑रुत॒ आ वृ॑णे

devanagari.text: त्र्यंबकं यजामहे सुगंधिं पुष्टिवर्धनं ।उर्वारुकमिव बंधनान्मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात् ॥
त्रिऽअम्बकम् । यजामहे । सुऽगन्धिम् । पुष्टिऽवर्धनम् ।उर्वारुकम्ऽइव । बन्धनात् । मृत्योः । मुक्षीय । मा । अमृतात् ॥

transliteration.text: trí-ambakam ǀ yajāmahe ǀ su-gándhim ǀ puṣṭi-várdhanam ǀurvārukám-iva ǀ bándhanāt ǀ mṛtyóḥ ǀ mukṣīya ǀ mā́ ǀ amṛ́tāt ǁ

Sukta 59.translation: “We worshipTryambaka, whose fame is fragrant, the augmenter of increase; may I be liberated fromdeath, and, like theurvārukafrom its stalk, but not to immortality; let us worshipTrayambaka, whose fame isfragrant, the augmenter of increase; may I be liberated from death like the urvāruka from its stalk, but not untoimmortality.”
Sukta 59.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्र्य॑म्बकं यजामहे सु॒गन्धिं॑ पुष्टि॒वर्ध॑नम् । उ॒र्वा॒रु॒कमि॑व॒ बन्ध॑नान्मृ॒त्योर्मु॑क्षीय॒ मामृता॑त्

devanagari.text: यदद्य सूर्य ब्रवोऽनागा उद्यन्मित्राय वरुणाय सत्यं ।वयं देवत्रादिते स्याम तव प्रियासो अर्यमन्गृणंतः ॥
यत् । अद्य । सूर्य । ब्रवः । अनागाः । उत्ऽयन् । मित्राय । वरुणाय । सत्यम् ।वयम् । देवऽत्रा । अदिते । स्याम । तव । प्रियासः । अर्यमन् । गृणन्तः ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ adyá ǀ sūrya ǀ brávaḥ ǀ ánāgāḥ ǀ ut-yán ǀ mitrā́ya ǀ váruṇāya ǀ satyám ǀvayám ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ adite ǀ syāma ǀ táva ǀ priyā́saḥ ǀ aryaman ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “Sūrya, when rising today, declare the truḥ toMitraandVaruṇa, that we are void of sin; may we,Aditi,be (approved of) among the gods; praising you,Aryaman, may we be dear to you.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद॒द्य सू॑र्य॒ ब्रवोऽना॑गा उ॒द्यन्मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय स॒त्यम् । व॒यं दे॑व॒त्रादि॑ते स्याम॒ तव॑ प्रि॒यासो॑ अर्यमन्गृ॒णन्त॑:

devanagari.text: एष स्य मित्रावरुणा नृचक्षा उभे उदेति सूर्यो अभि ज्मन् ।विश्वस्य स्थातुर्जगतश्च गोपा ऋजु मर्तेषु वृजिना च पश्यन् ॥
एषः । स्यः । मित्रावरुणा । नृऽचक्षाः । उभे इति । उत् । एति । सूर्यः । अभि । ज्मन् ।विश्वस्य । स्थातुः । जगतः । च । गोपाः । ऋजु । मर्तेषु । वृजिना । च । पश्यन् ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ syáḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ nṛ-cákṣāḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ út ǀ eti ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ jmán ǀvíśvasya ǀ sthātúḥ ǀ jágataḥ ǀ ca ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ ṛjú ǀ márteṣu ǀ vṛjinā́ ǀ ca ǀ páśyan ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “ThisSūrya, the beholder of man, rises,MitraandVaruṇa, upon both (heaven and earth), moving (inthe sky); he who is the preserver of all that is stationary or moveable, witnessing the upright acts or the sins ofmortals.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष स्य मि॑त्रावरुणा नृ॒चक्षा॑ उ॒भे उदे॑ति॒ सूर्यो॑ अ॒भि ज्मन् । विश्व॑स्य स्था॒तुर्जग॑तश्च गो॒पा ऋ॒जु मर्ते॑षु वृजि॒ना च॒ पश्य॑न्

devanagari.text: अयुक्त सप्त हरितः सधस्थाद्या ईं वहंति सूर्यं घृताचीः ।धामानि मित्रावरुणा युवाकुः सं यो यूथेव जनिमानि चष्टे ॥
अयुक्त । सप्त । हरितः । सधऽस्थात् । याः । ईम् । वहन्ति । सूर्यम् । घृताचीः ।धामानि । मित्रावरुणा । युवाकुः । सम् । यः । यूथाऽइव । जनिमानि । चष्टे ॥

transliteration.text: áyukta ǀ saptá ǀ harítaḥ ǀ sadhá-sthāt ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ īm ǀ váhanti ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ghṛtā́cīḥ ǀdhā́māni ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ yuvā́kuḥ ǀ sám ǀ yáḥ ǀ yūthā́-iva ǀ jánimāni ǀ cáṣṭe ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “He has harnessed his seven bay steeds,MitraandVaruṇa, (to come) from your commondwelling-plural ce, (the firmament); the horses that, shedding water, convey thatSūryawho, friendly to you both,(contemplates all) regions, and looks carefully upon living creatures as (a herdsman) upon the herd.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अयु॑क्त स॒प्त ह॒रित॑: स॒धस्था॒द्या ईं॒ वह॑न्ति॒ सूर्यं॑ घृ॒ताची॑: । धामा॑नि मित्रावरुणा यु॒वाकु॒: सं यो यू॒थेव॒ जनि॑मानि॒ चष्टे॑

devanagari.text: उद्वां पृक्षासो मधुमंतो अस्थुरा सूर्यो अरुहच्छुक्रमर्णः ।यस्मा आदित्या अध्वनो रदंति मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणः सजोषाः ॥
उत् । वाम् । पृक्षासः । मधुऽमन्तः । अस्थुः । आ । सूर्यः । अरुहत् । शुक्रम् । अर्णः ।यस्मै । आदित्याः । अध्वनः । रदन्ति । मित्रः । अर्यमा । वरुणः । सऽजोषाः ॥

transliteration.text: út ǀ vām ǀ pṛkṣā́saḥ ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ asthuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ aruhat ǀ śukrám ǀ árṇaḥ ǀyásmai ǀ ādityā́ḥ ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ rádanti ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “For yo, (MitraandVaruṇa), the sweet-flavoured viands have been prepared; the sun has ascended theshining firmament, for whom theĀdityasand the consentient Mitra, Varuṇa,Aryamanmake ready paths.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उद्वां॑ पृ॒क्षासो॒ मधु॑मन्तो अस्थु॒रा सूर्यो॑ अरुहच्छु॒क्रमर्ण॑: । यस्मा॑ आदि॒त्या अध्व॑नो॒ रद॑न्ति मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा वरु॑णः स॒जोषा॑:

devanagari.text: इमे चेतारो अनृतस्य भूरेर्मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो हि संति ।इम ऋतस्य वावृधुर्दुरोणे शग्मासः पुत्रा अदितेरदब्धाः ॥

transliteration.text: imé ǀ cetā́raḥ ǀ ánṛtasya ǀ bhū́reḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ hí ǀ sánti ǀimé ǀ ṛtásya ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ śagmā́saḥ ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ádabdhāḥ ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “These (deities),Mitra,Aryaman,Varuṇa, are the detecters of much untruth; these unconquered sons ofAditi, dispensers of happiness, are magnified in the hall of sacrifice.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मे चे॒तारो॒ अनृ॑तस्य॒ भूरे॑र्मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा वरु॑णो॒ हि सन्ति॑ । इ॒म ऋ॒तस्य॑ वावृधुर्दुरो॒णे श॒ग्मास॑: पु॒त्रा अदि॑ते॒रद॑ब्धाः

devanagari.text: इमे मित्रो वरुणो दूळभासोऽचेतसं चिच्चितयंति दक्षैः ।अपि क्रतुं सुचेतसं वतंतस्तिरश्चिदंहः सुपथा नयंति ॥
इमे । मित्रः । वरुणः । दुःऽदभासः । अचेतसम् । चित् । चितयन्ति । दक्षैः ।अपि । क्रतुम् । सुऽचेतसम् । वतन्तः । तिरः । चित् । अंहः । सुऽपथा । नयन्ति ॥

transliteration.text: imé ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ duḥ-dábhāsaḥ ǀ acetásam ǀ cit ǀ citayanti ǀ dákṣaiḥ ǀápi ǀ krátum ǀ su-cétasam ǀ vátantaḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ cit ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ su-páthā ǀ nayanti ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “These, the unsubduedMitra,VaruṇaandAryaman, animate with energies the unconscious (sleepers);repairing tot he intelligent performer (of pious acts), they lead (him), by safe pahs (to heaven), removing alliniquity.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मे मि॒त्रो वरु॑णो दू॒ळभा॑सोऽचे॒तसं॑ चिच्चितयन्ति॒ दक्षै॑: । अपि॒ क्रतुं॑ सु॒चेत॑सं॒ वत॑न्तस्ति॒रश्चि॒दंह॑: सु॒पथा॑ नयन्ति

devanagari.text: इमे दिवो अनिमिषा पृथिव्याश्चिकित्वांसो अचेतसं नयंति ।प्रव्राजे चिन्नद्यो गाधमस्ति पारं नो अस्य विष्पितस्य पर्षन् ॥

transliteration.text: imé ǀ diváḥ ǀ áni-miṣā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ cikitvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ acetásam ǀ nayanti ǀpra-vrājé ǀ cit ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ gādhám ǀ asti ǀ pārám ǀ naḥ ǀ asyá ǀ viṣpitásya ǀ parṣan ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “(Beholding) with unclosing eyes, and cognizant (of the things) of heaven and earth, they conduct theignorant man (to duty); in the lowes depth of the river, (through them), there is a bottom; may they lead us to theopposite shore of the vast expanse.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इ॒मे दि॒वो अनि॑मिषा पृथि॒व्याश्चि॑कि॒त्वांसो॑ अचे॒तसं॑ नयन्ति । प्र॒व्रा॒जे चि॑न्न॒द्यो॑ गा॒धम॑स्ति पा॒रं नो॑ अ॒स्य वि॑ष्पि॒तस्य॑ पर्षन्

devanagari.text: यद्गोपावददितिः शर्म भद्रं मित्रो यच्छंति वरुणः सुदासे ।तस्मिन्ना तोकं तनयं दधाना मा कर्म देवहेळनं तुरासः ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ gopā́vat ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śárma ǀ bhadrám ǀ mitráḥ ǀ yácchanti ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ su-dā́se ǀtásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ tokám ǀ tánayam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ karma ǀ deva-héḷanam ǀ turāsaḥ ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “Including our sons and grandsons in that preserving and auspicious felicity whichAditi,MitraandVaruṇa confer upon the liberal donor (of the oblation), may we never, acting precipitately, incur the displeasureof the deities.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यद्गो॒पाव॒ददि॑ति॒: शर्म॑ भ॒द्रं मि॒त्रो यच्छ॑न्ति॒ वरु॑णः सु॒दासे॑ । तस्मि॒न्ना तो॒कं तन॑यं॒ दधा॑ना॒ मा क॑र्म देव॒हेळ॑नं तुरासः

devanagari.text: अव वेदिं होत्राभिर्यजेत रिपः काश्चिद्वरुणध्रुतः सः ।परि द्वेषोभिरर्यमा वृणक्तूरुं सुदासे वृषणा उ लोकं ॥
अव । वेदिम् । होत्राभिः । यजेत । रिपः । काः । चित् । वरुणऽध्रुतः । सः ।परि । द्वेषःऽभिः । अर्यमा । वृणक्तु । उरुम् । सुऽदासे । वृषणौ । ऊं इति । लोकम् ॥

transliteration.text: áva ǀ védim ǀ hótrābhiḥ ǀ yajeta ǀ rípaḥ ǀ kā́ḥ ǀ cit ǀ varuṇa-dhrútaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀpári ǀ dvéṣaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ vṛṇaktu ǀ urúm ǀ su-dā́se ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “Let my adversary desecrate the altar by (ill-expressed) praises; repelled byVaruṇa, may he (undergo)various sufferings; mayAryamandefend us from those who hate us; confer, showerers (of benefits), a vastregion upon the liberal donor (of oblations).”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव॒ वेदिं॒ होत्रा॑भिर्यजेत॒ रिप॒: काश्चि॑द्वरुण॒ध्रुत॒: सः । परि॒ द्वेषो॑भिरर्य॒मा वृ॑णक्तू॒रुं सु॒दासे॑ वृषणा उ लो॒कम्

devanagari.text: सस्वश्चिद्धि समृतिस्त्वेष्येषामपीच्येन सहसा सहंते ।युष्मद्भिया वृषणो रेजमाना दक्षस्य चिन्महिना मृळता नः ॥

transliteration.text: sasváríti ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sám-ṛtiḥ ǀ tveṣī́ ǀ eṣām ǀ apīcyéna ǀ sáhasā ǀ sáhante ǀyuṣmát ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ vṛṣaṇaḥ ǀ réjamānāḥ ǀ dákṣasya ǀ cit ǀ mahinā́ ǀ mṛḷáta ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 60.translation: “The association of these (three deities) is of mysterious lustre; by their secret strength they overcome(all enemies); showerers (of benefits), through fear (of you our opponents) are trembling; have mercy upon us inthe mightiness of your strength.”
Sukta 60.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒स्वश्चि॒द्धि समृ॑तिस्त्वे॒ष्ये॑षामपी॒च्ये॑न॒ सह॑सा॒ सह॑न्ते । यु॒ष्मद्भि॒या वृ॑षणो॒ रेज॑माना॒ दक्ष॑स्य चिन्महि॒ना मृ॒ळता॑ नः

devanagari.text: यो ब्रह्मणे सुमतिमायजाते वाजस्य सातौ परमस्य रायः ।सीक्षंत मन्युं मघवानो अर्य उरु क्षयाय चक्रिरे सुधातु ॥
