Sukta 67.translation: “May the goat-bornePūṣanin all his paths be our protector; may he bestow maidens on us.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒वि॒ता नो॑ अ॒जाश्व॑: पू॒षा याम॑नियामनि । आ भ॑क्षत्क॒न्या॑सु नः

devanagari.text: अयं सोमः कपर्दिने घृतं न पवते मधु ।आ भक्षत्कन्यासु नः ॥
अयम् । सोमः । कपर्दिने । घृतम् । न । पवते । मधु ।आ । भक्षत् । कन्यासु । नः ॥

transliteration.text: ayám ǀ sómaḥ ǀ kapardíne ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ná ǀ pavate ǀ mádhu ǀā́ ǀ bhakṣat ǀ kanyā́su ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “ThisSomaflows toPūṣan, who wears a beautiful tiara like exhilarating ghī; may he bestow maidens on us.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं सोम॑: कप॒र्दिने॑ घृ॒तं न प॑वते॒ मधु॑ । आ भ॑क्षत्क॒न्या॑सु नः

devanagari.text: अयं त आघृणे सुतो घृतं न पवते शुचि ।आ भक्षत्कन्यासु नः ॥
अयम् । ते । आघृणे । सुतः । घृतम् । न । पवते । शुचि ।आ । भक्षत् । कन्यासु । नः ॥

transliteration.text: ayám ǀ te ǀ āghṛṇe ǀ sutáḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ná ǀ pavate ǀ śúci ǀā́ ǀ bhakṣat ǀ kanyā́su ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “ThisSomapoured for you, shining (Pūṣan) flows like pure ghī; may he bestow maidens on us.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं त॑ आघृणे सु॒तो घृ॒तं न प॑वते॒ शुचि॑ । आ भ॑क्षत्क॒न्या॑सु नः

devanagari.text: वाचो जंतुः कवीनां पवस्व सोम धारया ।देवेषु रत्नधा असि ॥
वाचः । जन्तुः । कवीनाम् । पवस्व । सोम । धारया ।देवेषु । रत्नऽधाः । असि ॥

transliteration.text: vācáḥ ǀ jantúḥ ǀ kavīnā́m ǀ pávasva ǀ soma ǀ dhā́rayā ǀdevéṣu ǀ ratna-dhā́ḥ ǀ asi ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Soma, genitive rator of the praises of the wise, flow in a stream; you are the dispenser of treasure among the gods.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वा॒चो ज॒न्तुः क॑वी॒नां पव॑स्व सोम॒ धार॑या । दे॒वेषु॑ रत्न॒धा अ॑सि

devanagari.text: आ कलशेषु धावति श्येनो वर्म वि गाहते ।अभि द्रोणा कनिक्रदत् ॥
आ । कलशेषु । धावति । श्येनः । वर्म । वि । गाहते ।अभि । द्रोणा । कनिक्रदत् ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ kaláśeṣu ǀ dhāvati ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ várma ǀ ví ǀ gāhate ǀabhí ǀ dróṇā ǀ kánikradat ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “He has flowed to the vessels as a falcon enters its nest and enters the wooden (vessels) with a cry.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ क॒लशे॑षु धावति श्ये॒नो वर्म॒ वि गा॑हते । अ॒भि द्रोणा॒ कनि॑क्रदत्

devanagari.text: परि प्र सोम ते रसोऽसर्जि कलशे सुतः ।श्येनो न तक्तो अर्षति ॥
परि । प्र । सोम । ते । रसः । असर्जि । कलशे । सुतः ।श्येनः । न । तक्तः । अर्षति ॥

transliteration.text: pári ǀ prá ǀ soma ǀ te ǀ rásaḥ ǀ ásarji ǀ kaláśe ǀ sutáḥ ǀśyenáḥ ǀ ná ǀ taktáḥ ǀ arṣati ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Your juice,Soma, spreads around when effused into the vessel as a swift falcon rushes along.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॒ प्र सो॑म ते॒ रसोऽस॑र्जि क॒लशे॑ सु॒तः । श्ये॒नो न त॒क्तो अ॑र्षति

devanagari.text: पवस्व सोम मंदयन्निंद्राय मधुमत्तमः ॥
पवस्व । सोम । मन्दयन् । इन्द्राय । मधुमत्ऽतमः ॥

transliteration.text: pávasva ǀ soma ǀ mandáyan ǀ índrāya ǀ mádhumat-tamaḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Flow,Soma, who are most sweet-flavoured, giving exhilaration toIndra.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑स्व सोम म॒न्दय॒न्निन्द्रा॑य॒ मधु॑मत्तमः

devanagari.text: असृग्रंदेववीतये वाजयंतो रथा इव ॥
असृग्रन् । देवऽवीतये । वाजऽयन्तः । रथाःऽइव ॥

transliteration.text: ásṛgran ǀ devá-vītaye ǀ vāja-yántaḥ ǀ ráthāḥ-iva ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “(TheSoma-juices) are let loose for the banquet of the gods like chariots desiring the wealth (of the enemy).”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: असृ॑ग्रन्दे॒ववी॑तये वाज॒यन्तो॒ रथा॑ इव

devanagari.text: ते सुतासो मदिंतमाः शुक्रा वायुमसृक्षत ॥
ते । सुतासः । मदिन्ऽतमाः । शुक्राः । वायुम् । असृक्षत ॥

transliteration.text: té ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ madín-tamāḥ ǀ śukrā́ḥ ǀ vāyúm ǀ asṛkṣata ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “These effused (Soma-juices), brilliant and extremely exhilarating, are let forth forVāyu.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते सु॒तासो॑ म॒दिन्त॑माः शु॒क्रा वा॒युम॑सृक्षत

devanagari.text: ग्राव्णा तुन्नो अभिष्टुतः पवित्रं सोम गच्छसि ।दधत्स्तोत्रे सुवीर्यं ॥
ग्राव्णा । तुन्नः । अभिऽस्तुतः । पवित्रम् । सोम । गच्छसि ।दधत् । स्तोत्रे । सुऽवीर्यम् ॥

transliteration.text: grā́vṇā ǀ tunnáḥ ǀ abhí-stutaḥ ǀ pavítram ǀ soma ǀ gacchasi ǀdádhat ǀ stotré ǀ su-vī́ryam ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Bruised with the stones and effused (by the worshippers), you,Soma; enter the filter, bestowing upon your praiser (wealth), accompanied with excellentmaleoffspring.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ग्राव्णा॑ तु॒न्नो अ॒भिष्टु॑तः प॒वित्रं॑ सोम गच्छसि । दध॑त्स्तो॒त्रे सु॒वीर्य॑म्

devanagari.text: एष तुन्नो अभिष्टुतः पवित्रमति गाहते ।रक्षोहा वारमव्ययं ॥
एषः । तुन्नः । अभिऽस्तुतः । पवित्रम् । अति । गाहते ।रक्षःऽहा । वारम् । अव्ययम् ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ tunnáḥ ǀ abhí-stutaḥ ǀ pavítram ǀ áti ǀ gāhate ǀrakṣaḥ-hā́ ǀ vā́ram ǀ avyáyam ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “This (Soma), bruised (with the stones), and praised by (all), the slayer ofrākṣasas, plural nge through the woollen filter (into the vessel).”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष तु॒न्नो अ॒भिष्टु॑तः प॒वित्र॒मति॑ गाहते । र॒क्षो॒हा वार॑म॒व्यय॑म्

devanagari.text: यदंति यच्च दूरके भयं विंदति मामिह ।पवमान वि तज्जहि ॥
यत् । अन्ति । यत् । च । दूरके । भयम् । विन्दति । माम् । इह ।पवमान । वि । तत् । जहि ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ ánti ǀ yát ǀ ca ǀ dūraké ǀ bhayám ǀ vindáti ǀ mā́m ǀ ihá ǀpávamāna ǀ ví ǀ tát ǀ jahi ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Whatever fear seizes me, near, afar off, or here, purified (Soma) dispel that (fear).”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यदन्ति॒ यच्च॑ दूर॒के भ॒यं वि॒न्दति॒ मामि॒ह । पव॑मान॒ वि तज्ज॑हि

devanagari.text: पवमानः सो अद्य नः पवित्रेण विचर्षणिः ।यः पोता स पुनातु नः ॥
पवमानः । सः । अद्य । नः । पवित्रेण । विऽचर्षणिः ।यः । पोता । सः । पुनातु । नः ॥

transliteration.text: pávamānaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ adyá ǀ naḥ ǀ pavítreṇa ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ potā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ punātu ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “May that purifiedSoma, the beholder of all, who is the purifier, purify us now by his purifying (might).”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑मान॒: सो अ॒द्य न॑: प॒वित्रे॑ण॒ विच॑र्षणिः । यः पो॒ता स पु॑नातु नः

devanagari.text: यत्ते पवित्रमर्चिष्यग्ने विततमंतरा ।ब्रह्म तेन पुनीहि नः ॥
यत् । ते । पवित्रम् । अर्चिषि । अग्ने । विऽततम् । अन्तः । आ ।ब्रह्म । तेन । पुनीहि । नः ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ te ǀ pavítram ǀ arcíṣi ǀ ágne ǀ ví-tatam ǀ antáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀbráhma ǀ téna ǀ punīhi ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Purify,Agni, our divine (body) with your purifying (light), which is diffused in the midst of the light.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यत्ते॑ प॒वित्र॑म॒र्चिष्यग्ने॒ वित॑तम॒न्तरा । ब्रह्म॒ तेन॑ पुनीहि नः

devanagari.text: यत्ते पवित्रमर्चिवदग्ने तेन पुनीहि नः ।ब्रह्मसवैः पुनीहि नः ॥
यत् । ते । पवित्रम् । अर्चिऽवत् । अग्ने । तेन । पुनीहि । नः ।ब्रह्मऽसवैः । पुनीहि । नः ॥

transliteration.text: yát ǀ te ǀ pavítram ǀ arci-vát ǀ ágne ǀ téna ǀ punīhi ǀ naḥ ǀbrahma-saváiḥ ǀ punīhi ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Purify us,Agni, with your purifying (light) which possesses the light; purify us with the effusion of theSoma.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यत्ते॑ प॒वित्र॑मर्चि॒वदग्ने॒ तेन॑ पुनीहि नः । ब्र॒ह्म॒स॒वैः पु॑नीहि नः

devanagari.text: उभाभ्यां देव सवितः पवित्रेण सवेन च ।मां पुनीहि विश्वतः ॥
उभाभ्याम् । देव । सवितः । पवित्रेण । सवेन । च ।माम् । पुनीहि । विश्वतः ॥

transliteration.text: ubhā́bhyām ǀ deva ǀ savitaḥ ǀ pavítreṇa ǀ savéna ǀ ca ǀmā́m ǀ punīhi ǀ viśvátaḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Shining (Soma), urger of all things, purify me by both, by your purifying (light) and by the effusion (of the Soma); purify me in every way”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒भाभ्यां॑ देव सवितः प॒वित्रे॑ण स॒वेन॑ च । मां पु॑नीहि वि॒श्वत॑:

devanagari.text: त्रिभिष्ट्वं देव सवितर्वर्षिष्ठैः सोम धामभिः ।अग्ने दक्षैः पुनीहि नः ॥
त्रिऽभिः । त्वम् । देव । सवितः । वर्षिष्ठैः । सोम । धामऽभिः ।अग्ने । दक्षैः । पुनीहि । नः ॥

transliteration.text: tri-bhíḥ ǀ tvám ǀ deva ǀ savitaḥ ǀ várṣiṣṭhaiḥ ǀ soma ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǀágne ǀ dákṣaiḥ ǀ punīhi ǀ naḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Purify us, shiningAgniPavamāna, urger of all things, with your three most mighty powerful forms.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्रि॒भिष्ट्वं दे॑व सवित॒र्वर्षि॑ष्ठैः सोम॒ धाम॑भिः । अग्ने॒ दक्षै॑: पुनीहि नः

devanagari.text: पुनंतु मां देवजनाः पुनंतु वसवो धिया ।विश्वे देवाः पुनीत मा जातवेदः पुनीहि मा ॥
पुनन्तु । माम् । देवऽजनाः । पुनन्तु । वसवः । धिया ।विश्वे । देवाः । पुनीत । मा । जातऽवेदः । पुनीहि । मा ॥

transliteration.text: punántu ǀ mā́m ǀ deva-janā́ḥ ǀ punántu ǀ vásavaḥ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀvíśve ǀ devāḥ ǀ punītá ǀ mā ǀ jā́ta-vedaḥ ǀ punīhí ǀ mā ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “May the worshippers purify me, may theVasuspurify (me) by their acts; purify me, all you gods, (Agni) the intelligent purify me.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पु॒नन्तु॒ मां दे॑वज॒नाः पु॒नन्तु॒ वस॑वो धि॒या । विश्वे॑ देवाः पुनी॒त मा॒ जात॑वेदः पुनी॒हि मा॑

devanagari.text: प्र प्यायस्व प्र स्यंदस्व सोम विश्वेभिरंशुभिः ।देवेभ्य उत्तमं हविः ॥
प्र । प्यायस्व । प्र । स्यन्दस्व । सोम । विश्वेभिः । अंशुऽभिः ।देवेभ्यः । उत्ऽतमम् । हविः ॥

transliteration.text: prá ǀ pyāyasva ǀ prá ǀ syandasva ǀ sóma ǀ víśvebhiḥ ǀ aṃśú-bhiḥ ǀdevébhyaḥ ǀ ut-tamám ǀ havíḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Soma, nourish (us), pour forth for the gods with all your juices the most excellent oblation.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र प्या॑यस्व॒ प्र स्य॑न्दस्व॒ सोम॒ विश्वे॑भिरं॒शुभि॑: । दे॒वेभ्य॑ उत्त॒मं ह॒विः

devanagari.text: उप प्रियं पनिप्नतं युवानमाहुतीवृधं ।अगन्म बिभ्रतो नमः ॥
उप । प्रियम् । पनिप्नतम् । युवानम् । आहुतिऽवृधम् ।अगन्म । बिभ्रतः । नमः ॥

transliteration.text: úpa ǀ priyám ǀ pánipnatam ǀ yúvānam ǀ āhuti-vṛ́dham ǀáganma ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ námaḥ ǁ

Sukta 67.translation: “Let us approach bearing the beloved loud-sounding youthful oblation fostered by our offerings.”

Sukta 67.translation: “May the battle-axe of the foe destroy the foe; alone flow tous, brightSoma; (slay) the villain only, bright Soma.”

devanagari.text: यः पावमानीरध्येत्यृषिभिः संभृतं रसं ।सर्वं स पूतमश्नाति स्वदितं मातरिश्वना ॥

Sukta 67.translation: “He who reads the hymns toPavamāna, the essence (of theVeda) collected by the ṛṣis, enjoys all (his food) purified, sweetened byMātariśvan.”
Sukta 67.sanskrit_wisdomlib: यः पा॑वमा॒नीर॒ध्येत्यृषि॑भि॒: सम्भृ॑तं॒ रस॑म् । सर्वं॒ स पू॒तम॑श्नाति स्वदि॒तं मा॑त॒रिश्व॑ना

Sukta 68.translation: “The exhilaratingSoma-juices flow towards the shining (Indra), as kine (have to their calves); the lowing kine sitting on thebarhisgrass hold in their udders the pure (juice) welling up.”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र दे॒वमच्छा॒ मधु॑मन्त॒ इन्द॒वोऽसि॑ष्यदन्त॒ गाव॒ आ न धे॒नव॑: । ब॒र्हि॒षदो॑ वच॒नाव॑न्त॒ ऊध॑भिः परि॒स्रुत॑मु॒स्रिया॑ नि॒र्णिजं॑ धिरे

Sukta 68.translation: “He with a noise re-echoes the principal (praises), separating the growing herbs, the green-tinted (Soma) sweetens them; passing through the filter, (he exerts) great speed, he annihilates therākṣasas, the shining (Soma) bestows wealth (upon the worshippers).”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स रोरु॑वद॒भि पूर्वा॑ अचिक्रददुपा॒रुह॑: श्र॒थय॑न्त्स्वादते॒ हरि॑: । ति॒रः प॒वित्रं॑ परि॒यन्नु॒रु ज्रयो॒ नि शर्या॑णि दधते दे॒व आ वर॑म्

Sukta 68.translation: “The exhilarating (Soma) who constructed the twin united (heaven and earth) does by means of his juice maintain them growing together, imperishable; he has distinguished these two great unbounded worlds, wandering everywhere, he has assumed imperishable strength.”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि यो म॒मे य॒म्या॑ संय॒ती मद॑: साकं॒वृधा॒ पय॑सा पिन्व॒दक्षि॑ता । म॒ही अ॑पा॒रे रज॑सी वि॒वेवि॑ददभि॒व्रज॒न्नक्षि॑तं॒ पाज॒ आ द॑दे

Sukta 68.translation: “The wise (Soma) wandering through the two worlds, sending forth the waters, flattens his station with food; the Soma-juice collected by the priests is mixed with the barley; it is united by the fingers; it protects the head.”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स मा॒तरा॑ वि॒चर॑न्वा॒जय॑न्न॒पः प्र मेधि॑रः स्व॒धया॑ पिन्वते प॒दम् । अं॒शुर्यवे॑न पिपिशे य॒तो नृभि॒: सं जा॒मिभि॒र्नस॑ते॒ रक्ष॑ते॒ शिर॑:

Sukta 68.translation: “The sage (Soma) is born with developed mind; having his plural ce in the womb of the water, he is deposited (by the gods) by rule from far off; even when young these two were distinct; the birth (of one half) was plural ced in secret, the (other) half was visible.”

Sukta 68.translation: “The wise (worshippers) know the form of the exhilaratingSoma-juice, the food that the falcon brought from afar; they cleanse in the waters the fostering (Soma) delighting (the gods), flowing around, and deserving laudation.”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒न्द्रस्य॑ रू॒पं वि॑विदुर्मनी॒षिण॑: श्ये॒नो यदन्धो॒ अभ॑रत्परा॒वत॑: । तं म॑र्जयन्त सु॒वृधं॑ न॒दीष्वाँ उ॒शन्त॑मं॒शुं प॑रि॒यन्त॑मृ॒ग्मिय॑म्

Sukta 68.translation: “The ten fingers cleanse you,Soma, when effused and plural ced in the vessels by the ṛṣis, with praises, religious rites and woollen filters; and collected by the priests with oblations to the gods you bestow food (upon the worshippers) for a gift.”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वां मृ॑जन्ति॒ दश॒ योष॑णः सु॒तं सोम॒ ऋषि॑भिर्म॒तिभि॑र्धी॒तिभि॑र्हि॒तम् । अव्यो॒ वारे॑भिरु॒त दे॒वहू॑तिभि॒र्नृभि॑र्य॒तो वाज॒मा द॑र्षि सा॒तये॑

Sukta 68.translation: “Intelligent praises celebrate the wide-flowing (god) delightingSomawho sits in good company, who exhilarating (falls) in a stream with his water from the sky (and) wealth-conquering, immortal, sends out his voice.”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प॒रि॒प्र॒यन्तं॑ व॒य्यं॑ सुषं॒सदं॒ सोमं॑ मनी॒षा अ॒भ्य॑नूषत॒ स्तुभ॑: । यो धार॑या॒ मधु॑माँ ऊ॒र्मिणा॑ दि॒व इय॑र्ति॒ वाचं॑ रयि॒षाळम॑र्त्यः

Sukta 68.translation: “ThisSomasends from heaven all water; bring filtered he settles in the vessels; effused with the stones, he is cleansed with water and milk; the filteredIndubestow delightful wealth.”
Sukta 68.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं दि॒व इ॑यर्ति॒ विश्व॒मा रज॒: सोम॑: पुना॒नः क॒लशे॑षु सीदति । अ॒द्भिर्गोभि॑र्मृज्यते॒ अद्रि॑भिः सु॒तः पु॑ना॒न इन्दु॒र्वरि॑वो विदत्प्रि॒यम्

Sukta 68.translation: “Somaoffering (wealth) as soon as you are sprinkled (with the water and milk), pour various kinds of food (upon us); let us invoke the friendly heaven and earth; do you, O gods, grant us wealth with excellentmaleoffspring.”

Sukta 69.translation: “(Our) praise is attached (toIndra) as an arrow to the bow; (theSoma-juice) is let loose to (Indra) the fosterer as a calf to the udder to its mother; (Indra sheds blessings) as a cow having a copious stream of milk yields it when coming into the presence (of the calf); in Indra's sacrifices the Soma is stimulated.”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इषु॒र्न धन्व॒न्प्रति॑ धीयते म॒तिर्व॒त्सो न मा॒तुरुप॑ स॒र्ज्यूध॑नि । उ॒रुधा॑रेव दुहे॒ अग्र॑ आय॒त्यस्य॑ व्र॒तेष्वपि॒ सोम॑ इष्यते

Sukta 69.translation: “The praise is united (toIndra); the excellent (Soma) is sprinkled; (the Soma stream) emitting plural asant juice is driven into (Indra's) mouth; the filtered diffused exhilarating swift-flowing (Soma) hastens to the fleece like the arrow of the combatants.”

Sukta 69.translation: “(Soma) seeking his spouse is filtered in the sheep-skin; he separates his grand-daughter on the earth for the sacrificer; green-tinted, adorable, collected (in the ladles), exhilarating, he overcomes (his foes); sharpening his vigour he shines like one of might.”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव्ये॑ वधू॒युः प॑वते॒ परि॑ त्व॒चि श्र॑थ्नी॒ते न॒प्तीरदि॑तेॠ॒तं य॒ते । हरि॑रक्रान्यज॒तः सं॑य॒तो मदो॑ नृ॒म्णा शिशा॑नो महि॒षो न शो॑भते

Sukta 69.translation: “The bull lows, the cows flow around him; the divine (praises) gather round the station of the radiant (Soma); Soma passes through the white sheep-skin; he clothes himself with it as it were a burnished armouṛ ”

Sukta 69.translation: “The immortal green-tintedSomawhen purified is arranged in an uncleaned shining vestment; he ahs created (Āditya) who stands on the back of the sky for the destruction (of sin) and purification, (and has created) Āditya's brilliance, the cover of the two worlds.”

Sukta 69.translation: “The rushing exhilarating foe-slayingSoma-juices when let loose flow together round the extended cloth like the sun's rays; they flow to no other person n exceptIndra.”

Sukta 69.translation: “The exhilarating (Soma-juices) poured forth by the sprinklers effect their way toIndraas in a waterfall of a river the percvading (waters find their way) to dry ground; bless on our return our two-footed and four-footed things; may food and offspring ever abide with us.”

Sukta 69.translation: “Pour upon us (wealth) comprising treasure, gold, horses, cattle, barley, and excellentmaleoffspring; you,Somaare my progenitors, the chiefs of heaven, plural ced (for sacrificial), the offerers of oblation.”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ न॑: पवस्व॒ वसु॑म॒द्धिर॑ण्यव॒दश्वा॑व॒द्गोम॒द्यव॑मत्सु॒वीर्य॑म् । यू॒यं हि सो॑म पि॒तरो॒ मम॒ स्थन॑ दि॒वो मू॒र्धान॒: प्रस्थि॑ता वय॒स्कृत॑:

Sukta 69.translation: “These filteredSoma-juices advance toIndraworthy of honour, as (Indra's) chariots advance to battle; expressed (with the stones) they pass through the woollen filter, casting off infirmity the horses go towards the rain.”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ते सोमा॒: पव॑मानास॒ इन्द्रं॒ रथा॑ इव॒ प्र य॑युः सा॒तिमच्छ॑ । सु॒ताः प॒वित्र॒मति॑ य॒न्त्यव्यं॑ हि॒त्वी व॒व्रिं ह॒रितो॑ वृ॒ष्टिमच्छ॑

Sukta 69.translation: “Indu, who do make (men) very happy, the blameless one, the destroyer of foes, flow for mightyIndra; bring to (me) your worshipper gratifying riches; heaven and earth, protect us with auspicious (riches).”
Sukta 69.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द॒विन्द्रा॑य बृह॒ते प॑वस्व सुमृळी॒को अ॑नव॒द्यो रि॒शादा॑: । भरा॑ च॒न्द्राणि॑ गृण॒ते वसू॑नि दे॒वैर्द्या॑वापृथिवी॒ प्राव॑तं नः

devanagari.text: त्रिरस्मै सप्त धेनवो दुदुह्रे सत्यामाशिरं पूर्व्ये व्योमनि ।चत्वार्यन्या भुवनानि निर्णिजे चारूणि चक्रे यदृतैरवर्धत ॥

Sukta 70.translation: “For him in the ancient sacrifice thrice seven kine milk forth the right mixture; he makes four other beautiful waters for purification when he is nourished with the sacrifices.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्रिर॑स्मै स॒प्त धे॒नवो॑ दुदुह्रे स॒त्यामा॒शिरं॑ पू॒र्व्ये व्यो॑मनि । च॒त्वार्य॒न्या भुव॑नानि नि॒र्णिजे॒ चारू॑णि चक्रे॒ यदृ॒तैरव॑र्धत

devanagari.text: स भिक्षमाणो अमृतस्य चारुण उभे द्यावा काव्येना वि शश्रथे ।तेजिष्ठा अपो मंहना परि व्यत यदी देवस्य श्रवसा सदो विदुः ॥

Sukta 70.translation: “He being solicited for auspicious ambrosia opens both heaven and earth by his intelligence, he covers the lustrious waters with his greatness, when (the priests) with the oblation recognize the station of the radiant (Soma).”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स भिक्ष॑माणो अ॒मृत॑स्य॒ चारु॑ण उ॒भे द्यावा॒ काव्ये॑ना॒ वि श॑श्रथे । तेजि॑ष्ठा अ॒पो मं॒हना॒ परि॑ व्यत॒ यदी॑ दे॒वस्य॒ श्रव॑सा॒ सदो॑ वि॒दुः

Sukta 70.translation: “May those his immortal, inviolable rays protect both classes of beings, wherewith he stimulates human (strength) and divine (food); thereupon praises reach the royal (Soma).”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते अ॑स्य सन्तु के॒तवोऽमृ॑त्य॒वोऽदा॑भ्यासो ज॒नुषी॑ उ॒भे अनु॑ । येभि॑र्नृ॒म्णा च॑ दे॒व्या॑ च पुन॒त आदिद्राजा॑नं म॒नना॑ अगृभ्णत

Sukta 70.translation: “Cleansed by the ten well-working (fingers), the companion (of the waters) stands among the midmost mothers to measure (the worlds); the beholder of men protecting sacred rites (for the sake) of auspicious ambrosia looks after both races.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स मृ॒ज्यमा॑नो द॒शभि॑: सु॒कर्म॑भि॒: प्र म॑ध्य॒मासु॑ मा॒तृषु॑ प्र॒मे सचा॑ । व्र॒तानि॑ पा॒नो अ॒मृत॑स्य॒ चारु॑ण उ॒भे नृ॒चक्षा॒ अनु॑ पश्यते॒ विशौ॑

devanagari.text: स मर्मृजान इंद्रियाय धायस ओभे अंता रोदसी हर्षते हितः ।वृषा शुष्मेण बाधते वि दुर्मतीरादेदिशानः शर्यहेव शुरुधः ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ marmṛjānáḥ ǀ indriyā́ya ǀ dhā́yase ǀ ā́ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ antáríti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ harṣate ǀ hitáḥ ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ śúṣmeṇa ǀ bādhate ǀ ví ǀ duḥ-matī́ḥ ǀ ādédiśānaḥ ǀ śaryahā́-iva ǀ śurúdhaḥ ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “Being filtered forIndra's world-supporting strength, stationed in the midst of both worlds he goes (everywhere); the showerer destroys the evil-minded by his vigour, challenging theasuraslike an archer.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स म॑र्मृजा॒न इ॑न्द्रि॒याय॒ धाय॑स॒ ओभे अ॒न्ता रोद॑सी हर्षते हि॒तः । वृषा॒ शुष्मे॑ण बाधते॒ वि दु॑र्म॒तीरा॒देदि॑शानः शर्य॒हेव॑ शु॒रुध॑:

devanagari.text: स मातरा न ददृशान उस्रियो नानददेति मरुतामिव स्वनः ।जानन्नृतं प्रथमं यत्स्वर्णरं प्रशस्तये कमवृणीत सुक्रतुः ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ mātárā ǀ ná ǀ dádṛśānaḥ ǀ usríyaḥ ǀ nā́nadat ǀ eti ǀ marútām-iva ǀ svanáḥ ǀjānán ǀ ṛtám ǀ prathamám ǀ yát ǀ sváḥ-naram ǀ prá-śastaye ǀ kám ǀ avṛṇīta ǀ su-krátuḥ ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “He repeatedly beholding his parents (heaven and earth) proceeds with a loud noise, like cows (looking at their calves and lowing), and with a roar (like the troop) ofMaruts; knowing that water to be the best which is good for all men, the intelligent (pavamāna) chose man to be the offerer of his praise.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स मा॒तरा॒ न ददृ॑शान उ॒स्रियो॒ नान॑ददेति म॒रुता॑मिव स्व॒नः । जा॒नन्नृ॒तं प्र॑थ॒मं यत्स्व॑र्णरं॒ प्रश॑स्तये॒ कम॑वृणीत सु॒क्रतु॑:

devanagari.text: रुवति भीमो वृषभस्तविष्यया शृंगे शिशानो हरिणी विचक्षणः ।आ योनिं सोमः सुकृतं नि षीदति गव्ययी त्वग्भवति निर्णिगव्ययी ॥

Sukta 70.translation: “The formidable showerer, the contemplator of all through desire for strength roars, sharpening his green-tinted horns; theSomasettles on his well-prepared station; the cowhide is his cleanser and the sheep-skin (too).”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रु॒वति॑ भी॒मो वृ॑ष॒भस्त॑वि॒ष्यया॒ शृङ्गे॒ शिशा॑नो॒ हरि॑णी विचक्ष॒णः । आ योनिं॒ सोम॒: सुकृ॑तं॒ नि षी॑दति ग॒व्ययी॒ त्वग्भ॑वति नि॒र्णिग॒व्ययी॑

transliteration.text: śúciḥ ǀ punānáḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ arepásam ǀ ávye ǀ háriḥ ǀ ní ǀ adhāviṣṭa ǀ sā́navi ǀjúṣṭaḥ ǀ mitrā́ya ǀ váruṇāya ǀ vāyáve ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ mádhu ǀ kriyate ǀ sukárma-bhiḥ ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “Brilliant cleansing his sinless body, the green-tinted (Soma) is plural ced on the high-plural ced fleece; sufficient forMitra,Varuṇa, andVāyuthe exhilarating (Soma) mixed with the three ingredients is prepared by the performers of good rites.”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शुचि॑: पुना॒नस्त॒न्व॑मरे॒पस॒मव्ये॒ हरि॒र्न्य॑धाविष्ट॒ सान॑वि । जुष्टो॑ मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय वा॒यवे॑ त्रि॒धातु॒ मधु॑ क्रियते सु॒कर्म॑भिः

devanagari.text: पवस्व सोम देववीतये वृषेंद्रस्य हार्दि सोमधानमा विश ।पुरा नो बाधाद्दुरिताति पारय क्षेत्रविद्धि दिश आहा विपृच्छते ॥

transliteration.text: pávasva ǀ soma ǀ devá-vītaye ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ índrasya ǀ hā́rdi ǀ soma-dhā́nam ǀ ā́ ǀ viśa ǀpurā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bādhā́t ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ áti ǀ pāraya ǀ kṣetra-vít ǀ hí ǀ díśaḥ ǀ ā́ha ǀ vi-pṛcchaté ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “FlowSoma, the showerer, for the banquet for the gods; enter the Soma-vessel dear toIndra; bring us safe past the hostile (rākṣasas) before the oppress us; for he who knows the country tells the direction to him who asks (the way).”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑स्व सोम दे॒ववी॑तये॒ वृषेन्द्र॑स्य॒ हार्दि॑ सोम॒धान॒मा वि॑श । पु॒रा नो॑ बा॒धाद्दु॑रि॒ताति॑ पारय क्षेत्र॒विद्धि दिश॒ आहा॑ विपृच्छ॒ते

devanagari.text: हितो न सप्तिरभि वाजमर्षेंद्रस्येंदो जठरमा पवस्व ।नावा न सिंधुमति पर्षि विद्वांछूरो न युध्यन्नव नो निदः स्पः ॥

transliteration.text: hitáḥ ǀ ná ǀ sáptiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vā́jam ǀ arṣa ǀ índrasya ǀ indo íti ǀ jaṭháram ǀ ā́ ǀ pavasva ǀnāvā́ ǀ ná ǀ síndhum ǀ áti ǀ parṣi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ yúdhyan ǀ áva ǀ naḥ ǀ nidáḥ ǀ sparíti spaḥ ǁ

Sukta 70.translation: “Hasten (to the vessel) as a horse when urged (hastens) to the battle; flowInduintoIndra's belly; all knowing (Soma) bear us (safe) across, as (boatmen bear people) across a river in a boat; fighting like a hero, defend us from the reviling (of the foe).”
Sukta 70.sanskrit_wisdomlib: हि॒तो न सप्ति॑र॒भि वाज॑म॒र्षेन्द्र॑स्येन्दो ज॒ठर॒मा प॑वस्व । ना॒वा न सिन्धु॒मति॑ पर्षि वि॒द्वाञ्छूरो॒ न युध्य॒न्नव॑ नो नि॒दः स्प॑:

devanagari.text: आ दक्षिणा सृज्यते शुष्म्यासदं वेति द्रुहो रक्षसः पाति जागृविः ।हरिरोपशं कृणुते नभस्पय उपस्तिरे चम्वोर्ब्रह्म निर्णिजे ॥
आ । दक्षिणा । सृज्यते । शुष्मी । आऽसदम् । वेति । द्रुहः । रक्षसः । पाति । जागृविः ।हरिः । ओपशम् । कृणुते । नभः । पयः । उपऽस्तिरे । चम्वोः । ब्रह्म । निःऽनिजे ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ sṛjyate ǀ śuṣmī́ ǀ ā-sádam ǀ véti ǀ druháḥ ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ pāti ǀ jā́gṛviḥ ǀháriḥ ǀ opaśám ǀ kṛṇute ǀ nábhaḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀ upa-stíre ǀ camvóḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ niḥ-níje ǁ

Sukta 71.translation: “The donation is given; the vigorous (Soma) enters his resting-plural ce, and, vigilant, guards (his worshippers) against the malignantrākṣasas; the green-tinted (Soma) produces the all-sustaining water of the sun; (he plural ces) the mighty sun to cover the two worlds, to purify (created things).”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ दक्षि॑णा सृज्यते शु॒ष्म्या॒३॒॑सदं॒ वेति॑ द्रु॒हो र॒क्षस॑: पाति॒ जागृ॑विः । हरि॑रोप॒शं कृ॑णुते॒ नभ॒स्पय॑ उप॒स्तिरे॑ च॒म्वो॒३॒॑र्ब्रह्म॑ नि॒र्णिजे॑

devanagari.text: प्र कृष्टिहेव शूष एति रोरुवदसुर्यं वर्णं नि रिणीते अस्य तं ।जहाति वव्रिं पितुरेति निष्कृतमुपप्रुतं कृणुते निर्णिजं तना ॥

Sukta 71.translation: “The powerful (Soma) advances with a roar like a slayer of men; he puts forth thatasura-slaying tint of his; he abandons bodily infirmity; the food goes to the prepared (altar); he assumes a form advancing to the outstretched (filter).”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र कृ॑ष्टि॒हेव॑ शू॒ष ए॑ति॒ रोरु॑वदसु॒र्यं१॒॑ वर्णं॒ नि रि॑णीते अस्य॒ तम् । जहा॑ति व॒व्रिं पि॒तुरे॑ति निष्कृ॒तमु॑प॒प्रुतं॑ कृणुते नि॒र्णिजं॒ तना॑

devanagari.text: अद्रिभिः सुतः पवते गभस्त्योर्वृषायते नभसा वेपते मती ।स मोदते नसते साधते गिरा नेनिक्ते अप्सु यजते परीमणि ॥

Sukta 71.translation: “Expressed with the stones by thehands(theSoma) flows; he moves like a bull; (worshipped) with praise he wanders through the firmament; he rejoices, he is embraced; (praised) with a hymn he fulfills (the desire of the worshippers), he is cleansed in the waters, he is honoured at the (god) protected (sacrifice).”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अद्रि॑भिः सु॒तः प॑वते॒ गभ॑स्त्योर्वृषा॒यते॒ नभ॑सा॒ वेप॑ते म॒ती । स मो॑दते॒ नस॑ते॒ साध॑ते गि॒रा ने॑नि॒क्ते अ॒प्सु यज॑ते॒ परी॑मणि

devanagari.text: परि द्युक्षं सहसः पर्वतावृधं मध्वः सिंचंति हर्म्यस्य सक्षणिं ।आ यस्मिन्गावः सुहुताद ऊधनि मूर्धंछ्रीणंत्यग्रियं वरीमभिः ॥
परि । द्युक्षम् । सहसः । पर्वतऽवृधम् । मध्वः । सिञ्चन्ति । हर्म्यस्य । सक्षणिम् ।आ । यस्मिन् । गावः । सुहुतऽअदः । ऊधनि । मूर्धन् । श्रीणन्ति । अग्रियम् । वरीमऽभिः ॥

Sukta 71.translation: “The powerful exhilaratingSoma-juices besprinkleIndrawho dwells in heaven, the augmenter of the clouds, the destroyer of the dwelling (of the foe); in whom on account of his greatness, the cows, the eaters of the oblations, mix the best (of their milk contained) in the uplifted udder.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॑ द्यु॒क्षं सह॑सः पर्वता॒वृधं॒ मध्व॑: सिञ्चन्ति ह॒र्म्यस्य॑ स॒क्षणि॑म् । आ यस्मि॒न्गाव॑: सुहु॒ताद॒ ऊध॑नि मू॒र्धञ्छ्री॒णन्त्य॑ग्रि॒यं वरी॑मभिः

devanagari.text: समी रथं न भुरिजोरहेषत दश स्वसारो अदितेरुपस्थ आ ।जिगादुप ज्रयति गोरपीच्यं पदं यदस्य मतुथा अजीजनन् ॥

Sukta 71.translation: “The ten fingers of the arms urge him near to the ground (of the sacrificial altar) like a chariot; he goes (to the vessels), he approaches the concealed (milk) of the cow when the praisers produce his resting plural ce.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: समी॒ रथं॒ न भु॒रिजो॑रहेषत॒ दश॒ स्वसा॑रो॒ अदि॑तेरु॒पस्थ॒ आ । जिगा॒दुप॑ ज्रयति॒ गोर॑पी॒च्यं॑ प॒दं यद॑स्य म॒तुथा॒ अजी॑जनन्

devanagari.text: श्येनो न योनिं सदनं धिया कृतं हिरण्ययमासदं देव एषति ।ए रिणंति बर्हिषि प्रियं गिराश्वो न देवाँ अप्येति यज्ञियः ॥

transliteration.text: śyenáḥ ǀ ná ǀ yónim ǀ sádanam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ kṛtám ǀ hiraṇyáyam ǀ ā-sádam ǀ deváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īṣati ǀā́ ǀ īmíti ǀ riṇanti ǀ barhíṣi ǀ priyám ǀ girā́ ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ devā́n ǀ ápi ǀ eti ǀ yajñíyaḥ ǁ

Sukta 71.translation: “The shining (Soma) approaches the golden seat the station constructed by his holy rites, as a falcon (approaches) his nest; (the worshippers) send the well-beloved by their praise to the sacred grass; the adorable Soma proceeds to the gods like a horse.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श्ये॒नो न योनिं॒ सद॑नं धि॒या कृ॒तं हि॑र॒ण्यय॑मा॒सदं॑ दे॒व एष॑ति । ए रि॑णन्ति ब॒र्हिषि॑ प्रि॒यं गि॒राश्वो॒ न दे॒वाँ अप्ये॑ति य॒ज्ञिय॑:

devanagari.text: परा व्यक्तो अरुषो दिवः कविर्वृषा त्रिपृष्ठो अनविष्ट गा अभि ।सहस्रणीतिर्यतिः परायती रेभो न पूर्वीरुषसो वि राजति ॥

Sukta 71.translation: “Radiant, wise, flowing in separate streams, (theSomadescends) from the firmament; the shower offered at the three libations responds to the praises (of the worshippers); led in a thousand directions, coming and going, he shines at many a sunrise like one who sings praises (to the gods).”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परा॒ व्य॑क्तो अरु॒षो दि॒वः क॒विर्वृषा॑ त्रिपृ॒ष्ठो अ॑नविष्ट॒ गा अ॒भि । स॒हस्र॑णीति॒र्यति॑: परा॒यती॑ रे॒भो न पू॒र्वीरु॒षसो॒ वि रा॑जति

Sukta 71.translation: “His ray creates a shining form; at whatever battle it is present, it beats down the adversaries; the giver of water goes with the oblation to the divine people, (it meets) with good praise; (Soma) is joined by (a hymn) demanding kine as the chief boon.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वे॒षं रू॒पं कृ॑णुते॒ वर्णो॑ अस्य॒ स यत्राश॑य॒त्समृ॑ता॒ सेध॑ति स्रि॒धः । अ॒प्सा या॑ति स्व॒धया॒ दैव्यं॒ जनं॒ सं सु॑ष्टु॒ती नस॑ते॒ सं गोअ॑ग्रया

devanagari.text: उक्षेव यूथा परियन्नरावीदधि त्विषीरधित सूर्यस्य ।दिव्यः सुपर्णोऽव चक्षत क्षां सोमः परि क्रतुना पश्यते जाः ॥

Sukta 71.translation: “Like a bull approaching the herbs (Soma) roars (as he approaches the praises); he appropriates the lustre of the sun; celestial, flying gracefully he looks down upon the earth; by his wisdom Soma contemplates mankind.”
Sukta 71.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒क्षेव॑ यू॒था प॑रि॒यन्न॑रावी॒दधि॒ त्विषी॑रधित॒ सूर्य॑स्य । दि॒व्यः सु॑प॒र्णोऽव॑ चक्षत॒ क्षां सोम॒: परि॒ क्रतु॑ना पश्यते॒ जाः

Sukta 72.translation: “They cleanse the green-tinted (Soma); he is harnessed like a swift horse; the Soma is combined in the pitcher with the products of the kine. He utters a sound, (the worshippers) send forth praise; how many (boons) abundantly delightint the utterer of many praises (does Soma bestow).”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: हरिं॑ मृजन्त्यरु॒षो न यु॑ज्यते॒ सं धे॒नुभि॑: क॒लशे॒ सोमो॑ अज्यते । उद्वाच॑मी॒रय॑ति हि॒न्वते॑ म॒ती पु॑रुष्टु॒तस्य॒ कति॑ चित्परि॒प्रिय॑:

devanagari.text: साकं वदंति बहवो मनीषिण इंद्रस्य सोमं जठरे यदादुहुः ।यदी मृजंति सुगभस्तयो नरः सनीळाभिर्दशभिः काम्यं मधु ॥

transliteration.text: sākám ǀ vadanti ǀ bahávaḥ ǀ manīṣíṇaḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ sómam ǀ jaṭháre ǀ yát ǀ ā-duhúḥ ǀyádi ǀ mṛjánti ǀ sú-gabhastayaḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀ sá-nīḷābhiḥ ǀ daśá-bhiḥ ǀ kā́myam ǀ mádhu ǁ

Sukta 72.translation: “Many wise men utter praise together, when they have milked theSomaintoIndra's belly, when fair-armed men cleanse the delightful exhilarating juice with their ten united (fingers).”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सा॒कं व॑दन्ति ब॒हवो॑ मनी॒षिण॒ इन्द्र॑स्य॒ सोमं॑ ज॒ठरे॒ यदा॑दु॒हुः । यदी॑ मृ॒जन्ति॒ सुग॑भस्तयो॒ नर॒: सनी॑ळाभिर्द॒शभि॒: काम्यं॒ मधु॑

devanagari.text: अरममाणो अत्येति गा अभि सूर्यस्य प्रियं दुहितुस्तिरो रवं ।अन्वस्मै जोषमभरद्विनंगृसः सं द्वयीभिः स्वसृभिः क्षेति जामिभिः ॥

Sukta 72.translation: “Unceasing, theSomagoes to mix with the products of the kine, he utters a cry dear to the daughter of the sun. The praiser brings delight to him; he is united to the two kindred sisters (thehands).”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अर॑ममाणो॒ अत्ये॑ति॒ गा अ॒भि सूर्य॑स्य प्रि॒यं दु॑हि॒तुस्ति॒रो रव॑म् । अन्व॑स्मै॒ जोष॑मभरद्विनंगृ॒सः सं द्व॒यीभि॒: स्वसृ॑भिः क्षेति जा॒मिभि॑:

Sukta 72.translation: “Shaken by the men, expressed by the stones, the delight (of the gods), the lord of cattle, ancient, distilling (in the vessels) born in due season, (theSomais plural ced) on the sacrd grass; intelligent, the material of the sacrifice of man, pure, the Soma flows for you,Indra,of his own accord.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नृधू॑तो॒ अद्रि॑षुतो ब॒र्हिषि॑ प्रि॒यः पति॒र्गवां॑ प्र॒दिव॒ इन्दु॑ॠ॒त्विय॑: । पुरं॑धिवा॒न्मनु॑षो यज्ञ॒साध॑न॒: शुचि॑र्धि॒या प॑वते॒ सोम॑ इन्द्र ते

Sukta 72.translation: “Urged by the arms of men, poured forth in a stream theSomaflows for you,Indra, for strength; you accomplish the rites, you overcome enemies at the sacrifice; the green-tinted Soma rests upon the cups like a bird perching on a tree.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नृबा॒हुभ्यां॑ चोदि॒तो धार॑या सु॒तो॑ऽनुष्व॒धं प॑वते॒ सोम॑ इन्द्र ते । आप्रा॒: क्रतू॒न्त्सम॑जैरध्व॒रे म॒तीर्वेर्न द्रु॒षच्च॒म्वो॒३॒॑रास॑द॒द्धरि॑:

Sukta 72.translation: “The seers, the experienced performers of holy acts, milk forth the seer, the loud-sounding undecayingSoma; the regenerated cattle and the praises combined repair to him at the plural ce of birth of the sacrifice.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अं॒शुं दु॑हन्ति स्त॒नय॑न्त॒मक्षि॑तं क॒विं क॒वयो॒ऽपसो॑ मनी॒षिण॑: । समी॒ गावो॑ म॒तयो॑ यन्ति सं॒यत॑ ऋ॒तस्य॒ योना॒ सद॑ने पुन॒र्भुव॑:

Sukta 72.translation: “The supporter of the vast heaven, (plural ced) upon the navel of the earth, moistened among the rivers in the wave of the waters, the thunderbolt ofIndra, the showerer (of benefits), the possessor of wealth,Somaauspiciously exhilarating distils into (Indra's) heart.”
Sukta 72.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नाभा॑ पृथि॒व्या ध॒रुणो॑ म॒हो दि॒वो॒३॒॑ऽपामू॒र्मौ सिन्धु॑ष्व॒न्तरु॑क्षि॒तः । इन्द्र॑स्य॒ वज्रो॑ वृष॒भो वि॒भूव॑सु॒: सोमो॑ हृ॒दे प॑वते॒ चारु॑ मत्स॒रः

Sukta 72.translation: “Performer of good deeds, flow quickly round the terrestrial region, giving (riches) to the worshipper and the shaker (of the libation); do not deprive us of the wealth that enriches our dwellings; may we be invested with abundant wealth of diverse kinds.”

Sukta 72.translation: “OnIndu, bring us quickly (wealth) with a hundred gifts, with horses, with a thousand gifts, with cattle and with gold; measure unto us abundant riches and food; come, purified one, to (hear) our praise.”

Sukta 73.translation: “(The streams) of the dripping effused (Soma) sound together on the jaw (of the sacrifice), the Soma-juices flow together to the plural ce of sacrifice. The powerful (Soma) has made the three exalted worlds for the use (of men and gods); the ships of the truthful (Soma) satisfy the pious worshipper.”

Sukta 73.translation: “The mighty (priests) assembled together send forth (theSoma) together; desirous (of heaven) they drive it to the wave of the river; genitive rating praise they nourish the previous body ofIndrawith the streams of the exhilarating Soma.”

Sukta 73.translation: “(The rays of theSoma) having the means of purification sit round the voice (of the firmament), their ancient father protects their (light-giving) work; Soma the all-developer has overspread the mighty firmament (with them); the skilful (priests) are able to conduct (the Soma) to the all-sustaining (waters).”

devanagari.text: सहस्रधारेऽव ते समस्वरंदिवो नाके मधुजिह्वा असश्चतः ।अस्य स्पशो न नि मिषंति भूर्णयः पदेपदे पाशिनः संति सेतवः ॥
सहस्रऽधारे । अव । ते । सम् । असरन् । दिवः । नाके । मधुऽजिह्वाः । असश्चतः ।अस्य । स्पशः । न । नि । मिषन्ति । भूर्णयः । पदेऽपदे । पाशिनः । सन्ति । सेतवः ॥

transliteration.text: sahásra-dhāre ǀ áva ǀ té ǀ sám ǀ asaran ǀ diváḥ ǀ nā́ke ǀ mádhu-jihvāḥ ǀ asaścátaḥ ǀásya ǀ spáśaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ní ǀ miṣanti ǀ bhū́rṇayaḥ ǀ padé-pade ǀ pāśínaḥ ǀ santi ǀ sétavaḥ ǁ

Sukta 73.translation: “(TheSomarays) in the firmament of a thousand streams (unite with the earth) below; in the summit of heaven, sweet-tongued, in separate drops, his rays, swiftly moving, nevershuttheir eyes; fixed each in his plural ce, they are the molesters (of sinners).”
Sukta 73.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒हस्र॑धा॒रेऽव॒ ते सम॑स्वरन्दि॒वो नाके॒ मधु॑जिह्वा अस॒श्चत॑: । अस्य॒ स्पशो॒ न नि मि॑षन्ति॒ भूर्ण॑यः प॒देप॑दे पा॒शिन॑: सन्ति॒ सेत॑वः

devanagari.text: पितुर्मातुरध्या ये समस्वरन्नृचा शोचंतः संदहंतो अव्रतान् ।इंद्रद्विष्टामप धमंति मायया त्वचमसिक्नीं भूमनो दिवस्परि ॥
पितुः । मातुः । अधि । आ । ये । सम्ऽअस्वरन् । ऋचा । शोचन्तः । सम्ऽदहन्तः । अव्रतान् ।इन्द्रऽद्विष्टाम् । अप । धमन्ति । मायया । त्वचम् । असिक्नीम् । भूमनः । दिवः । परि ॥

transliteration.text: pitúḥ ǀ mātúḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ā́ ǀ yé ǀ sam-ásvaran ǀ ṛcā́ ǀ śócantaḥ ǀ sam-dáhantaḥ ǀ avratā́n ǀíndra-dviṣṭām ǀ ápa ǀ dhamanti ǀ māyáyā ǀ tvácam ǀ ásiknīm ǀ bhū́manaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǁ

Sukta 73.translation: “(The rays) which were manifested in heaven and earth, illumined by the hymn (of praise), consuming the impious (sacrificers), drive away by their wisdom from earth and heaven the black-skinned (rākṣasas) hated byIndra.”
Sukta 73.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पि॒तुर्मा॒तुरध्या ये स॒मस्व॑रन्नृ॒चा शोच॑न्तः सं॒दह॑न्तो अव्र॒तान् । इन्द्र॑द्विष्टा॒मप॑ धमन्ति मा॒यया॒ त्वच॒मसि॑क्नीं॒ भूम॑नो दि॒वस्परि॑

devanagari.text: प्रत्नान्मानादध्या ये समस्वरंछ्लोकयंत्रासो रभसस्य मंतवः ।अपानक्षासो बधिरा अहासत ऋतस्य पंथां न तरंति दुष्कृतः ॥
प्रत्नात् । मानात् । अधि । आ । ये । सम्ऽअस्वरन् । श्लोकऽयन्त्रासः । रभसस्य । मन्तवः ।अप । अनक्षासः । बधिराः । अहासत । ऋतस्य । पन्थाम् । न । तरन्ति । दुःऽकृतः ॥

transliteration.text: pratnā́t ǀ mā́nāt ǀ ádhi ǀ ā́ ǀ yé ǀ sam-ásvaran ǀ ślóka-yantrāsaḥ ǀ rabhasásya ǀ mántavaḥ ǀápa ǀ anakṣā́saḥ ǀ badhirā́ḥ ǀ ahāsata ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pánthām ǀ ná ǀ taranti ǀ duḥ-kṛ́taḥ ǁ

Sukta 73.translation: “(The rays) which regulating praise and purposing rapidity of action, were manifested from the ancient firmament, them the blind and deaf avoid; the wicked traverse not the path of truth.”
Sukta 73.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र॒त्नान्माना॒दध्या ये स॒मस्व॑र॒ञ्छ्लोक॑यन्त्रासो रभ॒सस्य॒ मन्त॑वः । अपा॑न॒क्षासो॑ बधि॒रा अ॑हासत ऋ॒तस्य॒ पन्थां॒ न त॑रन्ति दु॒ष्कृत॑:

devanagari.text: सहस्रधारे वितते पवित्र आ वाचं पुनंति कवयो मनीषिणः ।रुद्रास एषामिषिरासो अद्रुहः स्पशः स्वंचः सुदृशो नृचक्षसः ॥
सहस्रऽधारे । विऽतते । पवित्रे । आ । वाचम् । पुनन्ति । कवयः । मनीषिणः ।रुद्रासः । एषाम् । इषिरासः । अद्रुहः । स्पशः । सुऽअञ्चः । सुऽदृशः । नृऽचक्षसः ॥

transliteration.text: sahásra-dhāre ǀ ví-tate ǀ pavítre ǀ ā́ ǀ vā́cam ǀ punanti ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ manīṣíṇaḥ ǀrudrā́saḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ iṣirā́saḥ ǀ adrúhaḥ ǀ spáśaḥ ǀ su-áñcaḥ ǀ su-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ nṛ-cákṣasaḥ ǁ

Sukta 73.translation: “The intelligent sages extol the voice (of the firmament) in the purifying extended (Soma) with its thousand streams; theRudrasare their servants, swift-moving, inviolable, revered, of goodly aspect, the beholders of men.”
Sukta 73.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒हस्र॑धारे॒ वित॑ते प॒वित्र॒ आ वाचं॑ पुनन्ति क॒वयो॑ मनी॒षिण॑: । रु॒द्रास॑ एषामिषि॒रासो॑ अ॒द्रुह॒: स्पश॒: स्वञ्च॑: सु॒दृशो॑ नृ॒चक्ष॑सः

devanagari.text: ऋतस्य गोपा न दभाय सुक्रतुस्त्री ष पवित्रा हृद्यंतरा दधे ।विद्वान्त्स विश्वा भुवनाभि पश्यत्यवाजुष्टान्विध्यति कर्ते अव्रतान् ॥
ऋतस्य । गोपाः । न । दभाय । सुऽक्रतुः । त्री । सः । पवित्रा । हृदि । अन्तः । आ । दधे ।विद्वान् । सः । विश्वा । भुवना । अभि । पश्यति । अव । अजुष्टान् । विध्यति । कर्ते । अव्रतान् ॥

transliteration.text: ṛtásya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ dábhāya ǀ su-krátuḥ ǀ trī́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ pavítrā ǀ hṛdí ǀ antáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dadhe ǀvidvā́n ǀ sáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ abhí ǀ paśyati ǀ áva ǀ ájuṣṭān ǀ vidhyati ǀ karté ǀ avratā́n ǁ

Sukta 73.translation: “(Soma) the protector of the sacrifice, the doer of good deeds cannot be resisted; he plural ces in his heart the three purifiers; he the all-wise looks over all worlds; he censures those who are hostile in action, who sacrifice not.”
Sukta 73.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तस्य॑ गो॒पा न दभा॑य सु॒क्रतु॒स्त्री ष प॒वित्रा॑ हृ॒द्य१॒॑न्तरा द॑धे । वि॒द्वान्त्स विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना॒भि प॑श्य॒त्यवाजु॑ष्टान्विध्यति क॒र्ते अ॑व्र॒तान्

devanagari.text: ऋतस्य तंतुर्विततः पवित्र आ जिह्वाया अग्रे वरुणस्य मायया ।धीराश्चित्तत्समिनक्षंत आशतात्रा कर्तमव पदात्यप्रभुः ॥
ऋतस्य । तन्तुः । विऽततः । पवित्रे । आ । जिह्वायाः । अग्रे । वरुणस्य । मायया ।धीराः । चित् । तत् । सम्ऽइनक्षन्तः । आशत । अत्र । कर्तम् । अव । पदाति । अप्रऽभुः ॥

transliteration.text: ṛtásya ǀ tántuḥ ǀ ví-tataḥ ǀ pavítre ǀ ā́ ǀ jihvā́yāḥ ǀ ágre ǀ váruṇasya ǀ māyáyā ǀdhī́rāḥ ǀ cit ǀ tát ǀ sam-ínakṣantaḥ ǀ āśata ǀ átra ǀ kartám ǀ áva ǀ padāti ǀ ápra-bhuḥ ǁ

Sukta 73.translation: “The threads of the sacrifice spread over the filter extends by its act to the tip ofVaruṇa's tongue; the wise approaching reached it;but he who is incompetent for the rite sinks (to hell) even in this world.”
Sukta 73.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तस्य॒ तन्तु॒र्वित॑तः प॒वित्र॒ आ जि॒ह्वाया॒ अग्रे॒ वरु॑णस्य मा॒यया॑ । धीरा॑श्चि॒त्तत्स॒मिन॑क्षन्त आश॒तात्रा॑ क॒र्तमव॑ पदा॒त्यप्र॑भुः

Sukta 74.translation: “Born in the water (theSoma) cries out like a child, when powerful and brilliant he wishes to enjoy heaven; he comes from the sky tomix with the water that nourish the kine; we ask him by our praises for an opulent dwelling.”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शिशु॒र्न जा॒तोऽव॑ चक्रद॒द्वने॒ स्व१॒॑र्यद्वा॒ज्य॑रु॒षः सिषा॑सति । दि॒वो रेत॑सा सचते पयो॒वृधा॒ तमी॑महे सुम॒ती शर्म॑ स॒प्रथ॑:

Sukta 74.translation: “The supporter of heaven, the prop (of the earth), theSoma-juice who, widely spreading, filling (the vessels), flows in all directions-- may he unite the two great worlds by his own strength; he has upheld them combined; (may he) the sage (bestow) food upon (his worshippers).”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वो यः स्क॒म्भो ध॒रुण॒: स्वा॑तत॒ आपू॑र्णो अं॒शुः प॒र्येति॑ वि॒श्वत॑: । सेमे म॒ही रोद॑सी यक्षदा॒वृता॑ समीची॒ने दा॑धार॒ समिष॑: क॒विः

Sukta 74.translation: “(There is) abundant food well-prepared made ofSomaand sweet for (Indra) who comes to the sacrifice; the way to earth is broad; (for Indra) who is the lord of the rain (that falls) here, the possessor of cattle, the showerer of water, the leader (of the sacrifice), whose road is hither, who is deserving of praise.”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: महि॒ प्सर॒: सुकृ॑तं सो॒म्यं मधू॒र्वी गव्यू॑ति॒रदि॑तेॠ॒तं य॒ते । ईशे॒ यो वृ॒ष्टेरि॒त उ॒स्रियो॒ वृषा॒पां ने॒ता य इ॒तऊ॑तिॠ॒ग्मिय॑:

Sukta 74.translation: “Full of sap the butter and milk is milked from heaven, the bond of the sacrifice, the water is genitive rated; the assembled liberal givers delight him; (theSoma-juices) the leaders, the protectors shower down the accusative ulated (water).”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ॒त्म॒न्वन्नभो॑ दुह्यते घृ॒तं पय॑ ऋ॒तस्य॒ नाभि॑र॒मृतं॒ वि जा॑यते । स॒मी॒ची॒नाः सु॒दान॑वः प्रीणन्ति॒ तं नरो॑ हि॒तमव॑ मेहन्ति॒ पेर॑वः

Sukta 74.translation: “Combining with the wave theSomautters a cry; he sprinkles his god-protecting body for the worshipper; he plural ces the germ upon the lap of the earth, whereby we acquire sons and grandsons.”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अरा॑वीदं॒शुः सच॑मान ऊ॒र्मिणा॑ देवा॒व्यं१॒॑ मनु॑षे पिन्वति॒ त्वच॑म् । दधा॑ति॒ गर्भ॒मदि॑तेरु॒पस्थ॒ आ येन॑ तो॒कं च॒ तन॑यं च॒ धाम॑हे

Sukta 74.translation: “May those (juices) which are in the third world, the world of many streams, unconnected, bestowing progeny, descend; the four digits (of theSoma) sent down from heaven bearing water bring the oblation and the nectar.”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒हस्र॑धा॒रेऽव॒ ता अ॑स॒श्चत॑स्तृ॒तीये॑ सन्तु॒ रज॑सि प्र॒जाव॑तीः । चत॑स्रो॒ नाभो॒ निहि॑ता अ॒वो दि॒वो ह॒विर्भ॑रन्त्य॒मृतं॑ घृत॒श्चुत॑:

Sukta 74.translation: “When theSomaseeks to gain (heaven) he assumes a white colour; showering (benefits), powerful he knows (how to bestow) abundant wealth (upon the worshippers). He by his wisdom is associated with excellent rites; he bursts asunder the rain cloud from heaven.”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श्वे॒तं रू॒पं कृ॑णुते॒ यत्सिषा॑सति॒ सोमो॑ मी॒ढ्वाँ असु॑रो वेद॒ भूम॑नः । धि॒या शमी॑ सचते॒ सेम॒भि प्र॒वद्दि॒वस्कव॑न्ध॒मव॑ दर्षदु॒द्रिण॑म्

Sukta 74.translation: “Thus theSomasuccessfully reaches the white water besprinkled pitcher like a horse (reaching) the goal; the devout (priests) stimulate him with their praise; (he bestows) cattle uponKakṣīvatwho has seen a hundred winters.”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अध॑ श्वे॒तं क॒लशं॒ गोभि॑र॒क्तं कार्ष्म॒न्ना वा॒ज्य॑क्रमीत्सस॒वान् । आ हि॑न्विरे॒ मन॑सा देव॒यन्त॑: क॒क्षीव॑ते श॒तहि॑माय॒ गोना॑म्

Sukta 74.translation: “PurifiedSoma, when you are diluted with the water your juice passes through the woollen fleece; cleansed by the sages, O exhilarating purified (Soma), be sweet-flavoured forIndrato drink.”
Sukta 74.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒द्भिः सो॑म पपृचा॒नस्य॑ ते॒ रसोऽव्यो॒ वारं॒ वि प॑वमान धावति । स मृ॒ज्यमा॑नः क॒विभि॑र्मदिन्तम॒ स्वद॒स्वेन्द्रा॑य पवमान पी॒तये॑

devanagari.text: अभि प्रियाणि पवते चनोहितो नामानि यह्वो अधि येषु वर्धते ।आ सूर्यस्य बृहतो बृहन्नधि रथं विष्वंचमरुहद्विचक्षणः ॥
अभि । प्रियाणि । पवते । चनःऽहितः । नामानि । यह्वः । अधि । येषु । वर्धते ।आ । सूर्यस्य । बृहतः । बृहन् । अधि । रथम् । विष्वञ्चम् । अरुहत् । विऽचक्षणः ॥

transliteration.text: abhí ǀ priyā́ṇi ǀ pavate ǀ cánaḥ-hitaḥ ǀ nā́māni ǀ yahváḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ yéṣu ǀ várdhate ǀā́ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ bṛhán ǀ ádhi ǀ rátham ǀ víṣvañcam ǀ aruhat ǀ vi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “(TheSoma) fit for good flows towards the delightful waters in which the mighty (Soma) is fostered; the beholder of all, the great (Soma) mounts themighty sun's chariot which go everywhere. ”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि प्रि॒याणि॑ पवते॒ चनो॑हितो॒ नामा॑नि य॒ह्वो अधि॒ येषु॒ वर्ध॑ते । आ सूर्य॑स्य बृह॒तो बृ॒हन्नधि॒ रथं॒ विष्व॑ञ्चमरुहद्विचक्ष॒णः

devanagari.text: ऋतस्य जिह्वा पवते मधु प्रियं वक्ता पतिर्धियो अस्या अदाभ्यः ।दधाति पुत्रः पित्रोरपीच्यं नाम तृतीयमधि रोचने दिवः ॥
ऋतस्य । जिह्वा । पवते । मधु । प्रियम् । वक्ता । पतिः । धियः । अस्याः । अदाभ्यः ।दधाति । पुत्रः । पित्रोः । अपीच्यम् । नाम । तृतीयम् । अधि । रोचने । दिवः ॥

transliteration.text: ṛtásya ǀ jihvā́ ǀ pavate ǀ mádhu ǀ priyám ǀ vaktā́ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dhiyáḥ ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ ádābhyaḥ ǀdádhāti ǀ putráḥ ǀ pitróḥ ǀ apīcyám ǀ nā́ma ǀ tṛtī́yam ǀ ádhi ǀ rocané ǀ diváḥ ǁ

Sukta 75.translation: “The tongue of the sacrifice (Soma) distils the delightful exhilarating (juice), speaking, lord of this rite, unassailable; the son (the sacrificer) assumes a third name unknown to his parents in the briliance of heaven.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒तस्य॑ जि॒ह्वा प॑वते॒ मधु॑ प्रि॒यं व॒क्ता पति॑र्धि॒यो अ॒स्या अदा॑भ्यः । दधा॑ति पु॒त्रः पि॒त्रोर॑पी॒च्यं१॒॑ नाम॑ तृ॒तीय॒मधि॑ रोच॒ने दि॒वः

devanagari.text: अव द्युतानः कलशाँ अचिक्रदन्नृभिर्येमानः कोश आ हिरण्यये ।अभीमृतस्य दोहना अनूषताधि त्रिपृष्ठ उषसो वि राजति ॥

Sukta 75.translation: “Shining, he cries aloud (descending) into the vessels, pressed by the priests into the golden receptacle; the milk of the sacrifice glorify him; the supporter of the three sacrifices shines (most) on the days of sacrifice.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव॑ द्युता॒नः क॒लशाँ॑ अचिक्रद॒न्नृभि॑र्येमा॒नः कोश॒ आ हि॑र॒ण्यये॑ । अ॒भीमृ॒तस्य॑ दो॒हना॑ अनूष॒ताधि॑ त्रिपृ॒ष्ठ उ॒षसो॒ वि रा॑जति

devanagari.text: अद्रिभिः सुतो मतिभिश्चनोहितः प्ररोचयन्रोदसी मातरा शुचिः ।रोमाण्यव्या समया वि धावति मधोर्धारा पिन्वमाना दिवेदिवे ॥

Sukta 75.translation: “Effused by the stones and by the praises, fit for food, illuminating heaven and earth the parents (of the universe), pure, (theSoma), flows between the sheep's hairs, diluted (with the water) the stream of the exhilarating beverage (is purified) day by day.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अद्रि॑भिः सु॒तो म॒तिभि॒श्चनो॑हितः प्ररो॒चय॒न्रोद॑सी मा॒तरा॒ शुचि॑: । रोमा॒ण्यव्या॑ स॒मया॒ वि धा॑वति॒ मधो॒र्धारा॒ पिन्व॑माना दि॒वेदि॑वे

devanagari.text: परि सोम प्र धन्वा स्वस्तये नृभिः पुनानो अभि वासयाशिरं ।ये ते मदा आहनसो विहायसस्तेभिरिंद्रं चोदय दातवे मघं ॥

Sukta 75.translation: “Soma, flow forth for our welfare; purified by the priests cloth yourself in the (milky) mixture; with the exhilarating loud-sounding mighty juices which you have, inspireIndrato bestow affluence upon us.”
Sukta 75.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॑ सोम॒ प्र ध॑न्वा स्व॒स्तये॒ नृभि॑: पुना॒नो अ॒भि वा॑सया॒शिर॑म् । ये ते॒ मदा॑ आह॒नसो॒ विहा॑यस॒स्तेभि॒रिन्द्रं॑ चोदय॒ दात॑वे म॒घम्

devanagari.text: धर्ता दिवः पवते कृत्व्यो रसो दक्षो देवानामनुमाद्यो नृभिः ।हरिः सृजानो अत्यो न सत्वभिर्वृथा पाजांसि कृणुते नदीष्वा ॥

Sukta 76.translation: “(Soma) the sustainer (of all) flows from the firmament, the purifiable juice, the invigorator of the gods, worthy tobe praised by the priests; green-tinted like a horse let loose by the charioteers he easily restores his vigour in the waters.”
Sukta 76.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ध॒र्ता दि॒वः प॑वते॒ कृत्व्यो॒ रसो॒ दक्षो॑ दे॒वाना॑मनु॒माद्यो॒ नृभि॑: । हरि॑: सृजा॒नो अत्यो॒ न सत्व॑भि॒र्वृथा॒ पाजां॑सि कृणुते न॒दीष्वा

devanagari.text: शूरो न धत्त आयुधा गभस्त्योः स्वः सिषासन्रथिरो गविष्टिषु ।इंद्रस्य शुष्ममीरयन्नपस्युभिरिंदुर्हिन्वानो अज्यते मनीषिभिः ॥

transliteration.text: śū́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhatte ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ sísāsan ǀ rathiráḥ ǀ gó-iṣṭiṣu ǀíndrasya ǀ śúṣmam ǀ īráyan ǀ apasyú-bhiḥ ǀ índuḥ ǀ hinvānáḥ ǀ ajyate ǀ manīṣí-bhiḥ ǁ

Sukta 76.translation: “Like a hero he carries weapons in hishands, desirous of enjoying felicity, mounting his chariot in quest of the cattle (of the worshipper), animating the strength ofIndra,Indu, urged by the wise performers of pious acts, is anointed (with the milk and curds).”
Sukta 76.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शूरो॒ न ध॑त्त॒ आयु॑धा॒ गभ॑स्त्यो॒: स्व१॒॑: सिषा॑सन्रथि॒रो गवि॑ष्टिषु । इन्द्र॑स्य॒ शुष्म॑मी॒रय॑न्नप॒स्युभि॒रिन्दु॑र्हिन्वा॒नो अ॑ज्यते मनी॒षिभि॑:

devanagari.text: इंद्रस्य सोम पवमान ऊर्मिणा तविष्यमाणो जठरेष्वा विश ।प्र णः पिन्व विद्युदभ्रेव रोदसी धिया न वाजाँ उप मासि शश्वतः ॥

Sukta 76.translation: “Somawho are purified, who desire strength enterIndra's belly in a mighty stream; milk heaven and earth for us as lightning (milks) the clouds; now with the rite meter (unto us) abundant food.”
Sukta 76.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्र॑स्य सोम॒ पव॑मान ऊ॒र्मिणा॑ तवि॒ष्यमा॑णो ज॒ठरे॒ष्वा वि॑श । प्र ण॑: पिन्व वि॒द्युद॒भ्रेव॒ रोद॑सी धि॒या न वाजाँ॒ उप॑ मासि॒ शश्व॑तः

devanagari.text: विश्वस्य राजा पवते स्वर्दृश ऋतस्य धीतिमृषिषाळवीवशत् ।यः सूर्यस्यासिरेण मृज्यते पिता मतीनामसमष्टकाव्यः ॥

transliteration.text: víśvasya ǀ rā́jā ǀ pavate ǀ svaḥ-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhītím ǀ ṛṣiṣā́ṭ ǀ avīvaśat ǀyáḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ ásireṇa ǀ mṛjyáte ǀ pitā́ ǀ matīnā́m ǀ ásamaṣṭa-kāvyaḥ ǁ

Sukta 76.translation: “(Soma) the soverign of the universe flows forth; surpassing the ṛṣis he desire the worship of the all-seeing truthful (Indra); he who is cleansed by the ray of he sun, the father of praise, the unequalled sage.”
Sukta 76.sanskrit_wisdomlib: विश्व॑स्य॒ राजा॑ पवते स्व॒र्दृश॑ ऋ॒तस्य॑ धी॒तिमृ॑षि॒षाळ॑वीवशत् । यः सूर्य॒स्यासि॑रेण मृ॒ज्यते॑ पि॒ता म॑ती॒नामस॑मष्टकाव्यः

Sukta 76.translation: “As a bull (entering) the herd you rush to the receptacle, on the top of the waters, showering (benefits) crying aloud; you flow forIndra, most exhilarating so that we may be victorious in battle protected by you.”
Sukta 76.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वृषे॑व यू॒था परि॒ कोश॑मर्षस्य॒पामु॒पस्थे॑ वृष॒भः कनि॑क्रदत् । स इन्द्रा॑य पवसे मत्स॒रिन्त॑मो॒ यथा॒ जेषा॑म समि॒थे त्वोत॑यः

devanagari.text: एष प्र कोशे मधुमाँ अचिक्रददिंद्रस्य वज्रो वपुषो वपुष्टरः ।अभीमृतस्य सुदुघा घृतश्चुतो वाश्रा अर्षंति पयसेव धेनवः ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ prá ǀ kóśe ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ acikradat ǀ índrasya ǀ vájraḥ ǀ vápuṣaḥ ǀ vápuḥ-taraḥ ǀabhí ǀ īm ǀ ṛtásya ǀ su-dúghāḥ ǀ ghṛta-ścútaḥ ǀ vāśrā́ḥ ǀ arṣanti ǀ páyasā-iva ǀ dhenávaḥ ǁ

Sukta 77.translation: “The sweet-flavoured beverage sounds in the pitcher, the thunderbolt ofIndra, more beautiful than the beautiful; (the stream) of this veracious (Soma) approach yielding much milk, dropping water, lowing like kine (laden) with milk.”
Sukta 77.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष प्र कोशे॒ मधु॑माँ अचिक्रद॒दिन्द्र॑स्य॒ वज्रो॒ वपु॑षो॒ वपु॑ष्टरः । अ॒भीमृ॒तस्य॑ सु॒दुघा॑ घृत॒श्चुतो॑ वा॒श्रा अ॑र्षन्ति॒ पय॑सेव धे॒नव॑:

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ pūrvyáḥ ǀ pavate ǀ yám ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ mathāyát ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yuvate ǀ vévijānaḥ ǀ ít ǀ kṛśā́noḥ ǀ ástuḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ áha ǀ bibhyúṣā ǁ

Sukta 77.translation: “The ancient (Soma) flows, which the hawk, despatched (for the purpose), brought down from heaven passing through the (third) world; he detaches the sweet-flavoured (Soma) flying downwards, with mind full of fear of the archerKṛśānu.”
Sukta 77.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स पू॒र्व्यः प॑वते॒ यं दि॒वस्परि॑ श्ये॒नो म॑था॒यदि॑षि॒तस्ति॒रो रज॑: । स मध्व॒ आ यु॑वते॒ वेवि॑जान॒ इत्कृ॒शानो॒रस्तु॒र्मन॒साह॑ बि॒भ्युषा॑

devanagari.text: ते नः पूर्वास उपरास इंदवो महे वाजाय धन्वंतु गोमते ।ईक्षेण्यासो अह्यो न चारवो ब्रह्मब्रह्म ये जुजुषुर्हविर्हविः ॥

Sukta 77.translation: “May the former and the latterSoma-juices flow to give us abundant food and milk, plural asing to look upon like beautiful well-adorned (women), which (juices) perform every prayer and every oblation.”

Sukta 77.translation: “May thisIndu, praised of many, knowing those who desire to slay us, slay them with united mind; who being in the dwelling of the lord (Agni) deposits a germ (in the herds) and hastens to (our) milk-giving herd of cattle.”

Sukta 77.translation: “The maker of all, clever in work, the juice, mighty unassailableVaruṇaflows from heaven for the sake of him who go hither and thither; the friend of the adorable (Soma) is effused in affliction uttering a sound like an ardent horse amidst a herd (of mares). [”

Sukta 78.translation: “This royal (Soma) producing a sound flows forth; clothing himself with the water he advances towards the praises (of the worshipper); the sheep with its fleece lays hold of the impure form; purified he approaches the station of the gods.”
Sukta 78.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र राजा॒ वाचं॑ ज॒नय॑न्नसिष्यदद॒पो वसा॑नो अ॒भि गा इ॑यक्षति । गृ॒भ्णाति॑ रि॒प्रमवि॑रस्य॒ तान्वा॑ शु॒द्धो दे॒वाना॒मुप॑ याति निष्कृ॒तम्

Sukta 78.translation: “You are effused by the priests,Soma, forIndra; you the observer of men, stimulated, intelligent, are immersed in the water; many are the paths for you to follow, infinite are the spreading green-tinted streams alighting on the cups.”
Sukta 78.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑य सोम॒ परि॑ षिच्यसे॒ नृभि॑र्नृ॒चक्षा॑ ऊ॒र्मिः क॒विर॑ज्यसे॒ वने॑ । पू॒र्वीर्हि ते॑ स्रु॒तय॒: सन्ति॒ यात॑वे स॒हस्र॒मश्वा॒ हर॑यश्चमू॒षद॑:

devanagari.text: समुद्रिया अप्सरसो मनीषिणमासीना अंतरभि सोममक्षरन् ।ता ईं हिन्वंति हर्म्यस्य सक्षणिं याचंते सुम्नं पवमानमक्षितं ॥

Sukta 78.translation: “The nymphs of the firmament seated in the midst flow towards the sagaciousSoma; they cherish him the sprinkler of the hall of sacrifice; (the worshippers) solicitPavamāna(the undecaying) for a boon.”
Sukta 78.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒मु॒द्रिया॑ अप्स॒रसो॑ मनी॒षिण॒मासी॑ना अ॒न्तर॒भि सोम॑मक्षरन् । ता ईं॑ हिन्वन्ति ह॒र्म्यस्य॑ स॒क्षणिं॒ याच॑न्ते सु॒म्नं पव॑मान॒मक्षि॑तम्

Sukta 78.translation: “Somaflows for us, the conqueror of cattle, of chariots, of gold, of heaven, of water, of thousandfold (wealth), whom the gods have made for (their) drinking, exhilarating, most sweet-flavoured, dropping, purple, causing happiness.”
Sukta 78.sanskrit_wisdomlib: गो॒जिन्न॒: सोमो॑ रथ॒जिद्धि॑रण्य॒जित्स्व॒र्जिद॒ब्जित्प॑वते सहस्र॒जित् । यं दे॒वास॑श्चक्रि॒रे पी॒तये॒ मदं॒ स्वादि॑ष्ठं द्र॒प्सम॑रु॒णं म॑यो॒भुव॑म्

Sukta 78.translation: “Bestowing all these true riches, loving us you flow,Soma, purified; destroy our enemy whether he be far or nigh; grant us a free road and freedom from danger.”
Sukta 78.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒तानि॑ सोम॒ पव॑मानो अस्म॒युः स॒त्यानि॑ कृ॒ण्वन्द्रवि॑णान्यर्षसि । ज॒हि शत्रु॑मन्ति॒के दू॑र॒के च॒ य उ॒र्वीं गव्यू॑ति॒मभ॑यं च नस्कृधि

Sukta 79.translation: “May the spontaneousSoma-juices flow to us at the brilliant (sacrifices), green-tinted, effused; may they be destroyed who are the withholders of food from us; may (our) foes be destroyed; may (the gods) enjoy our pious acts.”
Sukta 79.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒चो॒दसो॑ नो धन्व॒न्त्विन्द॑व॒: प्र सु॑वा॒नासो॑ बृ॒हद्दि॑वेषु॒ हर॑यः । वि च॒ नश॑न्न इ॒षो अरा॑तयो॒ऽर्यो न॑शन्त॒ सनि॑षन्त नो॒ धिय॑:

Sukta 79.translation: “May they flow to us, may they bring us riches-- the honey-droppingSoma-juices by whose aid we encounter the powerful (enemy); may we overcoming the opposition of every man always bear off his wealth.”
Sukta 79.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र णो॑ धन्व॒न्त्विन्द॑वो मद॒च्युतो॒ धना॑ वा॒ येभि॒रर्व॑तो जुनी॒मसि॑ । ति॒रो मर्त॑स्य॒ कस्य॑ चि॒त्परि॑ह्वृतिं व॒यं धना॑नि वि॒श्वधा॑ भरेमहि

Sukta 79.translation: “For the (Soma) verily is the foe of his own enemy and the destroyer of the enemy of another; as thirst overcomes one in a desert, so purified Soma, who are irresistible, slay (both) those (adversaries).”
Sukta 79.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒त स्वस्या॒ अरा॑त्या अ॒रिर्हि ष उ॒तान्यस्या॒ अरा॑त्या॒ वृको॒ हि षः । धन्व॒न्न तृष्णा॒ सम॑रीत॒ ताँ अ॒भि सोम॑ ज॒हि प॑वमान दुरा॒ध्य॑:

devanagari.text: दिवि ते नाभा परमो य आददे पृथिव्यास्ते रुरुहुः सानवि क्षिपः ।अद्रयस्त्वा बप्सति गोरधि त्वच्यप्सु त्वा हस्तैर्दुदुहुर्मनीषिणः ॥

Sukta 79.translation: “Your best juice (dwells) in the navel of heaven, that which receives (the oblation); your (members) grow up thrown upon the summit of the earth; the stones devour you upon the cowhide; the wise (priests) milk you into the water with theirhands.”
Sukta 79.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वि ते॒ नाभा॑ पर॒मो य आ॑द॒दे पृ॑थि॒व्यास्ते॑ रुरुहु॒: सान॑वि॒ क्षिप॑: । अद्र॑यस्त्वा बप्सति॒ गोरधि॑ त्व॒च्य१॒॑प्सु त्वा॒ हस्तै॑र्दुदुहुर्मनी॒षिण॑:

Sukta 79.translation: “Thus,Indu, the chief (priests) making the mixture send forth your well-lodged, well-formed juice (rasa); purifiedSoma, destroy (our) reviler; let your potent, delightful, exhilarating (juice) appoear.”
Sukta 79.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा त॑ इन्दो सु॒भ्वं॑ सु॒पेश॑सं॒ रसं॑ तुञ्जन्ति प्रथ॒मा अ॑भि॒श्रिय॑: । निदं॑निदं पवमान॒ नि ता॑रिष आ॒विस्ते॒ शुष्मो॑ भवतु प्रि॒यो मद॑:

Sukta 80.translation: “The stream of theSoma, the contemplator of man, flows forth; it invites by the sacrifice the gods (who dwell) above the sky; it shines forth at the voice of the sacrificer; the libations cover (the earth) like rivers.”
Sukta 80.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सोम॑स्य॒ धारा॑ पवते नृ॒चक्ष॑स ऋ॒तेन॑ दे॒वान्ह॑वते दि॒वस्परि॑ । बृह॒स्पते॑ र॒वथे॑ना॒ वि दि॑द्युते समु॒द्रासो॒ न सव॑नानि विव्यचुः

Sukta 80.translation: “Giver of food, whom the kine praise, you mount, bright-shining, your station fashioned by golden-hands; you,Soma, the health of the worshippers, increasing (their) abundant food flow forIndra, the showerer (of benefits), the giver of exhilaration.”

Sukta 80.translation: “The (Soma) flows toIndra's belly for (his) food, giving extreme exhilaration, clothed with vigour, giving good fortune he spreads forth towards all beings; sporting (on the altar), green-tinted, swift-moving, the showerer of benefits, he flows forth.”

Sukta 80.translation: “The priests, the ten fingers, milk you forth for the gods, most sweet-flavoured, flowing in a thousand streams; effused by the men, expressed with the stone, do you,Soma, the winner of thousand-fold wealth, flow to all the gods.”

Sukta 80.translation: “The ten fingers of the skillful (one) milk you forth with the stones into the water most sweet-flavoured, the showerer (of benefits);Soma, exhilaratingIndra(and) the celestial people, you rush forth, when filtered, like the wave of a river.”

Sukta 81.translation: “The graceful waves of the purifiedSomaflow intoIndra's belly when being effused and drawn forth (together) with the potent curds of the kine, they excite the hero to bestow (gifts to the worshippers).”

Sukta 81.translation: “The flows towards the pitchers, like a darught horse, lightly moving, the showerer; and knowing both races of gods-- those who come to (the sacrifice) from the other world and those who (come) from this world.”

Sukta 81.translation: “Soma, when purified, strew upon us wealth;Indu, who are possessed of affluence, be (the donor) of ample riches; dispenser of food, grant toVasuprosperity through (your) intelligence, scatter not our riches far from us.”

Sukta 82.translation: “TheSomahas been effused radiant, the showerer, green-inted; magnificent as a king, he cries aloud when approaching the waters; purified, he passes through the sheep's fleece, to alight on the water-moistened seat like a hawk (on its nest).”

Sukta 82.translation: “You, who are wise, pass through the adorable (filter) with a desire to perform the sacrifice; being cleansed you rush like a horse to the cattle. Driving away misfortunes be gracious (to us),Soma; clothed in water you proceed to the cleansing (vessel).”

Sukta 82.translation: “The mighty winged (Soma) whose father isParjanyahas plural ced his dwelling on the navel of the earth among the mountains; the sisters, the waters flow to (the produce of) the kine; he meets with the stones at the beloved sacrifice.”

Sukta 82.translation: “As a wife to her husband, so you (afford) delight to your worshipper; (Soma), offspring of Pajra, listen (to the praises) I address to you; in the midst of our adorations advance to grant us life; Soma, who are irreproachable, be vigilant against (our) foe.”

Sukta 82.translation: “As you,Indu, did attain strength for the ancient (ṛṣis), giving them hundred-fold (wealth), invulnerable, giving them thousand-fold (wealth); so now flow for (our) modern prosperity; the waters wait upon your functions.”

Sukta 83.translation: “Lord or prayer, your filter is stretched out; you who are the sovereign, enter its members from all sides; the raw (liquid) whose mass is not heated attains not this (filter); it is the boiled (liquids) bearing (the sacrifice) which attain it.”

Sukta 83.translation: “The filter of the foe-scorching (Soma) is spread on the summit of heaven; his shining filaments are separated, his swift-flowing (juices) protect the purifier (the worshipper), they dwell upon the summit of the sky in their wish (to approach the gods).”

Sukta 83.translation: “The chief sun of the dawn (theSoma) shines forth; sprinkler (of water), he nourishes the worlds, wishing (to have them) food; by his intelligence the intelligent build, thepitṛs, the beholders of men, support the germ (of vegetation).”

Sukta 83.translation: “Thegandharvaverily protects this station; the marvellous (Soma) preserves the races of the gods; the lord of cattle seizes (our enemy) with a snare, the doers of good attain the drinking of the sweet-juiced (Soma).”

Sukta 83.translation: “Possessed of water, you go clothed in the liquid water, to the great celestial abode to (take) the sacrifice; as king you ascend to the battle, mounted to your filter-chariot; armed with a thousand weapons you win (us) abundant food.”
Sukta 83.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ह॒विर्ह॑विष्मो॒ महि॒ सद्म॒ दैव्यं॒ नभो॒ वसा॑न॒: परि॑ यास्यध्व॒रम् । राजा॑ प॒वित्र॑रथो॒ वाज॒मारु॑हः स॒हस्र॑भृष्टिर्जयसि॒ श्रवो॑ बृ॒हत्

devanagari.text: पवस्व देवमादनो विचर्षणिरप्सा इंद्राय वरुणाय वायवे ।कृधी नो अद्य वरिवः स्वस्तिमदुरुक्षितौ गृणीहि दैव्यं जनं ॥

Sukta 84.translation: “Flow, the exhilarator of the gods, the far-seeing, the giver of water; forIndra,VaruṇaandVāyu; grant us this day wealth and health; call the celestial people on the spacious ground (of the sacrifice).”
Sukta 84.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑स्व देव॒माद॑नो॒ विच॑र्षणिर॒प्सा इन्द्रा॑य॒ वरु॑णाय वा॒यवे॑ । कृ॒धी नो॑ अ॒द्य वरि॑वः स्वस्ति॒मदु॑रुक्षि॒तौ गृ॑णीहि॒ दैव्यं॒ जन॑म्

devanagari.text: आ यस्तस्थौ भुवनान्यमर्त्यो विश्वानि सोमः परि तान्यर्षति ।कृण्वन्त्संचृतं विचृतमभिष्टय इंदुः सिषक्त्युषसं न सूर्यः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ tastháu ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ sómaḥ ǀ pári ǀ tā́ni ǀ arṣati ǀkṛṇván ǀ sam-cṛ́tam ǀ vi-cṛ́tam ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀ índuḥ ǀ sisakti ǀ uṣásam ǀ ná ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǁ

Sukta 84.translation: “The immortalSomawho is stationed upon the worlds, goes round about them all;Indu,binding and unloosing accompanies (the sacrifice) for its protection, as the sun the dawn.”
Sukta 84.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ यस्त॒स्थौ भुव॑ना॒न्यम॑र्त्यो॒ विश्वा॑नि॒ सोम॒: परि॒ तान्य॑र्षति । कृ॒ण्वन्त्सं॒चृतं॑ वि॒चृत॑म॒भिष्ट॑य॒ इन्दु॑: सिषक्त्यु॒षसं॒ न सूर्य॑:

devanagari.text: आ यो गोभिः सृज्यत ओषधीष्वा देवानां सुम्न इषयन्नुपावसुः ।आ विद्युता पवते धारया सुत इंद्रं सोमो मादयंदैव्यं जनं ॥

Sukta 84.translation: “TheSomawho is created by the (sun's) rays, (and whom they plural ce) in the herbs for the gratification of the gods, desiring to go (to the gods), taking wealth from (the foe), flows when effused in a brilliant stream, exhilaratingIndra(and) the people of heaven.”
Sukta 84.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ यो गोभि॑: सृ॒ज्यत॒ ओष॑धी॒ष्वा दे॒वानां॑ सु॒म्न इ॒षय॒न्नुपा॑वसुः । आ वि॒द्युता॑ पवते॒ धार॑या सु॒त इन्द्रं॒ सोमो॑ मा॒दय॒न्दैव्यं॒ जन॑म्

devanagari.text: एष स्य सोमः पवते सहस्रजिद्धिन्वानो वाचमिषिरामुषर्बुधं ।इंदुः समुद्रमुदियर्ति वायुभिरेंद्रस्य हार्दि कलशेषु सीदति ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ syáḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ pavate ǀ sahasra-jít ǀ hinvānáḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ iṣirā́m ǀ uṣaḥ-búdham ǀínduḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ út ǀ iyarti ǀ vāyú-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ índrasya ǀ hā́rdi ǀ kaláśeṣu ǀ sīdati ǁ

Sukta 84.translation: “This is theSoma, the conqueror of thousands, who flows stimulating the rapid voice (of the priests), awakened at dawn;Indusends forth his ocean and sinks into the pitchers intoIndra's heart.”
Sukta 84.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष स्य सोम॑: पवते सहस्र॒जिद्धि॑न्वा॒नो वाच॑मिषि॒रामु॑ष॒र्बुध॑म् । इन्दु॑: समु॒द्रमुदि॑यर्ति वा॒युभि॒रेन्द्र॑स्य॒ हार्दि॑ क॒लशे॑षु सीदति

devanagari.text: अभि त्यं गावः पयसा पयोवृधं सोमं श्रीणंति मतिभिः स्वर्विदं ।धनंजयः पवते कृत्व्यो रसो विप्रः कविः काव्येना स्वर्चनाः ॥

transliteration.text: abhí ǀ tyám ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ páyasā ǀ payaḥ-vṛ́dham ǀ sómam ǀ śrīṇanti ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ svaḥ-vídam ǀdhanam-jayáḥ ǀ pavate ǀ kṛ́tvyaḥ ǀ rásaḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ kā́vyena ǀ sváḥ-canāḥ ǁ

Sukta 84.translation: “The kine dilute with their milk that milk augmentingSomawho bestows all things by means of praises; (the Soma) the winner of (our foes') wealth flows purified by the rite, apt for the rite, wise, experienced, the (giver of) all food.”
Sukta 84.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि त्यं गाव॒: पय॑सा पयो॒वृधं॒ सोमं॑ श्रीणन्ति म॒तिभि॑: स्व॒र्विद॑म् । ध॒नं॒ज॒यः प॑वते॒ कृत्व्यो॒ रसो॒ विप्र॑: क॒विः काव्ये॑ना॒ स्व॑र्चनाः

devanagari.text: इंद्राय सोम सुषुतः परि स्रवापामीवा भवतु रक्षसा सह ।मा ते रसस्य मत्सत द्वयाविनो द्रविणस्वंत इह संत्विंदवः ॥

Sukta 85.translation: “Flow forth,Soma, well-effused forIndra; may disease and therākṣasasbe (kept) far off; let not the double-dealers be exhilarated by your juices; may the Soma-juices be full of wealth at this (sacrifice).”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑य सोम॒ सुषु॑त॒: परि॑ स्र॒वापामी॑वा भवतु॒ रक्ष॑सा स॒ह । मा ते॒ रस॑स्य मत्सत द्वया॒विनो॒ द्रवि॑णस्वन्त इ॒ह स॒न्त्विन्द॑वः

Sukta 85.translation: “Purified (Soma), animate us in battle; for you are powerful, dear to the gods, the exhilarator. Slay our foes, approach (us) who desire (to propitiate you by) praises;Indra, drink the Soma, destroy our adversaries.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्मान्त्स॑म॒र्ये प॑वमान चोदय॒ दक्षो॑ दे॒वाना॒मसि॒ हि प्रि॒यो मद॑: । ज॒हि शत्रूँ॑र॒भ्या भ॑न्दनाय॒तः पिबे॑न्द्र॒ सोम॒मव॑ नो॒ मृधो॑ जहि

devanagari.text: अदब्ध इंदो पवसे मदिंतम आत्मेंद्रस्य भवसि धासिरुत्तमः ।अभि स्वरंति बहवो मनीषिणो राजानमस्य भुवनस्य निंसते ॥

Sukta 85.translation: “You flow,Indu, the inviolable, the most exhilarating; you are yourself the best support forIndra; may sages approach and glorify you the ruler of this world.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अद॑ब्ध इन्दो पवसे म॒दिन्त॑म आ॒त्मेन्द्र॑स्य भवसि धा॒सिरु॑त्त॒मः । अ॒भि स्व॑रन्ति ब॒हवो॑ मनी॒षिणो॒ राजा॑नम॒स्य भुव॑नस्य निंसते

Sukta 85.translation: “The guide of thousands, flowing in a hundred streams, marvellous,Induflows forth forIndra, (his) beloved beverage; approach (the filter) winning (us) land, winning water, OSoma, sprinkler, make our path broad.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒हस्र॑णीथः श॒तधा॑रो॒ अद्भु॑त॒ इन्द्रा॒येन्दु॑: पवते॒ काम्यं॒ मधु॑ । जय॒न्क्षेत्र॑म॒भ्य॑र्षा॒ जय॑न्न॒प उ॒रुं नो॑ गा॒तुं कृ॑णु सोम मीढ्वः

Sukta 85.translation: “Crying aloud you are blended in the pitcher with curds and milk, you pass through the woollen fleece in the midst; being cleansed like a horse, distributing (gifts), you flow,Soma, intoIndra's belly.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: कनि॑क्रदत्क॒लशे॒ गोभि॑रज्यसे॒ व्य१॒॑व्ययं॑ स॒मया॒ वार॑मर्षसि । म॒र्मृ॒ज्यमा॑नो॒ अत्यो॒ न सा॑न॒सिरिन्द्र॑स्य सोम ज॒ठरे॒ सम॑क्षरः
