transliteration.text: svādúḥ ǀ pavasva ǀ divyā́ya ǀ jánmane ǀ svādúḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ suhávītu-nāmne ǀsvādúḥ ǀ mitrā́ya ǀ váruṇāya ǀ vāyáve ǀ bṛ́haspátaye ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ ádābhyaḥ ǁ

Sukta 85.translation: “Flow sweet for the celestial people, flow sweet forIndra, whose name is worthily invoked; sweet forMitra,Varuṇa,Vāyu,Bṛhaspati, you who are the sweet-flavoured, inviolable.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्वा॒दुः प॑वस्व दि॒व्याय॒ जन्म॑ने स्वा॒दुरिन्द्रा॑य सु॒हवी॑तुनाम्ने । स्वा॒दुर्मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय वा॒यवे॒ बृह॒स्पत॑ये॒ मधु॑माँ॒ अदा॑भ्यः

devanagari.text: अत्यं मृजंति कलशे दश क्षिपः प्र विप्राणां मतयो वाच ईरते ।पवमाना अभ्यर्षंति सुष्टुतिमेंद्रं विशंति मदिरास इंदवः ॥
अत्यम् । मृजन्ति । कलशे । दश । क्षिपः । प्र । विप्राणाम् । मतयः । वाचः । ईरते ।पवमानाः । अभि । अर्षन्ति । सुऽस्तुतिम् । आ । इन्द्रम् । विशन्ति । मदिरासः । इन्दवः ॥

transliteration.text: átyam ǀ mṛjanti ǀ kaláśe ǀ dáśa ǀ kṣípaḥ ǀ prá ǀ víprāṇām ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ vā́caḥ ǀ īrate ǀpávamānāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ arṣanti ǀ su-stutím ǀ ā́ ǀ índram ǀ viśanti ǀ madirā́saḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǁ

Sukta 85.translation: “The ten fingers clean the horse in the pitcher; among theviprasthe worshippers send forth praises; the filtered (juices) hasten to the fair praise, the exhilaratingSomajuices enterIndra.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अत्यं॑ मृजन्ति क॒लशे॒ दश॒ क्षिप॒: प्र विप्रा॑णां म॒तयो॒ वाच॑ ईरते । पव॑माना अ॒भ्य॑र्षन्ति सुष्टु॒तिमेन्द्रं॑ विशन्ति मदि॒रास॒ इन्द॑वः

devanagari.text: पवमानो अभ्यर्षा सुवीर्यमुर्वीं गव्यूतिं महि शर्म सप्रथः ।माकिर्नो अस्य परिषूतिरीशतेंदो जयेम त्वया धनंधनं ॥
पवमानः । अभि । अर्ष । सुऽवीर्यम् । उर्वीम् । गव्यूतिम् । महि । शर्म । सऽप्रथः ।माकिः । नः । अस्य । परिऽसूतिः । ईशत । इन्दो इति । जयेम । त्वया । धनम्ऽधनम् ॥

transliteration.text: pávamānaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ arṣa ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ urvī́m ǀ gávyūtim ǀ máhi ǀ śárma ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǀmā́kiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ asyá ǀ pári-sūtiḥ ǀ īśata ǀ índo íti ǀ jáyema ǀ tváyā ǀ dhánam-dhanam ǁ

Sukta 85.translation: “(Soma), when filtered, bring usmaleprogeny, extensive pastures, a large and spacious mansion; let no hinderer of this (rite) be lord over us;Indu, through you may we win all wealth.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑मानो अ॒भ्य॑र्षा सु॒वीर्य॑मु॒र्वीं गव्यू॑तिं॒ महि॒ शर्म॑ स॒प्रथ॑: । माकि॑र्नो अ॒स्य परि॑षूतिरीश॒तेन्दो॒ जये॑म॒ त्वया॒ धनं॑धनम्

devanagari.text: अधि द्यामस्थाद्वृषभो विचक्षणोऽरूरुचद्वि दिवो रोचना कविः ।राजा पवित्रमत्येति रोरुवद्दिवः पीयूषं दुहते नृचक्षसः ॥
अधि । द्याम् । अस्थात् । वृषभः । विऽचक्षणः । अरूरुचत् । वि । दिवः । रोचना । कविः ।राजा । पवित्रम् । अति । एति । रोरुवत् । दिवः । पीयूषम् । दुहते । नृऽचक्षसः ॥

transliteration.text: ádhi ǀ dyā́m ǀ asthāt ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ vi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǀ árūrucat ǀ ví ǀ diváḥ ǀ rocanā́ ǀ kavíḥ ǀrā́jā ǀ pavítram ǀ áti ǀ eti ǀ róruvat ǀ diváḥ ǀ pīyū́ṣam ǀ duhate ǀ nṛ-cákṣasaḥ ǁ

Sukta 85.translation: “The showerer, the beholder, has taken his station upon heaven, the seer has illumined the luminaries of heaven; the king passes through the filter with a shout, (theSomajuices) the beholders of men milk forth the ambrosia of heaven.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अधि॒ द्याम॑स्थाद्वृष॒भो वि॑चक्ष॒णोऽरू॑रुच॒द्वि दि॒वो रो॑च॒ना क॒विः । राजा॑ प॒वित्र॒मत्ये॑ति॒ रोरु॑वद्दि॒वः पी॒यूषं॑ दुहते नृ॒चक्ष॑सः

devanagari.text: दिवो नाके मधुजिह्वा असश्चतो वेना दुहंत्युक्षणं गिरिष्ठां ।अप्सु द्रप्सं वावृधानं समुद्र आ सिंधोरूर्मा मधुमंतं पवित्र आ ॥
दिवः । नाके । मधुऽजिह्वाः । असश्चतः । वेनाः । दुहन्ति । उक्षणम् । गिरिऽस्थाम् ।अप्ऽसु । द्रप्सम् । ववृधानम् । समुद्रे । आ । सिन्धोः । ऊर्मा । मधुऽमन्तम् । पवित्रे । आ ॥

transliteration.text: diváḥ ǀ nā́ke ǀ mádhu-jihvāḥ ǀ asaścátaḥ ǀ venā́ḥ ǀ duhanti ǀ ukṣáṇam ǀ giri-sthā́m ǀap-sú ǀ drapsám ǀ vavṛdhānám ǀ samudré ǀ ā́ ǀ síndhoḥ ǀ ūrmā́ ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ pavítre ǀ ā́ ǁ

Sukta 85.translation: “In the heaven of the bright (ssacrifice) the sweet-voicedVenasseverally milk forth the sprinkler, the mountain-haunting (Soma); (they sprinkle him) nourished in the waters, juicy, in the ocean (-like pitcher), in the wave of the river; (they sprinkle him) sweet-flavoured, in the filter.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वो नाके॒ मधु॑जिह्वा अस॒श्चतो॑ वे॒ना दु॑हन्त्यु॒क्षणं॑ गिरि॒ष्ठाम् । अ॒प्सु द्र॒प्सं वा॑वृधा॒नं स॑मु॒द्र आ सिन्धो॑रू॒र्मा मधु॑मन्तं प॒वित्र॒ आ

devanagari.text: नाके सुपर्णमुपपप्तिवांसं गिरो वेनानामकृपंत पूर्वीः ।शिशुं रिहंति मतयः पनिप्नतं हिरण्ययं शकुनं क्षामणि स्थां ॥
नाके । सुऽपर्णम् । उपपप्तिऽवांसम् । गिरः । वेनानाम् । अकृपन्त । पूर्वीः ।शिशुम् । रिहन्ति । मतयः । पनिप्नतम् । हिरण्ययम् । शकुनम् । क्षामणि । स्थाम् ॥

transliteration.text: nā́ke ǀ su-parṇám ǀ upapapti-vā́ṃsam ǀ gíraḥ ǀ venā́nām ǀ akṛpanta ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀśíśum ǀ rihanti ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ pánipnatam ǀ hiraṇyáyam ǀ śakunám ǀ kṣā́maṇi ǀ sthā́m ǁ

Sukta 85.translation: “The many voices of theVenaspraise (theSomawho dwells) in heaven, well-winged, falling (to earth); praises soothe the crying infant, the golden bird, reposing on the earth.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नाके॑ सुप॒र्णमु॑पपप्ति॒वांसं॒ गिरो॑ वे॒नाना॑मकृपन्त पू॒र्वीः । शिशुं॑ रिहन्ति म॒तय॒: पनि॑प्नतं हिर॒ण्ययं॑ शकु॒नं क्षाम॑णि॒ स्थाम्

devanagari.text: ऊर्ध्वो गंधर्वो अधि नाके अस्थाद्विश्वा रूपा प्रतिचक्षाणो अस्य ।भानुः शुक्रेण शोचिषा व्यद्यौत्प्रारूरुचद्रोदसी मातरा शुचिः ॥
ऊर्ध्वः । गन्धर्वः । अधि । नाके । अस्थात् । विश्वा । रूपा । प्रतिऽचक्षाणः । अस्य ।भानुः । शुक्रेण । शोचिषा । वि । अद्यौत् । प्र । अरूरुचत् । रोदसी इति । मातरा । शुचिः ॥

transliteration.text: ūrdhváḥ ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ nā́ke ǀ asthāt ǀ víśvā ǀ rūpā́ ǀ prati-cákṣāṇaḥ ǀ asya ǀbhānúḥ ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǀ ví ǀ adyaut ǀ prá ǀ arūrucat ǀ ródasī íti ǀ mātárā ǀ śúciḥ ǁ

Sukta 85.translation: “The elevatedgandharvaabides above the sun contemplating all its forms; the sun shines with white light, radiant he illumines the creative heaven and earth.”
Sukta 85.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऊ॒र्ध्वो ग॑न्ध॒र्वो अधि॒ नाके॑ अस्था॒द्विश्वा॑ रू॒पा प्र॑ति॒चक्षा॑णो अस्य । भा॒नुः शु॒क्रेण॑ शो॒चिषा॒ व्य॑द्यौ॒त्प्रारू॑रुच॒द्रोद॑सी मा॒तरा॒ शुचि॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “Your (juices), purified (Soma), all-pervading, quick as thought, go of themselves like the offspring of swift (mares); the celestial well-winged sweet-flavoured juices, great exciters of exhilaration, alight upon the receptacle.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र त॑ आ॒शव॑: पवमान धी॒जवो॒ मदा॑ अर्षन्ति रघु॒जा इ॑व॒ त्मना॑ । दि॒व्याः सु॑प॒र्णा मधु॑मन्त॒ इन्द॑वो म॒दिन्त॑मास॒: परि॒ कोश॑मासते

Sukta 86.translation: “Your exhilarating, all-pervading juices are let loose separately like chariot-horses; the sweet-flavoured (Soma) waves (go) toIndrathe wilder of the thunderbolt as a cow with her milk to the calf.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र ते॒ मदा॑सो मदि॒रास॑ आ॒शवोऽसृ॑क्षत॒ रथ्या॑सो॒ यथा॒ पृथ॑क् । धे॒नुर्न व॒त्सं पय॑सा॒भि व॒ज्रिण॒मिन्द्र॒मिन्द॑वो॒ मधु॑मन्त ऊ॒र्मय॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “Like a horse urged on to battle, do you who are all-knowing rush from heaven to the receptacle whose mother is the cloud;Somathe showerer (of benefits) is being purified at the top upon the woollen filter forIndra's strength which supports (the world).”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अत्यो॒ न हि॑या॒नो अ॒भि वाज॑मर्ष स्व॒र्वित्कोशं॑ दि॒वो अद्रि॑मातरम् । वृषा॑ प॒वित्रे॒ अधि॒ सानो॑ अ॒व्यये॒ सोम॑: पुना॒न इ॑न्द्रि॒याय॒ धाय॑से

Sukta 86.translation: “Purified (Soma), your celestial steed-like (streams) as quick as thought are poured along with the milk into the receptacle; the ṛṣis, the ordainers (of sacrifice), who cleanse you, O ṛṣi-enjoyed (Soma), pour your continuous (streams) into the midst (of the vessel).”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र त॒ आश्वि॑नीः पवमान धी॒जुवो॑ दि॒व्या अ॑सृग्र॒न्पय॑सा॒ धरी॑मणि । प्रान्तॠष॑य॒: स्थावि॑रीरसृक्षत॒ ये त्वा॑ मृ॒जन्त्यृ॑षिषाण वे॒धस॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “All-seeing (Soma), the mighty rays of you, who are the lord, encompass all the sphere; pervading (all things) you flow, Soma, through your functions; you rule lord of the whole world.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: विश्वा॒ धामा॑नि विश्वचक्ष॒ ऋभ्व॑सः प्र॒भोस्ते॑ स॒तः परि॑ यन्ति के॒तव॑: । व्या॒न॒शिः प॑वसे सोम॒ धर्म॑भि॒: पति॒र्विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य राजसि

Sukta 86.translation: “The rays, the tokens of the extant, steady, purifiedSoma, circulate from both worlds; when the green-tinted juice is cleansed upon the filter, reposing it alights upon its station, the pitchers.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उ॒भ॒यत॒: पव॑मानस्य र॒श्मयो॑ ध्रु॒वस्य॑ स॒तः परि॑ यन्ति के॒तव॑: । यदी॑ प॒वित्रे॒ अधि॑ मृ॒ज्यते॒ हरि॒: सत्ता॒ नि योना॑ क॒लशे॑षु सीदति

Sukta 86.translation: “Soma, the signal of sacrifice, the object of pious worship, flows filtered; it approaches the abode of the gods; the thousand-streamed rushes to the receptacle, the showerer passes roaring through the filter.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: य॒ज्ञस्य॑ के॒तुः प॑वते स्वध्व॒रः सोमो॑ दे॒वाना॒मुप॑ याति निष्कृ॒तम् । स॒हस्र॑धार॒: परि॒ कोश॑मर्षति॒ वृषा॑ प॒वित्र॒मत्ये॑ति॒ रोरु॑वत्

Sukta 86.translation: “The royal (Soma) plural nges into the firmament, (and) the rivers (thereof), mixed with the streams, he associates with the wave of the waters; being filtered he stands upon the uplifted woollen (filter) on the navel of the earth, the upholder of the vast heaven.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: राजा॑ समु॒द्रं न॒द्यो॒३॒॑ वि गा॑हते॒ऽपामू॒र्मिं स॑चते॒ सिन्धु॑षु श्रि॒तः । अध्य॑स्था॒त्सानु॒ पव॑मानो अ॒व्ययं॒ नाभा॑ पृथि॒व्या ध॒रुणो॑ म॒हो दि॒वः

Sukta 86.translation: “Thundering like the summit of the sky (theSoma) roars, by whose support both heaven and earth, (are upheld); the Soma flows acquiringIndra's friendship, purified he alights upon the pitchers.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वो न सानु॑ स्त॒नय॑न्नचिक्रद॒द्द्यौश्च॒ यस्य॑ पृथि॒वी च॒ धर्म॑भिः । इन्द्र॑स्य स॒ख्यं प॑वते वि॒वेवि॑द॒त्सोम॑: पुना॒नः क॒लशे॑षु सीदति

Sukta 86.translation: “The light of the sacrifice, he distils sweet (juice) delightful (to the gods), the parent of the gods, the genitive rator (of all), possessed of ample wealth; he supports the hidden wealth of heaven and earth, the most exhilarating, the exciting (Soma), the nourisher of (Indra), the juice.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ज्योति॑र्य॒ज्ञस्य॑ पवते॒ मधु॑ प्रि॒यं पि॒ता दे॒वानां॑ जनि॒ता वि॒भूव॑सुः । दधा॑ति॒ रत्नं॑ स्व॒धयो॑रपी॒च्यं॑ म॒दिन्त॑मो मत्स॒र इ॑न्द्रि॒यो रस॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “The rapid (Soma), thelord of heaven, the thousand-streamed, the beholder (of all), rushes crying aloud to the pitcher, the green-tinted one alights uponMitra's dwelling plural ce, cleansed by the sheep's hairs and the waters, the shower.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि॒क्रन्द॑न्क॒लशं॑ वा॒ज्य॑र्षति॒ पति॑र्दि॒वः श॒तधा॑रो विचक्ष॒णः । हरि॑र्मि॒त्रस्य॒ सद॑नेषु सीदति मर्मृजा॒नोऽवि॑भि॒: सिन्धु॑भि॒र्वृषा॑

Sukta 86.translation: “In the front of the waters rushes the filtered (Soma), foremost (he rushes) in the front of the voice, he goes among the rays; in the front he engages in battle (to win) food; well-armed, the showerer (of benefits), he is purified by the offerers of the oblation.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अग्रे॒ सिन्धू॑नां॒ पव॑मानो अर्ष॒त्यग्रे॑ वा॒चो अ॑ग्रि॒यो गोषु॑ गच्छति । अग्रे॒ वाज॑स्य भजते महाध॒नं स्वा॑यु॒धः सो॒तृभि॑: पूयते॒ वृषा॑

Sukta 86.translation: “This (Soma) possessed of agreeable (praise) filtered, and sent forth, (quick) as a bird goes with a stream (of juice) through the fleece; by your sustaining act, by your intelligence, sageIndra, the pure Soma flows purified through both heaven and earth.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं म॒तवा॑ञ्छकु॒नो यथा॑ हि॒तोऽव्ये॑ ससार॒ पव॑मान ऊ॒र्मिणा॑ । तव॒ क्रत्वा॒ रोद॑सी अन्त॒रा क॑वे॒ शुचि॑र्धि॒या प॑वते॒ सोम॑ इन्द्र ते

Sukta 86.translation: “Wearing a coat of mail reaching to heaven, the adorableSoma, who fills the firmament (with rain), plural ced in the waters, genitive rating heaven,passes with the water, (and) worships its ancient parent (Indra).”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्रा॒पिं वसा॑नो यज॒तो दि॑वि॒स्पृश॑मन्तरिक्ष॒प्रा भुव॑ने॒ष्वर्पि॑तः । स्व॑र्जज्ञा॒नो नभ॑सा॒भ्य॑क्रमीत्प्र॒त्नम॑स्य पि॒तर॒मा वि॑वासति

Sukta 86.translation: “(Soma), who first reachedIndra's glorious body, gives great happiness to the entrance of Indra (that Soma), whose station is in the highest heaven, and through whom (Indra) triumphs in all contests.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सो अ॑स्य वि॒शे महि॒ शर्म॑ यच्छति॒ यो अ॑स्य॒ धाम॑ प्रथ॒मं व्या॑न॒शे । प॒दं यद॑स्य पर॒मे व्यो॑म॒न्यतो॒ विश्वा॑ अ॒भि सं या॑ति सं॒यत॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “Indugoes toIndra's abode, the friend leaves not the stomach of his friend; as a young man meets maidens, so theSoma(meets) the pitcher by a hundred pathṣ ”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रो अ॑यासी॒दिन्दु॒रिन्द्र॑स्य निष्कृ॒तं सखा॒ सख्यु॒र्न प्र मि॑नाति सं॒गिर॑म् । मर्य॑ इव युव॒तिभि॒: सम॑र्षति॒ सोम॑: क॒लशे॑ श॒तया॑म्ना प॒था

Sukta 86.translation: “Your thoughtful worshippers (Soma), desiring an exhilarating sound, purposing praise, advance into the halls of sacrifice; the praisers the lords of intellect praise Soma, the kine approach him with their milk.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र वो॒ धियो॑ मन्द्र॒युवो॑ विप॒न्युव॑: पन॒स्युव॑: सं॒वस॑नेष्वक्रमुः । सोमं॑ मनी॒षा अ॒भ्य॑नूषत॒ स्तुभो॒ऽभि धे॒नव॒: पय॑सेमशिश्रयुः

Sukta 86.translation: “RadiantSoma, when filtered, pour upon us accusative ulated unwasting nutritious food, which is milked for us three times a day, without hindrance, giving forth a sound, yielding strength and delight and fairmaleoffspring.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ न॑: सोम सं॒यतं॑ पि॒प्युषी॒मिष॒मिन्दो॒ पव॑स्व॒ पव॑मानो अ॒स्रिध॑म् । या नो॒ दोह॑ते॒ त्रिरह॒न्नस॑श्चुषी क्षु॒मद्वाज॑व॒न्मधु॑मत्सु॒वीर्य॑म्

Sukta 86.translation: “The all-obsergantSoma, the showerer (of the desires) of his eulogists, the increase of the day, the dawn, the sun; maker of rivers he desires to enter the pitchers, penetrating toIndra's heart, (praised) by the wise. ”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वृषा॑ मती॒नां प॑वते विचक्ष॒णः सोमो॒ अह्न॑: प्रतरी॒तोषसो॑ दि॒वः । क्रा॒णा सिन्धू॑नां क॒लशाँ॑ अवीवश॒दिन्द्र॑स्य॒ हार्द्या॑वि॒शन्म॑नी॒षिभि॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “The ancient sage (Soma) is purified by the wise, guided by the priests he roars into the receptacles; genitive rating the water of the threefold (Indra), he distils sweet juice to gain Indra's andVāyu's friendship.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: म॒नी॒षिभि॑: पवते पू॒र्व्यः क॒विर्नृभि॑र्य॒तः परि॒ कोशाँ॑ अचिक्रदत् । त्रि॒तस्य॒ नाम॑ ज॒नय॒न्मधु॑ क्षर॒दिन्द्र॑स्य वा॒योः स॒ख्याय॒ कर्त॑वे

Sukta 86.translation: “(It is) he (who), when purified, illumines the dawn; he the maker of the world is (prosperous) for the rivers; thisSoma, having milked the thrice seven (cows) of their curds and milk, exhilarating, flows plural asantly to (go to) the heart.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒यं पु॑ना॒न उ॒षसो॒ वि रो॑चयद॒यं सिन्धु॑भ्यो अभवदु लोक॒कृत् । अ॒यं त्रिः स॒प्त दु॑दुहा॒न आ॒शिरं॒ सोमो॑ हृ॒दे प॑वते॒ चारु॑ मत्स॒रः

Sukta 86.translation: “Flow,Soma, to the heavenly abodes; let forth, OIndu, (proceed) to the pitcher, to the filter; alighting uponIndra's belly with a noise, guided by the priests, make the sun ascend the sky.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑स्व सोम दि॒व्येषु॒ धाम॑सु सृजा॒न इ॑न्दो क॒लशे॑ प॒वित्र॒ आ । सीद॒न्निन्द्र॑स्य ज॒ठरे॒ कनि॑क्रद॒न्नृभि॑र्य॒तः सूर्य॒मारो॑हयो दि॒वि

Sukta 86.translation: “Effused with the stones, you flow,Indu, into the filter entering the belly ofIndra;Soma, the contemplator, you do look upon man (with affection); you did open the cloud for theaṅgirasas.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अद्रि॑भिः सु॒तः प॑वसे प॒वित्र॒ आँ इन्द॒विन्द्र॑स्य ज॒ठरे॑ष्वावि॒शन् । त्वं नृ॒चक्षा॑ अभवो विचक्षण॒ सोम॑ गो॒त्रमङ्गि॑रोभ्योऽवृणो॒रप॑

Sukta 86.translation: “The pious worshippers desirous of preservation have glorified you,Soma, when being purified; the hawk brought you from heaven,Indu, adorned with all praises.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वां सो॑म॒ पव॑मानं स्वा॒ध्योऽनु॒ विप्रा॑सो अमदन्नव॒स्यव॑: । त्वां सु॑प॒र्ण आभ॑रद्दि॒वस्परीन्दो॒ विश्वा॑भिर्म॒तिभि॒: परि॑ष्कृतम्

Sukta 86.translation: “The seven kine approach the green-tinted (Soma) who flows purified in a stream through the woollen fleece, mighty men urge (you) the sage on the lap of the waters to the plural ce of sacrifice.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अव्ये॑ पुना॒नं परि॒ वार॑ ऊ॒र्मिणा॒ हरिं॑ नवन्ते अ॒भि स॒प्त धे॒नव॑: । अ॒पामु॒पस्थे॒ अध्या॒यव॑: क॒विमृ॒तस्य॒ योना॑ महि॒षा अ॑हेषत

Sukta 86.translation: “Indu, purified, plural nges through his foes making all things easy of access to the worshipper; making his body liquid, lovable and wise, he rishes through the filter sporting like a horse.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्दु॑: पुना॒नो अति॑ गाहते॒ मृधो॒ विश्वा॑नि कृ॒ण्वन्त्सु॒पथा॑नि॒ यज्य॑वे । गाः कृ॑ण्वा॒नो नि॒र्णिजं॑ हर्य॒तः क॒विरत्यो॒ न क्रीळ॒न्परि॒ वार॑मर्षति

Sukta 86.translation: “Separate, hundred-streamed, commingling (with theSoma), water-desiring, (the sun's rays) approach the green-tinted (Soma); the fingers cleanse him pervaded by rays, in the third sphere illumined by the sun.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स॒श्चत॑: श॒तधा॑रा अभि॒श्रियो॒ हरिं॑ नव॒न्तेऽव॒ ता उ॑द॒न्युव॑: । क्षिपो॑ मृजन्ति॒ परि॒ गोभि॒रावृ॑तं तृ॒तीये॑ पृ॒ष्ठे अधि॑ रोच॒ने दि॒वः

Sukta 86.translation: “All these are the offspring of your celestial effluence; you are the ruler of the whole world; so, purified (Soma) this universe is in subjection to you; you,Indu, are the foremost, the supporter of the house.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तवे॒माः प्र॒जा दि॒व्यस्य॒ रेत॑स॒स्त्वं विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य राजसि । अथे॒दं विश्वं॑ पवमान ते॒ वशे॒ त्वमि॑न्दो प्रथ॒मो धा॑म॒धा अ॑सि

Sukta 86.translation: “You, O sage, are the ocean, you are omniscient; these five regions (rest) on your support; you sustain both heaven and earth; the sun, OPavamāna(nourishes) your luminaries.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं स॑मु॒द्रो अ॑सि विश्व॒वित्क॑वे॒ तवे॒माः पञ्च॑ प्र॒दिशो॒ विध॑र्मणि । त्वं द्यां च॑ पृथि॒वीं चाति॑ जभ्रिषे॒ तव॒ ज्योतीं॑षि पवमान॒ सूर्य॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “PurifiedSoma, you are purified for the gods in the filter the supporter of the worlds; the chief (priests) desiring (you) lay hold (of you), all these worlds offer themselves to you.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं प॒वित्रे॒ रज॑सो॒ विध॑र्मणि दे॒वेभ्य॑: सोम पवमान पूयसे । त्वामु॒शिज॑: प्रथ॒मा अ॑गृभ्णत॒ तुभ्ये॒मा विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि येमिरे

Sukta 86.translation: “The sounding (Soma) passes through the woollen fleece; the green-tinted showerer cries in the waters; the worshippers desiring (the Soma) praise him together, the laudations soothe the infant as he cries.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र रे॒भ ए॒त्यति॒ वार॑म॒व्ययं॒ वृषा॒ वने॒ष्वव॑ चक्रद॒द्धरि॑: । सं धी॒तयो॑ वावशा॒ना अ॑नूषत॒ शिशुं॑ रिहन्ति म॒तय॒: पनि॑प्नतम्

Sukta 86.translation: “He invests himself with the rays of the sun stretching out the triple thread in the way he knows; guiding the recent adorations of the truthful (worshipper), the protection of women passes to the consecrated (vessel).”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स सूर्य॑स्य र॒श्मिभि॒: परि॑ व्यत॒ तन्तुं॑ तन्वा॒नस्त्रि॒वृतं॒ यथा॑ वि॒दे । नय॑न्नृ॒तस्य॑ प्र॒शिषो॒ नवी॑यसी॒: पति॒र्जनी॑ना॒मुप॑ याति निष्कृ॒तम्

Sukta 86.translation: “The sovereign of rivers flows pure, the lord of heaven goes with a shout by the paths of the sacrifice; the thousand-streamed green-tinted (Soma) is poured out, uttering a sound while being filtered, the bringer of wealth.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: राजा॒ सिन्धू॑नां पवते॒ पति॑र्दि॒व ऋ॒तस्य॑ याति प॒थिभि॒: कनि॑क्रदत् । स॒हस्र॑धार॒: परि॑ षिच्यते॒ हरि॑: पुना॒नो वाचं॑ ज॒नय॒न्नुपा॑वसुः

Sukta 86.translation: “Purified (Soma), you pour forth abundant juice; like the wonderful sun (you approach) the fleecy filters; purified by thehandsof the priests, expressed with the stones you flow for a mighty wealth-yielding conflict.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑मान॒ मह्यर्णो॒ वि धा॑वसि॒ सूरो॒ न चि॒त्रो अव्य॑यानि॒ पव्य॑या । गभ॑स्तिपूतो॒ नृभि॒रद्रि॑भिः सु॒तो म॒हे वाजा॑य॒ धन्या॑य धन्वसि

Sukta 86.translation: “You rush,Pavamāna, to (bring) food and strength; you alight on the pitchers like a falcon on its nest; (you) the exhilarating effused juice giving exhilaration toIndra, resembling the support of heaven, beholding (all things).”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इष॒मूर्जं॑ पवमाना॒भ्य॑र्षसि श्ये॒नो न वंसु॑ क॒लशे॑षु सीदसि । इन्द्रा॑य॒ मद्वा॒ मद्यो॒ मद॑: सु॒तो दि॒वो वि॑ष्ट॒म्भ उ॑प॒मो वि॑चक्ष॒णः

Sukta 86.translation: “The seven sister mothers approach the new-born, victorious sagacious infant,Soma, abiding amidst the waters, supporter of water, divine the contemplator of men to make him the ruler of the whole world.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स॒प्त स्वसा॑रो अ॒भि मा॒तर॒: शिशुं॒ नवं॑ जज्ञा॒नं जेन्यं॑ विप॒श्चित॑म् । अ॒पां ग॑न्ध॒र्वं दि॒व्यं नृ॒चक्ष॑सं॒ सोमं॒ विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य रा॒जसे॑

Sukta 86.translation: “Indu, who are the lord, you go (through) threse worlds, harnessing (to the car) your swift-moving steeds; let them dispense the sweet-flavoured shining liquor, may all men be presentSoma, at your worship.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ई॒शा॒न इ॒मा भुव॑नानि॒ वीय॑से युजा॒न इ॑न्दो ह॒रित॑: सुप॒र्ण्य॑: । तास्ते॑ क्षरन्तु॒ मधु॑मद्घृ॒तं पय॒स्तव॑ व्र॒ते सो॑म तिष्ठन्तु कृ॒ष्टय॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “You,Soma, are everywhere, the contemplator of men; you,Pavamāna, the showerer, hasten to these (waters); do you pour forth upon us (wealth), comprising various treasures and gold; may we be (able) to live in the worlds.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: त्वं नृ॒चक्षा॑ असि सोम वि॒श्वत॒: पव॑मान वृषभ॒ ता वि धा॑वसि । स न॑: पवस्व॒ वसु॑म॒द्धिर॑ण्यवद्व॒यं स्या॑म॒ भुव॑नेषु जी॒वसे॑

Sukta 86.translation: “Flow,Indu, who are the winner of cattle, wealth, and gold, the fructifier, plural ced upon the waters; you,Soma, are a hero, omniscient; you these sages approach with praise.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: गो॒वित्प॑वस्व वसु॒विद्धि॑रण्य॒विद्रे॑तो॒धा इ॑न्दो॒ भुव॑ने॒ष्वर्पि॑तः । त्वं सु॒वीरो॑ असि सोम विश्व॒वित्तं त्वा॒ विप्रा॒ उप॑ गि॒रेम आ॑सते

Sukta 86.translation: “The wave of the swee-flavoured (Soma) exfites voices (of praise); clothed in water the mighty one plural nges (into the pitcher); the king whose chariot is the filter mounts for the conflict, and, armed with a thousand weapons, wins ample sustenance (for us).”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: उन्मध्व॑ ऊ॒र्मिर्व॒नना॑ अतिष्ठिपद॒पो वसा॑नो महि॒षो वि गा॑हते । राजा॑ प॒वित्र॑रथो॒ वाज॒मारु॑हत्स॒हस्र॑भृष्टिर्जयति॒ श्रवो॑ बृ॒हत्

Sukta 86.translation: “The all-pervading (Soma) exfites both day and night all praises easily borne, productive of prosperity;Indu, when drunk, solicitIndra(to give) us food productive of progeny and riches filling our homes.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स भ॒न्दना॒ उदि॑यर्ति प्र॒जाव॑तीर्वि॒श्वायु॒र्विश्वा॑: सु॒भरा॒ अह॑र्दिवि । ब्रह्म॑ प्र॒जाव॑द्र॒यिमश्व॑पस्त्यं पी॒त इ॑न्द॒विन्द्र॑म॒स्मभ्यं॑ याचतात्

Sukta 86.translation: “At the beginning of the day the green-tinted delightful exhilarating (Soma) is recognized by the intelligence (of the praisers) and by their praises; approaching the two men he passes in the midst (of heaven and earth, bestowing) upon the upholder (of the rite) both human and divine (riches).”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सो अग्रे॒ अह्नां॒ हरि॑र्हर्य॒तो मद॒: प्र चेत॑सा चेतयत॒त अनु॒ द्युभि॑: । द्वा जना॑ या॒तय॑न्न॒न्तरी॑यते॒ नरा॑ च॒ शंसं॒ दैव्यं॑ च ध॒र्तरि॑

Sukta 86.translation: “(The priests) smear and grease and anoint (theSomawith milk); (the gods) taste the invigorating (juice); they smear it over with sweet (milk). Purifying it with gold, they plural nge it into those (waters) the sprinkler, the beholder, falling into the seething torrent.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ञ्जते॒ व्य॑ञ्जते॒ सम॑ञ्जते॒ क्रतुं॑ रिहन्ति॒ मधु॑ना॒भ्य॑ञ्जते । सिन्धो॑रुच्छ्वा॒से प॒तय॑न्तमु॒क्षणं॑ हिरण्यपा॒वाः प॒शुमा॑सु गृभ्णते

Sukta 86.translation: “Sing (you priests) to the intelligentPavamāna; like a mighty shower he sends forth food; like a snake he glides out of his old skin, sporting like a horse he hastens forth, the showerer, green-tinted.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वि॒प॒श्चिते॒ पव॑मानाय गायत म॒ही न धारात्यन्धो॑ अर्षति । अहि॒र्न जू॒र्णामति॑ सर्पति॒ त्वच॒मत्यो॒ न क्रीळ॑न्नसर॒द्वृषा॒ हरि॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “(Soma) going foremost, radiant, sanctified by water, plural ced in the firmament as the measure of days is glorified; green-tinted, shedding water, of goodly aspect, the source of moisture, borne in a chariot of light he flows giving wealth, friendly to the house.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ग्रे॒गो राजाप्य॑स्तविष्यते वि॒मानो॒ अह्नां॒ भुव॑ने॒ष्वर्पि॑तः । हरि॑र्घृ॒तस्नु॑: सु॒दृशी॑को अर्ण॒वो ज्यो॒तीर॑थः पवते रा॒य ओ॒क्य॑:

Sukta 86.translation: “The supporter of heaven the prepared exhilarating (Soma) is let loose, the triple (beverage) rushes to the waters; the worshippers taste the sounding Soma juice, when the reciters of holy texts approach the embodied (beverage) with praise.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अस॑र्जि स्क॒म्भो दि॒व उद्य॑तो॒ मद॒: परि॑ त्रि॒धातु॒र्भुव॑नान्यर्षति । अं॒शुं रि॑हन्ति म॒तय॒: पनि॑प्नतं गि॒रा यदि॑ नि॒र्णिज॑मृ॒ग्मिणो॑ य॒युः

Sukta 86.translation: “The rapid streams of you when you are purified,being collected together pass through the interstices of the fleece; when you are mixed with water in the ladles, you,Soma, on being effused alight on the pitchers.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र ते॒ धारा॒ अत्यण्वा॑नि मे॒ष्य॑: पुना॒नस्य॑ सं॒यतो॑ यन्ति॒ रंह॑यः । यद्गोभि॑रिन्दो च॒म्वो॑: सम॒ज्यस॒ आ सु॑वा॒नः सो॑म क॒लशे॑षु सीदसि

Sukta 86.translation: “Flow for us,Soma, cognizant of (our) worship and deserving praise; pour (your) beloved sweet-flavoured (juice) upon the woollen fleece; slay,Indu, all the voraciousrākṣasas; blessed with excellentmaleoffspring may we offer ample (praises) at the sacrifice.”
Sukta 86.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑स्व सोम क्रतु॒विन्न॑ उ॒क्थ्योऽव्यो॒ वारे॒ परि॑ धाव॒ मधु॑ प्रि॒यम् । ज॒हि विश्वा॑न्र॒क्षस॑ इन्दो अ॒त्रिणो॑ बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीरा॑:

Sukta 87.translation: “Flow fast (Soma), sit down on the receptacle, purified by the priests hasten (showing) food (to the sacrificer); cleansing you like a strong horse, they guide you with (their fingers for) reins to the sacred grass.”
Sukta 87.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र तु द्र॑व॒ परि॒ कोशं॒ नि षी॑द॒ नृभि॑: पुना॒नो अ॒भि वाज॑मर्ष । अश्वं॒ न त्वा॑ वा॒जिनं॑ म॒र्जय॒न्तोऽच्छा॑ ब॒र्ही र॑श॒नाभि॑र्नयन्ति

Sukta 87.translation: “The divine,Induwell-armed flows forth, the destroyer ofrākṣasas, averting calamity, the protector of the gods, the progenitor, the powerful one, the prop of heaven, the support of the earth.”
Sukta 87.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्वा॒यु॒धः प॑वते दे॒व इन्दु॑रशस्ति॒हा वृ॒जनं॒ रक्ष॑माणः । पि॒ता दे॒वानां॑ जनि॒ता सु॒दक्षो॑ विष्ट॒म्भो दि॒वो ध॒रुण॑: पृथि॒व्याः

Sukta 87.translation: “The ṛṣi, the sage, the foremost of men, the far-shining intelligent Uṣanas-- he verily by his poetic gift discovered the secret milk of those cows which was hidden and concealed.”
Sukta 87.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋषि॒र्विप्र॑: पुरए॒ता जना॑नामृ॒भुर्धीर॑ उ॒शना॒ काव्ये॑न । स चि॑द्विवेद॒ निहि॑तं॒ यदा॑सामपी॒च्यं१॒॑ गुह्यं॒ नाम॒ गोना॑म्

Sukta 87.translation: “For you,Indra, the showerer, this sweet-flavouredSomathe showerer has been poured into the filter; the giver of thousand-fold wealth, the giver of hundred-fold wealth, the giver of abundant wealth, the powerful is present at the eternal sacrifice.”

Sukta 87.translation: “TheseSoma-juices, (going towards) the thousand viands produced by the kine, purified, by the filters, are let loose for ample food and ambrosia, desiring food like horses victorious over a host.”

Sukta 87.translation: “Invoked by many, theSoma, undergoing purification, pours forth all food (for the sake of men); falcon-borne, bring us food, conveying wealth send forth your juice.”

Sukta 87.translation: “When effused, this quick-flowingSomahastens to the filter like a steed let loose; while alighting he moves like a buffalo sharpening his pointed horns, like a warrior on a foray for cattle.”

Sukta 87.translation: “ThisSomastream has come from on high and has detected the cattle which were in a stall (hidden) somewhere within the mountain; the stream of the Soma flows for you,Indra, thundering like lightning emitted by the clouds from heaven.”

Sukta 87.translation: “And being purified,Soma, you pursue the herd of (stolen) cattle in the same chariot withIndra; O you who give quickly, give (us) when invoked plural ntiful and abundant viands, for they are your (property) O you who abound in food.”

Sukta 88.translation: “ThisSomais expressed for you,Indra; for you is filtered; do you drink of it; it is theInduSoma which you have made, which you have chosen for your exhilaration, your companion.”

Sukta 88.translation: “It has been harnessed like a great wagon that bears heavy burdens in order to bring us many treasures; after this may all the races of men expecting our (attack) go to the desirable battle.”
Sukta 88.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स ईं॒ रथो॒ न भु॑रि॒षाळ॑योजि म॒हः पु॒रूणि॑ सा॒तये॒ वसू॑नि । आदीं॒ विश्वा॑ नहु॒ष्या॑णि जा॒ता स्व॑र्षाता॒ वन॑ ऊ॒र्ध्वा न॑वन्त

devanagari.text: वायुर्न यो नियुत्वाँ इष्टयामा नासत्येव हव आ शंभविष्ठः ।विश्ववारो द्रविणोदा इव त्मन्पूषेव धीजवनोऽसि सोम ॥

Sukta 88.translation: “You,Soma, who likeVāyuwith hisNiyutsteeds go where you list, who like theNāsatyāson hearing the invocation do grant abundant felicity, you are of yourself desired by all like the giver of wealth, you are likePūṣan, swift as thought.”
Sukta 88.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वा॒युर्न यो नि॒युत्वाँ॑ इ॒ष्टया॑मा॒ नास॑त्येव॒ हव॒ आ शम्भ॑विष्ठः । वि॒श्ववा॑रो द्रविणो॒दा इ॑व॒ त्मन्पू॒षेव॑ धी॒जव॑नोऽसि सोम

Sukta 88.translation: “You,Soma, who likeIndraperform mighty acts, are the slayer of theVṛtras, the destroyer of those who are called serpents; you are the slayer of everyDasyu.”
Sukta 88.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रो॒ न यो म॒हा कर्मा॑णि॒ चक्रि॑र्ह॒न्ता वृ॒त्राणा॑मसि सोम पू॒र्भित् । पै॒द्वो न हि त्वमहि॑नाम्नां ह॒न्ता विश्व॑स्यासि सोम॒ दस्यो॑:

devanagari.text: अग्निर्न यो वन आ सृज्यमानो वृथा पाजांसि कृणुते नदीषु ।जनो न युध्वा महत उपब्दिरियर्ति सोमः पवमान ऊर्मिं ॥

Sukta 88.translation: “Somawho, likeAgnilet loose in a forest, easily manifests his might in the waters like a man who fights shouting against his mighty (foe)-- so Soma when purified urges on his wave.”
Sukta 88.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒ग्निर्न यो वन॒ आ सृ॒ज्यमा॑नो॒ वृथा॒ पाजां॑सि कृणुते न॒दीषु॑ । जनो॒ न युध्वा॑ मह॒त उ॑प॒ब्दिरिय॑र्ति॒ सोम॒: पव॑मान ऊ॒र्मिम्

devanagari.text: एते सोमा अति वाराण्यव्या दिव्या न कोशासो अभ्रवर्षाः ।वृथा समुद्रं सिंधवो न नीचीः सुतासो अभि कलशाँ असृग्रन् ॥

transliteration.text: eté ǀ sómāḥ ǀ áti ǀ vā́rāṇi ǀ ávyā ǀ divyā́ ǀ ná ǀ kóśāsaḥ ǀ abhrá-varṣāḥ ǀvṛ́thā ǀ samudrám ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ nī́cīḥ ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ abhí ǀ kaláśān ǀ asṛgran ǁ

Sukta 88.translation: “TheseSoma-juices pass through the woollen fleece, like the rains of heaven showered by the clouds; the effused juices flow promptly to the pitchers as rivers running downwards (flow) into the ocean.”
Sukta 88.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ते सोमा॒ अति॒ वारा॒ण्यव्या॑ दि॒व्या न कोशा॑सो अ॒भ्रव॑र्षाः । वृथा॑ समु॒द्रं सिन्ध॑वो॒ न नीची॑: सु॒तासो॑ अ॒भि क॒लशाँ॑ असृग्रन्

devanagari.text: शुष्मी शर्धो न मारुतं पवस्वानभिशस्ता दिव्या यथा विट् ।आपो न मक्षू सुमतिर्भवा नः सहस्राप्साः पृतनाषाण्न यज्ञः ॥

Sukta 88.translation: “Flow strong as the army of theMaruts, like the divine blameless folk; like waters become quickly favourable to us; (you are) of a thousand shapes, adorable like (Indra) the victor in battle.”
Sukta 88.sanskrit_wisdomlib: शु॒ष्मी शर्धो॒ न मारु॑तं पव॒स्वान॑भिशस्ता दि॒व्या यथा॒ विट् । आपो॒ न म॒क्षू सु॑म॒तिर्भ॑वा नः स॒हस्रा॑प्साः पृतना॒षाण्न य॒ज्ञः

devanagari.text: राज्ञो नु ते वरुणस्य व्रतानि बृहद्गभीरं तव सोम धाम ।शुचिष्ट्वमसि प्रियो न मित्रो दक्षाय्यो अर्यमेवासि सोम ॥

Sukta 88.translation: “Your acts are (like) those of the royalVaruṇa, vast and profound,Soma, is your abode; you are pure as the belovedMitra, munificent are you, Soma, asAryaman.”
Sukta 88.sanskrit_wisdomlib: राज्ञो॒ नु ते॒ वरु॑णस्य व्र॒तानि॑ बृ॒हद्ग॑भी॒रं तव॑ सोम॒ धाम॑ । शुचि॒ष्ट्वम॑सि प्रि॒यो न मि॒त्रो द॒क्षाय्यो॑ अर्य॒मेवा॑सि सोम

Sukta 89.translation: “This horse of burden moves forth by the (sacrificial) paths; when purified you flow like the rain from heaven; the thousand-streamedSomasits down among us on his mother's lap in the water.”
Sukta 89.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रो स्य वह्नि॑: प॒थ्या॑भिरस्यान्दि॒वो न वृ॒ष्टिः पव॑मानो अक्षाः । स॒हस्र॑धारो असद॒न्न्य१॒॑स्मे मा॒तुरु॒पस्थे॒ वन॒ आ च॒ सोम॑:

devanagari.text: राजा सिंधूनामवसिष्ट वास ऋतस्य नावमारुहद्रजिष्ठां ।अप्सु द्रप्सो वावृधे श्येनजूतो दुह ईं पिता दुह ईं पितुर्जां ॥

Sukta 89.translation: “The sovereignSomahas put on the vestment of the waters, he has ascended the most straight-going ship of sacrifice; the dripping juice brought by the falcon has increased in the water; the father milks him-- milks him the son of the father.”
Sukta 89.sanskrit_wisdomlib: राजा॒ सिन्धू॑नामवसिष्ट॒ वास॑ ऋ॒तस्य॒ नाव॒मारु॑ह॒द्रजि॑ष्ठाम् । अ॒प्सु द्र॒प्सो वा॑वृधे श्ये॒नजू॑तो दु॒ह ईं॑ पि॒ता दु॒ह ईं॑ पि॒तुर्जाम्

Sukta 89.translation: “(The worshippers) reach the lion-like (Soma) the dispenser of water, green-tinted, red, the protector of this heaven; a hero in battles, first (among the gods) he seeks the (stolen) cows; by his might the sprinkler (Indra) protects (the universe).”
Sukta 89.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सिं॒हं न॑सन्त॒ मध्वो॑ अ॒यासं॒ हरि॑मरु॒षं दि॒वो अ॒स्य पति॑म् । शूरो॑ यु॒त्सु प्र॑थ॒मः पृ॑च्छते॒ गा अस्य॒ चक्ष॑सा॒ परि॑ पात्यु॒क्षा

Sukta 89.translation: “(The priests) attach to the broad-wheeled car the glossy-backed terrible active graceful horse; the sister fingers cleanse him; the kinsfolk invigorate the mighty (Soma).”
Sukta 89.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मधु॑पृष्ठं घो॒रम॒यास॒मश्वं॒ रथे॑ युञ्जन्त्युरुच॒क्र ऋ॒ष्वम् । स्वसा॑र ईं जा॒मयो॑ मर्जयन्ति॒ सना॑भयो वा॒जिन॑मूर्जयन्ति

Sukta 89.translation: “The four yielders of butter wait upon him, stationed in a common asylum; being purified they approach him with food, they surround him in numbers on every side.”

Sukta 89.translation: “The prop of heaven, the support of earth-- all beings (are) in hishands; may (Soma) the fountain (of desires) be possessed of horses for you (his) adorer; the filament of the sweet-flavoured (Soma) is purified for (the sake of winning) strength.”

Sukta 89.translation: “Conquering (and) unconquered approach the banquet of the gods;Soma, who are the slayer ofVṛtra, flow forIndra; grant us abundant and splendid riches, may we be masters of excellentmaleoffspring. ”

Sukta 90.translation: “Urged (by the priests) the genitive rator of heaven and earth advances like a chariot, wishing to distribute food; going toIndra, sharpening his weapons, holding all treasures in hishands.”

Sukta 90.translation: “The voices of the worshippers resound about him the triple-backed, the showerer (of benefits), the giver of food; arrayed in water asVaruṇa(is arrayed) in the rivers, the giver of precious wealth he bestows desirable riches.”

Sukta 90.translation: “Flow you who have a host of warriors, who have all the heroes, full of strength, victorious, the giver of riches, sharp-weaponed, rapid bowman, irresistible in battle, overthrowing the enemy (arrayed) in (hostile) armies.”

Sukta 90.translation: “Flow you whose paths are broad, giving security (to the worshipper), uniting heaven and earth, wishing to enjoy the waters of dawn, the sun and (his) rays you cry aloud, ( to bestow upon) us ample food.”

Sukta 90.translation: “Thus (glorified), to you (Soma) like a king, performing your functions, flow on destroying all evils by your might;Indu, give food (in answer) to (our) well-recited praise; do you (O gods) cherish us ever with blessings.”

Sukta 91.translation: “TheSomajuice effused by pious mortals (comes) down (to the sacrifice) for the food of the celestial people; which immortal (beverage) is purified by mortal (priests) with the filter, the curds and milk and the waters.”

Sukta 91.translation: “TheSomajuice the showerer (of benefits) roaring to the showerer (Indra) goes when being purified to (mix with) the glistening milk of the cow; greeted with laudation, cognizant of sacred praise, the hero passes through the filter by a thousand imperishable paths.”
Sukta 91.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वृषा॒ वृष्णे॒ रोरु॑वदं॒शुर॑स्मै॒ पव॑मानो॒ रुश॑दीर्ते॒ पयो॒ गोः । स॒हस्र॒मृक्वा॑ प॒थिभि॑र्वचो॒विद॑ध्व॒स्मभि॒: सूरो॒ अण्वं॒ वि या॑ति

Sukta 91.translation: “Demolish the strong dwellings of therākṣasa;Indu, when purified put on his strength; cut to pieces with your destructive weapon (therākṣasas) who come from above, from nigh, or from afar and their leader.”
Sukta 91.sanskrit_wisdomlib: रु॒जा दृ॒ळ्हा चि॑द्र॒क्षस॒: सदां॑सि पुना॒न इ॑न्द ऊर्णुहि॒ वि वाजा॑न् । वृ॒श्चोपरि॑ष्टात्तुज॒ता व॒धेन॒ ये अन्ति॑ दू॒रादु॑पना॒यमे॑षाम्

Sukta 91.translation: “Adorable (Soma), do you as of old grant the ancient paths to your new worshipper; doer of many acts, utterer of many sounds, may we obtain those (portions) of you which are difficult to defeat, inflicting injury (on foes) and mighty.”
Sukta 91.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स प्र॑त्न॒वन्नव्य॑से विश्ववार सू॒क्ताय॑ प॒थः कृ॑णुहि॒ प्राच॑: । ये दु॒:षहा॑सो व॒नुषा॑ बृ॒हन्त॒स्ताँस्ते॑ अश्याम पुरुकृत्पुरुक्षो

Sukta 91.translation: “Thus, being purified, bestow upon us the firmament and heaven and earth and many sons and grandsons;make our land prosper, diffuse the luminaries widely (in the firmament) and grant us long life to see the sun.”
Sukta 91.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा पु॑ना॒नो अ॒पः स्व१॒॑र्गा अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ तो॒का तन॑यानि॒ भूरि॑ । शं न॒: क्षेत्र॑मु॒रु ज्योतीं॑षि सोम॒ ज्योङ्न॒: सूर्यं॑ दृ॒शये॑ रिरीहि

Sukta 92.translation: “The green-tintedSomaeffused and sent forth (by the priests) is let loose, like a chariot upon the filter, for the acquisition (of riches); being filtered he acquires (Indra's) praise, he gratifies the gods with conciliatory (oblations).”

Sukta 92.translation: “The sage, the observer of men, retaining the water proceeds to his plural ce on the filter; like a ministrant priest sitting at the sacrifice (theSomaflows) into the cups; the seven wise ṛṣis approach him with praise.”

Sukta 92.translation: “Soma, the intelligent, the knower of the right path, accompanied by all the gods, undergoing purification goes to his constant abode; he is one who delights in all sacred praises; the sage endeavours to approach the five classes of beings.”

Sukta 92.translation: “OSomaPavamāna, you are the thrice eleven universal gods abiding in the secret (heaven); the ten (fingers) cleanse you with the waters upon the elevated fleece, the seven great rivers (cleanse you).”

Sukta 92.translation: “May thatplace of the truthfulPavamānabe quickly ours, when all the worshippers assemble (to praise him) the light (of theSoma) which gave manifestation to the day protectedManu-- Soma made it triumphant over theDasyu.”

Sukta 92.translation: “As theministrant priest proceeds to the hall where the victim is stationed, as a just king marches to battle, theSomaundergoing purification enters the pitcheers like the wild buffalo in the waters.”

Sukta 93.translation: “The sister (fingers) sprinkling together cleanse (theSoma), the ten fingers (are) the efffuse of the sagacious (Soma); the green-tinted one flows round the wives of the sun, he hastens like a swift horse to the pitcher.”

Sukta 93.translation: “InduPavamāna, do you with the gods, who do long for (our good) bestow upon us riches comprising horses; may your capacious mind longing for those who possess chariots (come) towards us to bestow treasures (upon us).”

Sukta 93.translation: “Soma, when you are purified, measure out to us riches and dependents and all-gratifying water.Indu, may the life of your praiser be prolonged; may (Soma) who acquires wealth by his intelligence come quickly at dawn.”

Sukta 94.translation: “When the fingers vie with each other in this (Soma), as the trappings on a horse or the rays in the sun, clothed in the waters he flows desiring his worshippers like (a cowherd going to) a plural asant cow-stall for the nourishment of his cattle.”

Sukta 94.translation: “Openingout the abode of the ambrosia on both sides (he passes between); for him, the omniscient, the worlds expand. Gratifying laudations eager for the sacrifice, call uponIndu, like kine (lowing) towards their stall.”

Sukta 94.translation: “When the sageSomagoes round the praises (of the wise) like a hostile chariot (going round) all the regions (of the battle-field), then desirous of bestowing upon mortals the wealth that abides with the gods, he (is) tobe glorified in the many plural ces of sacrifice for the preservation of the riches he has given.”

Sukta 95.translation: “The priests hurrying like the waves of the waters dispatch praises towardsSoma; adoring him they approach and come up together, longing for him who longs for them they enter him.”
Sukta 95.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒पामि॒वेदू॒र्मय॒स्तर्तु॑राणा॒: प्र म॑नी॒षा ई॑रते॒ सोम॒मच्छ॑ । न॒म॒स्यन्ती॒रुप॑ च॒ यन्ति॒ सं चा च॑ विशन्त्युश॒तीरु॒शन्त॑म्

Sukta 95.translation: “(The priests) milk forth theSomacleansed (dwelling) on a high plural ce like a buffalo, the sprinkler, plural ces between the grinding-stones; praises attend upon the longing Soma; (Indra) who dwells in three abodes supports him, the defeater of enemies, in the firmament.”

Sukta 95.translation: “Indu, being purified, stimulating the praise (of the worshippers) like the answer of thehotāset free the understanding; when (you) andIndraare present together (at the sacrifice) may we be prosperous, may we become the possessors of excellentmaleprogeny.”

Sukta 96.translation: “The leader of the host, a hero, advances in front of the chariots intent on seizing the cattle (of the enemy); his army exults; making their oblations toIndraprosperous for the friendly (worshippers),Somaassumes the hastily made robes (of curds and milk).”

Sukta 96.translation: “The priests express his green-tinted (juice); he mounts the chariot unyoked by the horse-driving salutations; the wiseSomathe friend ofIndragoes to meet the worshipper.”
Sukta 96.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सम॑स्य॒ हरिं॒ हर॑यो मृजन्त्यश्वह॒यैरनि॑शितं॒ नमो॑भिः । आ ति॑ष्ठति॒ रथ॒मिन्द्र॑स्य॒ सखा॑ वि॒द्वाँ ए॑ना सुम॒तिं या॒त्यच्छ॑

Sukta 96.translation: “DivineSoma, who are the beverage ofIndra, flow at our sacrifice for (his) abundant food; sending water, causing rain to fall upon heaven and upon this earth, (come) from the wide (firmament, and) being purified bestow upon us wealth.”
Sukta 96.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स नो॑ देव दे॒वता॑ते पवस्व म॒हे सो॑म॒ प्सर॑स इन्द्र॒पान॑: । कृ॒ण्वन्न॒पो व॒र्षय॒न्द्यामु॒तेमामु॒रोरा नो॑ वरिवस्या पुना॒नः

Sukta 96.translation: “Flow for our immunity from defeat and slaughter, flow for our welfare, for the great sacrifice for all the gods; all these my friends desire this; this I desire, OSomaPavamāna.”

Sukta 96.translation: “TheSomaflows, the genitive rator of praises, the genitive rator of heaven, the genitive rator of the earth, the genitive rator ofAgni, the genitive rator of the sun, the genitive rator ofIndra, and the genitive rator ofViṣṇu.”

Sukta 96.translation: “TheBrahmāof the gods, the guide of the sages, the ṛṣi of the pious, the buffalo of wild animals, the falcon of the vultures, the hatchet of deadly weapons, theSomapasses through the filter with a roar.”

Sukta 96.translation: “The purifiedSomaexcites gratifying praises as a river (excites) the wave of sound; the showerer (of benefits) beholding the hidden (treasure) presides over these irresistible powers, knowing about the cattle.”

Sukta 96.translation: “(Soma) who are the exhilarator, harming (the foe) in battles, (yourself) unharmed, who have a thousand streams, rush against the strength (of the enemy),Indu, who are being purified, the sage, uttering cries, urge on forIndrathe wave of juice.”

Sukta 96.translation: “The plural asing delightfulSomaapproached by gods (proceeds) to the pitcher to exhilarateIndra;Induthe thousand-streamed and vigorous proceeds like a strong horse to battle.”
Sukta 96.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॑ प्रि॒यः क॒लशे॑ दे॒ववा॑त॒ इन्द्रा॑य॒ सोमो॒ रण्यो॒ मदा॑य । स॒हस्र॑धारः श॒तवा॑ज॒ इन्दु॑र्वा॒जी न सप्ति॒: सम॑ना जिगाति

Sukta 96.translation: “The ancient (Soma) the finder of treasure as soon as genitive rated, cleansed in the waters milked on the stone, the defender against enemies, the sovereign of the world, purified for the sacrifice, shows (the worshipper) the right way.”

Sukta 96.translation: “SomaPavamāna, by you our ancient and wise progenitors performed their religious rites; harming the foes (yourself) unharmed slay therākṣasasand be liberal in enriching us withmaleoffspring and horses.”

Sukta 96.translation: “As you did flow toManupossessing food, slaying enemies, acquiring wealth, having oblations, so now flow bringing us riches; abide you inIndra; make manifest (your) weapons.”

Sukta 96.translation: “Somawho have exhilarating juice, who are connected with the sacrifice, clothed with water flow upon the elevated fleece; alight upon the water-holding pitchers, you who are most exhilarating, intoxicating, the especial beverage ofIndra.”

Sukta 96.translation: “(Soma), who flows in a hundred streams, pour rain from the firmament, you who are the giver of hundredfold (wealth), the bestower of food at the banquet of the gods; desirous of (the mixture) combine with the waters in the pitchers and with the curds and milk, prolonging our life.”

Sukta 96.translation: “ThisSoma(is) purified with praises, like a strong horse he overthrows (his) foes; (he is purified) like the strong milk milked from the cow, (flocked to by all) like a broad road, (and guided by the praisers) like a well-trained horse of burden.”

Sukta 96.translation: “Well-armed, purified by those who express you, send your concealed desirable form (into the pitchers); like a horse bring us food in our desire for food; divineSoma, bring us life, bring us cattle.”

Sukta 96.translation: “They cleanse the charming infant (Soma) at his birth; theMarutsdecorate the bearer (of boons) with their troop; bring wise with songs, wise with wisdom, Soma passes clamorous through the filter.”

Sukta 96.translation: “Thinking as a ṛṣi, acting as a ṛṣi, gaining heaven, praised by thousands, the guide of the wise, the mightySomadesiring to attain the third region (heaven), being praised adds lustre to the illustrious (Indra).”

Sukta 96.translation: “Flow,Indu, purified by the venerable (priests), rush through the filter crying repeatedly, sporting enter the plural nks purified, let your exhilarating beverage exhilarateIndra.”
Sukta 96.sanskrit_wisdomlib: पव॑स्वेन्दो॒ पव॑मानो॒ महो॑भि॒: कनि॑क्रद॒त्परि॒ वारा॑ण्यर्ष । क्रीळ॑ञ्च॒म्वो॒३॒॑रा वि॑श पू॒यमा॑न॒ इन्द्रं॑ ते॒ रसो॑ मदि॒रो म॑मत्तु

devanagari.text: प्रास्य धारा बृहतीरसृग्रन्नक्तो गोभिः कलशाँ आ विवेश ।साम कृण्वन्त्सामन्यो विपश्चित्क्रंदन्नेत्यभि सख्युर्न जामिं ॥

Sukta 96.translation: “His copious streams flow forth; blended with the milk and curds he enters the pitchers; uttering chants the skilful chanter (Soma) hasten invoking (the gods) towards (the cups) like (a libertine) to the wife of a friend.”
Sukta 96.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्रास्य॒ धारा॑ बृह॒तीर॑सृग्रन्न॒क्तो गोभि॑: क॒लशाँ॒ आ वि॑वेश । साम॑ कृ॒ण्वन्त्सा॑म॒न्यो॑ विप॒श्चित्क्रन्द॑न्नेत्य॒भि सख्यु॒र्न जा॒मिम्

Sukta 96.translation: “OPavamāna, eulogized (by the worshippers), distilling (into the receptacles), destroying the enemies, you go like a gallant to his mistress; falling like a bird alighting on the trees theSomawhen purified alights upon the pitchers.”
Sukta 96.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒प॒घ्नन्ने॑षि पवमान॒ शत्रू॑न्प्रि॒यां न जा॒रो अ॒भिगी॑त॒ इन्दु॑: । सीद॒न्वने॑षु शकु॒नो न पत्वा॒ सोम॑: पुना॒नः क॒लशे॑षु॒ सत्ता॑

Sukta 96.translation: “The lustres,Soma, of you when being purified, approach with abundant milk with copious streams like a woman (giving milk to her child); the green-tinted Soma, the desired of many, has been brought to the waters and cries repeatedly in the pitcher of the god-loving (worshippers).”
Sukta 96.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ ते॒ रुच॒: पव॑मानस्य सोम॒ योषे॑व यन्ति सु॒दुघा॑: सुधा॒राः । हरि॒रानी॑तः पुरु॒वारो॑ अ॒प्स्वचि॑क्रदत्क॒लशे॑ देवयू॒नाम्

devanagari.text: अस्य प्रेषा हेमना पूयमानो देवो देवेभिः समपृक्त रसं ।सुतः पवित्रं पर्येति रेभन्मितेव सद्म पशुमांति होता ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “The shining Somabeing purified by the goldenhandthat urges it forth, brings its juice into contact with the gods; when effused it proceeds with a roar to the filter like the ministrant priest to the halls prepared (for sacrifice) containing victims.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्य प्रे॒षा हे॒मना॑ पू॒यमा॑नो दे॒वो दे॒वेभि॒: सम॑पृक्त॒ रस॑म् । सु॒तः प॒वित्रं॒ पर्ये॑ति॒ रेभ॑न्मि॒तेव॒ सद्म॑ पशु॒मान्ति॒ होता॑

devanagari.text: भद्रा वस्त्रा समन्या वसानो महान्कविर्निवचनानि शंसन् ।आ वच्यस्व चम्वोः पूयमानो विचक्षणो जागृविर्देववीतौ ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “The great wiseSoma, clothed in his auspicious war-vestments, the inspirer of praises-- enter into the vessle when purified, you who are sagacious and vigilant at the banquet of the gods.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: भ॒द्रा वस्त्रा॑ सम॒न्या॒३॒॑ वसा॑नो म॒हान्क॒विर्नि॒वच॑नानि॒ शंस॑न् । आ व॑च्यस्व च॒म्वो॑: पू॒यमा॑नो विचक्ष॒णो जागृ॑विर्दे॒ववी॑तौ

Sukta 97.translation: “(Soma), the most famous of the famous, the earht-born, the conciliator, is cleansed for us in the elevated fleece; sound aloud in the firmament when purified; do you ever protect us with blessings.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: समु॑ प्रि॒यो मृ॑ज्यते॒ सानो॒ अव्ये॑ य॒शस्त॑रो य॒शसां॒ क्षैतो॑ अ॒स्मे । अ॒भि स्व॑र॒ धन्वा॑ पू॒यमा॑नो यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 97.translation: “Sing (to theSoma), let us praise the gods; send forth the Soma for (the acquisition of) great wealth. He passes sweet-flavoured pure through the fleecy filter; our (Soma) devoted to the gods alights on the pitcher.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र गा॑यता॒भ्य॑र्चाम दे॒वान्त्सोमं॑ हिनोत मह॒ते धना॑य । स्वा॒दुः प॑वाते॒ अति॒ वार॒मव्य॒मा सी॑दाति क॒लशं॑ देव॒युर्न॑:

devanagari.text: इंदुर्देवानामुप सख्यमायन्त्सहस्रधारः पवते मदाय ।नृभिः स्तवानो अनु धाम पूर्वमगन्निंद्रं महते सौभगाय ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “Inducoming to obtain the friendship of the god; flows in a thousand streams for (their) exhilaration, glorified by the priests (he proceeds) to his ancient station, he proceeds toIndrafor the sake of great prosperity (to the worshippers).”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्दु॑र्दे॒वाना॒मुप॑ स॒ख्यमा॒यन्त्स॒हस्र॑धारः पवते॒ मदा॑य । नृभि॒: स्तवा॑नो॒ अनु॒ धाम॒ पूर्व॒मग॒न्निन्द्रं॑ मह॒ते सौभ॑गाय

Sukta 97.translation: “(Soma), when our praise is offered, flow green-tinted and purified, to (bring us) riches, may your exhilarating beverage animateIndrato battle. Go in the same car with the gods to (procure us) wealth; do you ever protect us with blessings.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स्तो॒त्रे रा॒ये हरि॑रर्षा पुना॒न इन्द्रं॒ मदो॑ गच्छतु ते॒ भरा॑य । दे॒वैर्या॑हि स॒रथं॒ राधो॒ अच्छा॑ यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः

Sukta 97.translation: “Reciting sacred praise like Uṣanas the praiser (Vṛṣagaṇa) proclaims the births of the gods; assiduous in pious observances, of brilliant radiance, purifying (from sin), he approaches the filter making a noise (as) a wild boar (makes a noise) with its foot.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र काव्य॑मु॒शने॑व ब्रुवा॒णो दे॒वो दे॒वानां॒ जनि॑मा विवक्ति । महि॑व्रत॒: शुचि॑बन्धुः पाव॒कः प॒दा व॑रा॒हो अ॒भ्ये॑ति॒ रेभ॑न्

Sukta 97.translation: “The Vṛṣagaṇas (walking like) swans, (alarmed) at the strength (of the foe), having repaired to the house of sacrifice, to the swift-shooting foe-despising (Soma), the friends sound the flut to the praiseworthy irresistblePavamāna.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र हं॒सास॑स्तृ॒पलं॑ म॒न्युमच्छा॒मादस्तं॒ वृष॑गणा अयासुः । आ॒ङ्गू॒ष्यं१॒॑ पव॑मानं॒ सखा॑यो दु॒र्मर्षं॑ सा॒कं प्र व॑दन्ति वा॒णम्

devanagari.text: स रंहत उरुगायस्य जूतिं वृथा क्रीळंतं मिमते न गावः ।परीणसं कृणुते तिग्मशृंगो दिवा हरिर्ददृशे नक्तमृज्रः ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “He moves rapidly (following) the path of (him) the much-praised, (other) goers cannot overtake him (though he is) moving easily; sharp-horned he displays manifold (radiance); theSomaappears green-tinted by day, and clearly visible at night.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स रं॑हत उरुगा॒यस्य॑ जू॒तिं वृथा॒ क्रीळ॑न्तं मिमते॒ न गाव॑: । प॒री॒ण॒सं कृ॑णुते ति॒ग्मशृ॑ङ्गो॒ दिवा॒ हरि॒र्ददृ॑शे॒ नक्त॑मृ॒ज्रः

devanagari.text: इंदुर्वाजी पवते गोन्योघा इंद्रे सोमः सह इन्वन्मदाय ।हंति रक्षो बाधते पर्यरातीर्वरिवः कृण्वन्वृजनस्य राजा ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “The powerful, flowingSomahaving quantities o fjuice flowing down, streams forth infusing strength intoIndrafor his exhilaration; conferring wealth the king of strength slays therākṣasasand harasses the enemy.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्दु॑र्वा॒जी प॑वते॒ गोन्यो॑घा॒ इन्द्रे॒ सोम॒: सह॒ इन्व॒न्मदा॑य । हन्ति॒ रक्षो॒ बाध॑ते॒ पर्यरा॑ती॒र्वरि॑वः कृ॒ण्वन्वृ॒जन॑स्य॒ राजा॑

devanagari.text: अध धारया मध्वा पृचानस्तिरो रोम पवते अद्रिदुग्धः ।इंदुरिंद्रस्य सख्यं जुषाणो देवो देवस्य मत्सरो मदाय ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “Milked forth by the stones theSomaflows through the (sheep's) hair coming into contact (with the gods) with its sweet-flavoured stream; the divine exhilaratingIndudesiring the friendship ofIndraflows for the exhilaration of the deity. ”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अध॒ धार॑या॒ मध्वा॑ पृचा॒नस्ति॒रो रोम॑ पवते॒ अद्रि॑दुग्धः । इन्दु॒रिन्द्र॑स्य स॒ख्यं जु॑षा॒णो दे॒वो दे॒वस्य॑ मत्स॒रो मदा॑य

devanagari.text: अभि प्रियाणि पवते पुनानो देवो देवान्त्स्वेन रसेन पृंचन् ।इंदुर्धर्माण्यृतुथा वसानो दश क्षिपो अव्यत सानो अव्ये ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “Clothed in plural asant radiance suited to the season, the sportiveInduflows purified, reaching the gods with its juice; the ten fingers guide it to the elevated fleece.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि प्रि॒याणि॑ पवते पुना॒नो दे॒वो दे॒वान्त्स्वेन॒ रसे॑न पृ॒ञ्चन् । इन्दु॒र्धर्मा॑ण्यृतु॒था वसा॑नो॒ दश॒ क्षिपो॑ अव्यत॒ सानो॒ अव्ये॑

devanagari.text: वृषा शोणो अभिकनिक्रदद्गा नदयन्नेति पृथिवीमुत द्यां ।इंद्रस्येव वग्नुरा शृण्व आजौ प्रचेतयन्नर्षति वाचमेमां ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “(Calling out for the praises like) a red bull bellowing after the kine; theSomagoes with a roar through heaven and earth; (his voice) is heard as the voice ofIndra, manifesting (himself) he raises this voice.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वृषा॒ शोणो॑ अभि॒कनि॑क्रद॒द्गा न॒दय॑न्नेति पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्याम् । इन्द्र॑स्येव व॒ग्नुरा शृ॑ण्व आ॒जौ प्र॑चे॒तय॑न्नर्षति॒ वाच॒मेमाम्

devanagari.text: रसाय्यः पयसा पिन्वमान ईरयन्नेषि मधुमंतमंशुं ।पवमानः संतनिमेषि कृण्वन्निंद्राय सोम परिषिच्यमानः ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “plural asant to the taste, dripping with milk, you flow pouring forth the sweet-flavoured juice.Soma, when purified and sprinkled, you flow forIndrain a continuous stream.”

Sukta 97.translation: “Thus flow, the exhilarator, forIndra's exhilaration bowing down the rain-holder with (your) weapons, assuming brilliant colour, desirous of our cattle, flow,Soma, sprinkled (into the filter).”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा प॑वस्व मदि॒रो मदा॑योदग्रा॒भस्य॑ न॒मय॑न्वध॒स्नैः । परि॒ वर्णं॒ भर॑माणो॒ रुश॑न्तं ग॒व्युर्नो॑ अर्ष॒ परि॑ सोम सि॒क्तः

devanagari.text: जुष्ट्वी न इंदो सुपथा सुगान्युरौ पवस्व वरिवांसि कृण्वन् ।घनेव विष्वग्दुरितानि विघ्नन्नधि ष्णुना धन्व सानो अव्ये ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “Gratified (with our praises),Indu, flow into the large (vessel), granting us riches coming by holy paths and easily acquired; beating down therākṣasason every side as with a club, flow in a stream upon the elevated fleece.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: जु॒ष्ट्वी न॑ इन्दो सु॒पथा॑ सु॒गान्यु॒रौ प॑वस्व॒ वरि॑वांसि कृ॒ण्वन् । घ॒नेव॒ विष्व॑ग्दुरि॒तानि॑ वि॒घ्नन्नधि॒ ष्णुना॑ धन्व॒ सानो॒ अव्ये॑

Sukta 97.translation: “Sending us rain from heaven, quick-falling, food-giving, giving health to our home, promptly munificent; flow,Indu, seeking these lower winds your kinsmen as (one seeking his) beloved infants.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: वृ॒ष्टिं नो॑ अर्ष दि॒व्यां जि॑ग॒त्नुमिळा॑वतीं शं॒गयीं॑ जी॒रदा॑नुम् । स्तुके॑व वी॒ता ध॑न्वा विचि॒न्वन्बन्धूँ॑रि॒माँ अव॑राँ इन्दो वा॒यून्

Sukta 97.translation: “(Soma), when filtered loose (me) bound (by sin) as (one loose) a knot; (grant me) a straight path and strength. You, green-tinted, neigh like a horse (when you are) let loose; proceed divine (Soma) who are friendly to man, and have a dwelling.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ग्र॒न्थिं न वि ष्य॑ ग्रथि॒तं पु॑ना॒न ऋ॒जुं च॑ गा॒तुं वृ॑जि॒नं च॑ सोम । अत्यो॒ न क्र॑दो॒ हरि॒रा सृ॑जा॒नो मर्यो॑ देव धन्व प॒स्त्या॑वान्

Sukta 97.translation: “Indu, who are adequate for exhilaration flow in a stream to the elevated fleece at the sacrifice; thousand- streaming, fragrant, irresistible, flow for the acquisition of food in the combat.”

devanagari.text: अरश्मानो येऽरथा अयुक्ता अत्यासो न ससृजानास आजौ ।एते शुक्रासो धन्वंति सोमा देवासस्ताँ उप याता पिबध्यै ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “These brilliantSomajuices flow like horses let loose inbattle without reins, without chariots, unharnessed; approach them, you gods, to drink.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒र॒श्मानो॒ ये॑ऽर॒था अयु॑क्ता॒ अत्या॑सो॒ न स॑सृजा॒नास॑ आ॒जौ । ए॒ते शु॒क्रासो॑ धन्वन्ति॒ सोमा॒ देवा॑स॒स्ताँ उप॑ याता॒ पिब॑ध्यै

Sukta 97.translation: “So,Indu, at our sacrifice pour the water from the firmament into the vessels; maySomabestow upon us desirable riches in abundance withmaleoffspring and strength.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा न॑ इन्दो अ॒भि दे॒ववी॑तिं॒ परि॑ स्रव॒ नभो॒ अर्ण॑श्च॒मूषु॑ । सोमो॑ अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ काम्यं॑ बृ॒हन्तं॑ र॒यिं द॑दातु वी॒रव॑न्तमु॒ग्रम्

Sukta 97.translation: “When the praise of the zealous worshipper sanctiies him as that of a noisy (crowd) in front (praises) a distinguished (prince) for the support (he affords); then the cows come to the excellent exhilaratingIndu, the lord (of all, abiding) in the pitcher, eager to gratify him (with their milk).”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तक्ष॒द्यदी॒ मन॑सो॒ वेन॑तो॒ वाग्ज्येष्ठ॑स्य वा॒ धर्म॑णि॒ क्षोरनी॑के । आदी॑माय॒न्वर॒मा वा॑वशा॒ना जुष्टं॒ पतिं॑ क॒लशे॒ गाव॒ इन्दु॑म्

Sukta 97.translation: “The divine benefactor of givers, poured (boons) on givers, the intelligent (Soma) distils his true beverage for true (Indra); the radiant (Soma) is the upholder of strength, he is entirely restrained by the ten fingers.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प्र दा॑नु॒दो दि॒व्यो दा॑नुपि॒न्व ऋ॒तमृ॒ताय॑ पवते सुमे॒धाः । ध॒र्मा भु॑वद्वृज॒न्य॑स्य॒ राजा॒ प्र र॒श्मिभि॑र्द॒शभि॑र्भारि॒ भूम॑

devanagari.text: पवित्रेभिः पवमानो नृचक्षा राजा देवानामुत मर्त्यानां ।द्विता भुवद्रयिपती रयीणामृतं भरत्सुभृतं चार्विंदुः ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “Purified by the filters the observers of man, the sovereign of both gods and mortals, the lord of abundant wealth (Soma), is twofold;Indubears the auspicious collected water.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: प॒वित्रे॑भि॒: पव॑मानो नृ॒चक्षा॒ राजा॑ दे॒वाना॑मु॒त मर्त्या॑नाम् । द्वि॒ता भु॑वद्रयि॒पती॑ रयी॒णामृ॒तं भ॑र॒त्सुभृ॑तं॒ चार्विन्दु॑:

devanagari.text: अर्वाँ इव श्रवसे सातिमच्छेंद्रस्य वायोरभि वीतिमर्ष ।स नः सहस्रा बृहतीरिषो दा भवा सोम द्रविणोवित्पुनानः ॥

transliteration.text: árvān-iva ǀ śrávase ǀ sātím ǀ áccha ǀ índrasya ǀ vāyóḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vītím ǀ arṣa ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ bṛhatī́ḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ dāḥ ǀ bháva ǀ soma ǀ draviṇaḥ-vít ǀ punānáḥ ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “Hasten (Soma) to give food toIndraandVāyulike a horse, for (the sake of giving us) food, to acquire wealth; give us abundant thousand-fold food; Soma, when filtered become the dispenser of riches.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अर्वाँ॑ इव॒ श्रव॑से सा॒तिमच्छेन्द्र॑स्य वा॒योर॒भि वी॒तिम॑र्ष । स न॑: स॒हस्रा॑ बृह॒तीरिषो॑ दा॒ भवा॑ सोम द्रविणो॒वित्पु॑ना॒नः

Sukta 97.translation: “May theSomajuices which are gratifying to the gods when poured around (into the vessels) bring us a dwelling andmaleoffspring-- (the juice) endeavouring to gain the favour (of the gods), desired by all offering (to the gods) in heaven like the ministrant priests, most exhilarating.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दे॒वा॒व्यो॑ नः परिषि॒च्यमा॑ना॒: क्षयं॑ सु॒वीरं॑ धन्वन्त॒ सोमा॑: । आ॒य॒ज्यव॑: सुम॒तिं वि॒श्ववा॑रा॒ होता॑रो॒ न दि॑वि॒यजो॑ म॒न्द्रत॑माः

devanagari.text: एवा देव देवताते पवस्व महे सोम प्सरसे देवपानः ।महश्चिद्धि ष्मसि हिताः समर्ये कृधि सुष्ठाने रोदसी पुनानः ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “DivineSoma, who are the beverage of the gods, flow at the sacrifice for (their) abundant food; urged on (by you) may we overcome even mighty (foes) in battle; purified do you render heaven and earth happy abodes (for us).”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒वा दे॑व दे॒वता॑ते पवस्व म॒हे सो॑म॒ प्सर॑से देव॒पान॑: । म॒हश्चि॒द्धि ष्मसि॑ हि॒ताः स॑म॒र्ये कृ॒धि सु॑ष्ठा॒ने रोद॑सी पुना॒नः

Sukta 97.translation: “Yoked by the priests, you neigh like a horse, (you are) terrible as a lion, swifter than thought;Indu, pour happiness upon us by those which are the most direct of the paths leading hitherward.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अश्वो॒ नो क्र॑दो॒ वृष॑भिर्युजा॒नः सिं॒हो न भी॒मो मन॑सो॒ जवी॑यान् । अ॒र्वा॒चीनै॑: प॒थिभि॒र्ये रजि॑ष्ठा॒ आ प॑वस्व सौमन॒सं न॑ इन्दो

devanagari.text: शतं धारा देवजाता असृग्रन्सहस्रमेनाः कवयो मृजंति ।इंदो सनित्रं दिव आ पवस्व पुरएतासि महतो धनस्य ॥

Sukta 97.translation: “Your hundred streams manifested for the gods are loose; the sages cleanse those thousand (streams); pour wealth upon us,Indu, from heaven; you are the precursor of abundant riches.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: श॒तं धारा॑ दे॒वजा॑ता असृग्रन्त्स॒हस्र॑मेनाः क॒वयो॑ मृजन्ति । इन्दो॑ स॒नित्रं॑ दि॒व आ प॑वस्व पुरए॒तासि॑ मह॒तो धन॑स्य

Sukta 97.translation: “As the rays of the days of the sun are let loose (so are the streams of theSoma); a prudent king does not abandon his friend; as a son preserving in pious acts (wins) his father's (safety), do you pour upon this people immunity from defeat.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: दि॒वो न सर्गा॑ अससृग्र॒मह्नां॒ राजा॒ न मि॒त्रं प्र मि॑नाति॒ धीर॑: । पि॒तुर्न पु॒त्रः क्रतु॑भिर्यता॒न आ प॑वस्व वि॒शे अ॒स्या अजी॑तिम्

Sukta 97.translation: “Your exhilarating streams are let loose when you pass purified through the woollen fleece;Pavamānayou flow to the supporting (milk) of the kine, as soon as genitive rated you fill the sun with your radiance.”

devanagari.text: ऋजुः पवस्व वृजिनस्य हंतापामीवां बाधमानो मृधश्च ।अभिश्रीणन्पयः पयसाभि गोनामिंद्रस्य त्वं तव वयं सखायः ॥

transliteration.text: ṛjúḥ ǀ pavasva ǀ vṛjinásya ǀ hantā́ ǀ ápa ǀ ámīvām ǀ bā́dhamānaḥ ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ ca ǀabhi-śrīṇán ǀ páyaḥ ǀ páyasā ǀ abhí ǀ gónām ǀ índrasya ǀ tvám ǀ táva ǀ vayám ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “Flow you who are straight going, the slayer of the crooked-goer, driving away disease and enemies; mixing your juice with thejuice of the kine (you go to the cups); (you are)Indra's (friend), we (are) your friends.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ऋ॒जुः प॑वस्व वृजि॒नस्य॑ ह॒न्तापामी॑वां॒ बाध॑मानो॒ मृध॑श्च । अ॒भि॒श्री॒णन्पय॒: पय॑सा॒भि गोना॒मिन्द्र॑स्य॒ त्वं तव॑ व॒यं सखा॑यः

devanagari.text: मध्वः सूदं पवस्व वस्व उत्सं वीरं च न आ पवस्वा भगं च ।स्वदस्वेंद्राय पवमान इंदो रयिं च न आ पवस्वा समुद्रात् ॥
मध्वः । सूदम् । पवस्व । वस्वः । उत्सम् । वीरम् । च । नः । आ । पवस्व । भगम् । च ।स्वदस्व । इन्द्राय । पवमानः । इन्दो इति । रयिम् । च । नः । आ । पवस्व । समुद्रात् ॥

transliteration.text: mádhvaḥ ǀ sū́dam ǀ pavasva ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ útsam ǀ vīrám ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pavasva ǀ bhágam ǀ ca ǀsvádasva ǀ índrāya ǀ pávamānaḥ ǀ indo íti ǀ rayím ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pavasva ǀ samudrā́t ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “Pour forth a fountain of wealth distilling sweet juice, pour upon usmaleoffspring and riches; flow sweet forIndra, OIndu, when purified; and pour riches upon us from the firmament.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: मध्व॒: सूदं॑ पवस्व॒ वस्व॒ उत्सं॑ वी॒रं च॑ न॒ आ प॑वस्वा॒ भगं॑ च । स्वद॒स्वेन्द्रा॑य॒ पव॑मान इन्दो र॒यिं च॑ न॒ आ प॑वस्वा समु॒द्रात्

devanagari.text: सोमः सुतो धारयात्यो न हित्वा सिंधुर्न निम्नमभि वाज्यक्षाः ।आ योनिं वन्यमसदत्पुनानः समिंदुर्गोभिरसरत्समद्भिः ॥
सोमः । सुतः । धारया । अत्यः । न । हित्वा । सिन्धुः । न । निम्नम् । अभि । वाजी । अक्षारिति ।आ । योनिम् । वन्यम् । असदत् । पुनानः । सम् । इन्दुः । गोभिः । असरत् । सम् । अत्ऽभिः ॥

transliteration.text: sómaḥ ǀ sutáḥ ǀ dhā́rayā ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hítvā ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ ná ǀ nimnám ǀ abhí ǀ vājī́ ǀ akṣāríti ǀā́ ǀ yónim ǀ ványam ǀ asadat ǀ punānáḥ ǀ sám ǀ índuḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ asarat ǀ sám ǀ at-bhíḥ ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “TheSomaeffused in a stream, going like a horse flows powerful like a river down a descent; purified he alights on the wooden abode;Indumixes with the milk and curds, (mixes) with the water.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: सोम॑: सु॒तो धार॒यात्यो॒ न हित्वा॒ सिन्धु॒र्न नि॒म्नम॒भि वा॒ज्य॑क्षाः । आ योनिं॒ वन्य॑मसदत्पुना॒नः समिन्दु॒र्गोभि॑रसर॒त्सम॒द्भिः

devanagari.text: एष स्य ते पवत इंद्र सोमश्चमूषु धीर उशते तवस्वान् ।स्वर्चक्षा रथिरः सत्यशुष्मः कामो न यो देवयतामसर्जि ॥
एषः । स्यः । ते । पवते । इन्द्र । सोमः । चमूषु । धीरः । उशते । तवस्वान् ।स्वःऽचक्षाः । रथिरः । सत्यऽशुष्मः । कामः । न । यः । देवऽयताम् । असर्जि ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ syáḥ ǀ te ǀ pavate ǀ indra ǀ sómaḥ ǀ camū́ṣu ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ uśaté ǀ távasvān ǀsváḥ-cakṣāḥ ǀ rathiráḥ ǀ satyá-śuṣmaḥ ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ deva-yatā́m ǀ ásarji ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “The following sagaciousSomaflows into the cups,Indra, for you, who long (for him)--all-seeing, car-borne, of adequate vigour, who has been sent forth like the wish of the god-desiring (worshippers).”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष स्य ते॑ पवत इन्द्र॒ सोम॑श्च॒मूषु॒ धीर॑ उश॒ते तव॑स्वान् । स्व॑र्चक्षा रथि॒रः स॒त्यशु॑ष्म॒: कामो॒ न यो दे॑वय॒तामस॑र्जि

devanagari.text: एष प्रत्नेन वयसा पुनानस्तिरो वर्पांसि दुहितुर्दधानः ।वसानः शर्म त्रिवरूथमप्सु होतेव याति समनेषु रेभन् ॥
एषः । प्रत्नेन । वयसा । पुनानः । तिरः । वर्पांसि । दुहितुः । दधानः ।वसानः । शर्म । त्रिऽवरूथम् । अप्ऽसु । होताऽइव । याति । समनेषु । रेभन् ॥

transliteration.text: eṣáḥ ǀ pratnéna ǀ váyasā ǀ punānáḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ várpāṃsi ǀ duhitúḥ ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀvásānaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ tri-várūtham ǀ ap-sú ǀ hótā-iva ǀ yāti ǀ sámaneṣu ǀ rébhan ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “Flowing with (his) ancient food, enveloping the forms of the earth, covering the house of sacrifice which has a threefold protection, (plural ced) in the waters he advances calling aloud at the oblations like a ministrant priest.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ए॒ष प्र॒त्नेन॒ वय॑सा पुना॒नस्ति॒रो वर्पां॑सि दुहि॒तुर्दधा॑नः । वसा॑न॒: शर्म॑ त्रि॒वरू॑थम॒प्सु होते॑व याति॒ सम॑नेषु॒ रेभ॑न्

devanagari.text: नू नस्त्वं रथिरो देव सोम परि स्रव चम्वोः पूयमानः ।अप्सु स्वादिष्ठो मधुमाँ ऋतावा देवो न यः सविता सत्यमन्मा ॥
नु । नः । त्वम् । रथिरः । देव । सोम । परि । स्रव । चम्वोः । पूयमानः ।अप्ऽसु । स्वादिष्ठः । मधुऽमान् । ऋतऽवा । देवः । न । यः । सविता । सत्यऽमन्मा ॥

transliteration.text: nú ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǀ rathiráḥ ǀ deva ǀ soma ǀ pári ǀ srava ǀ camvóḥ ǀ pūyámānaḥ ǀap-sú ǀ svā́diṣṭhaḥ ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ deváḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ satyá-manmā ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “DivineSoma, who are car-borne, being filtered (at) our (sacrifice), flow quickly into the cups; most sweet-flavoured in the waters, full of delight, offered at the sacrifice, stimulator of all, who like a god are the object of true praise.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: नू न॒स्त्वं र॑थि॒रो दे॑व सोम॒ परि॑ स्रव च॒म्वो॑: पू॒यमा॑नः । अ॒प्सु स्वादि॑ष्ठो॒ मधु॑माँ ऋ॒तावा॑ दे॒वो न यः स॑वि॒ता स॒त्यम॑न्मा

devanagari.text: अभि वायुं वीत्यर्षा गृणानोऽभि मित्रावरुणा पूयमानः ।अभी नरं धीजवनं रथेष्ठामभींद्रं वृषणं वज्रबाहुं ॥
अभि । वायुम् । वीती । अर्ष । गृणानः । अभि । मित्रावरुणा । पूयमानः ।अभि । नरम् । धीऽजवनम् । रथेऽस्थाम् । अभि । इन्द्रम् । वृषणम् । वज्रऽबाहुम् ॥

transliteration.text: abhí ǀ vāyúm ǀ vītī́ ǀ arṣa ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ pūyámānaḥ ǀabhí ǀ náram ǀ dhī-jávanam ǀ rathe-sthā́m ǀ abhí ǀ índram ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vájra-bāhum ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “Being eulogized, hasten toVāyu, for (him to) drink; being purified, hasten toMitraandVaruṇa; (hasten) to the leader, who is quick as thought, mounted on a car, toIndra, the showerer, the wielder of the thunderbolt.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि वा॒युं वी॒त्य॑र्षा गृणा॒नो॒३॒॑ऽभि मि॒त्रावरु॑णा पू॒यमा॑नः । अ॒भी नरं॑ धी॒जव॑नं रथे॒ष्ठाम॒भीन्द्रं॒ वृष॑णं॒ वज्र॑बाहुम्

devanagari.text: अभि वस्त्रा सुवसनान्यर्षाभि धेनूः सुदुघाः पूयमानः ।अभि चंद्रा भर्तवे नो हिरण्याभ्यश्वान्रथिनो देव सोम ॥
अभि । वस्त्रा । सुऽवसनानि । अर्ष । अभि । धेनूः । सुऽदुघाः । पूयमानः ।अभि । चन्द्रा । भर्तवे । नः । हिरण्या । अभि । अश्वान् । रथिनः । देव । सोम ॥

transliteration.text: abhí ǀ vástrā ǀ su-vasanā́ni ǀ arṣa ǀ abhí ǀ dhenū́ḥ ǀ su-dúghāḥ ǀ pūyámānaḥ ǀabhí ǀ candrā́ ǀ bhártave ǀ naḥ ǀ híraṇyā ǀ abhí ǀ áśvān ǀ rathínaḥ ǀ deva ǀ soma ǁ

Sukta 97.translation: “Bring us handsome garments, bring us, when you are purified, cows easily milked; bring for our maintenance gratifying gold; divineSoma, bring us horses fit for chariots.”
Sukta 97.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि वस्त्रा॑ सुवस॒नान्य॑र्षा॒भि धे॒नूः सु॒दुघा॑: पू॒यमा॑नः । अ॒भि च॒न्द्रा भर्त॑वे नो॒ हिर॑ण्या॒भ्यश्वा॑न्र॒थिनो॑ देव सोम

devanagari.text: अभि नो वाजसातमं रयिमर्ष पुरुस्पृहं ।इंदो सहस्रभर्णसं तुविद्युम्नं विभ्वासहं ॥
अभि । नः । वाजऽसातमम् । रयिम् । अर्ष । पुरुऽस्पृहम् ।इन्दो इति । सहस्रऽभर्णसम् । तुविऽद्युम्नम् । विभ्वऽसहम् ॥

transliteration.text: abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ vāja-sā́tamam ǀ rayím ǀ arṣa ǀ puru-spṛ́ham ǀíndo íti ǀ sahásra-bharṇasam ǀ tuvi-dyumnám ǀ vibhva-sáham ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “Bring us,Indu, strength-bestowing riches, desired bymany, supporting many, far-celebrated and overcoming mighty (foes).”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒भि नो॑ वाज॒सात॑मं र॒यिम॑र्ष पुरु॒स्पृह॑म् । इन्दो॑ स॒हस्र॑भर्णसं तुविद्यु॒म्नं वि॑भ्वा॒सह॑म्

devanagari.text: परि ष्य सुवानो अव्ययं रथे न वर्माव्यत ।इंदुरभि द्रुणा हितो हियानो धाराभिरक्षाः ॥
परि । स्यः । सुवानः । अव्ययम् । रथे । न । वर्म । अव्यत ।इन्दुः । अभि । द्रुणा । हितः । हियानः । धाराभिः । अक्षारिति ॥

transliteration.text: pári ǀ syáḥ ǀ suvānáḥ ǀ avyáyam ǀ ráthe ǀ ná ǀ várma ǀ avyata ǀínduḥ ǀ abhí ǀ drúṇā ǀ hitáḥ ǀ hiyānáḥ ǀ dhā́rābhiḥ ǀ akṣāríti ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “When effused theSomajuice flows to the woollen (filter) as (a warrior) in a chariot is covered in mail; fitted into the wooden (cask), hurrying forth, it flows in streams.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॒ ष्य सु॑वा॒नो अ॒व्ययं॒ रथे॒ न वर्मा॑व्यत । इन्दु॑र॒भि द्रुणा॑ हि॒तो हि॑या॒नो धारा॑भिरक्षाः

devanagari.text: परि ष्य सुवानो अक्षा इंदुरव्ये मदच्युतः ।धारा य ऊर्ध्वो अध्वरे भ्राजा नैति गव्ययुः ॥
परि । स्यः । सुवानः । अक्षारिति । इन्दुः । अव्ये । मदऽच्युतः ।धारा । यः । ऊर्ध्वः । अध्वरे । भ्राजा । न । एति । गव्यऽयुः ॥

transliteration.text: pári ǀ syáḥ ǀ suvānáḥ ǀ akṣāríti ǀ índuḥ ǀ ávye ǀ máda-cyutaḥ ǀdhā́rā ǀ yáḥ ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ bhrājā́ ǀ ná ǀ éti ǀ gavya-yúḥ ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “TheSomajuice being effused flows through the fleece diffusing exhilaration; who, being exalted goes to the sacrifice in a stream desiring the milk and curds as (he goes to the firmament) with radiance.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॒ ष्य सु॑वा॒नो अ॑क्षा॒ इन्दु॒रव्ये॒ मद॑च्युतः । धारा॒ य ऊ॒र्ध्वो अ॑ध्व॒रे भ्रा॒जा नैति॑ गव्य॒युः

devanagari.text: स हि त्वं देव शश्वते वसु मर्ताय दाशुषे ।इंदो सहस्रिणं रयिं शतात्मानं विवाससि ॥
सः । हि । त्वम् । देव । शश्वते । वसु । मर्ताय । दाशुषे ।इन्दो इति । सहस्रिणम् । रयिम् । शतऽआत्मानम् । विवाससि ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ tvám ǀ deva ǀ śáśvate ǀ vásu ǀ mártāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀíndo íti ǀ sahasríṇam ǀ rayím ǀ śatá-ātmānam ǀ vivāsasi ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “For you, divineIndu, grant riches to every man who offers libations, thousand-fold and hundred-fold treasure.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स हि त्वं दे॑व॒ शश्व॑ते॒ वसु॒ मर्ता॑य दा॒शुषे॑ । इन्दो॑ सह॒स्रिणं॑ र॒यिं श॒तात्मा॑नं विवाससि

devanagari.text: वयं ते अस्य वृत्रहन्वसो वस्वः पुरुस्पृहः ।नि नेदिष्ठतमा इषः स्याम सुम्नस्याध्रिगो ॥
वयम् । ते । अस्य । वृत्रऽहन् । वसो इति । वस्वः । पुरुऽस्पृहः ।नि । नेदिष्ठऽतमाः । इषः । स्याम । सुम्नस्य । अध्रिगो इत्यध्रिऽगो ॥

transliteration.text: vayám ǀ te ǀ asyá ǀ vṛtra-han ǀ váso íti ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ puru-spṛ́haḥ ǀní ǀ nédiṣṭha-tamāḥ ǀ iṣáḥ ǀ syā́ma ǀ sumnásya ǀ adhrigo ítyadhri-go ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “Slayer of enemies, may we by your (people);Vasu, (may we be) extremely near your much-coveted wealth; irresistible (Soma), may we be near happiness.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: व॒यं ते॑ अ॒स्य वृ॑त्रह॒न्वसो॒ वस्व॑: पुरु॒स्पृह॑: । नि नेदि॑ष्ठतमा इ॒षः स्याम॑ सु॒म्नस्या॑ध्रिगो

devanagari.text: द्विर्यं पंच स्वयशसं स्वसारो अद्रिसंहतं ।प्रियमिंद्रस्य काम्यं प्रस्नापयंत्यूर्मिणं ॥
द्विः । यम् । पञ्च । स्वऽयशसम् । स्वसारः । अद्रिऽसंहतम् ।प्रियम् । इन्द्रस्य । काम्यम् । प्रऽस्नापयन्ति । ऊर्मिणम् ॥

transliteration.text: dvíḥ ǀ yám ǀ páñca ǀ svá-yaśasam ǀ svásāraḥ ǀ ádri-saṃhatam ǀpriyám ǀ índrasya ǀ kā́myam ǀ pra-snāpáyanti ǀ ūrmíṇam ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “Whom, celebrated, expressed by the stones, dear toIndra, beloved (by all) moving in streams, the twice fiver sister (fingers) bathe (in the sacred waters).”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: द्विर्यं पञ्च॒ स्वय॑शसं॒ स्वसा॑रो॒ अद्रि॑संहतम् । प्रि॒यमिन्द्र॑स्य॒ काम्यं॑ प्रस्ना॒पय॑न्त्यू॒र्मिण॑म्

devanagari.text: परि त्यं हर्यतं हरिं बभ्रुं पुनंति वारेण ।यो देवान्विश्वाँ इत्परि मदेन सह गच्छति ॥
परि । त्यम् । हर्यतम् । हरिम् । बभ्रुम् । पुनन्ति । वारेण ।यः । देवान् । विश्वान् । इत् । परि । मदेन । सह । गच्छति ॥

transliteration.text: pári ǀ tyám ǀ haryatám ǀ hárim ǀ babhrúm ǀ punanti ǀ vā́reṇa ǀyáḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ víśvān ǀ ít ǀ pári ǀ mádena ǀ sahá ǀ gácchati ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “Him, coveted (by all), green-tinted, brown, they purify with the filter; who goes to all the gods with (his) exhilaration.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: परि॒ त्यं ह॑र्य॒तं हरिं॑ ब॒भ्रुं पु॑नन्ति॒ वारे॑ण । यो दे॒वान्विश्वाँ॒ इत्परि॒ मदे॑न स॒ह गच्छ॑ति

devanagari.text: अस्य वो ह्यवसा पांतो दक्षसाधनं ।यः सूरिषु श्रवो बृहद्दधे स्वर्ण हर्यतः ॥
अस्य । वः । हि । अवसा । पान्तः । दक्षऽसाधनम् ।यः । सूरिषु । श्रवः । बृहत् । दधे । स्वः । न । हर्यतः ॥

transliteration.text: asyá ǀ vaḥ ǀ hí ǀ ávasā ǀ pā́ntaḥ ǀ dakṣa-sā́dhanam ǀyáḥ ǀ sūríṣu ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ dadhé ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ haryatáḥ ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “For you by his protection have drunk the strengthening (juice of thatSoma) who, beloved (by all) like the sun, has bestowed abundant food upon his worshippers.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अ॒स्य वो॒ ह्यव॑सा॒ पान्तो॑ दक्ष॒साध॑नम् । यः सू॒रिषु॒ श्रवो॑ बृ॒हद्द॒धे स्व१॒॑र्ण ह॑र्य॒तः

devanagari.text: स वां यज्ञेषु मानवी इंदुर्जनिष्ट रोदसी ।देवो देवी गिरिष्ठा अस्रेधंतं तुविष्वणि ॥
सः । वाम् । यज्ञेषु । मानवी इति । इन्दुः । जनिष्ट । रोदसी इति ।देवः । देवी इति । गिरिऽस्थाः । अस्रेधन् । तम् । तुविऽस्वनि ॥

transliteration.text: sáḥ ǀ vām ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ mānavī íti ǀ índuḥ ǀ janiṣṭa ǀ rodasī íti ǀdeváḥ ǀ devī íti ǀ giri-sthā́ḥ ǀ ásredhan ǀ tám ǀ tuvi-sváni ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “Divine heaven and earth the progeny ofManu, theSomajuice is genitive rated at your sacrifices, radiant, abiding in the grinding stones; (the priests) bruise him at the loud-sounding ceremony.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: स वां॑ य॒ज्ञेषु॑ मानवी॒ इन्दु॑र्जनिष्ट रोदसी । दे॒वो दे॑वी गिरि॒ष्ठा अस्रे॑ध॒न्तं तु॑वि॒ष्वणि॑

devanagari.text: इंद्राय सोम पातवे वृत्रघ्ने परि षिच्यसे ।नरे च दक्षिणावते देवाय सदनासदे ॥
इन्द्राय । सोम । पातवे । वृत्रऽघ्ने । परि । सिच्यसे ।नरे । च । दक्षिणाऽवते । देवाय । सदनऽसदे ॥

transliteration.text: índrāya ǀ soma ǀ pā́tave ǀ vṛtra-ghné ǀ pári ǀ sicyase ǀnáre ǀ ca ǀ dákṣiṇā-vate ǀ devā́ya ǀ sadana-sáde ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “You are poured forth,Soma, forIndra, the slayer ofVṛtra, to drink; and for the munificent worshipper who sits in the halls of sacrifice (to give oblations) to god.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: इन्द्रा॑य सोम॒ पात॑वे वृत्र॒घ्ने परि॑ षिच्यसे । नरे॑ च॒ दक्षि॑णावते दे॒वाय॑ सदना॒सदे॑

devanagari.text: ते प्रत्नासो व्युष्टिषु सोमाः पवित्रे अक्षरन् ।अपप्रोथंतः सनुतर्हुरश्चितः प्रातस्ताँ अप्रचेतसः ॥
ते । प्रत्नासः । विऽउष्टिषु । सोमाः । पवित्रे । अक्षरन् ।अपऽप्रोथन्तः । सनुतः । हुरःऽचितः । प्रातरिति । तान् । अप्रऽचेतसः ॥

transliteration.text: té ǀ pratnā́saḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀ sómāḥ ǀ pavítre ǀ akṣaran ǀapa-próthantaḥ ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ huraḥ-cítaḥ ǀ prātáríti ǀ tā́n ǀ ápra-cetasaḥ ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “Those ancientSomajuices flow into the filter at the dawn, driving away in the early morning the concealed and ignorant thieves.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: ते प्र॒त्नासो॒ व्यु॑ष्टिषु॒ सोमा॑: प॒वित्रे॑ अक्षरन् । अ॒प॒प्रोथ॑न्तः सनु॒तर्हु॑र॒श्चित॑: प्रा॒तस्ताँ अप्र॑चेतसः

devanagari.text: तं सखायः पुरोरुचं यूयं वयं च सूरयः ।अश्याम वाजगंध्यं सनेम वाजपस्त्यं ॥
तम् । सखायः । पुरःऽरुचम् । यूयम् । वयम् । च । सूरयः ।अश्याम । वाजऽगन्ध्यम् । सनेम । वाजऽपस्त्यम् ॥

transliteration.text: tám ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ puraḥ-rúcam ǀ yūyám ǀ vayám ǀ ca ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀaśyā́ma ǀ vā́ja-gandhyam ǀ sanéma ǀ vā́ja-pastyam ǁ

Sukta 98.translation: “May you and we, intelligent friends, eat the brightSomafragrant and invigorating, may we obtain food and dwellings.”
Sukta 98.sanskrit_wisdomlib: तं स॑खायः पुरो॒रुचं॑ यू॒यं व॒यं च॑ सू॒रय॑: । अ॒श्याम॒ वाज॑गन्ध्यं स॒नेम॒ वाज॑पस्त्यम्

devanagari.text: आ हर्यताय धृष्णवे धनुस्तन्वंति पौंस्यं ।शुक्रां वयंत्यसुराय निर्णिजं विपामग्रे महीयुवः ॥
आ । हर्यताय । धृष्णवे । धनुः । तन्वन्ति । पौंस्यम् ।शुक्राम् । वयन्ति । असुराय । निःऽनिजम् । विपाम् । अग्रे । महीयुवः ॥

transliteration.text: ā́ ǀ haryatā́ya ǀ dhṛṣṇáve ǀ dhánuḥ ǀ tanvanti ǀ páuṃsyam ǀśukrā́m ǀ vayanti ǀ ásurāya ǀ niḥ-níjam ǀ vipā́m ǀ ágre ǀ mahīyúvaḥ ǁ

Sukta 99.translation: “They stretch the bow of manhood for the beloved courageous (Soma); (the priests) wishing to worship spread out the white filter for the mighty (Soma) in the presence of the sage (deities).”
Sukta 99.sanskrit_wisdomlib: आ ह॑र्य॒ताय॑ धृ॒ष्णवे॒ धनु॑स्तन्वन्ति॒ पौंस्य॑म् । शु॒क्रां व॑य॒न्त्यसु॑राय नि॒र्णिजं॑ वि॒पामग्रे॑ मही॒युव॑:

devanagari.text: अध क्षपा परिष्कृतो वाजाँ अभि प्र गाहते ।यदी विवस्वतो धियो हरिं हिन्वंति यातवे ॥

transliteration.text: ádha ǀ kṣapā́ ǀ pári-kṛtaḥ ǀ vā́jān ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ gāhate ǀyádi ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ hárim ǀ hinvánti ǀ yā́tave ǁ

Sukta 99.translation: “Consecrated at the end of the night (theSoma) plural nges into the viands, when the fingers of the worshipper press out the green-tinted (juice) to go (to the vessels).”
Sukta 99.sanskrit_wisdomlib: अध॑ क्ष॒पा परि॑ष्कृतो॒ वाजाँ॑ अ॒भि प्र गा॑हते । यदी॑ वि॒वस्व॑तो॒ धियो॒ हरिं॑ हि॒न्वन्ति॒ यात॑वे

devanagari.text: तमस्य मर्जयामसि मदो य इंद्रपातमः ।यं गाव आसभिर्दधुः पुरा नूनं च सूरयः ॥
